title: Order-adaptive subspace scale learning for unsupervised anomaly detection under time-varying rotational speed conditions
abstract: Under time-varying speeds, rotating machinery experiences pronounced dynamic effects, making this operational phase highly susceptible to faults. Anomaly detection under such non-stationary condition is challenging, as speed-induced distribution shifts in vibration signals often lead conventional methods to mistake normal variations for faults, resulting in false alarms. Although data driven methods aim to learn speed-invariant representations, its generalization to unseen speed profiles remains limited. To address this, we propose a physics-informed Order-Adaptive Subspace Scale Learning (OASSL) method that integrates order tracking grounded in the physical relationship between vibration harmonics and shaft rotation. This approach resamples time-domain signals into the angular domain to generate unified order-frequency features, considerably eliminating the influence of speed fluctuations. Furthermore, a novel multi-subspace sampling and subspace scale learning strategy is introduced within the network, which enhances the extraction of subtle fault signatures and improves robustness against varying operating conditions. Experimental results on time-varying speed datasets demonstrate that the proposed OASSL significantly outperforms existing methods in reducing false alarms and accurately identifying faults under complex speed variations.

title: Model updating of structures by combining reduced order modelling and deep reinforcement learning
abstract: This paper presents an automated framework for structural model updating that integrates reduced-order modelling (ROM) with deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Continuous structural health monitoring (SHM) data are used to calibrate numerical models acting as digital twins of real structures, a task that becomes computationally prohibitive when high-fidelity finite element models are employed for highly uncertain systems. To address this challenge, a ROM is constructed from a physically consistent dataset generated by a full-order model and embedded within a DRL environment. An intelligent agent autonomously explores the parameter space and identifies optimal values by minimizing discrepancies between simulated and measured modal quantities. The proposed methodology, termed DRUM-Av2.0, is validated through two fictitious case studies of increasing complexity and a real prestressed concrete bridge. Results demonstrate up to two orders of magnitude reduction in computational time compared to FOM-based updating, while maintaining high accuracy in parameter identification. The framework provides a scalable and automated solution suitable for practical SHM applications and continuous digital twin calibration.

title: A sequential bayesian operational mode classification for SHM under discrete operational variability
abstract: Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) evaluates a structure’s condition by comparing its current state to a baseline representing a healthy state. However, many structures operate under multiple regimes, requiring multiple discrete baselines. This operational variability challenges conventional mitigation approaches, highlighting the need for methods that can automatically account for discrete variations in operation. This study leverages the concept of operational modes to address multiple discrete operating regimes as classes which are subsequently determined via a robust Bayesian classifier capable of handling variations, noise, and transition periods between modes. Specifically, a Bayesian Multinomial Logistic Regression model integrated with a Hidden Markov Model (BMLR-HMM) is proposed, where the probabilistic approach ensures robustness to noise, supports informed decision-making for each classification, and exploits the temporal structure in the evolution of the modes. The model was first tested on a simple. simulated dataset, and then using the vibrational responses from gearboxes on a Crew Transfer Vessel during operation. Results demonstrate high accuracy in mode classification, with the probabilistic nature of the model enabling uncertainty quantification, forming the basis for informed decision-making when classifications are less confident. This approach contributes to the development of robust classifiers for operational analysis in dynamic environments, with applications in SHM and other domains requiring mode identification for performance or integrity assessment.

title: Physics-informed neural operators for predicting structural intensity from laser Doppler vibrometry measurements of plates
abstract: Structural intensity is a powerful diagnostic tool for characterizing vibrational energy flow and identifying dominant transfer paths in structures. For thin-walled plates, the structural intensity can be computed from the transverse displacement field and its spatial derivatives. However, accurate estimation from experimental data remains challenging, as numerical differentiation is highly sensitive to measurement noise, particularly when computing higher-order spatial gradients. This study proposes a machine learning-based framework employing a physics-informed deep operator network to predict structural intensity directly from noisy displacement measurements. Instead of differentiating raw measurement data, the method first learns a smooth, fully differentiable neural-network surrogate of the displacement field, enabling stable and accurate evaluation of higher-order spatial derivatives via automatic differentiation. This eliminates noise-induced instabilities of conventional numerical differentiation methods and enables robust structural intensity prediction from experimental data. The methodology is assessed using two case studies: an analytical benchmark problem of a simply supported plate, and experimental laser Doppler vibrometry measurements of a plate structure for practical validation. The results demonstrate that the physics-informed deep operator network accurately predicts the displacement and structural intensity fields over a broad frequency range, capturing both magnitude distributions and directional patterns with high fidelity. Across all studies, the proposed data-driven approach consistently outperforms numerical differentiation techniques, demonstrating enhanced robustness and accuracy while confirming its applicability to problems in experimental structural dynamics and noise control engineering.

title: Terahertz characterization of internal debonding defects of composites under class imbalance condition using lightweight network
abstract: Terahertz (THz) technology, a promising alternative to traditional non-destructive testing (NDT) methods, emerges great potential for quantitative characterization of debonding defect in Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymer (GFRP) composites. However, during the intelligent identification of debonding defects inside composite, there are challenges with class imbalance in THz datasets leading to reduced accuracy, and traditional deep learning models struggle to balance classification precision with inference speed. Therefore, a lightweight THz three-dimensional characterization system based on Ghost Bottleneck Attention Module Network (GBAMNet) for THz class-imbalanced dataset is proposed to ultimately achieve the automatic characterization of hidden debonding defect inside GFRP. Ghost layer convolution and Bottleneck Attention Module (BAM) modules are specially designed to capture essential features from the raw THz signals with a low computational cost, and thus realizing real-time, high-accuracy categorization of THz signals. The ghost feature factor s is introduced to control the number of ghost feature mappings generated by linear transformations within the Ghost layer, increasing the quantity of feature mappings in the network to enhance representational capabilities with minimal computational and parameter overhead. Moreover, the Gradient Harmonizing Mechanism (GHM) Loss function addresses the class-imbalance issue by dynamically adjusting the gradient weights of each sample to achieve a balanced gradient distribution. The comprehensive performance of GBAMNet with respect to classification accuracy and inference velocity are validated by a series of experiments on the class-imbalanced dataset. Overall, our proposed system will promote the actual applications of Terahertz non-destructive testing (THz NDT) scenarios for automatic and real-time defect characterization.

title: Simulation of non-Gaussian wind pressure process based on machine learning-enhanced Hermite polynomial model
abstract: Accurately simulating non-Gaussian wind pressure fields on low-rise building roofs is critical for wind-resistant reliability design. This paper proposes a machine learning-enhanced Hermite polynomial model (ML-EHPM)-based method for the rapid and precise simulation of stationary non-Gaussian wind pressures. Building upon traditional moment-based HPM simulation methods, this study develops two machine learning models to enhance simulation accuracy and efficiency. First, in determining the ML-EHPM-based translation function, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), combined with the Bald Eagle Search optimization algorithm, is used to establish a nonlinear mapping from the first ten-order raw moments to the statistical moments of the translation function. This processing eliminates the need for integral solutions and monotonic interval constraints. Subsequently, a backpropagation neural network (BPNN) is employed to map non-Gaussian power spectra to Gaussian power spectra. To validate the simulation performance, three univariate simulation cases (strongly non-Gaussian, non-monotonic regions, and bimodal distributions) and one multivariate simulation case are given. Results indicate that the ML-EHPM approach offers substantially improved simulation accuracy than the conventional HPM method. Additionally, it can also simulate wind pressures in non-monotonic regions where the traditional HPM method is unavailable. Therefore, the proposed method provides a practical and efficient tool for high-precision simulation of non-Gaussian wind pressures.

title: Optimized S-transform embedded time–frequency interpretable neural network for aero-engine fault diagnosis
abstract: Convolutional neural network (CNN) has attracted significant attention for its powerful capability in fault feature extraction, and has has found widespread applications in intelligent fault diagnosis of mechanical systems. Nevertheless, its limited interpretability and vulnerability to noise remain key challenges in both academic and industrial contexts. Motivated by the strong theoretical foundations and physical interpretability of traditional signal processing methods, this study aims to enhance the performance of CNN by integrating signal analysis theory. Given the non-stationary characteristics and high noise levels commonly observed in aero-engine vibration signals, conventional time–frequency analysis methods often fail to provide optimal representations. To address this limitation, a first-order frequency function with two adjustable parameters are introduced into the Gaussian window function of the original S-transform, deriving an optimized S-transform (OST) that exhibits improved window adaptability and enhanced time–frequency representation capability. Then, an OST embedded time–frequency interpretable neural network (OSTNN) is proposed for fault diagnosis in aero-engines without any predefined parameters. This design enables the transformation of standard first layer convolutional kernel in the CNN method into OST convolutional kernel, whose parameters are continuously adjusted during the training procedure. The proposed OSTNN framework not only effectively suppresses noise interference effectively but also enhances model interpretability through visualization of learned time–frequency feature distributions and analysis of overall amplitude-frequency response. Extensive experiments on three aero-engine datasets, covering typical bearing and rotor faults, demonstrated that the OSTNN method consistently outperforms surpasses eight state-of-the-art diagnostic approaches in terms of effectiveness, noise robustness, interpretability, imbalance, generalization, and few-shot learning capability.

title: Utilization of acoustic emission signals for monitoring CFRP drilling quality with AI-based methods: evaluation, prediction, and morphological reconstruction
abstract: Drilling Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymers (CFRP) is a critical process in composite manufacturing, but ensuring high precision and quality poses significant challenges. The presence of defects such as delamination, fraying, and rough hole walls directly impacts the material’s performance and durability. Conventional quality control methods often involve post-process inspection, which is time-consuming and cannot prevent defects during manufacturing. There is a need for real-time, non-destructive monitoring methods to maintain high-quality standards while improving efficiency. This study aims to develop an advanced approach for real-time monitoring and prediction of CFRP drilling quality using Acoustic Emission (AE) signals and state-of-the-art machine learning models. A robotic drilling system was employed to conduct the experiments. During drilling, AE signals were collected, and hole edge images were captured using an industrial camera. White-light confocal profilometry was used to acquire hole wall morphology data. Relationships between drilling parameters and hole quality were analyzed, alongside AE signal features. Advanced AI models were proposed, including a probabilistic drilling stage identification model, K-means-based defect evaluation, a Transformer-based real-time defect monitoring model, and a VAE-Transformer hybrid model for reconstructing hole wall morphologies from AE signals. The proposed models successfully characterized drilling defects and enabled precise identification of drilling stages. Real-time defect monitoring based on AE signal slices showcased high accuracy, while the reconstruction model effectively predicted hole wall morphologies. This study introduces a transformative approach for real-time, non-destructive CFRP quality monitoring during drilling, significantly enhancing production efficiency and ensuring defect-free manufacturing in aerospace and automotive applications.

title: Digital twin of a pipe conveying fluid: Flow rate anomaly detection and quantification via multi-fidelity Kalman filters and event based cameras signals
abstract: This work is motivated by the need for scalable Digital Twins (DT) for hydro turbines. We propose a DT framework using Bayesian algorithms embedded with machine learning techniques to study a simplified pipe conveying fluid (PCF) system. The Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) is employed for parameter identification by estimating the unknown flow rate that excites the pipe by leveraging the known nonlinear dynamical equations. Experimental validation using event-based camera data and a 3D reconstruction algorithm demonstrates the effectiveness of the UKF, estimating the flow rate with an average estimation error of 6%. To enhance scalability and enable real-time anomaly detection, a Linear Kalman Filter (LKF) is coupled with Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD). DMD is trained on the states estimated by the UKF, providing physical insight to the data-driven model order reduction method. This embedded LKF-DMD approach reduces the complexity of the model and accelerates the computation by three orders of magnitude, from 12 s to 1 0 − 3 s per iteration. When the flow velocity changes, anomaly detection is performed by applying a steepest-ascent hill climbing method which quantifies the change in entropy of the distribution of the Euclidean distance between the trained DMD modal phase diagram and the LKF estimates. The integration of the UKF for system identification, and the accelerated LKF-DMD for state estimation and anomaly detection within a unified DT framework, which have been validated using the lab-scale PCF setup, highlights the potential of these techniques to develop scalable and predictive maintenance tools for engineering systems. • A Digital twin framework of a pipe conveying fluid is proposed. • An efficient approach reconstructs the 3D pipe motion with event-based cameras. • The integration of Bayesian methods enhanced with a data-driven technique is provided. • Anomaly detection and quantification through parameter identification is performed. • Validation is realized with a true experimental setup in real-time.

title: Deep learning-based mechanism- and signal-driven framework for early prediction of milling surface roughness
abstract: As a key part of intelligent machining systems, surface roughness prediction plays a vital role in improving machining efficiency and ensuring product quality. However, the prediction accuracy of traditional mechanism-based physical models is restricted by idealized assumptions, whereas data-driven approaches rely excessively on monitoring signals, limiting their ability to capture future machining information and lacking model interpretability. To address these issues, this study proposes a deep learning-based mechanism- and signal-driven framework for the early prediction of milling surface roughness. First, a physical model of surface morphology is established by comprehensively accounting for the tool rigid motion trajectory, runout, and deflection. The global mechanism knowledge generated by the physical model is embedded into the data-driven modeling process. Second, multi-source signals are synchronously monitored online during machining, and preliminary multi-domain features are extracted from the time-series data to support subsequent modeling. Third, an integrated mechanism- and signal-driven Transformer (IMSformer) is constructed, consisting of the deep mechanism knowledge mining module, deep signal feature extraction module, mechanism-signal fusion module, and regression prediction module. Mechanism knowledge and signal features are jointly used as inputs to IMSformer, enabling the prediction task through deep extraction and fusion of high-level representations. Experimental validation is conducted under both the same and different conditions using milling data collected from a machining center, demonstrating the superior performance of the proposed framework.

title: Phoneme-inspired acoustic frame embedded lightweight transformer for rolling bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Acoustic-based fault diagnosis has gained increasing attention due to its flexibility and applicability under diverse operating conditions. Recent studies have demonstrated that Transformer-based architectures exhibit remarkable capability in modeling long-range temporal dependencies, so they are particularly effective for complex time series representation and analysis. However, applying Transformers to acoustic fault diagnosis faces the following critical challenges. The primary hurdle lies in discriminating short-duration nonstationary acoustic features amidst complex environmental interference, Simultaneously, how to ensure model diagnostic performance under limited computing resources is a challenge. Inspired by the phoneme processing paradigm where continuous speech is discretized into meaningful units, this paper proposes a lightweight acoustic segment-frame embedded Transformer, termed ASFE-Transformer, to address these issues effectively. First, an Analytic Amplitude-Phase Representation Module is introduced to derive physically meaningful representations, ensuring that the instantaneous evolution characteristics of multidimensional acoustic signals are faithfully retained. Second, an Acoustic Frame Embedding Module is developed to aggregate continuous analytic samples into a single token during the embedding stage. This strategy generates a more efficient token sequence and explicitly enhances the discriminability of transient fault cues while substantially reducing the computational burden. Third, the feed-forward network of the Transformer is redesigned by proposing a novel Swish-Depthwise Gated Linear Unit. By embedding a lightweight depth-wise convolution within the Swish-activated gating mechanism, this module introduces local contextual awareness into the encoder. Comprehensive experiments on two bearing acoustic datasets verify that the proposed framework delivers robust diagnostic performance with a lightweight design and highlight its strong potential for real-world industrial deployment.

title: Hybrid generative-probabilistic machine learning approach for predicting residual tensile strength and elastic modulus of FRP coupons under environmental exposure
abstract: The continuous deterioration of concrete and masonry structures has increased the demand for rehabilitation and strengthening of aging civil assets. Fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites have been utilized to enhance the structural capacity of deteriorated structures. While these composites can be used in various environments, their performance is often compromised after exposure to harsh conditions, leading to a reduction in the structural capacity of the strengthened elements. Therefore, understanding the post-exposure residual performance of FRP composites, specifically residual tensile strength and elastic modulus is crucial for developing effective rehabilitation strategies. However, predicting the post-exposure performance of FRP coupons is inherently complex due to the involvement of multiple environmental and material parameters, as well as limited experimental data. This challenge necessitates the implementation of innovative modelling approaches to enhance both prediction accuracy and reliability and potentially mitigate the limitations of available small datasets. To address these challenges, this study employed credible synthetic data generated by advanced generative models, specifically a conditional tabular generative adversarial network (CTGAN) and a tabular variational autoencoder (TVAE), for machine learning model development. Moreover, probabilistic neural networks (PNNs) and natural gradient boosting (NGB) models were developed to predict the residual tensile strength and elastic modulus of FRP coupons and quantify the prediction uncertainty. The results indicated that the TVAE synthesizer demonstrated greater capability for generating credible synthetic data for predictive model development than the CTGAN synthesizer. Furthermore, the NGB model exhibited marginally better performance than the PNN model in predicting the residual tensile strength and elastic modulus of the FRP coupons, achieving testing coefficient of determination values of 0.9635 and 0.9914, respectively. In addition, the Shapley additive exPlanations feature importance analysis was employed to evaluate the influence of input parameters on the predictions, providing valuable insights into the performance evaluation of FRP composites under exposure conditions.

title: MS-DAWCAE: multi-scale deep adversarial wavelet convolutional autoencoder toward unseen fault diagnosis with limited data
abstract: Deep learning has achieved rapid development in mechanical fault diagnosis. However, it still faces challenges in practical applications due to limited fault samples and the emergence of unseen fault types. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Multi-Scale Deep Adversarial Wavelet Convolutional Autoencoder (MS-DAWCAE) for unseen fault detection and known fault diagnosis in small-sample scenarios. The model first integrates wavelet scattering transformation with multi-scale convolutional encoding to extract hierarchical features that capture both local anomalies and global structural patterns, thereby improving reconstruction of known categories and enlarging reconstruction errors for unknown faults. Accordingly, a collaborative adversarial learning module with dual discriminators is then designed to regulate latent representations and supervise reconstruction quality, effectively compressing intra-class variations and enhancing separability between known and unknown categories. Furthermore, a fully connected classifier is incorporated into a multi-task framework to enable accurate identification of known faults while maintaining sensitivity to novel ones. Extensive experiments on industrial datasets demonstrate that, compared with advanced machine learning and transfer learning–based methods, MS-DAWCAE achieved an F1 score of at least 0.90 on the FST dataset under various operating conditions. Moreover, on a publicly available centrifugal pump dataset, MS-DAWCAE outperforms the optimal method by 15%–25% under small-sample settings, validating its effectiveness, robustness, and scalability for practical industrial fault diagnosis.

title: Lamb wave-based cross-domain damage identification for CFRP composite structures using a modular deep learning framework
abstract: Machine learning in Lamb wave-based damage identification has significantly advanced diagnostic technologies due to its exceptional feature extraction capability in processing massive monitoring data. However, existing methods still exhibit significant limitations in identifying damage at locations not covered by the training data, which severely hinders their practical engineering applications. To address this, this study proposes a cross-domain damage identification method for CFRP composite structures based on a modular deep learning framework. The framework architecture integrates three core modules: a multi-channel signal fusion module, a feature extraction module, and a domain adaptation regression module. The multi-channel signal fusion module enhances the characterization of damage features by integrating Lamb wave damage-scattered signals from multiple sensing paths. The feature extraction module employs continuous wavelet convolutional layers to realize adaptive extraction and interpretability enhancement of sensitive features of Lamb wave signals. The domain adaptation regression module introduces a novel joint distribution adaptation approach, significantly improving the model’s generalization performance for unseen damage locations. Lamb wave signals are collected using the lead zirconate titanate (PZT) sensors array on a composite stiffened panel and an aluminum plate, covering four cross-domain damage localization tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves significantly lower localization errors in identifying unseen damage locations compared to the existing state-of-the-art damage localization methods. Meanwhile, the framework maintains its excellent cross-domain generalization ability under scenarios involving variations in damage size, material, and structure.

title: Two-stage autoencoder reconstruction based unsupervised delamination imaging using laser sensed wavefields
abstract: Delamination quantification using guided wavefields has gained attention due to the high sensitivity of ultrasonic guided waves and advances in wavefield scanning. Although supervised deep learning enhances wavefield analysis, its application is limited by the high cost of large-scale labeling. Semi-supervised approaches alleviate this issue but still depend on curated, defect-free reference data. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes an unsupervised framework that integrates Convolutional Autoencoders (CAE) with guided wavefields, requiring neither labels nor historical data. The framework enables delamination quantification from a single wavefield snapshot captured when direct waves fully cover the inspection region. It leverages neural networks’ tendency to overfit dominant healthy patterns, causing poor reconstruction in delaminated areas. The snapshot is divided into uniform patches and symmetrically flipped to enhance data diversity. Each patch is independently reconstructed by the CAE, and a pixel-wise reconstruction error map highlights delamination regions as high-error zone. A two-stage training strategy further reinforces healthy-region reconstruction. Experiments on scanning laser Doppler vibrometer data validate the effectiveness of the augmentation scheme, the two-stage strategy, and the framework’s robustness to varying defect shapes and locations. Overall, the proposed method provides a practical and robust solution for wavefield-based delamination detection without pre-collected or labeled data.

title: FCTransformer: An intelligent fault diagnosis method for multi-sensor information fusion based on Fourier convolution and transformer
abstract: Aiming at the problems of missing information and insufficient modelling in the frequency domain and time domain for the existing multi-sensor data fusion methods, an intelligent fault diagnosis method based on Fourier convolution and Transformer (FCTransformer) is proposed. Firstly, the method uses principal component analysis (PCA) to downscale high-dimensional and multi-modal sensor data, and converts them into RGB images by continuous wavelet transform (CWT). Then, a Fourier convolution (FC) is designed, which can not only effectively extract local periodic frequency domain features, but also enhances the nonlinear feature extraction capability of the model. Finally, a variational auto-encoding transformer (VAETransformer) is designed to achieve global dependency modelling, which enhances the identification for multi-sensor coupled features. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, experimental validation is carried out on the bearing and gearbox datasets. The results show that the average fault diagnosis accuracy of FCTransformer is 99.58% under normal sample conditions, and its average fault diagnosis accuracy is 96.10% under small sample conditions. This indicates that FCTransformer has superior fault diagnosis performance and can meet the requirements of rotating machinery fault diagnosis tasks.

title: Online detection of milling chatter based on multi-order graph convolutional neural network
abstract: Chatter is a type of self-excited vibration that occurs during machining, particularly when processing weak-rigidity aerospace parts, adversely affecting machining quality and efficiency. In order to prevent the detrimental effects of chatter in milling processes, a physically interpretable multi-order graph convolutional neural network (GCN)-based method is proposed for online chatter detection. In this method, the vertex and edge of the network are first constructed through the measured multi-channel vibration signal time series segments with short duration, establishing the groundwork for online chatter detection. Then, a multi-order GCN is developed by gathering feature information from multiple orders of neighbors of the target vertex to enhance its accuracy. Next, based on the multi-order GCN, a deep neural network is constructed and trained using the vibration data obtained by numerous milling experiments. During the training process, the edge weights are optimized by the gradient descent method. After that, an online chatter detection system is constructed, which demonstrates robust noise resistance through tests with different levels of noise interference added. Finally, experiments under various milling conditions validate that the proposed method can accurately detect milling chatter at its early weak stage, thereby successfully preventing its adverse effects.

title: Maximum prediction discrepancy domain adaptation network for rolling bearing RUL prediction under multiple cross-domain scenarios
abstract: Achieving cross-domain remaining useful life (RUL) prediction, improves efficiency of RUL prediction in ensuring the reliability of mechanical equipment. However, current research mainly focuses on single cross-domain scenario such as cross-working conditions, while few studies concerning applicability for multiple cross-domain scenarios. In practical applications, the challenge of extracting domain-invariant features caused by diverse data distribution discrepancies accompanying multiple cross-domain scenarios, coupled with the inherent limitations of existing methodological frameworks, limits the generalization performance and application efficiency of current cross-domain RUL prediction methods. Therefore, this paper proposes a maximum prediction discrepancy domain adaptation network (MP2DAN), to achieve rolling bearing RUL prediction under multiple cross-domain scenarios. In MP2DAN, to address the performance limitation under multiple cross-domain scenarios, a maximum prediction discrepancy (MPD) domain adaptation (DA) approach is proposed. Leveraging the correlation between decision boundaries of different RULs and target domain samples, MPD flexibly learns domain-invariant feature representations from diverse data distribution discrepancies, through a three-stage adversarial training designed between the feature extractor and two RUL predictors. Then, drawing on the characteristics of MPD framework, a synergistic adversarial self-supervised learning (SASL) approach is designed, which aims to empower the target domain to promote MPD in achieving DA, and constrain the feature generation of target domain to ensure the effectiveness of prediction results through knowledge transfer and self-supervised learning. Finally, the ablation and comparative experiments are performed on three bearing datasets. Through the performance quantification and visualization analysis, it is verified that MP2DAN can effectively and generically realize RUL prediction under multiple cross-domain scenarios.

title: Tool wear monitoring and multi-step forecasting in deep hole boring based on physics-informed neural network and ARIMA model
abstract: Tool wear monitoring (TWM) is critical for deep hole boring, significantly impacting production efficiency, machining quality, and cost reduction. Traditional TWM approaches, primarily relying on physics-based models or data-driven models, face limitations: physics-based models often fail under complex, non-idealized machining conditions, while data-driven models require substantial high-quality data. To overcome these challenges, this study first proposes a novel physics-informed neural network (PINN) with a dual-branch architecture: (1)A data-driven branch takes multi-channel features and flank wear width (VB) as inputs and outputs to model their relationship. The multi-channel features were extracted and selected based on relevance from cutting force, vibration, and audio signals, combined with time information. The VB values are derived through a detailed study of the wear mechanisms of boring tools, supported by measurement of the tool’s worn morphology. (2)A physics-informed branch takes as input the multi-channel features and VB, the first- and second-order derivatives of wear with respect to time and health indicators, as well as the mixed second-order derivative, and outputs the tool wear rate. This network implicitly learns the underlying partial differential equation governing wear dynamics. The total loss function combines data-driven loss, physics-informed loss, and a tool wear monotonicity constraint to align with physical wear mechanisms. Next, a hybrid approach employing second-order smoothing and an autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) model enables robust multi-step wear forecasting even with limited historical data. Finally, validated across 10 distinct deep hole boring conditions, the PINN model demonstrates superior performance: it reduces average prediction errors by over 42.9% compared to other models, while exhibiting enhanced robustness. Crucially, the multi-step forecasting achieves exceptional accuracy, maintaining a maximum prediction error below 0.04 mm across all boring conditions, significantly outperforming the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) model. This work provides both theoretical insights and practical guidance for implementing advanced tool condition recognition in deep hole machining applications.

title: Data-model-co-driven approach for real-time reconstruction of unmeasured responses via multi-fidelity surrogate modeling
abstract: The data-model-co-driven approach offers a promising solution for real-time reconstruction of structural responses without prior measurements, exemplified by unmeasured responses. However, the accuracy of existing co-driven approaches is highly dependent on the fidelity of the Finite Element (FE) model, which limits their practical applicability in Structural Health Monitoring (SHM). To tackle this issue, this study proposes a co-driven framework based on multi-fidelity surrogate modeling. In the proposed framework, a Low-Fidelity (LF) model substitutes the FE model to estimate the full-field structural responses, while a High-Fidelity (HF) model learns the error mechanism between FE-simulated and measured data and subsequently improves the accuracy of all LF outputs. The proposed approach is validated through the full-field reconstruction of cable forces in a cable net structure. For three cable force locations assumed to be unmeasured, an investigation into the influence of the correlation between LF outputs and measurements on reconstruction accuracy reveals that the proposed approach is not strictly dependent on the fidelity of the FE-simulated data. Meanwhile, the proposed approach achieves a maximum Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 17.93 kN at these measurement points, compared with RMSE values exceeding 38 kN obtained using an existing co-driven approach. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the proposed approach enables real-time reconstruction of unmeasured structural responses with acceptable accuracy, while reducing its dependence on the fidelity of the FE model.

title: Vibration Koopman Neural Operator: A Koopman-based approach for reliable remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Trustworthy maintenance decisions for industrial equipment depend on accurate prediction and uncertainty assessment of its Remaining Useful Life (RUL). However, the inherent nonlinear dynamics of the equipment degradation process pose a fundamental challenge to reliable uncertainty quantification (UQ). In nonlinear systems, the propagation of uncertainty is complex and analytically intractable, rendering existing UQ methods unreliable and poorly interpretable. To this end, this paper proposes an innovative framework for RUL prediction and UQ, rooted in the principle of Koopman-based lifting to a space of observables, where the dynamics evolve linearly. Its core contribution is the Vibration Koopman Neural Operator (VKNO), a deep network that, for the first time, learns a time-varying Koopman operator and transforms the complex evolution of non-autonomous (time-varying) systems into a stable and analytically tractable linear evolution in the learned observable space. Through a dual-branch architecture, the framework synergizes VKNO’s global dynamic insights with a data-driven branch’s ability to capture local patterns, and achieves dynamic UQ via a probabilistic output deeply coupled with the dynamics. Experiments on public and self-constructed datasets show that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models in both prediction accuracy (a 23.1% reduction in Mean Absolute Error) and uncertainty quantification (achieving a 99.87% Prediction Interval Coverage Probability), providing a new paradigm for high-reliability prognostics.

title: GC-TimeGAN: Time–frequency domain model for high-fidelity reconstruction of Maglev track irregularity
abstract: Track irregularity is one of the primary sources of vibration disturbances in maglev trains, and its precise modeling is critical to improving simulation model fidelity and optimizing controller design. This paper proposes a model for modeling high-speed maglev track irregularity that integrates both time domain and frequency domain, namely the globally conditioned time series generative adversarial network (GC-TimeGAN). The model captures the complexity of track irregularity comprehensively by conditioning on frequency spectrum information, which is relevant to engineering applications. It generates high-speed maglev track irregularity data that align with the spectral characteristics of the track. Experimental results demonstrate that GC-TimeGAN outperforms traditional methods and other generative models in terms of modeling accuracy and feature consistency. This research provides a more accurate and practical modeling approach for track irregularity data generation, with direct relevance to engineering applications.

title: Zero-shot bearing life state identification method based on multi-scale envelope entropy and contrastive generative Kolmogorov-Arnold network
abstract: Rolling bearings exhibit diverse failure modes, and obtaining fully annotated data for all failure modes in industrial scenarios is challenging, which limits the applicability of traditional diagnostic models. To address this issue, a zero-shot life-cycle state identification method is proposed. First, a Multi-Scale Envelope Entropy (MSEE) health indicator is constructed by integrating frequency-domain and time-domain features, enabling sensitive monitoring and division of degradation states. Second, a Contrastive Generative Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (CGKAN) model is proposed. This network utilizes B-spline functions to accurately fit local transient features, combined with radial basis functions to capture global patterns, allowing it to learn feature distributions from data of known failure modes. Additionally, Wasserstein distance and a gradient penalty mechanism are incorporated with contrastive learning to optimize the feature space, generating high-quality sample features for unknown failure modes and training a classifier to identify these unseen failure modes. The proposed method is validated on two full-life-cycle bearing datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the method effectively divides life-cycle states and, by leveraging data from known failure modes, achieves accurate identification of unknown failure modes not encountered during the training phase.

title: A bidirectional transfer learning method for tool life prediction in machine tools and robots based on the spatio-temporal features of multi-modal sensors and physics-informed constraints
abstract: Accurate prediction of remaining tool life is essential for developing intelligent machining systems in robotic milling. To address the challenges posed by pose variations, cross-equipment heterogeneity, and multi-modal signal integration, we propose a fine-tuning-based transfer learning framework named M−BLCAP−FTN, which integrates adaptive feature selection and physical information constraint mechanisms. The framework first enhances data quality using a combination of interquartile range analysis and wavelet soft-threshold denoising. Discriminative features are then selected via the maximum relevance and minimum redundancy algorithm. A BiLSTM model with Channel Attention is constructed to extract deeply coupled spatiotemporal features from multi-sensor signals. Furthermore, the incorporation of physical consistency and monotonicity loss terms ensures that model outputs adhere to underlying tool wear laws. By leveraging fine-tuning-based transfer learning, the proposed method enables effective knowledge migration from the CNC machine tools to robotic machining platforms. Without compromising robotic flexibility and while maintaining low implementation costs, our approach achieves high-accuracy cross-domain tool life prediction. Experimental results on public milling datasets and a robotic milling platform validate the effectiveness and superiority of the method. The RMSEs on public milling datasets, pose-varying robotic trials, and cross-equipment bidirectional transfer are as low as 0.0111, 0.0286, and 0.0277, respectively, demonstrating robust predictive performance.

title: Head-tracking active road noise control by real-time path adaptation using neural networks
abstract: Conventional active road noise control (ARNC) with virtual sensing requires accurate secondary path estimates and observation filters. However, these paths are dependent on the listener’s head position, and the use of fixed models results in modeling errors and consequent degradation in control performance. To overcome this limitation, this study proposed a head-tracking ARNC (HARNC) framework that uses neural networks (NNs) to update secondary path estimates and observation filters in real time based on the listener’s head position. In addition, a prefilter-based initialization scheme was introduced to accelerate the convergence of the control filter after head movements. NN models for estimating secondary paths and observation filters were trained using a dataset measured at multiple listener head positions and integrated into a virtual sensing ARNC algorithm. The proposed HARNC framework was validated through simulations and experiments, including a comparative assessment of prefilter initialization and path update strategies. Simulation results evaluated over 30–500 Hz showed that compared with conventional ARNC using fixed paths, the proposed HARNC achieved an additional noise reduction of 3.02 dBA on average. It was also compared with look-up table and interpolation-based updating strategies and outperformed them in terms of path estimation accuracy and noise attenuation in ARNC simulations. The framework was further validated through real-vehicle experiments, confirming its effectiveness in achieving robust ARNC performance under realistic driving conditions.

title: Physics-guided neural network for force identification in component-based transfer path analysis
abstract: In component-based transfer path analysis (TPA), the accuracy of estimated results depends on the treatment of accelerance matrix inversion for equivalent force identification. However, the measured accelerance often exhibits significant uncertainty, even though it should satisfy the reciprocity condition, which substantially degrades TPA accuracy. Conventional regularization methods, which use uncertain accelerance, mainly focus on mitigating ill-conditioning without effectively resolving the problem. In this study, an innovative physics-guided neural network model was proposed to replace the conventional matrix inversion process in component-based TPA. The proposed model acts as a trainable version of TPA capable of compensating for uncertainties in nondriving-point accelerance. Its architecture is designed to identify the equivalent forces at the hidden layer, and tailored training strategies improve estimation accuracy. Physical information, such as the driving-point accelerance and noise transfer function, is incorporated into the model to preserve the physical characteristics of the system during training. In addition, the output layer is virtually expanded by exploiting the property that the equivalent forces remain invariant to modifications in the passive part stiffness, thereby improving the accuracy of the estimated forces. The proposed method was validated through a numerical simulation in which intended uncertainty was imposed on the known accelerance, and the estimated equivalent forces closely matched the references despite the uncertainty. Furthermore, the application of a road noise vehicle experiment revealed that the suggested neural network-based method surpasses conventional inversion-based methods in accuracy and offers a reliable framework for component-based TPA in practical applications.

title: Data-Driven and Physics-Informed hybrid identification of a spacecraft simulator using optimized NARX neural networks
abstract: Spacecraft attitude dynamics simulators based on hemispherical air bearings are considered among the most innovative tools in the study of space system stability and control, as they provide unconstrained rotational motion and facilitate realistic ground-based testing of spacecraft. Nonetheless, the presence of nonlinear dynamics, external disturbances, frictional effects, complex aerodynamic phenomena within the air bearing, and inherent uncertainties has posed significant challenges to the development of high-fidelity analytical models for such systems. To tackle these limitations, this study proposes a hybrid identification approach that integrates physics-based modeling with data-driven learning. Accordingly, a NARX neural network is employed to account for the unknown residual dynamics not captured by nominal analytical models. To enhance model accuracy and generalization capabilities, two techniques—Genetic Algorithm and Taguchi method—are utilized to fine-tune the hyperparameters of the NARX network. The modeling process is quantitatively assessed using the Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Relative Root Mean Squared Error (RRMS) metrics under various input torques, including doublet and sinusoidal signals, as well as closed-loop control scenarios applied to the spacecraft simulator via reaction wheels. The results are compared with those from LSTM-based models, where the proposed model outperformed LSTM in terms of prediction accuracy, further demonstrating its suitability for aerospace applications. The high-fidelity model representation makes it valuable for the design and validation of control algorithms in aerospace applications.

title: Deep learning-based dynamic load reconstruction and localization: A novel multi-task learning framework with physical distance-aware graph attention
abstract: Direct measurement of dynamic loads is often infeasible due to deployment constraints or harsh environments, necessitating indirect inference through responses. Traditional methods face limitations due to reliance on precise modal parameters, while existing data-driven approaches often decouple reconstruction and localization tasks, ignoring their inherent coupling. This paper proposes a novel multi-task learning (MTL) framework for dynamic load identification that synergizes graph attention network (GAT) with physical distance-aware attention mechanism. The graph structure representing the dynamic load identification issue is constructed and the GAT layer-based shared feature encoder is introduced to process spatially distributed sensor response as node features. This design utilizes task-specific attention weights that facilitates cross-task knowledge transfer while preserving the uniqueness of each task, reconstruction and localization. Furthermore, physical distance between the sensor and the load locations is embedded as constraints of attention weight learning, which leads to the adaptive narrowing of solution space and the improvement of localization accuracy. A series of numerical and experimental scenarios are designed to validate the performance of the method. The findings demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve satisfactory outcomes in both reconstruction and localization tasks while circumventing the intricate process of modeling dynamic characteristics. Moreover, the proposed method is insensitive to sensor arrangement and can function even when the response data sources of the training and testing phases are different, rendering it practical in engineering scenarios.

title: Unsupervised deep learning framework for damage identification under ambient excitations: trait of damage localization and demonstrative applications
abstract: Developing unsupervised deep learning-based damage identification (uDLdi) under ambient excitations is crucial for civil engineering but remains hindered by insufficient feature extraction from complex original acceleration responses and a lack of damage localization capabilities. To address these issues, this study proposes a novel framework of uDLdi under ambient excitation (F-uDLdi-ae) by adopting the following innovative techniques: (1) a cube-shaped sample set is constructed to theoretically protrude damage information while suppressing interference information; (2) a self-attention module dedicated to protruding damage feature so as to largely identify damage samples is constructed; and (3) an uncertainty-weakened damage probability strategy for localizing damage accurately and reliably is proposed. Validation using a numerical steel truss bridge and a laboratory three-story frame structure demonstrates the superior damage discrimination and localization performance of the proposed framework. Specifically, in the numerical case under a high-noise environment (SNR = 5 dB), F-uDLdi-ae achieves an F‑score of 91.98%, outperforming several advanced unsupervised methods by 6.27% to 20.65%. In the three-story frame structure, F-uDLdi-ae achieves an F‑score of 100%. Furthermore, the framework is applied to a long‑span cable‑stayed bridge, Yonghe Bridge, where it achieves an F‑score of 99.17% and successfully localizes the damage via the maximum damage probability. The proposed F-uDLdi-ae overcomes the limitations of existing uDLdi, holding the promise for viably and intelligently identifying damage in practical engineering structures.

title: Decoupling the feature manifold structure: a domain incremental method for mechanical fault diagnosis under variable rotational speeds
abstract: Fault diagnosis of typical rotating machinery is of great significance for ensuring the safe and reliable operation of mechanical equipment. Machine learning-based intelligent diagnosis methods have achieved significant progress, but most existing approaches suffer from catastrophic forgetting and lack the ability to incrementally adapt to new operating conditions. To address this challenge, a domain-incremental fault diagnosis method with decoupled feature manifold structures (DFMS) is proposed for mechanical equipment operating under variable rotational speeds. In the proposed framework, although the physical fault types remain unchanged, vibration signals corresponding to the same fault exhibit significantly different data distributions under different rotational speeds, which can be interpreted as domain-dependent latent manifolds. To explicitly model these variations, vibration signals are first transformed into feature representations, and fault features acquired under different operating conditions are then mapped into fault-domain-specific latent subspaces using an autoencoder-based manifold representation. The reconstruction error is employed as a distance metric to characterize the proximity between an input feature and the corresponding fault-domain manifold. Furthermore, an adaptive weighted confusion contrast loss is designed to reduce classification ambiguity caused by manifold overlap across different domains. To alleviate catastrophic forgetting during incremental learning, a knowledge distillation loss with dynamic parameter adjustment is introduced to preserve the reconstruction-error distributions of previously learned fault-domain manifolds, and a feature distillation loss is employed to stabilize latent representations across incremental stages. The proposed DFMS method is applicable to fault diagnosis tasks under quasi-stationary operating conditions, such as constant-speed or piecewise constant-speed scenarios. Extensive experiments conducted on a gear transmission test rig and a high-speed wheelset bearing test rig demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method for domain-incremental fault diagnosis of typical rotating machinery under variable rotational speed conditions.

title: Dual-learning framework: Integrating deep and reinforcement learning for optimizing bio-inspired Helmholtz-porous acoustic metamaterials for railway noise mitigation
abstract: Urban railway noise pollution poses significant public health challenges, necessitating advanced mitigation solutions. This study presents a novel dual-learning framework to optimize bio-inspired Helmholtz-porous acoustic metamaterials (HPAM) for railway noise absorption between 500–2000 Hz. The framework uses a highly accurate surrogate model, ESKAN (Echo-state module with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks), which achieved an R 2 of 0.987. To find the best material designs, a Q-learning enhanced Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES) optimization algorithm efficiently explores complex 14-dimensional parameter spaces. This method successfully identifies optimal configurations for various material thicknesses (20–120 mm) and types, including porous materials like melamine sponge and rockwool, and shell materials ranging from soft polymers to rigid metals. Experimental tests on 3D-printed ABS prototypes confirmed the framework’s accuracy. The fabricated samples demonstrated excellent broadband absorption (SAC > 0.8) across the 480–2000 Hz range. This research introduces a generalizable method for designing next-generation metamaterials, overcoming previous optimization limitations while respecting manufacturing constraints.

title: Physics-guided generative data augmentation for vision-based signal processing under class-imbalanced conditions in directed energy deposition monitoring system
abstract: • Addresses signal processing limits from class-imbalanced DED molten pool signals. • Physics-guided CVAE-GAN synthesizes high-fidelity visual signals. • Thermodynamic losses enforce spatial and spectral signal consistency. • Augmented data improves decision boundaries for rare defect detection. • Validated on a real-world aerospace component with complex geometry. Vision-based signal processing is critical in metal additive manufacturing (AM), particularly within Directed Energy Deposition (DED), for capturing the rapid thermo-fluid dynamics essential for detecting process instabilities and ensuring structural integrity. While DED operates as an open, inherently non-stationary system and molten pool visual signals carry rich spatiotemporal information, effective processing is fundamentally constrained by the scarcity of anomalous events relative to stable deposition. This data sparsity leads to imbalanced training sets that fail to represent the full spectrum of transient process dynamics, causing classifiers to misclassify rare but critical failure modes and degrading overall monitoring performance. Crucially, conventional data augmentation techniques, being agnostic to the underlying physics, often introduce signal artefacts that violate governing thermodynamic constraints, thereby degrading the physical validity of the training data. To bridge the gap between data-driven feature learning and physical principles, this study proposes a physics-guided generative data augmentation framework based on a Conditional Variational Autoencoder–Generative Adversarial Network (CVAE-GAN). The framework explicitly learns the intrinsic physical manifold of the process, incorporating thermodynamically motivated loss functions to ensure the synthesis of high-fidelity, physically coherent molten pool visual signals. Validation through both spectral analysis and downstream classification confirms that the augmented signals preserve essential morphological and textural properties while significantly improving the decision boundaries of sequence classifiers. A case study on a complex aerospace component demonstrates the framework’s practical utility in enhancing robust in-situ monitoring under varying geometric conditions. By addressing the sparse representation of critical dynamics through a physics-aware methodology, this work offers a reliable pathway for advanced signal processing in data-scarce engineering systems.

title: A two-phase multi-fidelity framework for virtual sensing of a rotating shaft system with physics-informed machine learning
abstract: This paper proposes a physics-informed machine learning framework for virtual sensing in the unmeasurable regions of a rotating shaft system. This framework addresses the challenge of predicting dynamic responses in regions where direct sensor installation is difficult or infeasible, thereby enabling real-time full-field virtual sensing under diverse operating conditions. The proposed framework comprises two sequential phases with distinct objectives. First, a physics-guided multi-agent diverse generative adversarial network (PhyMAD-GAN) synthesizes high-fidelity full-field synthetic responses under specific operating conditions by integrating full-field low-fidelity data from multiphysics finite element analysis (FEA) with point-wise measurements. The PhyMAD-GAN employs multiple generators to enhance synthetic data diversity, a shared discriminator to ensure consistency with measurements, and a physics-guided loss to preserve physical constraints. Second, a physics-informed adversarial domain-adaptive deep operator network (PADO-NET) constructs a generalized surrogate model that performs virtual sensing across both trained and untrained operating conditions. PADO-NET integrates operator learning to represent nonlinear mappings, domain-adversarial alignment to extract domain-invariant features, and physics-informed regularization to supervise governing physics laws. Extensive validation using dynamic responses, measured from an induction motor testbed under diverse operating conditions, confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The systematic analysis demonstrated significant improvements in predictive accuracy, robustness, and generalization compared with conventional data-driven neural networks. The proposed framework contributes to the artificial intelligence transformation of mechatronic systems by enabling reliable full-field virtual sensing. This capability provides physically consistent and reliable full-field reconstructions of shaft dynamics, which are essential for intelligent condition monitoring and fault diagnosis.

title: Continuous flow matching framework for scalable density estimation in stochastic dynamical systems
abstract: The probability density function (PDF) plays a fundamental role in characterizing the evolutionary behavior of stochastic dynamical systems. However, the inherent high dimensionality, strong nonlinearity, and multiscale nature of most stochastic dynamical systems pose formidable challenges for both theoretical analysis and computational modeling. To address these issues, we propose a flow matching density estimation framework (FMDEF) for continuous modeling of complex distributions in stochastic systems. FMDEF leverages continuous normalizing flows (CNFs) with time-dependent vector fields to capture the temporal evolution of probability densities. The framework introduces a scalable, simulation-free training mechanism that directly optimizes vector fields to match target probability paths, eliminating the need for explicit stochastic process modeling while enabling direct extraction of probabilistic structures from system measurements. Extensive numerical experiments on stochastic systems demonstrate the method’s effectiveness and robustness. Both theoretical analysis and experimental results confirm FMDEF’s potential for extension to high-dimensional problems, establishing it as a rigorous and practical solution for real-world applications in stochastic dynamical systems.

title: Dual-stream spatiotemporal graph attention network guided by lamb wave physics for damage localization
abstract: Lamb wave technology has become a powerful tool in composite structural health monitoring, enabling the detection and characterization of internal damage. However, the pronounced anisotropy of composite structures gives rise to intricate spatiotemporal correlations among multi-channel Lamb wave signals. Existing methods typically treat these signals as independent Euclidean sequences, which restricts their capacity to capture the coupling characteristics across multiple channels. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a novel damage localization approach based on a dual-stream spatiotemporal graph attention network (DS-STGAT), which is explicitly grounded in the physical principles of Lamb wave propagation. First, a Lamb wave graph is constructed using transfer entropy (TE) and time-of-flight (ToF), providing a graphical representation of multi-channel Lamb wave signals. Second, a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) and a graph attention network (GAT) are employed to extract temporal and spatial features, respectively. Third, a bidirectional cross-attention (BCA) module is introduced to fuse spatiotemporal information, while damage localization regression is subsequently conducted using a multi-layer perceptron mixer (MLP-Mixer). Finally, experimental evaluations on simulated damage in composite plate structures demonstrate that DS-STGAT achieves superior damage localization performance, significantly outperforming existing benchmark methods.

title: A real-time and offline weld defect detection framework using planar EMT with selective measurement and deep learning
abstract: Electromagnetic tomography (EMT) offers a non-contact approach for weld defect imaging, yet traditional full-pair configurations suffer from low speed and limited adaptability to uneven weld surfaces. This study proposes an integrated real-time and offline weld-defect detection framework that couples selective coil-pair planar EMT with a prototype-guided similarity-fusion UNet (ProSiF-UNet). A 16-channel planar EMT sensor was developed, and a simplified sensitivity matrix using next-nearest coil pairs (d = 2) significantly reduced computation while preserving image fidelity. For real-time monitoring, a lightweight linear back projection (LBP)-based reconstruction enables 200+ frames per second (FPS) imaging, whereas an offline Landweber (LW) iteration ensures high-fidelity analysis. The prototype-guided similarity-fusion segmentation network (ProSiF-UNet) integrates cosine-similarity prototypes and exponential moving average (EMA)-based fusion to enhance defect segmentation on limited data, reducing missed detections by 40% compared with standard U-Net. The unified framework achieves a practical balance between speed, accuracy, and robustness, demonstrating strong potential for artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled industrial weld inspection.

title: A knowledge fusion-driven domain generalization diagnosis framework for unseen operating conditions
abstract: In engineering applications, deep learning-based fault diagnosis must balance generalization and model complexity amid dynamic conditions. High generalization often demands complex models, yet excessive complexity reduces computational efficiency and hinders deployment. To address this, we propose Multi-knowledge Domain Generalization with Dynamic Temperature Distillation (MDG-DTD), a knowledge fusion-driven framework. First, we introduce a distillation method that fuses multiple specialized teacher models via confidence weighting and feature alignment to derive a generalized teacher model. Second, a dynamic temperature distillation strategy integrates attention transfer and adversarial temperature regulation to adaptively adjust the distillation process, optimizing student model learning and efficiency. Experimental results on the motor current and industrial robot vibration datasets validate MDG-DTD’s superiority over existing domain generalization methods in diagnosing faults under unseen conditions. Notably, the student model, using only 0.15% of the teacher model’s parameters and 0.36% of its floating point operations, retains at least 96.33% and 97.78% of its performance, respectively.

title: Neural operators for ultrasonic full waveform inversion: A next-generation ultrasonic NDT with improved fidelity, efficiency, and robustness
abstract: Full waveform inversion (FWI), a computational wave imaging technique that fully incorporates the physics of wave propagation, enables high-resolution quantitative reconstruction of inhomogeneous media and promotes effective application in non-destructive testing (NDT). However, its widespread adoption is hindered by the intrinsic challenges of solving a nonlinear, ill-posed inverse problem, resulting in a high computational cost considering the iterative implementation, sensitivity to the initial model, and the possible convergence to a local minimum solution. Recent advances in data-driven FWI frameworks using neural networks have improved both accuracy and efficiency, yet challenges in robustness and generalization persist. Neural operators, an emerging paradigm in scientific machine learning, aim to learn mappings between infinite-dimensional function spaces, offering superior generalization and scalability for complex physical systems. Motivated by this, we propose a neural-operator-based framework for direct inversion of ultrasonic full-waveform data based on the Unet Fourier Neural Operator (U-FNO), extending the neural operator paradigm to ultrasonic NDT. By leveraging parameterized Fourier kernels to globally capture intricate wave physics, U-FNO demonstrates improved inference efficiency relative to classical FWI, and improved fidelity and robust reconstruction compared with representative data-driven models and total focusing method (TFM). Numerical and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides a promising direction for next-generation computational wave imaging technology in ultrasonic NDT.

title: Enhancing interpretability via fine-grained objectives: A manifold-learning structured model for fault diagnosis of rolling bearings under noisy conditions
abstract: Dictionary learning (DL) has emerged as an effective data-driven approach for fault diagnosis due to its powerful sparse representation capability. However, its application to rolling bearing fault diagnosis still faces several challenges, including low accuracy, vulnerability of sparse reconstruction to strong noise interference, and insufficient discriminative power of the encoding. To address the above challenges, we propose a bearing fault diagnosis method based on a dual-analysis dictionary learning (DADL) with non-local sparsity (NLS) and block-diagonal (BD). The proposed method introduces a NLS term to characterize the underlying geometric manifold structure of the samples, aiming to extract key class-discriminative features under strong noise conditions. In addition, a BD term is incorporated to constrain the encoding into structured and discriminative sparse subspaces, with the goal of constructing features that are more easily recognized by the classifier. The proposed method maps the two learned constraints into a first analysis dictionary and a second analysis dictionary, respectively. For test samples, diagnostic results can be obtained through a simple projection operation, making the process more computationally efficient. In addition, the dual-analysis dictionary not only mines the essential features of the data, but also encourages the sub-analysis dictionary to learn more refined and interpretable feature subspaces. Finally, a linear classifier is jointly trained to perform the fault identification task. Extensive experiments on three challenging bearing fault datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high average diagnostic accuracies. In addition, comparative results with several advanced DL methods further demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

title: Wind farm-level scour detection around offshore monopile foundations using unsupervised domain adaptation
abstract: This study proposes a novel Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) approach for scour detection around offshore wind turbines (OWT) at the wind farm level. In this approach, acceleration data collected from a single reference OWT (so-called source turbine) are used to detect scour presence around other turbines (so-called target turbines), located within the same wind farm. Acceleration data are collected along the tower height under varying environmental conditions and are processed to extract the tower bending modal frequencies, which serve as structural health features. To address the distributional shift in the data across OWTs within a wind farm - arising from changes in structural configurations, environmental loading conditions, and soil properties - four UDA techniques, Geodesic Flow Kernel (GFK), Unsupervised Domain-Invariant Component Analysis (UDICA), Subspace Alignment (SA), and Correlation Alignment (CORAL), are employed. By using these UDA methods, the healthy feature distributions from the source OWT are aligned with those of the target turbines and subsequently used to train an Autoencoder (AE) deep learning algorithm for scour detection. The study evaluates the limitations of traditional anomaly detection methods for scour in terms of their ability to be generalised across turbines, and demonstrates how UDA techniques enable model generalisation at the wind farm level. The results highlight the effectiveness of the GFK in mitigating feature distribution discrepancies and enabling an accurate detection of scour at multiple OWTs within the same wind farm, followed by SA and UDICA. However, CORAL demonstrated a lower capacity for reducing the distribution shift across different OWTs, making it less feasible for a scour detection application.

title: Probabilistic machine learning aided acoustic emission source localization in mode-I fracture test of multi-layer engineered wood
abstract: The mode-I fracture test is an important technique to evaluate materials’ fracture toughness and behaviors, where tracking the crack front is essential. This is usually done by visual inspection or computer vision, which could be problematic due to the large process zone and the difficulty of determining the onset of material cracking. Source localization via acoustic emission (AE) offers an alternative solution to this challenge. Locating AE sources in homogeneous materials is intuitively straightforward by leveraging phase differences from the measured time of arrival and potentially angle- or path-dependent velocity models. But it becomes complicated and intractable once the material heterogeneity comes into play. This is especially true for multilayer engineered wood, like laminated veneer lumber (LVL), where natural and manufacturing defects (knots, voids, discontinuity, and non-uniform textures) impose great challenges for 2D AE source localization. To cope with this problem, this study proposes probabilistic machine learning models, namely the Student-t process regression and the Gaussian process regression, for the 2D AE source localization on two LVL samples. To enhance prediction performance, both the multi-output Student-t and Gaussian process regression are developed. These probabilistic machine learning models are first trained and verified via pencil lead break tests and then applied to locate the crack tips in two mode-I fracture tests. Meanwhile, the Gaussian mixture models, along with Laplacian scores, are considered to identify AE events related to crack tip locations. The results suggest that the Student-t process can outperform the Gaussian process both in pencil lead break tests and mode-I fracture tests. The multi-output models can further enhance the prediction performance compared with the single-output processes. The multi-output Student-t process and the multi-output Gaussian process can support similar prediction performance when the degree of freedom of the Student-t process is large enough, and therefore, both are recommended for AE source localization in complex heterogeneous media like engineered wood.

title: Optimal reduced-order model for Vehicle-Bridge Interaction and bridge damage detection using model based SHM-ML techniques
abstract: • Optimal reduced-order vehicle-bridge interaction model. • Reliable Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) and damage detection. • VBI computational framework with significantly reduced computational cost. • Enriched model with realistic rail irregularities. • Experimental validation over multiple operating speeds, loads, and damage scenarios. Bridge structures subjected to moving vehicle loads exhibit complex dynamic behavior influenced by structural flexibility and rail surface irregularities. The correct approach and optimal modeling of vehicle-bridge interaction effects are crucial for the accurate computational determination of dynamic bridge vibrations, for reliable Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) and damage detection. The purpose of this work is twofold. First, a novel computational framework is introduced to generate an optimal reduced-order Vehicle-Bridge Interaction (VBI) model that captures the essential dynamics of the system with significantly reduced computational cost. This process begins with the development of a high-fidelity finite element (FE) model of the bridge which is updated using experimental modal data. This model is then reduced using Component Mode Synthesis (CMS) to enable efficient simulation while preserving the essential dynamic behavior and is combined with a simplified vehicle model enriched with realistic rail irregularities, producing an accurate and computationally efficient VBI system. Second, the study introduces a classification framework based on a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on numerically generated data from the validated VBI model. The CNN operates on frequency-domain features derived from bridge acceleration responses, which reflect damage-induced changes in stiffness and energy distribution of the structure. Using these features and an ensemble of independently trained CNNs, the framework classifies the structural health condition of the bridge.

title: Multi-channel chatter detection in robotic milling based on successive multivariate variational mode decomposition and hybrid deep convolutional neural network
abstract: Chatter is a critical factor that limits machining quality and production efficiency in robotic milling. Therefore, timely and accurate online chatter detection is essential for achieving high-precision and high-efficiency machining. However, the dynamic properties of milling robots are highly pose-dependent, which significantly increases the randomness and complexity of chatter. Furthermore, due to the strong nonlinearity and flexibility of milling robots, chatter induces coupled three-dimensional vibrations. As a result, relying on vibration signals from a single direction is insufficient for achieving reliable chatter detection. In this paper, a multi-channel online chatter detection method in robotic milling is proposed, based on successive multivariate variational mode decomposition (SMVMD) and hybrid deep convolutional neural network. First, the SMVMD method combined with a dimensionless chatter index is employed to adaptively extract the chatter components in the three-channel acceleration signals. Then, the energy ratio sequence between the reconstructed chatter signal and the milling signal is calculated. Finally, a hybrid deep convolutional neural network (ICR-DCN), composed of Inception, convolutional block attention module (CBAM), residual network (ResNet) and classification module, is constructed to automatically extract chatter features from the energy ratio sequence and achieve online chatter detection. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve high-precision online chatter detection across variations in different robotic poses, cutting parameters, workpiece materials and tools. Comparative studies further validate the accuracy and stability of the proposed method across various scenarios.
