title: Deep reconstruction of sparse elastic wavefield and graph-based damage detection for accelerated health monitoring of PZT ceramics
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) of piezoelectric ceramics, particularly Lead Zirconate Titanate (PZT) substrates, requires accurate acquisition of elastic wave propagation to detect and localize damage. However, full-field wave acquisition is experimentally intensive and time-consuming. This study presents a sparse nonlinear reconstruction framework based on Coulomb coupling measurements that reduces acquisition complexity while maintaining diagnostic accuracy. Spatiotemporal wavefields are first acquired at a coarser temporal resolution from both healthy and damaged PZT specimens. For the healthy condition, the reduced data are used to compute a proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) basis, and QR pivoting identifies optimal sensing locations. The corresponding sparse measurements are then used to train a shallow decoder network (Q-SDN) for wavefield reconstruction. Rather than training a separate decoder for the damaged condition, transfer learning adapts the Q-SDN model to the damaged dataset. This refines the learned representation to accommodate damage-induced variations while leveraging knowledge from the healthy data. Transfer learning allows the model to retain prior knowledge and adapt to new conditions without full retraining. However, the QR-selected sensor locations optimal for the healthy state may not be ideal for capturing wave propagation in the damaged case. Despite this, maintaining the same sensor layout avoids experimental reconfiguration. These locations effectively act as random placements in the damaged state, leading to the QR-Random-SDN (Q-R-SDN) framework. The proposed method avoids reconfiguration and separate model training for each state. Reconstruction performance is compared with a linear QR/POD baseline. The Q-R-SDN shows improved accuracy in both healthy and damaged scenarios. The reconstructed wavefields are further analyzed using an unsupervised Graph Deviation Network (GDN) trained only on healthy data. Damage localization is performed using forecast-based deviation scores, followed by contrast enhancement and morphological filtering.

title: Separated-variable physics informed neural operators for solving dynamic PDEs
abstract: Solving dynamic partial differential equations (PDEs) remains a fundamental challenge in computational science and engineering. Although physics-informed deep learning (PIDL) provides a mesh-free approach to solutions, it continues to face several persistent issues, such as spectral bias in high-frequency problems, optimization difficulties in high-order PDEs, and multi-objective optimization problem arising from complex boundary conditions. To address these challenges, we propose the separated-variable physics informed neural operators (SV-PINO). The method decomposes dynamic PDEs into a family of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) within the eigenfunction space, effectively transforming the original difficulties into a unified problem of learning ODE coefficients that are readily handled by neural operators. Beyond establishing a robust framework for a broad class of challenging PDEs, SV-PINO also demonstrates its versatility through successful extension to model the dynamic response of discrete systems that often lack definite PDE formulations. Extensive numerical experiments show that SV-PINO achieves high accuracy and strong generalization under demanding conditions, thereby offering a systematic solution to key bottlenecks in PIDL for engineering simulation and dynamics modeling.

title: A novel parallel feature fusion strategy-based machine learning approach for accurate prediction and early warning of wind-induced vibrations of solar towers
abstract: Solar towers are highly flexible structures prone to wind-induced vibrations, which can significantly reduce the operational efficiency of concentrated solar power (CSP) plants and, more critically, may jeopardize the structural integrity. With the growing maturity of structural health monitoring (SHM) technologies and the increasing availability of multi-source sensing data, data-driven prediction has emerged as a key method for real-time evaluation and early warning of wind-induced vibrations. However, conventional machine learning models often exhibit some randomness in their predictions and struggle to accurately predict wind-induced vibration responses arising from strong fluid–structure coupling, which is particularly pronounced in solar towers. In addition, these models typically require extensive hyperparameter tuning, leading to high computational cost and reduced prediction efficiency. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel data-driven prediction method based on a parallel feature fusion strategy. The model integrates Long Short-Term Memory Network(LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit(GRU), and improved Transformer within a dual-branch architecture, leveraging gated mechanisms and multi-head attention for multi-scale feature extraction. Then, an Extreme Learning Machine (ELM)-based hierarchical feature fusion module is designed to achieve efficient integration of multi-source features from both branches. The proposed approach is validated through wind tunnel experiments on a scaled aeroelastic model and tested against field measurements from a full-scale operational tower. Finally, an early warning system based on the model is developed and shown to be reliable for real-world wind hazard mitigation in CSP plants.

title: Topological mechanical neural networks as classifiers through in situ backpropagation learning
abstract: Recently, a new frontier in computing has emerged with physical neural networks (PNNs) harnessing intrinsic physical processes for learning. Here, we explore topological mechanical neural networks (TMNNs) inspired by the quantum spin Hall effect (QSHE) in topological metamaterials, for machine learning classification tasks. TMNNs utilize pseudospin states and the robustness of the QSHE, making them damage-tolerant for binary classification. We first demonstrate data clustering using untrained TMNNs. Then, for specific tasks, we derive an in situ backpropagation algorithm, a two-step, local-rule method that updates TMNNs using only local information, enabling in situ physical learning. TMNNs achieve high accuracy in classifications of Iris flowers, Penguins, and Seeds while maintaining robustness against bond pruning. Furthermore, we demonstrate parallel classification via frequency-division multiplexing, assigning different tasks to distinct frequencies for enhanced efficiency. Our work introduces in situ backpropagation for wave-based mechanical neural networks and positions TMNNs as promising neuromorphic computing hardware for classification tasks. • Mechanical analogue of in situ backpropagation allows for local physical learning. • Topological mechanical neural networks use pseudospin states for classification tasks. • We demonstrate high accuracy in various classification tasks. • We realize the implementation of classification tasks in parallel.

title: Knowledge-guided RUL prediction for multi-sensor devices under a data-model interactive framework
abstract: For complex industrial devices monitored by multi-sensors, accurate and reliable remaining useful life (RUL) prediction directly determines the effectiveness and economy of preventive maintenance strategies. Current mainstream methods either rely excessively on data-driven models, resulting in the lack of physical interpretability, or are limited by fixed knowledge constraints, making it difficult to adapt to the dynamic characteristics of multi-sensor data. To address this, this paper proposes a knowledge-guided RUL prediction method under a data-model interactive framework. Specifically, based on the composite health indicator (CHI) constructed by weighted fusion of multi-sensor monitoring data and the RUL predicted by stochastic degradation modeling under the concepts of first hitting time (FHT), an optimization objective function integrating RUL prediction accuracy, monotonicity, and slope consistency is designed. This forms a feedback loop for knowledge-guided CHI construction and stochastic degradation modeling, enabling optimal adjustment of fusion coefficients for multi-sensor data and failure thresholds corresponding to CHI. Thus, dual optimization of the accuracy and physical rationality of prediction results is achieved. Meanwhile, a Bayesian update method for degradation model parameters is proposed to realize online RUL prediction and quantification of prediction uncertainty. Finally, the advantages of the proposed method in improving RUL prediction accuracy, interpretability, and generalization are verified based on the C-MAPSS dataset and milling cutters dataset.

title: A Conditional constraint Generative adversarial networks model for predicting high cycle and very high cycle fatigue life of titanium alloy
abstract: Fatigue life prediction of aero-engine has been an important research topic in the aerospace industry. This study focuses on predicting the high cycle and very high cycle fatigue (HCF/VHCF) life of aero-engine titanium alloys under small-sample conditions. First, based on the test results and empirical phenomena, a dimensionless constraint index (δ) was designed to assign values to the test type (Typ) and fracture conditions (Fc), and life mapping characteristic variables were introduced to establish a foundation for subsequent data augmentation and predictive modeling. Second, a Kernel density estimation-Synthetic minority over-sampling technique (KDE-SMOTE) data enhancement method is proposed, which expands the dataset while preserving feature-variable correlations. Then, a Conditional constraint Generative adversarial network (C-cGAN) model was built by embedding δ and Fc computation as explicit constraints in the loss and implicitly guiding attention learning with adversarial training. Finally, under the conditions of high-density distribution test validation (Test set 1) and random test validation (Test set 2), the C-cGAN model shows better prediction results at 3–5-fold dispersion bands (satisfying 5-fold dispersion band) by training on KDE-SMOTE enhanced data, and extends to the fatigue life prediction studies of a variety of titanium alloys, which suggests that the model has a potential reference value.

title: A two-stage approach for predicting tribological variables via latent-regularized blind denoising and machine learning in microscratch testing
abstract: The development of predictive models in tribology has emerged as a tool for predicting key process variables. Penetration, tangential force, volume removed, coefficient of friction, and specific energy are critical parameters for minimizing energy consumption and reducing losses due to friction and wear. This work proposes a two-stage methodology that integrates signal denoising and predictive modeling. In the first stage, a recurrent autoencoder with contrastive learning and temporal smoothness constraints is employed to enhance the quality of force and position signals in a blind, unsupervised manner. In the second stage, a Random Forest (RF) model estimates tribological variables while integrating mechanical properties of the materials to improve generalization. The methodology was validated through microscratch tests performed on four steels (AISI 303, 304, 310, and H13) under normal loads between 40 and 100 mN, enabling analysis of material-dependent tribological responses at the microscale. Compared to conventional filters (Savitzky–Golay, moving average) and data-driven baselines (EMD, DAE), the proposed latent-regularized blind denoising autoencoder (LR-BDAE) achieved the highest signal preservation, with mean SNR improvements of 18.5dB and Pearson correlation exceeding 0.93 across materials. When integrated into the predictive stage, this denoising enhanced model consistency and reduced mean squared error by up to 42.3% for tangential force, 36.6% for penetration, 25.2% for the friction coefficient, and 20.8% for removed volume, with a minimum gain of 5.1% for specific energy. Incorporating material properties further increased R2 for specific energy by 26.2%, demonstrating robustness across distinct steels and supporting the general applicability of the framework to other tribological systems with noisy multi-sensor data. This proposal represents a step forward in integrating signal processing and machine learning techniques for tribological systems, providing a physically interpretable and scalable framework for industrial applications.

title: Estimating first-passage probabilities of stochastic dynamical systems: A POD–GPR based approximate Bayesian active learning approach
abstract: Evaluating the first-passage probabilities of stochastic dynamical systems is often required for assessing the safety and performance of modern engineered systems. However, despite significant progress, this task remains rather challenging both analytically and numerically. To address the challenge, this work presents a novel method—proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and Gaussian process regression (GPR) based approximate Bayesian active learning (ABAL), referred to as POD–GPR–ABAL. First, POD is employed to obtain an optimal low-rank representation of the stochastic dynamical response of interest using a compact set of basis functions and coefficients, and the POD coefficients are subsequently approximated by independent GPRs. Second, the integral of the first-passage probability is interpreted as a Bayesian inference problem by leveraging the Bayesian formulation of the combined POD–GPR model. Further, an approximate Bayesian inference scheme is developed, which avoids the computational intractability of the exact Bayesian inference. In this context, the mean of an approximate posterior first-passage probability is derived, which can be used a Bayesian estimator for the first-passage probability. In addition, we derive an upper bound on the standard deviation of the approximate posterior first-passage probability, which provides a uncertainty measure for the estimator. Third, based on the posterior statistics, a new stopping criterion is proposed to determine when the active learning process should terminate and a novel learning function is also developed to identify the best next evaluation point when the stopping criterion is not satisfied. Three numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed POD–GPR–ABAL method for evaluating the first-passage probabilities in stochastic dynamical systems. The results indicate that the proposed method achieves accurate first-passage probability estimates using only a small number of time-history analyses.

title: A hidden failure state identification method for steel-spring floating slab track isolators using MVFuseNet
abstract: Isolators in steel-spring floating slab track (SS-FST) systems can suffer from hidden failures, such as fractures and fluid leakage, which may lead to safety risks like train derailments. However, research on fault modeling and failure state identification is limited. This paper proposes MVFuseNet, a fault-diagnosis framework for identifying failure states of steel-spring isolators. The framework constructs a dataset from multi-source vibration signals generated from field wheel-drop tests and simulations, ensuring high-quality data for classification. In addition, a novel time–frequency feature extraction method based on phase-coupled time–frequency analysis (PC-TFA) enhances damage-sensitive features, while a multi-channel phase-enhanced variational decomposition (MC-PEVD) method generates robust inputs for deep learning. Finally, an improved deep residual network is used for high-precision classification of failure states. Experimental results show that MVFuseNet outperforms existing methods in feature representation and classification accuracy, providing valuable support for the safe operation of SS-FST systems.

title: Physics-guided residual correction model for monitoring machining deviations of complex thin-walled parts considering spatial–temporal dynamics
abstract: Machining deviation of complex thin-walled parts critically affects the product performance and stability. However, accurate deviation monitoring is significantly challenged by the complexity of the processing environment. Traditional theoretical models are computationally expensive, while existing deep learning methods often operate as black-box models with limited interpretability. To address these challenges, this study proposes a spatial–temporal physics-guided residual correction model (ST-PGRC), which integrates the theoretical machining deviation model with a Transformer-based learning module. Initially, a theoretical deviation model is established through machining dynamics and kinematics analysis. A spatial–temporal mapping module links vibration signals with the toolpath, converting temporal information into spatially meaningful features. Ultimately, the Transformer encoder learns the residuals between theoretical results and experimental results through its global attention mechanism, capturing the interactions between the theoretical model and spatial–temporal features and subsequently correcting the theoretical deviations. Experiments on thin-walled workpieces demonstrate that ST-PGRC achieves an RMSE of 0.0069 mm and reduces monitoring error by at least 22.5% compared with physics-guided neural networks, residual networks, and purely data-driven neural networks. The proposed method offers a reliable and interpretable solution for machining deviation monitoring.

title: Generative adversarial fault-tolerance for robust multimodal sensor fusion in industrial systems
abstract: Modern industrial systems rely heavily on multimodal sensor data to handle random emerging faults. To address this, we propose a novel generative adversarial framework embedded within a multimodal autoencoder architecture for active latent restoration of compromised sensor streams. Our method leverages a two-stage training process: first, a multimodal autoencoder is pre-trained on clean data to learn robust latent representations; then, a generative adversarial network is optimized to map corrupted latent vectors to their correct distributions while preserving cross-modal consistency through a task-specific penalty. Additionally, we adopt the discriminator optimization process to identify anomalies in the underlying data. Therefore, the discriminator is designed to conditionally initiate the generator’s fault-correction mechanism. Experiments on multimodal industrial robotic datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms conventional methods in reconstructing accurate signals from corrupted inputs, even under several failure scenarios. The proposed system not only enhances fault resilience but also opens new directions for generative models in industrial automation, bridging the gap between robust data fusion and real-time error recovery.

title: Learning to predict and control with sparse model discovery and deep temporal difference reinforcement learning
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has demonstrated remarkable success in complex decision-making tasks, yet its application to predictive control remains challenging due to high sample requirements and limited long-horizon generalization. Model-based DRL methods promise improved sample efficiency by leveraging learned dynamics, but their performance is often restricted by inaccuracies in online model learning, which degrade control quality. This work introduces the Model-Agnostic Predictive Temporal Difference (MAP-TD) framework, a deep reinforcement learning approach capable of controlling systems with unknown physics. MAP-TD employs a pre-trained, interpretable, and parsimonious dynamics model discovered offline using Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL), which is used for long-horizon trajectory prediction within the DRL architecture. This parsimonious model enhances predictive capability and enables the DRL agent to learn superior control strategies. The optimal control policies are learned by accumulating rewards and value functions along predictive trajectories, supported by a jointly trained terminal value function. For faster learning, we propose a hybrid strategy that periodically switches between fine and coarse solvers. MAP-TD delivers accurate long-horizon predictions while eliminating the need for online adaptation of approximate models. Numerical simulations on benchmark control tasks, including active vibration control of discrete and continuous structural dynamical systems, demonstrate that MAP-TD offers a computationally efficient and robust solution for predictive control.

title: PrecisionPINN-ABKDE: uncertainty-weighted physics-informed neural network with adaptive bandwidth kernel density estimation for milling surface roughness prediction
abstract: Surface roughness critically determines the quality and performance of machined workpieces. Predicting the surface quality of key components in manufacturing systems is inherently a risk-sensitive task where both prediction accuracy and stability are pivotal metrics. To enhance physical interpretability and quantify prediction uncertainty in surface roughness modeling, this study proposes a novel framework integrating uncertainty estimation with physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). The proposed approach employs an improved physical model that incorporates normalized cutting parameters and cutting forces to guide the training of a customized CNN-BiLSTM-attention network. Further, the prediction uncertainty is quantified using quantile regression with adaptive bandwidth kernel density estimation (QR-ABKDE). The QR-ABKDE uncertainty evaluation strategy quantifies both the local probability density and global error variance. It integrates locally adaptive noise (LAN) loss with a dynamically weighted loss function that adaptively balances the variance in prediction accuracy between the physics-based and data-driven models. Experimental validation through milling surface roughness monitoring demonstrates that the proposed method significantly improves the prediction accuracy and stability compared with existing approaches, achieving a 4.99% increase in R2 (0.8962 vs. 0.8536) and 15.08% reduction in root mean squared error (RMSE; 6.36 nm vs. 7.49 nm) over the baseline, while delivering near-perfect prediction coverage (prediction interval coverage probability, PICP, of 98.46%) with relatively small interval widths. These capabilities make the proposed framework well-suited for real-time surface quality monitoring and risk-aware process control in precision manufacturing environments.

title: Wave-PINN: a wavelet-based physics-informed neural network for continuous pavement roughness evaluation from vehicle dynamics
abstract: Automated pavement monitoring across pavement networks generates large volumes of high-frequency data that are typically non-stationary, multi-scale, and incomplete, making accurate, physically consistent, and robust prediction challenging. This paper presents Wave-PINN, a hybrid framework that integrates wavelet-based multiscale signal representation with a physics-informed neural network (PINN). Using the International Roughness Index (IRI) of asphalt pavements as a representative application, longitudinal pavement elevation profiles from more than 11000 pavement sections in the Long-Term Pavement Performance (LTPP) database were collected and analyzed. In the proposed framework, longitudinal pavement elevations and vehicle dynamic responses are projected into the wavelet domain, and the quarter-car model is embedded in the loss function via staged physics-informed training. Results demonstrate that Wave-PINN achieves high predictive accuracy (R2 > 0.999) while substantially improving physical consistency, with physics loss reduced by more than 80% as the training data fraction increases from 20% to 80%. The hybrid strategy maintains test accuracy comparable to purely data-driven models while, relative to purely physics-driven models, reducing physics loss by nearly 50% and lowering the coefficient of variation of physics loss by more than 44%. Compared with time-domain neural networks, Wave-PINN provides superior interpolation and extrapolation performance, with relative L2 errors consistently below 0.016. Under incomplete-data conditions, it improves prediction reliability over conventional IRI computation and remains applicable in extreme scenarios where the conventional method becomes inapplicable. These results support Wave-PINN as a robust and effective framework for continuous pavement-signal modeling and network-level pavement-condition assessment.

title: Using implicit correlations among synchronized vibration signals from pixels to improve the accuracy of structural damage detection
abstract: In recent years, deep neural networks have been used increasingly to process vibration signals for detecting structural damage. However, the effectiveness of deep neural networks relies on having many vibration signals, which are difficult to acquire in practical engineering scenarios. To address this limitation, a phase-based motion estimation (PME) technique has been introduced, which treats each pixel as an independent sensor, enabling the extraction of millions of vibration signals from a single video. PME not only provides sufficient training data for deep neural networks but also ensures that the signals obtained from multiple pixels are perfectly synchronized in the temporal domain. The implicit correlations among synchronized signals from multiple pixels (i.e., pixel-dependencies) have the potential to enhance damage detection. However, it remains challenging to use the pixel-dependencies effectively to facilitate damage detection. To address this issue, a multi-feature-attention network is proposed. Innovatively, the contribution of pixel-dependencies to damage detection is quantified. By assigning greater attention weights to pixel-dependencies with greater contributions, the network achieves a substantial improvement in damage detection performance. The effectiveness of the proposed method was validated by successfully detecting subtle bolt looseness in a steel structure, showcasing its superior performance in structural damage detection tasks.

title: Enhanced AR-based simulation method for non-Gaussian wind pressure process using machine learning model and piecewise Johnson transformation model
abstract: Accurate simulation of non-Gaussian wind pressures on low-rise buildings is essential for structural wind-resistant design. Recently, autoregressive (AR) models combined with the maximum entropy method (MEM) have been employed to develop an AR–MEM-based non-Gaussian wind pressure simulation approach, which has demonstrated satisfactory accuracy and convenience. However, this method suffers from low computational efficiency, limited applicability, and difficulty in extension to multivariate wind pressure simulations. This study comprehensively uses AR, piecewise Johnson transformation model (PJTM), machine learning model (ML), and proposes a novel ML-enhanced AR-PJTM (ML-AR-PJTM) method for simulating non-Gaussian wind pressure, which significantly improves simulation efficiency and widens the application range. In this method, the Extra Trees (ET) model is firstly adopted to map the target power spectral density to the parameters of a set of formulas to determine the first ten-order standardized central moments of the input process in AR model, in which a formulation for expanding the number of training samples based on limited experimental data has been developed. Subsequently, the Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) model, combined with Bayesian optimization (BO), is employed to establish a nonlinear mapping from the first ten-order standardized central moments to the corresponding statistical moments used to determine PJTM, in which another similar formulation for expanding the number of training samples based on limited experimental data has also been developed. Numerical cases show that the proposed method achieves significant improvements in computational efficiency while maintaining the same accuracy as the traditional AR-MEM-based method.

title: Bridge health monitoring via drive-by sensing: A novel CNN-based framework with full-scale field validation
abstract: This study introduces a pioneering approach to bridge Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) that integrates drive-by sensing with 1D Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). In one of the first known field tests that combined drive-by sensing and controlled damage of an in-service bridge, a full-scale reinforced concrete (RC) bridge in Nebraska was subjected to a series of progressive damage scenarios, with each subsequent damage state building upon the previous structural damage: healthy state (D0), saw-cutting of a parapet (D1), scour (D2), and deck damage (D3). A U-Haul truck, equipped with five strategically placed accelerometers, collected vibration data while traversing the bridge at speeds ranging from 0 to 30 mph (48 km/h), simulating real-world traffic conditions. The acquired time series from accelerometers were processed and input into a custom-designed 1D CNN model for damage detection and classification. The model demonstrated 99.9% training accuracy, 94.44% validation accuracy, and 93% testing accuracy. Detailed analysis of the confusion matrices revealed high classification precision across all damage states, with healthy (D0) and severely damaged (D3) conditions classified with over 95% accuracy, scour damage (D2) with over 92% accuracy, and parapet damage (D1) classified with slightly lower but robust performance exceeding 85%. This research represents the first successful application of 1D CNNs for damage detection of a full-scale, in-situ, bridge using drive-by sensing. These findings serve as an important step towards offering a non-intrusive, cost-effective, and scalable alternative to traditional SHM techniques. The proposed method demonstrated promising accuracy and efficiency in classifying bridge damage states, representing a significant first step toward advancing bridge health assessment practices. This approach has strong potential to enable safer and more resilient transportation infrastructure while optimizing maintenance resources.

title: Attention-enhanced transformer with prototype alignment for few-shot fault diagnosis under noisy cross-condition
abstract: This paper introduces a robust and adaptive few-shot learning framework for intelligent fault diagnosis under varying operating conditions and diverse noise interferences. The architecture integrates multi-scale signal encoding, adaptive condition modulation, prototype-driven alignment, and transformer-based decision modeling. To ensure noise robustness, raw sensor signals are first processed via parallel dilated depthwise separable convolutions and refined by a channel-spatial attention unit to enhance fault-relevant patterns. A context-aware modulation stage then recalibrates feature maps according to operating-condition indicators, promoting cross-condition generalization. For classification with limited labeled examples, prototype estimation is performed using a median-based reliable estimator, and query embeddings are aligned to these prototypes through a cross-domain attention-based alignment mechanism. A transformer encoder captures global interactions among aligned features and produces the final predictions. Training is guided by a composite loss combining classification, outlier, and dependency-aware terms, with a warm-up strategy to balance fitting and regularization. Evaluation on two industrial benchmarks, the Tennessee Eastman process and gold hydrometallurgy process, demonstrates that the framework consistently outperforms existing methods in noise resilience and domain adaptation.

title: Quality-aware gated cross-modal transformer for noise-robust underwater propeller fault diagnosis
abstract: Underwater propeller fault diagnosis is crucial for marine engineering applications and autonomous underwater vehicles; however, traditional methods can degrade severely in complex underwater environments where sensor reliability is unpredictable. This paper proposes a quality-aware gated cross-modal transformer (GCM-T) for robust fault diagnosis by fusing acoustic and visual information. The core innovations include (i) a quality-aware gating mechanism that dynamically adjusts modality weights based on domain-specific quality metrics and (ii) a gated cross-attention module that mitigates contamination from low-quality inputs via quality-guided feature enhancement. Evaluation on a novel underwater propeller dataset (7 fault categories, 17 scenarios ranging from clean conditions to extreme degradation) shows that GCM-T achieves 99.4% overall accuracy, maintains 100% accuracy under clean conditions, and remains robust under severe degradations. Sea-trial validation on a real AUV platform further demonstrates the framework’s practical applicability. Compared with existing methods, GCM-T delivers consistent gains under extreme conditions, demonstrating improved adaptability. Interpretability analyses validate the quality-aware design by revealing strong correlations between the learned gate weights and the measured modality-quality gaps.

title: DHFGAT: A dynamic heterogeneous fusion graph attention network for early gearbox fault detection
abstract: Accurate detection of early faults in industrial gearboxes is a critical but challenging task, particularly under dynamic operating conditions. Converting multi-sensor signals into graph-structured data via Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) offers a framework based on signal correlation modeling. However, the efficacy of this approach hinges on the quality of the graph structure, which is generally compromised by suboptimal construction methods and the inclusion of redundant features. To address these challenges, this study proposes a heterogeneous data fusion framework named Dynamic Heterogeneous Fusion Graph Attention Network (DHFGAT). Specifically, the current signal is first preprocessed to align its data morphology with the vibration signal. Then, to construct an information-rich graph structure, the Regularized Dual Averaging (RDA) algorithm adaptively selects the key feature subsets of the signal, thereby suppressing interference from redundant features. Subsequently, a training architecture that integrates the Spiking Neural Encoder (SNE) with the Simplified Graph Attention Network (SGAT) is adopted to achieve accurate and robust feature fusion and fault classification. Finally, extensive experiments were conducted on a test rig with eight fault types. The results demonstrate that DHFGAT achieves maximum average detection accuracies of 99.59% and 98.36% under constant and variable speed conditions, respectively. The proposed method provides a robust, reliable solution for early gearbox fault detection and offers insights into the optimal sensor combination for complex industrial scenarios.

title: Physics-guided multimodal neural operator for predicting point response under arbitrary impulse excitation in the medium with internal boundary
abstract: Predicting the stress wave propagation response in the medium with internal boundary has important applications in nondestructive testing. However, the existing methods focus on full-domain prediction, lack excitation generalization ability and computational efficiency. This paper proposes a stress wave propagation response calculation method based on physical a priori information, for predicting point responses in infinite medium containing internal boundaries such as holes or cracks under arbitrary excitation. Firstly, the waveform time–frequency invariant property was proved based on the fluctuation theory. This property constructed an excitation-independent operator which transforms the point response prediction into operator prediction. Then, a novel multimodal neural operator model was developed. This model integrated the internal boundary, material parameters, and excitation-reception point pairs to form a multimodal input, and cascaded the CNN, Bi-LSTM, and Self-Attention modules to achieve accurate prediction for the operators. The ablation experiments verified that the model architecture is rational. The comparison experiments demonstrated that the model’s prediction accuracy outperforms other deep learning algorithms. The case study revealed that the proposed prediction method can accurately compute the point response waveforms under arbitrary excitation and generate wavefield snapshots by multipoint parallel prediction. Combined with optimization algorithms, it can be used to achieve defect imaging. This study contributes a computational framework and algorithmic implementation for the complex medium fluctuation problem, which has excellent potential for structural health monitoring and nondestructive testing.

title: A physical knowledge-informed bearing fault feature extraction network based on Mamba
abstract: In contrast to signal processing methods that depend extensively on significant domain expertise, deep learning offers end-to-end feature self-learning capabilities, thereby providing a promising option for rolling bearing fault diagnosis. However, supervised learning paradigms that rely on categorical labels predominantly capture class-discriminative features, potentially resulting in the omission of essential fault-specific information within the feature space and diminishing the interpretability of the model. Therefore, this paper proposes an interpretable weak fault feature extraction framework, named Mamba-FeNet, which integrates Mamba’s exceptional sequence modeling strengths with physical prior knowledge of bearing fault. Firstly, a modal information estimation algorithm based on the marginal spectrum is introduced to extract potential resonance parameters from the frequency domain. This algorithm guides the resonance frequency settings in the simulation model and generates fault template signals based on prior physical knowledge. Secondly, the Mamba-FeNet is designed to model the vibration signals using selective state space, achieving end-to-end extraction of fault features under the encode-mask-decode paradigm. Thirdly, fault impact template signals are combined with normal signals scaled randomly in amplitude to form mixed signals for training the Mamba-FeNet, and a multi-model information weighted fusion strategy is designed based on the Envelope Spectrum Kurtosis (ESK). Finally, an interpretable analysis visualizes Mamba-FeNet’s internal structure and variables to intuitively demonstrate the fault feature extraction process. The proposed method is validated through simulations and experimental signals, showing superior performance compared to several advanced signal processing methods and deep learning methods.

title: A domain-correction framework for structural response reconstruction with imperfect FEM and sparse measurements
abstract: Deep learning for structural response reconstruction faces two fundamental barriers: scarce real-world data and the practical inevitability of imperfect finite element models (FEM). While FEM-generated data offer a solution, the systematic bias between simulation and reality is often overlooked, limiting generalization. This work proposes a domain-correction framework that strategically leverages this bias. We employ a minimally calibrated FEM as a biased simulator to pre-train a Bidirectional GRU network with Top-k sparse attention (BiGRU-SA), instilling physics-regularized priors. A Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) regularized transfer learning stage then actively corrects the simulation bias by aligning feature distributions, requiring only a tiny fraction of real data. Validated on a cantilever beam and a wind turbine blade, the framework demonstrates robust bias-correction capability. Crucially, despite significant time-domain discrepancies in the initial FEM, it achieves high-fidelity reconstruction (average R2 > 0.9966) using less than 20% of the available real data. This approach provides a practical and robust pathway for integrating deep learning into structural health monitoring under realistic constraints of model imperfection and data scarcity.

title: Deep generative models in condition and structural health monitoring: Opportunities, limitations and future outlook
abstract: Condition and structural health monitoring (CM/SHM) is a pivotal component of predictive maintenance (PdM) strategies across diverse industrial sectors, including mechanical rotating machinery, aircraft structures, wind turbines, and civil infrastructures. Conventional deep learning models, while effective for fault diagnosis and anomaly detection through automatic feature learning from sensor data, often struggle with operational variability, imbalanced or scarce fault datasets, and multimodal sensory data from complex systems. Deep generative models (DGMs) including deep autoregressive models, variational autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, diffusion-based models, and emerging large language models, offer transformative capabilities by synthesizing high-fidelity data samples, reconstructing latent system states, and modeling complex multimodal data streams. This review systematically examines state-of-the-art DGM applications in CM/SHM across the four main industrial systems mentioned above, emphasizing their roles in addressing key challenges: data generation, domain adaptation and generalization, multimodal data fusion, and downstream fault diagnosis and anomaly detection tasks, with rigorous comparison among signal processing, conventional machine learning or deep learning models, and DGMs. Lastly, we discuss current limitations of DGMs, including challenges of explainable and trustworthy models, computational inefficiencies for edge deployment, and the need for parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategies. Future research directions can focus on zero-shot and few-shot learning, robust multimodal data generation, hybrid architectures integrating DGMs with physics knowledge, and reinforcement learning with DGMs to enhance robustness and accuracy in industrial scenarios.

title: Analysis, optimization, and feature reduction in neural network models for quasi-static prediction in systems exhibiting Bouc-Wen hysteresis
abstract: This article addresses quasi-static torque prediction in systems with Bouc–Wen hysteresis, illustrated using a Vacuum Packed Particles Torsional Damper (VPPTD). A modified Bouc–Wen model (augmented with additional dry-friction and nonlinear stiffness components) was employed, with its parameters generalized as functions of chamber vacuum. The study was conducted on a dataset containing n=399,200 samples generated for multiple vacuum and material configurations. Five neural network architectures were compared, including a single-output model and multi-output variants predicting intermediate Bouc–Wen variables before estimating the torque M. Two input-reduction strategies were investigated: (S1) only physical parameters of the model, and (S2) a minimal control set (p,ABS) extended with selected intermediate signals. Feature selection was based on repeated-measures correlation (rmcorr), block-permutation clustering, and SHAP analysis; hyperparameter tuning was performed with Hyperopt. The highest accuracy was obtained for S2: the multi-output architecture with skip-connections achieved MAE(M)=0.043Nm (≈0.18%σM) for the full set of intermediates (INVI), while with only four inputs {φ,sign(φ̇),p,ABS} (INIVb) it maintained MAE(M)=0.051Nm (≈0.21%σM). Excluding dynamic signals (S1) increased the error to 0.38–0.61Nm (≈1.6–2.5%σM). Robustness tests (Gaussian noise, sign reversal of sign(φ̇), feature occlusion, repeated data splits) confirmed the greater stability of configuration INVI and the key role of φ and the correct sign of φ̇. A comparison with classical regressors (kNN, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting) indicated that although sometimes competitive under noise, they failed to provide consistent estimation of intermediate variables. The recommended solution is a multi-output architecture with skip-connections; in applications with limited sensor availability, a four-input configuration can be employed, with a conscious trade-off in robustness.

title: Online Adaptive Reinforcement Learning and Approximate Bayesian Computation (OARL-ABC) for real-time long-term calibration of rotordynamic models
abstract: Efficient, timely and accurate calibration of digital twins is critical for their application in real-time decision-making and condition monitoring. Digital twins, as dynamic virtual representations of connected physical systems, require continuous recalibration to adapt to evolving system states, environmental changes, and degradation over time. Without timely and effective recalibration, discrepancies between the digital and physical counterparts accumulate, potentially leading to compromised safety and operational inefficiencies. This study addresses these challenges by introducing the Online Adaptive Reinforcement Learning and Approximate Bayesian Computation (OARL-ABC) framework, a novel and model-agnostic calibration algorithm. Building upon the foundational RL-ABC framework, OARL-ABC offers enhanced adaptability, scalability, and robustness, facilitating real-time adjustment of model parameters across diverse systems. By integrating reinforcement learning strategies with approximate Bayesian computation, the proposed framework effectively accounts for uncertainties in model parameters and environmental variables, ensuring reliable predictions in complex and dynamic scenarios. To validate its efficacy, the OARL-ABC framework is applied to the calibration of a rotordynamic system for rotating machine fault diagnosis, demonstrating its capability to maintain alignment between the digital and physical domains in real-time. However, while the results demonstrate improved real-time calibration performance in this context compared to conventional calibration methods, OARL-ABC remains limited by its use of sampling techniques for repeated full-scale model runs. Further improvement should prioritize applying the method to a broader range of use cases, exploring simplified model forms, or enhancing the sampling scheme to run more efficiently.

title: FedSSLMfg: Federated self-supervised learning for heterogeneity-resilient and label-efficient condition monitoring in smart manufacturing
abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, reliable condition monitoring increasingly relies on cross-factory collaboration. However, operational data from industrial equipment are highly sensitive, leading to data silos that hinder collaboration and limit the development of generalizable diagnostic models. While federated learning (FL) provides a privacy-preserving paradigm that enables distributed factories to collaboratively train models without sharing raw data, its performance is often constrained by data heterogeneity and label scarcity. To address these two challenges, a federated self-supervised learning framework for heterogeneity-resilient and label-efficient condition monitoring in smart manufacturing, referred to as FedSSLMfg, is proposed. It involves three steps: signal preprocessing, federated self-supervised pre-training, and federated supervised fine-tuning. First, all vibration signals are unified to the same sampling frequency through anti-aliasing filtering and downsampling, and then transformed into time–frequency representations using the continuous wavelet transform. Then, feature representations are learned using a masked autoencoder-based self-supervised learning scheme within a federated setting. Lastly, the learned representations are transferred to downstream tasks by fine-tuning the federated models with labeled samples. The effectiveness of FedSSLMfg is validated on a federated setting consisting of three real-world rolling bearing datasets. Experiments show that it achieves high diagnostic accuracy and strong robustness under heterogeneous data distributions and label scarcity, outperforming both federated and non-federated baselines. Ablation studies further reveal that FedSSLMfg has low dependency on data augmentation, benefits from moderate masking ratios, and maintains high accuracy even when only a small fraction of samples are labeled.

title: A Riemannian-Hyperbolic Space-Based Algorithm for multisensor data fusion in spline degradation monitoring
abstract: Spline wear threatens the reliability of mechanical transmission systems, but conventional monitoring fails to reconcile heterogeneous data, capture dynamic degradation, or delineate hierarchical states. Here we present a geometric deep learning framework for multisensor fusion: vibration (macroscopic dynamics) and acoustic emission (AE, microscopic damage) signals are encoded as symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices to form a Riemannian manifold. Log-Euclidean metrics and Riemannian means mitigate cross-modal misalignment, while an attention-based graph neural network (GATConv) fuses features to learn spatiotemporal dependencies. Fused representations are embedded into Poincaré ball space—leveraging hyperbolic geometry’s exponential volume growth to enhance hierarchical wear separability—with unsupervised clustering and temporal mapping enabling time-resolved monitoring. On industrial datasets (slewing bearing, spline wear), the framework consistently outperforms mainstream methods by achieving effective cross-modal alignment, superior clustering quality, and accurate full-cycle wear tracking. This work establishes a geometric deep learning paradigm for mechanical health monitoring, advancing predictive maintenance in critical engineering systems.

title: Physics-informed kernel mixtures for structural dynamics
abstract: The effective integration of physical prior knowledge and measured data is critical for developing robust physics-informed machine learning frameworks. Calibrating the balance between structured physical approximations and data-driven flexibility is a key challenge of model development, particularly when physical models are only valid within specific operational regimes. In such cases, a global reliance upon a physical approximation can lead to model misspecification. This paper introduces a physics-informed kernel mixture framework for Gaussian process regression, capable of dynamically varying the reliance upon available physical knowledge based on identifiable switching variables. This ensures that physical understanding is prioritised in valid regimes and relaxed in favour of flexible data-driven components elsewhere. Rather than relying on soft constraints or loss-based penalties, known physics is explicitly embedded within the construction of kernels, enforcing desirable properties within predictions (e.g. quadratic lift force, localised behaviours). This allows model structure to mimic available physical intuition in an interpretable manner. Furthermore, the framework incorporates regime-dependent heteroscedastic noise to accurately capture varying uncertainty across different operational states. The versatility of the physics-informed kernel mixture framework is demonstrated through two distinct engineering case studies: the aerodynamic directional loading of a long-span suspension bridge and the prediction of aircraft wing strain during in-flight manoeuvres. The proposed kernel structures improve predictive accuracy and extrapolation whilst recovering an interpretable representation of regime-dependent system behaviour.

title: A novel mechanism-data dual-driven prediction method for tracking error in ultra-precision machining
abstract: The formation mechanism of tracking error in ultra-precision machining is highly complex, as it is influenced by multiple coupled factors.Traditional single-driven modeling methods—either mechanism-driven or data-driven—face inherent limitations: the former struggles to accurately capture the nonlinear dynamics of servo systems, while the latter suffers from poor interpretability.To fill this gap, this paper proposes a novel mechanism-data dual-driven tracking error prediction method. Firstly, a mechanism-driven prediction module for the deterministic physical components of tracking error is established based on servo control theory and parameter identification experiments. Then, based on the hybrid deep learning algorithm (TCN-BiLSTM-MHA), a data-driven module is developed to fit the unmodeled tracking error residuals. TCN and BiLSTM capture the long-term dependencies inherent in servo dynamics, while the MHA mechanism identifies key features and adaptively allocates their weights. Finally, a dual-driven prediction method is proposed by integrating the theoretical model with the residual prediction model. Experimental results demonstrate that compared with conventional single-driven methods, the proposed method achieves superior prediction accuracy, with a mean absolute error (MAE) as low as 0.000012 and a relative improvement of up to 65.71%. This work provides a reliable technical support for tracking error compensation and further improves the machining accuracy of optical components.

title: Data-driven predictive model and uncertainty analysis of vehicle-induced vibrations based on experimental measurements
abstract: Rapid urbanization has increased building construction near railway tracks, where ground vibrations induced by trains can damage structures and cause occupant discomfort, including headaches, nausea, and sleep disturbances. A number of different vibration comfort indicators were proposed for the assessment purposes, including the root mean square (RMS), vibration dose value (VDV), and maximum transient vibration value (MTVV). In order to better evaluate them, a multi-output chained gradient boosting model (MOC-GBM) is proposed in this paper, which adopts a strategy of integrating target variables into the input dataset and continuously updating the inputs during the predictions. Five locations across northern Poland were selected, and buildings with timber, steel, and reinforced concrete (RC) structural systems were investigated to compile a comprehensive dataset. They were used to evaluate the capability of MOC-GBM model. Then, two different locations were used to measure a new unseen dataset for general assessment of those predictive models. In the individual dataset, the proposed MOC-GBM model obtained accuracies of 98.2%, 99.2%, and 92.7% for predicting RMS, VDV, and MTVV, respectively. In addition, in mean value dataset, the proposed MOC-GBM model demonstrated very good predictive performance across all vibration comfort indicators with the accuracies of 99.4%, 99.7%, and 99.5% for predicting RMS, VDV, and MTVV, respectively, as well as the best fitted curve and promising results for curve fitting.

title: EPicMT: edge-aware physics-informed concurrent multiplexed transformer for high-fidelity signal compression, reconstruction, and diagnosis/prognosis
abstract: Prognostics & Health Management (PHM) systems collect high‑rate, multi‑sensor signals that must traverse bandwidth‑limited networks and run on resource‑constrained edge devices. Uniform, ratio-driven signal compression often erases weak yet diagnostic structures and degrades decision quality under operating drift. Many learned codecs store dense floating-point latent codes that are ill-suited to edge budgets, require per-sensor or per-fault specialization, and rarely embed physics. Under drift, these methods smear the sidebands and harmonics that carry critical evidence of degradation in vibration and acoustic signals. We introduce the Edge-aware Physics-informed Concurrent Multiplexed Transformer (EPicMT), a signal-processing framework, which couples selective transmission with physics-guided signal reconstruction within a single architecture spanning compression, reconstruction, and decision tasks. EPicMT implements content-aware token selection (sampling) to control the number of transmitted coefficients, and structure-aware, non-uniform quantization that assigns finer steps to harmonic/envelope bands and coarser steps to broadband background, achieving bit-budgeted signal compression rather than mere dimensionality reduction. On the decoder, a physics-guided Transformer with time–frequency priors, multi-scale envelope consistency and a physically-constrained diffuser, regularizes reconstruction so that spectral energy, phase relations, and envelope trends are preserved. Concurrent reflects the joint optimization of diagnostic and prognostic objectives within the same network, while multiplexed denotes parameter sharing across tasks through a common backbone and token interface, enabling unified training and signal-adaptive bit allocation under varying operating conditions. Case studies on an in-house gearbox testbed, the CWRU bearing dataset, and NASA CMAPSS demonstrate high-fidelity signal reconstructions at compression ratios up to 64:1 while maintaining or improving fault-classification accuracy and remaining useful life prediction relative to representative autoencoder and Transformer baselines. The learned gating reduces transmitted bits and on-device compute without hand-tuned heuristics, and an embedded deployment confirms feasibility on resource-constrained hardware.

title: Model-data integration and visual transfer for small sample intelligent fault diagnosis of spindle thrust bearing
abstract: The demand for condition monitoring and stable operation of high-precision equipment such as machine tools has promoted the optimization of maintenance strategies. However, the traditional equipment signal acquisition and intelligent diagnosis framework faces double limitations, that is, the scarcity of historical bearing fault data seriously affects the accuracy of the diagnosis model based on deep learning, and the contact vibration measurement method is difficult to cope with the layout requirements of complex industrial environments. For this reason, an intelligent diagnosis workflow of model-data integration and visual transfer is proposed for the raceway fault of thrust bearing of machine tool spindle. Firstly, the dynamic model of four-degree-of-freedom contact bearing is established to generate displacement simulation data with rich characteristics. Secondly, a sub-pixel visual vibration measurement method is proposed to collect the displacement signal of real equipment operation. Finally, the dynamic simulation data is migrated to the visual displacement data diagnosis. To address the inherent limitations of simulated signals and the instability in model accuracy caused by domain shifts, we propose a Mutual Information − Domain Adversarial Network. By incorporating the key principles of minimal-redundancy-maximal-relevance from information theory, this approach significantly enhances the robustness and accuracy of domain adaptation tasks. The effectiveness of the proposed method and diagnostic workflow is validated and analyzed through six simulation-to-reality transfer tasks. Results demonstrate that the intelligent diagnostic framework based on model-data integration and visual transfer effectively addresses the under-sampling problem and improves fault diagnosis accuracy.

title: An unsupervised domain adaptive fault diagnosis for rotating machinery based on physical wavelet convolution and joint distribution alignment
abstract: Under the conditions of strong noise and small samples, the subtle fault features of rotating machinery are often obscured, and traditional deep learning methods face the challenges of poor interpretability and a heavy reliance on large labeled datasets. To address these issues, an unsupervised fault diagnosis method based on an asymmetric modulated Gaussian difference wavelet kernel convolutional neural network (AMGDWKCNN) is proposed. Firstly, an asymmetric modulation physical convolution layer (AMPConv) is designed. By employing an asymmetrically modulated Gaussian difference wavelet kernel, it matches the asymmetric impact characteristics of vibration signals, thereby enhancing the model’s physical interpretability. Secondly, a dynamic nonlinear noise reduction mechanism is constructed, which employs a dual-attention-guided flexible soft threshold function to adaptively suppress noise interference, while leveraging the KAN activation function to enhance the nonlinear expression capability of fault features. Finally, a joint distribution alignment module is proposed. By combining category-conditional second-order statistical matching loss with predictive entropy uncertainty metrics, it dynamically weights and aligns category semantics with global distributions, thereby enhancing the model’s generalization performance across operating conditions. Experimental validation conducted on two publicly available bearing datasets and a self-built gearbox dataset demonstrates that the proposed method can effectively extract subtle fault features under the scenarios with strong noise and small samples, achieving high accuracy and strong generalization.

title: A rotating stall warning method for a contra-rotating compressor based on deep learning with automatic hyperparameter optimization
abstract: The dynamic pressure signals during the rotating stall process of a compressor exhibit pronounced nonlinearity and non-stationarity. In addition, the small amplitude of pre-stall disturbances makes early stall identification and warning a challenging signal-processing problem. Moreover, the hyperparameters of conventional neural network models rely on manual, experience-based tuning, which limits their prediction accuracy and robustness under complex operating conditions. To address these issues, this study proposes a rotating stall early warning method based on a convolutional neural network combined with a long short-term memory network (CNN-LSTM) with automatic hyperparameter optimization. A low-speed axial flow contra-rotating compressor is selected as the test object. Stall experiments are conducted under different inlet and rotational speed configurations. Dynamic pressure time series data are acquired using sensor arrays mounted at the blade tip of the front and rear rotors. After preprocessing, including filtering, normalization, and resampling, a dataset is constructed for neural network training and validation. The Northern Goshawk Optimization (NGO) algorithm is introduced to globally optimize key hyperparameters of the CNN-LSTM network. And the optimal NGO-CNN-LSTM model is then applied to predict dynamic pressure stall time series data. The results show that the NGO-CNN-LSTM model achieves higher prediction accuracy than the conventional CNN-LSTM model. Furthermore, a kernel density estimation (KDE) method is employed to adaptively determine stall warning thresholds for different operating conditions. Under uniform inlet conditions, the NGO-CNN-LSTM model achieves a stall warning lead time exceeding 10 s for most speed configurations and improves the poor warning performance of the CNN-LSTM model under some speed conditions. Under inlet distortion conditions, the proposed model still provides a stable stall warning time of no less than 7 s. Comparison between the predicted data and the original measurements indicates that the NGO-CNN-LSTM model can identify smaller amplitude pre-stall disturbances with clear physical significance at an earlier stage. Its predictions show higher consistency with the original data, leading to more reliable stall warning results.

title: Grey-box Gaussian processes for mode shape normalisation: Damage localisation under environmental and operational variability
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) offers a promising path towards automated, long-term monitoring of critical infrastructure such as offshore structures and bridges. A crucial component of such monitoring schemes is the localisation of damage, with model-based SHM providing a possible framework for this task. Here, damage localisation can be achieved by minimising the discrepancy between the modal properties of a damaged state and those of a healthy reference, but it is severely hindered by changes in the modal properties induced by environmental and operational variations (EOVs). This difficulty is compounded by the fact that measurement data are often limited, with data commonly unavailable across the full operational span, missing due to sensor failure and dropout, or sparsely sampled because of hardware constraints. In particular, mode shapes are often used without adequately accounting for the limited coverage of EOVs in continuous model-based damage localisation frameworks, resulting in inaccurate localisation. In this paper, we propose a regression-based data normalisation scheme that learns vector-valued mode shapes explicitly as functions of EOVs, allowing them to vary across a structure’s operating envelope and thereby enabling model-based damage localisation under varying environmental and operational conditions. To further alleviate the problem of limited training data, we consider two grey-box modelling strategies based on Gaussian processes that incorporate accessible engineering knowledge: (i) a Hilbert-space Gaussian process enforcing boundary conditions, and (ii) a Gaussian process with a physics-based prior mean given by finite-element mode shapes. We target long-term monitoring scenarios, where training data are limited and standard machine learning regression techniques underperform. Using the Leibniz University Test Structure for Monitoring, a representative real-world structure, we show that incorporating accessible engineering domain knowledge into a Gaussian process alleviates data scarcity and improves damage localisation under partially observed EOVs. This significantly extends the range of scenarios where model-based damage localisation is feasible, thereby improving the continuous, long-term monitoring capabilities of operational structures.

title: IAA-CRL: A universal information-adaptive augmentation based contrastive representation learning framework for remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearings
abstract: Accurate degradation-state identification and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of rolling-element bearings are pivotal for predictive maintenance, yet these tasks are severely challenged by ambient noise, complex operating conditions, and the intrinsic non-linearity of the degradation process. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Introspective Adaptive Augmentation Contrastive Representation Learning (IAA-CRL) framework tailored for bearing RUL prognosis. IAA-CRL innovatively integrates contrastive learning with a dynamically optimized data-augmentation strategy. An augmentation selector is introduced to adaptively determine the optimal fusion of transformations from a physics-constrained candidate pool, ensuring that the generated samples preserve critical degradation semantics while maximizing diversity in a purely data-driven manner, without requiring prior domain knowledge for the fusion strategy. Furthermore, a multi-scale contrastive loss is devised to effectively fuse instance-level and timestamp-level features, thereby capturing discriminative degradation representations. The superiority of IAA-CRL has been empirically validated through comprehensive benchmarking on both the FEMTO-ST and XJTU-SY datasets. Compared with state-of-the-art methods (including CBHRL, USL, SimCLR, and SupCon) IAA-CRL yields significant improvements in prediction accuracy on the majority of bearing samples, demonstrating enhanced robustness and generalizability.

title: Motion acceleration reconstruction of projectiles under launch conditions using generative adversarial networks
abstract: Accurate measurement of in-bore projectile acceleration is critical for optimizing artillery launch systems and evaluating interior ballistic performance. However, signals from projectile-borne storage tests are severely corrupted by high-frequency bore collision noise, masking low-frequency motion features and hindering accurate identification of projectile dynamics. Conventional denoising methods, which rely on cumbersome manual parameter tuning, prove ineffective against such stochastic high-amplitude coupled noise. This study proposes a physics-constrained generative adversarial network (GAN) that integrates physical priors with adversarial training. The method leverages the intrinsic physical mapping between projectile base pressure and in-bore acceleration, including synchronized time-domain peaks, consistent temporal trends, and shared underlying combustion and motion physics, to guide the denoising process. Specifically, the normalized base pressure signal serves as a conditional input to the discriminator, which evaluates the denoised acceleration produced by the generator. Physics-based constraints regulate the acceleration generation scale, enabling synergistic noise suppression and signal preservation while reducing reliance on extensive pristine training data. Simulations across ten noise levels demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms traditional techniques such as discrete wavelet transform and empirical mode decomposition, particularly in high-amplitude noise suppression. Three independent live-fire tests confirm its robustness and generalization capability, achieving a signal-to-noise ratio of up to 40 dB for the denoised in-bore acceleration. This work establishes a new paradigm for denoising dynamic signals in extreme launch environments, greatly enhancing the efficiency of ballistic testing and the accuracy of artillery performance assessment.

title: Adaptive wavelet-enhanced data-driven framework for surface quality prediction in ultra-precision manufacturing
abstract: Real-time surface roughness prediction is pivotal for enabling autonomous quality control in ultra-precision manufacturing, bridging the gap between process dynamics and product quality. However, the inherent non-stationarity of multi-source signals and harsh industrial noise pose significant challenges for existing predictive models. To address these limitations, this study presents a novel end-to-end data-driven framework that integrates differentiable parameterized Morlet wavelet encoding with deep spatiotemporal learning. Unlike traditional methods with fixed parameters, the proposed framework enables the adaptive learning of wavelet center frequency and scale via backpropagation, thereby providing a task-adaptive time–frequency representation for noisy sensor data. Validated on an ultra-precision lathe, the method achieves superior predictive performance with a coefficient of determination of 0.9715. Crucially, the framework demonstrates an ultra-low inference latency of 3.34 ms per sample, meeting the stringent real-time requirements of in-process monitoring on the investigated platform. This work provides an effective and computationally efficient framework for intelligent quality characterization under the investigated ultra-precision machining conditions, and offers a methodological basis for future validation in more complex manufacturing environments.

title: A dual-stage framework for industrial fault diagnosis under domain shift via enhanced voiceprint representation and hierarchical ensemble learning
abstract: While existing acoustic-based fault detection and diagnosis (AFDD) methods have achieved notable success, their performance in real industrial environments remains constrained by domain shifts, scarce fault samples, and limited computational resources. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a lightweight dual-stage framework that integrates enhanced voiceprint representation with hierarchical ensemble learning to achieve robust AFDD. First, an adaptive time–frequency feature modeling module is developed to construct enhanced local voiceprint representations from Mel spectrograms, effectively extracting fault-related acoustic patterns with improved discrimination and robustness under noisy and dynamic operating conditions. Second, a hierarchical ensemble learning strategy that integrates CatBoost, XGBoost, and logistic regression is designed to progressively refine the decision boundaries in the extracted feature space, thereby enhancing multi-level feature utilization, diagnostic stability, and decision process interpretability across different domains. Finally, extensive experiments on the DCASE 2022 Task 2 benchmark and a real-world power transformer dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior accuracy, robustness, and generalization capability compared to state-of-the-art AFDD approaches. Especially in various noise scenarios, the average diagnostic accuracy of the power transformer is improved by nearly 10%.

title: An evolutionary fusion framework with physics-informed and uncertainty-aware learning for tool wear prediction driven by milling force
abstract: In the context of intelligent manufacturing, achieving high-precision prediction of tool wear is crucial for enhancing manufacturing efficiency. However, this field currently faces three major challenges: the difficulty of directly measuring key physical quantities such as milling forces, the complexity of accurately interpreting process mechanisms, and the physical inconsistency and predictive uncertainty of purely data-driven models. To systematically address these issues, the objective of this research is to propose a novel paradigm that deeply integrates physical mechanisms with data-driven approaches. First, a multi-scale temporal convolutional network-frequency domain hybrid model (MSTCN-FD) is developed to achieve high-precision indirect perception of milling forces using easily measurable vibration signals. Secondly, a “physical wear value” is derived based on the physical relationship between force and wear, and embedded as a strong constraint into an ensemble learning physics-informed multi-source uncertainty-aware model (ELPI-MSUA). Thirdly, through a physics-guided loss function, data fitting and physical consistency are co-optimized, while uncertainties in the prediction process are quantified, thereby producing wear predictions with high accuracy and reliability. Finally, interpretability analysis methods are employed to reveal the physical basis of model decisions at the feature level. Experimental validation on two milling datasets under different working conditions shows that the wear prediction results achieve R2 values above 0.96, along with low RMSE and MAE values. The proposed framework not only accurately predicts milling forces and tool wear but also achieves deep closed-loop integration of physical mechanisms and data-driven approaches throughout the entire prediction process.

title: Spectrum- and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (SaPINNs) for input–state–parameter estimation in dynamic systems subjected to natural hazards-induced excitation
abstract: System identification under unknown external excitation is an inherently ill-posed problem, typically requiring additional knowledge or simplifying assumptions to enable reliable state and parameter estimation. The difficulty of the problem is further amplified in structural systems subjected to natural hazards such as earthquakes or windstorms, where responses are often highly transient, nonlinear, and spatially distributed. To address this challenge, we introduce Spectrum and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (SaPINNs) for efficient input--state--parameter estimation in systems under complex excitations characteristic of natural hazards. The proposed model enhances the neural network with governing physics of the system dynamics and incorporates spectral information of natural hazards by using empirically derived spectra as priors on the unknown excitations. This integration improves inference of unmeasured inputs, system states, and parameters without imposing restrictive assumptions on their dynamics. The performance of the proposed framework is demonstrated through comparative studies on both linear and nonlinear systems under various types of excitation, including the El Centro earthquake, where the seismic spectrum is assumed to be not precisely known. To account for predictive uncertainty, the proposed architecture is embedded within a Deep Ensemble (DEns) networks architecture, providing distributions over possible solutions. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms conventional PINNs, as the incorporation of spectral information introduces an inductive bias that guides the network more effectively through the solution space and enhances its ability to recover physically consistent state and parameter estimates with realistic uncertainty levels.

title: Remaining useful life prediction of complex equipment based on adaptive dual-branch multi-scale feature fusion model
abstract: Precise Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction is critical for ensuring the reliability and operational efficiency of complex equipment. However, existing data-driven methods are often limited by their inability to capture multi-scale degradation dynamics or sustain performance under fluctuating operating conditions. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes an Adaptive Dual-Branch Multi-Scale Feature Fusion (ADB-MSF) framework. The architecture integrates a self-attention mechanism to elucidate inter-sensor correlations, followed by a multi-scale Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) that simultaneously captures transient anomalies and long-term degradation trends. A gated enhancement module is further incorporated to refine feature representations by highlighting informative features while suppressing irrelevant noise. Uniquely, the model features an adaptive dual-branch prediction module that dynamically activates the most appropriate prediction pathway based on the input degradation state, ensuring robustness in complex environments. Additionally, a weighted Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss function is introduced to prioritize prediction accuracy near the critical end-of-life phase. Extensive experiments on stratospheric airship and C-MAPSS datasets confirm that ADB-MSF yields superior predictive performance compared to existing state-of-the-art baselines.
