title: Adaptive neural network control for ship-to-ship crane systems with dead-zone nonlinearity and actuator saturation
abstract: Ship-to-ship crane system plays a crucial role in offshore material transfer in modern maritime engineering. As a typical underactuated nonlinear system, the ship-to-ship crane system is subject to multiple challenges, including hull-coupling disturbances induced by ocean waves, parameter uncertainties, actuator dead-zone nonlinearity, and saturation constraints, all of which severely degrade positioning accuracy and swing suppression performance. To address these issues, an adaptive neural network control strategy is proposed in this paper. A smooth approximation function is employed to model actuator saturation, thereby avoiding potential instability and simplifying the controller design. A radial basis function neural network is applied to approximate the unknown nonlinear dynamics arising from system uncertainties and external disturbances, while an adaptive law is developed to compensate for the approximation errors and unknown parameters. By integrating the proposed adaptive mechanism, rapid swing elimination and accurate payload positioning are achieved simultaneously. Rigorous stability analysis based on Lyapunov theory and Barbalat’s lemma proves the asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system. Finally, experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed control scheme.

title: Evolutionary hypergraph: A Kalman-guided spatiotemporal dynamic hypergraph neural network for multi-sensor rolling bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Modern multi-sensor systems generate high-dimensional, noise-contaminated, and dynamically evolving multivariate time-series data, in which complex spatiotemporal dependencies play a key role in accurate fault diagnosis. However, effectively modeling these high-order correlations remains a significant challenge. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Kalman-guided spatiotemporal dynamic hypergraph neural network(KSD-HGNN), which is designed to comprehensively characterize high-order relationships and dynamic evolution among multiple sensors. The framework first employs a learnable band-pass filter bank for adaptive frequency-domain feature extraction, and then constructs and optimizes a dynamic spatiotemporal hypergraph to jointly encode spatial adjacency and cross-step temporal dependencies. Furthermore, by integrating Kalman filtering into hypergraph convolution, the model performs temporal smoothing and state estimation over hyperedge sequences, yielding more stable spatiotemporal representations. Finally, the state dynamics learned by the Kalman-guided branch and the structural dynamics captured by the adaptive topology branch are fused via a gating mechanism, yielding a more stable and comprehensive system representation. Experimental results demonstrate that KSD-HGNN consistently outperforms existing methods under varying operating and noise conditions, significantly improving multi-sensor bearing fault diagnosis performance.

title: In-situ optical emission spectroscopy monitoring of laser powder bed fusion based on spectral data prior knowledge and feature-decision level fusion network
abstract: Porosity defects are common quality issues in Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) manufacturing. Optical emission spectroscopy (OES), a key technique that reflects the interaction between the laser and the material, has been widely used in laser processing monitoring. However, the spectral signals in the LPBF process are extremely weak and complex, and there is a lack of reliable OES monitoring approaches. To address these challenges, this study proposed an OES monitoring framework driven by spectral data prior knowledge. First, the spectral signals and plasma features of different porosity defects in the LPBF process were systematically analyzed, and the correlation between the process and spectral signals was explored, revealing the defect-related spectral features of both emission lines and the background continuous spectrum, along with their underlying physical mechanisms. Building on this, a physics-informed spectral signal-to-image mapping method was proposed, which converted high-dimensional spectral data into dual-channel spectral grayscale mapping images, thereby enhancing spectral features strongly correlated with defects. Finally, the MSI-FDFNet model was developed for in situ porosity monitoring during the LPBF process. Results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively extracts distinctive features from different spectral bands, achieving an accuracy of 95.51% in identifying multiple porosity defects, significantly outperforming models using only feature-level or decision-level fusion. Additionally, visualization analysis confirms that the model can adaptively focus on defect-sensitive key spectral band information, enabling reliable monitoring through multi-level fusion. This study highlights the potential of physics knowledge-driven OES monitoring for in-situ monitoring of the LPBF process.

title: A cointegration-driven auto-adaptive neural network strategy for strain-based structural health monitoring of masonry structures and its application for damage detection in full-scale experimental testing
abstract: Strain is a highly effective damage-sensitive feature for Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) of masonry structures. However, Environmental and Operational Variations (EOVs), such as air temperature changes, can induce drifts in strain time series that mask damage-related patterns, requiring compensatory techniques for reliable novelty detection. This paper proposes a cointegration-driven, auto-adaptive neural network strategy for strain-based SHM in masonry structures, a field where effective approaches remain limited. The methodology integrates nonlinear cointegration principles with a customized Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) regressor at the sensor level. Unlike standard implementations, the MLP captures time dependency through a modified input matrix that incorporates historical information, enabling damage-sensitive features cleansed of EOV effects. Novelty analysis then combines stationarity assessment with statistically robust control charts for damage detection. A Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) validates the proposed time-dependent MLP model, and a Convolutional Autoencoder (CAE) is adopted as a benchmark to assess novelty detection against an established deep-learning paradigm. A case study consisting of a full-scale masonry building monitored through smart bricks and subjected to varying damage scenarios under real environmental conditions demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed strategy. Results show that the time-dependent MLP achieves higher computational efficiency than the RNN while maintaining accuracy, that the nonlinear cointegration approach overcomes key limitations of linear methods in EOV compensation and damage detection, and that the proposed framework matches the CAE in novelty detection at a markedly lower computational cost. Overall, this supports a broader and more effective application of strain-based SHM in masonry structures.

title: Generative adversarial networks for high frequency ultrasonic field modelling near fluid-solid interfaces
abstract: The propagation of high frequency ultrasonic waves enables the detection of fine inclusions and cracks in solid media, often induced by fatigue or impact loads. Accurate modelling of high frequency wavefields significantly enhances the ability of structural health monitoring systems to detect fatigue cracks and localize stress concentrations near defects within solid plates. Numerical solvers, such as the Finite Element Method (FEM), require fine meshing of the problem geometry, whereas semi-analytical modelling, such as the Distributed Point Source Method (DPSM), demand large number of distributed point sources to accurately model high frequency ultrasonic fields, resulting in significant computational overhead. However, such computational constraints limit their applicability in real-time or large-scale monitoring systems. To address these challenges, we propose a surrogate model for expensive numerical solvers (FEM/DPSM) to efficiently predict high frequency ultrasonic wavefields in isotropic solids coupled with a fluid medium. A conditional generative adversarial network (cGANs), based on the Pix2Pix architecture, which features a U-Net as a generator and a PatchGAN as a discriminator is employed for training. Multiple tailored loss functions, including frequency, edge, perceptual, and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) based losses are included within total generator loss to ensure physical accuracy and structural fidelity. The Pix2Pix model is trained on paired low- and high-frequency wavefield data encompassing both healthy and damaged configurations with a circular hole in the solid half-space. For both cases, the trained model demonstrates excellent predictive performance for generating high frequency wavefield, with SSIM values for displacement and normal stresses consistently exceeding 0.85.

title: A graph attention network framework utilizing Kolmogorov–Arnold networks for dynamic analysis of complex structures in unseen scenarios
abstract: The rise of deep learning (DL) has greatly improved the analysis of complex structural responses. However, traditional DL models are limited by their dependence on large datasets, which hampers generalization to unseen scenarios and adaptability to various structural forms. To address these challenges, this paper introduces GATKAN, a novel graph attention network framework based on Kolmogorov–Arnold networks (KAN). GATKAN models complex structures as graphs, integrating spatial topology into the training process. Utilizing a multi-head attention mechanism, it captures temporal response patterns and aggregates data from each graph node. The Kolmogorov–Arnold network updates potential states and projects data into the desired dimensions. Experimental results show that GATKAN generalizes well across unseen scenarios, particularly for complex systems with varying structural forms. The model’s robustness is further validated by noise introduction and sensitivity analyses. Comparison with baseline models demonstrates GATKAN’s superior prediction accuracy, especially in handling node features and dynamic system responses. Moreover, it reduces training data requirements while maintaining high accuracy, making it a promising tool for practical engineering applications.

title: An interpretable adaptive denoising convolutional network for intelligent fault diagnosis of rotating machinery
abstract: Deep learning has achieved significant success in intelligent fault diagnosis owing to its powerful nonlinear mapping capabilities. However, the lack of interpretability of deep learning-based fault diagnosis methods with black-box characteristics has seriously hindered their widespread industrial application. To address this issue, an interpretable adaptive denoising convolutional network (IADC-Net) is proposed for intelligent fault diagnosis of rotating machinery in this paper, which constructs a comprehensive interpretability framework. In this method, the interpretable signal processing layer is driven by adaptive fusion denoising wavelet convolution (AFDWC) module, enhancing the model’s generalization capabilities in various scenarios. The AFDWC integrated with multiple wavelet basis kernel can capture abundant multi-scale mechanical fault information. The adaptive soft threshold denoising (ASTD) dynamically removes noise interference on channel features, and the energy-entropy ratio channel weighting adaptively highlights frequency bands more relevant to faults. Then, the interpretable feature extraction layer leverages the sparse interaction characteristics of traditional convolutions to elucidate its intrinsic mathematical implications through sparse representation, which is of great significance to the engineering applications of various convolutional networks. And, the interpretable result analysis layer visualizes the model results with attention weight and output features to help users understand the decision process and trust diagnosis results. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified and analyzed by the public fault datasets and the industrial robot experimental platform, demonstrating the interpretability of model, the rationality of network structure and the superiority of diagnostic performance. The code library is available at: https://github.com/GTH25/IADC-Net.

title: Robust physics-informed thermal error modeling for ball screw feed drives via in-process data assimilation
abstract: Thermally induced positioning error (TIPE) in ball screw feed drives critically affects the machining accuracy of high-precision machine tools. Existing thermal error models are challenged by their reliance on extensive labeled datasets, which increases data acquisition costs and prolongs production cycles. In addition, these models utilize sparse temperature measurements as inputs, which are insufficient for reconstructing the full temperature field and therefore limit the characterization of non-uniform TIPE distributions under complex feed motions. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a physics-informed digital twin (PIDT) framework for TIPE prediction that does not require labeled TIPE data for supervised training or parameter fitting, while explicitly incorporating the time-varying nut trajectory. First, an independent reduced thermal domain of the screw shaft is established by assimilating measured boundary temperatures, while a convolution-based physics-informed solver reconstructs the transient temperature field induced by the moving nut and stationary bearings. Subsequently, the TIPE profile along the feed axis is derived by integrating the axial temperature distribution and is dynamically constrained by a novel in-process end-displacement (IPED) measurement, thereby enabling online correction without interrupting machining. Across four operating conditions with different feed rates and reciprocating ranges, the proposed model achieves accurate and robust prediction under parameter uncertainty, reducing the maximum TIPE from 42.3, 56.7, 58.3, and 53.7 μm to 2.9, 4.6, 4.1, and 3.6 μm, respectively. This framework provides an efficient, physically interpretable, and cost-effective solution for TIPE compensation under complex and variable machining conditions.

title: Towards trustworthy milling chatter detection via physics-assisted feature extraction and stacking-based decision-level fusion
abstract: Chatter is an instability phenomenon in the milling process that may adversely affect surface quality and machining efficiency. To achieve high-performance machining, online chatter detection is of critical importance in mechanical manufacturing. However, existing methods primarily rely on signal processing techniques and single classifiers, which limits their interpretability and generalization capability, thereby resulting in untrustworthy detection results under variable cutting conditions. To deal with this limitation, this paper proposes a milling chatter detection method via physics-assisted feature extraction and stacking-based decision-level fusion. First, a physics-assisted feature extraction method is proposed to extract interpretable and discriminative features by modeling dynamic milling forces and characterizing the chatter evolution mechanism. Then, multiple deep learning-based classifiers are constructed as base models, including a convolutional neural network, a residual network, an Inception network, a capsule network, and a dilated convolutional network. Subsequently, a stacking ensemble learning based on XGBoost is designed to perform decision-level fusion of the outputs from these base models. Milling experiments are conducted to construct a dataset under different cutting conditions, and cross-validation is employed to demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

title: PI-DSTHP: A Physics-Informed dynamic symplectic tracking and Hamiltonian projection framework for roller bearing RUL prediction under multi-source noise interference
abstract: Accurate Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction for roller bearing is severely hindered by static decomposition and multi-source noise interference, which often lead to mode mixing and feature fractures during long-term service. To address these bottlenecks, this paper proposes a novel Physics-Informed Dynamic Symplectic Tracking and Hamiltonian Projection (PI-DSTHP) framework. First, a dynamic symplectic tracking model is developed to continuously track physical mode identities via Hamiltonian minimum action path optimization, fundamentally eliminating mode mixing and ensuring continuous feature evolution across the full lifecycle. Second, an asynchronous Hamiltonian defense mechanism driven by Hamiltonian intrinsic momentum gliding is constructed, which isolates noise into independent phase-space orbits to adaptively bypass and restore distorted signal regions via physical inertia. Finally, the Hamiltonian energy trajectory projection model transforms RUL evaluation into a deterministic geometric intersection problem within the phase space, which can utilize the relative energy expansion effect to quantify system degradation and enable robust cross-domain prediction without target-domain priors. Experimental validation on two full-lifecycle roller bearing datasets demonstrates the significant superiority of the PI-DSTHP model in continuous degradation tracking and prognostic accuracy, offering full-chain physical interpretability from symplectic geometry to final life extrapolation.

title: Study on real-time prediction for porosity in laser melting based on a digital twin-driven deep learning framework
abstract: The keyhole-induced pore defect is recognized as a major nuisance in laser melting (such as welding and 3D printing). As a crucial indicator for assessing the specific severity of pores, porosity has long been obtained only through complex and offline internal inspection after manufacturing. In this paper, guided by the formation mechanism of pores revealed via numerical simulation, a digital twin-driven deep learning framework (DTDLF) is proposed that enables direct and real-time porosity prediction during laser beam welding. In the perception field, keyhole depth and keyhole opening circumference are acquired through multi-sensing measurement and signal processing. In the physical field, simulation can acquire maximum temperature on the bottom wall of the keyhole. Subsequently, a sparse auto-encoder is constructed to fuse the original fluctuation characteristics mined from their respective digital twin data sources, and all of the obtained overall features are demonstrated to be highly correlated with porosity. In the DTDLF, a tandem structure of two deep neural networks (DNNs) connected in series is adopted, where the former DNN conducts online prediction of the fused overall feature in the physical field utilizing process parameters to circumvent the long simulation runtime, and the latter DNN couples all the fused overall features in the perception-physics fields for predicting porosity online. The final results indicate that the DTDLF has a significant accuracy advantage over monitoring frameworks that use solely single-field information, and meanwhile its real-time performance is not compromised.

title: A hypergraph-enhanced state space model-Mamba framework for cross-domain response reconstruction guided by physical information
abstract: In data-driven structural response signal reconstruction tasks, the scarcity of high-quality, well-marked batch response data and the ambiguous spatial dependency patterns between response data constitute critical bottlenecks that constrain the performance of response reconstruction models. To address this challenge, this work proposes a novel cross-domain response reconstruction method based on a Hypergraph-enhanced Mamba (State Space Model) network (HeMamba) — a dual-stream framework that simultaneously processes temporal and spatial information. Specifically, the method utilizes the Mamba to capture long-term dynamic dependencies in multi-sensor signals, employs hypergraphs to model the higher-order spatial relationships among sensors, incorporates a designed two-layer Hypergraph Convolutional Network (HGCN) to capture their spatial dependency patterns, and additionally introduces a physics-based loss function derived from Power Spectral Density (PSD) to constrain the training process. Furthermore, a physics-informed transfer learning paradigm is introduced, wherein the model is pre-trained using finite element numerical simulation data. By freezing the spatial encoding module, the knowledge of structural physical response laws and intrinsic patterns learned by HeMamba is transferred to scenarios with limited real measured data for fine-tuning, thereby guiding the Mamba model to perform response signal reconstruction in the measured domain under physical constraints. Experiments on a tower steel structure indicate that the proposed method effectively alleviates the reconstruction accuracy degradation caused by data scarcity. With fine-tuning on a small amount of measured data, the reconstructed signals achieve an R2 value of 0.9798 and exhibit high-precision response reconstruction across the full frequency band, significantly outperforming baseline models trained directly. Notably, even under structural damage conditions, the proposed method still can transfer physical knowledge learned from the source domain to response reconstruction in the target domain. This study provides a feasible technical pathway for high-precision cross-domain response reconstruction under small-sample conditions.

title: Open-set domain generalization residual feature reconstruction network for intelligent fault diagnosis under unknown time-varying working conditions
abstract: Currently, deep learning has garnered significant attention for addressing fault diagnosis challenges. However, in real-world industrial settings, the complexity of equipment and diversity of operating conditions can lead to unknown faults occurring under target conditions. Consequently, open-set domain generalization fault diagnosis (OSDGFD) has emerged as a critical research direction. However, existing open-set domain generalized fault diagnosis suffers from negative transfer, drastic changes in feature distributions under non-stationary time-varying rotational speed conditions, and insufficient revelation of fault features. These issues severely hinder performance research in open-set domain generalized fault diagnosis. Therefore, this paper proposes the Residual Feature Reconstruction Network for Intelligent Fault Diagnosis in Unknown Time-Varying Conditions (RFR-OSDG). First, a compact and reconstructable latent representation for known-class features is learned using known-class feature distribution mechanisms, while KL divergence constrains the normality of the latent distribution. Unknown classes, failing to conform to this distribution, exhibit larger reconstruction errors and are thus preliminarily distinguished. Building upon this foundation, an adaptive domain-aware class boundary loss constructs a dynamic decision boundary. This boundary constrains intra-class samples to remain within the boundary region while excluding out-of-class samples, thereby enhancing the model’s boundary recognition for known classes and reducing cross-class confusion and misclassification of unknown classes. By minimizing the triplet loss, the aggregation of similar features and the separation of dissimilar features are enhanced. An entropy-enhanced category-aware mechanism is designed to address the issue of inconsistent data distribution between the source domain and the target domain. Finally, experimental results under non-stationary time-varying speed show that the proposed method, RFR-OSDG, has better clustering and classification performance as well as superior generalization.

title: A Class-Aware Supervised Contrastive Graph Network for CNC machining condition monitoring with class-imbalanced data
abstract: Machining state monitoring plays a critical role in ensuring quality, productivity, and reliability in CNC manufacturing. However, real-world industrial scenarios are often characterized by severe class imbalance and limited annotated data, which significantly challenge the robustness and generalization of existing learning-based approaches. To address this issue, we propose a Class-Aware Supervised Contrastive Graph Network (CSCGN), a unified framework that rethinks imbalanced industrial signal learning from a representation-centric perspective. Instead of treating signal segments independently, the proposed approach explicitly models the intrinsic structural relationships of one-dimensional sensor signals through a dynamic graph mechanism, while incorporating class-aware contrastive learning to enhance discriminative representation under imbalance. By jointly integrating multi-view signal representations, physics-informed topological modeling, and imbalance-aware optimization, the proposed framework effectively captures both structural dependencies and minority-class characteristics in noisy industrial environments. Extensive experiments on representative CNC machining tasks, including chatter detection and tool wear monitoring, demonstrate that CSCGN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various imbalance settings. The results highlight its strong capability in minority-class recognition while maintaining overall robustness, indicating its potential for reliable deployment in real-world industrial systems.

title: Dynamics-guided disentangled hypersphere prototype for rotor system fault diagnosis under variable operating conditions with limited data
abstract: Rotor systems are fundamental components of rotating machinery, and their accurate fault diagnosis is the cornerstone of equipment safety. However, in practical industrial scenarios, existing data-driven methods are challenged by the coupling effect of variable operating conditions and limited training data. The feature variations induced by variable operating conditions typically require massive data for complex distribution fitting, which inherently conflicts with the reality of limited data. To address this dilemma, a dynamics-guided disentangled hypersphere prototype (DG-DHP) framework is proposed, which integrates physics-based dynamics modeling with data-driven representation disentanglement and prototype learning. First, a dynamic model of the rotor system is constructed to simulate a large amount of diverse data, and real-world noise patterns are injected to enhance data fidelity, thereby alleviating the scarcity of training data. Second, a representation disentanglement mechanism based on Brownian distance covariance is proposed to extract fault-related representations that are invariant to variable operating conditions via an explicit statistical regularization. Finally, adaptive hypersphere prototype learning is developed to replace traditional classifiers for fault diagnosis, thereby simultaneously facilitating the fitting of complex distributions and rapid adaptation to limited real-world samples. The proposed DG-DHP framework is validated on two rotor systems, demonstrating its superiority in rotor system fault diagnosis under variable operating conditions with limited data.

title: Upper approximation bounds for neural oscillators
abstract: Neural oscillators, originating from second-order ordinary differential equations (ODEs), have demonstrated strong performance in stably learning causal mappings between long-term sequences or continuous temporal functions, as well as in accurately approximating physical systems. However, theoretically quantifying the capacities of their neural network architectures remains a significant challenge. In this study, the neural oscillator consisting of a second-order ODE followed by a multilayer perceptron (MLP) is considered. Its upper approximation bound for approximating causal and uniformly continuous operators between continuous temporal function spaces and that for approximating uniformly asymptotically incrementally stable second-order dynamical systems are derived. The established proof method of the approximation bound for approximating the causal continuous operators can also be directly applied to state-space models consisting of a linear time-continuous complex recurrent neural network followed by an MLP. Theoretical results reveal that the approximation error of the neural oscillator for approximating the second-order dynamical systems scales polynomially with the reciprocals of the widths of two utilized MLPs, thus overcoming the curse of parametric complexity. The convergence rates of two established approximation error bounds are validated through four numerical cases. These results provide a robust theoretical foundation for the effective application of the neural oscillator in science and engineering.

title: Generative digital twin: A Sparse-xLSTM based self-evolution hybrid modeling approach for complex equipment
abstract: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into digital twins (DTs) offers transformative potential for characterizing the non-linear dynamics of complex equipment. However, realizing high-fidelity, self-evolution generative DTs remains challenging due to the computational prohibitiveness of Transformer based architectures and the insufficient long-term memory of traditional recurrent networks. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel generative digital twin (GDT) method driven by a Physics-Guided Sparse-xLSTM. First, we construct a Sparse-xLSTM architecture designed to model high-dimensional temporal dynamics efficiently. By leveraging exponential gating and matrix memory, this architecture achieves linear computational complexity while effectively capturing long-range dependencies, overcoming the quadratic bottleneck of conventional attention mechanisms. A sparse attention strategy is further incorporated to extract distinct state features from noisy sensor data, enhancing representation robustness. Second, to ensure physical consistency and generalization, a hybrid modeling mechanism is devised. Physical priors are embedded as input feature, and governing equations are integrated into the optimization objective as physical constraints, effectively confining the generative solution space to physically valid trajectories and mitigating model hallucinations. Third, addressing the imperative for continuous adaptation, a low-rank adaptation (LoRA)-based self-evolution engine is developed. This mechanism enables the GDT to perform online updates using limited streaming data by fine-tuning low-rank matrices, ensuring rapid synchronization with the time-varying states of the physical entity without catastrophic forgetting. Experimental validation on CNC machine tool wear datasets demonstrates that the proposed approach significantly outperforms advanced baselines in both prediction accuracy and adaptation efficiency, providing a robust paradigm for intelligent predictive maintenance of complex equipment.

title: Data-informed simulation of temperature effects in finite element models for structural health monitoring using inverse surrogate modeling
abstract: This work presents a data-informed framework to simulate temperature effects in a finite element model (FEM) for structural health monitoring (SHM), enabling realistic generation of synthetic modal data for both healthy and damaged states. A challenge in vibration-based SHM is that real damaged data are rarely available, so damage detection and classification methods are often validated using FEM simulations. However, temperature strongly affects modal data through changes in stiffness, connections, and boundary conditions, and these effects are difficult to reproduce realistically using standard thermo-mechanical assumptions, especially when only few temperature measurements are available. The proposed approach combines field monitoring data with an updated FEM through inverse surrogate modeling. First, an inverse surrogate model is trained on FEM simulations to recover temperature-sensitive mechanical parameters (e.g., Young’s modulus of elasticity) from modal frequencies. Then, this surrogate is applied to long-term monitoring data to estimate how these parameters evolve with temperature. A second regression model then learns a direct mapping from temperature to FEM parameters. Injecting these temperature-dependent parameters into the FEM allows simulation of realistic temperature-frequency trends, for both healthy and damage scenarios. The method is demonstrated on a numerical truss and on the KW51 railway bridge. Results show high accuracy in modal frequency prediction and consistent anomaly detection performance, indicating that the framework reproduces in-situ thermal effects without requiring explicit thermo-mechanical modeling, while preserving damage detectability under temperature variations.

title: Deep Learning-Accelerated inverse design of NURBS-Based phononic crystals with customized bandgaps
abstract: Phononic crystals (PnCs) enable effective control of elastic wave propagation through the formation of frequency bandgaps, but their design is computationally demanding due to the complex relation between geometry and dynamic behavior. To address this challenge, this study proposes a deep learning–accelerated inverse design framework for non-uniform rational B-spline (NURBS)-based phononic crystals. In the proposed approach, a NURBS parameterization scheme is employed to represent the unit-cell geometry using control points and weights, enabling smooth, fabricable, and highly flexible curved-edge design. A deep neural network (DNN) is trained to accurately predict the full dispersion relations of PnCs, replacing finite element (FE) analysis with millisecond-level inference. The trained model is integrated with an improved real-coded genetic algorithm (IRGA) to perform global optimization under multiple objective functions, including single-bandgap maximization, dual-bandgap enhancement, target-frequency bandgap control, and dispersion customization. The results demonstrate that the DNN surrogate achieves an R2 of 0.996, with 84.2% of test samples exhibiting a mean relative error below 4.5%. The DNN–IRGA framework efficiently identifies optimized geometries that exhibit desired bandgap properties, validated by FE simulations and a 3D-printed experimental specimen showing strong attenuation (up to − 85 dB) within the predicted bandgap. This work establishes a unified framework that bridges geometric parameterization, deep learning prediction, and inverse optimization, providing a powerful tool for rapid and customizable bandgap design of two-dimensional NURBS-based phononic crystals.

title: Decoupling compound faults under data imbalance: A multi-task dynamic balanced learning network for gearbox fault diagnosis
abstract: Gearbox is a core component in mechanical transmission systems, and its accurate fault diagnosis is critical for ensuring operational safety of mechanical equipment. Although intelligent diagnosis methods have achieved promising results, they still face significant challenges. First, gearbox is a complex system with tightly coupled components (e.g., gears and bearings). Most existing methods focus on diagnosing isolated components, failing to effectively decouple and identify multi-component compound faults. Second, in actual engineering, fault data is usually scarce and severely imbalanced compared to normal data, which significantly degrades the performance of conventional data-driven models. To address these challenges, a multi-task dynamic balanced learning network is proposed for compound fault decoupling diagnosis with imbalanced data. Specifically, gearbox compound fault diagnosis is reformulated as a component-level multi-task diagnosis problem. First, a shared backbone network is designed to extract common features from vibration signals, followed by two kernel-adaptive task-specific branch networks that hierarchically disentangle component-level fault features for different tasks. Then, an adaptive balance loss is utilized to reweight training samples and alleviate the class imbalance influence. Finally, a task dynamic balancing strategy is incorporated to dynamically coordinate and optimize multiple diagnostic tasks during training. Extensive experiments are conducted on both real-world engineering and public datasets. The results show that the proposed method still achieves over 98% diagnostic accuracy on both gear and bearing diagnosis tasks even under severe class imbalance condition, demonstrating its superiority and robustness compared to other advanced methods.

title: A self-supervised learning approach for intelligent surface roughness monitoring in thin-walled component machining
abstract: Surface roughness monitoring is essential for process quality control in intelligent manufacturing, yet reliable prediction in thin-walled component milling remains challenging because roughness labels are sparse and multi-channel vibration responses are spatially and dynamically heterogeneous. This study proposes a spatially aware self-supervised contrastive learning framework using six-channel spindle–worktable vibration signals. The task is formulated as sparse-label anchor-bag roughness regression: only the bag corresponding to the central small region in each large region is assigned a measured roughness label, whereas the remaining small-region bags are used as unlabeled data for representation learning. The framework integrates a multi-channel vibration encoder, a physics-guided gated bag aggregation module, and a spatially aware weighted InfoNCE objective. Bag-level self-supervised pretraining enables the model to learn transferable representations while reducing excessive separation between physically related neighboring bags; the pretrained encoder and aggregation module are then fine-tuned using only labeled anchor bags. Experiments on two thin-walled helical milling datasets, Ti2AlNb and GH4169D, demonstrate robust performance under sparse annotation and material variation using a workpiece-level evaluation protocol. The proposed method achieves R2 = 0.9431 ± 0.0337 and RMSE = 0.0274 ± 0.0145 μm on Ti2AlNb, and maintains strong performance on GH4169D with R2 = 0.9246 ± 0.0424, RMSE = 0.0171 ± 0.0093 μm. Comparative and ablation analyses support the effectiveness of self-supervised pretraining, spatially aware contrastive learning, multi-channel fusion, and the anchor-bag supervision setting, providing a label-efficient route for surface quality monitoring in intelligent manufacturing.

title: Self-supervised ViT-driven whole-line alignment of multi-date rail ultrasonic B-scan data for longitudinal infrastructure inspection
abstract: Multi-channel rail ultrasonic B-scan data provide critical evidence for defect identification, cross-period reinspection, and longitudinal condition assessment. However, reliable comparison of inspection records acquired on different dates requires mileage alignment, so that B-scan indications from the same physical rail locations can be compared over time. Existing alignment methods generally follow two routes. Methods relying on external mileage or positioning references may suffer from accumulated drift, initialization offsets, and local data loss during long-distance inspection, whereas methods based on local signal similarity are easily disrupted by sparse indications, noise, missing features, and false alarms. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a whole-line cross-date alignment framework for multi-channel rail ultrasonic B-scan data. The method first converts pseudo-color B-scan indications into structured event-level cues and extracts repeatable local patterns from unlabeled inspection data. These cues are then used to estimate a global coarse offset, construct reliable candidate correspondences, enforce global order consistency, and fit a piecewise mileage mapping between inspection runs. Experiments on real multi-date heavy-haul railway inspection data show that the proposed method achieves stable whole-line alignment under noise, data discontinuities, and missing indications, suppresses drift accumulation, and reduces the mean alignment error to within 3 m. The results indicate that the proposed framework can provide a reliable mileage reference for cross-date ultrasonic reinspection and long-term rail condition assessment.

title: Neural network assisted-augmented Kalman filter for joint input-state estimation
abstract: The augmented Kalman filter (AKF) is widely used for joint input-state estimation by augmenting the state vector with unknown inputs. However, its performance critically depends on the Gaussian white noise assumption and the proper selection of noise covariance matrices, making it sensitive to modeling errors in the state-space representation and hyperparameter tuning in practice. To address these challenges, this study proposes an AKF-inspired hybrid learned observer, termed AKFNet, for joint input-state estimation from sparse output-only measurements. Unlike the classical AKF, AKFNet no longer computes the Kalman gain analytically based on the minimum mean square error principle; instead, it is a hybrid data-driven and model-based algorithm that embeds a recurrent neural network (RNN) module into the AKF recursion and empirically learns the gain directly from measurements. The RNN module learns to map the information of real data within the state-space model to an effective Kalman gain, thereby improving the accuracy and robustness of joint input-state estimation in practical scenarios where model mismatches and complex noises are present. The proposed AKFNet is first validated on a numerical 9 DOF building for seismic input-state estimation, and compared with the classical AKF, dual Kalman filter (DKF) and an adaptive AKF with online covariance adjustment. Subsequently, an experimental shaker table test is conducted on a three-story frame to further validate its effectiveness. Finally, the AKFNet is used to estimate wind loads on a real-world large-span cable-stayed bridge using field data. In all tested scenarios, AKFNet provides competitive or improved accuracy, demonstrating its robustness and adaptive capability in the presence of modeling errors and non-white Gaussian noise.

title: Application of machine-vision-driven physics-informed neural networks in pantograph–catenary system state detection
abstract: The pantograph–catenary system is a core component for energy transmission in electrified railways for high-speed trains, and its stability directly affects train operation safety and power supply quality. With the continuous increase in train operating speed and line power demand, accurate state detection of the pantograph–catenary system has become increasingly important. However, traditional monitoring schemes rely on sensor installation and structural modification of the pantograph, which not only increases cost and may alter the original dynamic characteristics, but is also susceptible to external environmental interference, thereby limiting their practical application. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) embed system physical equations into network training, providing a potential approach for high-precision modeling and state prediction of the multiscale spatiotemporal nonlinear frequency-response characteristics of the pantograph–catenary coupling process without additional hardware cost. However, existing PINN methods still face three major challenges in pantograph–catenary system applications. At the feature extraction level, existing methods struggle to fully exploit the spatiotemporal multidimensional physical features of event-stream images. At the physical-variable processing level, they have difficulty deeply characterizing the complex nonlinear coupling between time-domain and frequency-domain physical quantities in the pantograph–catenary system. At the model training level, adaptive loss-weight learning based on gradients requires repeated solution of high-dimensional quadratic optimization subproblems, resulting in excessive training complexity and computational cost. Therefore, this paper proposes a machine-vision-driven physics-informed neural network (VIPINN) for state detection and prediction of the pantograph–catenary system. First, event-stream images are regarded as heat sources, and spatiotemporal physical features are effectively extracted through frequency-domain Fourier transform and diffusion-process simulation, thereby enhancing the physical interpretability of visual embeddings. Then, Fourier neural operator and liquid time-constant network modules are combined to deeply explore system dynamics from the frequency domain and time domain, respectively, enabling comprehensive perception of multiscale nonlinear features. Finally, a random loss-weighted optimization strategy is proposed, which dynamically balances data loss, physical loss, and partial-derivative loss by randomly sampling mini-batch data and weights for each loss function. Without quadratic optimization, this strategy can avoid gradient conflicts and local minima, improving training efficiency and stability. Experimental results show that the proposed method significantly improves detection accuracy in pantograph–catenary system state detection and exhibits strong robustness, effectively addressing noise interference in complex environments and verifying the great potential of VIPINN methods in practical applications.

title: Understanding biases in machine learning-based strain predictions for fighter aircraft
abstract: The use of machine learning models for strain prediction in aircraft structural health monitoring has shown a considerable interest in recent years. The confidence we can place in these models however depends on our ability to understand when and why they can make biased predictions, which is particularly important in critical applications. In fatigue monitoring, such biases may shift the mean stress level of the reconstructed signal and therefore affect fatigue damage estimation. In this context, our work investigates the origin of systematic prediction biases observed when estimating strains from standard flight parameters on a fighter aircraft. Similar biases were already mentioned in the literature, but no in-depth study was dedicated to their analysis. About a hundred flights of a Rafale fighter aircraft was used for this study. An amount of 20 input variables was also used for strain predictions, some of them representing environmental measures and other ones the flight controls. Our study identifies the source of bias in three steps. It first shows that the biases are not due to model-specific limitations, but rather to the data and/or physics-driven mechanism. We then combine explainability tools with aeronautical expertise, which shows that the trained models over-emphasize inertial variables, which govern high-frequency strains, while variables describing the flight environment have substantially weaker influence. Building on this insight, we finally decompose the measured strains into inertial components and environmental baselines. Each part is predicted separately using exclusively physically relevant variables. Interestingly, only the environmental baseline carries the systematic bias, while the inertial part is reconstructed accurately. These findings demonstrate that bias originate from the environmental contribution of the strain signal, with temperature effects emerging as a plausible root cause. The study thus provides a principled diagnostic framework for identifying and interpreting bias mechanisms in data-driven structural monitoring.

title: Physics-guided safe collaboration: an uncertainty-gated heterogeneous semi-supervised regression framework for tool wear prediction
abstract: To address the dual challenges of labeled sample scarcity and poor physical interpretability in tool wear prediction, this paper proposes a Physics-Guided and Uncertainty-Gated Safe Collaboration Regression (PGS-CoReg) framework. This heterogeneous dual-branch design achieves closed-loop calibration between mechanism-driven and data-driven paradigms. Specifically, a Physics-Guided Gaussian Process Regression (PGGPR) embeds Zhu’s wear mechanism as a Bayesian prior to anchor global trends, employing combinational kernels to decouple non-stationary fluctuations. Concurrently, a Physics-Constrained Long Short-Term Memory (PG-LSTM) network introduces a multi-task loss with monotonicity and mechanism consistency constraints, ensuring predicted trajectories strictly adhere to thermodynamic laws. Crucially, the framework utilizes PGGPR’s posterior variance as a dynamic gate to filter pseudo-labels, effectively blocking error accumulation and logical drift. Experiments on the PHM 2010 dataset demonstrate that PGGPR and PG-LSTM reduce prediction errors by 10.0% and 18.2% against baselines. With only 20% labels, PGS-CoReg achieves an RMSE of 17.50 μm, surpassing the fully supervised LSTM baseline. Incorporating Non-IID heterogeneous data further reduces error by 19.6%, increasing the Confidence Interval Coverage Rate to 94.0%. Remarkably, cross-scenario validations on the NASA dataset confirm its robust sensor-agnostic transferability, effectively overcoming mathematically ill-posed early-stage extrapolation and massive blind-zone interpolation under severe domain shifts and extreme label scarcity (merely 3 labels). This study establishes a verifiable methodology for highly reliable predictive maintenance and tool health management in small-sample industrial scenarios.

title: Physics-guided neural network architectures for modeling nonlinear behaviors: Application to shape memory alloy wires
abstract: A novel physics-guided machine learning framework is proposed for the numerical simulation of complex nonlinear behaviors and to improve the generalization capability of data-driven models under limited information conditions. It combines an a priori physics-based model with a new neural network (NN) architecture designed to compensate for its inaccuracies. A differential evolution algorithm is adopted for the parametric identification of the physics-based model. On the other hand, an original transformer-based NN, enhanced with a long short-term memory (LSTM) feature fusion layer, is employed to capture the inherent aspects of the nonlinear behavior that are overlooked by the physics-based model so as to reduce overall errors.This approach is applied to simulate the hysteretic tensile behavior of NiTiNOL shape memory alloy wires subject to different loading rates. A comprehensive experimental comparative assessment is carried out between a physics-based (phenomenological) model and four NN architectures, including the uni- and bi-directional LSTM models, a transformer model, as well as the proposed model merging LSTM and transformer components. These NN architectures are employed both in a fully data-driven setting and within the physics-guided framework herein conceived with the purpose of mitigating the inaccuracies arising from the selected phenomenological model.The results indicate that the proposed NN architecture connecting LSTM and transformer components achieves the best overall performance. Furthermore, the physics-guided approach consistently improves both accuracy and reliability of the predictions.

title: Interpretable multiscale algorithm unrolling network using learnable Gabor filters for fault diagnosis
abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis has emerged as a pivotal research area in intelligent maintenance systems, stressing interpretable intelligence and trustworthy decision-making for reliable and safe engineering applications. To this end, this study proposes the Interpretable Multiscale AlGorithm unrolling Network using learnable Gabor filters (IMAG-Net). Specifically, IMAG-Net establishes a physically optimization-unrolling framework that integrates learnable Gabor filtering with multiscale convolutional sparse coding, embedding the sparsity prior of fault-induced into a trainable neural architecture for adaptive and interpretable fault diagnosis. Distinct from traditional deep learning approaches, the proposed framework enhances interpretability and decision transparency through structured convolutional sparse coding and adaptive multiscale decomposition, where Gabor filters with learnable center frequencies automatically capture dominant signal components that correspond to fault characteristic frequencies and their harmonics. To further ensure physical fidelity, the learned multiscale representations are analyzed alongside sparsity-guided signal reconstructions derived from salient sparse activations, thereby validating the reliability and internal consistency of the network’s decision logic. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a diagnostic accuracy exceeding 94% under high-noise conditions (σn=1.0), consistently outperforming conventional deep learning baselines while preserving physically meaningful and interpretable diagnostic representations.

title: A robust approach for vehicle load identification based on physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold network
abstract: Overloaded vehicles may induce fatigue damage and accelerate pavement deterioration, potentially leading to cracking and even catastrophic bridge failures. Vehicle load information is essential for bridge safety assessment and maintenance. The vehicle load can be inferred by the bridge influence lines (ILs), and the accuracy of vehicle load identification depends critically on the reliable extraction of ILs from measured bridge responses induced by a calibrated truck. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have been widely investigated to incorporate physical relationships between measured responses and ILs into the learning process, enabling vehicle load identification with limited data. Existing PINN-based methods typically rely on multilayer perceptron architectures with limited interpretability and insufficient capability for precisely representing ILs. Measurement noise, vehicle-bridge dynamic interaction effects, and incomplete calibration information can interfere with PINN-based IL identification, thereby undermining the accuracy of vehicle load estimation. This paper proposes a physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (PIKAN) for robust vehicle load identification. First, by embedding the physical relationships into the learning process, the proposed method enables the joint optimization of ILs and vehicle axle weights, even when partial axle weights of the calibration vehicle are unknown. Second, the PIKAN architecture enhances functional representation capability under noise and dynamic effects. Third, multi-location bridge response data are utilized to enhance the robustness and accuracy of vehicle load identification. A computational vehicle-bridge interactive model and a nine-span bridge are employed to assess the performance of the proposed method PIKAN for vehicle load identification. The results demonstrate that PIKAN achieves high accuracy and strong robustness in vehicle load identification.

title: Physics informed terahertz multi-label dual adversarial network for intelligent identification of composite overlapping defects under variable testing conditions
abstract: Composite overlapping defects, occurring between the interfaces in multilayer composite, bring great challenges for accurate structural integrity evaluation due to the complexity and unpredictability. Terahertz (THz) technique, as a novel nondestructive testing (NDT) method, has emerged great potentials for complex multilayer composites. However, current THz feature extraction methods, including physics-driven and pure data-driven methods, mainly focus on the identification of simple defect form, such as single non-overlapping defect, while ignoring the applicability of multiple overlapping defects. In addition, the variations of THz testing conditions can cause the variations of THz signals from the same sample, which will inevitably degrade the generalization performance of methods. Therefore, in this work, a physics informed THz multi-label dual adversarial network (PI-THzMDANet) is proposed for intelligent identification of composite overlapping defects under variable testing conditions. It includes a data alignment layer, a multi-label classification layer, and the dual adversarial network. Initially, the data alignment layer is constructed to align the different temporal THz signals in data space based on the transmission and variation characteristics of THz wave. Then, the multi-label classification layer with multi-attention class encoding module (MACE) is innovatively proposed to accommodate the output form of composite overlapping defects. Finally, the dual adversarial network, including the global and local adversarial learning processes, is proposed to improve the generalization performance of PI-THzMDANet under different THz testing conditions by aligning the source and target THz data in latent feature space. The experimental results indicate that the effectiveness of proposed PI-THzMDANet for intelligent identification of composite overlapping defects under variable testing conditions, which provides a novel paradigm for the structural integrity evaluation of complex defect forms in multilayer composites in THz NDT.

title: Conditional diffusion-based time–frequency data augmentation with multi-scale coordinate attention for diesel engine fault diagnosis
abstract: Diesel engine vibration signals are characterized by multi-source impulsive excitations and strong non-stationarity. The scarcity of fault samples and severe class imbalance make it difficult for existing generative models to simultaneously achieve high generation quality and effective diagnostic improvement after augmentation, and often lead to attenuation of mid- and high-frequency textures as well as over-smoothed edges in generated time–frequency images. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multi-scale time–frequency coordinate-attention conditional diffusion model (MSTFCA-CDM) for fault time–frequency sample augmentation in diesel engines. Continuous wavelet transform (CWT) time–frequency images are used as the generation target, and a multi-scale time–frequency coordinate-attention module is embedded into the conditional diffusion framework to enhance the representation of impulsive structures at different scales and critical time–frequency regions. In addition, a frequency-domain consistency loss is introduced to constrain the two-dimensional spectral magnitude distributions of the predicted and true noise, thereby improving the recovery of mid- and high-frequency textures and local edge details. Experiments on the TBD234 diesel engine dataset show that the proposed method achieves better performance than the compared methods in terms of generation quality, distribution consistency, and augmentation-assisted diagnostic performance within the investigated experimental setting. When the sample ratio between the normal class and each fault class is gradually balanced from 20:1 to 1:1, the classification accuracy improves from 58.34% to 98.90%. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of multi-scale modeling, coordinate attention, and frequency-domain consistency constraints. The results suggest that MSTFCA-CDM is effective for fault time–frequency sample augmentation and diagnosis under severe class imbalance in a controlled experimental setting.

title: Hybrid Kalman filter and physics-informed long short-term memory network for enhanced fault diagnosis of aircraft angle-of-attack sensors
abstract: Angle-of-attack (AoA) sensor faults have historically contributed to several aviation accidents. To address this issue, a sensor fusion-based fault diagnosis framework is introduced that integrates first principles of physics with sensor data. A reduced-order aircraft model that incorporates sensor biases and gains is first developed using first principles of physics. This model is used to propose a two-stage fault detection scheme: an extended Kalman filter (EKF) innovation monitoring with covariance regularization (IMCR) for initial fault detection and Euclidean bias/gain deviations (EBGD) for fault confirmation. A physics-informed long short-term memory (PILSTM) network is then trained as a virtual sensor for use in the case of dual AoA faults. Finally, a fault mitigation method is developed to determine the appropriate actions in the event of a fault. It uses the IMCR-EBGD fault detection, aircraft sensor redundancy, and the PILSTM virtual sensor. The full framework is validated using flight data from the Advanced Technologies Testing Aircraft System (ATTAS) under both fault-free and fault-injected conditions. The proposed method detects ramp-type AoA faults within 0.18 s and yields a lower 95% Clopper–Pearson false alarm upper bound under fault-free scenarios. A sensitivity analysis incorporating Gaussian noise shows the proposed method achieves a lower false alarm rate. Furthermore, under the dual AoA fault test, the best estimation performance was obtained when the PILSTM loss function included a 15% contribution from the physics-informed loss function. These results demonstrate that hybridizing data-driven learning with first principles of physics improves fault diagnosis in complex sensor environments.

title: Physics-informed stereo vision for structural displacement measurement with uncertainty quantification
abstract: Accurate displacement measurement with uncertainty quantification is essential for structural vibration testing and health monitoring. However, existing vision-based methods process frames independently without leveraging structural dynamics knowledge, limiting computational efficiency and robustness under challenging conditions. This paper proposes a Physics-Informed DIC framework integrated with Stereo Vision and Temporal filtering (PI-DIC-SVT) that reformulates vision-based displacement measurement as a physics-constrained Bayesian state estimation problem. Three key contributions are presented: (1) a physics-guided search constraint that leverages Extended Kalman Filter predictions to adaptively reduce the search range from ± 30 pixels to approximately ± 10 pixels, achieving 2.5–3.0 × computational speedup; (2) a quality-adaptive Bayesian fusion mechanism that ensures robust tracking under adverse imaging conditions; and (3) a multi-source uncertainty quantification framework that decomposes measurement uncertainty into physically interpretable components. The method was validated through shaking table experiments under sinusoidal and seismic excitations. Results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves sub-millimeter accuracy (RMSE of 0.31 mm) that remains below 0.5 mm even under ± 50% natural frequency mismatch, while providing reliable uncertainty estimates with 94.3% coverage rate for 95% confidence intervals.

title: A physics-informed dual-stream convolutional neural network method for in-situ continuous bolt preload monitoring and detection
abstract: Accurate perception of bolt preload is crucial for ensuring the reliability and safety of critical equipment such as aero-engines, high-speed trains, and wind turbines. To address the limitations of existing data-driven methods, including poor interpretability, heavy reliance on labeled data, and weak out-of-distribution generalization, this paper proposes a Physics-informed Dual-stream Convolutional Neural Network (PI-CNN) method for bolt preload detection. The core of the method lies in embedding the experimentally verified linear physical relationship between the square of natural frequency of bolt vibration and the preload into the neural network training process in the form of a gradient consistency loss. The model adopts a dual-channel 1D-CNN architecture to extract features from the raw vibration acceleration signals and their frequency spectra separately. It then incorporates handcrafted feature, specifically the squared natural frequency, to construct a data-physics dual-driven loss function. This design constrains the model predictions not only to fit the data but also to strictly adhere to known physical law, thereby significantly enhancing the physical interpretability of the model. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method, guided by physical principles, markedly improves model interpretability, reduces dependency on labeled data, and enhances generalization performance under unseen working conditions, offering an efficient data-physics dual-driven solution for bolt preload detection.

title: Adaptive and robust motor intent decoding for cross-day dexterous finger force predictions
abstract: Motor intent decoding based on neural signals provides a promising pathway for intuitive human-robot interactions. Among various neural signal sources, binary spiking activities of motor units (MUs) serve as a reliable basis for intent decoding. However, the non-stationary nature of MU action potential poses a major challenge for robust intent decoding. To address this issue, we developed an adaptive motor intent decoding framework that dynamically refined the MU pool to maintain cross-day reliability. The framework integrated three modules: (1) a cross-validation component for selecting MUs with consistent decoding performance across days, (2) a flag policy to exclude inactive and inaccurate MUs based on temporal activation consistency, and (3) a refinement component to retain only finger-specific MUs that can lead to accurate individual finger force predictions. We validated our new approach by quantifying finger force performance. We obtained high-density surface electromyographic (sEMG) recordings over three days. We then performed adaptive source separation to extract neuronal firing spikes for subsequent motor intent decoding. We also demonstrated the feasibility of our approach during real-time control of a robotic finger. The results demonstrate that our developed adaptive motor intent decoder consistently achieved higher prediction accuracy across multiple days than the non-adaptive decomposition method. Compared with deep learning approaches, our approach outperformed Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), while achieving comparable performance to CNN-Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) across days. These findings highlight the robustness of MU-level adaptive motor intent decoding in overcoming cross-day neural signal variations, thereby contributing to the development of accurate and robust signal processing strategies for reliable and practical applications in human-robot interactions.

title: Noise-firewall: mitigating pseudo-label poisoning in semi-supervised fault diagnosis via parameter decoupling
abstract: Data-driven fault diagnosis in industrial settings faces the dual challenges of scarce supervision and label noise. Although semi-supervised learning (SSL) can leverage unlabeled data, it becomes fragile under label noise because corrupted supervision distorts representation learning and subsequently contaminates pseudo-labels, causing confirmation bias and error propagation. To mitigate this issue, this paper proposes a Noise-Firewall framework that couples robust representation learning with SSL via additive parameter decomposition (ω=σ + γ) and dynamic regularization. The σ-branch is encouraged to learn stable fault representations, while the auxiliary γ-branch absorbs noise-induced optimization pressure, thereby structurally shielding σ from corrupted labels. Built upon the protected σ-branch, Confidence-Aware Pseudo-Labeling (CAPL) is further developed: pseudo-labels are generated strictly from σ predictions, and the γ-branch is frozen during pseudo-label backpropagation to prevent pseudo-label poisoning. Extensive experiments under multiple noise types (20%/40%) and up to 40% unlabeled data on two public benchmarks—Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) and Paderborn University (PU)—validate the mechanism and stability of the proposed components, and further perform systematic comparisons with representative SSL methods on a real robotic belt-grinding dataset. For example, on CWRU with 40% symmetric noise, accuracy improves from 61.8 ± 6.9 to 78.6 ± 1.1; under the joint setting of 40% symmetric noise with 40% unlabeled data, PU and the robotic dataset reach 93.15% and 90.2% accuracy, respectively. Finally, γ is discarded at inference, enabling a “train-complex, infer-simple” deployment with no additional inference overhead.

title: A domain knowledge informed approach for anomaly detection of electric vehicle interior sounds
abstract: The detection of anomalies in automotive cabin sounds is critical for ensuring vehicle quality and maintaining passenger comfort. In many real-world settings, this task is more appropriately framed as an unsupervised learning problem rather than the supervised case due to the scarcity or complete absence of labeled faulty data. In such an unsupervised setting, the model is trained exclusively on healthy samples and detects anomalies as deviations from normal behavior. However, in the absence of labeled faulty samples for validation and the limited reliability of commonly used metrics, such as validation reconstruction error, effective model selection remains a significant challenge. To overcome these limitations, a domain-knowledge-informed approach for model selection is proposed, in which proxy-anomalies engineered through structured perturbations of healthy spectrograms are used in the validation set to support model selection. The proposed methodology is evaluated on a high-fidelity electric vehicle dataset comprising healthy and faulty cabin sounds across five representative fault types viz., Imbalance, Modulation, Whine, Wind, and Pulse Width Modulation. This dataset, generated using advanced sound synthesis techniques, and validated via expert jury assessments, has been made publicly available to facilitate further research. Experimental evaluations on the five fault cases demonstrate the selection of optimal models using proxy-anomalies, significantly outperform conventional model selection strategies.

title: Towards a more realistic evaluation of machine learning models for bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Reliable detection of bearing faults is essential for maintaining the safety and operational efficiency of rotating machinery. While recent advances in machine learning (ML), particularly deep learning, have shown strong performance in controlled settings, many studies fail to generalize to real-world applications due to methodological flaws, most notably data leakage. This paper investigates the issue of data leakage in vibration-based bearing fault diagnosis and its impact on model evaluation. We demonstrate that common dataset partitioning strategies, such as segment-wise and condition-wise splits, introduce spurious correlations that inflate performance metrics. To address this, we propose a rigorous, leakage-free evaluation methodology centered on bearing-wise data partitioning, ensuring no overlap between the physical components used for training and testing. Additionally, we reformulate the classification task as a multi-label problem, enabling the detection of co-occurring fault types and the use of prevalence-independent metrics based on the ROC curve. Beyond preventing leakage, we also examine the effect of dataset diversity on generalization, showing that the number of unique training bearings is a decisive factor for achieving robust performance. We evaluate our methodology on four widely adopted datasets: Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), Paderborn University (PU), University of Ottawa (UORED-VAFCLS) and Hanoi University of Science and Technology (HUST bearing). This study highlights the importance of leakage-aware evaluation protocols and provides practical guidelines for dataset partitioning, model selection, and validation, fostering the development of more trustworthy ML systems for industrial fault diagnosis applications.

title: A hybrid deep learning framework for reliable and interpretable remaining life estimation in turbofan Engines: Focusing on Robustness, Generalization, and Sensor-Level interpretability
abstract: Reliable prediction of Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is crucial for improving maintenance planning and operational safety in turbofan engines. This study proposes a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network–Gated Recurrent Unit (CNN–GRU) framework for prognostic analysis using the NASA C-MAPSS benchmark dataset. The CNN layers are employed to extract local degradation-related features from multivariate sensor measurements, while the GRU structure captures temporal degradation trends over long operational sequences. Beyond conventional accuracy-focused evaluations, the proposed framework emphasizes robustness, reproducibility, and interpretability through a reliability-oriented experimental strategy. Comparative analyses were conducted against standalone CNN and GRU models together with component-level ablation experiments and repeated training runs to assess statistical stability. In addition, SHAP and LIME methods were utilized to provide global and local explanations of model behavior and sensor importance. Experimental validation across FD001–FD004 subsets demonstrates that the hybrid CNN–GRU model achieves competitive prediction accuracy with improved consistency under varying operating conditions and fault scenarios. The explainability analysis further reveals strong dependence on degradation-sensitive thermodynamic sensor signals. Overall, the proposed framework offers an interpretable and reproducible deep learning approach for benchmark aero-engine RUL prediction while also acknowledging limitations related to real-world industrial deployment.

title: Physics-inspired multiwavelet KAN for interpretable bearing fault diagnosis under harsh operating conditions
abstract: Deep learning models for rotating machinery diagnosis often lack interpretability and suffer severe performance degradation under strong noise. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Physics-Inspired Multiwavelet Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) for robust and transparent bearing fault diagnosis. Building upon the Wav-KAN architecture, we develop a parallel multiwavelet expert framework utilizing Morlet, Laplace, and Mexhat activations to structurally capture complementary fault signatures. An adaptive evidence-weighting fusion mechanism is further introduced to dynamically balance expert contributions based on input signal characteristics. Extensive experiments across three bearing datasets, including a complex turbopump test rig, demonstrate the framework’s superior noise robustness. Notably, it achieves 92.05% accuracy on the PU dataset under severe −10 dB noise, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art deep learning, wavelet-based, and single-wavelet KAN baselines. Further analyses show that the learned wavelet scales remain close to theory-derived characteristic scales, that fusion weights vary across fault categories, and that decision attribution focuses on localized fault-related signal regions, providing supportive evidence for the interpretability of the proposed framework.

title: A noise-corrected data-driven approach for nonlinear dynamical system modeling in frequency domain
abstract: The development of parsimonious and accurate models is highly dependent on the quality of training data. To extract the underlying physical laws from noisy data, we introduce a noise-corrected data-driven approach. It begins by formulating a nonlinear sparse least-squares problem in the frequency domain, where noise correction terms and physical parameters are treated as unknowns. To solve this problem, we present a novel nested Levenberg-Marquardt (LM)-Sequential Thresholded Least-Squares (STLS) approach, which inherits the strengths of LM algorithm for solving nonlinear optimization problems and the sparsity-promoting capabilities of the STLS. This approach also offers a simple and intuitive way to incorporate prior physical knowledge into the sparsification process, preventing small coefficient terms from being pruned due to excessively large thresholds. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated by both numerical simulations and experimental tests. The results indicate its effectiveness in extracting underlying dynamic structures from measured data, which might be corrupted not only by white noise but also by distorted streaming.

title: An improved unsupervised domain adversarial transfer network for motor eccentricity monitoring assisted by simulation data
abstract: Rotor eccentricity in motors frequently leads to severe vibration. Although deep learning algorithms provide an effective approach for monitoring eccentricity conditions, labeled data for such faults is typically scarce in real-world industrial settings. To address this, we propose a novel unsupervised domain adversarial transfer network, assisted by simulation data, for monitoring motor eccentricity. First, a multiphysics-coupled model integrating electromagnetics and stator structure is established to simulate the vibration response of the stator casing under different rotor eccentricity conditions, thereby generating a simulated dataset with varying eccentricity levels. Then, an electromagnetic–mechanical excitation separation test device is designed to validate the multiphysics model through modal testing. Next, an adaptive wavelet image style transfer network is employed to migrate the “style” of the time–frequency images from the experimental data to those of the simulated data, enhancing their similarity in the time–frequency domain. Finally, the stylized simulated images serve as the source domain, while the unlabeled experimental images constitute the target domain. Within the framework of a domain adversarial neural network (DANN), joint distribution adaptation (JDA) and conditional contrastive domain (CCD) adaptation loss functions are incorporated to jointly optimize the model. Experimental results on the electromagnetic–mechanical excitation separation device demonstrate that the proposed method effectively detects the degree of rotor eccentricity.
