title: Bayesian learning in structural dynamics: a comprehensive review and emerging trends
abstract: Bayesian learning has emerged as a compelling and vital research direction in the field of structural dynamics, offering a probabilistic lens to understand and refine the analysis of complex dynamical systems. This review meticulously traces the three-decade evolution of Bayesian learning in structural dynamics, illuminating core principles, groundbreaking methodologies, and diverse applications that have significantly influenced the field. The narrative commences by delving into the basics of Bayesian theory, clarifying essential concepts, and introducing primary methods for deriving posterior distributions, with an in-depth exploration of three types: Laplace approximation, stochastic sampling, and variational inference. Subsequently, the text explores the implementation of two types of Bayesian learning in structural dynamics: physical model learning and data-centric statistical model learning. Physical model learning emphasizes inferring physical model parameters within a Bayesian framework for system identification and prediction, while statistical model learning integrates Bayesian learning methodologies into data-centric statistical modeling within probabilistic machine learning. Both types resonate across various applications, such as modal analysis, model updating, damage detection, and reliability updating, highlighting their pivotal role in enhancing comprehension of dynamical systems and decision-making. The paper also navigates obstacles by proposing ways to enhance existing Bayesian inference strategies. Distinguished from previous research, this study offers a thorough examination of both traditional and cutting-edge Bayesian methods. It not only underscores the transformative influence of Bayesian approaches but also serves as a beacon, guiding researchers in the judicious selection and refinement of suitable methods for various challenges in structural dynamics.

title: Stiffness-constrained bandgap tailoring in sinusoidal compression-torsion metamaterials: inverse design and MIGA-PINN optimization
abstract: Effectively attenuating low-to-mid-frequency vibrations while maintaining load-bearing stiffness remains a critical engineering challenge. This study introduces a novel sinusoidal compression-torsion coupling metamaterial, whose vibration bandgap characteristics and mechanical stiffness can be synergistically tailored. Analytical models for stiffness and bandgap boundary frequencies are derived theoretically to provide physical constraints for a physics-informed neural network (PINN)-based forward model. Conversely, a neural network (NN)-based inverse model maps target mechanical properties back to unit cell geometric parameters. Subsequently, a Multi-Island Genetic Algorithm (MIGA)-PINN optimization strategy is implemented to tailor vibration bandgaps to target ranges while satisfying stiffness constraints. The optimization targets include: (1) minimizing the onset frequency of the first bandgap; (2) minimizing the interval between the first two bandgaps; (3) maximizing the bandgap width; and (4) customizing bandgap ranges. Experimental and numerical validations demonstrate the efficacy of both the forward-inverse design and the MIGA-PINN optimization strategy, with predictions showing strong agreement with experimental and simulation data. Notably, an optimized metamaterial subject to a stiffness constraint of 5000 N/m achieves stable vibration attenuation across the 100–1000 Hz range. These findings demonstrate the targeted vibration control capabilities of the metamaterials under stiffness constraints and provide a computationally efficient approach for their rational designs.

title: Research on generative diffusion-based over-threshold restoration for oil and gas pipeline signals
abstract: Oil and gas pipeline detection signals are critical for pipeline defect diagnosis and assessment. However, during field signal acquisition, complex operating conditions, harsh detection environments, and inherent limitations of detector response and signal conversion may lead to over-threshold distortion in pipeline signals. Since the true complete defect distribution of field distorted signals is inaccessible, traditional supervised deep learning methods face limitations in constructing paired distorted-clean training samples. To address this problem, this study proposes an Over-Threshold Distortion Restoration (OTDR) method based on the diffusion probabilistic principle. OTDR adopts unsupervised forward diffusion training to learn the feature distribution of normal pipeline defect signals and incorporates a progressively guided restoration mode with a dynamic resampling mechanism to reconstruct over-threshold distorted regions during reverse diffusion. Case validations indicate that OTDR can reconstruct the main morphological structures, local details, and statistical feature distributions of field distorted signals. In the quantitative tests based on simulated distortion conditions, the restoration results achieve an average MAE of 0.045. The effects of different resampling strategies, prediction models, and diffusion strategies on restoration performance are further analyzed, and failure-case analysis is conducted under constructed extreme distortion conditions. Overall, the experimental results suggest that OTDR provides a feasible generative diffusion restoration mode for over-threshold distorted signals in oil and gas pipeline detection.

title: Remaining useful life estimation of ball-screw feed drives using a nonlinear digital twin and PINN–AIDB framework
abstract: Ball-screw feed drives (BSFDs) govern positioning accuracy and operational availability in computer numerical control (CNC) machine tools, yet reliable remaining useful life (RUL) estimation remains challenging owing to constrained controller sensing and complex electromechanical interactions. This study presents a real-time RUL estimation framework operating exclusively on controller-resident OPC–UA telemetry, without auxiliary vibration instrumentation. A validated nonlinear digital twin, confirmed at 0.020%–0.026% stroke error under pseudo-random binary sequence (PRBS) excitation, provides surrogates for frictional dissipation and torsional microslip, defining a physics-derived degradation driver Φ(t). This driver regularises a compact physics-informed neural network fused with an anchor-informed degradation baseline (PINN–AIDB). The framework incorporates residual ODE constraints, monotonicity enforcement, and anchor consistency, whereas the Weibull model serves as a transparent statistical baseline. Pre- and post-accelerated life test (ALT) states calibrate an acceleration factor AF∗≈82.6 that maps laboratory exposure to an equivalent field horizon of approximately 8260h, consistent with catalogue-referenced BSFD fatigue lives. Validation under no-load and loaded conditions (0kg to 150kg, 5000 to 20 000 mm/min) confirms severity-consistent RUL compression across a 249h range (≈3% of nominal lifetime). The proposed PINN–AIDB projects the field horizon with a deviation of 11h from the catalogue-anchored reference, a 90% confidence-interval width of 211h, and 100% threshold-crossing feasibility, while reducing feedrate-order monotonicity violations from five (baseline estimators) to one across all 16 operating conditions. Ablation confirms that Φ(t), monotonicity enforcement, and anchor constraints address complementary identifiability limitations under controller-resident sensing without auxiliary condition-monitoring hardware.

title: Multimodal spatiotemporal graph attention network with uncertainty quantification for aircraft engine prognostics
abstract: Aircraft engine prognostics is critical for safety, cost reduction, and efficient fleet management. Despite the availability of rich multimodal sensor data, most current prognostic approaches are limited to single-modality analysis, lack uncertainty quantification, and rely on predefined sensor graphs. To address these limitations, this paper introduces the Multimodal Spatiotemporal Graph Attention Network with Uncertainty Quantification (MST-GAT-UQ), a novel deep learning framework for aircraft engine prognostics. The proposed model integrates temporal patterns via CNN-LSTM networks, spatial correlations through graph attention mechanisms, and frequency signatures using Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) with 2D CNN processing. Key innovations include a correlation-driven graph construction method that automatically learns sensor relationships from operational data, hierarchical attention fusion to adaptively weight different modalities, and Monte Carlo dropout augmented by temperature scaling for simultaneous Remaining Useful Life (RUL) and health state prediction with calibrated uncertainty intervals. The framework is comprehensively validated on a real-world operational dataset comprising 84 sensors and 43,492 samples from F100-PW-229 turbofan engines, achieving R 2 = 0.911, RMSE = 0.087, MAE = 0.072 on a normalized RUL scale within a synthetic-label verification framework (no ground-truth operational RUL is available for this dataset; reported metrics quantify the model’s fidelity in reproducing a synthetically imposed linear degradation trajectory and should not be interpreted as ground-truth remaining-life predictions), and a synthetic health-state replication accuracy of 99.5% (auxiliary task; health-state labels are a deterministic step-function of the synthetic RUL signal and carry no independent diagnostic information). Comparative analysis against the standard NASA C-MAPSS benchmark is presented as a zero-shot domain-transfer diagnostic, characterising the label-distribution shift between the two datasets, and confirms that native C-MAPSS training yields positive R 2 across all four subsets (FD001–FD004: R 2 = 0.607–0.863). This work represents a significant step toward reliable, uncertainty-aware, and multimodal prognostic systems for safety–critical aviation applications, with uncertainty intervals that are directionally informative but moderately overconfident (empirical coverage 88.7% at the 95% nominal level; ECE = 0.254), indicating that further calibration refinement is required before safety–critical operational deployment.

title: Kalman filter-aided vision transformer for seismic deformation measurement of self-centering structures
abstract: Accurate, long-duration, and marker-free measurement of seismic deformation is critical for evaluating the performance of self-centering structures. Conventional contact sensors offer limited spatial coverage and are challenging to deploy, while vision-based tracking is susceptible to baseline instability and jitter, especially under small, cyclic, and non-monotonic joint opening responses. This study proposes KF-STARK, a Kalman filter-aided vision-transformer tracking framework for self-correcting, non-contact deformation measurement. By coupling transformer-based template–search region matching with Kalman filter-based state estimation, KF-STARK enforces motion continuity, stabilizes the measurement baseline, and suppresses transient tracking errors and jitter, with negligible computational overhead. Validated through pseudo-dynamic tests on T-shaped and cruciform self-centering frame joints subjected to eight earthquake-like excitations, KF-STARK achieves a maximum normalized root mean square error of 3.08% for column-top displacement, 7.80% for joint opening displacement, and 4.41% for joint opening rotation, compared to sensor-based reference measurements. It reduces tracking jitter by more than 40%, supports marker-free tracking on natural targets, maintains accurate global displacement tracking under random frame drops, and enables real-time processing of 4096 × 3000-pixel image sequences, demonstrating its effectiveness as a vision-based deformation measurement framework.

title: A semi-supervised tool wear monitoring approach integrating physics-guided weak labels and uncertainty quantification
abstract: Driven by the Industry 5.0 paradigm, tool wear monitoring has become essential for ensuring machining quality and production efficiency. However, the supervision asymmetry between readily available sensor signals and scarce labeled data hampers the industrial deployment of monitoring models. To address this issue, a physics-guided semi-supervised learning method with uncertainty quantification is proposed. First, multi-source heterogeneous features that characterize local cutting dynamics and historical degradation information are constructed via adaptive feature filtering. Second, the improved parallel symbolic regression learns trend-constrained symbolic degradation mappings and generates physics-guided weak labels that are consistent with the irreversible evolution of tool wear, thereby alleviating the supervision bottleneck caused by insufficient true labels. Subsequently, a staged conformal prediction strategy quantifies stage-related uncertainty of weak labels and constructs adaptive loss weights to reduce the interference of low-reliability weak labels during model training. Finally, a physics-guided cross-attention fusion module is designed to leverage degradation trend information as guidance for adaptive interactions among heterogeneous features, while a raw-feature bypass is introduced to preserve data-driven information and reduce the risk of negative transfer caused by local weak-label bias. Ablation studies confirm the advantages of the proposed method in preserving trend smoothness, suppressing heteroscedastic noise, and improving late-stage identification accuracy. Compared with the best-performing baseline, the proposed method reduces RMSE and MAE by 14.2 % and 10.9 %, respectively, while R2 increases by 1.2 %. Further validation shows that the proposed method can robustly adapt to different cutting conditions. Meanwhile, its lightweight online inference architecture enables deployment on resource-constrained industrial edge devices.

title: A data-driven digital twin update technology based on an invertible attention-enhanced conditional invertible neural network
abstract: The fidelity of a digital twin is maintained by continuously updating the models embedded in its virtual entity with real-time sensor data. Conditional invertible neural networks (cINNs) offer a promising data-driven approach for likelihood-free model updating. However, they struggle to capture strong couplings among model parameters and often fail to effectively use suboptimal or limited sensor measurements. Additionally, epistemic uncertainty cannot be rigorously quantified in standard cINNs. To address these issues, an invertible attention-enhanced cINN (IA-cINN) is proposed. A novel invertible attention layer is integrated into the architecture. This layer explicitly models intrinsic correlations among model parameters and cross-dependencies between parameters and measurements through self- and cross-attention mechanisms while rigorously preserving invertibility. Monte Carlo dropout is incorporated into the IA-cINN to quantify epistemic uncertainty. The method was validated on two engineering cases. In a simulated case of a material handling device, three material parameters of structural components were updated using only strain and deformation measurements. In an experimental bearing case, contact stiffness, defect length, and radial clearance were updated using vibration features. In both cases, the IA-cINN outperformed the conventional cINN, as well as a Bayesian updating method based on Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling. The IA-cINN achieved significantly higher updating accuracy, especially for parameters that exhibited complex coupling relationships with others. It produced more reliable uncertainty intervals in both cases, as indicated by lower interval scores. These intervals were shown to be sensitive to key sources of epistemic uncertainty, including data scarcity and insufficient model learning.

title: Continuously updatable temperature-displacement hybrid neural network model for tracking performance degradation of expansion joints in long-span bridges
abstract: The neural network models driven by long-term monitoring data of structural temperature and thermal displacement in expansion joints are commonly employed to understand the operational condition of expansion joints in long-span bridges. But the continuous performance deterioration of expansion joints during the long-term operational period would change the temperature-displacement relationship and reduce the reliability of the corresponding neural network model. This paper presents a continuously updatable temperature-displacement hybrid neural network model for tracking the time-dependent performance degradation of expansion joints. First, a multi-domain feature fusion model fusing time-domain, difference-domain and spatial-domain features of long-term monitoring data is proposed by integrating a bidirectional long-short term memory network, an encoder-decoder, and a graph convolutional network to describe the complicated temperature-displacement relationship of expansion joints. Then, a model update method based on residual guidance and knowledge distillation was developed to continuously update the multi-domain feature fusion model so that the model could adapt to the degraded condition of expansion joints. Finally, long-term monitoring data from a long-span cable-stayed bridge is adopted as a case study to examine the accuracy of the proposed multi-domain feature fusion model and the effectiveness of the developed model updating method. The results indicate that the multi-domain feature fusion model has the capability of accurately capturing the historical temperature-displacement relationship embedded in expansion joints. The model updating method enables efficient and continuous updating of the temperature-displacement neural network, and the updated model can accurately track the performance degradation of expansion joints.

title: Physics-informed identification of stochastic vibration for the bearing-rotor system
abstract: Uncertainty quantification and prediction of vibration characteristics in bearing-rotor systems constitute critical challenges in energy, marine, and aerospace engineering applications. In this regard, a physics-informed fusion approach is presented for stochastic vibration identification in bearing-rotor systems by integrating a virtual physical model with multi-source heterogeneous information. The proposed virtual bearing-rotor model incorporates multi-physics coupled interactions among transient temperature, lubrication, and vibration. Meanwhile, an adaptive strategy for acquiring high-quality information is developed. Multi-source heterogeneous prior statistical information for the bearing-rotor system is established based on expert knowledge and high-quality data. The initial configuration of the bearing-rotor system is inversely identified by integrating Bayesian inference with transient thermal information. Subsequently, the stochastic vibration of the bearing-rotor system is characterized in terms of inverse identification results. Eventually, the inverse inference and stochastic vibration identification capabilities of the physics-informed fusion framework are experimentally validated. The proposed physics-informed fusion approach provides theoretical guidance for cross-physical field inference from temperature to vibrations in aero-engine, marine propulsion, and wind turbine rotor systems.

title: PIDUQ: an interpretable physics-informed distribution uncertainty quantification network for unsupervised cross-domain fault diagnosis of rolling bearings
abstract: In practical industrial scenarios, distribution shifts induced by varying operating conditions severely hinder the accuracy and reliability of cross-domain fault diagnosis for rolling bearings. Moreover, existing domain adaptation methods generally lack interpretability and still face challenges in handling unreliable pseudo-labels in the target domain. To address these issues, a novel Physics-Informed Distribution Uncertainty Quantification network (PIDUQ) is proposed. First, a Physics-Constrained Differentiable Convolution (PCDConv) module is constructed to replace the conventional first-layer convolution. Through parameterized modeling and physics-based regularization, PCDConv reconfigures convolutional kernels into learnable band-pass filter banks, enabling the network to adaptively focus on fault-induced resonance frequency bands and thereby enhancing the physical consistency and noise robustness of feature extraction. Subsequently, the Uncertainty-guided Local Maximum Mean Discrepancy (ULMMD) metric is introduced. By jointly quantifying prediction reliability using normalized entropy and confidence margins, ULMMD employs a dynamic reweighting strategy to suppress the interference of highly uncertain samples during subdomain alignment, thereby alleviating negative transfer and refining decision boundaries. Extensive experiments are conducted on the Paderborn University and Mechanical Fault Simulation datasets. The results show that PIDUQ achieves accuracies of 95.15%-98.27% on the PU dataset and an average accuracy of 89.87% on co-located transfer tasks of the MFS dataset, while maintaining superior performance under multi-speed, cross-location, and compound fault scenarios. Furthermore, visualized filter responses validate the capability of the proposed method to capture physical information. Code is available at GitHub.

title: ToolMamba: a physics-informed framework for interpretable tool condition monitoring under various machining conditions
abstract: Although data-driven tool condition monitoring (TCM) has demonstrated promising results, its generalization across different tools and varying machining conditions remains a critical challenge. To address this issue, this study proposes a physics-informed tool condition monitoring framework for cross-tool and cross-machine applications. First, sensitive features are selected based on the Altintas cutting-force model and tree-based SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to quantify feature importance, yielding a compact set of physically interpretable features. Then, a physics-informed framework, ToolMamba, is developed by integrating convolutional layers with a structured state-space sequence model to capture temporal dependencies from machining signals, augmented with physics-informed loss functions that enforce monotonicity and boundary constraints consistent with irreversible wear progression. Finally, Meta-learning with Stochastic Gradient Descent (Meta-SGD) is employed to adapt the model across different tool and machine domains with minimal retraining. Experimental validation on the PHM 2010 benchmark dataset yields an RMSE of 2.268 μm and MAE of 1.514 μm, representing a reduction of over 53% in RMSE compared to the best-performing baseline. Cross-tool transfer achieves R2 > 0.93 across all tested tools on both PHM 2010 and HMoTP 2024 datasets, and cross-machine transfer to a local milling dataset attains R2 = 0.938 on the best-aligned target tool. The proposed framework offers a robust, interpretable, and transferable solution for tool condition monitoring under various machining conditions.

title: A Time-Frequency Fusion Spiking Neural Network for Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Learnable Neuronal Dynamics
abstract: Bearing fault diagnosis under varying operating conditions often suffers from insufficient feature representation and unstable performance. Many existing spiking neural network (SNN)-based methods use fixed neuronal dynamic parameters, which may limit their ability to accommodate operating-condition variations. Moreover, some diagnostic frameworks construct two-dimensional time-frequency representations before model training, introducing an additional offline transformation stage. In addition, some SNN-based diagnostic frameworks place less emphasis on explicit frequency-domain information. To address these issues, this paper proposes a time-frequency fusion SNN for bearing fault diagnosis based on learnable neuronal dynamics. First, one-dimensional vibration segments are replicated across four simulation time steps, and spectral information is modeled by an embedded Sinc-based branch. Then, temporal features and frequency-domain information are fused within a unified SNN framework, where learnable neuronal dynamics adjust temporal integration and spike-generation behavior during training to better match vibration patterns at different temporal scales. Experiments on the MFPT and JNU datasets show that the proposed model achieves accuracies of 98.33% and 99.33%, respectively, demonstrating competitive diagnostic performance.

title: End-to-end prediction and inverse identification of gear grinding and EOL performance based on physics-informed neural networks
abstract: Existing open-loop quality control paradigms and traditional dynamic models are inadequate for actively suppressing high-frequency whine and ghost noise in electric vehicle (EV) gears, primarily due to unmodeled boundary uncertainties and time-varying transfer functions. Furthermore, purely data-driven methods are inherently constrained by causal feature leakage and insufficient out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization capabilities. To overcome these fundamental bottlenecks, this paper proposes an end-to-end differentiable gray-box framework based on physics-informed integration, which rigorously decouples the forward physical deduction process from the inverse parameter identification process. During the forward prediction phase, the compensation network (NNgrind) exclusively processes remote machine tool vibrations to reconstruct the microscopic three-dimensional (3D) surface waviness. Facilitated by a differentiable smooth relaxation operator, the inverted waviness formulation subsequently drives a 16-degree-of-freedom (16-DOF) gearbox ordinary differential equation (ODE) model. Concurrently, the state-dependent neural operator (NNdyn) strictly extracts transient physical states (i.e., displacement and velocity) to autonomously compensate for nonlinear dynamic residuals, thereby mathematically mitigating the computational overhead and convergence instabilities associated with implicit algebraic loops.During the inverse identification phase, empirical end-of-line (EOL) vibration data serves uniquely as the ground-truth supervision label. Driven by automatic differentiation, the spectrum error gradient backpropagates directly through the ODE solver, achieving the closed-loop calibration of the dual operators with zero causal feature leakage. Blind bench test validations demonstrate that the predicted vibration root mean square error (RMSE) is reduced to 0.052 g. Crucially, this framework strictly complies with cross-axis kinematic conversion laws, precisely resolving the mapping of non-integer ghost frequencies (e.g., accurately tracing a 3.1st-order machine tool excitation to a 26.87th-order macroscopic response on the input shaft). Finally, process sensitivity analysis confirms that actively reshaping the waviness topology can sever its geometric coupling with the line of action, thereby suppressing the ghost noise amplitude by up to 79% directly at the manufacturing source.

title: A unified framework for equation discovery and dynamic prediction of hysteretic systems
abstract: Hysteresis is a nonlinear phenomenon with memory effects, where a system's output depends on both its current state and past states. It is prevalent in various physical and mechanical systems, such as yielding structures under seismic excitation, ferromagnetic materials, and piezoelectric actuators. Analytical models like the Bouc-Wen model are often employed but rely on idealized assumptions and careful parameter calibration, limiting their applicability to diverse or mechanism-unknown behaviors. Existing equation discovery approaches for hysteresis are often system-specific or rely on predefined model libraries, which limit their flexibility and ability to capture the hidden mechanisms. To address these challenges, this research classifies equation discovery problems for hysteretic systems and develops a unified framework in which the state-space form is reformulated, and hysteretic variables are treated as trainable parameters from data. The framework further employs symbolic regression (SR) to automatically recover explicit governing equations without relying on predefined libraries, unlike methods such as sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method is effective in recovering governing equations for hysteretic systems, even in a challenging Full Equation Discovery setting, where prior information is extremely limited, and solving the equations naturally enables the dynamic prediction of hysteretic systems.

title: Cross-specification abrasive belt wear monitoring: a physics-informed deep learning framework with acoustic emission burst indicator
abstract: In abrasive belt grinding, switching between belts of differing grit sizes reduces the predictive accuracy of data-driven wear monitoring models. To address this issue, a physics-informed deep learning framework is proposed for continuous abrasive belt wear monitoring across varying belt specifications, in which grinding mechanics are encoded as mechanism-derived input features and physical constraints are embedded in the loss function to guide network learning. An analysis of grain-workpiece contact mechanics reveals that progressive grain dulling shifts the dominant energy dissipation from efficient cutting to parasitic friction. To capture this transition, Acoustic Emission (AE) signals are leveraged, and a novel indicator, the Cumulative Impulse Density–Duration Ratio (CIDDR), is introduced. This metric captures the statistical evolution of AE burst characteristics providing a physically interpretable proxy for the progressive loss of cutting effectiveness. Subsequently, the framework employs a denoising-aware Stacked Sparse Auto-Encoder (SSAE) to extract compact latent representations from these physics-enhanced inputs, followed by a Physics-informed Causal Temporal Convolutional Network (PI-CTCN) regularized by physics-informed loss to ensure physically consistent wear monitoring. To achieve cross-specification generalization, a parameter-based transfer learning strategy adapts the learned representations to belt-induced domain shifts through selective fine-tuning. Experimental validation on two belt specifications (A45 and A160) grinding TC4 titanium alloy demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves an RMSE of 33.54 mg and R² of 0.9857 under cross-belt transfer conditions, reducing RMSE by approximately 20% compared to training from scratch on the target belt, while maintaining stable and continuous wear monitoring.

title: Physics-regularized Bayesian neural network with time-of-arrival refinement for acoustic emission-based damage source localization in concrete beams
abstract: Accurate acoustic emission (AE) source localisation is essential for structural health monitoring (SHM) of concrete structures; however, heterogeneous material properties and complex wave propagation limit the reliability of conventional approaches. This study proposes PR-BNN-ATR, a physics-regularised Bayesian neural network (BNN) with acoustic time-of-arrival refinement for uncertainty-aware AE localisation. Time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) features extracted using an adaptive Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) picker are used to train a variational BNN, whose hybrid loss combines data fidelity, geometric feasibility, TDOA kinematic consistency, and Kullback–Leibler (KL) regularisation. A deterministic artificial neural network (ANN) and Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout serves as accuracy and uncertainty baselines, respectively. Validated on five notched concrete beams (notch positions 80–40 mm), PR-BNN-ATR achieved mean localisation errors of 3.10–6.19 mm (overall mean 4.04 mm) compared to 1.47–6.58 mm for the ANN. Although the ANN produced lower point errors, PR-BNN-ATR provided calibrated event-wise uncertainty estimates, with Spearman correlation positive for all five beams (ρ = 0.110–0.387), and Mahalanobis joint coverage averaging 91.3% at the 95% nominal level. The variational BNN outperformed MC Dropout on Negative Log-Likelihood in four of five beams. A semi-supervised calibration experiment using a calibration beam b0 with true physical ground-truth coordinates reduced cross-beam error by 82%, confirming genuine localisation learning beyond multilateration replication. Independent digital image correlation (DIC) strain-field measurements confirmed spatial co-localisation of BNN-predicted sources with crack trajectories and linked elevated predictive uncertainty to crack branching, dual crack interaction, and boundary reflection zones, providing non-circular physical validation. These results establish PR-BNN-ATR as an accurate, interpretable, and uncertainty-aware method for risk-informed SHM of concrete structures.

title: Impact acoustic-based damage identification of bridge expansion joints under vehicle-induced excitation using attention-enhanced one-class learning
abstract: Bridge expansion joints are susceptible to deterioration under long-term vehicle loading and environmental effects. The resulting damage may affect structural performance and driving comfort, making rapid and reliable damage identification important for bridge maintenance. This study proposes an impact acoustic-based damage identification method for bridge expansion joints under vehicle-induced excitation using attention-enhanced one-class learning. Acoustic sensors are integrated into a moving load system to acquire acoustic responses from key components, including the center beam, support bar, and concrete in the anchorage zone. The resulting acoustic signals are characterized using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs). On this basis, a compact Transformer encoder with an Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) mechanism, termed ECA-TinyTransformer, is constructed to jointly model global temporal dependencies and critical frequency-band information. At the decision level, Deep Support Vector Data Description (DeepSVDD) models damage identification as anomaly detection using only healthy samples, addressing the scarcity of damage data. Experimental results demonstrate that, under the fully damaged condition (State 4), healthy and damaged samples are clearly separated in the learned feature space. The proposed method achieves accuracies of 0.968, 0.965, and 0.968 for the center beam, support bar, and concrete in the anchorage zone, respectively, with recall values approaching 1.000. Comparative studies further demonstrate the superiority of the proposed framework over representative temporal modeling architectures and one-class anomaly detection methods. The proposed framework provides an effective and practical solution for intelligent condition assessment of bridge expansion joints under moving-load excitation, highlighting the potential of one-class acoustic monitoring for bridge infrastructure inspection.

title: Anti-load performance evaluation method for electro-hydrostatic actuators based on physics-embedded attention mechanism
abstract: High-precision performance degradation evaluation of electro-hydrostatic actuators (EHAs) is critical for aerospace reliability. Among all potential hardware degradation, internal leakage stands out as the most frequent and dominant fault in EHA systems. However, existing methods often fail in dynamic flight environments, where genuine internal leakage signatures are deeply entangled with external variable load disturbances. To address this load-fault coupling challenge, this study proposes an Anti-load Performance Evaluation Method. Firstly, an EHA dynamic model is established to analytically derive a Baseline Contribution Score (BCS), explicitly quantifying the relative sensitivities of multi-source signals to faults versus loads. Then after a dual-screening purification of statistical features, the BCS is deployed as a dual-purpose physical constraint linking the subsequent core modules. It first functions as a physical prior in a Physics-Embedded Channel Attention Mechanism to adaptively highlight fault signatures while suppressing load noise, and then acts as a regularization penalty within a Correlation-Regularized Stacked Autoencoder to constrain the deep fusion process. Driven by this sequential BCS guidance, the network ultimately condenses these refined representations into a highly robust, anti-load 1D Health Indicator. Validated through simulations and physical testbench experiments, the ACFN successfully disentangles complex coupled signals into a linearly separable manifold. It achieves a superior diagnostic accuracy of 95.24% under the 3 kN load. This physics-guided framework effectively bridges the gap between mechanistic interpretability and deep learning, providing a highly robust solution for EHA health management.

title: A physics-guided evidential multimodal uncertainty framework for small-sample welding defect detection using magneto-optical and infrared imaging
abstract: Traditional data-driven welding defect detection methods often suffer from poor interpretability, performance degradation under small-sample conditions, and an inability to quantify decision-making reliability. To address these issues, this study proposes a novel Physics-guided Evidential-based Multimodal Uncertainty Framework (PEMUF) for weld defect classification using magneto-optical imaging (MOI) and infrared thermography (IRT). A coordinated MOI-IRT nondestructive testing system is developed to acquire complementary magnetic and thermal responses of weld defects. Based on the distinct physical sensitivities of the two modalities, leakage magnetic field information from MOI and heat diffusion characteristics from IRT are explicitly encoded into modality-specific prior channels, improving the physical interpretability and discriminability of input representations. PEMUF further combines hierarchical multimodal interaction, spectral manifold augmentation, and evidential fusion. The hierarchical attention mechanism enhances intra-modal representation learning and cross-modal complementary interaction, while spectral manifold augmentation enriches the effective feature distribution under limited training samples. In addition, Dempster-Shafer evidential fusion with Dirichlet uncertainty modeling is introduced to generate both defect-category predictions and uncertainty scores. Experiments are conducted on a four-class resistance spot weld defect dataset, including defect-free, crack, pit, and incomplete fusion samples. Using the full training set, PEMUF achieves an Accuracy of 99.04 %, a Macro F1 of 0.9908, and a Brier Score of 0.0271. More importantly, when only 20 % of the training samples are used, the model still maintains an Accuracy of 96.31 %, a Macro F1 of 0.9617, and a Brier Score of 0.0529, demonstrating strong robustness and probability calibration under small-sample conditions. Comparative experiments, ablation studies, confusion matrices, t-SNE visualization, Grad-CAM++ analysis, and uncertainty evaluation further confirm that physical priors, spectral manifold augmentation, and evidential fusion jointly improve feature discrimination, generalization, and reliability-aware decision-making. These results indicate that PEMUF provides an effective and reliable solution for small-sample multimodal weld defect inspection.

title: Intelligent identification of bearing dynamic parameters using a two-stage physics-informed residual KAN with TSA and frequency-domain integration
abstract: This paper proposes a two-stage physics-informed residual Kolmogorov–Arnold Network framework integrated with Time Synchronous Averaging and frequency-domain integration for identifying the equivalent mass and damping parameters of bearing–rotor systems from measured acceleration signals. First, a two-degree-of-freedom bearing dynamic model is established to derive the time-varying equivalent stiffness in the selected direction. Time Synchronous Averaging is then applied to the measured acceleration signal, and the corresponding velocity and displacement signals are reconstructed through frequency-domain integration. In Stage 1, a constrained linear physical backbone, mathematically equivalent to a linear regressor, traverses the simulated stiffness phases and provides preliminary estimates of the equivalent mass and damping. In Stage 2, the principal nonlinear role of KAN is realized through an additive B-spline residual representation, which accounts for unmodeled dynamics while keeping the physical mass and damping terms explicitly separated. A near-optimal stiffness-phase ensemble strategy is further employed to reduce parameter sensitivity to small phase deviations. Experimental results at 1800 and 2400 r/min yielded equivalent masses of 4.3201 and 4.3385 kg, respectively, with a cross-speed difference of 0.43%. Under the same residual-capacity limit, the residual KAN and residual MLP achieved similar equation-reconstruction errors, whereas the residual KAN provided more stable equivalent-mass estimates. The proposed framework provides a physically structured residual-learning approach in which the explicit physical coefficients are separated from the nonlinear model-discrepancy representation.

title: Hydraulic system compound fault diagnosis based on decoupling-oriented feature optimization and uncertainty-aware evidential fusion
abstract: Compound fault diagnosis in complex hydraulic systems remains challenging because of strong feature coupling among fault combinations. This paper proposes a D-S (Dempster-Shafer) theory-enhanced convolutional neural network (DSNN) integrating decoupling-oriented feature optimization with uncertainty-aware evidential fusion. The proposed method reconstructs the original diagnosis task into several similarity-aware subtasks to improve the separability of compound fault features under coupled fault modes. Fault categories are first grouped according to feature-distribution distances. The divided groups are used as the focal elements for subsequent D-S theory-based diagnostic reasoning, where uncertainty-aware soft grouping allows overlapping focal elements. Then, dedicated CNN-based submodels are trained to estimate basic probability assignments (BPAs) for divided focal elements while performing task-specific feature optimization. Finally, a differentiable D-S evidence fusion layer combines the BPAs from all submodels and indicates conflicts among submodel evidence through the conflict factor. Experiments on an SCM hydraulic test rig and an open-source hydraulic dataset show that DSNN achieves superior diagnostic accuracy and robustness.

title: Robust feature selection for cross-domain fault diagnosis using deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Recent research on deep learning-based fault diagnosis has made significant progress. However, over-parameterized models often introduce redundant features, leading to degraded cross-domain generalization and limited deployability on resource-constrained devices. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a reinforcement-learning-based robust feature selection (RFS) framework for cross-domain fault diagnosis. Unlike existing methods that treat network pruning and domain adaptation as separate processes, the proposed approach integrates them at the decision level via a domain-aware reward formulation. Specifically, channel pruning is formulated as a sequential decision-making problem, where a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agent learns an adaptive pruning policy. Meanwhile, domain alignment loss is incorporated into the reward function, enabling the pruning policy to directly optimize cross-domain feature robustness during the decision-making process rather than through post-hoc feature alignment. This mechanism promotes the retention of features that are both discriminative and transferable, while eliminating redundant or domain-specific components. This framework offers a principled approach for jointly optimizing model compactness and cross-domain generalization, rather than treating them as independent objectives. Extensive experiments on two gearbox datasets under various domain shift scenarios demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently improves cross-domain diagnostic performance while reducing model complexity. In particular, the method achieves up to 19.59 % improvement in target-domain accuracy and reduces computational cost by up to 73.87 % in FLOPs, with reduced inference latency. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in jointly achieving robust cross-domain generalization and efficient model deployment in practical industrial scenarios.

title: FRP-M2DA: cross-modal multi-source domain adaptation via frequency-domain recurrence and multi-level adversarial alignment for cross-condition bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: In complex variable operating-condition scenarios, bearing fault diagnosis faces two coupled challenges: pronounced distribution shift and insufficient discriminative information from a single view. To address these issues, this paper proposes FRP-M2DA, a frequency-domain recurrence plot (FRP)-guided multimodal multi-source adversarial domain adaptation framework for robust cross-domain diagnosis. FRP transforms one-dimensional spectral sequences into a two-dimensional structured representation that explicitly captures recurrence structures and global correlations associated with fault-induced impulsive components. A heterogeneous dual-stream encoder is then constructed, where a Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT) extracts multi-scale global texture semantics from FRP, and a multi-scale CNN (MSCNN) models local transients from the raw vibration sequence, enabling complementary “global–local” representation learning via feature fusion. To handle multi-source transfer, FRP-M2DA introduces multi-level multi-source adversarial alignment by placing domain discriminators in both modality-specific subspaces and the fused space, thereby enforcing domain invariance at multiple representation levels and mitigating insufficient alignment and negative transfer. Moreover, a bidirectional cross-view contrastive regularization (InfoNCE) is incorporated to enhance semantic consistency across heterogeneous views, promoting intra-class compactness and inter-class separability on the unlabeled target domain. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks (JNU cross-speed and PU cross-load) and an engineering test-rig dataset with coupled speed–load shifts demonstrate that FRP-M2DA consistently outperforms representative baselines and state-of-the-art domain adaptation methods, achieving superior generalization, balanced class-wise performance, and reliable fault detectability under composite operating-condition variations.

title: Koopman Neural Operator-based surrogate modelling for high-frequency dynamics of high-speed rail pantographs
abstract: Stable sliding contact between the pantograph and catenary is essential for reliable current collection in high-speed rail. As operating speeds increase beyond 350 km/h, the pantograph-catenary system exhibits unprecedented high-frequency dynamic behaviors caused by the excitation of flexible structural modes. Traditional lumped mass pantograph models are unable to represent the structural flexibility, while fully flexible finite element models, though accurate, are computationally constrained for large-scale simulations. To fill this gap, a Koopman Neural Operator-based surrogate modeling framework is proposed to integrate dynamic theory into a data-driven learning scheme, enabling efficient and accurate representation of the high-frequency pantograph dynamics. The surrogate model integrates a deep autoencoder for the observable and inverse-observable functions with a modified Transformer as the evolution operator. Training data are generated from an accurate fully flexible pantograph model, which has been validated via experimental tests, under broadband random excitations. The training process is supervised by a combined loss of multi-step prediction and physical consistency. Inference tests demonstrate that the surrogate model maintains finite element-level accuracy while reducing computational time by three orders of magnitude when predicting 1000-step dynamic responses. Comparative analyses confirm its superior balance between physical interpretability and forecasting performance, highlighting its potential as a powerful tool for real-time simulation, efficient optimization, and comprehensive evaluation of the high-frequency behaviors of a high-speed pantograph-catenary system.

title: DRN-PISSM: a pitch bearing fault diagnosis network integrating dilated residual convolution and a Physics-Informed State-Space model
abstract: Pitch bearings in wind turbine equipment operate for long periods under extremely low rotational speeds and time-varying loads. Under such conditions, fault-induced impulses are weak and span long periods, while diagnostic information is easily masked by background noise. As a result, conventional signal-processing methods and purely data-driven models often show insufficient stability under strong noise and cross-load conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Dilated Residual Network with a Physics-Informed State-Space Model, termed DRN-PISSM. The proposed method first uses a one-dimensional dilated residual convolutional network to extract multiscale temporal features, thereby enhancing the perception of weak fault information in low-speed heavy-load bearings. A physics-informed state-space recurrent branch is then designed to explicitly strengthen the modelling of periodic information associated with fault characteristic frequencies, improving both physical interpretability and feature discriminability. Finally, adaptive gated fusion, together with joint constraints of physical consistency and noise invariance, is used to improve robustness and generalization under strong noise and load variations. Experimental results show that the proposed method maintains high diagnostic accuracy under different noise intensities and outperforms several comparison models in cross-load transfer tasks with noise disturbance, demonstrating good robustness and generalization capability.

title: Collaborative denoising of multi-point vibration signals using a physics-guided graph neural network
abstract: The acquisition of clean vibration signals is a fundamental prerequisite for structural health monitoring. With the development of distributed monitoring technologies, a key challenge for traditional single-point denoising methods is how to denoise signals from densely distributed measurement points while simultaneously preserving data quality and enforcing physical constraints. To address this issue, this study proposes a physics-guided graph neural network framework for collaborative denoising of multi-point vibration signals. The framework constructs a physics-embedded adjacency matrix to define node connections and introduces a physics-guided loss function with partial differential equation constraints, together with a boundary compensation mechanism, so that the denoised results not only conform to the statistical characteristics of the data but also satisfy mechanical laws. Experimental results from multiple test cases show that, compared with existing denoising methods, the proposed model achieves superior performance across all evaluation metrics and preserves the consistency of physical field characteristics more effectively. This study provides a new approach for vibration noise suppression in structural health monitoring.

title: Physics-informed dual digital twin for online friction updating and decoupled wear identification in robots
abstract: Joint friction is influenced by reversible variations in temperature and load and by irreversible degradation caused by wear. This leads to challenges in friction identification, including operating condition coupling, strong nonlinearity, and poor long-term stability. We present a Physics-Informed Dual Digital Twin (PIDT) framework to overcome these issues. This framework comprises a baseline digital twin trained offline and an evolving digital twin updated online. They enable accurate friction modeling, robust online updating, and decoupled wear monitoring under varying operating conditions. The baseline digital twin uses a ResNet based hybrid deep kernel to learn nonlinear features of temperature and load coupling, and then constructs the kernel function. A multi output sparse variational Gaussian process (SVGP) provides a probabilistic friction model and quantifies predictive uncertainty. The evolving digital twin performs mini batch incremental learning while keeping part of the structural parameters fixed and enforcing physics constraints. Taking the difference between the evolving digital twin and the baseline digital twin suppresses reversible fluctuations and extracts wear related drift. Experiments on the JAKA MiniCobo show that the baseline digital twin reduces RMSE by at least 16.1% compared with conventional methods. The online updating process further improves accuracy and refines uncertainty estimates. The estimated wear related health indicator (HI) correlates with the simulated HI with r = 0.996. The framework remains stable during long duration experiments on the real robot.

title: A differentiable physics-embedded framework for thermally informed Neural-UniTire modeling and identification
abstract: To address the need for thermally informed tire modeling for handling-oriented force prediction under limited thermal sensing, this paper presents a differentiable physics-embedded sequential framework for thermally informed Neural-UniTire modeling and identification. First, a differentiable radial thermal model is developed from a continuous radial thermal formulation through finite-volume Crank–Nicolson discretization, with hybrid global, physics-parameterized, and neural thermal coefficients used to reconstruct radial multilayer thermal states from sparse boundary measurements. Then, a Physics-Embedded Neural-UniTire model is developed by embedding neural networks into the UniTire framework and extending it to unsteady conditions through a second-order hysteresis element. Finally, a thermally informed correction mechanism is introduced for the Physics-Embedded Neural-UniTire model, in which reconstructed radial multilayer thermal states with operating-condition information are used to generate neural thermo-correction factors for stiffness- and friction-related parameters. Experiments on an MTS flat-track test rig with a passenger-car tire and a semi-slick tire under pure lateral-slip and longitudinal-slip conditions show good agreement with the measured temperature and force responses. The radial thermal model achieves accurate temperature estimation from sparse boundary measurements. The unsteady Physics-Embedded Neural-UniTire model improves force prediction over the steady-state formulation, especially in the nonlinear slip region and phase lag. The thermally informed model improves force prediction over the baseline and sparse-input ablation models under pulse-excitation conditions, while the learned thermal correction remains physically interpretable.

title: An unsupervised deep learning method for extracting weak reflections from strong guided waves in array data
abstract: The separation of overlapping wavefields in array sensor measurements is a fundamental challenge in acoustic and vibration diagnostics, with critical applications from structural health monitoring to subsurface imaging. A particularly challenging scenario occurs when extremely weak target signals (e.g., geological reflections from fractures) are completely masked by strong guided-wave interference in borehole acoustic reflection imaging. Traditional methods inadequately suppress guided waves, resulting in residual interference that obscures the weak reflections. Furthermore, supervised deep learning methods face practical constraints due to the limited availability of labeled data in field applications. To address these limitations, we propose a novel unsupervised approach that integrates the time-frequency network (TF-GridNet) with a Multi-Frame Wiener Filter (MFWF). Our approach exploits the distinct kinematic properties of guided waves and reflections in array data to achieve separation without requiring labeled training sets. Comprehensive validation on both simulated and field data from complex geological lithologies demonstrates our method’s superiority. On simulated data, it achieves a lower separation residual (L2-norm) than conventional F-K and Multichannel Singular-Spectrum Analysis (MSSA) methods. Crucially, on field data, it enables the reliable extraction of weak reflections, producing significantly clearer images of high-dip-angle fractures and fracture networks with enhanced continuity and reduced artifacts. This work presents a robust, label-free solution for extracting weak signals from strong interference in waveguide structures, as demonstrated in borehole acoustics. The method shows strong potential for advancing structural health monitoring applications that rely on guided-wave sensing.

title: A Frequency-Aware Residual Decomposition Network for Extracting Incipient Fault Signatures in Rotating Machinery
abstract: Signal decomposition is an important task in Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) of mechanical transmission systems characterized by nonlinear and non-stationary vibration responses. However, conventional signal processing methodologies are often constrained by fixed basis functions and manual parameter tuning, which compromise noise robustness and limit their ability in capturing transient signatures of incipient faults. Leveraging the paradigm of signal processing-informed neural networks, this paper proposes an interpretable Frequency-Aware Residual Decomposition Network (FARCD-Net), which unfolds iterative filtering into a learnable framework to reduce reliance on manually designed optimization objectives. Specifically, a Generalized Adaptive Decomposition Module (GADM) is constructed via residual learning to generalize the conventional filtering operator, preserving the underlying decomposition principle. To enhance feature extraction in noisy environments, a data-driven Frequency Masking Layer (FML) is introduced. The layer learns adaptive spectral weights, enabling the network to dynamically localize transient signatures within resonance bands. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations on a run-to-failure benchmark and a high-speed train bogie system demonstrate effective extraction of fault-induced transients, with physical interpretability supported by intermediate network representations.

title: Physics-informed online intelligent discharge state identification for high-energy electrical discharge milling: Theory and methods
abstract: High-energy electrical discharge milling (HEDM) offers considerable potential for high-efficiency machining of difficult-to-machine materials in aerospace and other advanced manufacturing sectors. However, compared with conventional electrical discharge machining (EDM), HEDM is characterized by substantially higher single-pulse energy, greater fluctuations in discharge behavior, and lower process stability. To address the limitations of purely data-driven models in terms of physical interpretability and cross-condition generalization, this paper proposes a physics-informed semi-supervised learning framework for online HEDM discharge state identification. First, a time-threshold-based semi-automatic labeling method is developed to generate discharge state labels and identify key pulse-level physical information. Second, an empirical model for estimating the equivalent plasma channel radius is established based on high-energy single-pulse discharge experiments. The estimated radius is then combined with the actual single-pulse input energy and equivalent short-circuit conduction to construct a multi-level physical supervision framework. These three quantities characterize the spatial scale of thermal effects, heat input intensity, and short-circuit-related conduction behavior, respectively. By jointly optimizing the pulse-level classification loss and the window-level physical consistency loss, the proposed framework enables the model to learn discriminative features while constraining its predictions using discharge-related physical quantities. Comparative and ablation experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an identification accuracy of 99.17 ± 0.75% under the new operating conditions and improves both cross-condition generalization and physical consistency. Real-time validation further confirms its capability for online HEDM monitoring, thereby providing a theoretical and technical basis for future intelligent control of HEDM processes.

title: AWT-DDFN: an end-to-end adaptive wavelet transform-dual domain fusion network for bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Deep learning has been widely used in intelligent fault diagnosis of rolling bearings. Existing fault diagnosis methods usually use multi-scale wavelet transforms to convert raw 1D vibration signals into time–frequency representations as model inputs. However, such preprocessing brings high computational cost, inevitable information loss and tedious manual parameter tuning, which hinders real end-to-end diagnosis. To overcome these drawbacks, we propose an adaptive wavelet transform–dual domain fusion network (AWT-DDFN), a complete end-to-end framework that directly processes raw vibration signals without manual preprocessing. AWT-DDFN adopts a learnable wavelet convolution layer to replace fixed wavelet transforms, realizing joint optimization of feature extraction and fault diagnosis. Meanwhile, the network uses a dual-branch structure to capture complementary discriminative features: a frequency-domain branch based on pointwise convolution and a time-domain branch combining grouped convolution and dilated convolution. This structure effectively reduces model complexity and parameters, making the model lightweight and robust to noise and trivial signal variations. The features of the two branches are fused by element-wise addition before being sent to the classifier for fault identification, forming a seamless end-to-end diagnosis pipeline. Experiments on PU and CWRU datasets show that AWT-DDFN achieves superior diagnosis performance and stronger noise robustness than state-of-the-art methods, with fewer parameters and lower computation cost. By discarding handcrafted preprocessing, the proposed framework provides a lightweight, end-to-end and deployable intelligent diagnosis solution with strong practical value for industrial scenarios under complex working conditions and strong noise.

title: Flow-induced vibrations in tandem square cylinders: machine learning analysis of structural response and energy harvesting under variable size and spacing ratios
abstract: Flow-induced vibrations (FIV) provide an effective mechanism for renewable energy harvesting, with potential applications in powering autonomous sensors, smart infrastructures, and low-power electronics. In tandem bluff-body configurations, wake interactions play a key role in modifying the structural response, leading to nonlinear and spacing-dependent vibration characteristics. This study experimentally investigates the performance of piezoelectric energy harvesters (PEHs) employing tandem square cylinders. Five configurations were tested at three spacings (S = 4, 8, and 12 cm) and flow velocities ranging from 2.4 to 13 m/s. The results show that the tandem arrangement significantly modifies both vibration amplitude and electrical output through wake-interaction effects. Depending on the size ratio and spacing, the system exhibits either enhanced or constrained oscillatory behavior. In particular, when a 4 cm cylinder is placed upstream of a 5 cm cylinder (Case 3), increased displacement and RMS voltage are observed compared with the isolated case, with maximum improvements of 356.5% in displacement and 171.9% in voltage. However, the response is strongly dependent on spacing, and no single configuration remains optimal across all flow conditions. This variability is addressed through the introduction of an integrated energy metric combined with normalized power comparison, enabling consistent evaluation across the full velocity range. To complement these findings and capture the nonlinear coupling among flow parameters, structural response, and harvested power, a CatBoost-based machine learning (ML) framework was developed and optimized using 10-fold cross-validation, incorporating an out-of-fold residual filtering step to suppress measurement noise and refine model accuracy. The combined experimental-ML approach enabled accurate prediction and facilitated the interpretation of trends associated with wake interference, achieving R2 = 0.98 for displacement and 0.85 for power, and demonstrates the potential of such tandem configurations within the investigated operating conditions for flow-adaptive energy harvesting systems and self-powered sensing applications.

title: Physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold networks for sound field estimation
abstract: The sound field estimation method based on a physics-informed neural network (PINN) integrates physical prior information, which not only significantly reduces dependence on the size of the training set but also improves the accuracy of sound field estimation. However, PINN usually employs multilayer perceptrons with fixed activation functions, resulting in limited model interpretability and flexibility, which constrains its performance in complex acoustic environments. Therefore, this study proposes a sound field estimation method based on a physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold network (PIKAN). PIKAN constructs its edge activation functions as a linear combination of radial basis functions (RBFs) and adaptively learns the RBF coefficients during training, thereby substantially enhancing the interpretability and expressive capability. The proposed method is evaluated on sound field interpolation and extrapolation tasks across small and large meeting rooms at multiple frequencies, and benchmarked against plane wave expansion (PWE) and PINN. Analysis of the learned edge activation functions reveals that they spontaneously exhibit sinusoidal-like oscillatory characteristics. For interpolation, PIKAN demonstrates clear advantages over PINN and PWE under sparse training conditions at mid-to-high frequencies. For extrapolation, PWE retains a competitive advantage. Furthermore, to improve the performance under high reverberation, a transfer learning strategy is introduced, fine-tuning parameters pre-trained under moderate reverberation. Overall, this study demonstrates PIKAN as a promising alternative for sound field estimation, with results highlighting its potential for practical acoustic modeling.

title: System-dynamics-oriented design of electromagnetic active suspension via physics-informed modeling
abstract: Electromagnetic active suspension (EAS) performance is fundamentally governed by actuator dynamics, where the thrust saturation and ripple of permanent magnet linear synchronous motors (PMLSMs) directly affect the ride comfort under random road excitations. In conventional FEA-driven actuator design, the pathway linking electromagnetic design variables to system-level vibration responses is not explicitly revealed, which renders performance-oriented optimization computationally prohibitive. This study proposes a physics-informed modeling and optimization framework that establishes an explicit knowledge pathway from suspension dynamics to electromagnetic actuator design. An analytical Optimal Equivalent Radius-Maxwell Stress Tensor (OMST) formulation is developed to characterize the electromagnetic thrust, and embedded together with Maxwell equations into a physics-informed neural operator (PIMNO) built upon an enhanced Fourier Neural Operator. This enables accurate magnetic field and thrust prediction with substantially reduced data requirements. A MORIME scheme is further introduced to synergize with the PIMNO-OMST model for efficient design exploration. More importantly, device performance requirements are derived directly from system-level vibration simulations using a dual-condition robust weighting strategy, allowing actuator optimization to be guided by vibration and signal-domain indices rather than purely electromagnetic criteria. Experimental results demonstrate that the designed actuator yields suspension vibration responses, power spectral density characteristics, and ride comfort performance nearly identical to those obtained using FEA-driven optimization, while reducing computational cost by over 99%. The proposed framework provides a computationally efficient and physically consistent method for system-dynamics-oriented force performance design in EAS, bridging electromagnetic field-to-force modeling and mechanical system vibration analysis.

title: A kriging-based data-driven approach for localization of simultaneous impacts in composites
abstract: Detection of simultaneous low-velocity impacts in composite structures involve fundamental challenge as the uniqueness of time-difference-of-arrival (TDoA) features is compromised by guided wave superposition. This challenge becomes significantly more pronounced in the presence of simultaneous multiple impacts. We propose an artificial neural network (ANN)-based framework for both single and multiple impact localization on laminated composite plates employing TDoA features enhanced through singular value decomposition (SVD) for mitigating indeterminacy of source due to wavefield superposition. The effectiveness of the proposed methodology in localizing single and simultaneous impacts without explicit signal separation and densification of sensors has been demonstrated. The ANN trained solely on finite-element simulation data has been shown be robust enough when tested on unseen numerical and experimental datasets, including unequal energy levels and time delays between impacts. The robustness is further enhanced through a kriging-based post-processing correction without retraining. For dual impacts, the proposed framework exhibits 90% probability-of-detection between 24.01and 38.65 mm.

title: High-Order Fourier-Basis LSTM-PINN for angle-dependent bias waveform reconstruction in whole-angle vibratory gyroscopes
abstract: The bias of a whole-angle vibratory gyroscope is not a stationary offset but an angle-dependent waveform shaped by structural errors, circuit-induced control and detection errors, and thermally driven operating variations, whose coupled effects are represented in the present observation model by effective Fourier bias components rather than separated into source-specific parameters. Existing bias models usually rely on low-order angular harmonics, especially the 2θ and 4θ components, which limits their ability to represent high-order angle-dependent bias structures. This study proposes a High-Order Fourier-Basis Long Short-Term Memory Physics-Informed Neural Network (LSTM-PINN) framework for angle-dependent bias waveform reconstruction and harmonic component characterization. High-order potential and Rayleigh dissipation functionals are retained up to the eighth order, from which a 2/4/6/8 even-order Fourier harmonic basis is derived. This Lagrangian-derived harmonic structure defines the Fourier-basis analytical decoder of the LSTM-PINN solver. Instead of treating the angle-dependent bias waveform as an unconstrained regression target, the solver infers the scale-factor term and Fourier bias components from historical sequences of the amplitude-control envelope, quadrature-control envelope, and resonant frequency, and reconstructs the angle-dependent bias waveform through the Lagrangian-derived analytical decoder. Experiments on 16-electrode micro-shell gyroscopes show stable reconstruction, with a mean RMSE of 6.62×10−4 deg/s and a mean R2 of 0.9886. Architecture ablations show that both the PINN and the LSTM are necessary: relative to the black-box LSTM baseline and the MLP-PINN baseline, the full LSTM-PINN reduces the 1 Hz mean RMSE by 90.5% and 59.2%, respectively. Expanding the physically admissible basis from 2θ/4θ to 2θ/4θ/6θ/8θ reduces the across-label mean RMSE by 32.0%, while repeated-segment tests show quasi-stationary inferred high-order components. Over a seven-day evaluation horizon at ±1 and ±8deg/s, the Day-7 across-rate mean RMSE and R2 were 9.765×10−4deg/s and 0.9857, respectively. Within the validated micro-shell device and laboratory operating range, these results support the proposed framework as a device-physics-constrained temporal method for angle-dependent bias waveform reconstruction.

title: High-fidelity wear simulation of gas foil bearing-rotor systems in hydrogen fuel cell air compressors using a physics-guided neural network
abstract: A Gas Foil Bearing (GFB)-rotor system is critical to a hydrogen fuel cell air compressor, yet highly susceptible to wear under frequent start-stop operations. Existing simulation models rarely consider wear and lack simulation accuracy, inadequately assessing lubrication performance and frictional power loss of GFB-rotor systems. To address this issue, this study proposes a high-fidelity dynamic model for a GFB-rotor system based on a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN), coupling a physics-based GFB-rotor dynamic model with a neural network used for model error compensation. The GFB-rotor dynamic model incorporates wear-induced gas film thickness variation, Reynolds equation, foil structural dynamics, and rigid rotor motion equations. To compensate for deviations from theoretical simplifications, the neural network embeds a learnable model discrepancy term into the GFB-rotor dynamic model. The model parameters and neural network weights are then iteratively optimized via experimental calibration. The simulated results of the proposed high-fidelity model match well with experimental data, with relative errors below 5.73% across all operating conditions. Parametric analyses demonstrate that wear significantly deteriorates gas film lubrication performance. Increased wear depth and worn region reduce minimum gas film thickness, raise maximum gas film pressure, and shift the pressure field from single-peak to dual-peak concentration. Wear amplifies viscous shear dissipation via reduced gas film thickness and elevated gas film pressure, increasing frictional power loss of the GFB-rotor system by up to 44.5% under 20,000 rpm. The proposed high-fidelity model enables accurate condition monitoring of GFB-rotor systems, ensuring stable performance and optimal efficiency of hydrogen fuel cell air compressors.

title: End-to-End predictive modeling of excavator hydraulic systems
abstract: Accurate prediction of the dynamic response of excavator hydraulic systems is a key prerequisite for model-based control applications. However, existing studies have not established a direct mapping from cylinder outputs to joystick signals. To address this issue, this study proposes an end-to-end predictive model that integrates a joystick-signal baseline with data-driven modeling. Specifically, the joystick-signal baseline is jointly determined by the mechanism-based relationship between cylinder motion and hydraulic flow and the predefined electro-hydraulic control mappings, providing an initial prediction reference for the model. Subsequently, a two-stage long short-term memory (LSTM) network is introduced for data-driven modeling. In the first stage, sensitivity-based weighting dynamically adjusts the weights of the input variables to capture the dynamic nonlinear characteristics of the system. In the second stage, the weighted input features from the first stage are combined with the joystick-signal baseline to form a new input sequence, which is then modeled using a multilayer LSTM. In addition, a delay-aware structure is designed to account for the non-fixed delays between joystick signals and cylinder states. Experimental results show that the prediction errors remain within 10 % under in-distribution validation, while R2 values above 0.88 are achieved on an independently collected gravel excavation dataset from another excavator of the same model, demonstrating good prediction performance and generalization capability. The proposed architecture requires only 4 MB of storage and achieves an inference time of less than 2 ms per prediction, indicating strong potential for real-time applications.

title: SFDM: Structural full-field dynamic displacement monitoring utilizing computer vision-enhanced targetless monitoring system
abstract: Full-field dynamic displacement monitoring with high spatial resolution provides a more comprehensive representation of the dynamic characteristics of bridge structures, thereby significantly enhancing the effectiveness of bridge structural health monitoring (BSHM). In this study, a structural full-field dynamic displacement monitoring (SFDM) method is proposed to overcome the limitations of traditional discrete-point measurement techniques. To achieve targetless and accurate extraction of the lower edge of bridge structures, an effective computer vision framework is developed by integrating a robust fusion image processing (RFIP) strategy with a row-wise adaptive edge detection (RAED) approach. Additionally, a multi-target displacement transformation model (MDTM) is proposed to convert subpixel-level image displacements into physical displacements. A tied-arch bridge field test was conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed method. The experimental results indicate that the proposed SFDM achieved correlation coefficients higher than 0.964, while the corresponding RMSE and NRMSE remained below 0.282 mm and 9.178% across all test cases, respectively, thereby confirming its accuracy and effectiveness for full-field displacement monitoring in BSHM applications.
