title: Evidence-causality dual adversarial framework for fault diagnosis in dynamic open environments
abstract: The practical implementation of deep learning models for real-time mechanical fault diagnosis in open environments remains challenging, primarily due to data acquisition difficulties, dynamic industrial fluctuations, and the emergence of novel failure modes in real-world applications. Conventional open-set domain generalization (OSDG) methods often fail to generalize to such scenarios, as they typically necessitate extensive offline training data spanning multiple source domains. To address these limitations, an evidence-causality dual adversarial framework for single-source OSDG is proposed, enabling online fault diagnosis in dynamic open conditions under limited data. Specifically, a sample weight-aware evidential loss is introduced to mitigate overconfidence in boundary-ambiguous samples. Furthermore, an evidential neural network is employed for uncertainty quantification, thereby enhancing diagnostic reliability and the robust detection of unknown failure modes. Concurrently, an uncertainty-guided data generation module is developed to augment data diversity while preserving semantic consistency. Finally, an adversarial causal feature disentanglement module is designed to extract highly discriminative causal features, effectively suppressing spurious correlations induced by dynamic distribution shifts. Extensive experimental evaluations conducted on three rotating machinery datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in fault diagnosis under dynamic, open industrial environments. The code will be available on GitHub at https://github.com/Fanyang199711/SOSDG.

title: Interpretable U-Net RCNN for blind peak detection in vibration spectra
abstract: Accurate peak detection in vibration spectra is key to early fault diagnosis but remains challenging due to noise and unknown spectral content. This paper presents a hybrid approach combining the benefits of U-Nets and Region-based Convolutional Neural Networks for blind peak detection, trained on complex simulated 1D data with extension to real-world signals. The model combines classification and regression to identify and localise peaks without prior knowledge of the signal or machine. Its performance is benchmarked against the Exact Order Model Estimation of Signal Parameters via Rotational Invariance Technique and a Topological Peak Identification approach using labelled simulated data, demonstrating robustness and practical effectiveness. The method is further tested on real offshore wind turbine data, where it successfully detects visually identifiable peaks, confirming its applicability in real-world scenarios.

title: Chatter-sensitive feature construction and dual-branch learning for machining state identification in micro-milling of glow discharge polymer
abstract: Glow discharge polymer (GDP) ablators with micro-milled modulated microstructures are increasingly used in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) applications. However, self-excited vibration/chatter, generated from an insufficient-stiffness manufacturing system, could degrade the resultant surface quality and process productivity during micro-milling. In this study, a physically guided data-driven framework was developed for chatter-sensitive feature construction and machining-state identification in micro-milling of GDP polymers. Tri-directional milling-force and acceleration signals were in-situ acquired during micro-milling with a single-edge diamond tool. Wavelet packet decomposition (WPD) was initially employed for noise suppression and signal reconstruction, with optimal parameters determined using an energy-weighted feature evaluation strategy. Variational mode decomposition (VMD) was then applied to isolate state-sensitive intrinsic mode functions (IMFs), and a state-discriminative energy–entropy criterion was developed to determine task-oriented decomposition parameters. Based on the selected chatter-sensitive modes, eight multi-domain features were extracted and organized into two heterogeneous feature tensors. A dual-branch Inception Residual network (DIR-Net) was constructed to independently encode force- and acceleration-related features before high-level feature fusion. Experimental results showed that WPD improved the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the milling-force and acceleration signals by 65.8 % and 43.0 %, respectively. DIR-Net achieved an identification accuracy of 97.08 % and a macro-averaged F1-score of 97.02 % on the independent test set, outperforming conventional CNN and ResNet benchmarks. Feature visualization and online monitoring results further indicated improved separability among air-cut, stable cutting, and chatter states, as well as stable recognition performance under the unseen tool-overhang and tool-size conditions. The proposed research framework provides an interpretable solution for chatter identification and online monitoring in ultra-precision micro-milling of GDP.

title: A deep reinforcement learning method applied to remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearings
abstract: As an important component of mechanical equipment, the health status of rolling bearings directly affects the reliability and safety of the equipment. Due to the harsh working environment of rolling bearings and the difficulty in identifying the early degradation trends, the accuracy of remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is significantly challenged. To address these issues, this paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) prediction model based on the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm, which reconfigures the RUL prediction task as a sequential decision-making problem under Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework in a continuous action space. The DDPG algorithm can effectively capture the temporal dependencies among original data. By combining the feature extraction capabilities of residual networks (ResNet) and the time series modeling capabilities of long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, high-precision RUL prediction is achieved. Firstly, a reinforcement learning (RL) agent based on ResNet-LSTM is constructed to extract deep degradation features from the original data. Subsequently, by designing appropriate reward functions and action spaces, the agent learns to map the current operating state of the rolling bearing to its RUL under the guidance of the DDPG algorithm through repeated trials and optimization. The proposed model was validated on two open-source datasets and a private dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves lower root mean square error (RMSE) and more stable degradation trend prediction compared with other approaches.

title: Multi-task mixture-of-experts vision transformer for cross-bridge anomaly detection
abstract: Structural health monitoring systems deployed on large-scale bridges accumulate massive amounts of anomalous data, which undermines the reliability of structural condition assessment and damage identification. As monitoring targets gradually expand from individual bridges to bridge groups, the costs associated with model training and management continue to increase, placing higher demands on unified model deployment and centralized system management. Meanwhile, although anomalous patterns from different bridges contain potentially shareable information, such commonality cannot be fully exploited through simple data aggregation. This study proposes a multi-task mixture-of-experts Vision Transformer (MT-MoE ViT) framework for data anomaly diagnosis, which imposes parallel constraints during the joint optimization of multi-bridge tasks to reduce reliance on structure-specific or local condition features and instead learn anomalous features that remain discriminative across multiple bridge scenarios. To further characterize task-level differences among bridges, task embeddings are incorporated into the gating network to guide adaptive expert selection and balance shared representation learning with task-specific modeling. To mitigate routing collapse and optimization conflicts in multi-task learning, sparse routing strategies achieve feature-level expert selection, while adaptive multi-task optimization mechanisms dynamically adjust gradient weights and expert load balancing. Experimental validation conducted on real structural health monitoring data from nine long-span bridges of different structural types demonstrates that the proposed method enables stable cross-bridge anomaly representation and collaborative diagnosis within a unified model framework.

title: Parameter identification and unknown excitation inversion of piezoelectric cantilever beams using multi-network PINNs with Fourier feature mapping
abstract: Constructing a highly accurate multiphysics coupling model is a fundamental prerequisite for advancing piezoelectric energy harvesting systems from theoretical design to practical engineering applications. However, in real engineering scenarios, external excitations are often uncertain, and key system parameters, such as mass, stiffness, and damping ratio, are easily affected by operating conditions, leading to significant deviations from their theoretical design values. Conventional system identification methods strongly rely on known external excitations and stationary operating assumptions, and therefore are difficult to apply to piezoelectric systems with time-varying parameter uncertainty and complex oscillatory dynamic responses. As a result, identification failure and insufficient accuracy are commonly encountered in practice. To address these challenges, a multi-network-structure physics-informed neural network (PINNs) method embedded with temporal Fourier feature mapping is proposed in this study. The proposed method improves the representation capability of the multiphysics model for oscillatory responses and local temporal details, thereby enabling accurate identification of key parameters and inversion of unknown excitation forces in piezoelectric systems. Numerical results show that, under free vibration, sinusoidal excitation, and random excitation conditions, the relative errors of the identified equivalent mass, equivalent stiffness, and equivalent damping ratio are all less than 5%. In addition, the unknown excitation force can also be accurately inverted. The proposed method demonstrates satisfactory identification accuracy and robustness, and can provide effective methodological support for high-precision modeling and practical design of piezoelectric energy harvesting systems.

title: Physics-inspired graph fusion and reinforcement learning agent for unsupervised cross-domain fault diagnosis
abstract: The reliable operation and accurate fault diagnosis of machinery under complex, varying operating conditions are crucial to the safety and reliability of industrial systems. However, existing unsupervised cross-domain fault diagnosis methods still suffer from limitations in modeling sample relationship topology and domain alignment. Physical information is difficult to integrate effectively with data-correlation features, and the dynamic domain alignment process lacks adaptive regulation. To address these issues, an embodied intelligence motivated physics-inspired graph fusion and reinforcement learning-based domain adaptation (PIFRLDA) method is proposed. First, a physics-inspired residual gated graph fusion mechanism is designed to construct an adaptive topology. It builds a physics-inspired graph in a latent dynamic space and adaptively fuses it with the data-driven graph through residual gating, thereby preserving sample relationships while introducing weak dynamics-related guidance into cross-condition feature interaction. A dual-path transformer sample-and-aggregate graph network is developed on the constructed graph to capture within-sample feature interactions and cross-sample topological relationships, thereby enhancing adaptability to structural correlations under complex conditions. In addition, a dual-agent cooperative domain adaptation framework is introduced to jointly optimize sample selection and feature perturbation, improving dynamic perception and adaptive regulation under varying operating conditions. Experimental results show that, compared with existing advanced unsupervised fault diagnosis methods, the proposed method offers significant advantages in both diagnostic accuracy and cross-condition generalization.

title: A novel method for bearing fault diagnosis based on deep compressive sensing and contrastive transfer learning
abstract: Bearing health monitoring is crucial in rail transit vehicles, and deep compressive sensing has gained attention for its low redundancy, minimal storage, and fast signal reconstruction. However, conventional networks often adopt single-branch convolutional structures, limiting feature stability and temporal modeling, especially under complex conditions and strong noise. Moreover, typical transfer learning approaches rely on a single loss function during fine-tuning, which, under small sample scenarios, can cause intra-class feature dispersion, blurred inter-class boundaries, and reduced discriminative ability. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a cross-domain bearing fault diagnosis method combining deep compressive sensing and contrastive transfer learning. In the compressive sensing stage, a multi-branch attention-based reconstruction network is designed to capture key signal features under complex conditions, enhancing feature richness and providing a conditional analytical explanation for the possible domain-discrepancy suppression mechanism between source and target data. In the transfer learning stage, a staged loss optimization strategy is employed: pre-training uses contrastive loss to obtain discriminative embeddings, while fine-tuning combines Triplet Loss and Cross Entropy to balance embedding structure and classification power. Experiments on Case Western Reserve University bearing open datasets and BJTU-RAO Bogie Datasets demonstrate the method’s effectiveness, achieving a signal MSE of 0.00321 and fault diagnosis accuracy of 98.51 %, highlighting its superior cross-domain diagnostic performance under small sample conditions.

title: Integrated physics-informed and unsupervised learning assessment of hemp-reinforced masonry barrel vaults under shaking table testing
abstract: The seismic assessment of strengthened masonry vaults through full-scale shaking-table testing remains limited, particularly for sustainable, heritage-compatible systems. This study investigates the dynamic response and damage evolution of full-scale masonry barrel vaults strengthened with a hemp-mesh biocomposite embedded in a cocciopesto matrix. A two-phase experimental campaign was carried out on two geometrically identical vaults subjected to progressively scaled three-component earthquake records, enabling the analysis of three representative structural configurations: unreinforced, newly reinforced, and damaged-then-reinforced. Reinforcement effectiveness and damage progression were assessed through a multi-indicator framework combining modal parameters with two proposed indicators: an energy-based indicator derived from Arias intensity and an autoencoder-based indicator. Each is formulated in a baseline-relative (excitation-dependent) form and in an input-normalized form where the energy-based indicator is normalized by the Arias intensity of the input and the autoencoder-based indicator by the squared RMS of the input. It follows that the input-normalized indicators isolate structural regime transitions from the excitation amplitude growth. Results show that the reinforcement, in both newly reinforced and damaged-then-reinforced configurations, enhances seismic capacity and damage tolerance, with delayed damage onset and reduced stiffness degradation. The proposed indicators consistently captured structural regime transitions and damage evolution across all configurations, showing strong agreement with modal trends. In particular, energy-based indicators provide a straightforward signal-level description of regime changes, while the feature-based autoencoder approach proves effective in detecting subtle statistical deviations that may precede visible damage, confirming its effectiveness in tracking stiffness degradation and nonlinear structural response.

title: Physics-guided Siamese tracker for robust vision-based structural displacement monitoring under visibility degradation
abstract: The vision-based structural displacement monitoring technique has significant potential for structural health monitoring (SHM). However, its field applications are severely limited due to reduced target visibility caused by factors such as occlusion, fog, and light changes. To address these challenges, this paper presents a robust vision-based displacement monitoring framework named CP-SiamRPN. It makes use of an enhanced deep Siamese network architecture, along with a physical consistency mechanism to eliminate non-physical drift and a confidence-guided mechanism to quantify tracking uncertainty and adjust parameters accordingly. In contrast to existing deep learning-based methods, the proposed framework has zero-shot generalization capabilities, which enable deployment on new target instances without target-specific retraining or fine-tuning. This is particularly valuable for reliable structural displacement monitoring of diverse target types under traffic or environmental interference. Systematic validation has been conducted by impact testing on simply supported beams, shake table testing on five-story frame structures, and field monitoring of bridges. The results demonstrate that, under the visibility-degradation scenarios examined (occlusion, illumination variation, and progressive blur), the proposed method maintains accurate displacement measurement and provides an explicit indicator of tracking reliability.

title: Image-to-image translation-based visual vibration displacement measurement of a rotating body with tilted viewing angle in horizontal plane
abstract: In the modern industrial field, the dynamic stability of rotating bodies is crucial to the operational efficiency and safety of equipment, and accurate measurement of their vibration displacement is of great significance. Although image recognition algorithms have already realized the visual measurement of vibration displacement of rotating bodies, the existing algorithms still have problems such as targeted data processing and relying on manual labeling. For this reason, this paper proposes a method for measuring the vibration displacement of rotating bodies with tilted viewing angles in the horizontal plane, integrating image-to-image translation with traditional vision techniques. Image-to-image translation is leveraged to convert images of rotors with tilted viewing angles captured at different oblique angles into a unified perspective. This method effectively reduces data dependency in vibration displacement extraction. Additionally, considering the characteristic features of rotor vibration images, a spatial integration and cross-dimensional optimization strategy is designed. A stepwise downsampling scheme, a DepthCascade Block (DCB) module, and a Cross-Axis Grouped Residual Block (CAGRB) module are introduced to optimize the generator network of pix2pixHD, thereby improving the quality of view transformation. The proposed method combines deep learning and traditional vision techniques to realize the vibration displacement measurement of the rotor, while eliminating human-induced errors caused by manual labeling. Based on ablation experiments, comparisons with multiple neural networks model, and comparisons with eddy current sensor data, the results show that at an acquisition rate of 2000 frames per second, the root mean square error (RMSE) for vibration displacement measurements at the three oblique angles was as low as 0.0236 mm, 0.0288 mm, and 0.0348 mm, respectively, with peak signal-to-noise ratios (PSNR) reaching 41.18 dB, 39.98 dB, and 39.65 dB, respectively. Furthermore, in comparison with image-recognition-based vibration displacement extraction methods, the proposed method can effectively extract rotor vibration displacement under stable illumination and at the three fixed tilted viewpoints tested in this study. However, a clear failure boundary is observed at viewpoint 3 under the combined effects of low illumination and a complex background.

title: A physics-informed framework for online cable force identification and Bayesian corrosion-fatigue life updating of stay cables
abstract: To address the need for cable force identification and fatigue life assessment of in-service stay cables under long-term structural health monitoring, this study proposes a monitoring-informed framework that integrates time-varying frequency extraction, rapid cable force identification, corrosion-fatigue damage evaluation, and Bayesian life updating. First, based on multi-year monitoring data from the Qingzhou Channel Bridge of the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge, the amplitude and phase estimation of a sinusoid method is employed to extract time-varying frequencies from cable acceleration responses. A dynamic-stiffness-guided micro physics-informed neural network (µDS-PINN) is then developed for rapid and accurate identification of time-varying cable forces. Second, based on time-varying stress data and combined with wind speed and temperature, a corrosion-fatigue coupled damage model is established. Finally, a Bayesian life updating model is developed to update the intercept parameter of the S–N curve posteriorly, thereby quantifying the remaining life distribution and failure probability. The results show that µDS-PINN significantly improves cable force identification efficiency while maintaining high accuracy, meeting the demand for rapid identification in long-term online monitoring scenarios. The proposed life prediction method enables probabilistic characterization of remaining life and failure risk. Long-term monitoring results show distinct cable-to-cable differences in daily fatigue damage, and the remaining life obtained through online updating is significantly negatively correlated with daily fatigue damage, demonstrating that the proposed method can continuously revise life prediction results as damage accumulates. This study provides a practical basis for fatigue state tracking, life management, and risk warning of in-service stay cables.

title: Causal Bayesian optimization for sensor placement and deconfounding in structural health monitoring
abstract: Structural health monitoring systems must distinguish genuine damage from environmental effects. Current methods rely on correlational reasoning that cannot separate causal influences from spurious associations. Temperature variations, for instance, often produce larger shifts in natural frequencies than actual structural damage does. Here, we introduce a causal inference framework that addresses this limitation at its root. A structural causal model encodes the physical relationships among environmental conditions, structural properties, damage states, and sensor measurements. Formal causal reasoning then separates the genuine effect of damage on sensor responses from the confounding influence of environmental conditions. Counterfactual analysis further allows engineers to evaluate hypothetical scenarios, such as alternative sensor layouts or different environmental conditions, without physical experimentation. Built on this causal foundation, a multi-objective Bayesian optimization algorithm identifies Pareto-optimal sensor placements that balance detection probability, localization accuracy, false alarm robustness, and instrumentation cost. Validation spans numerical and experimental benchmarks together with an end-to-end evaluation on a full-scale bridge. Causal deconfounding lowers false alarm rates compared to conventional normalization, the optimizer reaches better Pareto fronts with far fewer evaluations than evolutionary alternatives, and the advantages persist under model misspecification and hidden confounding.

title: LCA-PINN: A lightweight condition-aware physics-informed neural network for interpretable tool wear monitoring
abstract: Tool wear monitoring (TWM) is essential to ensuring product quality and sustaining the efficiency of intelligent manufacturing. However, the variability of cutting parameters across different configurations results in significant condition differences, making it difficult to generalize hybrid models built on physical formulas or empirical knowledge for specific conditions to unseen parameter combinations. To address this limitation, a lightweight condition-aware physics-informed neural network (LCA-PINN) is proposed for interpretable TWM under unseen cutting conditions. Specifically, key physical coefficients are dynamically learned by minimizing the residual between the tool wear physics equation and the observed wear. On this basis, a conditional mapping between cutting parameters and physical coefficients is established, enabling adaptive and physically consistent learning across parameter combinations. In addition, a joint data-driven and physics-driven output strategy is employed to estimate tool wear, ensuring accurate monitoring while maintaining physical consistency. Experiments on a full-lifecycle dataset covering a wide range of cutting parameter settings show that, compared with the best-performing baseline, LCA-PINN achieves relative reductions in RMSE, MAE, and MAPE of 36.30%, 34.38%, and 34.57%, respectively, along with an improvement of 2.07% in R2. Moreover, LCA-PINN exhibits favorable complexity, requiring only 5.86 kFLOPs and 23.69 KB memory, meeting the requirements for lightweight deployment in industrial applications. This study offers a feasible pathway to deploying reliable and physically consistent intelligent monitoring in advanced manufacturing environments.

title: Fusing multi-sensor data in graph convolutional networks for robust structural damage detection against environmental and operational variations
abstract: In structural health monitoring, environmental and operational variations (EOVs), along with extreme class imbalance in damage severity datasets, substantially compromise damage detection accuracy and reliability. To address these challenges, a collaborative node-edge graph convolutional network (CNEGCN) is proposed for structural damage detection, incorporating advanced feature extraction, node-edge co-embedding, and a physics-informed loss formulation. First, a reference signal reconstruction method combined with wavelet coherence is developed to extract features sensitive to structural damage while remaining robust to environmental variations. Second, a network architecture employing collaborative node-edge embedding is constructed to effectively fuse heterogeneous multi-location sensor data, specifically acceleration and strain measurements. Finally, a two-stage training scheme transitioning from conventional cross-entropy loss to a physics-informed multiple damage location assurance criterion loss is implemented to mitigate overfitting on minority damage classes. Validated across three experimental and numerical cases of varying complexity, the proposed CNEGCN demonstrates stable classification performance and strong robustness to noise and EOVs, achieving classification accuracies exceeding 0.98 and competitive Macro F1 scores. The proposed CNEGCN offers an efficient online diagnostic solution for real-time structural damage monitoring under complex environmental conditions.

title: A multi-scale frequency domain information-driven method for ultrasonic welding quality prediction
abstract: Ultrasonic welding is extensively used in industries such as automotive and electronics, where the tensile strength of the welding joints serves as a critical indicator of manufacturing quality, yet is subject to fluctuations caused by multiple uncertain factors during production. Moreover, the complex physical interactions of the process produce time series features rich in high-frequency ultrasonic information, which is critical for achieving accurate predictions of quality performance. This work develops a deep learning framework that accurately predicts joint tensile strength by fusing multi-source signals. Specifically, a high-fidelity acquisition system was established to synchronously capture high-frequency vibration, pressure, and displacement signals during welding. The proposed Gated Multi-scale Fast Fourier Transform Network (GMS-FFTNet) operates directly in the frequency domain, integrating a global Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to capture long-range dependencies and a local Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) to resolve transient details. It is enhanced by an adaptive spectral filtering mechanism that dynamically emphasizes critical frequency bands, overcoming the limitations of conventional time-domain models that often struggle with spectral information loss. To synergize the insights from different sensors, a dedicated gating network effectively fuses the multi-source signal features. The model accurately predicts tensile strength, achieving a coefficient of determination of 82.17%. Furthermore, the visualization of attention weights serves to correlate the model’s inference with the manufacturing process of the ultrasonic welding. This method not only presents a robust solution for reliable quality monitoring of ultrasonic welding but also offers a generalizable framework for other dynamic manufacturing processes with high-frequency information.

title: Physics-informed unit-normalized selective embedding with harmonic loss for fault identification using vibration and acoustic signals
abstract: Induction motors generate vibration and acoustic signals from mechanical imbalance, electromagnetic forces, and structural transmission through the machine housing. Interpreting harmonic fault signatures from these responses becomes difficult when different types of sensors are used due to bandwidth and signal scaling limitations. This work investigates how physics-informed signal representation can improve fault diagnosis using both industrial sensors and cell phone sensors. A unit-consistent normalization approach is introduced to allow comparison between vibration acceleration and acoustic pressure signals by converting both signals into equivalent vibration velocity representations. Based on this formulation, a structured signal processing framework named Unit-Normalized Selective Embedding with Harmonic Loss (UNSE-HL) is proposed, combining unit normalization, selective embedding, and a physics-informed harmonic loss function to improve the representation of modulation patterns during diagnosis. Experiments are conducted using the induction motor datasets collected under multiple operating conditions with both structurally mounted sensors and cell phones. Envelope spectral analysis shows that rotor harmonics are observable across cell phone sensors after normalization; this observability does not by itself establish classification reliability, which is evaluated separately. Time-frequency representations combined with the proposed embedding strategy improve diagnosis accuracy and classification stability relative to conventional signal representation approaches on the datasets and devices evaluated in this study. These findings highlight the importance of signal transmission physics in condition monitoring and indicate that, for the specific smartphone sensors and operating conditions tested here, appropriate preprocessing improves the usability of low-bandwidth sensors for fault diagnosis.

title: CNSAO: A complex number space anomaly observer with multi-task masked LLM autoencoder for bearing health monitoring under time-varying speeds
abstract: Health monitoring of bearings under time-varying speed conditions remains a critical challenge in industrial applications. The speed fluctuations may disrupt the phase consistency of fault-related characteristics and lead to the dispersion of fault energy. This makes it difficult to capture stable fault modes for health monitoring in the dynamic scenario. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a complex number space-based anomaly observer (CNSAO) for bearing health monitoring under time-varying speed conditions. Firstly, a multi-task autoencoder (AE) is constructed to perform signal reconstruction and rotational speed prediction. Secondly, a pre-trained large language model-based AE (LLMAE) is used as the backbone for feature extraction and noise reduction. Moreover, a residual connection is applied to LLMAE to enhance information propagation. Thirdly, a complex number space health index (CHI) is constructed to quantify bearing health degradation from both amplitude and phase similarity perspectives, which can sensitively capture phase asynchrony caused by continuous speed variations. In order to verify the effectiveness of CNSAO, three bearing health monitoring tests are performed. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed CNSAO can achieve robust early fault detection. It outperforms traditional methods in terms of detection accuracy. Moreover, the visualization results illustrate that CNSAO can accurately extract the amplitude and phase differences in the dynamic industrial scenarios.

title: A novel hybrid data-driven approach for rapid estimation of building vibration responses in urban rail transit systems
abstract: Environmental vibration assessment conducted during the preliminary stage plays a critical role in identifying vibration-sensitive objectives along the railway that may experience excessive vibrations, thereby guiding the subsequent screening process and the design of vibration mitigation measures. This assessment typically relies on empirical formulas; however, the predictive accuracy of these formulas presents certain challenges, such as the risk of overly conservative evaluations, which may lead to unnecessary design expenditures. According to the core idea of multi-stage correction of empirical formulas, this study introduces a hybrid methodology that combines Bayesian Neural Networks with soil-structure coupling loss and building impedance models to enable efficient prediction of train-induced building vibration responses. Ground vibration data were first collected from seven different locations and synthesized into a comprehensive dataset. The spatial distribution of ground vibrations and the characteristics of vibration amplification zones were then systematically examined. Thereafter, a Bayesian Neural Network model was implemented to predict ground vibrations across 1/3 octave frequency bands, while effectively addressing the inherent uncertainties in the data. In the subsequent phase, the predicted ground vibration data were used as inputs in soil-structure coupling loss and building impedance models to calculate the soil-structure coupling loss and the corresponding building vibration responses. Finally, a case study was carried out to validate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed hybrid prediction framework.

title: A joint optimization network for force identification on nonlinear structures
abstract: Accurate force identification is fundamental to the structural health monitoring and integrity assessment of complex engineering systems. However, nonlinear structural dynamics invalidate the superposition principle and render the inverse problem ill-posed, making dynamic force identification highly challenging. Existing model-driven and algorithm unrolling (AU) methods rely on explicit analytical forward models to compute Jacobian matrices, which are often unavailable for practical nonlinear structures. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a joint optimization network (JO-Net) for nonlinear structural force identification. JO-Net replaces the analytical Jacobian with an automatically differentiable surrogate model embedded in a deep unrolling framework. The surrogate network learns nonlinear forward dynamics and provides sensitivity information via automatic differentiation, while the proximal gradient descent algorithm is unrolled into a layer-wise network with a convolutional encoder–decoder serving as a learnable proximal operator. A key feature of JO-Net is the simultaneous optimization of the surrogate model and the inverse AU network, enabling adaptive refinement of structural mappings and mitigation of modeling errors. Numerical and experimental validations on nonlinear structures demonstrate that JO-Net significantly outperforms purely data-driven and model-based Kalman filter methods. By combining the surrogate model gradient with a data-driven gradient mapping matrix, the proposed method achieves a better balance between robustness and accuracy. Furthermore, JO-Net demonstrates superior robustness against measurement uncertainties and maintains reliable identification performance for unseen force–amplitude ranges within the tested nonlinear structures.

title: Deep learning based reconstruction of fiber orientation in short fiber reinforced composites from ultrasonic wave responses
abstract: Fiber orientation plays an important role in the mechanical behavior of short fiber-reinforced composites, yet its internal distribution is difficult to characterize nondestructively. This study proposes a deep learning-based framework to reconstruct fiber orientation fields from boundary ultrasonic wave responses. A two-dimensional anisotropic wave propagation model with free-boundary conditions was developed to simulate wave signals in composite plates, where the local anisotropy was governed by sectional fiber orientation. Based on this model, a synthetic dataset was generated using a sectional representation of the plate. The simulated sensor signals were used as inputs to a multilayer perceptron, while the section-wise principal-direction angles were encoded using an angle aware representation to account for periodicity. The trained model directly predicted the orientation field from the simulated boundary wave responses. Reconstruction accuracy was evaluated using wrap-aware angular error metrics. Parametric studies were conducted to examine the effects of dataset size, excitation frequency, anisotropy strength, sensor ablation, and wave transmission factor on prediction performance. The results show that the proposed framework can effectively reconstruct the main features of the section-wise principal-direction field and remains reasonably robust under varying sensing and material conditions. The proposed approach provides a promising data-driven strategy for nondestructive characterization of internal fiber orientation in short fiber-reinforced composites.

title: Intelligent non-destructive evaluation of complex defects using magnetization-excited infrared thermography
abstract: Aircraft hydraulic pipelines are critical components of aircraft hydraulic systems, and reliable inspection of their surface defects is essential for ensuring operational safety and maintenance efficiency. Existing inspection methods for ferromagnetic surface defects are often limited by specimen contamination, insufficient adaptability to complex curved structures, or low inspection efficiency. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an intelligent inspection framework that integrates Dual-mode Electromagnetic Magnetization-excited Infrared Thermography (DEMIT) with deep learning-based defect detection. By employing controllable circumferential and longitudinal magnetization, DEMIT enables rapid and non-contact inspection without contaminating the specimen surface, while promoting more uniform thermal excitation and more consistent defect-sensitive thermal responses in complex curved components. The proposed framework is further implemented in a self-developed automated inspection system to support efficient defect imaging and intelligent recognition. For accurate localization and classification of weak and small defects under complex backgrounds, a Calibration Guided Super Resolution Enhanced Transformer Detector is developed. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves mAP by 2.5 percentage points over the best-performing baseline and achieves the best overall performance on Scratch, Pit, and Mesh defects, especially for weak and small Pit defects. This study provides an efficient and practically deployable solution for intelligent inspection of surface defects in aircraft hydraulic pipelines and other complex ferromagnetic components commonly found in industrial systems.

title: A rotor dynamic balancing method without trial weights based on multi-sensor feature fusion with an attention mechanism
abstract: Accurate identification of unbalance parameters lies at the core of rotor dynamic balancing technology. In this paper, a deep learning approach is integrated with rotor dynamic balancing theory, and a multi-sensor feature fusion dynamic balancing method without trial weights based on the attention mechanism is proposed. First, considering the unique nature of the dynamic balancing process, a rotor model with varying unbalance parameters was established, and the dataset for model training was augmented by adding bandpass noise. Subsequently, a neural network model for unbalance identification based on the multi-head attention mechanism was designed, and ablation experiments were conducted to verify its superiority over single-sensor models and the feature fusion model without attention. Finally, both a finite element simulation model and an experimental model of a triple-disk rotor system were established for dynamic balancing validation. The simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed dynamic balancing method can substantially reduce the vibration amplitudes of the rotor across all critical speed regions. Moreover, compared with the influence coefficient method (ICM), the proposed method requires only a single run-up process to complete the dynamic balancing procedure, significantly improving the balancing efficiency and achieving superior balancing performance across all critical speed regions.

title: A semi-supervised compound fault diagnosis method based on hierarchical attention and self-supervised graph learning for the rotary components of robots’ joints
abstract: Rotating machinery, which is a key component of industrial robots and precision equipment, is frequently susceptible to compound faults. However, diagnosing such faults remains challenging because of the coupling interference among fault features and the scarcity of labeled fault samples. To address this issue, this study proposes a semi‑supervised intelligent fault diagnosis method that integrates hierarchical attention and self‑supervised graph learning. The proposed method employs a three-layered progressive framework. At the node level, a multi-head self-attention mechanism screens and enhances the local features of each sample. At the edge level, a self-supervised graph autoencoder based on graph attention is constructed to model the correlations between samples from different sensors at the same time steps, thereby extracting and enhancing the features of various fault types. At the feature level, global similarity matching is applied to all extracted features to uncover the intrinsic relationships between compound and single faults. Finally, only a small set of labeled samples is used to train a multi‑label classifier to achieve an accurate diagnosis and effective decoupling of fault categories. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an average accuracy of over 99.0% in diagnosing compound faults, maintaining excellent generalization and stability, even with limited training samples. This study not only presents an effective technical solution for the compound fault diagnosis of rotating machinery but also provides substantial theoretical support for the development of predictive maintenance systems in precision machinery applications.

title: Nonlinear stiffness triboelectric vibration sensor for UAV blade damage monitoring through hybrid deep learning
abstract: Real-time damage type monitoring of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) blades is essential for flight safety and operational efficiency. Vibration analysis serves as an effective approach to characterize blade damage types. However, existing vibration monitoring technologies exhibit limited responsiveness to low-acceleration vibrations and struggle to capture damage-induced signatures during flight. To address these limitations, this study proposes a nonlinear stiffness triboelectric vibration sensor (NS-TVS). Leveraging its nonlinear stiffness mechanism, the sensor achieves a broad monitoring frequency range of 5 to 1500 Hz and sensitivity to anomalous vibration responses induced by blade damage. Experimental results demonstrate the output characteristics of the NS-TVS and its adaptability to UAV. Outperforming conventional vibration sensors, the NS-TVS achieves a peak sensitivity of 8.33 V/g, an acceleration detection limit of 0.1 g, and an SNR of 45.27 dB under weak excitation. Accounting for merely 5% of a single UAV arm’s payload, it imposes negligible disturbance on blade aerodynamics. For signal processing and condition assessment, a gated-attention-based convolutional recurrent neural network (GA-CRNN) was developed for feature extraction and classification across seven predefined blade types. Experimental findings revealed that the proposed model achieved an average classification accuracy of 95.96% in identifying the predefined blade damage types. The GA-CRNN was subsequently deployed on a UAV onboard computer, and actual flight tests verified the sensor’s engineering practicality and reliability.

title: Physics-constrained neural parameter calibration of a Bouc-Wen hysteresis model for bolted joint assemblies
abstract: Bolted joints are characterized by friction-induced hysteresis and response dependence on excitation and tightening conditions, which complicates the calibration of reduced-order nonlinear models. A physics-constrained neural framework is introduced for calibrating a Bouc-Wen model using mean vibration records obtained under varying tightening torques. For each torque, a bounded neural generator proposes admissible model parameters, and a differentiable forward solver integrates displacement, velocity, and the model-internal hysteretic state. Calibration relies exclusively on measured velocity and measurement-derived displacement, while additional excitation levels are reserved for evaluating the torque-specific calibrated ensembles. Multiple independent calibration paths are maintained according to a prescribed convergence criterion and are organized using loss-informed empirical Gibbs weighting. Complete joint parameter vectors are then propagated to obtain time-domain, receptance, and hysteresis summaries. The results indicate torque-conditioned parameter organizations, consistent convergence behavior across most calibration paths, and close agreement with measured resonance locations. Propagation at excitation levels excluded from calibration further demonstrates that the calibrated ensembles can reproduce the principal amplitude-dependent response trends. The proposed framework thus offers a systematic approach for neural parameter calibration and empirical variability propagation, while preserving the prescribed Bouc-Wen dynamics throughout the inverse problem. • Physics-constrained neural calibration of Bouc-Wen bolted-joint parameters. • Mean-response calibrations are performed independently at two torques levels. • The unobserved hysteretic state is integrated using a measured-only loss. • Converged optimization paths form loss-informed joint empirical ensembles. • Frozen ensembles are propagated to amplitudes excluded from calibration.

title: Power Bond graph-embedded causal flow-aware graph neural network for fault localization of electro-hydraulic systems
abstract: To achieve precise fault localization for electro-hydraulic systems of mechanical, a Causal Flow-aware Graph Neural Network (CFAGNN) is proposed, which integrates power bond graph topology with deep learning. A power bond graph model is constructed to characterize energy transfer mechanisms and clarify dynamic coupling relationships among subsystems, providing quantifiable physical constraints and edge-node attributes. To accommodate real-time operating conditions, learnable edge attributes are constructed with embedded dynamic correction parameters. These physical priors are embedded into the Causal Flow Attention (CFA) mechanism, where physical regularization and causal direction loss are utilized to constrain attention coefficients to conform to energy transfer laws, thereby enabling accurate tracking of fault propagation paths. Validation on a real engineering machinery dataset demonstrates that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art models. The results indicate that CFAGNN balances diagnostic accuracy and computational efficiency effectively, providing a reliable solution for the fault diagnosis of complex electro-hydraulic systems.

title: Early anomaly detection in wind Turbines by Causality-based graph attention networks
abstract: Early anomaly detection is a key issue for ensuring reliability, availability and efficiency in Wind Turbines (WTs) operation. Traditional condition monitoring techniques struggle to identify anomalies because of: i) the strong interconnections among the subsystems of a WT, which induce complex spatio-temporal dependencies in the measured signals and can enable the cascading propagation of the effects of anomalies, ii) the variability of the operating conditions, which can affect the anomaly signatures, and iii) the presence of control systems that can mask the anomalies signatures. To address these challenges, this work proposes a novel anomaly detection method employing a Graph Neural Network (GNN) autoencoder. GNN is selected for its capability in modeling the interconnected nature of subsystems and capturing the spatio-temporal dependencies in operational signals. A key contribution is the use of the Granger causality test to generate the GNN functional graph. By leveraging the causal relationships among turbine signals, the obtained graph ensures that the learned topology reflects the underlying physical dependencies rather than spurious correlations, as it may occur in traditional graphs. To handle variability of the operating conditions, graph attention layers adaptively weight sensor relationships, while gated recurrent units process the temporal dynamics. The proposed method is validated on synthetic data simulated using a high-fidelity WT model and applied to SCADA data collected from real WTs. Results demonstrate a 4% increase in recall and a 45% reduction in detection delay compared to state-of-the-art methods.

title: Multistage health state estimation and uncertainty quantification for bearing remaining useful life via graph-guided representation learning
abstract: Bearing degradation follows stochastic and nonlinear trajectories, which makes the accurate prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) a critical challenge in industrial prognostics. Recent deep learning-based methods have achieved promising performance in bearing RUL prediction. However, they have limited ability to explicitly account for changes in degradation behavior during the prognostic process. Health-stage information has been employed to characterize degradation progression, but it is typically used only for stage estimation rather than guiding degradation representation learning or RUL prediction. To address this limitation, we propose the Stage-Aware Graph-guided Embedding-Uncertainty Quantification (SAGE-UQ) framework. The proposed framework consistently leverages health-stage information through degradation representation learning and uncertainty-aware RUL prediction. Specifically, graph-guided spectral representation learning and stage-aware temporal contrastive learning were employed to jointly estimate health-stage information. This estimated stage information is further exploited to learn degradation representations that capture health-stage transition characteristics. It is then leveraged to guide uncertainty-aware RUL predictions. The proposed framework explicitly incorporates health-stage transition ambiguity into predictive uncertainty. Experimental results demonstrate that SAGE-UQ consistently outperforms representative baselines and recent state-of-the-art methods. It achieves an average root-mean-square error (RMSE) reduction of approximately 17.4%. The lightweight architecture and low inference latency enhance its practicality for online prognostic applications.

title: TimeXer-based main bearing temperature prediction and Bayesian fault early warning for offshore wind turbines via transfer learning
abstract: Main bearing failures are a primary driver of offshore wind turbine unplanned downtime, yet data-driven monitoring methods lack cross-turbine generalization and probabilistic fault detection. This study proposes an integrated framework combining the TimeXer model, transfer learning, and a two-stage Bayesian fault early warning system for main bearing temperature prediction. The TimeXer model applies patch-level tokenization to endogenous variables and cross-variable attention to exogenous SCADA inputs, capturing temporal dependencies and inter-variable coupling. Fault early warning sequentially applies a three-sigma threshold, Bayesian posterior probability estimation, and a three-step persistence criterion to suppress false alarms. A two-phase transfer learning protocol adapts the source-domain model to target turbines using limited data. Validated on 41,906 ten-minute SCADA samples from Yangjiang, China, the model achieves R2 = 0.9898, RMSE = 0.3172 °C, and MAE = 0.1636 °C on the 58# 8.3 MW source turbine, surpassing Transformer, LSTM, and XGBoost baselines by up to 42.1% in RMSE. Transfer to the 24# 6.8 MW and 33# 8.3 MW target turbines yields R2 = 0.9851 and 0.9840, with RMSE below the source baseline. The early warning system attains a step-level false alarm rate of 2.1% with a 94.4% detection rate, and component-wise ablation, prior sensitivity analysis and residual normality testing are reported to substantiate each design choice. Normalized error analysis further shows that the lower target-domain RMSE reflects the reduced temperature variability of the target machines rather than an accuracy gain. The framework provides a scalable pathway for offshore wind turbine predictive maintenance.

title: Feature–label similarity-aware hypergraph attention network: A semi-supervised fault diagnosis method for machinery under extremely low label rate scenarios
abstract: Label propagation algorithms (LPAs) and graph neural networks (GNNs) are semi-supervised learning models that have yielded satisfactory results in machinery fault diagnosis under limited labeled data conditions. However, LPAs consider only label similarity, while GNNs primarily focus on feature similarity, and both encode pairwise connections that inherently fail to capture high-order correlations, consequently limiting the ability to make full use of scarce labeled and massive unlabeled data. To address the above limitations, this paper proposes a novel semi-supervised learning model, named feature–label similarity-aware hypergraph attention network, to jointly model high-order feature and label similarities for machinery fault diagnosis under extremely low label rate scenarios. Firstly, a hypergraph of all samples is constructed to encode their high-order correlations beyond pairwise connections. Then, a hypergraph attention network is constructed, in which a cross-attention mechanism is employed to adaptively learn the importance weights of node–hyperedge interactions, facilitating propagation and aggregation of class-specific features along hyperedges from both labeled and unlabeled samples. Subsequently, a hypergraph LPA is integrated into the proposed framework, propagating label information from labeled samples to their neighbors, to fully exploit scarce label information. Finally, the semi-supervised fault diagnosis model is jointly optimized by imposing supervised constraints on classifier predictions and propagated labels for labeled samples, along with a consistency constraint between them for unlabeled samples. Experimental results on three machinery fault diagnosis datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior diagnostic accuracy compared with the state-of-the-art approaches, especially when the label rate is as low as 1 %. The related code was released at https://github.com/yushi1006/FLSHGAT-for-semi-supervised-fault-diagnosis.

title: An integrated autoencoder-based framework for unsupervised domain adaptation in structural health monitoring of bridges
abstract: The limited availability of long-term bridge-monitoring data presents a significant obstacle to the application of machine learning in structural health monitoring (SHM). Domain adaptation offers a means of addressing this data scarcity, but existing methods often have limited generalization and are sensitive to hyperparameter choices. This study proposes a reconstruction-based domain adaptation framework in which target-domain observations are geometrically aligned with the latent space learned by an autoencoder trained on data from a source bridge and, subsequently, reconstructed using its decoder. Unlike conventional feature-alignment approaches, the proposed formulation transfers the reconstruction model itself, enabling target-domain evaluation without labels, classifier retraining, or threshold recalibration. The autoencoder is trained on baseline data collected during commissioning of the source bridge, using observations composed of natural frequencies as damage-sensitive features. Adaptation is performed through orthogonal Procrustes alignment in the latent space, followed by reconstruction with the source-trained decoder. Validation using the Z24 Bridge dataset demonstrates that the framework mitigates seasonal domain shift while preserving sensitivity to controlled damage. The approach is then transferred to a twin bridge over the Itacaiúnas River using only latent-space alignment and no model retraining. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables damage assessment across bridges while substantially reducing the data and training requirements for practical deployment.

title: Tool-grounded large language models for decision-level fusion in fault diagnosis
abstract: Modern condition-monitoring systems generate heterogeneous information, such as high-rate sensor streams, derived health indicators, and discrete event histories, that must be combined into actionable diagnostic statements. Large language models (LLMs) are attractive as a decision-level fusion mechanism because they natively handle the textual modality, but their use in safety-critical fault diagnosis is impeded by hallucinated numerical content and stochastic outputs. This paper proposes a two-level information-fusion framework that uses an LLM as a constrained fusion operator rather than as a generator of facts. At the feature level, a recursive joint state-and-fault estimator built on a linear state-space model produces a vector of derived indicators, including an estimate of the actuator-fault parameter and its uncertainty. At the decision level, the LLM is restricted to interact with the estimator state and the event history exclusively through a finite library of typed deterministic tools, and must copy every numerical token in its response from a tool output. Grounding of the response is then satisfied by construction, and consistency follows once the sequence of tool calls is fixed. The framework is illustrated on a realistic actuator-fault scenario in which an autopilot-driven autonomous surface vessel encounters three fault events of different characters and the LLM produces reproducible operator-facing reports. A structured comparison against the two alternative reporting architectures available for this task, a rule-based template reporter driven by the same estimator and a flat-prompt LLM given the same numerical context, identifies open-ended query coverage at fixed numerical reliability as the property that neither alternative provides, and states the metrics under which that claim is to be tested.

title: Performance-based probabilistic RUL prediction via particle filtering with neural-guided inference
abstract: Accurate prediction of the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is essential for efficient operations and predictive maintenance of industrial systems. Prognostics is traditionally structured as a two-step procedure comprising estimation of the current system condition and prediction of future behavior and condition. Many data-driven approaches map sensor measurements directly to RUL without explicitly modeling degradation dynamics. We propose a data-driven prognostic framework that preserves this estimation–prediction structure without requiring physics-based state models. In the estimation stage, health indices are inferred from sensor measurements. Degradation parameters are treated probabilistically and inferred within a Bayesian framework, with online sequential updates via particle filtering. In the prediction stage, the stochastic degradation model is evaluated conditioned on the inferred parameter posterior, yielding an RUL distribution as a random variable with a hitting time. An offline-trained neural network serves as a particle-filter (PF) controller to improve adaptability while maintaining principled uncertainty propagation. Evaluation on the N-CMAPSS benchmark demonstrates competitive RUL accuracy and statistically grounded uncertainty across operating conditions, and comparisons indicate the advantages of explicitly separating estimation from prediction in data-driven prognostics.

title: Cost-sensitive active learning for rotating machinery fault diagnosis under data imbalance
abstract: Data-driven fault diagnosis has become an important approach for ensuring the reliability and safety of rotating machinery. However, practical deployment is often hindered by severe data imbalance and label scarcity. Active learning (AL) mitigates label scarcity by selecting the most informative samples for annotation to improve model performance. Nevertheless, conventional AL strategies typically optimize for overall accuracy and treat all misclassifications equally. Consequently, they fail to account for the asymmetric operational costs of diagnostic errors, particularly the greater losses caused by missed detections and severity underestimation. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a cost-sensitive active learning (CS-AL) framework tailored for highly imbalanced fault distributions. In this framework, raw vibration signals are first transformed into two-dimensional time–frequency representations via continuous wavelet transform (CWT). A Bayesian convolutional neural network, integrated with a convolutional block attention module, is developed to extract fault-sensitive features, while epistemic uncertainty is quantified through Monte Carlo (MC) dropout. To explicitly penalize high-risk errors during sample selection, an asymmetric diagnostic cost matrix is constructed to formulate a cost-sensitive acquisition score based on the expected pairwise misclassification cost. To optimize annotation efficiency, a diversity-aware clustering mechanism selects representative prototypes from this high-risk candidate pool. Experimental validations on the CWRU bearing and MCC5-THU gearbox datasets demonstrate that the CS-AL framework achieves enhanced diagnostic performance and significantly reduces high-cost misclassification risks compared to representative AL baselines. The results confirm the effectiveness of CS-AL in accurately allocating limited labeling resources to rare, safety-critical faults while minimizing total operational risk under imbalanced conditions.

title: Deep reinforcement learning for semi-active structural control using a variable inerter device
abstract: Structural control devices employing inerters have attracted considerable attention owing to their superior vibration mitigation performance. Variable inerter devices, which enable real-time adjustment of inertance and damping, offer further performance enhancement but also introduce a challenging nonlinear control problem. This paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based control strategy for a tuned variable inertial mass electromagnetic transducer (TVIMET) installed in a five-story base-isolated building. The proposed controller is developed using recurrent proximal policy optimization (RPPO) with long short-term memory (LSTM) networks to account for both the partially observable nature of practical structural control and the history-dependent nonlinear behavior of the lead–rubber bearing (LRB) isolation system. Numerical simulations are conducted under a wide range of earthquake excitations, and the proposed method is compared with passive base isolation, a passive tuned viscous mass damper (TVMD), and a semi-active tuned inertial mass electromagnetic transducer (TIMET). The proposed TVIMET successfully adapts both the inertance and damping coefficient according to the changing dynamic characteristics of the structure. Unlike the passive TVMD, which is designed assuming post-yield structural behavior, the proposed controller remains effective even under earthquake excitations that do not induce significant yielding of the isolation layer. It also achieves the best overall vibration reduction, particularly in terms of the RMS structural responses. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of simultaneously adapting the inertance and damping through DRL for nonlinear structural vibration control.

title: Adaptive and uncertainty-aware surrogate modeling for reliability analysis of nonlinear dynamic systems
abstract: Reliability analysis of nonlinear inelastic dynamic systems under uncertainty remains a critical challenge, owing to the path-dependent, high-dimensional nature of the problem. To this end, this paper proposes an adaptive and uncertainty-aware surrogate modeling framework comprising three synergistic components. The first component is the aLSTM–SNGP surrogate model, an uncertainty-aware surrogate for nonlinear dynamic systems that integrates an attention-enhanced LSTM (aLSTM) encoder with a Spectral-normalized Neural Gaussian Process (SNGP) predictor, jointly optimized through end-to-end co-training. The aLSTM encoder processes excitation sequences and system parameters together, capturing temporal dependencies while implicitly reducing dimensionality; the SNGP predictor provides scalable uncertainty-aware prediction through random Fourier feature approximation. The second component develops two surrogate-based failure probability estimation methods: Method I (aLSTM-SNGP-MCS) based on direct Monte Carlo simulation, and Method II (aLSTM-SNGP-IS) based on importance sampling with an adaptively constructed proposal density that concentrates sampling effort in failure-prone regions. The third component is an adaptive exploration–exploitation refinement strategy that iteratively refines the surrogate model by combining active learning with an alternating training scheme of full training and local fine-tuning. The framework is validated under stochastic seismic excitations through two examples: a numerical example based on a six-story nonlinear inelastic shear building model with Bouc-Wen hysteresis, and a practical engineering example based on a nine-story SAC steel frame represented by a nonlinear finite element model. Results demonstrate that both methods yield accurate failure probability estimates while significantly reducing the number of evaluations to the simulation model relative to crude Monte Carlo simulation, with Method II outperforming Method I.

title: Physics-informed identification of dynamic propeller excitations via EM-based Kalman filtering
abstract: Accurate identification of propeller-induced hydrodynamic loads is crucial for vibration control and structural reliability in propeller propulsion systems. However, direct measurement of propeller excitation is infeasible due to the harsh operating environment and inherent structural constraints, which necessitates indirect identification approaches such as Kalman filtering. While these methods enable online estimation external inputs, the conventional random-walk assumption fails to represent the colored nature of hydrodynamic excitations, leading to spectrum mismatch and potential instability. To address this limitation, this study proposes an adaptive identification framework that integrates a scaled spherical simplex filter (S3F) with a physics-informed latent force model. The latent model combines an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck (OU) process with a single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) system to simultaneously capture the broadband attenuation and hump-resonance features of propeller loads. Furthermore, to mitigate the difficulty of filter parameter tuning, an adaptive expectation–maximization (EM) strategy is incorporated to update noise covariances directly from structural response measurements, thereby enhancing robustness against uncertain prior settings. Numerical simulations and experimental validations confirm that, compared with the random-walk assumption, the proposed method significantly suppresses low-frequency drift, improves estimation accuracy, and maintains stability under varying noise conditions. These results highlight the method’s potential as a reliable strategy for indirect hydrodynamic load identification in propeller propulsion systems.

title: FNO-PD: A Fourier neural operator-based physics-based data-driven framework for efficient dynamic response computation in vehicle-track coupled systems
abstract: Accurate and efficient computation of dynamic responses in vehicle-track coupled systems is essential for safe, smooth, and reliable high-speed railway operation and maintenance optimization. However, traditional numerical simulation methods exhibit a significant efficiency bottleneck in solving large-scale dynamic problems, while existing deep learning approaches struggle to accurately characterize the global dynamic coupling characteristics of the system. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel Fourier neural operator-based physics-based data-driven (FNO-PD) framework for the efficient prediction of dynamic responses in vehicle-track coupled systems. The framework comprises a physics-driven module and a data-driven module: the physics-driven module integrates physical information into FNO to predict train dynamic responses, while the data-driven module combines proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) with FNO for rail displacement field prediction. The accuracy and efficiency of the proposed framework are evaluated using the probability density evolution method (PDEM) as a benchmark. Within the same vehicle-track numerical framework, the model is assessed for numerical generalization under measured track irregularity inputs, near-range speed extrapolation, and robustness to noise interference. Results demonstrate that the FNO-PD framework achieves high prediction accuracy and online computational efficiency, with good agreement between its predictions and the PDEM results. During online prediction, the proposed method achieves an approximately 1200-fold speedup over PDEM. Tests conducted with measured track irregularity inputs at speeds within and just outside the training range, together with noise interference tests, indicate satisfactory numerical generalization and noise robustness under the tested conditions. This study provides a novel and efficient technical pathway for the numerical prediction of dynamic responses in vehicle-track coupled systems, with potential for large-scale numerical analyses in high-speed railway engineering.

title: Complex-amplitude design of dynamic acoustic holography via physics-assisted neural network
abstract: Acoustic holography promises diverse applications, including high-resolution imaging, water–air communication, and in-vivo tissue/organ printing. While complex-amplitude design of acoustic holography yields superior performance in resolution and information content for sophisticated acoustic fields, but most holograms are spatially and temporally static once fabricated. This dilemma may be addressed by introducing the incident wavefront modulation as an additional degree of freedom, and dynamic holography would be realized by tuning the incident wavefronts via electrically switching a transducer array. Here, we propose a physics-assisted neural network optimization framework for the complex-amplitude design of dynamic acoustic holography, which enables joint optimization of multiple incident amplitude and phase profile. The framework embeds an angular-spectrum propagation model into neural network and introduces amplitude-binarization regularization to enable dynamic control through an electrically switched partitioned transducer. Furthermore, the proposed method exhibits remarkable versatility, supporting the phase modulations in either continuous or binary manner and even cascaded configuration. As a proof-of-concept demonstration, it successfully achieves the dynamic display of three-frame animations and 26 alphabetic letters, creating compelling “acoustic movies”. Quantitatively, the proposed method outperforms traditional designs both numerically and experimentally, which reduces mean squared error by 24.1% and 32.1%, respectively. We believe this work would greatly advance acoustic holography and imply unprecedented opportunity for broad acoustics.

title: Sensitivity-driven model updating for bridge structures using operational modal analysis and enhanced batched Thompson sampling-based Bayesian optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a robust and effective finite element model updating (FEMU) framework for inverse parameter identification of bridge structures by integrating operational modal analysis (OMA) and variance-based global sensitivity analysis (GSA) with an enhanced batched Thompson sampling-based Bayesian optimization (ETS-BO) method. Specifically, a Gaussian process (GP) model is constructed to approximate the nonlinear relationship between uncertain structural parameters and the corresponding modal responses. Leveraging the trained GP model, the variance-based GSA identifies the most influential parameters governing the dynamic behavior of the bridge, thereby significantly reducing the dimensionality of the FEMU problem and improving computational efficiency. Building upon the reduced parameter space, the ETS-BO method is developed by integrating an adaptive trust-region selection strategy with an enhanced batched Thompson sampling (ETS) method to efficiently solve the FEMU problem. The adaptive trust-region selection evaluates the improvement potential at the regional level, guiding the search toward promising regions of the parameter space while avoiding over-exploration of less promising ones. The trust region method is then applied to perform local optimization, whereby each trust region is adaptively expanded or contracted based on its observed improvement history, and local optimization runs exhibiting greater potential for further improvement are selectively continued. Within the selected trust regions, the ETS method is employed to determine the optimal updating parameters by iteratively selecting batches of candidate solutions sampled from the posterior distributions of the corresponding independent GP models. The effectiveness of the proposed ETS-BO is validated through a real-world case study of a bridge structure equipped with wireless accelerometers for vibration monitoring. Ambient vibration responses recorded under normal traffic conditions are analyzed using OMA to identify modal parameters, which subsequently serve as targets for updating the finite element (FE) model developed to represent the structural behavior of the bridge. The results demonstrate that the proposed ETS-BO requires substantially fewer FE evaluations than conventional optimization methods while achieving rapid convergence toward the optimal solution. Furthermore, the updated FE model closely reproduces the experimentally identified modal parameters, including natural frequencies and mode shape correlations, thereby providing a reliable numerical representation of the in-service dynamic behavior of the bridge and demonstrating the potential of the proposed framework to support long-term structural health monitoring of large-scale civil infrastructure systems.

title: A multimodal fusion network guided by environmental semantics for reconstructing missing bridge strain trends
abstract: Long term bridge strain trends describe the gradual evolution of structural responses under environmental actions and operational loads, providing important information for structural health monitoring and condition assessment. However, communication interruptions, sensor abnormalities, and unstable data transmission can lead to missing strain data, which affects the completeness of monitoring records and the reliability of subsequent analysis. This study proposes an environmental semantics-guided multimodal fusion network for reconstructing missing bridge strain trends. The network mainly consists of an environmental semantic modulation module and a temporal reconstruction module. The environmental semantic modulation module encodes environmental textual descriptions into semantic representations and introduces environmental contextual information through feature-wise semantic modulation. The temporal reconstruction module uses a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D CNN) to extract local trend variation features and a modified Transformer encoder to model long-range temporal dependencies, enabling environment-aware strain trend reconstruction. Based on strain data obtained from a real bridge field monitoring experiment, this study constructs several typical missing scenarios and validates the proposed method through comparison with multiple baseline methods. The results show that the proposed model can effectively recover the original strain trends under different missing conditions and outperforms the compared methods in terms of reconstruction accuracy and robustness. Ablation experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of the environmental semantic modulation and temporal reconstruction modules.
