title: LLM-CECM: A simulation framework for strategic generation behavior in coupled electricity-carbon markets
abstract: The deep integration of electricity and carbon markets creates a coupled decision environment in which generators must coordinate energy offers, quota positions, and expectations about policy shocks. Traditional market simulators often either simplify strategic cognition or incur prohibitive computational cost when richer reasoning is introduced. This paper proposes LLM-CECM, a rolling multi-agent simulation framework in which carbon-order submission, carbon-cost feedback, and electricity dispatch interact at every time step. The framework combines: (1) LLM-enabled agents with persona, memory, and belief modules; (2) an Adaptive Decision Frequency (ADF) mechanism that allocates expensive reasoning only to informative periods; and (3) a fixed-depth Iterated Belief Revision with Counterfactual Reasoning (IBR-CR) heuristic for anticipating rival responses. In the reported IEEE 118-bus/AEMO-based experiments, ADF reduces LLM calls by 80.5% and runtime by 81.5%, while IBR-CR lowers the rolling price-volatility proxy from 5.49 to 2.69 CNY/MWh. Event-window diagnostics further show that thermal agents increase markups and quota purchases during a pre-announced multi-event stress sequence involving demand tightening, coal outages, and later renewable relief. These results should be interpreted as empirical evidence from a rolling simulation framework rather than a proof of equilibrium existence, uniqueness, or Nash convergence in the underlying coupled market game.

title: A hybrid intelligent approach for university building energy management: Integrating GABP prediction with improved PSO scheduling
abstract: Accurate energy load forecasting is crucial for optimizing the dispatch of integrated renewable energy systems, specially building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) systems, and advancing the “dual carbon” goals in the building sector. A comprehensive energy system study should encompass precise load forecasting, efficient energy systems, and effective optimization scheduling. While neural network-based forecasting models are prone to falling into local optima, traditional PSO for microgrid optimization suffer from slow convergence and rigid constraint handling mechanism. Therefore, this paper proposes a GABP (Genetic Algorithm-based Back Propagation‌) load forecasting model based on energy-level classification and establishes a microgrid system comprising teaching buildings, laboratory buildings, and dormitory buildings. To minimize the daily comprehensive power supply cost, an improved PSO algorithm is adopted for low-carbon dispatch. Improvements include an adaptive inertia weight linearly decreasing from 0.9 to 0.4 to balance global and local search, and a mutation after velocity updates to expand the search range and escape local optima. The results demonstrate that the optimized load forecasting model achieves higher accuracy, with reductions in MAE, RMSE, and MSE, along with increases in R2 by 9%, 5.7%, and 1% for teaching buildings, laboratory buildings, and dormitory buildings, respectively. Following optimization, the economic benefits on each typical day increased by 503.2% (June 23rd), 450.3% (September 11th), and 96.5% (December 25th). The three typical days reduced carbon emissions by 160.0 kg, 197.2 kg, and 485.5 kg respectively. This study provides theoretical insights for the development of zero-carbon campus microgrids.

title: Reducing market risk in run-of-river hydropower: The economic value of improving predictions of day-ahead production
abstract: Accurate streamflow forecasts are essential for optimizing hydropower production and reducing market imbalance costs, particularly for small-scale hydropower plants with limited storage capacity. This study evaluates the potential of an LSTM neural network for hourly streamflow prediction at operationally monitored hydropower systems with limited historical observations and assesses its economic value in a hydropower production context. The effect of two aspects on prediction accuracy is investigated: (i) including back-calculated streamflow data from 110 run-of-river hydropower plants during training, and (ii) implementation of a data assimilation (DA) approach using back-calculated streamflow as input. The performance of the model is assessed in a perfect weather forecast context using regional reanalysis data and compared with both a persistence model and the operational model currently used by the largest small-scale hydropower operator in the Nordics, Småkraft AS. The results show that including data from hydropower plants in training provides the model with valuable information, while data assimilation yields the greatest performance gain. The proposed model has the potential to decrease annual imbalance fees for Småkraft AS by 23.6% (143 kEUR) compared to the model currently used and reduces exposure to extreme prices in the balancing market by reducing the CVaR 75 with 16% (380 kEUR). The findings demonstrate that enhanced hydrological forecasting reduces imbalance cost and market risk, while supporting more stable grid operations.

title: Transformer prediction decomposition dual-driver for maximum power point tracking under partial shading conditions of photovoltaic power generation systems
abstract: Solar power, as a form of environmentally friendly and sustainable energy, has attracted considerable attention in the field of renewable energy power generation. However, the power curves of photovoltaic arrays are highly complex due to the inherent nonlinear characteristics of photovoltaic modules. To address the challenges of global maximum power point tracking under complex conditions, this study proposes a Transformer prediction decomposition dual-driver algorithm. The Transformer prediction decomposition dual-driver algorithm first utilizes a Transformer network to rapidly and accurately predict global maximum power point values of photovoltaic systems. Subsequently, the proposed algorithm integrates complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise mode decomposition, fractional order proportional-integral-derivative control, and deep Q-network technology to achieve dual-mode control, thereby enhancing the stability of the control process. This study compares the Transformer prediction decomposition dual-driver algorithm with conventional algorithms and intelligent optimization algorithms under various shading conditions through simulation and hardware-in-the-loop experiments. Compared to other algorithms, the Transformer prediction decomposition dual-driver algorithm achieves a minimum increase in mean tracking efficacy of 0.1034% while concurrently reducing the mean tracking duration by no less than 0.0371 s. In physical experimental results, the proposed method exhibits minimal power disturbance compared to the reference algorithms.

title: Optimization of wind-PV-storage aggregated inertia coefficient using physics-informed neural network to suppress frequency oscillations in hydropower-dominated power systems
abstract: Low-frequency oscillations can severely threaten frequency stability of hydropower-dominated power systems. Although such oscillations can be mitigated by adjusting the proportional-integral-derivative parameters of hydro turbine governors, this adjustment compromises the primary frequency regulation capability of hydro units. Wind, photovoltaic and energy storage systems are increasingly being integrated into hydropower delivery networks, and the fast regulation capabilities of these renewable sources offer an alternative solution to suppress both hydro unit power swings and system frequency oscillations. To make use of these capabilities, this paper proposes a novel coordinated control strategy for wind-photovoltaic-energy storage systems to suppress frequency oscillations in hydropower-dominated power grids. The key innovation of the proposed strategy lies in the use of a physics-informed neural network to dynamically optimize the aggregated virtual inertia coefficient of the wind-photovoltaic-energy storage system. This enables adaptive allocation of active power among wind, photovoltaic and energy storage units under different frequency deviation deadbands. Importantly, the proposed method achieves effective oscillation damping without modifying the existing hydro turbine governors. The performance of the proposed strategy is validated through real-time simulations on an RTLAB-based wind-photovoltaic-hydro-energy storage delivery system model. The corresponding results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively suppresses power oscillations in the multi-source system and significantly enhances the primary frequency regulation performance, confirming its potential for practical implementation.

title: 3D urban solar potential assessment using data-efficient deep learning in Lhasa (City of sunshine)
abstract: Low-carbon energy transitions are essential for climate change mitigation, yet urban solar potential assessments often emphasize rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems. Consequently, façade solar potential, solar-thermal (ST) yield, and solar supply–demand contributions are underexplored. It is an acute gap for Lhasa, China (“City of Sunshine”), where solar resources are abundant, but potential remains unquantified. The study proposes a three-dimensional assessment method integrating geographical potential (rooftop and façade solar radiation), technical potential (PV and ST outputs), and comprehensive potential (solar contribution to building energy consumption) to address this gap. A deep learning model for building height estimation was developed, reducing training images by 72.1% while cutting errors by 18.2%. A 3D urban model was derived, and three-tiered solar potential was calculated. The results highlight notable facades and ST potential. During the heating season, roofs and south facades receive comparable solar radiation. With an optimal PV-ST configuration, annual electricity production covers Lhasa’s residential demand, and thermal energy meets 69.5% of heating requirements. Solar energy supply proportion varies significantly across land use types and block forms. Transportation Land exhibits the highest solar energy supply proportion (54.5%), while Industrial and Mining Land shows the lowest (29.6%). High floor area ratio blocks can effectively utilize facade solar energy. The work extends solar potential analysis to include facades and thermal systems, providing an evaluation method adaptable to cities globally.

title: Machine learning model of hydrokinetic energy harnessing for tandem cylinders in flow-induced oscillation based on limited systemic data
abstract: The vortex-induced vibration for aquatic clean energy converter with two tandem cylinders, on elastic end-supports, can extract marine hydrokinetic energy into electricity through synergistic flow-induced oscillation. Its performance depends strongly on the spacing ratio of tandem oscillators and other flow and system parameters. In this paper, the energy harvesting potential at a high spacing of 4.57 diameters is explored, compared with the previous values of 1.57, 2.0, and 2.57. To achieve rapid parameter optimization for power and efficiency harvesting, we propose an efficient optimization framework combining an accurate machine learning prediction model with a levy flight particle swarm optimization algorithm. The main conclusions are: (1) A spacing ratio of 4.57 improves the harvested power and efficiency from flow-induced oscillation owing to wake interference. (2) By refining parameter resolution, particularly by capturing the optimal spacing ratio of 3.5, the optimization framework improves vortex-induced vibration power by 1.09-3.28 times compared to experimental optima from limited parameters. (3) The tandem-cylinder system outperforms a single-cylinder system, achieving 2.09-8.25 times higher optimal power and 37%-288% greater optimal efficiency based on the Betz Limit. (4) The global maximum power efficiency occurs at the end of galloping with a high spacing ratio of 4.57, low spring stiffness, and damping ratio. Global optimization reveals novel synergistic parameter effects on energy harvesting—patterns not discernible through conventional methods—and offers direct design guidance.

title: Resilient real-time operational planning of smart grids with electric vehicle battery swapping stations
abstract: The growing deployment of electric vehicle battery swapping stations, distributed generation, dynamic switches, and communication-based controllers, together with renewable generation variability, uncertain demand, network reconfiguration requirements, false data injection attacks, and communication delays, makes the operation of modern distribution networks a complex cyber-physical challenge. This paper proposes a real-time operational planning framework that integrates a multi-objective optimization method with a long short-term memory neural network for hour-ahead decision-making. The framework jointly considers battery swapping station operation, uncertainty modelling through fuzzy Monte Carlo simulation, cyber-physical disturbances, dynamic network reconfiguration, short-circuit level and loadability constraints, expected energy not supplied, environmental penalties, and dynamic security assessment based on a virtual synchronous generator model. Operational scenarios generated during the offline stage are used to train the neural network. During online operation, the trained model predicts near-optimal generation dispatch, power exchange at battery swapping stations, and dynamic switch states without repeatedly solving the optimization problem. Simulation results obtained from a modified 118-bus test system expanded to 124 buses for distribution-level operational studies and incorporating microgrids, renewable energy resources, battery swapping stations, energy storage systems, and dynamic switches show reductions in operating cost and expected energy not supplied, together with improvements in voltage security, reliability, resilience, loadability, and short-circuit level control compared with existing methods.

title: Cooperative wake steering for wind farm power enhancement under dynamic inflow conditions: An entropy-regularized multi-agent reinforcement learning approach
abstract: Wake interactions among wind turbines can significantly reduce wind farm energy production under dynamically varying inflow conditions. To improve wind farm power generation while mitigating wake-induced losses, this study develops a cooperative yaw-control framework for active wake steering under steady and time-varying wind conditions. The framework is based on a multi-agent reinforcement learning approach, enabling coordinated yaw-angle regulation among multiple turbines while accounting for wake interactions and changing inflow conditions. Simulation studies were conducted with a reduced-order wind farm flow model across steady and dynamic wind scenarios. The proposed strategy was compared with conventional greedy control, differential evolution optimization, and deep deterministic policy gradient control. The results demonstrate faster convergence, improved power generation, and more stable yaw-control behavior. Under dynamically varying wind conditions, the strategy effectively mitigates wake effects and achieves improved power performance with stable yaw control. Across multiple dynamic wind scenarios, it achieves an average power improvement of approximately 8.6% relative to greedy control and generally outperforms the comparison methods. Reduced cumulative yaw activity further indicates improved control smoothness and lower actuator utilization. A separate held-out generalization evaluation using stochastic wind episodes shows that the learned policy maintains robust performance on previously unseen wind realizations within the predefined scenario ranges. These results demonstrate the potential of cooperative wake steering to enhance wind farm energy capture and provide a promising framework for dynamic wind farm control.

title: Probabilistic voltage forecasting of hydrogen fuel cells with a data-driven mean-guided model for performance assessment
abstract: Accurate voltage forecasting is essential for performance assessment and safe operation of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) in renewable hydrogen systems. However, PEMFC voltage exhibits strong stochasticity and nonstationarity under degradation and varying operating conditions, which limits deterministic forecasting methods and complicates predictive maintenance. In this study, we propose DMG-PVF, a data-driven mean-guided probabilistic voltage forecasting framework for multi-step PEMFC performance assessment. DMG-PVF first employs an Attention-based Feature Extraction (AFE) module to capture temporal dependencies and cross-series interactions from historical stack-voltage sequences and generate a structured mean prior. This prior is then incorporated into a modified conditional diffusion process, guiding both forward perturbation and reverse generation so that the model produces future voltage distributions rather than only point estimates. Experiments on two real-world PEMFC datasets show that DMG-PVF achieves relative error reductions of 19.51% and 23.33% over TimeDiff on FC1 and FC2, and 29.13% and 27.17% over D3VAE, while producing uncertainty-aware prediction intervals. These results indicate that probabilistic voltage forecasting can support predictive maintenance, risk-aware dispatch, and reliable performance assessment of PEMFC-based systems powered by renewable hydrogen.

title: Data-driven artificial intelligence for wind speed forecasting: A decade review and multi-site benchmark for operational wind energy applications
abstract: Accurate wind speed forecasting is essential for the reliable and cost-effective integration of wind energy into modern power systems. This paper provides a comprehensive state-of-the-art review on data-driven artificial intelligence methods for wind speed forecasting from 2014 to early 2026 and evaluates their practical performance through a multi-site benchmark. The bibliometric trend analysis is conducted to identify the methodological evolution. These methods are categorized into four groups, i.e., statistical, machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid, with particular attention to decomposition enhanced forecasting frameworks. Ten representative forecasting methods combined with three data decomposition techniques are evaluated using four datasets from China, Norway, and a public benchmark. The results show that hybrid models with wavelet based decomposition generally improve the accuracy and robustness of short-term wind speed forecasting. Decomposition enhanced Transformer and Gaussian process models achieve relatively stable performance across different datasets and forecasting horizons. It is suggested that model selection relies on multiple factors including data characteristics, forecasting horizon, and computational constraints. Based on the review and benchmarking results, this study provides practical guidance on model selection for wind energy applications and identifies key research directions, including long-term forecasting, data-physics fusion learning, forecasting under extreme conditions, adaptive learning and explainable AI for broader climatic and operational scenarios. The findings offer actionable insights for improving forecasting reliability in large scale wind energy deployment.

title: Wind-solar complementary hydrogen production strategy based on coordinated ratio and rotation optimization of heterogeneous electrolyzers
abstract: Power fluctuations in off-grid wind-solar-storage hydrogen production systems trigger unstable electrolyzer operation, frequent equipment start-stop cycles, and accelerated equipment performance degradation. To enhance the operational stability and durability of the system, this paper proposes a coordinated strategy combining capacity ratio optimization and rotational dispatching for arrays of alkaline electrolyzers (ALK) and proton exchange membrane electrolyzers (PEM). The cold-start sensitivity inherent to alkaline electrolyzers is fully integrated into system capacity allocation and global operational dispatching processes. First, a convolutional neural network-bidirectional long short-term memory (CNN-BiLSTM) model is constructed to conduct classified prediction of wind and solar power, delivering time-interval prior information to support electrolyzer dispatching. Afterwards, an optimization framework based on K-means-genetic algorithm (K-Means-GA) is developed. With comprehensive consideration of investment costs and start-stop losses, the optimal capacity ratio between ALK and PEM electrolyzers is solved, which realizes a balanced optimum among system economic performance, renewable energy accommodation capacity and equipment loss. In addition, a cooperative greedy optimal dispatching strategy (CO-GA) is designed by introducing the priority principle of hot-state operation range, anti-jitter judgment and local cost gradient decision-making mechanism. Simulation results verify that the proposed method effectively cuts down unnecessary equipment switching and cold-start behaviors, and raises the effective service time and hydrogen production power of facilities. The established optimization framework that accounts for cold-start characteristics can offer solid technical support for the safe, reliable, economical and efficient operation of off-grid renewable energy hydrogen production systems.

title: Causality-enhanced interpretable assessment of renewable-driven hydrogen potential for regional multi-energy decarbonization
abstract: Hydrogen is emerging as a low-carbon energy carrier that links renewable electricity with end-use sectors, including industry, transport, and long-duration energy storage, and thus supports multi-energy decarbonization. Assessing regional hydrogen potential is important for infrastructure planning and policy design, but it is complicated by heterogeneous regional conditions and nonlinear interactions among renewable resources, demand characteristics, and infrastructure readiness. Although statistical and machine learning models have been used for regional assessment, most remain correlation driven and offer limited causal interpretation for planning-oriented decisions. This paper presents the Causality-Enhanced Hydrogen Potential Evaluation Framework (CE-HPEF), an interpretable hybrid approach that combines tree-based feature screening, domain-guided treatment selection, and leakage-aware variable exclusion with Causal Forest and Double Machine Learning to estimate heterogeneous treatment-effect patterns of key regional drivers, including renewable supply indicators, industrial demand, and transportation-related factors. The estimated causal effects are incorporated into an augmented feature representation and used for model-agnostic downstream hydrogen-potential classification. Experiments on two public hydrogen datasets show that CE-HPEF improves average classification performance across diverse downstream classifiers after causal-feature augmentation. The inferred effect patterns further provide region-specific diagnostic insights for hydrogen planning under renewable-based energy transitions.

title: Developing response surface methodology and machine learning for analyzing the continuous biodiesel production in a controlled ultrasonic micro-channel
abstract: A controlled ultrasonic micro-channel was introduced for increasing biodiesel production through waves’ irradiation and cavitation phenomenon. Two oils of flax and sesame seeds were analyzed, alone and mixed. Flaxseed oil with methanol played an important role in producing the biodiesel in the presence of potassium hydroxide as catalyst. Response surface methodology (RSM) designed the experiments by Box-Behnken approach. Results revealed that maximum fatty acid methyl ester (FAME %) of 99.66 % was attained in optimum independent variables (reaction temperature of 64 C°, catalyst amounts of 1.352, methanol to oil ratio of 8.472:1, and 5 piezoelectric sets), and a residence time of 350 s. Ultrasonic waves not only increased the FAME % but prepared the energy of the reaction (specialized power and frequency). Moreover, a quadratic model was developed and the variables were examined due to analysis of variance. The reaction temperature and interaction between catalyst amount and number of piezoelectric presented a significant degree of importance in the experiments. To further evaluation of modeling and obtaining a general model, machine learning was employed through artificial neural network (ANN). The outputs confirmed that the ANN was powerful in predicting the experimental data with a higher agreement in comparison with the RSM.

title: Energy pile thermal performance in saturated layered ground considering mixed convection: A numerical modeling and machine learning approach
abstract: Geothermal piles, serving as both structural and thermal elements, play a vital role in sustainable development by reducing energy consumption. These geo-structures exploit geothermal energy for building heating and cooling across different seasons. Careful consideration of the governing heat transfer mechanisms is essential for accurate design of energy geo-structures. Although many studies have examined the thermo-hydraulic behavior of geothermal piles, such simulations often involve high computational costs and are therefore less common in practical applications. However, recent advancements in machine learning and data science technologies suggest that trained machine learning models can provide a promising pathway to bridge the gap between research-oriented analyses of energy piles and practical design applications. In this study, a coupled thermo-hydraulic finite element model was developed to assess the thermal performance of a geothermal pile embedded in saturated layered soil, accounting for heat conduction and mixed convection. The results indicate that thermal performance is primarily controlled by the effective thermal conductivity of the surrounding soil. Accordingly, sandy soil exhibits the highest thermal performance, with values 59.6% higher than clayey soil and 22.1% higher than layered soil. Four machine learning models were developed to predict outlet fluid temperature, with the random forest model achieving the highest accuracy across five sensor placement scenarios. Optimal prediction accuracy was achieved when the sensors were positioned downstream of the groundwater flow at a radial distance of 0.6 m from the pile center. These findings provide valuable insights into energy pile site selection and the design of temperature sensor placement strategies.

title: An efficient prediction strategy for biogas yields based on machine learning and private optimization technique
abstract: Optimizing operating conditions in anaerobic digestion (AD) systems is essential for maximizing biogas production; however, identifying optimal parameter settings remains challenging due to reactor-specific variations and the nonlinear nature of the process. This paper proposes a Private Optimization based Biogas Prediction (POBP) strategy, which combines a Naïve Bayes (NB) classifier with a modified Gray Wolf Optimizer (MGWO) to determine suitable operating conditions for a laboratory-scale biogas reactor. In the proposed framework, NB is used as a probabilistic predictor to estimate biogas yield classes, while MGWO performs parameter optimization through an enhanced prey localization mechanism. The approach is evaluated using a reactor-specific dataset constructed from experimental measurements and optimization-generated samples. Results demonstrate that the proposed method improves reactor performance, achieving up to 62.72% improvement for the best solution and an average improvement of ≈33% after 10 iterations. Rather than relying on direct regression, the proposed framework utilizes a Naïve Bayes-based value predictor that estimates biogas yield by classifying yield intervals and mapping the predicted interval to a representative numerical value, achieving a classification accuracy of 96.1% on the tested dataset. These findings indicate that the proposed POBP strategy demonstrated effectiveness for the investigated laboratory-scale reactor and provides preliminary evidence for the feasibility of reactor-specific optimization under limited-data conditions.

title: Evaluation of the importance of urban morphological parameters in albedo-based three-dimensional solar potential estimation
abstract: Solar photovoltaic deployment is pivotal for achieving carbon neutrality by harnessing renewable energy in urban environments. Accurately assessing the role of urban morphology in shaping solar potential distribution is critical for policy design, particularly in metropolitan areas where vertical surfaces constitute a significant share of directly sun-exposed urban areas. However, conventional models relying on fixed albedo values oversimplify multi-reflective dynamics, underestimating indirect radiation contributions and introducing systemic errors in solar potential estimation. This simplification further obscures the interplay between urban morphology and solar redistribution, leading to an incomplete understanding of morphological impacts. In this work, we propose a machine learning-based framework that integrates material-specific albedo with 3D urban geometry to quantify morphological importance. Simulation results identify the mean façade albedo as the dominant annual-scale driver (22.7% relative importance), followed by building volume (21.6%) and façade area (7.5%). Seasonal and diurnal analyses reveal temporal dependencies: volumetric factors govern solar gains by affecting shadow effects during temporal transitions, while density and aggregated neighborhood reflectance synergistically enhance multi-reflections in these periods. These findings underscore the necessity of balancing urban morphology with material albedos to maximize solar harvesting in urban planning.

title: Oxidative pretreatment assisted hydrothermal carbonization of rice straw and sewage sludge for improved fuel properties: Mechanistic insights and understandings through machine learning
abstract: In the current study, sewage sludge and rice straw were co-hydrothermally carbonized to produce high quality hydrochar as potential fuel candidate alternatives to fossil-based coal. The HTC temperature of (160-240) 0C were applied with H2O2 concentration of (4, 6, 8, 10 and 12) % on w/w basis. The 8% concentration of H2O2 was concluded optimum to achieve higher heating value of 24.77 MJ/kg, 80.35% hydrochar yield and fuel ratio of 0.42. The oxidative treatment has significantly reduced the ash contents of the hydrochar from 17% to 3.75%. To evaluate the potential commercial scale competitiveness of the produce hydrochar, the O/C and H/C were estimated on atomic basis and van Krevelen diagram were studied. The hydrochar produced from 8% concentration of H2O2 had provided the lowest H/C and O/C values of 0.24 and 0.63 respectively which is very closer to that of peat. The thermal decay of lignin, cellulose, hemi-cellulose, carbohydrates and proteins were discovered detailed mechanism. Oxidative pretreatment had significantly altered the combustion behavior of the developed hydrochar and most of the energy was recovered before 4500C. The Pearson co-relation also concluded the role of oxidative cleavage treatment in enhancing energy contents, higher hydrochar yield and fuel ratio. Random forest and linear regression model have provided excellent fitness up to R2 of 0.96 and 0.80 respectively.

title: Hybrid algorithm for medium-term photovoltaic power prediction. Two-stage clustering-CNN-BiLSTM-Attention: Case study Lima (Peru)
abstract: The dimensioning of a solar plant requires historical information on seasonal meteorological variability where it will be installed. To ensure efficient photovoltaic (PV) energy production, accurate predictions that recognize variability are necessary. There are various hybrid prediction models without clear verification of the quality of clustering. Current PV prediction models have architectures with more accurate results but with a significant increase in computational time. A novel hybrid model is proposed that uses real historical data with a two-stage clustering process: physical-deterministic clustering for climatic seasons and clustering with the K-Medoids method to segment overcast and clear days, the results of which are incorporated into the CNN-BiLSTM-Attention prediction model trained on the residual over the cluster-mean baseline, allowing competitive results to be obtained over time horizons of 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, and 21 days. The clustering quality is supported by the joint optimization of three indices: Silhouette Score (SS) between 0.6698 and 0.8616, Calinski-Harabasz (CHI) up to 655.86, and Davies–Bouldin (DBI) as low as 0.4320, identifying 𝐾 ∗ = 2 as optimal across all four seasons. The proposed model attains 𝑅 2 between 0.8330 and 0.8453, RMSE between 0.1585 and 0.1627 kW, and MAE between 0.1156 and 0.1171 kW across the six horizons evaluated under stratified 7-daily split, 5-fold expanding-window cross-validation, 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, and Diebold–Mariano testing. During the 2023–2024 Coastal El Niño event, the model performs ＋2.6% better in 𝑅 2 than under normal conditions (0.8721 vs. 0.8498), demonstrating the robustness of two-stage clustering under anomalous climatic regimes.

title: Physics-informed solar modulation attention based dual-branch Transformer for ultra-short-term photovoltaic power forecasting with operational benefits analysis
abstract: Accurate ultra-short-term photovoltaic power forecasting is critical for real-time grid operation but remains challenging due to strong seasonal biases in input features, as well as physically inconsistent predictions during nighttime periods. To address these issues, this study proposes PhyMADformer, a physics-informed dual-branch Transformer that integrates physically meaningful solar priors into the attention-based representation learning process. The model explicitly decouples strongly seasonal trend components and weakly seasonal components via a dual-branch architecture, enabling more effective representation learning across heterogeneous temporal patterns. Unlike conventional physics-informed approaches that rely on external physical modeling, feature correction, or physics-informed probabilistic components, the proposed method embeds physical knowledge directly into the attention representation, improving interpretability and consistency. Extensive experiments on six utility-scale photovoltaic plants and multiple baselines show that PhyMADformer outperforms existing methods, achieving average reductions of 12.19% in root mean square error and 34.01% in mean absolute error. It also improves physical consistency, reducing nighttime absolute energy and nighttime mean absolute error by 74.26% and 74.51%, respectively. In addition, system-level evaluations demonstrate reductions in upward reserve requirement (48.02%), balancing cost (46.84%), and photovoltaic curtailment (40.21%), highlighting its practical value for real-world grid operation and improved dispatch efficiency.

title: Exergy-aware design, deep learning PINN-deriven multi objective optimization of a next-generation solid oxide fuel cell–organic Rankine cycle–photovoltaic-thermal solar collectors hybrid power system
abstract: This study presents a next-generation hybrid power system that integrates a solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC), an organic Rankine cycle (ORC), photovoltaic–thermal (PVT) solar collectors, and an electrolyzer to simultaneously address the dual challenges of achieving high-efficiency energy conversion and enabling sustainable distributed power generation. While previous studies often relied on steady-state models or black-box optimizers, the proposed framework addresses this gap by combining rigorous first- and second-law thermodynamic modeling with a hybrid optimization strategy based on deep learning, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). Embedding physical constraints directly into the learning process enables accurate yet computationally efficient exploration of design and operating conditions. The novelty of this research lies in both system-level integration and methodological advancement. This study develops one of the fully coupled SOFC–ORC–PVT–Electrolyzer hybrid configurations with a comprehensive thermo-economic–environmental assessment. Moreover, the study establishes a physics-constrained optimization framework that avoids the pitfalls of black-box machine learning and purely heuristic optimization by using hybrid model. The results reveal that the SOFC provides high-temperature electrochemical power, the ORC recovers low-grade heat at 120 °C using R601 as working fluid, and the PVT collectors supply both electrical and thermal energy under realistic solar boundary conditions. Multi-objective optimization demonstrates operating points that maximize exergy efficiency (up to 63.2%) while minimizing the levelized cost of electricity to competitive values. The PINN surrogate achieves strong predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.87 for cost, R2 = 0.75 for exergy efficiency), demonstrating its ability to capture nonlinear thermo-economic interactions with physical fidelity.

title: Optimization of sandstone geothermal reinjection: Integrating field tests, numerical simulations and machine learning
abstract: The decline in reinjection capacity reduces the resource efficiency and long-term sustainability of sandstone geothermal systems. To address this critical challenge while accounting for complex geological heterogeneity and multi-physics constraints, this study establishes an integrated decision-making framework that combines field tests, numerical simulation, and machine learning. Firstly, multi-stage stepped-pressure reinjection field tests and hydrochemical analysis quantitatively characterize the nonlinear response of near-wellbore fluid dynamic resistance and scaling risk. Furthermore, a vertical heterogeneous numerical model is constructed, revealing the control mechanisms of near-well head loss accumulation and dominant layer-driven flow distribution. Based on this, a stacking ensemble surrogate model driven by heterogeneous learners is constructed, and the SHAP method is used to conduct interpretability analysis. Finally, a preferred operating condition is selected from the Pareto front. The results show that while high-pressure reinjection boosts the driving force, the marginal reinjection gain decreases under persistent near-wellbore hydraulic resistance and increasing non-Darcy dissipation. Additionally, under the investigated hydrochemical conditions, lower-temperature reinjection reduces the calcite scaling potential. Therefore, a moderate-pressure and low-temperature reinjection strategy is identified from the Pareto analysis. Within the parameter space under study and based on the specified economic assumptions, the selected Pareto-optimal solution is predicted to increase thermal energy extraction capacity and hourly benefit by 35.66% and 28.91%, respectively, compared to the natural reinjection baseline case. This study elucidates the reinjection mechanism in porous reservoirs and provides technical support for the efficient and sustainable operation of geothermal systems.

title: Large language model-based swarm intelligence for parameter identification of photovoltaic cells
abstract: Accurate parameter extraction for photovoltaic models is critical for optimizing system efficiency and ensuring operational stability. However, conventional deterministic and metaheuristic methods often suffer from premature convergence due to the strong nonlinearity and multimodality of the objective function. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a framework capable of adaptive strategy selection, termed large language model-based swarm intelligence. By embedding Meta LLaMA-3.1-405B-Instruct as the high-level strategic reasoning core, the proposed method integrates a triple stagnation detection mechanism that dynamically switches between optimization algorithms to prevent local optima entrapment. Furthermore, a physics-informed validation module is incorporated to enforce boundary constraints and ensure the physical feasibility of the identified parameters. Comparative experiments demonstrate that large language model-based swarm intelligence yields superior accuracy over state-of-the-art metaheuristics, achieving root mean square error reductions of 84.6% for the single diode model, 84.3% for the double diode model, and 82.1% for the triple diode model.

title: Reaction behavior and kinetic analysis in the fast co-pyrolysis of bituminous coal with typical biomasses under CO2/N2 atmospheres: leveraging machine learning for char yield prediction
abstract: Co-pyrolysis of bamboo (BB), sawdust (SD), and wheat straw (WS), with Hongshaquan bituminous coal (HSQ), were conducted at 1000 K min−1 under CO2/N2 atmospheres. The maximum mass loss rates for the three biomass-coal blends were 0.94-3.29, 0.99-3.21, and 0.78-2.67%·K−1. Higher biomass proportion increased the maximum instantaneous reactivity, intrinsic reaction rate, and comprehensive pyrolysis index, with optimal performance for HSQ-BB at 30% CO2 and for HSQ-SD and HSQ-WS at 60% CO2. The contributions of CO2 on char yield for the three coal-biomass blends were 4.12-10.18%, 2-10.58%, and 3.8-9.88%, respectively. During the primary pyrolysis stage, the interaction effects depended on biomass properties and CO2 concentration. With increasing CO2 concentration, the effects shifted from inhibiting to promoting for BB, while opposite trends for SD and WS. A comprehensive interaction intensity index was established, with the values of 0.07-0.60, 0.04-0.52, and 0.12-0.63, suggesting HSQ-WS > HSQ-BB > HSQ-SD. The Avrami-Erofeev equation (n = 4) could best represent the co-pyrolysis process. As biomass proportion increased, the activation energy increased, while it decreased at higher CO2 concentration. The discrepancy between experimental and theoretical activation energy was correlated with the interaction intensity. A backpropagation neural network coupled with a genetic algorithm was employed to predict the char yield. The 13×8 node configuration yielded the best performance, with RMSE of 2.4090 and R2 of 0.9691. With larger datasets, the model's performance is expected to improve. This study provides a theoretical basis for coal-biomass co-combustion in industrial processes.

title: Study on operational characteristics and performance prediction of a water-cooled photovoltaic and thermal system
abstract: Water-cooled photovoltaic-thermal systems have garnered significant attention for their combined power and heat generation capabilities. However, existing studies suffer from insufficient operating conditions, low prediction accuracy, and incomplete regional applicability analyses. To remedy these deficiencies, an experimental platform was established to investigate the heating and power generation performance of a water-cooled photovoltaic-thermal system under various seasonal operating conditions. Subsequently, an innovative performance prediction model was developed based on a back-propagation neural network and further optimized using a hybrid optimization framework integrating the ant colony algorithm, the beetle antennae search algorithm, and the variable neighborhood local search algorithm. The coefficient of determination of the optimized model increased by 15.2 %, and the mean absolute error decreased by 75.51 %. It was applied to analyze Beijing, Guangzhou, and Lijiang, revealing average annual heating powers of 136 W, 178 W, and 126 W, and power generation of 38 W, 29 W, and 46 W, respectively. Finally, annual performance predictions were conducted for 15 representative cities in typical climate zones, and the performance curves of a single water-cooled photovoltaic-thermal module under variable operating conditions were analyzed. The results demonstrated that increasing ambient temperature from −10 °C to 40 °C raised peak heating power from 476 W to 769 W, while reducing electrical power from 230 W to 189 W. Furthermore, elevating solar irradiance from 0 to 1000 W/m2 increased heating output to 769 W and electrical output to 230 W.

title: Sobol-based global sensitivity analysis of D-shaped bluff body piezoelectric energy harvesters using SVM surrogate model
abstract: To address the unclear parameter regulation mechanism of D-shaped bluff body piezoelectric micro wind energy harvesters caused by strong geometric-system parameter coupling and pronounced nonlinearity, this study develops a synergistic parameter analysis framework combining Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Sobol global sensitivity analysis to investigate the effects and synergistic mechanisms of wind speed, aspect ratio, mass damping ratio and system stiffness on amplitude ratio.540 sets of full-condition vibration response data were obtained via three-factor three-level orthogonal tests and continuous wind speed scanning. An SVM surrogate model with radial basis function kernel was established, achieving a test set coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9655, meeting high-precision analysis requirements. Global sensitivity analysis shows that wind speed dominates amplitude ratio across all conditions with a total effect index of 59.00%, followed by aspect ratio (19.05%), stiffness (10.33%) and mass damping ratio (8.92%). Mass damping ratio exhibits strong interaction effects, while aspect ratio acts almost independently. Dominant parameters evolve significantly with wind speed: mass damping ratio dominates at low speeds, stiffness at medium speeds, and both aspect ratio and stiffness at high speeds. This study reveals the multi-parameter mechanism under coupled vortex-induced vibration (VIV) and galloping in D-shaped bluff bodies, providing an efficient analytical tool and theoretical support for parameter matching and optimal design of micro wind energy devices.

title: A hybrid approach for the techno-economic analysis of wind power plants
abstract: This study presents an integrated framework combining design of experiments, the System Advisor Model, and machine learning to improve energy production and economic forecasting for wind power plants. A multi-level full factorial design of experiments generated 2688 scenarios by varying four critical parameters—turbine spacing (3–8 rotor diameters), hub height (80–140 m), rotor diameter (75–110 m), and wind speed (5.66–10.18 m/s)—across eight U.S. regions. These scenarios were simulated in the System Advisor Model to compute five techno-economic outputs: annual energy production, net present value after tax, levelized cost of energy, net capital cost per watt, and total balance-of-system cost. Five machine learning algorithms—neural networks, support vector machines, partial least squares, k-nearest neighbors, and stochastic gradient descent—were then trained on the system advisor model dataset. Among the eight sites, Wyoming yielded the highest energy production (659,434 MWh/year) and the lowest levelized cost of energy (1.59 ¢/kWh), while Florida recorded the lowest production (317,876 MWh/year). Neural networks and support vector machines demonstrated superior predictive performance, with neural networks achieving R2 values of 0.964 for the levelized cost of energy and 0.944 for the annual energy production. The sensitivity analysis using a box plot confirmed the robustness and reliability of the developed models. These results demonstrate that integrating the design of experiments, the system advisor model, and machine learning provides accurate, scalable, and robust forecasting tools for the wind power plants’ planning and investment decisions.

title: Carbon-responsibility-aware peer-to-peer trading mechanism for microgrids with heterogeneous energy
abstract: Peer-to-peer (P2P) trading enables microgrids, acting as prosumers, to exchange surplus electricity locally. The traded power often originates from heterogeneous sources such as photovoltaics, gas turbines, and energy storage systems, each with distinct carbon intensities. However, most existing P2P profit distribution mechanisms treat electricity as a homogeneous commodity and overlook the carbon heterogeneity among energy sources, thus failing to capture the environmental implications of trading behaviors. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a carbon-responsibility-aware P2P trading mechanism that embeds carbon responsibility into the cooperative benefit allocation process, thereby extending traditional P2P trading from economic optimization to environmentally accountable decision-making. Specifically, a carbon responsibility attribution model is developed based on a carbon-weighted graph neural network, which embeds the carbon intensities of heterogeneous energy sources into the adjacency matrix to capture the propagation of carbon emissions along trading paths and accurately learn the mapping between electricity flows and transaction-level carbon responsibility. Furthermore, an asymmetric bargaining mechanism is designed, where heterogeneous carbon responsibilities are converted into environmental values to determine bargaining factors, and an asymmetric exponential weighting function is introduced to adjust allocation coefficients. Compared to the standard graph convolutional network, the proposed model improves the coefficient of determination for carbon attribution by 16.60%. Furthermore, the trading framework reduces aggregate carbon emissions by 12.14% while incurring a marginal 0.90% operational cost increase for the heterogeneous energy cluster, providing an economical and efficient approach to transitioning the system toward low-carbon operation.

title: Data-driven prognostic algorithm based on Bi-LSTM transformer model for proton exchange membrane fuel cell
abstract: The complex interaction of internal physical phenomena makes predicting the degradation of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) under dynamic operating conditions a critical but persistent challenge. To address this, the present work develops a hybrid model based on Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) layers with a multi-head self-attention mechanism to capture degradation dependencies across both short and long time-frames. When benchmarked against state-of-the-art architectures, including attention-based LSTM variants and the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT), the model achieves a reduction of up to 52.7% in Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). The model’s accuracy is confirmed across single-step, multi-step, and long-term forecasting scenarios, where it consistently maintains high predictive accuracy ( R 2 ≥ 0.998 ) for prediction horizons of up to 175 steps ahead. Furthermore, this high performance is achieved with notable data efficiency, requiring a training dataset of 300 h. These combined strengths in accuracy, long-term reliability, and data efficiency make the proposed Bi-LSTM Transformer an effective tool for predictive health management under dynamic load cycles.

title: A Deep learning-based market mechanism providing reasonable incentives for low-carbon power system
abstract: Current electricity market mechanism based on marginal pricing theory lacks incentives that ensure competitive equilibrium and fairness with the increasing proportion of renewable energy and generalized energy storage in the low carbon power system. This paper first introduces a social welfare contribution degree (SWCD) mechanism, allocating welfare based on marginal contributions without generating opportunity costs or surpluses, thereby preventing the competitive disequilibrium often arising from such factors. Also, it aligns incentives with contributions, adhering to Adams’ equity theory. To improve SWCD’s computational efficiency, we developed a deep learning method combining multi-head self-attention and residual network, named MHSA-ResNet, creating the final automatically calculated SWCD (AC-SWCD) mechanism. Simulations show that MHSA-ResNet performs better than some other classic neural networks. The proposed mechanism is compared with the locational marginal price and Vickrey-Clarke-Groves mechanisms through case studies. Results show that it can provide incentive signals with high computational efficiency ensuring competitive equilibrium and incentive fairness.

title: Interpretable machine learning analysis of anode operating parameters on the performance of a high-power PEMFC system
abstract: In the global transition to carbon neutrality, hydrogen serves as a vital carrier for storing intermittent renewable energy such as wind and solar power. Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFC) are essential devices for reconverting hydrogen into electricity. However, the complex multiphysics coupling of gas, water, electricity, and heat makes output behavior difficult to predict through mechanistic models. Consequently, optimizing stack performance by adjusting auxiliary system parameters remains a significant control challenge at current stage. Based on system experiments, machine learning models, and the Shapley Additive Explanation (SHAP) methodology derived from game theory, this paper systematically explores the effects of operating parameters of the hydrogen supply subsystem on the output performance of high-power fuel cell systems. First, controlled-variable experiments were designed to investigate the voltage response under diverse operating conditions. Subsequently, the experimental data were preprocessed and subjected to feature selection to construct a neural network-based prediction model. Finally, interpretability analysis based on SHAP values was conducted globally at different current densities. The results show that at low current density, operating temperature has a significant negative effect on the output voltage, while ambient water vapor pressure ratio exhibits a strong positive effect. At high current density, anode hydrogen concentration, anode molar flow rate, and anode water vapor concentration become the three parameters with the highest contribution. This study quantifies the effects of anode operating parameters on high-power fuel cell system performance, providing optimization solutions for hydrogen supply subsystem and guidance for formulating control strategies to enhance hydrogen utilization efficiency.

title: Dynamic wind turbine wake estimation based on non-intrusive reduced order modeling
abstract: Accurate modeling of dynamic wind turbine wakes is essential for wind turbine structural analysis and wind farm power optimization. To predict dynamic wakes under different inflow conditions and wind turbine layouts, this paper proposes a dynamic wake estimation framework based on non-intrusive reduced order modeling that integrates a two-step proper orthogonal decomposition, a modified feedforward neural network, and a Transformer network. Specifically, the two-step proper orthogonal decomposition is applied to separately compress the temporal and parametric subspaces of a single wind turbine wake, extracting low-dimensional modes and corresponding projection coefficients. By incorporating attention mechanisms and residual blocks, a modified feedforward neural network is proposed to predict the projection coefficients for reconstructing the high-fidelity single wind turbine wake. In addition, to enable multiple wind turbine wake estimation, the Transformer network establishes a mapping from the projection coefficients of a single wind turbine wake to those of multiple wind turbine wakes, effectively and accurately modeling wake superposition. The proposed framework is evaluated for cases of the single wind turbine and multiple wind turbines under different wind speeds, yaw angles, and aligned layouts. Results show that the proposed method reduces the root mean square error by approximately 3% relative to the compared methods. For the reported 3×3 case, The LES farm-averaged power ranges from 2554.7 to 2650.7 kW, while the DWTWE range from 2367.0 to 2818.0 kW. Hence, the proposed method provides dynamic wake estimation for the single wind turbine and multiple wind turbines. The computational efficiency of the framework may support future studies on dynamic wake control after further validation.

title: Transfer learning and convolutional neural networks for solar photovoltaic systems detection in distributed power grids
abstract: Accurate mapping and characterization of distributed solar photovoltaic (PV) systems are essential for energy planning, net demand forecasting, and policy-making. Traditional methods for collecting data on distributed electricity generation are often labor-intensive, costly, or impractical. This study leverages recent advances in machine learning, introducing state-of-the-art image segmentation architectures for automated PV panel detection from remotely sensed data. To address constraints in training time and dataset size, transfer learning is applied using pre-trained large-scale deep neural networks as feature extractors. Additionally, a novel hard example mining scheme is proposed to enhance detection accuracy. Through a comprehensive framework, factors influencing prediction accuracy, such as PV recognition thresholds, segmentation model architecture, sampling strategies, and encoder parameter freezing, are systematically examined. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms other models, achieving an F1 score above 0.91 and an IoU exceeding 0.83. This research advances automated infrastructure mapping, providing scalable solutions for monitoring distributed PV systems and offering transferable methodologies for broader applications.

title: Plantwide dynamic optimization of a hybrid solar thermal power plant modeled using deep neural networks
abstract: We present a plantwide dynamic optimization framework for optimal economic operation of a multi-concentrator hybrid solar thermal power plant (HSTPP) integrating parabolic trough collectors (PTC) and a linear Fresnel reflector (LFR). The existing first-principles HSTPP model involves more than 120,000 coupled ordinary differential equations obtained after spatial discretization of distributed parameter concentrator models. While it provides detailed dynamic representation of interactions across multiple concentrators, heat-exchangers, and the power block, it remains computationally prohibitive for use in plantwide optimization. To enable tractable plantwide dynamic optimization, neural network (NN) based digital-twin framework is developed by replacing the concentrator models with data-driven surrogates. A feedforward NN predicts PTC outlet oil temperature, while a nonlinear finite impulse response long short-term memory model with moving window average captures steam drum pressure of the LFR-Steam drum (SD) subsystem. Both surrogates are trained using dynamic data from a validated first-principles simulator and achieve high predictive accuracy in infinite-step-ahead simulation, with the PTC-FFNN model giving R2:0.9964, RMSE 2.58 °C, and fit 93.96%, and the LFR-SD NFIR-LSTM model giving R2:0.9922, RMSE 1.12 bar, and fit 91.19%. The resulting gray-box HSTPP-Surrogate model reduces the standalone plantwide simulation time from 42.7 min to 1.33 min, corresponding to a 32.1 times speed-up. The surrogate-based multi-concentrator digital twin is integrated with a first-principles model of balance-of-plant components of the HSTPP to solve a market-driven revenue maximization problem using a genetic algorithm. The resulting optimal operation increases daily revenue from Rs. 26,424 to Rs. 37,199, corresponding to a 40.78% improvement over the nominal fixed-flow base operation.

title: Wind-induced optical degradation in heliostats: A site-specific probabilistic assessment with joint wind–tracking sampling
abstract: Wind-induced structural deformation poses a critical threat to the optical performance and operational reliability of heliostats in tower-type Concentrating Solar Power (CSP) plants. Conventional assessments based on worst-case uniform hazard assumptions tend to overestimate operational risk and yield overly conservative designs. This study presents a probabilistic aero-structural-optical reliability and fragility framework for a representative heliostat at the Golmud CSP site. A physics-guided Kriging surrogate model is constructed using wind-tunnel-validated multi-physics simulation data. By integrating site-specific meteorological statistics with solar-tracking kinematics, this model establishes a joint spatiotemporal sampling strategy to enable efficient Monte Carlo analysis. Sensitivity analysis reveals that wind direction governs structural loading, whereas optical degradation is primarily controlled by the sun-heliostat-receiver geometric configuration rather than peak aerodynamic conditions. For a 15% concentrating efficiency loss threshold, the probability of exceeding this limit is approximately 2% under site-specific wind–tracking sampling, compared to about 7% when all wind–tracking conditions are assumed to be equally probable. Fragility analysis indicates that when the average mirror deformation reaches 15.20 mm, the probability of exceeding this threshold reaches 50%. Furthermore, concentrating efficiency losses above 15% occur predominantly when solar-noon tracking states (13:00–15:00) coincide with frontal to near-frontal winds (βw ≤ 40°); these wind–tracking conditions account for only 1.75% of annual conditions but contribute 84% of all cases exceeding the 15% loss threshold. These findings support the design of wind-adaptive stow strategies and risk-informed operational control for CSP heliostats.

title: Integrating Gaussian splatting and machine learning for solar analysis in sustainable buildings
abstract: This study presents a geometry-aware framework for residential solar energy estimation that integrates unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based photogrammetry, three-dimensional Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), physics-based energy modeling, and multimodal machine learning (ML) for active and passive solar prediction. Building geometries are reconstructed from low-cost UAV video using segment anything model 3 (SAM 3) segmentation, structure-from-motion, and dense reconstruction, with 3DGS generating scene representations that preserve roof and facade features relevant to solar analysis, converted into watertight level of detail 3 (LOD3) building envelopes with integrated fenestration and transformed into EnergyPlus-compatible energy models at five performance levels. Validation across 33 residential buildings confirms good agreement between reconstructed and ground-truth dimensions and realistic thermal energy demand trends. Solar simulations evaluate annual photovoltaic (PV) potential, sunlit area, and internal solar gains, and a multimodal graph neural network (GNN) jointly processing geometry-aware and scalar building features for rapid, simulation-free estimation, achieving testing R 2 values of 0.890, 0.753, and 0.815 for annual internal solar gain, PV generation, and total sunlit area, respectively. The results demonstrate the potential of geometry-aware scene representations and machine learning as a scalable approach for rapid solar-performance assessment.

title: Medium-term wind power forecasting based on the strategy of “independent encoding - joint decoding” considering multi-source data
abstract: The precision and dependability of wind power forecasting are significant for the safe and stable operation of the power system. Longer prediction horizons and higher forecasting accuracy are required with wind power development. However, current research primarily focuses on intra-day (generally 4-6h) and day-ahead (generally 1-3 days) forecasting, with limited attention to medium-term (generally 1-10 days) forecasting. Furthermore, research on medium-term wind power forecasting is mainly based on operation data of the wind farm and weather prediction data, neglecting the mesoscale meteorological data around the stations that can provide information on weather changes under large-scale, as well as the differential contributions of various data to the forecasting results. Aiming at the above problems, a medium-term wind power forecasting method based on the strategy of “independent encoding - joint decoding” considering multi-source data is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a multi-variable selection module is constructed based on the gating mechanism to select the most important features at each time point as input for subsequent modules. Then, a multi-encoding module is built based on independent parameters, employing a sequence-to-sequence approach to handle the different features of multi-source data, and transform them into unified temporal features. Finally, a joint decoding module based on multi-head attention mechanism is constructed, which can dynamically integrate the information obtained from each independent encoder to improve the forecasting accuracy. To validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method, different types of data are used as inputs, and four commonly used models, including CNN, LSTM, GRU, and Transformer, are employed as basic models for comparison. Two wind farms in North China are taken as examples, the results show that the forecasting error can be reduced by 0.53% to 30.97% when RMSE is used as the evaluation index, 0.55% to 34.34% when MAE is used as the evaluation index.

title: From yaw to 3D wake steering: A cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning approach for wind farm power–aerodynamic-load-proxy trade-offs
abstract: Dense wind farm layouts intensify wake interactions, resulting in significant power losses and increased aerodynamic loading on downstream turbines. Conventional yaw-only wake steering controls horizontal deflection but neglects vertical wake dynamics. This work proposes a three-dimensional wake steering strategy coordinating both yaw and tilt angles to redirect wakes laterally and vertically. A customized Multi-Agent Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient framework learns cooperative yaw-tilt policies under dynamic inflow, using a reward function that balances farm power output with aerodynamic-load-proxy reduction. Using an engineering wake-model simulation across six wind scenarios, from idealized fixed conditions to variable wind speeds and directions, we compare the joint strategy with matched yaw-only and tilt-only controls. Under strongly fluctuating high-wind conditions, the representative joint-control policy yields a power gain of 3.296% and an aerodynamic-load-proxy reduction of 13.416%, compared with 2.7% and 5.0% for yaw-only control and 1.1% and 13.0% for tilt-only control. These results demonstrate the added value of cooperative horizontal–vertical wake steering over single-degree-of-freedom control under strongly fluctuating high-wind conditions, highlighting tilt-enabled wake steering as a promising direction for future power–load-aware wind-farm operation.

title: Two-stage degradation threshold-time estimation for crystalline-silicon PV modules using long-term operating data and short-term measurements
abstract: Long-term photovoltaic module degradation affects energy yield, asset value, and reliability management. System-level records provide long-term evidence of climate-dependent performance loss rates, while short-term module measurements resolve technology-specific performance and electrical-state variation. A scale-resolved hierarchical framework integrated public operating and accelerated-aging data with regional observations and paired current–voltage and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements from Hainan, Hailar, and Turpan. Expected-power normalization and regional calibration established long-term distributions of performance loss rates. Accelerated aging constrained technology- and stage-dependent responses, and grouped machine learning estimated current and next-stage maximum-power retention. A continuous two-stage model separated early-stage loss from stable degradation and propagated uncertainty to threshold-crossing times through Monte Carlo simulation. Quality screening retained 33 of 51 public photovoltaic systems. Climate transfer and regional calibration yielded annual performance loss rates of 0.739% yr−1 in Hainan, 0.624% yr−1 in Hailar, and 0.655% yr−1 in Turpan. Passivated emitter and rear cell technology showed the largest early-stage loss, while regional variation in stable rates exceeded technology adjustments. Measured current–voltageretention reduced median current-state root mean square error from 0.6 to below 0.2 percentage points, with impedance spectroscopy providing modest sample-specific residual refinement. Estimated times to 90%, 85%, and 80% maximum-power retention were 12.4/19.9/27.8, 14.3/22.9/32.1, and 14.1/22.4/31.2 years, respectively. These conditional estimates support technology and region-specific risk screening. Independent long-term module validation remains necessary for service-life qualification.

title: A physics-guided dual-channel convolutional neural network wake model for a wind turbine over a hill
abstract: Wind turbine wakes over hilly terrain are influenced by the combined effects of the turbine and the underlying terrain. Terrain-induced flow acceleration, separation, and other complex flow phenomena pose major challenges to analytical wake models. To accurately predict wake flow fields over hilly terrain, this study proposes a physics-guided dual-channel convolutional neural network wake model. The model first decomposes the target flow field into a turbine-induced velocity deficit field and a terrain-induced background flow field, then combines low-fidelity physical representation, data-driven enhancement, and fusion-based reconstruction to predict the high-fidelity wake field. A high-fidelity dataset covering different hill slopes and turbine operating conditions is constructed using a limited number of large-eddy simulations. Physics-based methods then transform the turbine operating conditions and terrain information into low-fidelity velocity deficit and background flow fields, which serve as physics-guided inputs to the network. Both fields contain representation errors arising from simplified physical assumptions, and their direct superposition cannot adequately represent the nonlinear coupling between the turbine wake and terrain-induced flow. The dual-channel convolutional neural network therefore encodes and enhances the two low-fidelity fields separately to reduce the errors associated with their respective physical approximations. The resulting features are then fused to learn the nonlinear coupling and reconstruct the high-fidelity wake field. Generalization tests show that the proposed model achieves a mean absolute percentage error of 4.98% relative to large-eddy simulation results. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining flow-field decomposition, low-fidelity physics guidance, and data-driven fusion for wind turbine wake prediction over a two-dimensional hill.

title: A novel adaptive control strategy for hydro-turbine governing systems based on physics-informed neural networks
abstract: Hydropower units are critical regulating resources that mitigate power fluctuations induced by renewable energy grid integration and provide rapid frequency support for power systems. With limited labeled trajectories and continuously changing loads, however, fixed-parameter proportional-integral-derivative controllers struggle with the nonlinearities and coupled constraints of operation over a wide operating range. Frequent intraday load transitions can consequently degrade regulation performance or cause instability. This study integrates physics-informed state-transition prediction with composite adaptive regulation to address state evolution under exogenous loads and regulation across operating conditions. Simulations of a 100 MW Francis turbine unit show improvements in both prediction credibility and regulation performance. Compared with a same-architecture data-only network, the physics-informed neural network reduces physical residuals by 39.3%-43.1% and 300-step free-running prediction errors by 66.3%-80.5%. Compared with fixed-parameter control, the composite adaptive controller reduces maximum overshoot and the integral of absolute error by 58.4% and 86.4%, respectively. Continuous-load and disturbance tests further show adaptability to substantial operating-point changes, identifying rapid load ramp-down and high-load operation as the principal performance-sensitive stages. The framework provides a systematic approach to intelligent state awareness and adaptive control of hydropower units with limited operating data.

title: Research on multi-objective optimization of wave-trapezoidal flow channels in proton exchange membrane fuel cell considering the impact of mechanical properties on gas diffusion layer deformation
abstract: The flow channel structure of bipolar plates plays a crucial role in improving the performance of proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC). In this study, a novel wave-trapezoidal flow channel (WTFC) was proposed, which adopts the constant cross-sectional area design concept, enabling effectively enhanced mass transfer performance while maintaining a relatively low pressure drop. Furthermore, the effect of mechanical properties on gas diffusion layer deformation was considered. To improve the overall performance of the PEMFC, the optimization objectives were defined as net power density (Pnet), maximum liquid water saturation (MLWS) at the interface between the cathode gas diffusion layer and the cathode catalyst layer, and effective mass transfer coefficient (EMTC) at the same interface, while the optimization variables included flow channel geometric parameters and cell operating conditions. The BO-CNN-LSSVM model establishes the mapping between optimization variables and optimization objectives. The optimal wave-trapezoidal flow channel (OWTFC) is obtained through multi-objective optimization. Results show high agreement between BO-CNN-LSSVM regression predictions and numerical simulations, with all R2 values higher than 0.98 for the three objectives. Compared with the genetic algorithm-back propagation neural network, it reduces fitting time by 45.12% while improving accuracy. OWTFC outperforms trapezoidal flow channel and single straight flow channel: Pnet increases by 5.13% and 20.58%, MLWS decreases by 11.05% and 38.33%, and EMTC rises by 8.43% and 29.65% respectively under the same conditions.

title: Machine learning approaches in solar forecasting across different climate types: A unified evaluation framework
abstract: With the continuous development of solar energy technology, solar forecasting has become increasingly important. Accurate short-term solar forecasting could help maintain grid stability and provide reliable power. It is also critical for scheduling in intra-day electricity markets and grid operations. Compared to Deep Learning models, Machine Learning models offer the advantages of faster computation and better adaptability to small datasets. However, there is a lack of a unified evaluation framework to evaluate Machine Learning models due to the diversity of datasets, time step, forecasting horizon, set up and evaluation metrics. This work addresses this gap by evaluating six validated Machine Learning methods including Linear Regression, Polynomial Regression, Support Vector Regression, Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting and Artificial Neural Network for hourly solar irradiance forecasting across five different geographical regions: Canberra, Shanghai, Miami, Amherst and Kitakyushu. Results reveal that all Machine Learning models outperform the Smart Persistence Model (SPM) at the one-hour horizon; tree-ensemble methods, specifically Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost, achieve the highest overall accuracy and provide predictive performance competitive with DL models at the one-hour-ahead horizon. In stable-sky locations such as Canberra, the RF model achieved a normalized Root Mean Square Error (nRMSE) of 48.97% and a coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) of 0.8859, whereas the nRMSE increased to 61.47% in the highly variable conditions of Kitakyushu. This work helps establish a consistent framework for future studies, facilitating better comparison and improvement of Machine Learning models in solar forecasting.

title: Prediction of transient heat exchange performance of energy pile groups using a physics-constrained DeepONet
abstract: Rapid prediction of transient heat exchange performance of energy pile groups becomes particularly challenging when thermal interference among piles, groundwater seepage, and intermittent operation act simultaneously. Numerical simulations are computationally expensive, whereas previous data-driven studies have mainly focused on the quasi-steady-state response of an isolated pile. This study developed an integrated framework of an analytical model and a physics-constrained deep operator network for transient thermal performance of energy pile groups under groundwater seepage and intermittent operation. The analytical model for pile groups was based on the moving finite cylindrical source theory, thermal resistance model, and spatiotemporal superposition principles. After validation against numerical and experimental results, the analytical model was used to generate 15,000 cases comprising 3000 independent physical-parameter sets evaluated under five operation strategies. Three machine-learning models were developed to predict the time-dependent heat exchange response and were evaluated over five runs with different random seeds. The physics-constrained deep operator network generally showed superior performance in the test set, and an ablation study was conducted to quantify the contribution of each embedded constraint. Independent examples further demonstrated that the machine-learning model can reproduce the transient thermal performance of individual piles and pile groups over a 90-day period within 1 s. SHAP analysis identified the relative importance of ten input features, and initial ground temperature and operation strategy were dominant for thermal performance of energy pile groups. The proposed framework provides a physically credible and computationally efficient surrogate model for preliminary design and operation optimization of energy pile groups.
