title: PFM-TMLC: Physics-Guided microscopic trajectory reconstruction from fixed sensors under emergencies
abstract: Urban traffic monitoring systems often suffer from trajectory loss due to occlusion, blind spots, and sensing failures, which become particularly critical under emergencies such as incidents, evacuations, or extreme weather. In these conditions, incomplete trajectories can degrade situational awareness, bias traffic state estimation, and delay operational responses, thereby undermining the resilience of smart city transport systems. This study proposes the Particle-Filtered Mamba − Trajectory Matching and Lane Change recognition (PFM-TMLC) model, a unified microscopic trajectory reconstruction framework that integrates three complementary modules. First, a Mamba-based longitudinal reconstruction model learns long-range temporal dependencies from fixed-sensor observations and surrounding-vehicle states, enabling accurate recovery of missing longitudinal motion. Second, a particle-filter refinement model enforces physics consistent evolution and scenario adaptive constraints to filter and correct data-driven predictions, improving robustness in different conditions while preventing physically implausible behaviors. Third, a multi-task learning component jointly performs trajectory matching and lane-change recognition, allowing disjoint trajectories to be reconciled at the trajectory level and lane transitions to be inferred during missing intervals. Experiments on the NGSIM I-80 dataset across four representative car-following scenarios show that the particle-filter refinement reduces longitudinal reconstruction errors substantially relative to the baseline, achieving up to about 47 % reduction in position and speed Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), while eliminating collision cases observed in purely data-driven baselines. The multi-task module further delivers reliable lateral completion, with trajectory matching accuracy exceeding 82 % and lane-change direction accuracy exceeding 83 % for left and 72 % for right maneuvers. These results indicate that PFM-TMLC model can provide accurate and physically plausible trajectory completion to support robust traffic operations, especially when sensing quality deteriorates during emergencies.

title: FedGNN-SFCP: Federated graph neural networks for ship fuel consumption prediction with heterogeneous data fusion and missing data imputation
abstract: Machine learning (ML)-based ship fuel consumption prediction (SFCP) methods have attracted considerable attention from scholars in recent years due to their robust feature extraction capabilities. However, these methods highly depend on the quantity and quality of ship fuel consumption data. In practice, individual ships generate at most 365 noon reports per year, and privacy concerns prevent data sharing across companies, leading to data scarcity. Additionally, noon reports suffer from coarse daily granularity and missing values, compromising data quality. When ML-based SFCP models are trained on datasets with poor data quantity and quality, their performance degrades dramatically. To address these issues, we propose a novel federated learning (FL)-based method combining graph neural networks (GNN) and generative adversarial networks (GAN) for SFCP, named FedGNN-SFCP. First, to enhance data quality, we propose a GAN-based imputation method for handling missing data in ship noon reports and automatic identification system (AIS) data. Meanwhile, to address the low data granularity of noon reports, we leverage high-frequency AIS data, which provides hundreds of records per day. Specifically, we propose a novel multiple-layer heterogeneous graph construction method and employ a heterogeneous graph transformer to effectively fuse these heterogeneous data sources, thereby improving prediction performance. Second, to enhance data quantity, we introduce FL to SFCP tasks to enable collaborative training, allowing the model to learn from more data while preserving privacy. Furthermore, we propose adaptive federated proximal to address the challenge of training on heterogeneous data feature distributions from different ships. To evaluate FedGNN-SFCP, we conduct a series of experiments on three real-world ship fuel consumption datasets. The proposed FedGNN-SFCP achieves relative reductions of at least 7.21%, 9.63%, and 4.15% in root mean square error, mean absolute error, and mean absolute percentage error, respectively, compared to baseline methods. This demonstrates the effectiveness and robustness of FedGNN-SFCP as a privacy-preserving solution under different data missing rates for SFCP in the maritime industry.

title: Learning-based emergency egress trajectory planning for UAV in mixed terminal airspace
abstract: Advanced air mobility (AAM) is expected to introduce increasingly heterogeneous low-altitude operations, and mature AAM deployment may create locally high-density traffic around capacity-constrained vertiports. This paper considers mixed operational scenarios in which unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft share the same vertiport and surrounding terminal airspace. In such environments, eVTOL operations typically follow air traffic management (ATM) procedures and are strategically deconflicted in advance, resulting in schedules that are largely inflexible. By contrast, certain UAV missions, such as time-critical medical deliveries following intercity eVTOL transport, require immediate departure and cannot wait for global replanning. Safely allowing emergency UAVs to egress from locally dense or capacity-constrained terminal airspace without disrupting pre-planned eVTOL operations therefore poses significant operational challenges. To address this problem, we develop an Asynchronous Proximal Policy Optimization (APPO) based reinforcement learning approach for emergency UAV egress that explicitly encodes separation safety and egress efficiency. A distributed policy-training framework based on Ray RLlib is developed, and the simulation environment incorporates the AirLib flight-control model from AirSim to represent low-level UAV maneuver responses during speed and heading command execution. Simulation results demonstrate that, under locally dense terminal traffic conditions, the proposed approach demonstrates stronger overall robustness than APF, VO, RRT, Modified CL-RRT, and MCTS-UCT in terms of safe-egress performance, separation maintenance, and online computational efficiency.

title: Interactive Bi-LSTM: A novel approach for multi-channel vessel traffic flow prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of vessel traffic flow (VTF) is essential for enhancing maritime safety and improving the efficiency of cargo transportation and port operations. In multi-channel waterways, VTF exhibits strong temporal variability, pronounced fluctuations, and complex inter-channel correlations, which pose significant challenges for reliable forecasting. Existing deep learning methods often fail to effectively capture the dynamic interaction effects among channels, as well as the coupled spatiotemporal dependencies inherent in VTF data, leading to suboptimal prediction accuracy and stability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Multi-Objective Interactive Deep Learning Network (MOIDLNet) based on the Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) architecture. The proposed model introduces a novel hidden-state interaction mechanism that enables dynamic information exchange across channels within a unified temporal modeling framework, thereby effectively capturing inter-channel dependencies and their evolving patterns. In addition, a hybrid loss function, termed MSEDTW, is developed by integrating Mean Squared Error (MSE) with Dynamic Time Warping (DTW), allowing the model to jointly optimize point-wise accuracy and global temporal consistency. Extensive experiments are conducted on real-world AIS datasets collected from the Chengshan Jiao Promontory (CJP) and Caofeidian Port (CFDP). Sensitivity analyses on key hyperparameters, including iteration number, learning rate, and input sequence length, are performed to determine optimal model configurations. The experimental results demonstrate that MOIDLNet consistently outperforms conventional machine learning methods and representative deep learning models in terms of prediction accuracy and stability. These findings highlight the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach and its potential for supporting intelligent maritime traffic management.

title: Adaptive air traffic management via large language model augmented reinforcement learning
abstract: Urban Air Mobility (UAM) presents a transformative approach to urban transportation by enabling safe and rapid air travel. However, ensuring safety remains a critical prerequisite for large-scale deployment. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has demonstrated promise as a tactical deconfliction method, offering real-time speed advisories to maintain safe separation between aircraft. Yet, the manual design of reward functions and hyperparameter tuning is time-consuming and often lacks adaptability across varying scenarios. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an LLM-augmented MARL framework that uses LLMs to generate candidate reward-weight configurations offline and then selects among pre-trained MARL policies according to user preferences and system-level performance metrics. Rather than performing online reward reshaping during execution, the proposed framework improves adaptability by decoupling reward-parameter exploration from preference-conditioned policy recommendation. The results demonstrate the feasibility of using LLMs to reduce manual reward tuning effort and support human-preference-aware tactical deconfliction under diverse operational priorities.

title: Vessel traffic flow prediction for smart port logistics: A hierarchical adaptive spatio-temporal transformer
abstract: Reliable vessel traffic flow (VTF) prediction is essential for proactive port management and maritime safety. However, current VTF prediction paradigms are hindered by four critical challenges: (1) heterogeneity among the retained prediction inputs, including vessel counts, spatial descriptors, and temporal indicators; (2) multi-scale noise in non-stationary temporal dynamics; (3) rapid topological shifts in port networks; and (4) temporal observation sparsity impacting long-horizon prediction robustness. To address these limitations, we propose a Hierarchical Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Transformer (HAST-Former). The approach integrates four specialized modules: (1) a Data Embedding Layer (DEL) to align vessel counts, spatial descriptors, and temporal indicators into a common latent space; (2) a Multi-Scale Temporal Guidance (MSTG) module to suppress recording noise while capturing hierarchical temporal patterns; (3) an Adaptive Spatial Graph Convolution (ASGC) module to reconstruct port topologies based on real-time traffic states; and (4) a Spatio-Temporal Self-Attention (STSA) mechanism with partitioned heads and relative temporal biases (ALiBi) to ensure stable long-horizon prediction under sparse and noisy observed conditions. Extensive evaluations on large-scale datasets from Shanghai and Zhoushan ports demonstrate that HAST-Former consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method and highlight its potential for smart port logistics applications.

title: Learning from risk: LLM-guided generation of safety-critical scenarios with prior knowledge
abstract: Autonomous driving faces critical challenges in rare long-tail events and complex multi-agent interactions, which are scarce in real-world data yet essential for robust safety validation. This paper presents a high-fidelity scenario generation framework that integrates a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) with a large language model (LLM). The CVAE encodes historical trajectories and map information from large-scale naturalistic datasets to learn latent traffic structures, enabling the generation of physically consistent base scenarios. Building on this, the LLM acts as an adversarial reasoning engine, parsing unstructured scene descriptions into domain-specific loss functions and dynamically guiding scenario generation across varying risk levels. This knowledge-driven optimization balances realism with controllability, ensuring that generated scenarios remain both plausible and risk-sensitive. Extensive experiments in CARLA and SMARTS demonstrate that our framework substantially increases the coverage of high-risk and long-tail events, improves consistency between simulated and real-world traffic distributions, and exposes autonomous driving systems to interactions that are significantly more challenging than those produced by existing rule- or data-driven methods. These results establish a new pathway for safety validation, enabling principled stress-testing of autonomous systems under rare but consequential events.

title: Prompt and sequential selection transfer based large language model for traffic prediction with limited data
abstract: In the field of intelligent transportation systems, data scarcity severely constrains the generalization capability and precision of prediction models. Existing transfer learning methods often suffer from negative transfer due to discrepancies between source and target domains, compromising prediction performance. Although current LLMs exhibit strong feature learning capabilities, they primarily depend on pretrained knowledge and make insufficient use of source city data for targeted training. Moreover, they fail to conduct in-depth exploration of the characteristics inherent in limited datasets. To address this issue, we propose a Prompt and Sequential Selection Transfer based Large Language Model (PST-LLM) for traffic prediction with limited data, which represents the first effort to leverage LLMs specifically for traffic prediction under limited data without relying on conventional transfer learning frameworks. First, we develop a Source City Sequential Selection (SCSS) strategy for knowledge fusion. Combined with simulated fine-tuning on data-rich source cities, this approach precisely identifies optimal transfer paths to mitigate negative transfer induced by data scarcity. Second, we incorporate text prompts to enable deep fusion of semantic cues with spatio-temporal data. This integration guides the model to efficiently capture traffic patterns under limited data. Finally, a joint pruning and freezing strategy is adopted to streamline model parameters, suppressing overfitting during limited data training and significantly enhancing generalization capability. Experimental results show that PST-LLM consistently outperforms state-of-the-art(SOTA) across real-world datasets under identical settings. Furthermore, PST-LLM not only can generates predictive outputs but also can produces interpretable reasoning analysis and actionable travel recommendations. This is achieved through a dedicated reasoning branch that decodes the model’s high-level embeddings into natural language based on prompt engineering. The source code for PST-LLM is available at https://github.com/pku-smart-city/source_code/tree/main/PST-LLM.

title: Physics-informed multi-agent deep reinforcement learning for dynamic emergency resource scheduling in marine oil spills
abstract: An efficient marine oil spill response is essential for mitigating environmental impacts. However, dynamic ocean conditions and uncertain spill evolution make timely and flexible emergency resource scheduling challenging. This study proposes a physics-informed multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework for maritime oil spill response. The framework integrates oil evolution processes and environmental dynamics into the decision-making environment, enabling agents to adapt scheduling strategies under changing spill conditions. A multi-objective reward mechanism is developed to balance recovery performance, response time, and resource utilization. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed MADDPG-based method consistently outperforms benchmark approaches across multiple objectives. Furthermore, the framework is validated using a real-world Bohai Sea oil spill scenario, demonstrating its applicability under realistic marine conditions. Multi-seed experiments show stable performance with a low coefficient of variation of 2.7% for the Overall Performance Index, confirming the robustness and reliability of the proposed approach for intelligent oil spill emergency response.

title: A dual-channel model integrating wavelet denoising and multi-head self-attention mechanism for predicting train travel times of China-Europe railway express
abstract: The China-Europe Railway Express (CRE) is an important logistics corridor linking China and Europe. However, due to various influencing factors during transportation, existing prediction models generally fail to correctly represent the complex nonlinear spatio-temporal aspects of the CRE train travel times, leading to incorrect train travel time predictions. To overcome this challenge, this study proposes a Multi-scale Wavelet Denoising (MWD)-Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) dual-channel model incorporating a Multi-head Self-attention Mechanism (MHSA) (MWD-CNN-GRU-MHSA) to forecast CRE train travel times. The MWD is first employed to extract features and reduce the noise in the historical train travel times, aiming to improve data quality. Then, a dual-channel model combining CNN and GRU is established, where the CNN learns local spatial patterns and the GRU handles time-dependent features, processing the input time series in parallel. MHSA is introduced into the dual-channel model to flexibly allocate weights on salient fused features derived from the two branches. A series of comparative experiments are conducted to evaluate the proposed method based on real-world CRE round-trip train travel time data. The experimental findings show that the MWD-CNN-GRU-MHSA framework outperforms thirteen mainstream baseline models in forecasting performance and generalization. Specifically, the MWD-CNN-GRU-MHSA model exhibits robust performance in CRE train travel time estimation, with root mean square error (RMSE) of 7.516 hours, mean absolute error (MAE) of 5.053 hours, mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 1.259%, and coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.907. In conclusion, the MWD-CNN-GRU-MHSA model demonstrates strong stability and robustness, with good adaptability to complex transportation data. It offers reliable technical support for rail dispatching optimization and CRE service quality improvement.

title: Deep reinforcement learning for optimizing mobile depots allocation and hybrid order dispatch in last-mile delivery under multi-participants behavioral uncertainty
abstract: As last-mile delivery demand continues to grow and customer preferences become increasingly diverse, traditional single-mode logistics systems are inadequate in addressing the complexity and variability of modern urban delivery environments. In this paper, we propose an innovative hybrid last-mile delivery system that leverages mobile depots as intermediate hubs, integrating crowd-shipping, and customer self-pickup, to enhance cost-effectiveness. However multiple stakeholders in the system have conflicting interests, ignoring their behavioral uncertainties can impair operational efficiency and increase delivery costs. For example, customers and crowd-shippers may compete for the limited storage capacity of mobile depots, and crowd-shippers may be unwilling to deliver orders that customers decline to pick up. Specifically, the study captures crowd-shippers’ order-acceptance behavior and customers’ self-pickup choice through two binomial logit models, and embeds these behavioral components into a stochastic mixed-integer programming model. This model jointly optimizes mobile depots allocation and order dispatch decisions, aiming to minimize the expected total operational cost. Considering computational complexity of this model, we propose PRiME-DQN, a reinforcement learning framework that incorporates behavior-prioritized resource filtering, action biasing, and model-efficient temperature tuning to accelerate convergence and improve solution quality. A case study on Amazon’s last-mile delivery in Seattle shows that the proposed hybrid model achieves up to 49.5% cost reduction in low-shipper settings and 11.3% in higher-shipper settings compared to a crowd-shipping system, while also consistently surpassing the self-pickup baseline by 3–6%. Extensive scaling experiments show that PRiME-DQN produces high-quality feasible solutions efficiently. For the largest instances, it achieves delivery costs 1.97% lower than Gurobi’s best incumbent solution obtained within the 3,600-second time limit, while reducing the solution time to approximately 1400 seconds.

title: Generative AI and Machine learning collaboration for container dwell time prediction via data standardization
abstract: Import container dwell time (ICDT) prediction is a key task for improving productivity in container terminals, as accurate predictions enable a reduction in container rehandling operations by yard cranes. Achieving this objective requires accurately predicting the dwell time of individual containers. However, the primary determinants of container dwell time are recorded as unstructured text, limiting their effective use in machine learning models. To address this limitation, this study proposes a collaborative framework that integrates generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) with machine learning. The proposed framework employs Gen AI to standardize unstructured information into standard international codes, with dynamic re-prediction triggered by electronic data interchange state updates, thereby enabling the machine learning model to predict ICDT accurately. Extensive experiments conducted on real container terminal data demonstrate that the proposed methodology achieves a 13.88 % improvement in mean absolute error over conventional models that do not utilize standardized information. Furthermore, applying the improved predictions to container stacking strategies achieves up to a 13.07 % reduction in the number of relocations, thereby empirically demonstrating the potential of Gen AI to enhance productivity in container terminal operations. Overall, this study provides technical and methodological insights into the adoption and effectiveness of Gen AI in port logistics.

title: Constrained reinforcement learning for the dynamic inventory routing problem under stochastic supply and demand
abstract: Green hydrogen has multiple use cases and is produced from renewable energy, such as solar or wind energy. It can be stored in large quantities, decoupling renewable energy generation from its use, and is therefore considered essential for achieving a climate-neutral economy. The intermittency of renewable energy generation and the stochastic nature of demand are, however, challenging factors for the dynamic planning of hydrogen storage and transportation. This holds particularly in the early-adoption phase when hydrogen distribution occurs through vehicle-based networks. We therefore address the Dynamic Inventory Routing Problem (DIRP) under stochastic supply and demand with direct deliveries for the vehicle-based distribution of hydrogen. To solve this problem, we propose a Constrained Reinforcement Learning (CRL) framework that integrates constraints into the learning process and incorporates parameterized post-decision state value predictions. Additionally, we introduce Lookahead-based CRL (LCRL), which improves decision-making over a multi-period horizon to enhance short-term planning while maintaining the value predictions. Our computational experiments demonstrate the efficacy of CRL and LCRL across diverse instances. Our learning methods provide near-optimal solutions on small scale instances that are solved via value iteration. Furthermore, both methods outperform typical deep learning approaches such as Proximal Policy Optimization, as well as classical inventory heuristics, such as (s,S)-policy-based and Power-of-Two-based heuristics. Furthermore, LCRL achieves a 10% improvement over CRL on average, albeit with higher computational requirements. Analyses of optimal replenishment policies reveal that accounting for stochastic supply and demand influences these policies, showing the importance of our addition to the DIRP.

title: Simulation-based Bayesian optimization for large-scale dynamic lane allocation
abstract: The current traffic research highly relies on Simulation-Based Optimization (SBO) to evaluate complex operational strategies. However, large-scale network problems often involve hundreds of control decisions that make the search space extremely high-dimensional and computationally prohibitive. This study develops an advanced Bayesian Optimization (BO) method for the large-scale SBO and applies it to solve the Dynamic Lane Allocation (DLA) problem, which grants ride-sharing vehicles conditional access to Dedicated Bus Lanes (DBLs) with allocation decisions varying across both location and time. As a result, the problem requires binary decisions across hundreds of space–time units, creating an extremely high-dimensional, combinatorial search space that existing optimization methods cannot handle efficiently. To address this challenge, we introduce a Grouped Automatic Relevance Determination (GARD) Hamming kernel that separates temporal and spatial relevance in the Gaussian Process (GP) surrogate, a dynamic group-aware dimension-reduction mechanism that identifies influential regions of the solution space, and a trust-region adaptation tailored to binary decisions to improve sampling efficiency. These components are combined with hybrid candidate generation and mixed batch sampling to enhance robustness under limited simulation budgets. The method is evaluated using a trip-based Macroscopic Fundamental Diagram (MFD) multimodal simulator on both a controlled virtual grid and the large-scale Barcelona network. Results show that the proposed BO approach consistently converges faster, achieves higher solution quality, and maintains feasibility under strict bus-service constraints compared with metaheuristic methods. The framework also demonstrates stable performance across varied OD patterns and scalability to real-world city networks.On the large-scale Barcelona network, the proposed method achieves, on average, a 14.2% lower final objective and 2.16 × faster convergence than Large Neighborhood Search (LNS), as well as a 1.1% lower final objective and 1.52 × faster convergence than Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS). These findings highlight the potential of the proposed method to support efficient decision-making in large-scale, binary, network-level traffic optimization.

title: Global maritime logistics resilience amid trade conflicts: forecasting port risk and identifying critical roles via spatiotemporal graph neural networks
abstract: The escalation of trade conflicts since 2018, compounded by geopolitical disruptions including the COVID-19 pandemic, the Russia–Ukraine conflict, and the Red Sea crisis, has placed unprecedented strain on global maritime logistics. Using a spatiotemporal graph neural network framework and AIS data from January 2019 to December 2024, this study aims to forecast port operational risk and identify critical port roles in risk propagation. We construct monthly shipping networks for four vessel types, namely container ships, bulk carriers, general cargo ships, and oil tankers, and synthesize a composite risk index from standardized in-port time and waiting time. The selected ST-GNN models outperform both the LSTM and ARIMA baselines, while the neighborhood dependency analysis provides further evidence that network information contributes additional predictive value. Model-extrinsic counterfactual analysis quantifies three port role dimensions, namely Source, Sink, and Mediator, representing risk emission, risk absorption, and network bridging, respectively, and identifies differentiated role profiles and high-intensity transmission links. Results reveal that the most active ports in risk propagation are predominantly small and medium-sized specialized ports, and that the strongest transmission follows direct Source-to-Sink connections. Risk propagation patterns differ across vessel categories and are consistent with differences in their network structures and underlying shipping and trade patterns during a period characterized by sustained disruptions.

title: A large language model-empowered approach to trajectory prediction for edge deployment on ships
abstract: Large language models (LLM) are driving the deep integration of artificial intelligence and intelligent shipping, ushering in a new technological paradigm. Although existing deep learning–based ship trajectory prediction methods have achieved significant progress, their capacity to integrate non-numerical semantic knowledge remains insufficient, yet such knowledge is crucial for accurately characterizing ship behavior patterns. To bridge this gap, we propose LLM-EdgeSTP, the first LLM-empowered and edge-deployable ship trajectory prediction framework that unifies continuous automatic identification system (AIS) trajectories with discrete maritime textual knowledge through cross-modal reasoning. The method comprises three core components. (1) The maritime semantic prompt unit (MSPU) transforms raw AIS trajectories into context-aware natural language prompts. (2) The navigational interaction representation unit (NIRU) models ship–ship interactions by fusing convolutional and attention mechanisms and maps them into the LLM embedding space through representation–language reconstruction to enable semantic understanding of encounter and avoidance intentions. Lightweight LLMs such as LLaMA and Gemma then fuse navigational states and interaction semantics to generate trajectory predictions in natural language form and decode them into precise coordinates. (3) Edge deployment supports real-time inference on low-power hardware. Experiments across three representative maritime regions demonstrate that LLM-EdgeSTP outperforms ten baseline models by an average of 40% in terms of average displacement error (ADE) and final displacement error (FDE) while satisfying real-time latency requirements. This work lays a key technical foundation for building interpretable, efficient, and practical autonomous navigation systems.

title: A deep reinforcement learning-based algorithm for regional drone routing problem with nonlinear fuel consumption
abstract: With the boom of e-commerce and increasing policy support, regional logistics serving medium- and short-distance transportation have grown rapidly. Large fuel-powered drones are increasingly adopted in this field due to their flexibility and efficiency, yet their deployment has raised concerns regarding pollutant emissions and environmental sustainability. To balance logistics efficiency with environmental responsibility, this paper proposes a regional drone routing problem using large fuel-powered drones, accounting for nonlinear fuel consumption and multiple pollutant emissions. The problem is formulated as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming model to minimize the total cost, including fuel consumption cost, pollutant emission cost, and operational cost. To accurately estimate fuel consumption, a nonlinear fuel consumption function is formulated by comprehensively considering variable payload, fluctuating fuel load, empty weight, the entire flight process, and wind. A deep reinforcement learning-based algorithm, namely a double-deep Q-network with attention mechanism based large neighborhood search algorithm, is designed to solve the model. The effectiveness of the algorithm and the nonlinear fuel consumption function is validated by comparative experiments on simulated instances, and then the impacts of refueling availability and wind conditions on the total cost are further investigated. Furthermore, based on a real-world case, this paper shows that drones can reduce the total cost, while sensitivity analyses evaluate the impact of key factors on environmental and economic performance. The results indicate that the proposed model and algorithm can effectively enhance operational efficiency and environmental performance.

title: Saline patch identification using a semi-supervised knowledge integration deep learning framework based solely on UAV RGB imagery
abstract: Soil saline patches, as a direct and early indicators of soil salinization degradation, pose a serious threat to agricultural productivity and land sustainability in coastal and arid areas. However, most existing studies focus on regional-scale classification using medium- and low-resolution imagery, lacking fine-grained, high-precision identification of soil salinity patches. In this study, we propose a semi-supervised knowledge integration (SSKI) framework for the accurate extraction of soil saline patches using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) RGB imagery. To address the time-consuming and labor-intensive problem of sample labeling, a dual-sample optimization strategy is designed. It simultaneously enhances the diversity of labeled samples via color and spatial augmentation, and selects reliable pseudo-labels for unlabeled samples through sample stability evaluation. Moreover, considering the unique characteristics of soil saline patches, a multimodal information learning network is proposed, which integrates multi-scale soil saline patch information, spectral-ecological features, and texture-semantic joint information, aiming to enhance boundary precision and inter-class discrimination. We validate the proposed method using a newly constructed UAV dataset (DongY) covering approximately 16 km2 of saline-affected farmland in Dongying, China in 2022 and 2024. Experimental results show that SSKI consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. In particular, the multi-year, UAV-based saline patch identification demonstrates the strong temporal generalization capability of the proposed method. Furthermore, by mapping the spatial distribution of soil saline patches, the study provides a basis for assessing the impact of salinization on crop growth and offers essential data support for the management and remediation of saline-alkali land.

title: A top-view transformer-based framework for tiny tea bud detection with gradient-guided attention and position-sensitive loss
abstract: Accurately detecting tea buds under top-view imaging is essential for automating tea harvesting. However, this task is particularly challenging due to the buds’ extremely small size, blurred boundaries, high visual similarity to background leaves, and low inter-class variance—all of which result in sparse features and frequent mislocalization. Existing CNN-based detectors often struggle to preserve fine spatial details while modeling global context in such scenarios. To address these issues, we propose a Transformer-based framework for robust top-view tea bud detection, leveraging its global attention mechanism to enhance feature discrimination for tiny and ambiguous objects. Specifically, a Gradient-guided Class Activation Attention module enhances spatial sensitivity by generating attention maps from mid-level CNN features via gradient signals, allowing the model to focus on weak yet semantically relevant regions. An Explicit-Guided Decoder reinforces inter-layer consistency and structural modeling by leveraging feedback from previous predictions and stage-wise feature injection. In addition, a Spatial Position-Sensitive Enhancement Loss introduces a Gaussian-based weighting mechanism to emphasize central object regions, improving localization accuracy for tiny targets. Experiments on a top-view tea bud dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art baselines (YOLOv11, DETR, RT-DETR), achieving a Precision of 0.8371 and mAP@0.5 of 0.8013. Moreover, evaluations on three public tiny-object detection datasets further confirm its generalization across domains. These results highlight the effectiveness and transferability of the proposed approach in both agricultural and general tiny-object detection scenarios.

title: IBOA-SDAE: A tool wear condition monitoring model for cotton stalk crushing
abstract: A tool wear monitoring system was designed to address the problems of tool wear severely and the lack of monitoring device leading to work failure in the operation of cotton straw crushing and returning to the field. This monitoring system used STM32 microcontroller as the main controller to monitored different wear states of the tool based on sensor technology and deep learning algorithm. In order to solve the problem of selecting the hyperparameters of Stacked Denoising Auto Encoder (SDAE), a method of monitoring the wear state of cotton straw crushing tool (IBOA-SDAE) was proposed by integrating the Improved Butterfly Optimization Algorithm (IBOA) and SDAE. The hyperparameters of the SDAE model were adaptively selected by using the IBOA algorithm to determine the final model structure. To verify the validity of the IBOA-SDAE model, repeated comparison tests were conducted for a number of models in the same parameter setting environment. The experimental results show that compared with the seven models of SDAE, PSO-SDAE, SSA-SDAE, BOA-SDAE, HHO-SDAE, CWBOA-SDAE, and SIBOA-SDAE, the IBOA-SDAE model improves the accuracy of the wear condition monitoring and that the accuracy of a single trial is maintained at a high level. The IBOA-SDAE model was embedded into the monitoring system and field validation tests were conducted, which showed that the developed tool wear condition monitoring system has good performance in terms of recognition accuracy and robustness.

title: A hybrid and high-performance model for tea cultivars discrimination using canopy images with convolutional neural network and machine learning algorithm
abstract: Accurate and rapid discrimination of tea cultivars under field conditions is essential for precision tea plantation management. Traditional discrimination approaches rely on expensive instrumentation, labor-intensive manipulation, and destructive sampling, which causes difficult to implement. In this study, a hybrid and high-performance tea cultivar discrimination model, named EFLS_Model, was developed by combining convolutional neural network (CNN), feature extraction, dimensionality reduction and machine learning (ML) algorithm. A field dataset of 8,000 canopy images for 16 tea cultivars was constructed, and four discrimination methods were investigated based on EfficientNetV2. The results demonstrated that: 1) The fine-tuned EfficienetNetV2_L achieved 96.00% accuracy required long training time; 2) The approach of using the pre-trained EfficientNetV2 as the feature extractor and combined with ML algorithm substantially reduced training time; 3) Dimensionality reduction of the extracted deep features via linear discriminant analysis (LDA) alleviated redundancy and improved performance; 4) Better discrimination performance was achieved by integrating deep features and manually-extracted features. Among the developed models, the dimensionality of the combined features (including deep features extracted by the pre-trained EfficientNetV2_M, and manually-extracted color and texture features) was reduced to 15 by LDA. The EFLS_Model developed by support vector machine performed optimally with an accuracy of 98.50% and a training time of only 0.12 min. The discrimination performance of EFLS_Model outperformed other CNN models, including GoogLeNet, ResNet, VGG, MobileNetV3, and ConvNeXt. This study enables accurate discrimination of tea cultivars under field conditions, providing technical and theoretical support for developing intelligent tea plantation management platforms, while also offering a valuable reference for cultivar discrimination in other crops.

title: An efficient and physics-informed regional maize yield estimation scheme by combining data assimilation and machine learning
abstract: Accurate regional crop yield prediction is essential for agricultural development and food security. Data assimilation (DA) frameworks combined with satellite observations improve regional yield estimation but remain computationally intensive at large scales. This study aims to develop an efficient, physics-informed regional yield estimation framework by integrating DA with machine learning (ML) to reduce computational costs and improve accuracy. An iterative ensemble smoother DA algorithm was applied with SWAP crop growth model to generate “virtual” yield observations across randomly selected maize pixels. These observations, together with remote sensing data, were used to train four ML models—Feature Tokenizer Transformer (FTT), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Random Forest (RF)—for regional maize yield estimation in Shandong Province, China. The results reveal that the DA-ML framework significantly reduces computational costs compared to traditional pixel-based DA methods (i.e., achieving a computational time saving of over 99.8 %), while maintaining comparable yield estimation accuracy. Among the model, RF achieved the best performance, with regional yield estimates across 114 counties showing R 2 = 0.62, RMSE = 1.19 × 10 5 t in the calibration year and R 2 = 0.49, RMSE = 1.28 × 10 5 t in the validation year. Furthermore, relative importance analysis from the DA–ML framework indicates that radiation, soil moisture, and rainfall during the jointing stage are the most influential variables for regional maize yield estimation, followed by wind speed, air humidity, and temperature during the reproductive stage, highlighting the critical role of environmental conditions in the later growth stages for determining final yield outcomes. This study showcases a reliable DA-ML system for rapid-responsive regional crop yield estimation and management decisions, with potential applicability to other crops and regions.

title: EPDNet: A method for identifying tomato leaf diseases with uneven samples
abstract: Tomato industry is one of the important parts of agriculture, and the timely diagnosis of leaf diseases plays a key role in ensuring its production safety. At present, most of the mainstream recognition technologies are based on laboratory standard images to construct recognition models. Although they can achieve accurate analysis of isolated leaves, it is difficult to cope with the practical challenges such as complex climate and environmental factors of plant growth in open environments. The recognition is difficult due to the influence factors of open environment, such as the distortion of disease spots caused by light, the occlusion of branches and leaves, and the confusion of soil attachment and real disease spots. To solve the problem of unbalanced distribution of tomato leaf disease samples in open environment and the big difference of similar diseases, this study proposes a single-modal recognition architecture for tomato leaf diseases based on Efficient localization and Physical information and Dynamic adaptive optimization Network (EPDNet). Firstly, an efficient positioning feature enhancement module is designed to effectively enhance the network’s attention to important regions by calculating and fusing the horizontal and vertical attention weights. Then, a physical information neural network-cross entropy hybrid loss function was designed to ensure the accuracy of prediction, while restricting the smoothness and continuity of the feature map to improve the robustness of the model. Finally, a dynamic adaptive optimization algorithm was designed to iteratively update the learning rate to improve the feature discrimination ability, so as to reduce the identification differences of diseases within the class. Experimental results show that the accuracy of EPDNet on the tomato leaf dataset reaches 93.62%, and the F1 score reaches 93.31 %, which is significantly better than the existing methods. This study provides an effective solution for the application of deep learning methods in crop diseases.

title: Diagnosis of maize nitrogen status under contrasting water and nitrogen regimes using a canopy-stratified and multi-source remote sensing framework
abstract: Maize leaf nitrogen exhibits significant vertical heterogeneity within the canopy, which often compromises the accuracy of remote sensing-based nitrogen status diagnosis. To address the limited consideration of leaf-layer contributions and multi-source feature integration, this study proposed a three-dimensional coupled nitrogen diagnosis framework integrating progressive leaf-layer labeling, multi-source feature fusion, and machine learning modeling, based on spring maize experiments under various water and nitrogen regimes in Xinjiang, China. Stratified ground sampling was conducted to obtain leaf nitrogen weight (LNW) from the upper, middle, and lower canopy layers, and 22 vegetation indices (VIs), eight texture features (TFs), and 15 texture indices (TIs) were extracted from UAV multispectral imagery to construct a multi-source feature set. Results demonstrated that the combination of upper and middle canopy leaves best represented overall plant nitrogen status. Feature fusion significantly enhanced model performance, with extreme gradient boosting achieving the highest estimation accuracy for the nitrogen nutrition index (NNI) (R2 = 0.68, RPD = 1.77), and convolutional neural networks performing best in LNW estimation (R2 = 0.83, RPD = 2.31). The critical nitrogen dilution curves derived from the estimated LNW revealed that irrigation levels significantly influenced the curve intercepts and slopes, highlighting the dual regulatory effects of water on nitrogen uptake and dilution. Coupled with ArcGIS-based spatial visualization, the framework enabled dynamic monitoring of NNI across V6, VT, R3, and R6 growth stages. Overall, this framework effectively improved both the spatiotemporal resolution and estimation accuracy of maize nitrogen status, providing a theoretical basis and technical support for precision nitrogen management and the transition toward sustainable agriculture.

title: High-Frequency, real-time parcel-level agricultural monitoring Framework: Integrating Tower-Based cameras and artificial intelligence
abstract: Traditional remote sensing approaches for agricultural monitoring are frequently constrained by limited temporal resolution, discontinuous coverage, and high operational costs. These limitations hinder the delivery of high-frequency, continuous, and unmanned agro-information that is critical for precision agriculture—especially in smallholder and autonomous farming scenarios. Meanwhile, communication towers equipped with video cameras are ubiquitously deployed in rural landscapes yet remain underutilized for agricultural applications. This study presents a high-frequency, tower-based, unmanned agricultural monitoring framework that progressively addresses three fundamental challenges, thereby enabling real-time, parcel-level agro-monitoring. In particular, our framework tackles: (1) accurate geo-referencing of oblique imagery through a quaternion-based geographic coordinate transformation, which precisely maps video streams to field parcels; (2) robust segmentation of cultivated parcels via a GIS-guided approach that integrates field boundary data with the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for automatic delineation; and (3) comprehensive temporal intelligence by leveraging a large language model (LLM)-based recognition strategy that fuses time-series imagery, crop rotation history, and field management data to identify crop types, growth stages, farming operations, and anomalies at the parcel level. The resulting hierarchical framework combines front-end local processing for initial event detection with cloud-based advanced analysis, enhancing operational efficiency while ensuring rapid responses. Field deployments in three agricultural regions of China demonstrate that the framework supports automated, hourly-to-daily monitoring of farming activities and crop conditions within a 1–2 km radius of each tower, with key agricultural events, growth stage transitions, and parcel-level anomalies tracked and mapped in near real time. Compared to conventional satellite and aerial remote sensing, this approach offers substantial improvements in monitoring frequency, spatial continuity, and labor efficiency.

title: A multi-scale linear cross-modal fusion architecture for tomato leaf disease segmentation
abstract: Tomato, as a globally important economic crop, requires precise and timely disease management to secure yield and quality. Yet segmentation robustness is often limited by weak semantic understanding from single-modality images, narrow receptive fields of convolutional structures, and discontinuous boundary predictions. To address these issues, we propose the Multi-scale Linear Cross-modal Fusion Architecture for Tomato Leaf Disease Segmentation (MS-LCFNet). We construct a real-world field dataset covering five major tomato leaf diseases, annotated by experts with detailed textual descriptions to enable multimodal learning. MS-LCFNet strengthens semantic representation via cross-modal fusion, captures local and global context through an Adaptive Long-short Distance Perception module, and improves boundary continuity with a Physics-informed Smoothness-constrained Loss. Experiments show that MS-LCFNet achieves 87.13 % mIoU on our dataset and 90.78 % on PlantVillage, improving over previous state-of-the-art methods by + 4.62 % and + 4.48 %, respectively, and demonstrating superior accuracy and robustness in complex agricultural scenarios.

title: A multi-class deep learning segmentation approach for automated analysis of axial and lateral roots in barley plants
abstract: Accurate segmentation and analysis of root images from soil-grown plants are critical for advancing our understanding of root growth and plasticity under varying environmental conditions. Most approaches typically rely on binary segmentation of the entire root system architecture (RSA), which limits their ability to capture the hierarchical complexity of root structures, including axial and lateral roots. To address this, our study evaluated five convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures for multi-class (i.e. axial/lateral) segmentation of 2D root images from barley plants grown in rhizoboxes: (i) U-Net, (ii) U-Net with Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (UnetASPP), (iii) U-Net with Attention Block (UnetAtt), (iv) DeepLabV3+ with MobileNetV2 (DLMB), and (v) DeepLabV3+ with ResNet-50 (DLR50). Among these, the DLR50 model achieved the highest segmentation accuracy, particularly for distinguishing lateral roots within complex RSA structures. Furthermore, analysis of root traits derived from the segmented images confirmed that DLR50 produced the most reliable estimations of phenotypic traits compared to ground truth measurements. These findings highlight the strong potential of advanced multi-class CNN models—especially DLR50—for detailed and quantitative analysis of soil-root systems, providing new insights into root responses to environmental conditions. • Evaluated five CNN models for multi-class segmentation of 2D root images, distinguishing axial and lateral roots. • DLR50 (DeepLabV3+ with ResNet-50) outperformed all models in accurately segmenting complex root structures. • Improved trait prediction accuracy using DLR50-segmented images compared to ground truth data. • Enables fine-grained analysis of root plasticity in response to environmental changes.

title: Routing enabled optimization and deep recurrent VGG-16 model for plant disease detection in IoT
abstract: Agricultural productivity is the major source of the economy of the agrarian nation and is also considered the major source of human activities. It is vital to detect and manage plant diseases to enhance the overall growth and quality of agricultural produce. Modern agriculture increasingly uses IoT and automation tools to monitor and collect valuable information on plant health and disease occurrence. Here, the plant disease is detected using Deep Recurrent Visual Geometry Group-16 (DRVGG-16) in the IoT platform with routing based on the Adam Dung Beetle Optimization (ADBO) algorithm. The DRVGG-16 is the combination of Deep Recurrent Neural Network (DRNN) with Visual Geometry Group-16 (VGG-16) and ADBO is the fusion of Adam optimizer with Dung Beetle Optimization (DBO). Initially, the captured agricultural images are transmitted to the base station via ADBO-optimized routing for plant disease detection. The base station initiates disease detection by applying a bilateral filter to preprocess the input plant leaf images. The preprocessed images are segmented using the DeepLabV3+ model, and features are subsequently derived from the segmented leaf areas. Finally, plant disease detection is performed using the proposed DRVGG-16 model. Furthermore, the performances of the proposed schemes are validated, where ADBO attained distance, delay and energy of 0.343 m, 0.305 ms and 0.375 J. The DRVGG-16 obtained superior results of 91.43 % accuracy, 90.63 % True Positive Rate (TPR), 90.73 % precision, 92.34 % True Negative Rate (TNR) and 90.68 % F1-score. Therefore, the proposed IoT-based framework combining DRVGG-16 and ADBO routing effectively detects plant diseases with high accuracy while optimizing energy and transmission efficiency.

title: Dual-branch frequency-domain fusion for RGB-D tree trunks instance segmentation
abstract: Tree trunk instance segmentation is a crucial task in vision-based perception systems for forestry robots, enabling precise autonomous navigation in complex forest environments. However, existing RGB-only methods struggle to achieve adequate accuracy due to challenges such as uneven illumination and occlusions. To overcome these limitations, we propose TrunkInst, a dual-branch, frequency-domain fusion RGB-D network for tree trunk instance segmentation. TrunkInst employs a Frequency-Domain Decomposition Gate Fusion (FDGF) module that decomposes and selectively fuses RGB and depth features in the frequency domain, enhancing segmentation accuracy by suppressing noise and preserving important details. The Multi-Head Dynamic Upsampling (MDU) module generates higher-quality upsampled feature maps by learning multiple offset groups, improving the resolution of small tree trunks. Finally, a Transformer decoder, using cross-modal queries between RGB features and fused representations, mitigates the negative effects of degraded depth maps. We also propose the Trunk-Depths dataset, which includes 1,326 finely annotated RGB-depth image pairs for tree-trunk instance segmentation. On this dataset, TrunkInst achieves a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 52.8%, with 85.3% AP at IoU=0.5 and 54.4% AP at IoU=0.75—improvements of +2.6%, +1.4%, and +4.6% over an RGB baseline, respectively. Further experiments on the public COME15K and NYU-Depth-V2 datasets demonstrate the generality and robustness of the model. TrunkInst also delivers real-time inference at 45 fps, achieving a good trade-off between accuracy and speed.

title: FM-SAM: individual tree crown delineation and classification based on Segmentation Anything Model (SAM) and YOLOv10 in UAV imagery for forest monitoring
abstract: Forest monitoring plays a crucial role in the sustainable management and conservation of natural resources, with tree crown delineation being a key task for assessing forest structure and tree health. This study presents a novel framework, FM-SAM, integrating YOLOv10 and the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for precise tree crown segmentation and species identification in UAV imagery. The framework combines YOLOv10’s real-time detection capabilities with SAM’s strong segmentation, significantly improving segmentation and classification accuracy. SAM is also employed as a semi-supervised branch in FM-SAM to expedite the annotation process, offering a solution that reduces the need for extensive manual labeling. Experimental results on the MixedForestDataset , comprising both coniferous and broadleaf tree species, demonstrate that FM-SAM outperforms traditional deep learning frameworks such as DeepLabv3 and YOLO-based models, achieving high accuracy, precision, and recall values. The proposed method excels in complex forest environments, enhancing the effectiveness of tree crown delineation and classification for large-scale forest monitoring applications. • FM-SAM framework merges YOLOv10 and SAM for high-accuracy tree crown segmentation. • Efficient labeling with Semi-Supervised Approach, making MixedForestDataset . • The brightness of the images is correlated with the segmentation accuracy.

title: AdaFishCount: Advancing domain-invariant learning via domain-specific perturbation for cross-domain fish counting
abstract: Deep learning-based fish counting is crucial for intelligent aquaculture management. However, variations in water transparency, fish distribution, and camera perspectives introduce significant domain gaps, limiting the adaptability of data-driven counting methods across diverse real-world scenarios. To address this challenge, an unsupervised domain adaptation framework, named AdaFishCount, is designed for fish counting. AdaFishCount integrates domain-specific feature perturbation and domain-invariant feature learning. Specifically, the Domain-Specific Feature Perturbation (DSFP) module performs controllable perturbations in the source feature space to generate target-style samples, simulating domain shifts between different aquaculture environments. Subsequently, domain-invariant feature learning leverages an Attention-guided Domain-Invariant Selector (ADIS) and a Long-term Domain-Invariant Memory (LDIM) module to extract stable and discriminative fish representations. Moreover, a comprehensive loss function is devised to ensure consistent density distributions under various style perturbations and to enhance focus on domain-invariant features. Experimental results demonstrate that AdaFishCount achieves superior cross-domain performance, notably improving MAE, RMSE, and MAPE by 14.66, 15.24, and 43.96, respectively, compared to the state-of-the-art method on the target domain Tank 2, highlighting its strong robustness to domain gaps.

title: A unified Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone with Penalty Outside Point Loss for monocular body measurement of Binglangjiang buffaloes
abstract: Binglangjiang buffalo ( Bubalus bubalis ), a China’s national-level protected livestock genetic resource, lacks comprehensive body measurement data due to its nervous temperament, which impedes conservation and research. However, existing non-contact measurement schemes often rely on expensive multi-camera setups (depth or point cloud), leading to high equipment costs and complex deployment. To overcome these limitations, we propose a cost-effective monocular camera-based body measurement method. It employs a unified Vision Transformer-based backbone network for feature extraction, seamlessly integrating 2D image keypoints detection along with depth estimation via a dedicated head, and introduces a novel Penalty Outside Point Loss. This loss function enhances keypoints localization accuracy by penalizing predictions outside the body region, outperforming conventional loss functions in boundary-sensitive scenarios. Experimental results show that the depth estimation achieves an absolute relative error of 0.159, an average precision of 94.83% for keypoints detection and an interior point ratio of 95.14%. The mean absolute percentage errors for body height, hip height, oblique body length, chest circumference, and abdominal circumference are 7.37%, 6.79%, 13.67%, 8.39%, and 7.35%, respectively. By applying this method, we have successfully completed body measurements for 424 Binglangjiang buffaloes, effectively filling the long-standing gap in comprehensive body measurement data for this breed. This study establishes a reliable, low-cost framework for buffalo body measurement data, offering crucial technical support for efficient conservation and advancing precision livestock management practices.

title: Microalgal density modeling using a low-cost spectral sensor: A Kolmogorov–Arnold network approach
abstract: Microalgae cultivation has recently captured several applications in the field of biotechnology. Microalgae produce biomass that can be converted into a variety of valuable products, including biofuels, bioplastics, dietary supplements, and feed for aquaculture. In microalgae cultivation, monitoring microalgal density estimation is necessary. Traditional microalgae estimation techniques, such as manual counting and the use of a spectrophotometer, are prone to error, costly, and time-consuming. In this paper, we develop a low-cost integrated circuit (IC)-based spectral sensor with Kolmogorov–Arnold network (KAN) as the estimator model for density. The results indicate that the proposed KAN outperforms feedforward neural networks (FNNs). It shows that, despite its limited resolution, the sensor is capable of achieving acceptable performance.

title: Enhancing poultry multi-behavior detection with semi-supervised auto-labeling and prompt-driven zero-shot recognition
abstract: The poultry industry faces growing challenges in ensuring animal welfare, preventing disease outbreaks, and addressing labor shortages. Traditional vision intelligence-based behavior monitoring needs intensive manual labeling, which is impractical for large-scale operations, necessitating advanced, efficient, and scalable solutions. Therefore, this study explores a novel label-efficient learning approach that integrates semi-supervised and text-prompt-based zero-shot learning to enhance poultry behavior detection. Furthermore, the study introduced a dataset that includes 11 common poultry behaviors essential for monitoring to improve health, welfare, and productivity. A dataset comprising 200 annotated images (I-200) with 3,870 instances and 640 annotated images (I-640) with 14,552 instances was utilized for both supervised and semi-supervised training. Additionally, 2,500 unannotated images were incorporated to enhance the model’s performance through semi-supervised learning. This research aims to fully utilize the dataset, facilitate behavior monitoring, and support data-driven decision-making in poultry management by developing and refining an auto-labeling model using an active learning technique. The integration of prompt-then-detect zero-shot models (Clip, GDINO, and YOLOWorld) with a user-friendly text-based detection system further enhances the performance of the semi-supervised model. The results of this study demonstrated that the YOLOv9s model outperformed other supervised learning models, achieving strong performance metrics with a precision of 81.1 %, a recall of 77.9 %, and an F1-score of 79.5 %. With that as the starting point, the semi-supervised I-640 model, which utilized 2,500 pseudo-labeled images, achieved 86.9 % precision, 84.3 % recall, and an 84.9 % F1-score, outperforming all other supervised and semi-supervised baselines. This model improved performance by more than 4.6 % in precision compared to supervised model validation, but also achieved improvements of 5.8 %, 6.4 %, and 5.4 % in precision, recall, and F1-score for prediction results. Furthermore, the trained semi-supervised I-640 model with the integration of YOLOWorld text-prompt feature showed further performance improvements. This text prompt not only helps to detect specific behaviors but also assists users to easy auto-label images. This enhancement can significantly reduce manual annotation efforts and supporting timely intervention. These findings highlight the potential of AI-driven approaches for precision poultry monitoring, offering a scalable and efficient solution for sustainable poultry farming.

title: Robustness of CNN-Based model assessment for pig vocalization classification across diverse acoustic environments
abstract: • Robust pig vocalization classification model using Mixed-MMCT features and CNN. • Built datasets from three commercial pig farms for robustness evaluation. • Proposed a uniform 3-seconds segmentation method for real-time sound processing. • Achieved up to 91% average precision, recall, and F1-score in robustness evaluation. The study on pig vocalization classification has attracted the attention of many researchers. However, since it arises from different environmental conditions of pig farms, developing a robust model that works well across various farms remains a significant challenge. To address these challenges, this study employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to assess the effectiveness of a pig vocalization classification model in diverse farm environments. For the experiment, three datasets named GJDS, ISDS, and JEDS were collected from three actual pig farms. Each dataset consists of 4,000 audio files (1,000 non-vocal, 1,000 coughing, 1,000 screaming, and 1,000 normal), each with a duration of three seconds. A CNN with three convolutional layer blocks, max-pooling, and two fully connected layers is trained using spectrogram features. This study employed a 10-fold cross-validation to evaluate the performance of the model. Through rigorous experiments, the model achieved accuracy of 97.68%, 99.18%, and 97.45% on the GJDS, ISDS, and JEDS datasets, respectively. Robust experiments were conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the model on an unseen dataset by using the combination of two datasets as a training set and one as a testing set. The average performances of robust experiments in terms of precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy were 91.96%, 91.36%, 91.66%, and 91.32%, respectively. The model shows high reliability in classifying pig vocalizations within farm environments. Although performance drops under unfamiliar acoustic conditions, these findings point the way toward future improvements in model generalization.

title: Semantic segmentation of plastic greenhouse frames and its application to finite element model reconstruction for structural response assessment
abstract: Plastic greenhouses (PG) are widespread, low-cost agricultural structures that are highly vulnerable to extreme weather events. However, reliable on-site methods for evaluating structural safety are still lacking. Furthermore, no prior study has presented a pipeline for reconstructing finite element (FE) model of a PG from its point cloud data (PCD) using semantic segmentation. This study proposes and validates a semi-automated framework to address this gap through: 1) automated segmentation of steel frames from PCD extracted through LiDAR scanner; 2) conversion of segmented PCD into as-built FE model; and 3) evaluation of structural response. A transformer-based semantic segmentation model, GHFrameFormer, was trained on a diverse dataset of four PG and evaluated on a completely independent, large-scale test PG. GHFrameFormer achieved the highest mean intersection-over-union of 65.97 %, outperforming baseline models (e.g., Point Transformer v1) and maintaining high computational efficiency. The segmented PCD was converted into a FE model via a density-controlled iterative clustering algorithm. Geometric validation across three independent PG confirmed high fidelity, with a mean absolute percentage error remaining below 0.7 % compared to on-site measurements. Finally, on-site loading test results were compared with the FE analysis results of the reconstructed FE model. The reconstructed FE model reliably reproduced the structural response (load–displacement) in a linear-elastic range with a normalized root mean squared error of 3.6 %. The proposed framework demonstrates that an AI-based approach can dramatically reduce manual post-processing of raw PCD while delivering geometric fidelity and reliable structural response prediction, establishing a foundation for digital-twin-enabled structural monitoring in horticulture applications.

title: Integrating tree-based machine learning with CROPWAT and ENSO for optimizing maize sowing dates in response to climate variability
abstract: Although machine learning (ML) offers advantages in agriculture, its practical adoption by farmers and extension services remains challenging, emphasizing the need for accessible tools that translate data-driven insights into actionable decisions. This study developed and evaluated a hybrid approach integrating tree-based ML models with the crop water requirement model (CROPWAT 8.0) and El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) data to predict optimal sowing dates for maize in rainfed systems in northern Thailand. Using daily climate and rainfall data from 1991 to 2022, CROPWAT 8.0 estimated maize yield reductions for different planting dates, and six tree-based ML models—Decision Tree, Bagging, Random Forest, AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost—were assessed to identify criteria for minimizing yield reduction and selecting sowing windows by ENSO phase. The Random Forest model achieved the lowest RMSE (4.312), lowest MAE (1.948), and highest R2, adjusted R2, and NSE (0.959). After hyperparameter tuning, rainfall during the crop’s mid-season growth stage was identified as crucial for minimizing yield loss. For ≤ 5 % yield reduction, rainfall during this stage should be at least 108.75 mm and the number of days exceeding 35 °C during the development stage should not exceed 12.5 for sandy loam soils; for soils with higher moisture availability, the rainfall requirement decreases to 81.85 mm. Using these criteria, suitable sowing date ranges were determined and categorized by ENSO code. This hybrid approach provides practical tools for extension services, enabling farmers to plan more than a month in advance and enhance farm management and resource organization.

title: Assessing airflow perturbations in naturally ventilated barns: A comparative study of image similarity metrics using machine learning
abstract: While natural ventilation is crucial for maintaining an ideally optimized air exchange rate (AER) and animal wellbeing, measuring the accurate airflow patterns is indeed challenging. This study investigates the behavior of a wide range of image similarity indices to detect differences between computational fluid dynamics (CFD) images of barn ventilation. To this end, a comprehensive dataset of barn airflow patterns was generated via CFD simulations under diverse conditions, then systematically distorted using swirl transformations to simulate controlled perturbations in airflow images with known ground truth. A broad set of image similarity indices was included to evaluate their sensitivity in the context of CFD images. We further fitted 14 state-of-the-art machine learning regressor models to predict the ground truth perturbation from the similarity indices and investigated which index has the highest feature importance. The strongest predictive performance (R 2 = 0.89) is achieved using a stacked model of top 6 regressors, namely LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, Gradient Boosting, Extra Trees and Random Forest, achieving R 2 of 0.879, 0.872, 0.870, 0.868, 0.860 and 0.840, respectively. We also show that DCT subband similarity (DSS), Mean Deviation Similarity Index (MDSI) and Deep Image Structure and Texture Similarity (DISTS) have the highest feature importance in predicting the swirl extent. Our findings further reveal that top 7 image similarity metrics can reasonably predict the perturbations in CFD simulation images. Lastly, we validated the trained models on a real-world low resolution dataset from a dairy barn, showing a high empirical power of 0.96 for our stacked model.

title: Comparative analysis of machine learning models to restore gaps in multivariate time series leaf wetness sensor data
abstract: IoT (Internet of Things) has been utilized in agriculture in many ways. When collecting data from IoT-based sensors, errors can occur due to various factors. Exploring the ways to predict missing data is needed to ensure the reliability, accuracy, and completeness of datasets for effective decision-making and analysis. This study focused on predicting missing leaf wetness (LW) sensor data using Machine Learning (ML) models, including Multiple Linear Regression (MLR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Gradient Boosting (GB), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Random Forest (RF), Deep Neural Network (DNN) and a hybrid stacked model. Cross-validation and correlation were performed for feature selection to select significant variables and interactions. Several environmental parameters, including temperature (T; ˚C), humidity (H; %), soil moisture (SM; %), rainfall (R; mm), rain event (RE) and their interactions (R x T, R x H, R x SM) were used to predict the LW through ML models. To overcome the limitations of traditional methods in handling the spatial and temporal complexity of environmental data, a hybrid stacked machine learning model, which integrates the strengths of RF (for robust imputation on interaction terms) and DNN (for capturing complex patterns) with dropout for L1 and L2 regularization techniques, was tested. The RF model performed better in training with a low Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.032, a high R2 of 0.967 and a Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) of 0.919 but failed to capture LW peaks. DNN and Fused Regularized DNN (FDNN) showed moderate MSE (AM: 0.46, 0.45; PM: 0.33,0.49) and satisfactory R2 (AM: 0.53, 0.54; PM: 0.66,0.50), KGE (AM: 0.54, 0.61; PM: 0.7, 0.56), but slightly underestimated LW in training dataset. FDNN performed well compared to RF and DNN in testing data sets, while the hybrid model outperformed other ML models. Through evaluation, it was observed that the hybrid ML model significantly outperformed individual models in both training and validation phases, achieving lower MSE (training = 0.002, validation = 0.113), higher R2 (training = 0.963, validation = 0.887), and improved KGE (training = 0.968, validation = 0.848). This ensemble modeling approach improves the accuracy of gap-filling in LW data and contributes to precise agricultural decision-making and management practices.

title: A thermal machine vision sensing system for quality assurance of quail eggs − freshness assessment and grading
abstract: Challenges in transporting one-day-old chicks long distances impact logistics, costs, and animal welfare in the quail industry. Transporting fertilized eggs for hatching as an alternative is viable since the quality of eggs can be assessed after transportation. In this study, we propose a new methodology that includes concept equipment for real-time grading of quail eggs according to their freshness level. By calculating the proportion of the segmented air cell size via a thermal imaging machine vision system calibrated with standard methods, the Haugh unit (HU), and the pH of albumen, our proposed method revealed that when the proportion of the thermographic air cell size was less than 3 % of the total egg area, there was significant evidence of high freshness quality; conversely, relative areas above 15 % indicated lack of optimal freshness conditions correlated with the HU (rs = −0.61) and the pH of albumen (rs = 0.57). The F1 scores of the thermal imaging machine vision system trained on the YOLOv8x-segmentation and Mask R-CNN deep learning object detection algorithms were 71.9 % and 77.8 %, respectively, on the sorting testing dataset. This study contributes to the field by proposing an innovative method for grading the freshness level of quail eggs in real time as a fast, noncontact and nondestructive alternative to supply the related industry and alleviate the animal welfare constraints associated with the transportation of avian living cargo.

title: CSLTSM-Net: A lightweight two-stream mixed neural network for chicken sound recognition
abstract: Monitoring the physiological state and behavior of poultry during breeding was of great significance for the welfare and intelligent development of poultry breeding. Poultry audio contained a large amount of physiological state and behavioral activity information. Driven by the development of artificial intelligence, computer auditory monitoring of poultry based on machine learning has attracted more attention by researchers. This paper introduced CSLTSM-Net, a lightweight two-stream mixed neural network designed for processing chicken sounds. The aim was to explore deep learning applications in poultry physiological state and behavior monitoring. First, teacher-model convolutional neural network (TMCNN) and teacher-model time-series neural network (TMTSNN) for chicken sound recognition with complex structure and many training parameters were constructed. After training, both models demonstrated strong abilities to recognize poultry feeding sounds (99.75 % accuracy in TMCNN and 95.25 % accuracy in TMTSNN). Second, student-model convolutional neural network (SMCNN) and student-model time-series neural network (SMTSNN) with simple structure and few training parameters were constructed, and both student models were trained using their corresponding teacher models. Finally, SMCNN and SMTSNN model were mixed together to form a lightweight two-stream neural network CSLTSM-Net. The experimental results showed that the performance of the student model trained by the teacher model was higher than that directly trained by the original training set. SMCNN with teacher training achieved 96.25 % accuracy, 94.69 % specificity, 97.93 % recall, 94.5 % precision and 96.18 % F1-score in the test set. SMTSNN with teacher training achieved 94.25 % accuracy, 95.79 % specificity, 91.55 % recall, 96.06 % precision and 93.75 % F1-score in the test set. SMCNN with original dataset training achieved 95.75 % accuracy, 94.2 % specificity, 97.4 % recall, 94 % precision and 95.67 % F1-score in the test set. SMTSNN with original training set achieved 91.75 % accuracy, 93.72 % specificity, 89.95 % recall, 94 % precision and 91.93 % F1-score in the test set. The proposed CSLTSM-Net achieved 97 % accuracy, 97 % specificity, 97 % recall, 97 % precision and 97 % F1-score in the test set. Compared with SMCNN and SMTSNN alone, the overall performance was better. The lightweight two-stream mixed neural network could be compressed to a large extent at the cost of a small amount of recognition performance, which is conducive to solving the problem that the direct use of deep neural networks with complex structure and numerous parameters was not conducive to embedding in the miniaturized low-cost equipment with small storage capacity and weak computing power in poultry farms.
