title: An end-to-end vision–language framework with LLM-based reasoning for decision-oriented tomato leaf disease management in greenhouse environments
abstract: Tomato foliar diseases pose a persistent threat to global food security, causing substantial yield losses and relying heavily on subjective, labor-intensive manual inspection. Although deep learning models achieve high accuracy under controlled laboratory conditions, their performance degrades markedly in real agricultural environments due to visual variability, background clutter, and inconsistent illumination. Moreover, existing automated systems fail to reflect how agricultural experts diagnose diseases by jointly considering global plant condition and localized symptom patterns. This paper presents an end-to-end framework for tomato leaf disease management that integrates vision–language disease recognition, lesion-aware representation learning, spatial aggregation, and large language model (LLM)–based reasoning for decision-oriented greenhouse deployment. At the core of the framework is the Dual-Level Contrastive Alignment Framework (DLCAF), which mirrors expert diagnostic reasoning by combining Global Disease-Description Alignment to accommodate linguistic and regional variability with Local Symptom Consistency Learning to focus on disease-specific lesions using expert annotations. Leaf-level predictions are aggregated into row- and greenhouse-level indicators to enable spatial analysis and temporal monitoring, which are subsequently interpreted by an LLM to generate actionable management recommendations. Extensive evaluation across laboratory, field, and greenhouse environments demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach. DLCAF achieves 58.1% accuracy on PlantVillage, 72.5% under natural field conditions on FieldPlant, and 36.2% on the Taiwan Tomato Leaf Disease Dataset, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art vision–language models including CLIP, LongCLIP, and AgriCLIP. Additional validation on a newly collected real-world greenhouse dataset from Abu Dhabi (502 images) further confirms robust performance under practical deployment conditions, achieving 74.3% accuracy. Ablation studies show that expert-guided lesion supervision and multi-description semantic alignment provide more informative learning signals than random sampling or single-caption training. These results demonstrate that integrating global semantic understanding, localized symptom analysis, and LLM-based reasoning enables robust, interpretable, and practically deployable disease detection and decision-support systems for precision agriculture. To support reproducibility and future research, the implementation code is publicly available at GitHub , along with our collected AD Dataset released at Figshare .

title: A drone- and deep-learning-based harvest planning model for determining the optimal harvesting sequence of broccoli fields
abstract: Because broccoli matures asynchronously within the same field, growers often rely on multiple manual inspections to determine the multistage harvest schedule. To reduce labor and improve harvest planning accuracy, this study proposes a broccoli harvest planning model using drone remote sensing and deep learning algorithms. First, a multi-harvest-stage broccoli head image dataset was constructed from fields at different harvesting rounds. Next, YOLO11n was employed to localize broccoli heads in drone images, and the resulting bounding boxes were used as prompts for the SAM2 segmentation model to extract accurate broccoli head masks. Based on the obtained mask contours, a distance-based discriminative factor was introduced, and a circle fitting strategy combining the least squares method and the minimum enclosing circle algorithm was applied to estimate broccoli head diameters. Finally, field maturity density, defined as the number of broccoli heads with estimated diameters greater than or equal to 12 cm per square meter, was calculated to determine whether a field met the harvesting threshold. For harvestable fields, the harvesting sequence was further optimized by evaluating the unit-time harvestable profit, enabling optimal harvest scheduling. Experimental results showed that the YOLO11n achieved an average detection accuracy of 0.979, with accuracy in all harvesting stages remaining no lower than 0.963, while demonstrating strong generalization capability across different planting patterns. The SAM2-based segmentation achieved an IoU of 0.846, and the average estimation error of broccoli head diameter was 4.35%, meeting practical application requirements. The case study further confirmed that the two-dimensional yield distribution maps and key indicators (such as maturity density and unit harvest profit) generated by the proposed model effectively supported broccoli harvest scheduling. The proposed broccoli harvest planning model may serve as a reference for developing harvest planning methods for other crops.

title: A shapley additive exPlanations-informed, threshold-based environmental variable optimization strategy for enhancing soil organic carbon content
abstract: Machine learning combined with the Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) algorithm can identify the local influencing factors of soil organic carbon (SOC) in farmlands, facilitating the enhancement of SOC content through agricultural measures and soil environment optimization strategies. However, current studies offer only qualitative recommendations, such as improving irrigation and agricultural patterns, without providing schemes for quantitatively optimizing environmental variables and estimating SOC improvement after optimization. To address this gap, this study proposes a novel SHAP-informed, threshold-based environmental variable optimization strategy for augmenting SOC content. Initially, machine learning models incorporating SHAP were used to investigate the global and local control factors of SOC. SHAP dependency plots were subsequently utilized to determine the baseline and optimal thresholds for each environmental variable. These thresholds served as the target values for optimization. Finally, the spatial maps of the optimized results for each covariate were presented, along with the estimates of the SOC improvement. Wangkui County, which is a typical agricultural area in China, was selected as the study site. Among the six evaluated predicted models, Light Gradient Boosting Machine exhibited superior performance, achieving a predicted fitted R2 of 0.983, root mean square error of 0.150, and Lin’s concordance correlation coefficient of 0.991. SHAP analysis identified total nitrogen, total phosphorus, microbial diversity, total potassium, and pH as the main influencing factors of SOC, but their relative importance varied considerably across different subregions. SHAP dependency plots illustrated the nonlinear relationship of SOC with these five factors, enabling the identification of baseline points (168 mg/kg, 43 mg/kg, 108.3, 202.5 mg/kg, and 7.2) and optimal thresholds (192 mg/kg, 46 mg/kg, 107.6, 194 mg/kg, and 6.6 mg/kg). When all independent variables reached their respective baseline or optimal thresholds, the average SOC across the study area was projected to increase by 4.5% or 17.4%, respectively. This threshold-based approach offers a novel framework for quantitatively optimizing environmental variables and estimating SOC improvement outcomes.

title: Enhanced leaf area index estimation in the Drip-Irrigated kiwifruit orchard based on optimized multi-source UAV-based indices
abstract: Accurate and timely Leaf Area Index (LAI) estimation is critical for monitoring kiwifruit canopy growth and supporting precision orchard management. UAV remote sensing is widely used for LAI estimation, but traditional methods relying on single sensors or fixed band combinations perform poorly in estimating LAI of perennial fruit trees across different growth stages. To solve this problem, this study developed optimized spectral index (VI_MS), spectral-texture index (VI_MT), and thermal infrared-texture index (VI_TT) by leveraging UAV-acquired multispectral, thermal infrared data, and their derived texture features. Then, six machine learning regression (MLR) models were constructed for LAI estimation, including Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest Regression (RFR), and four Boosting-based algorithms. Results showed that: (i) Optimized VI_MS, VI_MT, and VI_TT all strengthened the correlation with LAI across growth stages, and VI_MT performed best; (ii) Among all models, RFR had the highest prediction accuracy, followed by Boosting-based algorithms, while SVR performed worst; (iii) Combining VI_MT with RFR further improved kiwifruit LAI estimation accuracy. Notably, stage-specific LAI estimation was better than full growth cycle estimation, with mean R2 values of 0.916 ± 0.036 and 0.893 ± 0.083, and mean MAE values of 0.039 ± 0.008 and 0.043 ± 0.017, respectively. Overall, coupling optimized VI_MT with RFR or Boosting models improves kiwifruit LAI estimation under varying conditions. These results provide new insights for dynamic monitoring of orchard canopy growth in changing agro-environments.

title: A deep ensemble learning framework for precision image-level weed classification in paddy fields
abstract: Paddy cultivation plays a pivotal role in global agriculture, especially in regions where maximizing yield and sustainability is imperative. Among the most persistent challenges is the presence of weeds, which compete aggressively with crops for critical resources such as nutrients, water, sunlight, and space—ultimately suppressing plant growth and reducing productivity. This study presents a deep learning-based image-level weed classification framework tailored for paddy fields, designed to support precision agriculture by reducing the reliance on manual labor and chemical herbicides. A diverse dataset comprising approximately 950 field-acquired images was curated and annotated to reflect real-world conditions across different seasons and lighting variations. For image-level weed classification, a majority-voting ensemble of five pre-trained CNNs (InceptionV3, Xception, AlexNet, ResNet50, and VGG19) was created. This eliminated segmentation and allowed for quick on-device inference. Predictions were combined using an ensemble majority voting technique to improve classification reliability and overcome the shortcomings of individual models. Ties were settled by choosing the prediction from the model with the best validation accuracy. The proposed model achieved outstanding performance on the test dataset, with an accuracy of 99.70%, precision of 100%, recall of 98.87%, F1-score of 99.51% and AUC 99.42%. These results highlight the potential of deep ensemble learning in delivering accurate, consistent, and scalable solutions for intelligent weed management in precision rice farming.

title: Short-term time series predictions of greenhouse gas emission from dairy houses based on diverse machine learning models
abstract: Open-type dairy houses are significant sources of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, yet accurate quantification remains challenging due to complex indoor-outdoor environmental interactions and the prohibitive costs of continuous monitoring. Furthermore, existing predictive research predominantly relies on monolithic models that struggle to balance computational efficiency with the highly diverse volatility profiles of different trace gases. To address these deficiencies, this study proposes a novel, adaptive Hybrid Time Series Prediction (TSP) framework tailored for short-term GHG emission forecasting. The framework's architecture is grounded in a systematic multi-paradigm evaluation encompassing statistical (ARIMA), classical machine learning (SVM), and deep learning (BPNN, LSTM) models. Utilizing continuous monitoring data (CO 2 , N 2 O, NH 3 , and CH 4 ) from 10 sampling points across two naturally ventilated dairy houses, we conducted a comprehensive multi-dimensional assessment encompassing computational efficiency, predictive precision, spatial–temporal robustness, and cumulative error propagation mechanisms to optimize gas-specific model allocation. Results reveal a critical performance divergence contingent on gas characteristics: for high-concentration, stable gases (CO 2 and CH 4 ), the Support Vector Machine (SVM) exhibits an optimal balance of ultra-fast computational speed, minimal memory consumption (1–3 MiB), and robust accuracy. Conversely, for low-concentration, highly volatile trace gases (N 2 O and NH 3 ), the Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN) demonstrates superior non-linear mapping capabilities to filter stochastic noise. By adaptively integrating SVM and BPNN, the framework successfully minimizes asynchronous estimation errors. Additionally, a 5–10 min sampling interval was identified as the optimal operational balance. This hybrid approach offers a cost-effective, highly accurate solution for real-time GHG monitoring, demonstrating significant potential for deployment on resource-constrained edge devices in the global precision livestock sector.

title: A machine learning approach with SHAP interpretation for predicting fruit inertial force in vibration harvesting of Camellia oleifera
abstract: Vibration harvesting is an effective approach for the mechanized harvesting of Camellia oleifera fruit. Accurate prediction of fruit inertial force is crucial for enhancing harvesting efficiency, yet it remains challenging due to the complex interactions between excitation parameters and tree structural characteristics. In this study, a pendulum dynamics model of the fruit-branch system was established, and a multidimensional dataset was collected through field tests. Six machine learning models were subsequently trained and evaluated using this dataset. Results showed that the Random Forest (RF) model provided the best predictive performance, with mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and coefficient of determination (R2) values of 1.05, 1.73, and 0.79, respectively. Subsequently, the SHAP method was employed to interpret the RF model and quantify feature importance. The analysis revealed that excitation parameters were the primary determinants of fruit inertial force, contributing 73.6%, compared with 26.4% from tree structural parameters. Among all features, excitation frequency exhibited the greatest influence, contributing 42.06%. Feature selection further improved the predictive performance of the RF model. On the test set, the MAE, RMSE, and R2 values were 1.01, 1.64, and 0.82, respectively. Field validation tests confirmed a low error rate of 6.22% between the model predictions and the measured inertial forces. These findings provide a theoretical basis for precision vibration harvesting of Camellia oleifera and offer a useful reference for the harvesting of other forest fruits.

title: Rigid-flexible coupling errors calibration based on machine learning for robotic harvesting arm in orchard
abstract: Apple harvesting robots provide a solution for the mechanized picking of fresh fruits, in which the dedicated apple picking robotic arms are the core components. However, various errors reduce the positioning accuracy and dynamic performance of the apple picking robotic arm, such as system errors from manufacturing tolerances and assembly errors, compliance errors caused by self-weight and load structures, and nonstructural errors caused by gear backlash. This paper introduces a novel method to improve the positioning accuracy of long-stroke picking robotic arm. A rigid-flexible coupling pose error model was established that integrates system error, self-weight and load compliance errors. Meanwhile, redundant parameters were eliminated to optimize the model through parameter error classification and analysis of the parameter error ratio. Moreover, a hybrid calibration method was proposed, combining iterative least squares method for parameter identification with a residual network for nonstructural error estimation. The identified errors were then compensated for using the error compensation method based on inverse kinematics. Simulation experiments demonstrated that the identification accuracy of the removing redundant parameters model was 93.478%. Compared with other traditional methods, the proposed method achieved the highest error estimation accuracy and the minimal calibration error. Physical experiment showed that the positioning error of the picking robotic arm decreased after calibration. The average position error and root mean square error of the picking robotic arm compensated by the proposed method were 0.278 and 0.202 mm, respectively, and the average orientation error and root mean square error were 0.230° and 0.178°, respectively. Compared to before calibration, the average position error and root mean square error decreased by 95.221% and 95.182%, respectively, and the average orientation error and root mean square error decreased by 94.080% and 93.541%, respectively. This work provides a methodological reference for error calibration in fruit picking robotic arms.

title: Plant 3D-2D-ResNet-SE: Monitoring the changes of leaf water content and chlorophyll in Betula luminifera seedlings during drought stress
abstract: Betula luminifera, a tree species of notable ecological and economic value, has leaf water content (LWC) and leaf chlorophyll content (LCC) as vital phenotypic traits, crucial for plant health assessment and forestry productivity. This study proposed a hybrid convolutional neural network (CNN)-based model utilizing hyperspectral images as inputs to directly predict the LWC and LCC of Betula luminifera leaves. The model accepts hyperspectral images as input without the tedious steps of manually selecting regions of interest (ROI) and converting hyperspectral data into average spectra in traditional methods, and directly predicts the LWC and LCC of Betula luminifera leaves. The hybrid convolutional neural network model combines 3D convolution kernels to capture spectral information and 2D convolution kernels to extract spatial features, effectively improving the accuracy of prediction. To refine feature selection further, this study uniquely incorporated Competitive Adaptive Reweighted Sampling (CARS) and the Successive Projection Algorithm (SPA) band-selection methods. Shapley values were used to assess the relevance of each wavelength, identifying those most critical to prediction. Five-fold cross-validation was incorporated into the results to reduce the randomness of data splitting. Results show that the 3D-2D-ResNet-SE model demonstrates outstanding performance in predicting LWC and LCC, with R2 reaching 0.86 and 0.85, respectively, marking the first instance of regression predictions from direct hyperspectral image inputs. The study confirms the efficacy of SPA and CARS in selecting key hyperspectral image bands and introduces a novel hybrid deep learning framework for accurate physiological parameter detection in Betula luminifera leaves. This method provides substantive advancements for plant health monitoring and seedling management, with significant potential to support the development of precision agriculture.

title: Cross-attention driven RGBD fusion in lightweight CNN–Transformer for real-time stress classification of seedlings during robotic transplanting
abstract: Timely selection of high-quality seedlings during robotic transplanting is crucial for ensuring optimal crop growth and productivity. However, accurate real-time seedling grading is technically challenging due to subtle visual differences among stress levels and the limited computational capacity of edge devices. To address this, we propose a lightweight RGBD (RGB and depth) multimodal framework for six-level stress classification of bell pepper seedlings. Our approach integrates a dual-stream CNN–Transformer architecture in which hierarchical cross-attention modules fuse color-texture cues from the RGB stream with depth-derived geometric cues at both shallow and deep feature layers. The compact tokenizer rapidly extracts multi-scale fused features, which allow transformer encoders to capture long-range dependencies, and an attention-pooling head produces class logits. To validate our algorithm, a dedicated dataset of 1537 paired RGBD images was collected with an oblique-view sensor during the pick-and-place cycle. Deployed on an edge-device, the network achieves an overall accuracy of 95.8 % and maintains 5.2 frames per second when integrated into the parallel transplant-control pipeline. Ablation studies reveal that effective fusion of RGBD channel can improve accuracy by 4.9 % over RGB-only baseline model, which supports the effectiveness of the modality-aware design. This study integrates RGBD imaging with an edge-ready hybrid network to provide a practical tool for automated seedling transplanting and an effective solution for multimodal perception in precision agriculture.

title: Accurate visual diagnosis of cadmium distribution in rice leaves based on data rolling bidirectional residual network and 1D-to-2D spectra of laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy
abstract: The rapid and accurate detection of cadmium (Cd) in rice leaves is crucial for the prevention and control of heavy metal pollution. Compared to traditional chemical methods, laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) serves as a fast, chemical-free method for the analysis of hazardous metals. However, the detection capabilities of LIBS are influenced by matrix effects, which have long been a core bottleneck limiting the quantitative accuracy of LIBS. In this study, a data rolling method was introduced, which enhanced the local receptive field of the convolutional kernel and provides global interaction of spectral information through data rolling changes. By combining a ResNet18-based bidirectional convolutional network, this approach significantly improved the detection accuracy of Cd in rice leaves and effectively mitigates matrix effects in spectral analysis. The results indicate that data rolling bidirectional residual network (DR-BiResNet) outperforms traditional machine learning models, achieving correlation coefficient (R) of 0.9486, root mean square error (RMSE) of 6.4771 mg/kg and relative prediction deviation (RPD) of 3.16 on the prediction set. DR-BiResNet successfully captured the Cd I 228.80 nm and Cd II 214.44 nm signals and effectively learned the global interactions as observed by Grad-CAM++. Additionally, visual diagnostics were conducted on the external samples, allowing for a direct observation of the distribution of Cd in rice leaves, with R of 0.9618. The combination of DR-BiResNet and LIBS provides an accurate and efficient analytical method for the detection of Cd in rice leaves, which has great potential for environmental protection.

title: Quantifying the adaptability of China’s dominant maize varieties to future climate change: A combined approach of crop modeling and explainable machine learning
abstract: China’s dominant maize varieties, developed through breeding improvements, achieve high yields under current climatic conditions but face significant uncertainties in adapting to future climate change, posing risks to food security. This study assessed the impacts of future climate change on these varieties using a calibrated APSIM-Maize model under SSP126 (low-emission) and SSP585 (high-emission) scenarios. To enhance interpretability, we integrated crop modeling with explainable machine learning, specifically a Random Forest (RF) surrogate model combined with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), to identify key climatic drivers of yield variation. Results indicated that under current conditions, varieties like MY73, ZD958, and JK968 exhibit high yields and large cultivation areas. However, future climatic scenarios projected shortened growth periods and widespread yield declines, with national maize yield expected to decrease by 5.4 % under SSP126 and 10.0 % under SSP585. Northeast China would experience the most severe yield reductions, with declines of 10.7 % by the 2050s and up to 19.0 % by the 2080s under SSP585. Mechanism analysis revealed that temperature-related factors negatively influenced maize yield under SSP126, while solar radiation and cold days had positive effects under SSP585, with other variables exerting significant negative impacts. These findings demonstrate the vulnerability of current maize varieties to future climate change and emphasize the necessity for breeding programs to develop stress-tolerant varieties, particularly with enhanced resistance to extreme temperatures. Additionally, by integrating crop modeling and explainable machine learning methods, this research provides a feasible approach for understanding how climate change affects crop production and guiding adaptation strategies to ensure food security.

title: A shuffle-normalized Pix2Pix GAN framework with Elastic ArcFace and YOLO for occlusion-free cattle identification
abstract: In recent years, biometric-based cattle identification, particularly using muzzle patterns, has emerged as a reliable and non-invasive solution. However, real-world muzzle images often suffer from occlusions caused by grass, dirt, and environmental noise, which adversely affect identification performance. Generative Adversarial Networks, especially Pix2Pix GAN, offer a promising approach for translating noisy images into clean, realistic representations. Nevertheless, GAN training is challenging due to instability and mode collapse. Traditional normalization techniques like Batch Normalization provide limited benefits, as they fail to fully exploit the architectural characteristics of GANs. To address these issues, this work proposes a novel normalization technique called Shuffle Normalization, integrated into the Pix2Pix GAN framework for generating clean muzzle images from noisy inputs. Shuffle Normalization improves training stability and image quality by preserving semantic information and mitigating gradient saturation. For cattle identification, an Elastic Face Margin Loss-based classifier is employed, trained on real muzzle images and evaluated using GAN-generated outputs. The proposed method achieves a Frechet Inception Distance score of 13.92, indicating high visual fidelity of the generated images, and an identification accuracy of 98.7%, demonstrating the effectiveness of the overall framework. This work advances generative modeling in animal biometrics and provides a robust solution for real-world cattle identification, while also establishing a practical generative AI–based paradigm for occlusion-robust data augmentation and biometric recognition in precision livestock farming.

title: Two-stage deep learning model for non-destructive leaf counting in tomato crops
abstract: Research is limited in longitudinal leaf counting across different growth phases of tomatoes, particularly for agrivoltaics where variations in light and surrounding environmental conditions can influence plant structure and growth. Practical greenhouse monitoring requires a lightweight method for consistent, automated leaf counting that can adapt to noisy backgrounds, overlapping leaves, and variations in canopy structure. This study presents the first tomato-focused leaf counting pipeline developed and validated using weekly image data collected under greenhouse and agrivoltaic greenhouse conditions. The dataset includes 36 tomato crops over five weeks, with ground truth counts and pseudo-labeled counts where manual counting was infeasible. The pipeline is based on a two-stage deep learning approach: 1) convolutional neural network (CNN) regression model based on MobileNetV2 is trained directly to predict the leaf counts from top-view crop images and 2) U-Net segmentation model based on a subset of manually annotated images enhances predictions, especially in cases of occluded and overlapped leaves. Across the test datasets, the CNN regression model consistently produced good predictions within a ±3 margin for actual leaf manual counts. The model’s performance was evaluated using the coefficient of determination (R2) which ranges between 0.7 and 0.9, which is comparable or exceeds the performance reported in recent leaf-counting studies. The CNN regression stage efficiently learned structural and textural features from limited data, while the U-Net refinement enhanced spatial understanding which provides segmentation-based visual validation. This combination ensured both computational efficiency and model transparency which is important for operational use in greenhouse monitoring and edge-AI deployment.

title: Data-driven greenhouse climate regulation in lettuce cultivation using BiLSTM and GRU predictive control
abstract: Efficient greenhouse management is essential for sustainable food production, but the high energy demand for climate regulation poses significant economic and environmental challenges. While traditional process-based greenhouse models exist, they are often too complex or imprecise for reliable control. To address this, our study introduces a novel data-driven predictive control framework using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) neural networks within a Model Predictive Control (MPC) architecture. Training data were generated from a validated dynamic model simulating lettuce cultivation under various environmental conditions. The LSTM and GRU networks were trained to predict future greenhouse states — including temperature, humidity, CO 2 concentration, and crop dry matter — with robustness confirmed via 10-fold cross-validation. These networks were embedded into an online MPC controller to optimize heating, ventilation, and CO 2 injection, aiming to minimize energy consumption and maximize crop yield while respecting biological constraints. Results showed that both the LSTM- and GRU-based controllers significantly outperformed a conventional MPC baseline. For example, humidity violations dropped from 54.77% (MPC) to 15.45% (GRU) and 17.71% (LSTM), while day–night temperature deviations were kept below 2 ∘ C . The GRU controller further achieved up to 40% lower computation time than its LSTM counterpart, confirming its real-time feasibility. Overall, the proposed GRU-driven predictive control approach offers a robust and computationally efficient solution for intelligent greenhouse climate automation under practical operational constraints. • GRU and LSTM models were applied for greenhouse climate predictive control. • GRU reduced climate violations by 5% compared to LSTM while matching yield. • GRU required 40% less computation time than LSTM in real-time scenarios. • Both models maintained high crop yield and economic performance. • GRU offers a practical solution for energy-efficient greenhouse control.

title: Horticultural temporal fruit monitoring via 3D instance segmentation and re-identification using colored point clouds
abstract: Accurate and consistent fruit monitoring over time is a key step towards automated agricultural production systems. However, this task is inherently difficult due to variations in fruit size, shape, occlusion, orientation, and the dynamic nature of orchards where fruits may appear or disappear between observations. In this article, we propose a novel method for fruit instance segmentation and re-identification on 3D terrestrial point clouds collected over time. Our approach directly operates on dense colored point clouds, capturing fine-grained 3D spatial detail. We segment individual fruits using a learning-based instance segmentation method applied directly to the point cloud. For each segmented fruit, we extract a compact and discriminative descriptor using a 3D sparse convolutional neural network. To track fruits across different times, we introduce an attention-based matching network that associates fruits with their counterparts from previous sessions. Matching is performed using a probabilistic assignment scheme, selecting the most likely associations across time. We evaluate our approach on real-world datasets of strawberries and apples, demonstrating that it outperforms existing methods in both instance segmentation and temporal re-identification, enabling robust and precise fruit monitoring across complex and dynamic orchard environments. • We propose a new performant approach to autonomous fruit tracking in real greenhouses. • It segments fruits using learning-based instance segmentation and RGB 3D point clouds. • Segmented fruits are encoded by a 3D CNN and matched via attentive data association. • Experiments on real strawberry and apple datasets show our method outperforms others. • Our approach enables precise temporal fruit monitoring in real and complex scenarios.

title: An end-to-end video-based action recognition pipeline for precision monitoring and success scoring of broiler breeder mating behavior
abstract: Efficient and accurate detection, tracking, and monitoring of successful mating behavior in broiler breeders are critical for assessing welfare, reproductive performance, and overall productivity in commercial farms. Computer vision and machine learning offer practical means for acquiring detailed insights into mating behaviors. Regardless, these technologies have rarely been applied to monitor mating events in their full dynamic context. In this study, we proposed an end-to-end video-based pipeline for recognizing and monitoring mating behavior in broiler breeders using a behavior recognition approach. The pipeline identified a four-step mating pattern through four main components: detection, tracking, action recognition, and scoring. The tracking algorithm was refined to manage movement challenges better, resulting in a 2% performance gain, while a Re-Identification module enhanced tracking during mating events by 70%. In addition, we introduced four datasets collected and annotated from a commercial broiler breeder farm, along with a scoring step designed to estimate the success probability of each mating event. The proposed pipeline achieved an overall accuracy of about 90% across multiple metrics. Despite the complexity of action-based mating behaviors, the results demonstrate strong potential for reliable automation in commercial use.

title: Integrating plant physiology with deep learning for fresh weight prediction across lettuce growth cycles
abstract: Crops exhibit substantial phenotypic variation throughout their growth cycles, making accurate fresh weight estimation challenging, particularly during early seedling stages when morphological features are limited. This study proposes a unified framework that integrates plant physiological knowledge with deep learning to improve fresh weight prediction across the entire growth cycle. The framework utilizes RGB-D canopy images and incorporates a biologically constrained loss function derived from allometric scaling relationships between canopy area and biomass. To enhance prediction robustness across different growth stages, three adaptive strategies are introduced, including regional weight indexing, error sensitivity adjustment, and micro-sample weight amplification. These mechanisms improve the model’s ability to handle difficult samples at early growth stages while maintaining accurate predictions during later developmental phases. Experiments conducted over complete growth cycles demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving an acceptable prediction rate of 92.96% within a ± 10% error range. The proposed framework improves fresh weight prediction accuracy across growth stages while particularly enhancing performance during early seedling stages, providing a reliable solution for crop phenotyping, automated plant factories, and precision agriculture applications.

title: A novel benchmark for rice lodging assessment with X-band UAV-PolSAR and 3D-RLMamba
abstract: Typhoon-induced lodging disaster seriously affects the rice quality and yield. Timely acquisition of lodging information plays a pivotal role in the post-disaster management and agricultural insurance claims. Spaceborne optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) remote sensing is constrained by limited spatiotemporal resolution, which prevents the precise depiction of regional rice lodging heterogeneity. UAV optical remote sensing excels at characterizing the physiological changes of lodged rice rather than capturing direct structural transformations. However, its efficacy remains constrained by a high sensitivity to meteorological and lighting conditions. To circumvent these limitations, this work proposes a novel framework that integrates cutting-edge UAV-based Polarimetric SAR (UAV-PolSAR) with a state-of-the-art (SOTA) 3D Rice Lodging Mamba (3D-RLMamba) architecture for rice lodging assessment. This comprehensive framework establishes a benchmark for the intelligent inversion of key lodging parameters by detailing every stage from data acquisition and feature construction to algorithm development and parameter calculation. Initially, a full-polarization X-band UAV-PolSAR was deployed to acquire structure-sensitive radar imagery of rice fields in the aftermath of a super typhoon. A stacked feature cube was subsequently constructed, encompassing polarimetric backscatter coefficients, radar vegetation indices, and Pauli polarimetric decomposition features. To effectively capture local details and global dependencies embedded in complex spatial-polarimetric SAR features, 3D-RLMamba was designed as a novel patch-wise image classification algorithm. This new architecture facilitates cross-dimensional interaction and fusion of lodging-related information by combining the Mamba model with a multi-group strategy. A comprehensive performance comparison was conducted between 3D-RLMamba and numerous mainstream SOTA baselines, including classification models based on machine learning, CNN, Transformer, and Mamba architectures. The results indicate that 3D-RLMamba achieves the best performance, reaching an Overall Accuracy (OA) of 93.78%. Specifically, the classification accuracy for lodged rice reaches 87.87% even within natural backgrounds containing complex landcovers. These impressive classification performances lay a solid foundation for accurately mapping the spatial distribution of lodged regions and extracting their specific area and proportion. Overall, this study underscores the unique capability of advanced UAV-PolSAR in capturing the morphological features of lodged rice. Furthermore, it affirms the advantages of the 3D-RLMamba for global–local context modeling and spatial-polarimetric feature interaction. Consequently, the integration of SOTA deep learning and UAV-PolSAR technologies within this benchmark establishes a transformative paradigm for agricultural remote sensing.

title: Improving wheat yield prediction in breeding under climate change via a new method of correcting and reconstructing meteorological data and weighing multiple crop model outputs
abstract: Climate change increasingly affects wheat growth, yield, and quality, making accurate yield prediction essential for breeding climate-resilient crops. This study proposes a new prediction method to assess the impact of climate change on the yield of various wheat germplasms, experimentally carried out in Zhejiang Province, China. The method integrates a multivariable correction super-resolution diffusion model (MCSDM) and a multiple crop model weight distribution network (MCMWDN). First, MCSDM corrects and reconstructs daily historical and future meteorological data from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 multiple global climate models (GCMs). Then, crop models (WOFOST, AquaCrop, and DSSAT) were driven using corrected and reconstructed historical meteorological data to complete model calibration and validation. Finally, corrected and reconstructed future meteorological data were used to drive the calibrated and validated crop models, and the outputs of multiple crop models were integrated using MCMWDN to obtain future yield predictions for different wheat breeding germplasms under climate change. The results showed that the R2 of all seven GCM variables increased and the RMSE decreased under different future scenarios. MCMWDN integrated the outputs of multiple crop models, resulting in more accurate yield predictions (R2 = 0.823, RMSE = 443.6 kg/ha), which is superior to single crop models. Results show significant variation in the responses of different wheat germplasms to future climate scenarios. Norin 61 maintains relatively high yields, while Festin and Jagger/W94-244–132 perform poorly. Lumai 5 and Zhoumai 31 remain relatively stable overall. Yields tend to increase slightly under SSP1-2.6, stay stable under SSP2-4.5, and decline under SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5, especially by 2071–2100. This study provides a relatively robust and generalizable method for predicting crop yields, supporting climate-resilient breeding and management decisions for sustainable agriculture in the face of climate change.

title: Concept and rule guided neural network for early crop leaf nutrient deficiency diagnosis
abstract: Crop nutrition deficiency poses a major challenge to achieving optimal yield, particularly in smallholder farming systems where timely expert diagnosis is limited. Early detection is crucial to minimize losses and reduce unnecessary fertilizer or pesticide usage. While deep learning offers potential for automated visual diagnosis, most existing approaches operate as black boxes and lack interpretability, explainability, or actionable recommendations. In this work, we present a neurosymbolic framework for early nutrient deficiency detection in ash gourd leaves using the EarlyNSD dataset. Our approach integrates a ResNet-50 backbone with a dual-head design: a classification head for deficiency prediction and a concept-prediction head that quantifies physiologically meaningful visual patterns such as yellowing, edge discoloration, spots, and vein greenness. These concept scores are combined with predefined domain rules to guide the learning of the neural component and to generate transparent, human-aligned explanations for each diagnosis. Building on the model outputs, we incorporate a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)-based pipeline along with an agricultural knowledge base to generate targeted recommendations. This approach overcomes key shortcomings of pure neural models by incorporating domain knowledge in the form of differentiable fuzzy logic rules. The study demonstrates that the proposed framework improves both classification performance and interpretability compared to standard ResNet baselines. Grad-CAM analysis demonstrates that concept-guided attention aligns with symptom-specific regions, such as yellowed areas for Nitrogen deficiency or marginal discoloration for Potassium deficiency, providing visual validation of the reasoning process. Since EarlyNSD is limited in scale and visual diversity, the results are not directly comparable to large open-field datasets. Overall, our results establish a proof of concept for integrating neural detection with symbolic reasoning, enabling interpretable, actionable, and domain-informed nutrient management for practical applications.

title: Design and development of a low-cost industrial prototype of spot-specific spraying system for potato weed detection using deep learning
abstract: Conventional sprayers uniformly distribute agrochemicals on crops, even though weed distribution is typically patchy, leading to increased costs and environmental pollution. Spot-specific AI-driven sprayer offers a solution to optimize this challenge. The primary objective of this research is to develop a low-cost, smart, and fast-response industrial prototype of the spot-specific spraying system integrated with deep learning-based object detection techniques. The study aims to distinguish various weed species to enable the precise application of herbicides on potato crops. To ensure a real-world representation, a diverse dataset was collected from the real potato fields, covering various climatic conditions, irrigation methods, and timestamps. This data was utilized for training YOLOv8, YOLOv9, and YOLOv12 detection models, resulting in detection accuracies of 90%, 92%, and 93% respectively. The results indicate that the YOLOv12 model obtained higher detection accuracy while localizing the weed instances accurately. Additionally, the average processing speed of 35 frames per second and 320 ms lag time between image acquisition and activation demonstrate the efficacy of the adopted YOLOv12 model. Following the result analysis, the high detection model (YOLOv12) is integrated with the spot-specific sprayer system for real-time detection of weeds in potato fields. The system accurately identified the weeds in the potato field and triggered the nozzles accordingly. The microcontroller is responsible for controlling this system to ensure the precise application of weedicide. The results indicate that the developed spot-specific sprayer system not only achieves a nearly 40% reduction in herbicide usage, leading to cost savings, but also reduces the environmental impact.

title: Pose estimation-guided CNN for tea bud detection and plucking point identification
abstract: Accurate detection of tea buds and precise identification of plucking points are the essential prerequisites for intelligent tea-plucking robots. However, this task is challenging as the color of the targets exhibit color similarity with the background, and their shape, size, and morphology do not always coincide. Additionally, the tea buds are densely distributed and might undergo mutual occlusion within a visual horizon. In this paper, we draw inspiration from the analogy between plucking points and human keypoints and propose a framework, named PENet, that reformulates the plucking point localization task as a pose estimation problem. PENet splits the localization of the plucking points into two stages: tea bud detection and plucking point identification. In the first stage, we enhance a DINO-based detector by integrating spectrum attention module and multi-scale feature fusion, enhancing sensitivity to subtle color/texture contrasts. In the second stage, a modified High-Resolution Network with spatial coordinate encoding and bottlenecks transformer is used to accurately localize plucking points, even under occlusion or clustering. Owing to these two sequential stages, PENet can leverage the strengths of each stage to enhance flexibility on tea bud detection and plucking point identification in natural tea plantation environment. Through extensive experiments, PENet achieves competitive performance, with a mAP of 77.9% for tea bud detection and 86.2% for plucking point identification, outperforming several recent approaches under the same evaluation setting. These results demonstrate that PENet is a robust framework for intelligent tea harvesting—achieving high detection accuracy and plucking precision while reducing labor dependency and boosting operational efficiency in large-scale plantations.

title: UAV-mounted electrochemical soil probing system for geospatial phosphorus mapping
abstract: • UAV-mounted system enables autonomous in situ soil phosphorus sensing. • Electrochemical probing overcomes limitations of imaging-based nutrient estimation. • Spatially informed machine learning converts sparse samples into coherent P maps. • Field validation across Canada and Tanzania achieved F1-scores up to 0.91. • Framework supports scalable, data-driven fertilizer management systems. Accurate spatial mapping of soil phosphorus remains challenging due to the high cost and limited spatial density of laboratory soil analyses and the poor performance of remote-sensing approaches for phosphorus estimation. This study presents a UAV-mounted soil sensing system that integrates autonomous mechanical probing with in-situ electrochemical measurement and spatial machine learning to enable high-resolution phosphorus mapping under field conditions. The platform combines a lightweight drone-deployable probing mechanism, an ion-selective electrochemical probe, onboard control electronics, and wireless telemetry to collect GPS-referenced soil nutrient measurements during automated flight operations. Field experiments were conducted at two contrasting agricultural sites: a vineyard in British Columbia, Canada, and an intensively managed flower farm in Arusha, Tanzania. Three complementary datasets were generated to evaluate spatial nutrient structure at both location and within-location scales. Spatial feature engineering incorporated positional geometry and neighborhood statistics, and spatial autocorrelation was assessed using Moran’s I and variogram analysis. Random Forest classifiers were trained using spatially grouped cross-validation to prevent performance inflation due to spatial dependence. Across study sites, the proposed approach achieved weighted F1-scores ranging from 0.82 to 0.91, representing improvements of 25–40% over baseline classifiers. The resulting phosphorus maps were spatially coherent and agronomically plausible, successfully identifying low-phosphorus zones in the Canadian vineyard despite limited nutrient variability, and distinct low- and high-phosphorus regions in the Tanzanian field where fertility gradients were stronger. Analysis of feature importance highlighted the dominant role of local spatial contrast and neighborhood information, underscoring the importance of explicitly modeling spatial context when using in situ electrochemical sensors. The results demonstrate that coupling UAV-based automated soil probing with spatially informed machine learning provides an effective pathway for transforming sparse physical measurements into continuous phosphorus distribution maps. This integrated sensing-to-mapping framework offers a scalable foundation for site-specific nutrient management and can be extended to additional soil properties and precision agriculture applications.

title: Cropland soil salinity retrieval using a spectral-spatial cross-attention deep learning framework with environmental interpretability
abstract: Cropland soil salinization severely constrains crop growth and leads to substantial yield reductions, thereby constituting a critical ecological threat to national food security. Owing to its extensive spatial coverage and high temporal efficiency, remote sensing has become an indispensable tool for large-scale soil salinity monitoring. However, conventional remote sensing-based retrieval approaches are challenged by weak salinity-related spectral signals, complex coupling between soil salinity and environmental factors, and limited model generalization capability, which collectively hinder accurate characterization of cropland salinity patterns. To address these limitations, this study develops a multimodal deep learning framework, termed Spectral and Spatial Soil Net (SS-SoilNet), to retrieve soil salinity in coastal croplands of the Yellow River Delta. To enhance retrieval accuracy and capture the nonlinear interactions between soil salinity and the geo-environment, the model integrates multi-source inputs, including remote sensing observations, topographic features, and crop growth parameters. Specifically, SS-SoilNet incorporates a spectral sequence convolution module to extract dynamic spectral characteristics, a spatial attention module to account for surface heterogeneity and environmental features, and a multi-head cross-attention mechanism in which spatial features serve as queries to selectively guide spectral and vegetation index representations. Experimental results demonstrate that: (1) Compared with conventional machine-learning models such as Random Forest and Support Vector Regression, SS-SoilNet exhibits improved and more stable predictive performance. On the validation dataset, SS-SoilNet achieves an RMSE of approximately 3.6 g kg −1 , an MAE of about 1.7 g kg −1 , and an R 2 of around 0.68. (2) The integration of multimodal deep learning with multi-source covariates, including hydrological conditions, crop vigor indicators, and topographic factors enhances retrieval robustness relative to spectral-only approaches. (3) Interpretability analysis of covariate contributions reveals pronounced coupling effects among soil salinity, crop growth, and terrain. Overall, SS-SoilNet not only improves the accuracy and interpretability of soil salinity retrieval in coastal croplands but also provides quantitative evidence for understanding the environmental processes underlying soil salinization.

title: Multi-objective hierarchical reinforcement learning for efficient and safe robotic manure cleaning in dairy barns
abstract: Autonomous mobile robots for manure removal in dairy barns must resolve conflicting objectives of cleaning efficiency, environmental impact, and animal welfare under highly cluttered and dynamic barn conditions. We introduce a Multi-Objective Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (MO-HRL) framework that integrates a Global Evolutionary Scheduler (GES) for long-horizon cleaning task planning with an Adaptive RL-based Executor (ARE) for real-time, risk-aware robot motion control. The GES solves a multi-objective optimization problem over the robot’s travel distance, ammonia emissions, and cleaning yield via an evolutionary algorithm. The ARE employs a constrained Markov decision process enriched with historical high-loss weighting, adaptive action masking, and a final execution shield to guarantee smooth, non-injurious contacts with cows. In Webots simulations across three barn layouts (with ten, twenty, and thirty free-roaming cows, respectively), MO-HRL maintains high task completion ( ≥ 93 . 03 % ) with low comfort-distance violations ( ≤ 6 . 67 % ), achieves a peak throughput of 1 . 98 kg/min , and shortens completion time by up to 6× versus PPO (up to 8× in Small). Ammonia emission reduction reaches up to 0.144 kg m − 3 . These results indicate that hierarchical, risk-aware RL can translate long-horizon scheduling and real-time safety constraints into tangible gains for rapid, safe, and sustainable barn sanitation.

title: GDYEY: Grape detection and yield estimation framework based on YOLO architecture
abstract: Accurate yield estimation is crucial for optimizing agricultural management and market forecasting. However, the variable scale and occlusion of grapes cause their detection to have a negative impact, thereby reducing the precision of yield estimation. This study proposes a Grape Detection and Yield Estimation framework based on the YOLO architecture (GDYEY) by integrating a grape detection network into a depth estimation network. Specifically, a complex and diverse grape detection dataset was first constructed to facilitate verifying estimation performance and offer convenience to this research field. Moreover, a novel target detection mechanism based on Knowledge Distillation and Enhanced Convolutional Neural Networks (KD-ECNN) is designed by employing knowledge distillation to effectively transfer semantic information from the teacher to the student network. Generalization capability is enhanced through this approach. Additionally, a new yield estimation strategy based on Depth Estimation was presented by embedding the LapDepth Network to improve the accuracy of yield estimation. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a mAP of 81.6% in grape detection, surpassing 15 mainstream detection models. Additionally, grape yield estimation shows a significant improvement, with accuracy gains of approximately 25% and 10% over the counting-only and area-based estimation methods, respectively.

title: DynROI-Hybrid: Dynamic modeling of functional regions for feeding and drinking behavior detection in laying hens
abstract: The automatic identification of feeding and drinking behaviors in commercial laying hen houses remains challenging due to of high stocking densities, frequent occlusions, and the pendular movement of feeding and drinking equipment, which compromise approaches that rely solely on fixed regions or bounding boxes. This study proposes the DynROI-Hybrid framework, which integrates object detection with YOLOv11, selective segmentation with Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2), and dynamic modeling of functional interaction regions associated with feeders and drinkers. The methodology combines spatial criteria (overlap, proximity, and intersection) with temporal stabilization via hysteresis, enabling distinction between true interaction events and mere spatial proximity. Results demonstrate robust performance, achieving 94% overall accuracy and a Cohen’s Kappa coefficient of 0.91 compared to gold-standard validation. The proposed approach reduces false positives caused by equipment movement and structural resource geometry while maintaining computational feasibility for Edge AI applications. The method contributes to automated monitoring of feeding-related behaviors in commercial poultry production systems, with potential applications in welfare assessment and decision support within Precision Livestock Farming.

title: Automated detection system based on type-3 fuzzy logic for evaluating fly infestation level in cattle
abstract: Horn fly (Haematobia irritans) infestation represents a persistent challenge in cattle production, affecting animal welfare, productivity, and economic sustainability. Although recent advances in computer vision have enabled automated fly detection and counting, translating these outputs into reliable infestation severity assessments remains an open problem, particularly under uncertainty and subjective interpretation. This study proposes an integrated framework for automated assessment of horn fly infestation that combines deep learning-based vision models with a Type-3 Fuzzy Logic System (T3FLS) to provide an uncertainty-aware, interpretable evaluation. The proposed system employs You Only Look Once version 11 (YOLOv11) for animal segmentation and small-object fly detection under real-world conditions. From the detection results, three complementary descriptors are proposed: fly density, fly count, and spatial coverage. These descriptors are normalized using robust empirical references and serve as inputs to a Mamdani-type T3FLS, which explicitly models uncertainty arising from detection noise, environmental variability, and ambiguous infestation boundaries. The fuzzy system outputs a continuous infestation index in the range [0, 1] together with a linguistic classification (Low, Moderate, High). Experimental validation was conducted using 150 images evaluated by the proposed system and by three human experts. Comparative results show that the Type-3 fuzzy model clearly outperforms lower-order fuzzy systems, achieving balanced accuracy, macro F1-score, and Cohen’s kappa coefficient of 0.905, 0.891, and 0.854, respectively, indicating strong agreement with expert assessments. The proposed framework advances automated fly assessment beyond simple counting toward a holistic, uncertainty-aware infestation evaluation, providing a robust and practical decision-support tool for livestock management.

title: Automated on-site viable primordia count estimation for Hypsizygus marmoreus through enhanced RSL-YOLOv8m based segmentation
abstract: The viable primordia in edible mushroom cultivation are the most critical factor determining yield and quality, yet its accurate quantification remains challenging due to morphological variability and low-contrast backgrounds. This study proposes an enhanced RSL-YOLOv8m-seg framework that significantly improves segmentation robustness through multi-scale feature enhancement and adaptive fusion mechanisms. Validated on a Hypsizygus marmoreus dataset containing 200,000 annotated instances, the model achieves 68.1% mAP@0.5–surpassing the baseline by 1.9 percentage points–while maintaining stable performance in industrial cultivation environments. The synergistic module integration elevates recall to 48.5% and true positive rate to 89.2%, with computational cost constrained within industrial deployment limits. Convex hull contour fitting is utilized to precisely quantify the aspect ratios of primordia. Subsequently, viable primordia are defined using an aspect ratio criterion greater than four. To the best of the researchers’ knowledge, this represents the first application of deep learning for detection and analysis of Hypsizygus marmoreus primordia, providing reliable technical support for intelligent cultivation regulation.

title: Non-destructive quantitative assessment of rice seedling transplanting injury using a CSI–hyperspectral framework
abstract: Mechanical transplanting often induces complex root–stem-coupled injury to rice seedlings, a critical bottleneck for stable yield formation that remains difficult to quantify. This injury mode generates a synergistic, non-additive stress state between root and stem tissues, driving a persistent high-stress regime that explains delayed regreening and seedling mortality. Existing assessment methods rely on subjective field sampling or isolated physiological indicators. These approaches fail to capture systemic root–stem synergy, yielding unstable ground truths for non-destructive phenotyping. To address this, we developed and validated a Comprehensive Stress Index–Hyperspectral Imaging (CSI–HSI) framework. Under controlled conditions, graded root–stem-coupled injury was imposed while measuring malondialdehyde (MDA), proline (Pro), soluble sugars (SS), the SPAD chlorophyll index, and chlorophyll fluorescence (Fv/Fm). Principal component analysis (PCA) integrated these variables into the CSI, which served as a linearized, robust modeling ground truth for systemic stress. Using hyperspectral data, we developed prediction models based on partial least squares regression (PLSR), support vector regression (SVR), random forest regression (RFR), and convolutional neural networks (CNN). When CSI was the response variable, model accuracy and robustness consistently outperformed those of models targeting single indicators. The CSI-targeted SPA–PLSR model (successive projections algorithm combined with PLSR) achieved the highest accuracy (Rp2 = 0.914, 95% CI: 0.882–0.923; RPD = 2.645), higher than the best single-indicator model (SPAD-targeted, Rp2 = 0.882). The CSI–HSI framework provides a physiologically grounded, non-destructive solution for quantifying complex transplanting injury, establishing a foundation for transplanter design optimization and intelligent, real-time quality monitoring.

title: RapeseedNet: a lightweight deep learning model for rapeseed quality detection based on near-infrared spectroscopy
abstract: Rapid detection of key quality indicators of rapeseed and edge deployment are crucial for improving oil processing efficiency, ensuring feed safety, and optimizing storage management. This study analyzed the responses of oil content, protein content, glucosinolate content, and moisture content of 681 rapeseed samples from multiple varieties and regions to near-infrared spectroscopy (NIR). It also explored the effects of different preprocessing methods and data partitioning strategies on model performance. To address the limitations of traditional detection methods (time-consuming, destructive) and insufficient generalization of existing models, a base model RapeseedNet-Base was constructed by fusing ResNet modules, Transformer encoder layers, and Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP). This model outperformed traditional machine learning methods in quality prediction tasks, with determination coefficients (R2) of 0.893, 0.818, 0.917, and 0.815 for oil content, protein content, glucosinolate content, and moisture content prediction on the test set, respectively. Through multi-scale knowledge distillation and unstructured pruning optimization, it was upgraded to a lightweight model RapeseedNet, with a 61.2% reduction in parameters, 56% shorter computation time, and no significant loss of accuracy. After deploying the model to a portable detector, on-site verification showed R2 = 0.867 for oil content prediction and R2 = 0.819 for glucosinolate content prediction, with a single detection time of approximately 15 s, meeting real-time detection needs. This study provides strong technical support for rapid rapeseed quality detection and precise processing, and also offers a reference for non-destructive detection of other oilseed crops.

title: LeafCLIP: A detection method for the lesion areas of outdoor plants in complex lighting scenarios
abstract: Plant disease detection under complex natural field conditions is critical for sustainable agriculture but remains challenging due to severe photometric variations, frequent occlusions, and limited annotated data. Traditional visual models often struggle to generalize in real-world scenarios, where irregular shadows, dense foliage, and background clutter substantially degrade detection accuracy and robustness. To address these issues, we propose a unified and robust framework based on a cascaded CLIP architecture that combines multi-scale semantic feature alignment with physics-aware shadow correction. The framework introduces structure-preserving synthetic anomaly generation to enrich training diversity, lightweight adapters to fuse multi-depth CLIP visual features for precise lesion localization, and domain-specific learnable text prompts to enhance cross-modal alignment. Additionally, a dynamic mask-aware diffusion model is devised to reconstruct illumination-invariant representations by jointly refining shadow masks and restoring degraded regions. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple datasets on various benchmarks, such as Image-AUROC, mean Average Precision (mAP). In particular, on the Rice Leaf Images detection, our method reaches an image-level AUROC of 0.9900 and a mAP of 0.9973. Overall, the results verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework to appearance-level distribution shifts under challenging agricultural field conditions.

title: DyRFA-Net: Apple flower blooming stage detection based on anther color features
abstract: Monitoring the blooming stages of apple flowers is crucial for orchard management, as different floral stages directly influence the timing and success of pollination. A novel deep learning framework, DyRFA-Net, is proposed in this study, where the blooming stages of apple flowers are detected based on anther color features as the core visual indicator. Instead of adopting conventional physiological definitions, this study classifies apple flowers into two blooming stages based on anther color. Flowers with unopened florets or pale-yellow anthers are considered to be in the early blooming stage, while those with orange anthers are regarded as being in the later stage of flowering. DyRFA-Net integrates a Receptive-Field Attention Convolution (RFAConv) to enhance flower feature extraction in complex orchard scenes. A Partial Multi-Scale Attention (PMA) module is introduced to capture subtle changes in stamen color while maintaining a lightweight model architecture. Additionally, Dynamic Upsampling (DySample) is employed to improve detection precision for small and densely clustered flowers. The model is evaluated on a self-constructed apple flower dataset annotated according to the anther color-based blooming stage. Experimental results show that DyRFA-Net achieves mAP50 detection accuracies of 88.2% for flowers in the later blooming stage and 86.7% for those in the early blooming stage, with an overall mAP50 of 87.4%. For mAP50–95, the model achieves 69.3% and 68.2%, respectively. The proposed method also outperforms several state-of-the-art detectors in stage classification accuracy. These results demonstrate that DyRFA-Net provides an effective and biologically grounded solution for apple flower blooming stage detection, offering practical support for intelligent orchard management and precise pollination scheduling.

title: Comparative evaluation of machine learning models integrated with optimization algorithms for daily transpiration estimation in citrus orchards of dry-hot valley region in China
abstract: Accurate estimation of canopy transpiration (T) is essential for optimizing irrigation scheduling and improving water-use efficiency. Machine learning (ML) approaches have become critical for T estimation in smart agriculture. This study was conducted in citrus orchards within the Yuanjiang Dry-hot Valley, Yunnan Province, China. From 2020 to 2022, sap flow was monitored using thermal dissipation probes (TDP), and these data were integrated with multi-source meteorological and soil variables to develop T estimation models. The Random Forest-Recursive Feature Elimination (RF-RFE) algorithm was applied for feature selection. Twelve models were developed by combining three ML models, Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), with three hyperparameter tuning algorithms, Grid Search (GS), Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO). Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) was used to interpret the drivers of the best-performing model. Results demonstrated that RF-RFE effectively reduced input variables from 17 to 5 key factors: day of year (DOY), average air temperature (Ta), wind speed (u2), soil volumetric water content (VWC), and actual vapor pressure (ea). Among the 12 models, the GWO-XGB combination achieved the best performance (R2 = 0.91, KGE = 0.94, and RMSE = 0.18 mm d-1), ranking first in the Global Performance Indicator (GPI). SHAP analysis further revealed that DOY characterized seasonal climatic variations and phenological rhythms, Ta and u2 positively contributed to T, while ea showed a negative contribution, and VWC imposed a limiting effect at low levels. The proposed RF-RFE and GWO–XGB framework provides accurate and interpretable T estimation using only five key inputs. It offers a practical and scalable solution for precision irrigation decision support in dry-hot valleys.

title: MIRAGE: Biomechanically interpretable 3D generation and reconstruction of maize plants
abstract: Accurate 3D modeling is essential for automated plant phenotyping and biomechanical analysis. We present MIRAGE (MaIze Reconstruction And GEneration), a biomechanically guided framework for generating and reconstructing 3D maize plants from a single image. At its core is MaizeBR, an interpretable and controllable 3D biomechanical representation that introduces a novel parameterization model for maize organs. MaizeBR is motivated by plant biomechanics, incorporating structural constraints informed by biological principles, including stalk cylindricality, anisotropic leaf curvature, and phyllotactic attachment patterns, commonly observed as the key traits in real maize plants. These constraints enhance the structural integrity and biological plausibility of the reconstructed models. MIRAGE generates 3D structures using a voxel-based diffusion model, followed by NURBS (Non-Uniform Rational B-Splines) surface reconstruction guided by MaizeBR. To enhance generalization, we incorporate domain-specific augmentations that simulate natural plant variations such as leaf curvature and elongation. Experiments across multiple maize datasets show that MIRAGE outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both reconstruction quality and biological plausibility. Additionally, by enabling accurate 3D skeletonization, MIRAGE supports more precise phenotypic trait extraction compared to traditional 2D-based approaches.

title: A machine learning-based wearable system for automated detection of sheep parturition events using accelerometer data
abstract: • Wearable accelerometer technology enables the detection of lambing events by monitoring ewe discomfort and lying bouts. • A learning model was developed to define time intervals leading up to lambing. • The learning model identifies time intervals based on lying bout patterns. • The detection system provides near real-time lambing detection. The quality and safety of sheep farming increasingly depend on automated monitoring systems, with parturition detection representing a critical challenge due to its direct impact on lamb survival. This study presents the development and evaluation of two machine learning approaches for predicting sheep parturition: a lightweight model designed for deployment on collar-mounted devices with limited computational resources, and a full-featured model intended for scenarios without such constraints. The models were developed using data from 53 parturition events collected via collar-mounted accelerometers and thermometers, within a system that supports real-time data acquisition, processing, and visualization of parturition predictions. The lightweight model, operating under strict computational and memory limitations, achieved an accuracy of 0.74 and a Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.71. In contrast, the full-featured model delivered superior performance, reaching an accuracy of 0.81 and an MCC of 0.79 when predicting time to birth up to 11 h in advance. Additionally, temporal filtering optimization contributed to stable performance in extended validation scenarios for both models. The work included the development of a detection tool based on the use of an MQTT broker, that includes two subscribers that perform detection, and alarm triggering, and a producer that streams monitoring data gathered by the the collars. Overall, this work advances precision livestock farming by offering two practical solutions for automated parturition monitoring, enabling farmers to select either a resource-efficient or a high-performance approach according to their specific operational requirements and available infrastructure.

title: TARAG: A time-aware retrieval-augmented generation framework for supporting precision crop pest and disease management through large language models
abstract: Plant diseases and pests cause significant annual crop losses, severely threatening global food security. To mitigate crop losses, large language models (LLMs) demonstrate the ability to alleviate challenges in accessing precise farming support by acting as intelligent assistants that provide farmers with timely and precise decision support services. However, existing efforts still fall short in precision due to the neglect of time-sensitive nature in agricultural practices. They implicitly treat domain knowledge as time-irrelevant, ignoring the impact of crop phenology and pest life stages in their generated recommendations. To address this challenge, we propose a Time-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework (TARAG), comprising a time-aware knowledge base construction module, a hybrid retrieval module, and a time-based generation module to provide precise pest management suggestions. Firstly, the time-aware knowledge base construction module constructs a time-annotated knowledge base from unstructured documents to provide supplementary agricultural knowledge. Secondly, the hybrid retrieval module performs coarse-grained sparse retrieval to ensure relevance, with a time-sensitive re-ranking stage that refines the results to achieve both semantic relevance retrieval and time alignment with user queries. Finally, the time-aware generation module leverages the top-k retrieved documents and an instruction prompt to produce the final suggestion. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, we contribute TAQA, the first bilingual, time-annotated agricultural question-answering dataset. Experiments demonstrate that TARAG significantly outperforms state-of-the-art RAG frameworks in retrieval precision and suggestion quality, with 99.14% retrieval recall and an F1 score of 66.85% for generated suggestions. The implementation and datasets for this work are available in https://github.com/lee-hash1/agri_rag.

title: Behavior recognition and abnormality detection for Muscovy ducks under various lighting conditions using an IoT-Based system
abstract: The proposed system is based on an IoT-controlled lighting platform and enables real-time monitoring of poultry behavior under different illumination conditions. By integrating an IoT-based environmental control system with an improved deep learning model (DBR-YOLOv8), the proposed framework enables long-term behavioral data collection under multiple illumination conditions and provides intuitive interpretability through heatmap visualization and statistical analysis, thereby reducing the difficulty of manual observation in complex lighting environments. Using the IoT platform, lighting parameters including illuminance, exposure duration, and spectral configuration were precisely controlled, while video data were recorded. Under regular light, simulated sunlight, spectral variation, and dark night conditions, DBR-YOLOv8 achieved mAP values of 92.0%, 93.4%, 96.1%, and 95.8%, respectively, demonstrating robust behavior recognition performance across variable lighting environments. Based on data collected from 180 Muscovy ducks and over 18 million images across a multi-group, replicated experimental design involving 18 housing units, the system further enabled quantitative analysis of four abnormal behaviors. The results indicated that light duration, high-intensity exposure time, illumination intensity, and spectral variation significantly influenced abnormal behavior frequency. In particular, regression analysis suggested a 4-hour high-intensity period at 3000 lx with a simulated sunlight spectrum as a prioritized candidate configuration associated with reduced abnormal behavior expression.

title: Beetroot type classification based on 3D structure constructed with neural radiance fields
abstract: The phenotypic traits of beetroot are of great significance for revealing the relationship between their morphology and functional traits, as well as for the breeding high-quality cultivars. The 3D models can provide a more comprehensive and accurate description of beetroot structural features, offering richer phenotypic information compared to traditional 2D imaging methods. This study developed a novel framework that integrates Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) for high-fidelity 3D reconstruction, multi-dimensional phenotypic traits extraction and an end to end network, named as Point-SugarRoot based on point cloud and deep learning for precise classification. The results indicated that NeRF-derived phenotypic traits strongly correlated with actual measurements, achieving R2 values exceeding 0.92. NeRF-reconstructed point clouds exhibited less noise, with an average C2C distance of 0.11 cm, a SC rate of 94.6%, and a 12.9% reduction in reconstruction time, outperforming the Structure from Motion (SfM)-Multi-View Stereo (MVS) method in precision and efficiency. The Point-SugarRoot network surpassed the baseline PointNet++ model, delivering Precision, Recall, F1 score, and Balanced Accuracy of 91.3%, 90.8%, 91.1%, and 93.0%, respectively, and outperformed phenotype- and 2D image-based classification methods by 13% to 33% across all metrics. This research presents a novel solution for high-fidelity 3D reconstruction and phenotypic analysis of beetroots, while also providing valuable technical insights for cultivar breeding and crop management.
