title: Leaf area extraction framework: Transformer-based segmentation and geometric-based completion approaches for accurate extraction of field maize leaf area from point clouds
abstract: The accurate determination of the maize leaf area is crucial for precision agriculture and yield optimization. Three-dimensional point-cloud technology provides a non-destructive and efficient alternative to traditional methods, which are often inefficient and inaccurate. This study aims to develop a robust field-compatible framework for maize leaf area extraction. It focuses on two key challenges: interference from environmental factors, such as strong sunlight, during point-cloud collection, and the mutual occlusion of leaves under complex field conditions. To address the first challenge, we propose a structured light-based point-cloud acquisition system that is optimized to minimize sunlight interference, thus enabling high-fidelity data collection in outdoor environments. We then utilize a Transformer-enhanced semantic segmentation network to isolate individual leaves accurately, achieving high precision across key evaluation metrics, including the precision, recall, F1-score, and intersection over union. The leaf area is subsequently calculated through triangulation. Our analysis revealed distinct performance variations between the vegetative and reproductive growth phases. While the framework demonstrated exceptional accuracy during the early stages, the performance declined significantly during the tasselling-to-maturity phase, owing to increased leaf occlusion and geometric complexity. To address this issue, we introduce two novel geometric processing algorithms: leaf contour completion and leaf body completion. These algorithms collectively enhance the accuracy, and the improvement effect becomes more significant as the point-cloud loss intensifies. Consequently, the most pronounced improvements are observed in the later growth stages. This work contributes to precision agriculture by establishing a growth-stage-adaptive leaf area extraction framework that aligns technical innovations with agronomic needs.

title: Combination of metric-based few-shot and contrastive learning for soybean high-throughput phenotype under high temperature stress
abstract: Soybeans play a crucial role in global food security, and the increasing severity of heat stress due to climate change in recent years has highlighted the growing importance of phenotypic assessment for breeding. While unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing offers a low-cost, high-throughput, and non-destructive approach for canopy phenotyping, variations among soybean genotypes and across growing seasons lead to scarce labeled data, which limits the applicability of traditional deep learning models. This study aims to develop a novel few-shot learning algorithm for identifying soybean canopy phenotypes under high-temperature stress (HT) and control (CK) conditions, utilizing two years of UAV RGB and near-infrared (NIR) imagery. This study proposes the Soybean Contrastive Prototypical Network (SCProtoNet), a metric-based few-shot learning model designed for accurate phenotypic analysis of soybean canopies. Specifically, SCProtoNet employs a dual-branch architecture to jointly process RGB and NIR images, effectively capturing phenotypic differences in soybean canopies caused by genotypes by optimizing prototype representations and contrastive learning instance discrimination based on few-shot scenarios. As a result, in the first year, SCProtoNet achieves an accuracy of 91.56% in a 1-shot training setting. In the second year, weights transferred from the first year are used to validate the generalization performance of the model across experimental years. Retraining the model in a 16-shot setting achieves experimental results of 87.65% and 100%. This few-shot learning model has been effectively tested on canopy images of 3232 different soybean genotypes. Experimental results demonstrate the robustness and generalization performance of the model across different experimental periods. SCProtoNet provides a valuable reference for implementing soybean genotype selection and lays the foundation for phenotypic analysis tasks in other crops under few-shot conditions. The source code and trained models are available at https://github.com/Lzylearn/SCProtoNet-Soybean.

title: Agrosense v2: An AI-enabled system for precision orchard sensing and tree-level monitoring
abstract: Precision orchard management requires robust sensing systems that operate reliably under unstructured field conditions while providing actionable, tree-level information. Despite advances in computer vision and edge computing, most approaches focus on isolated tasks and lack integration into deployable, orchard-scale systems. This study presents Next-Generation Agrosense (Agrosense v2), an AI-enabled, system-oriented framework for real-time orchard sensing and tree-level monitoring. Agrosense v2 integrates tree detection and counting, canopy density classification, tree height estimation (inherited from Agrosense v1, not validated in detail in this study), and detection-based fruit counting on both the tree and the ground into a unified pipeline. Compared with the previous version (Agrosense v1), Agrosense v2 improves tree identification through temporal tracking, strengthens canopy density classification by leveraging image sequences, and adds fruit counting via image-level detection, with all outputs aggregated into tree-level spatiotemporal summaries, presented by a self-developed tree-level visualization tool. Field experiments in three citrus orchards with contrasting management conditions totaled 3,696 trees across two commercial orchards (Field A&B) and a research station (SWFREC). Tree counting accuracies were 95.96% (SWFREC), 92.73% (Field A), and 97.79% (Field B), and canopy density classification accuracies were 94.1% to 96.8%. For fruit detection, the transformer-based RT-DETR model achieved the highest mAP@0.5 up to 0.837 and 0.722 for fruits on the tree and ground, respectively, demonstrating robustness under dense canopy and cluttered ground conditions. To our knowledge, Agrosense v2 is the first real-time, field-deployable orchard sensing system that delivers multiple tree-level attributes within a single framework. By unifying perception, inference, and geo-referenced aggregation, Agrosense v2 provides a scalable foundation for data-driven precision orchard management.

title: Event triggered disturbance observer based nonlinear MPC for agricultural machinery trajectory tracking control
abstract: Autonomous operation of agricultural machinery in uneven and slippery terrain necessitates highly accurate trajectory tracking control. While Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) provides a robust formulation for this task, its real-time implementation is often limited by high computational demands, model uncertainties, and time-varying external disturbances. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel event-triggered disturbance observer based NMPC framework for agricultural machinery trajectory tracking to enhance tracking performance while reducing computational time. A nonlinear disturbance observer integrated with an Actor–Critic Neural Network (ACNN) is developed to dynamically estimate and compensate for both model uncertainties and time-varying external disturbances. A novel Pseudo-Huber cost function is utilized to formulate a dynamically smooth input saturation model to manage actuator constraints and prevent saturation-induced instability. To further reduce computational overhead, an event-triggered mechanism is implemented, where optimization updates are activated only when the prediction error between the system’s optimal forecasted state and its actual measured state exceeds a predefined threshold. This mechanism reduces the frequency of optimization computations, thereby alleviating the computational burden inherent in conventional NMPC, without compromising control performance. Comprehensive simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme. The results demonstrate that the event-triggered disturbance observer based NMPC method not only achieves substantial savings in computational resources compared to NMPC but also maintains high trajectory tracking accuracy under the influence of disturbances.

title: Estimation of cercospora leaf spot disease severity in table beets from UAS multispectral images
abstract: Cercospora leaf spot (CLS), caused by the fungus Cercospora beticola Sacc., is a severe foliar disease that affects the health of table beet crops. Remote sensing techniques, specifically unmanned aerial systems (UAS), could offer a valuable solution for evaluating disease progression and targeted fungicide application towards effectively managing CLS. We conducted UAS flights over C. beticola inoculated table beet plots at Cornell Agritech in Geneva, NY, USA during the growing seasons of 2021, 2022 and 2023. Five-band (475,560, 668, 717 and 840 nm) multispectral imagery was collected for the 2021 and 2022 flights, while for 2023 flights, a four-band (560, 650, 730 and 860 nm) sensor was used. CLS disease severity was assessed in situ at regular intervals, severity was evaluated using both spectral and textural features. Vegetation indices, derived from multispectral imagery, are known to be effective in assessing plant health and disease determination. Texture features also have been reported to be effective in determining plant traits since they provide additional pixel-spatial information to the model. Extensive selection was used to obtain the most relevant features. Our best-performing machine learning model used a random forest regressor to estimate disease severity at an R2test = 0.82 and RMSEtest = 9.31%. Furthermore, the disease progression was tracked using area-under-disease- progression-stairs (AUDPS) and the predicted values had a correlation coefficient of 0.84, 0.94 and 0.81 with 2021, 2022 and 2023 data, respectively. These results are strongly encouraging to support table beet growers with advanced data collection and analysis methodologies, enabling them to implement rapid and efficient foliar disease management strategies.

title: Slide-DQN: Adaptive slip control for crawler agricultural machinery in hilly and mountainous terrains using modified deep Q-network
abstract: Maintaining driving stability control in crawler agricultural machinery under non-stationary operating conditions in hilly and mountainous terrain remains challenging due to strong nonlinearities, continuous time-varying uncertainties, and unpredictable dynamics. Existing approaches lack robust models for instability prediction under soil texture fluctuations, and the compensation mechanisms of drive control systems remain inadequately characterized, hindering optimal torque distribution between tracks. This study proposes Slide-DQN, an adaptive slip control method based on a modified Deep Q-Network (DQN). The approach features targeted designs of the state-action space, neural network architecture, and reward function. Slide-DQN is integrated with the pure pursuit navigation algorithm to achieve adaptive navigation and slip control. Experimental validation was conducted using a crawler slip experiment platform. Results demonstrate that in adaptive navigation control experiments under Scene N2, the maximum tracking deviation decreased by 75.0% and over-correction distance was reduced by 40.0%. Under Scene N9, maximum deviation decreased by 70.6% and over-correction distance was reduced by 55.6%. These results validate the algorithm’s superiority in enhancing trajectory tracking stability during slip conditions in hilly and mountainous terrains, significantly improving navigation accuracy.

title: Clustering in mixed broiler chicken batches for improvement of daily average weight
authors: Laura Emmanuella A. dos S. Santana
abstract: Flock management for industrial processing highly depends on the monitoring of their average body weight and uniformity. This paper presents a novel approach based on artificial intelligence clustering to improve the estimated average daily weight when the birds are reared together despite their sex (mixed batches), without additional hardware and based on data collected from existing scales within automatic weighing systems inside aviaries. Results from actual production cycle in 15 aviaries and 195,000 birds demonstrated that 86% of these batches reduced the Mean Absolute Error of the weight growth curve when compared to the reference weights and simple arithmetic average. Moreover, this new clustered average, used as input for the slaughter weight prediction model, reclassified 35.19% of the batches to the fully acceptable market tolerance of 2%, which refers to the difference between the actual and predicted slaughter weight. These achievements suggest that the application of even simple AI techniques brings remarkable improvement for the overall poultry processing industry.

title: In situ orange soluble solids content estimation based on hyperspectral imaging and transformer
abstract: The in-field estimation of the oranges’ soluble solids content (SSC) using hyperspectral imaging(HSI) holds significant importance in facilitating the implementation of automated agricultural robots for selective harvesting operations and ensure the fruit quality. However, HSI analysis primarily utilizes the conventional machine learning approaches trained on small-scale datasets, which restricts prediction accuracy and generalization capability. Additionally, the high cost of hyperspectral cameras greatly hampers their widespread application in agricultural scenarios. This study proposed the utilization of transformer-based models for HSI analysis to SSC of oranges. Moreover, it explored the use of spectral reconstruction algorithms in reconstructing hyperspectral images from RGB images. A dataset for citrus was first established, which comprises 1536 samples; each sample includes a hyperspectral image, a RGB image and its corresponding SSC value, collected the growth of citrus from early maturity to late harvest across various field conditions. The hyperspectral images without reflectance calibration and dimensional reduction were utilized as input for training the transformer-based model for SSC prediction. The proposed transformer-based SSC prediction model on raw data demonstrated 14.8% better performance than PLS in terms of R2 (0.70 vs. 0.61), 11.7% better in terms of RMSE (0.83°Brix vs. 0.94°Brix). To validate the effectiveness of spectral reconstruction models, reconstructed hyperspectral images from RGB images are used for estimating the SSC of oranges. Their SSC prediction results consistently outperformed those derived from the corresponding RGB images, whether these were rendered from hyperspectral images (R2 = 0.64 vs. 0.56) or captured using a smartphone RGB sensor (R2 = 0.48 vs. 0.42). These results indicated that the capabilities of deep learning technologies to reduce costs and enhance accuracy, which can help promote the widespread application of automated selective harvesting operations and ripeness monitoring in agricultural scenarios.

title: Light-TDNN: A lightweight acoustic model for panic stress recognition of caged laying hens in intensive farms
abstract: Panic stress is a prevalent environmental stressor in laying-hen production, leading to severe consequences such as weakened immunity and reduced egg production. Traditional monitoring methods, including manual inspection and physiological sampling, are labor-intensive and invasive; moreover, blood sampling itself may induce secondary stress. Video-based monitoring is also constrained in intensive battery-cage systems due to severe visual occlusion. In contrast, acoustic signals are well suited to complex cage environments because of strong penetration, flexible deployment, and high information density. Leveraging these advantages, a lightweight panic stress vocalization recognition model, the Lightweight Time Delay Neural Network (Light-TDNN), was constructed. To support model development and evaluation, an acoustic dataset collected under diverse typical stressor stimuli was established. Built upon the TDNN architecture, Light-TDNN integrates three key optimization strategies: (1) a Dilated-Shuffle module that substantially reduces model size while capturing long-range temporal dependencies via an expanded receptive field; (2) a Time-Frequency attention module that focuses on the most discriminative time–frequency features and enhances the recognition of easily confused sounds like panic-induced cage noise and feeding sounds; and (3) a relational knowledge distillation strategy that transfers teacher model knowledge and elevates the student model’s performance ceiling without increasing inference cost. Experiments in real farming scenarios show that Light-TDNN achieves a precision of 96.44% and a recall of 93.75%, with only 0.34 M parameters and 39.86 M FLOPs, delivering a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off compared with mainstream models. Additionally, a real-time monitoring system was developed by deploying Light-TDNN on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge architecture. The system achieves an average end-to-end latency of 23.89 ms per 4-s window, enabling low-latency real-time monitoring in large-scale farms. This work offers a robust on-device solution for non-invasive stress detection, providing a quantitative metric to assess the welfare compatibility of intelligent agricultural machinery and inform welfare-oriented equipment design.

title: FENE: Fish-conditioned Expert Network using deep learning for multi-species marine distribution modeling
abstract: Accurate species distribution modeling (SDM) is essential for sustainable fisheries management and marine ecosystem conservation, particularly in environmentally heterogeneous regions such as the Mediterranean Sea. While existing SDM approaches capture aspects of non-linear relationships, spatial variability, or uncertainty, relatively few jointly model species-specific responses, geospatial structure, and predictive uncertainty within a unified multi-species framework. In this study, we propose FENE (Fish-conditioned Expert Network), a deep learning architecture that integrates environmental predictors, spatial information, and species identity for multi-species SDM. The framework combines species-conditioned feature modulation, continuous spatial encoding, and a mixture-of-experts prediction mechanism to capture heterogeneous ecological responses while producing probabilistic outputs. We evaluate the model on a public Mediterranean dataset comprising eight commercially important pelagic fish species. FENE achieves strong predictive performance (RMSE = 0.071, R2 = 0.952), outperforming commonly used machine learning baselines, including tree-based and kernel-based methods, under the same evaluation setting. Performance further improves with feature selection (RMSE = 0.060, R2 = 0.968), indicating robustness to high-dimensional environmental inputs. Beyond predictive accuracy, the model enables species-specific interpretation via feature-attribution analysis and produces spatially explicit uncertainty estimates. Higher uncertainty is observed in ecotonal and data-sparse regions, indicating reduced model confidence under environmental variability. These results demonstrate that FENE can jointly model species-specific responses and quantify predictive uncertainty within a multi-species SDM setting.

title: Wintertime pollutant forecasting in northern sheep houses via a physics-constrained, multi-modal deep hybrid model
abstract: During winter in northern regions, the enclosed conditions of sheep houses result in poor ventilation, leading to the accumulation of pollutants, which severely impacts the health of mutton sheep. Realizing Precision Livestock Farming (PLF) necessitates high-precision forecasting models to transition management strategies from reactive responses to proactive, fine-grained interventions. To enable such proactive monitoring of the sheep house environment, this study proposes a deep hybrid model based on multi-modal fusion, FA-TMViT-XGB, for the prediction of indoor concentrations of NH3, CO2, PM2.5, and humidity specifically in enclosed sheep houses during winter. The study initially employs a sequential denoising strategy: Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) is utilized to adaptively separate high-frequency noise from valid signal modes, followed by Kalman filtering to robustly track the underlying trend state. Subsequently, in the temporal branch, a frequency attention module is introduced to focus on low-frequency periodic components, combined with trend decomposition, periodic modulation, and a TimeMixer network to extract multi-scale temporal features. Simultaneously, the time series are encoded into two-dimensional images via Gramian Angular Fields (GAF) and Markov Transition Fields (MTF), which are then input into a Vision Transformer (ViT) to extract spatial patterns. The extracted temporal and image features are fused through a gated mechanism, optimized with a physics-constrained heuristic regularization loss, and finally fed into an XGBoost regressor to generate the concentration prediction results.In the single-step prediction of NH3 concentration, the FA-TMVIT-XGB model demonstrated superior performance, achieving a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0270, a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.0354, and an R2 of 0.9836 against the denoised reference trend. Crucially, robustness tests on raw sensor inputs confirmed the model’s resilience to high-frequency noise (R2>0.88). Compared to a pure Transformer model, the MAE and RMSE decreased by 73.6% and 70.8% respectively, and R2 increased by 21.8% Furthermore, multi-step forecasting experiments confirmed the model’s robustness (R2>0.9), serving as a supplementary safety buffer for risk warning. This complements the foundational single-step prediction, which satisfies the stringent precision requirements of PLF, enabling fine-grained ventilation adjustments to effectively prevent cold stress. By balancing immediate thermal stability with future air quality management, the model provides a comprehensive solution for improving flock health and production efficiency in wintertime enclosed sheep houses.

title: Latent diffusion meets semi-supervised learning: Enhancing plant disease detection with minimal labels
abstract: Accurate assessment of plant disease severity is essential for sustainable agriculture, but is often limited by the scarcity of annotated data. Generative models offer a promising solution by producing realistic synthetic samples that can enrich training datasets and improve model generalization. However, most existing approaches rely on large, fully labeled datasets, limiting their applicability when expert annotations are costly or difficult to obtain. This study introduces a semi-supervised latent diffusion model for the conditional generation of wheat leaf images with controllable yellow rust ( Puccinia striiformis ) disease severity. The model conditions generation on leaf segmentation masks and disease severity scores, leveraging a small labeled subset and a large set of unlabeled images. This enables the creation of realistic, severity-controllable synthetic images that effectively augment limited training datasets. Experimental results demonstrate substantial improvements in downstream regression performance, particularly under extreme annotation scarcity. Notably, when applying a per-range reduction strategy with only ten labeled images (one per disease severity bin), the baseline regression model trained exclusively on real labeled images achieved an R 2 of 0.44, whereas augmentation with semi-supervised synthetic images increased R 2 to 0.79—a gain of ＋0.35. Improvements were observed across all annotation levels, with consistent reductions in MAE and RMSE, highlighting the effectiveness of combining semi-supervised generative training with balanced sampling. These findings confirm that leveraging unlabeled data in generative diffusion models produces realistic, controllable synthetic images that enrich supervised learning. The proposed approach provides a scalable, cost-effective pathway to reduce dependence on large labeled datasets while maintaining precise control over disease severity.

title: Soybean drought recognition method based on multi-view 3D image Fourier transform
abstract: Drought stress is an important adversity factor for soybean production. Accurate determination of drought is significant for water-saving irrigation and management. Existing low-cost 3D imaging technology based on Kinect sensors can capture the structural and phenotypic changes of plant canopies, but it is difficult to characterize the relationship between the spectral features of soybean 3D images and environmental factors changes. Thus, in this study, a soybean drought recognition method was proposed based on multi-view 3D image Fourier transform. First, the multi-view projection algorithm of the 3D point cloud was used to obtain 21 view projection images based on the depth and color information of the soybean canopy. Second, a discrete Fourier transform was performed to calculate the frequency-domain features of the images in each projection direction. In addition, a quantum genetic algorithm (QGA) was applied to obtain the optimal combination of feature weights. Finally, the features of the optimal projection images were extracted to establish the drought recognition model of soybeans based on a radial basis function (RBF) neural network. The result showed that the model’s recognition accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score were 95.75%, 95.70%, 91.70%, and 93.60%, respectively, and the four evaluation indexes have been improved by 8.39%, 11.57%, 0.2%, and 5.83%, respectively, compared with the back propagation (BP), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM) methods. This research realized rapid and non-destructive detection of drought stress for the soybean plant, and provided a relevant basis and support for soybean water-saving irrigation and cultivation management.

title: Hyperspectral response and quantitative monitoring of soil organic carbon on the Loess Plateau
abstract: The accurate estimation of soil organic carbon (SOC) is crucial for effective soil resource management, improvement agricultural productivity, and mitigating climate change. To investigate the hyperspectral response mechanisms of SOC and its influencing factors, this study was conducted based on a long-term conservation tillage experiment in a winter wheat field. Soil samples were collected from a depth of 0–60 cm during 2020–2023. Hyperspectral data were analyzed using multiple preprocessing and feature selection techniques, and prediction models for SOC and its influencing factors were constructed. The quantitative relationships between different transformed spectra and SOC, as well as its influencing factors, were determined. The optimal spectral features for SOC and its influencing factors were identified. Based on the response of SOC content to its stabilization mechanisms, the optimal spectral features of influencing factors were reorganized to form new characteristic wavelength combinations. These combinations were further used to develop an indirect spectral model for SOC prediction. This approach enabled the identification of the spectral response mechanisms of SOC stabilization processes. The results indicated that spectral reflectance was inversely correlated with SOC, GSSI (general soil structure index), Dm (fractal dimension of mechanical aggregates), MI-OC (microaggregate organic carbon), and SSA (soil sucrase activity). The characteristic regions for SOC were primarily distributed at 400–430 nm, 675–691 nm, and 713–754 nm. These regions were primarily located within the visible spectrum and did not overlap with the optimal characteristic wavelengths of its influencing factors. In the direct modeling of SOC, the optimal preprocessing and wavelength selection methods were the 1st-order differentiation and SBS (sequential backward selection), respectively. RF (random forest) was identified as the most effective modeling method (R v 2 = 0.69, RMSE v = 0.32, MAE v = 0.25). In the spectral estimation methods for SOC influencing factors, the 1st-order differentiation was the optimal preprocessing method, and RF demonstrated superior performance as the modeling approach. The spectral response effects of SSA, GSSI, mechanical aggregate parameters, and FSP-OC (total Organic Carbon of Free Silt and clay Particles) were higher than those of SOC. The indirect model for SOC constructed from the optimal combination of characteristic wavelengths of its influencing factors exhibited higher accuracy (R v 2 = 0.74, RMSE v = 0.27, MAE v = 0.21) than the direct model. SOC sequestration was influenced by the combined effects of multiple soil factors rather than a single indicator. The results confirm the feasibility of hyperspectral SOC monitoring and support its application in rapid soil fertility assessment.

title: Detection of tea heat stress in UAV multi-spectral remote sensing images based on spatial-frequency two stream network
abstract: Accurate detection of tea heat stress (THS) using uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) multi-spectral remote sensing images combined with deep learning techniques is crucial for THS management. However, most existing multi-spectral image fusion detection networks lack robustness in complex scenes and perform poorly in small-target feature extraction, leading to low detection accuracy. To address these issues, a spatial-frequency two-stream network (SFTNet) is proposed. It employs spatial feature extraction (SFE) and frequency feature extraction (FFE) branches to extract high-resolution spatial details from RGB images and rich frequency-domain features from NIR images, respectively. A feature enhancement structure with multiple attention mechanisms and channel interaction was designed at the output end of the FFE branch to effectively aggregate shallow and deep semantic information from the hierarchically aggregated feature maps. For multi-scale feature fusion, a multi-spectral spatial-frequency feature fusion (MSFF) module is developed to achieve tight alignment and integration of RGB and NIR features. To improve small target detection, a multiscale cross-attention aggregation (MCA) module has been proposed. By extracting fine-grained horizontal and vertical features while incorporating a cross-fusion strategy, the MCA module enhances SFTNet’s learning of small target THS features, thereby improving detection accuracy for small target THS. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed SFTNet outperforms state-of-the-art networks across 4 m, 6 m, and 8 m datasets, achieving mAP@50 improvements of 5.9%, 7.7%, and 4.6% respectively. Furthermore, when evaluated on terminal devices in a non-deployment testing setup, SFTNet achieves an inference speed of 15.3 ms per RGB-NIR image pair, suggesting high computational efficiency under these specific conditions.

title: Research on an automated detection for sheep estrus based on multimodal fusion of thermal images and sensor data
abstract: Estrus monitoring is essential for improving reproductive efficiency and optimizing artificial insemination timing in ewes. However, existing studies mainly focus on binary estrus detection and often rely on wearable sensors, invasive physiological measurements, or vision-based behavioral analysis methods, which are insufficient for fine-grained estrus stage discrimination and are limited by animal stress, high deployment cost, and sensitivity to farm environmental disturbances. To address these limitations, this study proposes a non-contact multimodal framework for classifying ewe estrus stages into diestrus, estrus, and metestrus. Thermal infrared features were extracted using an improved ResNet18 incorporating initial convolution (INC), squeeze-and-excitation (SE), and multi-scale fusion (MSF) modules, denoted as INC-SE-MSF-ResNet18. In parallel, bilateral eye temperature features and environmental temperature and humidity features were extracted by multilayer perceptron (MLP)-based eye temperature feature extractor and MLP-based environmental variable feature extractor. These three types of features were then concatenated into a multimodal feature and classified using a Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM). Under the same LightGBM classifier, INC-SE-MSF-ResNet18 generated more discriminative thermal infrared features than ResNet18, MobileNetv3, EfficientNet, ShuffleNet, and DenseNet, yielding improvements of up to 15.10% in recall, 7.67% in F1-score, and 3.10% in accuracy. Under the same feature extraction and fusion strategy, LightGBM consistently outperformed support vector machine (SVM), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT), random forest (RF), decision tree (DT), logistic regression (LR), and convolutional neural network (CNN) across all estrus stages, with precision improvements of up to 21.23% over CNN, 13.17% over DT, and 11.11% over RF. Temperature analysis further revealed clear stage-dependent divergence between bilateral eye temperatures and rectal temperature (RT). The bilateral eye temperatures peaked during estrus, whereas rectal temperature decreased during estrus and increased markedly during metestrus. These results indicate that surface and core temperatures reflect different physiological processes and exhibit unsynchronized temporal dynamics across the estrous cycle. Overall, this study extends infrared thermography-based ewe estrus monitoring from conventional binary detection to protocol-defined estrus stage classification, providing a feasible approach for ovulation timing inference and precision reproductive management in large-scale sheep farming systems.

title: In-situ 3D reconstruction and analysis of droplet motion characteristics in downwash flow of multi-rotor UAV
abstract: Precise pesticide application using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in unstructured orchards requires accurate characterization of droplet deposition and drift states. However, complex outdoor lighting conditions and strong rotor downwash interference pose notable challenges. Therefore, continuous in situ monitoring and analysis of fine droplet motion remain difficult in smart agriculture. To address these challenges, this study proposes a three-dimensional dynamic perception and visualization system based on light detection and ranging. First, a dual-UAV collaborative data acquisition strategy is employed, and an autonomous perception platform is established for dynamic droplet monitoring. Second, deep learning semantic segmentation is integrated with point cloud voxelization. This achieves precise extraction and preprocessing of droplet point clouds against complex backgrounds. Finally, a local optical flow estimation algorithm is applied to invert and analyze the microscopic motion field of droplet groups. The proposed method is evaluated in a real-world orchard scenario. Experimental results indicate the successful development of a comprehensive visualization framework spanning field data acquisition to microscopic motion analysis. The model demonstrates favorable performance in terms of training loss, intersection over union, and accuracy metrics. Furthermore, the dynamic characteristics of droplet flow fields under different operational heights and velocities (e.g., 1.5 and 2.5 m/s) are effectively resolved. Overall, this study achieves a synergistic integration of robust field perception and high-precision droplet dynamics inversion. A valid end-to-end solution is provided for evaluating UAV spraying effectiveness and optimizing operational parameters.

title: Centralized and vertical federated learning for Climate-Based crop yield prediction
abstract: Accurate crop yield assessment is critical for food security planning and climate impact analysis, yet centralized machine learning approaches are increasingly constrained by data privacy requirements and institutional fragmentation. Climate variables, crop model simulations, and yield data are often distributed across organizations, making centralized data integration impractical. This study evaluates federated learning as a privacy-preserving alternative for large-scale crop yield modeling by systematically comparing Centralized Federated Learning (CFL) and Vertical Federated Learning (VFL). Using Ethiopia as a case study, we integrate ERA5 climate variables with maize and wheat yield simulations from the LPJmL and DSSAT models under irrigated and rainfed conditions. While CFL assumes centralized access to all features and labels, VFL employs a split neural network in which data remain at separate institutions and only latent representations are exchanged. Results show that CFL achieves the highest predictive accuracy (R 2 = 0.88–0.91), while VFL exhibits a modest performance reduction (R 2 = 0.765–0.897) but maintains stable convergence and minimal train–test divergence. Validation against FAO yield statistics over a 15-year period confirms that both approaches capture interannual variability and long-term trends. This work provides the first systematic empirical comparison of CFL and VFL for climate-driven crop yield modeling and demonstrates that vertical federated learning can deliver reliable predictions under realistic data-governance constraints, thereby enabling privacy-preserving agricultural yield assessment at scale.

title: FishKeypoints: A comprehensive stereo vision framework for fish behaviour monitoring and size measurement in aquaculture
abstract: The shift towards Precision Fish Farming (PFF) requires reliable, automated tracking of individual fish in dense, dynamic underwater environments. Many approaches targeting this topic are based on using computer vision methods and AI to detect and track the fish automatically. Most conventional approaches rely on the use of Horizontal Bounding Boxes (HBBs), however this approach has proven inadequate for accurately localising slender fish with variable orientation, particularly in scenes where fish density and occlusion is high. This study presents a new computer stereo vision framework that leverages Oriented Bounding Boxes (OBBs) for fish detection followed by keypoint detection for the localisation of the anatomical features of the detected fish. The method was set up to directly estimate 3D positions of the detected fish and keypoints and track these over time without external calibration targets. When applied to stereo video data collected from two field trials at commercial fish farms, the method estimated fish-camera distances and fish lengths that corresponded with reference data obtained through other sensors and manual sampling. These results imply that this new approach represents a step forward in non-invasive, automated monitoring and analysis of fish behaviour and growth, giving more detailed insights into farmed fish dynamics and contributing to further progress in the realisation of PFF.

title: Portable moisture-robust VNIR system integrating a PEPO algorithm for rapeseed chlorophyll quantification
abstract: Chlorophyll content is a critical determinant of rapeseed quality, significantly influencing the processing efficiency and oxidative stability of the resulting oil. However, moisture fluctuations during the harvest-to-processing cycle interfere with visible near-infrared spectroscopy, as moisture-induced spectral variance overlaps with chlorophyll spectral features. This study developed, a portable detection device for rapeseed analysis, and a partial external parameter orthogonalization (PEPO) method was implemented to reduce moisture interference. Compared to full-spectrum correction, PEPO uses a partial correlation analysis to calibrate moisture-sensitive wavelengths, aiming to retain target-specific spectral information. A comparison of machine learning architectures showed that an artificial neural network (ANN) combined with PEPO resulted in the highest predictive performance among the tested models. The model yielded a coefficient of determination in the prediction set of 0.891 and a root mean square error of prediction of 2.7 mg/kg. Relative to standard full-spectrum correction, the proposed approach reduced the performance gap between calibration and prediction sets, indicating improved model generalization. This study not only provides a technical basis for the rapid and non-destructive detection of rapeseed chlorophyll content but also offers an effective correction approach for the spectral analysis of complex agricultural materials susceptible to moisture interference.

title: KDYOLO-Tracker: A Deep Learning Approach to Behavior Recognition and Tracking for Sika Deer
abstract: Accurate recognition and tracking of basic behaviors are key to intelligent health monitoring for sika deer farming. To solve the problems that the current object recognition algorithms have low recognition real-time and low accuracy of identity association caused by the diversity of deer farming environments and the rapid movement speed of sika deer, this research proposes an efficient sika deer behavior recognition approach KDYOLO and a tracking approach MO-Tracking, and constructs a multi-object behavior recognition and tracking method KDYOLO-Tracker. First, a sparse training mechanism is proposed which introduces a scaling factor in the batch normalization layer to adaptively screen and remove unimportant channels, so that the computational efficiency of the model is effectively improved. Second, this paper proposes to integrate the channel pruning algorithm into the KDYOLO to further reduce model size and computation, while the pruned model is fine-tuned by adjusting the learning rate and parameters to mitigate potential accuracy losses. In addition, this paper proposes a multi-object tracking algorithm MO-Tracking, which enhances the matching space for trajectory by expanding the detection buffer, to improve the accuracy of trajectory association. The proposed KDYOLO recognition algorithm is embedded into the MO-Tracking to construct the KDYOLO-Tracker tracking model, so that the performances of recognition and tracking are further improved. The experimental results show: compared with YOLOv8l, the proposed KDYOLO not only improves the detection accuracy but also reduces the model complexity (GFLOPs, parameters, and size) by more than 58%, among which GFLOPs are reduced by 71.66%; the mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 of KDYOLO reach 97.20% and 85.90%, respectively. Compared with mainstream algorithms of SSD, Faster R-CNN, and different versions of YOLO, KDYOLO consistently maintains the highest accuracy, with mAP@0.5 increased by up to 17.05% and mAP@0.5:0.95 increased by up to 31.46%. In terms of tracking performance, the HOTA, MOTA, MOTP, and IDF1 of KDYOLO-Tracker reach 85.70%, 88.30%, 93.60%, and 90.30%, respectively, which are all the highest compared with those of the five multi-object tracking algorithms DeepSort, ByteTrack, DeepMot, BotSort, and MO-Tracking. In addition, the detection speed of KDYOLO-Tracker has reached 108FPS, an increase of 19FPS compared with that without improvement. This research provides the technical support for monitoring the health status and alerting for abnormal behavior of livestock farming animals.

title: Deformable transformer framework for automated calf respiratory health scoring
abstract: • Developed a deformable transformer framework for calf respiratory health scoring. • Evaluated model on real-farm images across ocular, nasal, and ear indicators. • Built a dataset of 5,374 annotated frames from 100 Holstein calves. • Verified interpretability through Grad-CAM visualization of key facial regions. Respiratory diseases significantly impact calf health, welfare, and productivity. Traditional health evaluations rely on subjective human observation, leading to inconsistent diagnoses and scalability challenges in large herds and group housing systems. This study proposes a computer vision framework that automates visual health scoring of calves using images captured by mobile devices under natural farm conditions. The model focuses on key phenotypic indicators—ocular discharge, nasal discharge, and ear posture—associated with bovine respiratory disease. A vision transformer-based architecture was developed, incorporating a Swin Transformer backbone for multi-scale feature extraction, a deformable attention encoder for spatial adaptability, and a query-based decoder to perform 4-class classification aligned with standard scoring guidelines. A dataset of 5374 annotated frames from 100 Holstein calves was collected and labelled by three trained individuals using a standardized 4-point respiratory health scoring system. Evaluation on field-collected data achieved strong performance on the ocular task (Precision: 0.87, Recall: 0.85, F1-score: 0.86), nasal task (Precision: 0.86, Recall: 0.89, F1-score: 0.88), and ear posture task (Precision: 0.75, Recall: 0.90, F1-score: 0.82). Comparative analysis with baseline architectures confirmed the superiority of our method particularly in handling subtle variations in mild and moderate symptoms. Grad-CAM visualizations revealed that the model attends to biologically relevant regions. Additionally, an annotation consistency analysis was conducted and found that inter-annotator agreement significantly influenced model performance, especially in ambiguous scoring cases. These findings highlight the importance of standardized annotation protocols for model generalizability. This work contributes a scalable, non-invasive solution for early respiratory disease monitoring in calves, with potential to improve health outcomes and increase labor efficiency.

title: Mango Expert: a harvest-optimizing wearable decision support system based on multimodal optoelectronic fusion and graph temporal neural networks
abstract: As a tropical cash crop, the precise quality assessment of mangoes directly determines optimal harvest timing and supply chain efficiency. Premature harvesting results in insufficient flavor, while delayed harvesting leads to spoilage and decay. Traditional manual or static imaging methods suffer from high subjectivity and inability to capture the dynamic ripening process. To address this, we propose Mango Expert, an intelligent decision-support system integrating visible/near-infrared spectroscopy and impedance sensing via a flexible optoelectronic sensor network. The system combines EfficientNet-B1 for image feature extraction, a BiLSTM model with positional encoding for temporal modeling, and a Graph Attention Network (GAT) to dynamically model inter-fruit relationships. By fusing spectral and impedance data, our approach overcomes limitations of unimodal methods, achieving 98.54% classification accuracy, outperforming state-of-the-art techniques. Key innovations include adaptive graph construction and time-continuous batch sampling, which preserve biological correlations and enhance robustness. Deployed in real-world harvesting, the system reduces labor costs by 60% and increases premium fruit value by 20–30%. The system developed in this study demonstrates clear application value in precision fruit harvesting, providing a key tool for the fine-grained harvest decision-making in smart agriculture.

title: Cypnet enabled spatiotemporal modeling of UAV hyperspectral imagery for wheat yield prediction and drought tolerant genotype identification
abstract: Accurate yield prediction and rapid identification of drought tolerant genotypes are critical for wheat breeding under increasing water scarcity. Despite recent advances in UAV based hyperspectral remote sensing and deep learning, a major unresolved challenge remains the robust modeling of high dimensional hyperspectral data across multiple phenological stages, particularly in large and genetically diverse breeding populations. Existing approaches often fail to simultaneously capture spatial spectral features, temporal dynamics of crop growth, and the unequal contributions of different growth stages to yield formation, limiting their applicability for breeding-oriented decision making. Here, we developed a hybrid deep learning framework, termed CYPNet, that integrates convolutional neural networks, bidirectional long, short term memory networks, and a multi head self-attention mechanism to enable end-to-end learning and adaptive temporal fusion of multi-temporal unmanned aerial vehicles(UAV)hyperspectral data. Field experiments were conducted using 535 wheat genotypes (262 recombinant inbred line families and 273 natural populations) grown under irrigation and water efficiency conditions in the Huang Huai Hai Plain. Canopy hyperspectral imagery was acquired at four key phenological stages (heading, flowering, early filling, and mid filling). Results showed that multi temporal spectral fusion substantially improved yield prediction accuracy, with CYPNet achieving the highest performance when all stages were integrated (R2 = 0.73, RMSE = 0.75 t/ha, MAE = 0.57 t/ha), outperforming traditional machine learning models, including optimized support vector regression (R2 = 0.62). Model performance exhibited environmental dependence, with slightly higher accuracy under irrigation than under water stress, reflecting increased spectral yield complexity under drought conditions. Importantly, yield predictions from CYPNet were further translated into a breeding-oriented decision framework by integrating drought resistance index, geometric mean productivity, and stress sensitivity index, enabling systematic ranking of drought tolerance across all genotypes. This framework identified 54 highly drought-tolerant wheat lines with stable performance and substantial yield potential, supported by high generalized heritability (H2 = 0.88). Collectively, this study addresses key methodological and application gaps in UAV based yield prediction by linking spatiotemporal hyperspectral modeling with quantitative drought resistance screening, providing a scalable and actionable phenotyping framework to accelerate genetic gain in wheat breeding under water limited environments.

title: Advancing site-specific disease and pest management in precision agriculture: From reasoning-driven foundation models to adaptive, feedback-based learning
abstract: Site-specific disease management (SSDM) in agricultural crops has witnessed tremendous advancements over the past few decades using conventional machine and deep learning (ML & DL) approaches for real-time computer vision applications. This research has evolved from handcrafted feature extraction to large-scale automated feature learning in single-modality datasets. However, with the rise of foundation models (FMs), the way large-scale crop disease datasets are processed is being fundamentally transformed. Unlike convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which are inherently single-modality architectures and require post-fusion strategies to integrate heterogenous data streams, vision-language FMs provide unified embedding spaces where visual and textual representations are jointly learned from the same training dataset. This enables richer, more coherent cross-modal reasoning, allowing models to interpret disease symptoms described in text, infer relationships between symptoms and management factors, and support interactive Q&A platforms for growers and extension educators. Beyond visual and textual reasoning, FMs are also serving as backbone architectures for robotic perception and decision-making, bridging the gap between scene understanding and physical action in field environments. In this context, the integration of adaptive, imitation, and reinforcement learning (AL, IL, & RL) in robotics is enabling novel applications for field-based disease management. Therefore, this study reviewed ≈40 research articles to highlight the application of FMs for SSDM in crops, focusing on two primary themes: large-language models (LLMs), and vision language models (VLMs). Additionally, the extended role of FMs in enabling AL, IL, RL, and digital twin (DT) frameworks for robotics-based targeted spraying is also discussed. Based on the results and discussion, several key conclusions emerge from this review: (a) FMs are gaining traction, with a notable increase in reported technical literature during 2023-2024, (b) VLMs are being leveraged more than LLMs, with a five-to-tenfold increase in published articles from 2023 to 2024, (c) RL and AL remain in their infancy for developing smart spraying technologies that learn from experience, (d) integrating DTs with RL in cyber-physical systems offer a transformative approach for simulating targeted spraying in virtual environments, (e) addressing sim-to-real gap, the performance drop when models trained in simulated environments are deployed in real-world disease scenarios, will be critical for robust and scalable management systems, (f) while perception models for disease detection are advancing, human-robot collaboration and human-in-the-loop (HiTL) approaches remain underexplored in field-scale crop disease management systems where robots autonomously detect early symptoms and humans validate uncertain cases, and (g) continued advancements in FMs. Multi-modal integration, and real-time feedback are expected to drive the next generation of SSDM technologies.

title: Energy-Saving performance of Kalman filtering and artificial neural network algorithm for axle torque and battery SOC estimation of electric tractor using AMESim model
abstract: Electric tractors operate under highly variable soil resistance conditions during tillage, which induces rapid axle torque fluctuations and increases battery energy consumption when conventional motor controllers respond rely solely on delayed feedback. This study evaluated the energy-saving performance of a filtering-algorithm-integrated proportional–integral–derivative (PID) motor speed controller for a 19 kW single-motor electric tractor during plow tillage across three gear stages (L-2500, L-2800, and M−2000). For this, a one-dimensional electric tractor simulation model was developed in AMESim, incorporating motor torque–speed–voltage characteristics, efficiency maps, drivetrain components, and field-measured tillage load datasets. A Kalman Filter Algorithm (KFA) was integrated into the PID control framework to estimate axle torque and battery state of charge (SOC) in real time, and its performance was compared with an artificial neural network (ANN)-based estimator and a conventional PID controller without predictive filtering. Simulation results revealed that the KFA-integrated controller improved torque-estimation accuracy, suppressed transient overshoot, and stabilized motor-current response under dynamically varying field loads. Relative to the ANN and conventional PID controllers, the KFA-based controller maintained motor operation closer to the high-efficiency region and reduced battery energy consumption by approximately 0.38%, 0.42%, and 0.53% at L-2500, L-2800, and M−2000, respectively. These findings affirm that KFA-based predictive workload estimation enhances control stability and energy efficiency across gear stages, supporting the applicability of the proposed controller for next-generation electric tractors under energy-intensive tillage conditions.

title: Generative diffusion models for agricultural AI: Plant image generation, indoor-to-outdoor translation, and expert preference alignment
abstract: Agricultural AI is often constrained by limited, imbalanced plant image datasets and pronounced domain shift when models trained on controlled indoor imagery are deployed in field conditions. To address these challenges, we propose an integrated diffusion-based framework with three components that can be used independently or as complementary stages: (1) text-conditioned plant image synthesis to expand labeled training data, (2) indoor-to-outdoor image translation to mitigate domain shift, and (3) expert preference-aligned fine-tuning to improve agronomic realism and output stability. Our implementation builds on a Stable Diffusion v1.4 backbone fine-tuned with our domain-specific image dataset, which is then served as the base model for the image-translation module using the DreamBooth strategy. The fine-tuned generative model is further optimized by a reward-weighted mechanism using expert scores to refine image quality. We evaluate the framework using standard generative metrics (IS, FID) and downstream agricultural tasks, including phenotype classification and weed detection with YOLOv8. Results indicate that the components are synergistic: the synthesis model provides a strong initialization for translation, translation improves field realism while retaining utility for data augmentation, and preference alignment further enhances consistency and expert-perceived quality. Overall, the proposed framework offers a practical, data-efficient, and expert-aware generative pipeline for real-world agricultural AI.

title: Multi-source remote sensing of banana LAI across full growth cycle using canopy spectral-morphological features and temporal Transformer-LSTM
abstract: Accurate estimating of banana leaf area index (LAI) is essential for growth monitoring and yield assessment, yet dense canopy three-dimension (3D) structure and temporal dynamics challenge remote sensing approaches. We propose a banana LAI estimation method based on multi-source remote sensing data fusion and a Transformer-LSTM temporal deep learning model. We develop a Regional Volume (RV) metric, a refined morphological parameter that excludes the void space beneath the dense banana canopy. Vegetation indices (VIs), texture features (TFs), and canopy morphological parameters (CMPs) are extracted from UAV multispectral imagery and terrestrial LiDAR point clouds. The hybrid Transformer-LSTM model was developed for banana LAI estimation throughout the eight growth stages, based on VIs, TFs, CMPs and their combinations. The results demonstrate the superior capability of the proposed RV metric over the conventional canopy height volume (CV) for LAI estimation, improving the testing R2 by over 0.14 to 0.878 with an RMSE of 0.72. Meanwhile, the Transformer-LSTM models using feature combinations (VIs + TFs, VIs + CMPs, VIs + TFs + CMPs) achieved better performance than those using single features (VIs, TFs, CMPs), with the VIs + CMPs combination yielding the highest accuracy (R2 > 0.93, RMSE < 0.52). The Transformer-LSTM model effectively captured both temporal dynamics and global dependencies, achieving optimal performance for banana LAI estimation on the full-cycle dataset (testing R2 = 0.951, RMSE = 0.458). Additionally, the model maintained stable performance across all growth stages, with testing R2 exceeding 0.93 at the seedling stage and reaching nearly 0.90 at the flowering stage while maintaining RMSE as low as 0.3. This study presents a reliable approach for accurate banana LAI estimation across the full growth cycle through the integration of the improved RV parameter and a temporal deep learning model.

title: Towards automated insect farming: A robust control framework for yield optimization and resource management in black soldier fly larvae rearing
abstract: To maximize biomass production and economic efficiency in the industrial rearing of Black Soldier Fly Larvae (BSFL), precise control of the production environment is required. This paper presents a robust hierarchical control framework designed to automate and optimize the BSFL rearing process. The proposed architecture consists of a supervisory upper level that generates climate trajectories, balancing trade-offs between optimal larval growth and operational costs derived from energy pricing and local weather forecasts. A lower-level Deep Reinforcement Learning controller ensures precise tracking of the trajectories despite potential actuator malfunctions. To address BSFL biological variability, a Moving Horizon Estimation algorithm is employed to estimate unmeasured states — specifically, current biomass of the larvae — and strain-specific parameters using only standard medium temperature and moisture measurements. This estimation capability allows the framework to dynamically re-optimize trajectories to correct for growth deviations, rendering the system robust to larval strains with uncharacterized responses to specific climatic variables, such as metabolic fluctuations under varying temperature and moisture gradients. Results demonstrate that this adaptive approach enhances production efficiency, yielding a projected revenue increase of up to 27.6%, representing a significant advancement in computational agriculture and offering a scalable solution for fully automated, profit-optimized insect farming.

title: EnvGreenAE: A denoising-enhanced transformer autoencoder for greenhouse anomaly detection
abstract: Timely and reliable anomaly detection is critical for intelligent greenhouse systems, as abnormal environmental conditions will adversely affect crop growth and yield. However, greenhouse anomaly detection remains particularly challenging, as environmental variables exhibit strong coupling and are simultaneously influenced by biological processes, management operations, and external meteorological conditions, producing complex spatiotemporal dynamics. To address these challenges, two key observations motivate this work. First, greenhouse variables form a coupled system, necessitating full-environment multivariate detection rather than single-variable analysis. Second, reconstruction-based modeling is more appropriate than forecasting for greenhouse monitoring, as it captures normal patterns without predicting complex environmental changes, thus avoiding overfitting to noise and minor fluctuations in the data. Based on these, EnvGreenAE, a self-supervised autoencoder framework with denoising enhancement, is proposed. The model integrates a Transformer encoder for capturing long-range temporal dependencies and inter-variable relationships, a dilated temporal decoder to extract multi-scale features for reconstruction, and a denoising training strategy to improve robustness against noise. The overall architecture is intentionally lightweight, as greenhouse data are typically limited in scale but rich in inter-variable correlations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EnvGreenAE outperforms a range of state-of-the-art baselines across various evaluation metrics, achieving a precision of 0.9410, recall of 0.9738, accuracy of 0.9797, and F1-score of 0.9571. In summary, EnvGreenAE offers a robust solution for anomaly detection in intelligent agriculture, supporting timely responses to microclimate variations and contributing to the stability and efficiency of data-driven greenhouse management.

title: Automated sea cage geometry detection from 3D multibeam sonar using machine learning
abstract: Reliable interpretation of acoustic observations in aquaculture systems requires accurate knowledge of the spatial structure being monitored. In flexible sea cages, geometric deformation under varying hydrodynamic conditions alters the spatial reference frame used to analyse sensor data and can lead to errors in automated monitoring and analysis. This study presents an automated, data-driven approach for detecting sea cage geometry directly from 3D multibeam sonar observations collected at a commercial salmon farm. The approach combines time-synchronised acoustic measurements with physics-based simulation-derived reference geometries and trains a 3D convolutional neural network to infer cage geometry from sonar data alone. The final implementation was developed in PyTorch using supervised training on matched sonar–geometry pairs. Validation results show strong agreement between predicted and reference cage geometries, with overlap-based similarity values in the range of approximately 0.93–0.94. These results demonstrate that cage geometry can be inferred directly from sonar observations without relying on external deformation sensors during operation. The proposed method provides a non-invasive and scalable approach for real-time cage-scale monitoring and supports downstream applications such as fish behaviour analysis, biomass interpretation, and precision aquaculture decision support.

title: SMART: Structured multimodal agricultural retrieval-augmented transformer for plant disease diagnosis
abstract: Real-world plant disease diagnosis requires robustness to long-tailed class distributions and variable input quality, yet prevailing multimodal approaches do not explicitly address these challenges. This study presents SMART, a framework that integrates structured linguistic guidance with retrieval-augmented inference. Evaluation of 37,586 images across 48 disease categories yields three findings. First, structured captions outperform LLM-generated narratives, with the vision-only baseline exceeding all LLM approaches on the 20-class pilot, demonstrating that semantic precision, not descriptive complexity, drives effective vision-language alignment. Second, we distinguish between training-time and inference-time challenges: long-tailed degradation is mitigated through asymmetric loss design, while input quality variability is addressed through a dual-pathway mechanism in which semantic anchoring constrains predictions under related errors, and the retrieval-based safety net ensures bounded degradation under noisy inputs. Third, frequency-stratified analysis reveals a division of labor: semantic anchoring benefits high-frequency classes, while the retrieval-based safety net preferentially compensates rare classes. These complementary mechanisms support a human-in-the-loop workflow that transforms single-pass diagnosis into collaborative verification. SMART achieves F1 = 0.9767, surpassing fine-tuned CNNs (best F1 = 0.9118) and 22 multimodal foundation models (best F1 = 0.8904). The primary contributions of this work are: (i) a systematic benchmark of caption form-structured versus LLM-generated as an experimental variable in agricultural vision-language alignment; (ii) a factorial decomposition that quantitatively isolates the independent and complementary roles of semantic anchoring and retrieval-based compensation across frequency strata; and (iii) a statistically validated, human-in-the-loop diagnostic framework applicable to large-scale, imbalanced disease taxonomies.

title: Hail damage assessment in tomato crops using UAV-based vegetation indices and machine learning-based regression
abstract: Hailstorms are extreme weather events that severely damage plants and reduce crop yields. Traditional hail simulations often use leaf defoliation to assess plant damage, but hail damage is typically classified into several categories. In this study, we simulated eight hail scenarios on tomato plants using water-absorbed and frozen pumice stones of various sizes and quantities to replicate real hail. These simulations were conducted at four developmental stages of the tomato plant. We calculated 62 vegetation indices before and after each simulation. The percentage of hail damage was then estimated using six machine learning regression models and five feature selection methods, including correlation, ReliefF, LASSO, Random Forest Feature Importance (RFFI), and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE). The combination of RFE and the Random Forest model provided the most accurate estimates, with a Pearson correlation coefficient (R) of 0.9019, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.7287, and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 5.6991.

title: An interpretable framework using foundation models for fish sex identification
abstract: Accurate sex identification in fish is vital for optimizing breeding and management strategies in aquaculture, particularly for species at the risk of extinction. However, most existing methods are invasive or stressful and may cause additional mortality, posing severe risks to threatened or endangered fish populations. To address these challenges, we propose FishProtoNet, a robust, non-invasive computer vision–based framework for sex identification of delta smelt ( Hypomesus transpacificus ), an endangered fish species native to California, across its full life cycle. Unlike the traditional deep learning methods, FishProtoNet provides interpretability through learned prototype representations while improving robustness by leveraging foundation models to reduce the influence of background noise. Specifically, the FishProtoNet framework consists of three key components: fish regions of interest (ROIs) extraction using visual foundation model, feature extraction from fish ROIs and fish sex identification based on an interpretable prototype network. FishProtoNet demonstrates strong performance in delta smelt sex identification during early spawning and post-spawning stages, achieving the accuracies of 74.40% and 81.16% and corresponding F1 scores of 74.27% and 79.43% respectively. In contrast, delta smelt sex identification at the subadult stage remains challenging for current computer vision methods, likely due to less pronounced morphological differences in immature fish. The source code of FishProtoNet is publicly available at: https://github.com/zhengmiao1/fish_gender_recognition.git .

title: Adaptive rotary tillage depth control with RBF-ADRC based on time-series prediction of tractor chassis pitch angle
abstract: To mitigate tillage-depth fluctuations induced by surface undulations and actuator nonlinearities in horticultural electric tractors, this study develops a predictive depth control method. A novel MSCNN–BiLSTM–Attention model is constructed to forecast pitch-angle variations. It utilizes multi-scale convolution to extract disturbance features across different temporal scales, while bidirectional temporal modeling combined with a multi-head attention mechanism enhances temporal representations. Model hyperparameters are optimized using an improved beluga whale optimization algorithm. The predicted pitch angle is integrated as feedforward compensation into the control loop. By fusing this prediction with a rotary-tillage kinematic model, future tillage depth is estimated, enabling the design of an RBF-based active disturbance rejection controller (RBF-ADRC) for adaptive compensation of system nonlinearities and time-varying disturbances. The proposed prediction model achieved MAE and RMSE of 0.0526° and 0.0686°, respectively, with a test-set R2 of 0.9931, and errors primarily within ± 0.03°. Simulations demonstrated that the proposed prediction-assisted control strategy outperforms RBFPID, optimal sliding mode, and model predictive controllers under step, sinusoidal, and slope disturbances, achieving zero overshoot, a steady-state error of 0.001 cm, and reduced dynamic errors. Greenhouse field experiments further validated the method, yielding average tillage depths of 4.03, 8.14, and 11.59 cm against targets of 4, 8, and 12 cm, with maximum fluctuations of approximately 0.6 cm. Overall, this deep learning-based predictive feedforward strategy significantly improves tillage-depth stability and control precision under complex surface conditions, providing a practical solution for intelligent electric tractors in protected horticulture.

title: Joint prediction of potato yield and nitrogen status at row closure using multi-task deep learning and UAV-derived LiDAR–multispectral data
abstract: • Fused UAV multispectral and LiDAR data quantified potato canopy structure and petiole nitrate-N at row closure. • Joint modelling of yield and petiole nitrate-N improved predictive performance compared with single-task approaches. • LiDAR height and structural metrics added complementary information to multispectral predictors. • Single-date UAV data at the row-closure stage were sufficient for nitrogen prediction but less informative for yield. • Feature attribution analyses indicated physiologically consistent relationships between canopy structure and nitrogen status.

title: Development and validation of an interpretable EEG-based deep learning framework for estrus detection in dairy cows
abstract: Electroencephalographic (EEG) signals exhibit stable and reproducible differences between estrus and non-estrus dairy cows, indicating that central nervous system activity reflects estrus-related regulation beyond external behavioral expression. Analysis across multiple EEG domains shows that estrus-associated neural modulation involves coordinated changes across frequency bands and recording channels and remains identifiable under varying behavioral conditions. Using multi-channel EEG recordings collected from 90 dairy cows, estrus detection was evaluated in a cross-subject evaluation, in which training and testing were conducted on data from different individuals. Under this evaluation protocol, the EEG-based approach achieved an accuracy of 92.7 ± 1.5%, an area under the curve of 94.0 ± 1.4%, a sensitivity of 94.1 ± 1.4%, and a specificity of 95.4 ± 1.3%, demonstrating robust discrimination across individuals rather than reliance on individual-specific neural patterns. Comparative model evaluation under unified experimental conditions indicates that appropriate feature representation and modeling strategies consistently capture estrus-related neural patterns. Attention-based interpretability analysis further reveals that EEG frequency bands contribute unequally to estrus discrimination, with low-frequency components, particularly the delta band, exhibiting the highest and most stable contribution across behavioral conditions. These results support EEG as a physiologically meaningful and interpretable information source for cross-individual estrus detection in dairy cows.

title: Data-driven optimization of CO2 regulation intervals in controlled environment agriculture
abstract: Precision carbon regulation in controlled environment agriculture (CEA) is essential for promoting crop growth and enhancing energy use efficiency. However, existing CO2 regulation strategies are predominantly based on fixed setpoints or empirically defined intervals, which fail to adequately capture nonlinear crop physiological responses, environmental interactions, and multiobjective trade-offs under practical conditions. To address these issues, this study formulates a data-driven CO2 regulation optimization problem and proposes a hybrid optimization framework. First, a support vector regression-based photosynthetic rate (Pn) model is developed to provide quantitative feedback for regulation design. Second, a biologically-informed constrained non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II is designed to identify feasible CO2 regulation intervals under physiological and operational constraints, improving both convergence efficiency and solution quality. Third, a hybrid decision-making module integrates the best-worst method for weight determination and the measurement of alternatives and ranking according to compromise solution method for solution ranking, enabling robust selection from the Pareto-optimal set. Comprehensive comparative and ablation experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Compared with Pn maximum strategies, the proposed method reduced Pn by 17.48% while significantly improving CO2 utilization efficiency (CUE) by 42.16%. It also achieves comparable Pn and CUE with lower CO2 input and fewer device activations than threshold-based strategies. Real-world validation shows reductions of over 40% in CO2 supplementation frequency and 16% in total CO2 dosage. Additional experiments on cucumber and eggplant further demonstrate the transferability of the proposed framework across crop types. Overall, this study provides an extensible solution for sustainable CO2 management in CEA systems.

title: An intelligent data-driven framework for optimizing wheat management toward high yields with reduced nitrogen inputs
abstract: Achieving a balance between high and stable wheat yields and reduced nitrogen inputs remains a major challenge for sustainable agriculture. To address the limited generalizability of current nitrogen management models across environment and management gradients, this study develops an AI- and data-driven decision framework for wheat based on a harmonized global field trial database. The framework is built on datasets compiled from published field experiments and integrates two modeling solutions (AutoGluon and TabPFN) to predict and optimize wheat yield and nitrogen uptake across different climate zones. The models exhibit strong performance and robustness, with an R 2 of 0.88 and an RMSE of 26.3 kg N·ha⁻ 1 for predicted nitrogen uptake and an R 2 of 0.82 and an RMSE of 865.9 kg DM·ha⁻ 1 for predicted yield. Scenario analysis shows that nitrogen application can be reduced by 13% while maintaining yield, and that improved management can increase average yield by 19.6% while reducing nitrogen application by 18.2%, demonstrating the potential for multi-factor synergistic optimization. Analysis of management contributions using sensitivity analysis and Shapley decomposition revealed that improvements in nitrogen application methods and forms, as well as multiple applications, had the greatest impact on yield enhancement. Shapley decomposition further validated these conclusions and quantified the relative contributions of each management factor under multi-factor conditions. Overall, this study provides quantitative evidence that AI-driven management can identify agronomic interventions that increase yields while reducing nitrogen inputs, thereby informing scalable, environment-specific decision frameworks for wheat production.
