title: Physics-Informed Neural Network methods for predicting plant height development
abstract: ABSTRACT Plant growth is a dynamic process affected by genes and growing environment, with all kinds of interactions between them. These complex relationships make the prediction of plant growth challenging. We propose a hybrid modelling framework that combines a logistic ordinary differential equation model with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network, resulting in a Physics Informed Neural Network (PINN). While PINNs have been widely applied to physical dynamical systems, their use in modelling the dynamics of plant growth systems is still largely unexplored. We illustrate the construction of a PINN on plant height data in wheat and compare its performance with alternative models for longitudinal plant data. All temporal prediction models only require time and temperature as input. Among a set of competing models, our PINN had the lowest average root mean squared error (RMSE) of prediction and the smallest standard deviation across multiple random initialisations. Therefore, we conclude that incorporating biological growth constraints into data-driven growth models can enhance prediction accuracy of longitudinal plant traits. Highlights Integrating plant growth equations into a temporal neural network improves plant height growth prediction over ordinary differential equations and machine learning models, especially when training data are limited.

title: Quality-aware generative distillation for robust and efficient livestock detection
abstract: Vision-based livestock monitoring in open pastures confronts two distinct bottlenecks: a quality problem—severe image degradation from variable illumination (e.g., nighttime, strong snow reflection) yields abundant but low-quality frames—and a scarcity problem—extreme weather events (e.g., heavy snow, rain) are rare, leaving few training samples for such critical conditions. Generative image editors can in principle enhance degraded inputs and synthesize rare scenarios. However, unsupervised generation frequently introduces semantic artifacts and geometric distortions; naïvely incorporating these corrupted samples into training misleads detectors and degrades performance. To harness generative data reliably while meeting edge-device constraints, we propose a quality-aware generative distillation framework. First, a dual-branch editing pipeline—built on the large-scale instruction-driven editor Qwen-Image-Edit—restores visibility in low-quality inputs (enhancement branch) and simulates diverse adverse-weather views from clear daytime images (style-edit branch), addressing both quality and scarcity issues at the data level. Second, because generative outputs are unreliable, we design a multi-metric quality assessment module combining perceptual similarity (LPIPS), region-of-interest edge consistency, and CLIP-based semantic alignment to automatically filter corrupted edits before training. Third, to avoid deploying heavy generative models at inference, we train a robust teacher detector on this curated multi-domain dataset, then distill its localization features into a lightweight student via feature-level knowledge transfer; the student trains only on raw images, incurs no enhancement overhead at deployment, yet inherits cross-weather robustness. Experiments on our SnowLivestockDet dataset demonstrate that YOLOv11 and RT-DETR students achieve up to 12.5% mAP@50–95 improvement on adverse-weather subsets compared to single-domain baselines, validating the effectiveness of quality-aware generative distillation.

title: Automated homogeneity-check of agricultural parcels using machine learning: increased performance in compliance with EU common agricultural policy
abstract: Accurate assessments of agricultural parcel geometries are crucial for calculating financial subsidies. Today, authorities use aerial images to check parcels for homogeneous cultivation and incorrect parcel geometries (homogeneity-check). Due to the large number of parcels and the limited resources in authority offices, there is a need for an automated method of preselecting a manageable sample of parcels for manual review. To this end, this study introduces (i) a novel method for automated homogeneity-check including (ii) a user utility metric reflecting its ability to preselect presumably heterogeneous parcels, i.e., those that benefit from manual review. The new is metric (ii), called Precision of Prioritized Items (PPI), was used to evaluate the performance of four machine learning approaches for homogeneity checking (i): Image Classification, Semantic Segmentation, Edge Detection, and Clustering. Moreover, the evaluation also assessed the robustness of these approaches regarding image resolution. The results show that all approaches performed similarly in terms of the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and the PPI metric; Image Classification: AUROC = 77.4%, PPI = 90%, Semantic Segmentation AUROC = 83.0%, PPI = 100%, Edge Detection: AUROC = 79.2%, PPI = 90%, and Clustering: AUROC = 84.4%, PPI = 100%. However, only the Clustering approach consistently maintained a stable PPI of 100%, regardless of image resolution, demonstrating superior robustness. The implementation of the Clustering approach enabled the authorities to improve their performance in this task by 294% from 2023 to 2024.

title: Mapping Alpine pasture biomass and nutritional value from hyperspectral field and spaceborne sensors
abstract: Pastures are important components of Alpine cultural landscapes. However, due to unbalanced grazing pressure and climate change, the quality of pastures is degrading, diminishing their capacity to deliver essential ecosystem services and leading to widespread abandonment. Adaptive grazing management practices can address the challenge of under- or over-exploitation of pasture resources, balancing livestock forage demand and pasture productivity. This study evaluates the capabilities of spaceborne hyperspectral data for mapping pasture productivity and nutritional characteristics (i.e. biomass, protein and fiber content) in mid- to high-elevation Alpine environments. Agronomic and reflectance data (350-2500 nm) were collected in the field across different vegetation phenological stages for 128 pasture samples in two distinct Alpine regions. Field spectra were convoluted to simulate satellite PRISMA hyperspectral and Sentinel-2 multispectral sensor configurations, both used to calibrate and validate Gaussian Process Regression machine learning models. Hyperspectral-based models significantly outperformed multispectral-based ones, with an average R c v 2 improvement of 58.05% and an average R M S E c v reduction of 9.83% ( R c v 2 : 0.67, R M S E c v : 225.79 g m − 2 for AGB; R c v 2 : 0.55, R M S E c v : 1.87 % for CP; R c v 2 : 0.65, R M S E c v : 1.71 % for ADF; R c v 2 : 0.62, R M S E c v : 2.66 % for NDF). The best-performing models were demonstrated on a real PRISMA scene, and the estimations were evaluated against in-situ data, showing overall good agreement (average R 2 of 0.60 and average rRMSE of 11%) and high coherence with spatial patterns induced by pasture composition, grazing and topography. Our results confirm the potential of current (e.g., PRISMA, EnMAP) and upcoming operational hyperspectral missions (e.g., ESA’s CHIME) for regional forage biomass and nutritional quality assessment.

title: Semantic metadata extraction from crop model components with large language models to facilitate platform interoperability
abstract: Process-based crop models encapsulate agro-ecosystem knowledge in modular components, yet structural heterogeneity across platforms limits component reuse and demands manual curation of semantic metadata, which is error-prone and time consuming. Here, we present a workflow that leverages large language models (LLMs) to automatically create Crop2ML model specifications by extracting input/output variables specifications and by generating descriptions, from source code written in three different languages among six simulation platforms. Evaluation on eight soil temperature components from six widely used platforms and on 31 various components from three platforms showed F1-Score above 93% for input/output variables extraction. The workflow successfully inferred plausible metadata when documentation was ambiguous or incomplete. These findings demonstrate that LLM-assisted extraction can accelerate the creation of interoperable, semantically rich model documentation while preserving accuracy, thereby lowering the barrier to crop model reuse.

title: Unified nitrogen diagnosis in winter oilseed rape (Brassica napus L.): Integrating Bayesian critical N dilution curves and fractional-order three-dimensional spectral indices
abstract: Unified and management-oriented nitrogen (N) diagnosis in mulched dryland crops requires a physiologically consistent baseline that can support consistent interpretation across tested management scenarios and be retrieved non-destructively. To address this, we conducted multi-season field experiments on winter oilseed rape (Brassica napus L.) on the Loess Plateau using three mulching treatments (no mulching, straw mulching, and film mulching) and five N rates (0–280 kg N ha−1). Specifically, we aimed to integrate Bayesian physiological modeling with hyperspectral sensing. Aboveground dry matter (DM), leaf N concentration (LNC), canopy hyperspectral reflectance, and seed yield were measured across key growth stages. A Bayesian framework was used to estimate the critical N dilution relationship and quantify parameter uncertainty, supporting pooling across years and mulching treatments (posterior probability of practically negligible differences > 0.95). The resulting unified critical curve was LNCc = 35.732 × DM−0.15, enabling a consistent nitrogen nutrition index (NNI) threshold interpretation across mulching scenarios. To enable rapid diagnosis, canopy spectra were transformed using 0.8-order fractional derivatives, and tri-band three-dimensional spectral indices were optimized to predict NNI with machine learning. The best model (XGBoost) achieved R2 = 0.682 with RMSE = 0.092 on a held-out validation set. Agronomically, film mulching increased mean seed yield by ∼ 31.6% relative to no mulching, and yield response exhibited a clear N plateau: FMN3 produced yields only 1.05%–1.74% lower than FMN4 while reducing N input by 25%. The spectral NNI showed a consistent linear–plateau relationship with relative yield, with the plateau occurring near NNI ≈ 1.0. Overall, combining Bayesian Nc–NNI standardization with hyperspectral NNI retrieval provides a unified, management-oriented pathway for N diagnosis within the tested multi-year mulching conditions; however, further external validation across sites, cultivars, and independent years is still required, together with additional assessment of phenology-specific spectral bias, canopy vertical N redistribution, and uncertainty associated with large 3D-OSI feature screening.

title: A multisource weakly supervised high-resolution crop mapping framework based on low-resolution noise labels
abstract: High-resolution (HR) crop maps are the foundation data for conducting precise agricultural monitoring and land use change analysis. However, HR crop mapping remains hindered by costly manual annotations, label noise from low resolution (LR) products, convolutional neural network (CNN) architectural limitations, and spatial-spectral constraints of single source remote sensing imagery. LR crop classification products serve as cost-effective weak supervision but introduce geometric and semantic label noise. Conventional CNNs struggle with preserving fine spatial details and modeling long-range contexts, while data-level multi-source fusion blurs parcel boundaries. To address these issues, we propose a multisource weakly supervised crop classification framework (MSWCF) that utilizes LR products to guide HR mapping. The MSWCF features dual parallel branches: the HR branch extracts parcel boundaries, while the LR branch captures semantic information. Each branch integrates spatial resolution preserving and Vision Transformer modules to concurrently extract local details and global contexts. A cross-attention module (CAM) adaptively fuses these features, while a noise label removal module suppresses boundary and semantic errors in LR labels. Experiments were conducted in Heilongjiang Province, China. Results show that MSWCF achieves superior performance (Overall Accuracy = 93.8 %) surpassing state-of-the-art baselines. Cross-spatiotemporal application indicates that it has generalization capabilities. Ablation studies confirm that the dual-branch structure and CAM fusion effectively utilize spatial-spectral information, preventing boundary smoothing. Feature visualization verifies that SRP focuses on boundaries while ViT captures global objects. MSWCF enables accurate, fine-grained crop mapping without manual annotations, validating its practicality for largescale HR crop mapping.

title: A trajectory prediction method for vibrating fruits based on the LSTM-DA-iTransformer fusion model
abstract: In the process of intelligent fruit harvesting, the vibrations caused by external disturbances significantly affect the robot’s ability to quickly grasp the fruit. Accurately predicting the trajectory of the vibrating fruit is crucial for efficient grasping. However, traditional trajectory prediction models often struggle to achieve an effective balance between dynamic adaptability and long-term sequence prediction accuracy. To address this issue, this paper proposes a hybrid model—LSTM-DA-iTransformer. The model utilizes LSTM to capture local temporal features and integrates a Differential Attention Mechanism (DA) module to dynamically optimize attention weights in real time, adapting to variations in the vibration amplitude of the fruit. Additionally, the iTransformer strengthens long-term sequence dependency modeling to effectively mitigate the vanishing gradient problem. Moreover, to further improve the model’s prediction accuracy and performance, the dataset was feature-adjusted by replacing position features with the position increments between time steps and timestamp features with the time differences between time steps. This adjustment helps avoid the impact of large-scale position features on model training and accelerates model convergence. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model delivers superior performance in long-term sequence prediction tasks spanning 3 to 5 s. Specifically, within the 4-second time window, the Average Displacement Error (ADE) registers at 1.5475 cm, representing reductions of 41.6 %, 30.2 %, and 43.3 % relative to the GRU, BiLSTM, and Transformer models, respectively. In the 5-second time window, the Final Displacement Error (FDE) amounts to 2.2185 cm, marking a decrease of 22.7 % to 39.2 % compared with the baseline models, alongside a 33.8 % to 48.3 % reduction in the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). Additionally, ablation experiments rigorously verify the essentiality of each integrated module; notably, the DA module yields a remarkable improvement in prediction accuracy under complex vibrational scenarios.

title: Dead pine tree detection using an iterative semi-supervised framework integrating expert annotation and active learning
abstract: Pine wilt disease (PWD) poses a severe threat to forest ecosystems and resources, and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing combined with deep learning (DL) has become a widely used approach for its detection. However, DL-based methods typically rely on large-scale labeled datasets, while semi-supervised learning (SSL) still faces a key limitation in practice: the lack of a principled strategy for determining optimal annotation ratios, often leading to either insufficient supervision or unnecessary labeling cost, and existing static training schemes fail to adapt to dynamically evolving data distributions. To address this gap, we propose a human–machine interactive framework that integrates active learning (AL) with SSL through interactive training and expert-driven annotation. An AL method, object uncertainty sampling (OUS) strategy was employed to enhance annotation efficiency. Our results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves detection accuracy comparable to fully supervised approaches while using only 30 % of the labeled data (mAP = 64.9 %, mAP50 = 94.1 %), and improves performance by 3.1 %–11.4 % in mAP compared with other SSL methods. Moreover, when applied to new datasets, this method supports transfer learning, allowing the model to retain prior knowledge while improving performance on new data, with mAP and mAP50 reaching 55.32 % and 93.3 %, respectively. By integrating automated learning with expert judgment, it reduces manual effort and achieves optimal detection with minimal annotation. Additionally, the proposed strategy exhibits cross-model generalization and can be combined with multiple object detection models, including SSD, YOLOv12, and DETR, enhancing the performance of baseline models while reducing annotation requirements. This approach offers a novel perspective on PWD detection and control and demonstrates strong potential for broader applications in diverse object recognition and detection scenarios.

title: A generative compressed sensing-based method for reconstructing in-situ soil monitoring data
abstract: In-situ soil monitoring systems typically operate autonomously in field conditions, where hourly measurements consume substantial energy and accelerate equipment degradation. Compressed sensing (CS) can mitigate these issues through low-frequency sampling and subsequent reconstruction without sacrificing monitoring accuracy. In agricultural and environmental fields, however, standard CS methods are constrained by a theoretical minimum sampling ratio of 20% to 30%. Meanwhile, generative compressed sensing (GCS) methods, which hold promise for addressing this limitation through deep neural networks, remain insufficiently studied. This study proposes a GCS-CVAE method to achieve ultra-low frequency sampling in soil monitoring and establish a methodological foundation for the development of soil monitoring systems. This method utilizes the decoder of a high-latent-dimensional convolutional variational autoencoder (CVAE) as a data reconstructor, coupled with a multiple-optimization strategy derived from GCS mechanism analysis. Experimental results on a soil moisture content (SMC) dataset demonstrate that GCS-CVAE outperforms existing CS and deep learning methods in both accuracy and stability. Notably, it can reconstruct hourly SMC series at highly reduced sampling rates of 10% and 15%, achieving average R2 values that exceed 0.8 and 0.9, respectively. For future deployment, GCS-CVAE can be integrated with wireless sensor networks or the Internet of Things via asynchronous sampling and multi-node collaboration to alleviate temporal feature loss during sparse sampling.

title: Planar array radar–capacitive multi-sensor fusion for powdery organic fertilizer flow rate monitoring
abstract: The rational partial substitution of chemical fertilizers by organic fertilizers has turned out to be mainstream fertilization practice in contemporary crop production. With the advent of Precision Agriculture, one can now find growing research work involving monitoring outflow rate or discharge flow rate of granular fertilizers through sensing and computing methodologies. However, monitoring solutions for powdery fertilizers are not completely researched. A multi-source data fusion monitoring system comprising Planar Array Radar, Capacitive measurement chip, and rotational speed sensor was conceived in this work to fill such a void. Six Machine Learning (ML) models—including XGBoost (XGB), Random Forest (RF), Extremely Randomized Trees (ET), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP)—were employed to develop two prediction models: one involving Filling Coefficient of fertilizer as well as one involving discharge flow rate of powdery organic fertilizer. XGBoost (XGB) and SVR showed optimum prediction ability among them all, with Coefficient of Determination (R2) achieving 0.904 and 0.958 and Root Mean Squared Errors (RMSE) achieving 0.058 and 0.61, respectively. Experimental results showed that proposed models compress relative prediction error by as much as 29.85 % compared to traditional empirical formulas and therefore verify their robustness and precision. This study offers one new and feasible reference for non-intrusive real-time monitoring and precision regulation for powdery fertilizer dosing and catalyzes wider sustainable development in agriculture.

title: Optimized ensemble learning frameworks for early grain yield prediction in winter wheat using static and multitemporal multispectral UAV data
abstract: A stacked ensemble learning framework was developed leveraging the large-scale spatial and temporal diversity in a winter wheat breeding program. Multispectral data were collected from 1098 plots comprising 586 genetically diverse advanced breeding lines at tillering, stem elongation, reproductive, early grain filling, mid grain filling, and late dough stages. Raw spectral information, 28 vegetation indices and 16 grey-level co-occurrence matrices were used– both individually and in combination –to train five machine learning algorithms– elastic net , support vector regression , k-nearest neighbours , random forest , and extreme gradient boosting . Static and temporal models were trained for spatial interpolation and genetic extrapolation, followed by internal and external validation. Multispectral features showed stage-specific discriminatory power for separating yield groups, peaking between the reproductive and mid grain filling stages. Classification was limited by overlap between medium- and high-yielding groups. Models integrating multispectral data across growth stages outperformed all other strategies. Elastic net performed best overall, while support vector regression showed the most consistent ranking. Base learners achieved average prediction accuracy of 55.85 % and 46.00 %, with AUC values of 0.73 and 0.66 for internal and external validation, respectively. Selected base-learners were used for stacked elastic net ensemble learning, which increased overall prediction (∼18 %) and classification (∼7 %) accuracies, while reducing errors (∼10 %). These improvements were primarily attributed to reduced bias. Overall, this study presents a scalable machine learning framework trained and validated on an operational breeding program for data-driven UAV-assisted early generation selection, providing a methodological reference for future research and deployment.

title: An integrated SNR-adaptive diffusion model and lightweight dual-backbone network for orchard obstacle detection under dataset imbalance and edge deployment constraints
abstract: Accurate and real-time obstacle detection plays a critical role in ensuring the safety and operational reliability of orchard robots. However, existing detection frameworks are constrained by class imbalance prevalent in agricultural datasets, which degrades model performance, in addition to the high computational overhead associated with Transformer architectures, thereby hindering practical implementation in resource-limited edge platforms. To overcome these limitations, the present work introduces a framework that integrates a novel generative data augmentation strategy with a lightweight dual-backbone detection network. First, a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) adaptive normalization denoising diffusion probabilistic model (SNRA-DDPM) was designed to mitigate the scarcity of minority class samples. By incorporating an SNR-aware adaptive normalization mechanism, SNRA-DDPM dynamically regulates feature distributions according to noise intensity, thereby generating high-fidelity samples to effectively rebalance the dataset distribution. Second, a lightweight detector, DBFNet, was developed based on the Transformer architecture. This network employs a dual-backbone structure combining High-Performance Graphics Processing Unit Network version 2 (HGNetv2) with an improved Cross Stage Partial Darknet (CSPDarknet), designed to synergistically capture global semantic information and fine-grained frequency-domain features. Furthermore, a dual-backbone fusion (DFusion) module was designed to address the inherent feature heterogeneity between the two backbones. This module utilizes channel and position attention mechanisms to adaptively align and fuse these features, significantly enhancing cross-branch information interaction and feature complementarity. The experimental results showed that SNRA-DDPM obtained Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) scores of 42.8348 and 46.4346 for minority classes, including baskets and ladders, respectively, exceeding the performance of the standard DDPM. In detection tasks, DBFNet achieved an 88.21% mean Average Precision (mAP) and 208.79 frames per second (FPS) with only 34.1 giga floating-point operations (GFLOPs), surpassing the Real-Time DEtection TRansformer based on Residual Network-18 (RT-DETR-r18) baseline in both accuracy and efficiency. Notably, the integration of the SNRA-DDPM augmentation strategy further improved model accuracy. Deployment on a harvesting robot platform showed that the proposed method achieved an inference speed of 44.48 FPS at 640-pixel resolution using 16-bit floating-point (FP16) precision, corresponding to a 17.2% improvement over the baseline and confirming its real-time capability in orchards. These results demonstrate that integrating generative data augmentation with lightweight detection networks is both effective and engineering-feasible for alleviating data imbalance and enabling deployment on resource-constrained edge devices in agricultural vision tasks.

title: Machine learning–based decision support for harvest optimization in commercial microalgae photobioreactors: A field validation study
abstract: Operational decision-making in commercial microalgae cultivation remains largely heuristic despite the increasing availability of high-frequency farm data. In photobioreactor-based production systems, harvest fraction selection is a key management decision that affects short-term biomass recovery, culture stability, and overall production efficiency. This study presents a machine learning–based decision-support framework for optimizing harvest management in commercial tubular photobioreactors cultivating Nannochloropsis sp. The framework integrates three years of heterogeneous farm data, including operational logs, meteorological variables, and FlowCam (a digital imaging system used to measure microalgae concentration and cell morphology) data. A supervised regression approach was used to predict next-day post-harvest cell concentration, and several learning algorithms were evaluated. A Random Forest model achieved the best predictive performance (R2 = 0.705), demonstrating robust prediction under noisy commercial production conditions. The trained model was implemented in an inference module that evaluates candidate harvest fractions and recommends the fraction expected to maximize short-term biomass recovery. The system was validated in a four-week farm-scale experiment across 12 commercial photobioreactors (96 planned harvest events), comparing model-guided and operator-guided harvest decisions. While the machine learning–guided strategy achieved comparable productivity levels to expert human decision-making, it reduced variability. These results provide a successful proof-of-concept for the operational feasibility of a data-driven framework to stabilize and scale commercial microalgae management. These findings demonstrate the practical feasibility of integrating machine learning into daily farm operations as a hybrid human–AI decision-support layer. The proposed framework highlights the potential of data-driven decision systems to enhance stability and scalability in commercial microalgae photobioreactor production.

title: A generic framework for evaluating the effectiveness of bio-stabilization: Integrating data-driven and model-driven approaches
abstract: Single-dimensional assessments often fail to capture the coupled chemical and structural effects of bio-stabilization, defined here as biologically mediated soil strengthening and contaminant immobilization, on soil functionality. To address this limitation, this study develops an integrated framework to evaluate both the effectiveness and potential side effects of microbial-induced carbonate precipitation (MICP), a representative bio-stabilization technique based on microbially driven carbonate mineralization, at the pore scale. Multi-level and piecewise mixed-effects modeling demonstrates that MICP efficiency plays a dominant role in cadmium (Cd) immobilization and overall stabilization performance (β=−0.43,p<0.01). High-resolution micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) analysis shows that increasing bio-stabilization intensity reduces porosity from 51.0% to 46.9% and shifts the structural model index (SMI) from 2.111 to −2.617, accompanied by an increase in isolated pores and improved structural integrity. To overcome the limited data volume inherent to micro-CT imaging, a conditionally constrained deep generative model based on a conditional variational autoencoder and a Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (CVAE-WGAN-GP) is employed to support continuous analysis of pore-scale structural evolution. The results show that intensified bio-stabilization enhances anisotropy and pore network heterogeneity, while confining seepage to a few dominant flow channels, with potential implications for soil water retention and nutrient transport. Overall, the proposed framework provides a quantitative basis for optimizing bio-stabilization strategies and supporting risk-informed decision-making in sustainable soil remediation.

title: Advancing digital agri-food systems through integrated AI, robotics, IoT, and blockchain with a bibliometric analysis
abstract: Digital Agri-Food Systems (DAFS) are transforming agriculture by combining digital and intelligent technologies to enhance automation, traceability, and data-driven decisions. This study evaluates technical advancements in DAFS by examining 332 peer-reviewed articles retrieved from Scopus. Using a hybrid evidence-synthesis approach that integrates Systematic Mapping and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA), it enables wide theme coverage requiring thorough screening, explicit inclusion criteria, and repeatability. The study identifies dominant research trajectories, methodological trends, and cross-domain technological interactions spanning crop production, livestock systems, food safety, and supply chain management. The findings show a marked transition toward hybrid intelligent frameworks that merge multimodal sensing with advanced analytical models for real-time crop monitoring, early disease detection, yield forecasting, autonomous robotics, and verifiable supply chain traceability. Internet of Things (IoT) sensor networks and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based imaging continue to strengthen precision agriculture practices, while blockchain-enabled systems support transparency, trust, and fraud prevention. Additionally, bibliometric analysis reveals strong international collaboration clusters and rapidly expanding research in precision agriculture, agricultural robotics, and intelligent supply chains. Key challenges persist, such as limited datasets, inconsistent validation, high computational costs, and insufficient focus on cybersecurity. The study shows that advancing DAFS requires scalable, unified architectures linking artificial intelligence (AI)-driven decision tools, interoperable IoT systems, and secure blockchain technologies. The integration is essential for building resilient, efficient, and sustainability-driven agri-food systems.

title: Forecasting adult emergence dynamics of wood-boring pests using time-series X-ray imaging and deep learning
abstract: Forecasting adult emergence dynamics of wood-boring pests is critical for improving monitoring efficiency and optimizing control timing. However, because these insects remain concealed within tree trunks before emergence, conventional approaches cannot exploit empirically observed developmental dynamics, limiting both forecast reliability and temporal resolution. To address this, we developed a field-deployable, non-destructive forecasting framework that integrates portable X-ray radiography, deep learning-based life-stage discrimination, and developmental-lag mapping to predict adult emergence dynamics from concealed development. We acquired X-ray images of wood-boring pests inside infested logs and developed X-BorerStageNet, a lightweight two-class life-stage detector (larva vs. pupa-adult). X-BorerStageNet introduces two task-specific networks—a structure-preserving backbone, the Efficient Dual-Stream Fusion Network (EDSFNet), and a frequency-aware multi-scale encoder, the Spectral-Attentive Multi-Scale Fusion Network (SAMFNet)—comprising five novel modules in total. Within EDSFNet, the Anisotropic Pseudo-Shift Downsampling Module (APSDM) preserves directional structural cues during early downsampling, and the Dual-Stream Hierarchical Ghost Block (DSHGB) reduces redundancy via complementary parallel branches that jointly capture fine details and coarser context. Within SAMFNet, the Spectral-Enhanced MetaFormer Block (SEMFB) couples global attention with FFT-based spectral modulation to enhance pest contours while suppressing repetitive wood textures; the Progressive Hybrid Aggregation Module (PHAM) strengthens cross-scale integration through an anchor–refinement design; and Tri-Scale Focused Fusion (TSFF) fuses three adjacent feature scales to balance fine details with semantic context. The model achieves 66.3% AP50:95 and 92.8% AP50, exceeding the D-FINE-N baseline by 6.9 and 4.2 percentage points, respectively, with fewer parameters and fast inference. Applied to time-series X-ray monitoring of 9 infested logs, the framework recovered the pupation dynamics of 72 Anoplophora glabripennis individuals and translated them into emergence forecasts using a mean pupation-to-emergence interval of approximately 20 days. Predicted emergence dynamics closely matched observations at both 3-day (r = 0.913, WAPE = 0.278) and weekly (r = 0.972, WAPE = 0.167) scales, and accurately recovered key phenological landmarks, including emergence onset, peak timing, and the 10%, 50%, and 90% cumulative-emergence dates. This framework offers an effective and interpretable approach for forecasting wood-boring pest emergence dynamics, supporting early warning and timely control. Source code: https://github.com/bihaojie/X-BorerStageNet.

title: Fusion of keypoint detection and posture-aware correction for body measurement of dairy cattle
abstract: Accurate and efficient non-contact body measurement of dairy cattle is essential for Precision Livestock Farming (PLF), enabling data-driven monitoring, management, and genetic improvement. Keypoint-based computer vision methods offer a powerful approach to this task. However, two critical challenges hinder its effective implementation: (1) Inaccurate localization of keypoints caused by weak visual features, and (2) Measurement deviations induced by non-standard postures. To address these issues, a novel method named CowSizeNet was proposed, which integrates keypoint detection, initial size estimation, and posture-aware correction into a coherent process. In the first stage, the Cattle Keypoint Detection Network (CKDNet) was developed to achieve reliable keypoint localization. Two dedicated modules introduced in this study, the Bidirectional Feature Enhancement Module (BFEM) and the Hyper-Graph Association Enhancement Module (HGAEM), were incorporated to enrich visual representations and strengthen spatial associations, significantly improving the localization accuracy of visually ambiguous regions. In the second stage, stereo image disparity and camera parameters were utilized to obtain depth information, enabling 3D projection of detected keypoints and initial body size estimation. In the final stage, a Posture-aware Correction Graph Convolutional Network (PC-GCN) was introduced to learn the nonlinear relationships among keypoint geometry, joint angles, and body measurement deviations under varying postures. By regressing and compensating posture-related deviations, the model yielded more accurate and consistent body size estimations. Experiments verified the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method. For Body Length (BL), Body Height (BH), and Hip Height (HH), the Mean Absolute Percentage Errors (MAPE) were 4.26%, 1.97%, and 2.19%, respectively, satisfying the accuracy requirements for automated body measurement in PLF. Furthermore, the design and development of supporting terminal devices and visualization platforms further enhanced the practical value of the proposed method, promoting its use in dairy farm management.

title: A computer vision driven ecosystem for cattle monitoring: Multi-disease classification with severity grading, multi-view individual identification, and weight estimation
abstract: This study introduces a computer vision based cattle monitoring ecosystem, which (i) performs multi-disease classification and severity grading with 85.88% hierarchical accuracy, (ii) achieves multi-view cattle identification with 89.80% Rank-5 accuracy under cross-view-angle and domain shift conditions, and (iii) estimates body weight from four view RGB images and metadata with an MAE of 35.10 kg, developed using custom-collected, curated datasets combined with publicly available datasets. For the disease module, a hierarchical cross-attentional multi-task architecture classifies Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD), Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD), Infectious Bovine Keratoconjunctivitis (IBK), and Healthy cattle, while grading diseased cases into Stage-1 (mild), Stage-2 (moderate), and Stage-3 (severe) using clinically graded veterinarian supervised annotations, achieving 89.96% disease classification accuracy, 83.75% severity staging accuracy, and 85.88% hierarchical accuracy (disease → severity). On a custom collected dataset, YOLOv8s localizes cattle from left, right, front, and back views with an IoU of 0.93 and mAP@0.5 of 0.97, providing the basis for identification and weight estimation. Multi-view individual cattle identification achieves Rank-1 accuracies of 96.40% (Rank-5: 100%) under Leave-One-View-Out evaluation and 74.56% (Rank-5: 89.80%) under cross-view-angle and domain-shift testing using ConvNeXt-Tiny. In weight estimation module, ensemble learning over multi-view images and metadata achieves an MAE of 35.10 kg. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of an affordable, low-shot, non-invasive RGB-based system for disease diagnosis with severity grading, multi-view cattle identification, and practical live-weight estimation without invasive sensors.

title: Unified vision: Multi-task learning for retinal image-based cattle trait classification
abstract: Reliable identification of demographic traits such as gender, breed, and age is fundamental to automated herd management in precision livestock farming. Traditional approaches based on external morphology or manual tagging are often labour-intensive, error-prone, or susceptible to tampering. In contrast, retinal imaging provides a non-invasive and stable biometric modality with high inter-individual variability. This study proposes a multi-task learning (MTL) framework for simultaneous classification of gender, breed, and age group from cattle retinal fundus images. The architecture incorporates multi-scale spatial feature fusion to capture fine-grained vascular patterns and broader retinal structures, positional encoding combined with Transformer-based relational modeling to enhance spatial dependency learning, and uncertainty-weighted multi-task optimization to balance task contributions adaptively. Experiments were conducted on a dataset of 1,206 retinal images from 233 individual cattle, annotated with demographic labels. The proposed model achieved strong performance across all three tasks. For gender classification, it attained 0.909 in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Breed classification yielded scores of 0.880, 0.886, 0.880, and 0.883, while age classification achieved 0.926, 0.929, 0.926, and 0.927, respectively. Visualization analyses using t-SNE demonstrated that the multi-task framework produced more compact intra-class clustering and greater inter-class separability compared to single-task baselines. Grad-CAM visualizations further confirmed that the proposed model consistently focused on anatomically meaningful regions, particularly the optic disc and major vascular bifurcations. Comparative analysis confirmed the superiority of integrating multi-scale feature extraction, spatial relational modeling, and task uncertainty weighting in retinal image-based livestock phenotyping. This work highlights the potential of retinal imaging combined with multi-task learning for developing scalable, interpretable, and automated livestock phenotyping systems.

title: Optimization of efficiency and stability in a front-axle direct torque-coupled hybrid tractor during plowing via regenerative braking: a coordinated multilayer control strategy
abstract: Tractors plow energy efficiency and stability jointly determine economic performance and operational quality. In this paper, the previously proposed front-axle direct torque-coupled hybrid tractor powertrain (FADTC-HTP) is adopted. Mathematical and simulation models oriented to plowing scenario are then developed for this architecture. Based on these models, an efficiency-stability coordinated multilayer control strategy (ES-CMCS) is proposed to enhance longitudinal speed stability, lateral deviation stability, and energy efficiency during plowing. In the ES-CMCS, the FADTC-HTP is formulated as a linear state-space model with time-varying disturbance inputs. Based on this model, a linear time-varying model predictive control (LTV-MPC) strategy is employed to regulate the engine, front-axle torque-coupled motors, and eLSD clutch pressure, with the objective of improving tire-soil interaction efficiency and speed stability. The LTV-MPC is supported by a self-learning hidden Markov model-based predictor that provides tire longitudinal and tractive force predictions over a 0.5 s horizon to ensure reliable solutions of the time-varying parameter model. Meanwhile, a nonlinear MPC (NMPC) is adopted to enhance tractor lateral stability by regulating the front-wheel steering angle using the LTV-MPC outputs together with real-time tractor dynamic parameters. To compensate for the inability of MPC to explicitly exploit engine and motor efficiency maps as prior knowledge, a deep reinforcement learning-based action compensator is introduced to further optimize control commands. Finally, the proposed hybrid tractor powertrain system and control strategy is evaluated on a controller-hardware-in-the-loop (CHIL) test bench. The results indicate that, compared with a steer-only control strategy, the equivalent fuel consumption rate is reduced by 7.11 %, the standard deviation of lateral path deviation decreases by 28.70 %, and the RMSE of longitudinal speed tracking is lowered by 65.88 %. Relative to other baseline multi-objective control methods, operational stability and energy efficiency are also improved markedly. Another noteworthy finding is that, under the proposed FADTC-HTP configuration, operating the front-axle electric machines in regenerative braking mode during plowing effectively constrains tire slip, enhances tire-soil interaction efficiency, and positively affects diesel engine fuel economy. This study offers an alternative perspective for the structural design and model-data hybrid driven control strategy development of hybrid tractors.

title: MaizeStereo: 2D Gaussian splatting-driven stereo foundation model for in-field proximal 3D maize phenotyping
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) maize phenotyping is instrumental in capturing the spatial structural features essential for crop breeding and guiding agricultural practices. Among existing 3D sensing technologies, stereo vision has achieved remarkable progress in reconciling cost‑effectiveness, environmental robustness, and operational efficiency, owing to its inherent advantages as a passive sensing modality. However, its limited precision collectively impedes the broader application for organ-level phenotyping. Building on advancements in stereo vision propelled by supervised stereo matching paradigms and large-scale foundation models, this study proposes a 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS)-driven stereo foundation model approach for in-field proximal 3D maize phenotyping (MaizeStereo), which capitalizes on the intrinsic generalization potential of stereo foundation models while enhancing the adaptability to field proximal sensing via domain-specific optimization. Field experiments were conducted using a custom binocular image acquisition system on 50 maize plants across five growth stages (V3, V5, V7, V12, R3). The proposed MaizeStereo framework addresses real-field scenarios by synthesizing a high-fidelity stereo matching dataset through an advanced multi-view 2DGS reconstruction method. Leveraging the dataset for supervision, an optimal module-freezing strategy is developed to fine-tune the stereo foundation model for domain-specific performance enhancement. Based on the resulting disparity predictions, the framework further implements organ-level phenotypic trait extraction. Evaluated results showed that the fine-tuned foundation model outperformed benchmark methods in stereo matching with a global end-point error (EPE) of 1.846 pixels and a D1 error of 6.806%, achieving only a marginal 5.55% EPE increase compared to full fine-tuning while reducing trainable parameters by 45.7%. For phenotypic trait extraction, the pipeline delivered high accuracy with mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) of 3.822% for plant height, 3.432% for stem diameter, and 7.741% for leaf area. The corresponding coefficient of determination (R2) values were 0.994, 0.952, and 0.986 respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed method enables efficient and precise maize phenotyping in complex field conditions, providing a valuable tool for crop breeding and agricultural research.

title: A weed detection model based on dual-stream attention and multiscale contextual fusion
abstract: To address the limitations in detection accuracy of existing deep learning-based weed detection algorithms, particularly under conditions characterized by significant background complexity and target scale variation, this paper proposes an improved object detection model designated as DEA-YOLO11. First, a Dual-Stream Vision Network (DSV-Net) is introduced in place of the original backbone to strengthen the complementary extraction of shallow local textures and deep global contexts. Second, an Enhanced Receptive Field Module (ERFM) is designed to augment the model’s capability for capturing multiscale targets without compromising spatial resolution. Finally, an Adaptive Context Guided Fusion Module (ACGF) is constructed to replace the conventional concatenation operation, facilitating the dynamic suppression of background interference while actively promoting focus on target regions. Experimental results on a self-constructed Xinjiang Weed Dataset (XWD) demonstrate that the proposed DEA-YOLO11 achieves a mean Average Precision (mAP50) of 91.50% and an F1-Score of 88.10%, representing performance increments of 3.82 and 2.84 percentage points over the YOLOv11n baseline, respectively. Furthermore, evaluations conducted on multiple public benchmark datasets corroborate the model’s superior generalization capabilities. This research thus provides a robust implementation that attains a highly favorable balance between detection accuracy and operational efficiency, establishing it as a practical solution for real-time weed detection in complex agricultural environments.

title: Visual-language-guided task planning for horticultural robots
abstract: Crop monitoring is essential for precision agriculture, but current systems lack high-level reasoning. We introduce a novel, modular framework that uses a Vision Language Model (VLM) to guide robotic task planning by actively querying heterogeneous data sources—including enriched RGB camera feeds and 2D semantic occupancy maps—interleaved with robotic action primitives. We contribute a comprehensive benchmark for short- and long-horizon crop monitoring tasks in monoculture and polyculture environments. Our results show that while zero-shot VLMs perform robustly for short-horizon tasks (achieving 87% success, comparable to human experts), success drops significantly to under 10% for complex long-horizon, multi-target tasks. Despite this decline, task completion rates remain above 76% under noiseless conditions. Critically, the system degrades when relying on noisy semantic maps, demonstrating a key limitation in current VLM context grounding for sustained robotic operations. This work offers a deployable framework and critical insights into VLM capabilities and shortcomings for complex agricultural robotics. Supplementary material: https://kendallkoe.com/Visual-Language-Guided-Task-Planning-for-Horticultural-Robots/ .

title: Supervised contrastive regression learning for predicting soluble solids content of blueberries using hyperspectral imaging
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging technology enables rapid and non-destructive assessment of fruits. However, acquiring a large-scale and well-balanced labeled dataset remains a significant challenge, primarily due to destructive reference measurements and difficulty sourcing samples that cover a wide and balanced distribution of quality attributes, which exacerbates overfitting risk when sample diversity is limited. Additionally, most deep learning methods optimize using mean squared error and regularization losses without explicitly learning feature representations relevant to regression tasks, making it difficult to learn robust, continuous feature representations. To address these challenges, we propose a spectral quantitative regression framework with supervised contrastive learning (SQR-SCL). A C-Mixup method selects sample pairs based on target-value similarity and interpolates their features and target values, enhancing sample diversity. A differential preservation and continuity feature learning (DPCFL) module learns continuous feature representations while preserving differences between samples. The DPCFL module draws samples with similar target values closer together and pushes those with differing values further apart, sorting features in the embedding space by target value. Such ordering prevents the model from making significantly different predictions for similar inputs, thereby improving prediction stability. A projection head in the DPCFL module ensures that extracted features preserve inter-sample differences and enhances their discriminative power. In this study, reflectance hyperspectral images and soluble solids content (SSC, ∘Bx) were acquired for 1010 blueberries in five sample groups. On this dataset, SQR-SCL achieved a test R2 of 0.884 and an RMSEP of 0.641(∘Bx), outperforming compared deep learning and traditional methods.

title: In-Season monitoring of rice phenology for massive germplasm resources using Explainable Machine learning and a Transformer CNN model
abstract: Timely, accurate, and intelligent monitoring of rice phenology is crucial for selecting germplasm resources of suitable phenology, but previous research on phenological estimation has been based primarily on a few major rice cultivars in large scale field, lacking numerous germplasm resources in small breeding plots. Consequently, we proposed an in-season phenology monitoring framework that first identifies the growth stage of each rice plot and then estimates the initiation dates of key phenological stages for massive germplasm resources. This study utilized UAV to acquire time series imagery of 3112 rice germplasm resources across eight ecological sites. The improved CNN-Vision Transformer combined model classified the phenological stages, and based on these results, vegetation indices (VIs) for different germplasm resources at various growth stages were calculated. Subsequently, a Bayesian random forest regression model estimated the initiation dates of key phenological stages, and its performance was validated using an independent dataset. Additionally, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis assessed the contributions of different VIs to phenological stages. The results demonstrated that Re-ViTAE achieved an accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score and MCC (Matthews Correlation Coefficient) values of 93.59 %, 93.03 %, 93.15 %, 93.08 % and 91.84 %, correspondingly, superior to all other eleven CNN and Vision Transformer models. RMSE of estimated initiation dates was 3.9d, 4.7d, 4.5d, and 3.7d for jointing, heading, grain-filling, and maturity, respectively, and the independent data validation accuracy was 5.6d, 5.3d, 5.8d, and 5.0d, respectively. Compared with the traditional RF model, the Bayesian-optimized RF model reduced the RMSE by 1.2 d, 1.2 d, 1.0 d, and 1.6 d, respectively. SHAP analysis revealed that different VIs contributed unequally to the estimation of key rice phenological initiation dates. Specifically, MTCI, NDVI, OSAVI, and Clgreen contributed most to the estimation of jointing, heading, grain filling, and maturity, respectively. The results of this study enable the quantitative classification for growth stages and estimation of initiation dates for massive rice germplasm resources, providing technical support for breeding scientists and companies in the selection of superior germplasms.

title: Physics-guided GAN and ANN hybrid framework for small-sample performance prediction of seed-maize harvester conveying device
abstract: The scarcity of simulation data limits the modeling accuracy for performance prediction of seed-maize harvester conveying devices. This study proposes a hybrid intelligent modeling framework that integrates physical mechanisms with data-driven methods. First, a high-quality dataset of 32 sample points is constructed using a DEM-MBD coupled simulation. The dataset incorporates three key operational parameters: conveyor belt speed, elevator inclination angle, and secondary stalk-roll speed. To overcome small-sample learning challenges, a physics-constrained Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (PC-WGAN) is developed. This network embeds differentiable constraints, derived from projectile motion equations and collision momentum conservation laws, into the generator’s loss function. The PC-WGAN subsequently generates 100 physically credible augmented samples. Based on this, the proposed PC-WGAN-GP-ANN hybrid framework achieved an R2 value of 0.827 in predicting the stalk removal rate and ear damage rate of the conveying device, representing a 219.28% improvement compared to the baseline ANN model. Although the random forest (RF) achieved a slightly higher R2 (0.832) on the same augmented data, the proposed method enables the otherwise poor-performing ANN (original R2 = 0.259) to achieve competitive accuracy, demonstrating its effectiveness in leveraging generated data under small-sample conditions. Field validation tests demonstrate that under the optimal parameter combination (conveyor speed: 3.452 m/s, inclination angle: 55.2°, stalk-roll speed: 652 r/min), the stalk removal rate reaches 96.2%. This field result is essentially consistent with the simulation predictions. This study confirms that incorporating physical prior knowledge as constraints into the generative data augmentation process enhances the accuracy and generalization capability of agricultural equipment performance prediction models under small-sample conditions. Therefore, the proposed PC-WGAN-GP-ANN hybrid model provides an effective data-driven solution for the intelligent design of agricultural machinery under small-sample conditions.

title: Stage-specific estimation of rice leaf area index and above-ground biomass from UAV LiDAR-derived structural features
abstract: Accurate extraction of phenotypic traits in low-stature crops is essential for precision agriculture and phenomics research. This study evaluates a stage-specific framework for estimating rice leaf area index (LAI) and above-ground biomass (AGB) using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data across four key growth stages: tillering, jointing, booting, and heading. Following point cloud preprocessing and the extraction of canopy structural features, we identified stage-wise candidate predictors using random forest recursive feature elimination (RF-RFE) and Spearman correlation. Physically informed variables, such as the transformed canopy-cover term −ln(1−fcover) and a derived volume metric, were integrated into the modeling process. For evaluation, multiple linear regression (MLR), random forest (RF), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) were compared using plot-level grouped cross-validation for LAI and a plot-aware within-plot validation strategy for AGB, acknowledging the limited sample size and spatial dependence of samples. The results demonstrate that LAI can be estimated with reliable performance across all growth stages. The gap-fraction-based baseline model achieved RCV2 values of 0.743–0.919, while the best multivariate models yielded RCV2 values of 0.747–0.917 with low error metrics. In contrast, AGB estimation exhibited stronger stage dependence and lower overall performance, with the best test R2 ranging from 0.306 to 0.586 and relatively better performance observed at the booting and heading stages. Because the AGB results were evaluated under a plot-aware within-plot validation strategy, they should be interpreted as indicative of within-plot predictive performance rather than as evidence of fully plot-independent generalization. Notably, MLR frequently matched or exceeded the performance of machine learning models (RF and XGBoost) under limited-sample conditions, highlighting the advantage of using compact, physically interpretable predictor combinations. These findings suggest that a stage-aware modeling approach using LiDAR-derived structural features provides a useful basis for rice phenotyping, although the generalizability of these results across different cultivars and environments warrants further investigation.

title: AI-enabled electromagnetic sensor architecture for precision welfare monitoring in small ruminant production systems
abstract: Climate change and increasing heat stress present growing challenges for the welfare and productivity of small ruminants raised in arid and hot environments. In many production systems, animal health and welfare are still assessed primarily through visual observation, which may delay the detection of subtle physiological or behavioural changes associated with emerging welfare risks. Recent developments in precision livestock farming offer new possibilities for continuous and objective monitoring of animal conditions through advanced sensing technologies. This review explores recent progress in electromagnetic sensing technologies and their integration with artificial intelligence (AI) for monitoring animal welfare in small ruminant production systems. A literature search was conducted using the Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases, focusing mainly on studies published over the past decade related to sensor-based livestock monitoring, electromagnetic sensing approaches, and AI-supported welfare assessment. Studies examining physiological, behavioural, or environmental indicators relevant to livestock welfare were considered. Recent studies indicate that electromagnetic sensing technologies—including microwave antennas, radar-based monitoring systems, metamaterial sensors, and dielectric sensing devices—can detect a range of welfare-related indicators such as respiration patterns, locomotor activity, and hydration status. When combined with machine-learning algorithms, these systems enable the interpretation of complex data streams and support more proactive approaches to welfare management. Based on the reviewed literature, this paper proposes a conceptual framework that integrates three key monitoring modules thermal comfort, locomotor stability, and hydration balance to illustrate how multi-sensor data can be analyzed through AI-driven approaches in small-ruminant production systems under arid climatic conditions. While these technologies show considerable promise, practical challenges remain, including sensor robustness in farm environments, economic feasibility, and the need for appropriate farmer training. Further research is therefore required to evaluate integrated sensor–AI systems under commercial farming conditions and to develop scalable decision-support tools for precision livestock management. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first reviews to specifically focus on the integration of electromagnetic sensing technologies and artificial intelligence for welfare monitoring in small ruminants under arid climatic conditions.

title: Deep learning-based keypoint detection for 3D biometric measurement of tuna using underwater stereo vision
abstract: Accurate and scalable estimation of tuna size during transfer and farming operations is essential for stock assessment and management. This study presents a fully automatic processing pipeline that combines deep learning-based keypoint detection with stereoscopic vision geometry to estimate fish length, height, and width from underwater stereoscopic imagery. The system exploits videos acquired while freely swimming fish under real underwater conditions from two different viewpoints: a lateral view, from which length and height are measured, and a ventral view, which provides length and width. Having measurements of individual fish in all three dimensions can significantly improve the accuracy of estimating biomass and schools for large-bodied species. For each view, a Keypoint R-CNN model was trained on heterogeneous datasets of 850 stereo pairs annotated independently by three human operators. To account for annotation variability, per-keypoint normalization constants were computed and used to adapt COCO-style Object Keypoint Similarity (OKS) metrics to this domain. The proposed Keypoint R-CNN system achieved 2D keypoint localization accuracy comparable to human annotators (mean OKS = 0.91). The resulting 3D biometric measurements yielded relative errors of approximately 1%–2% for length-related dimensions and 2%–5% for height and width, within the range observed for inter-annotator variability. Measurement bias remained below 0.2% for all evaluated dimensions, and no systematic over- or under-estimation trends were observed. Automatic and manual size distributions were statistically indistinguishable, while processing throughput was compatible with offline operational analysis requirements. Overall, the proposed approach provides a reliable and scalable foundation for automated 3D size monitoring in tuna aquaculture.

title: PA-SWE: a posture-aware sow weight estimation framework via skeleton-calibrated multimodal fusion
abstract: Accurate body weight monitoring of gestating sows is critical for precision feeding and reproductive performance optimization. While deep learning has shown promise in image-based weight estimation, existing RGB-based methods are sensitive to posture variation, and depth-based alternatives incur higher deployment costs and environmental constraints. This study introduces Posture-Aware Sow Weight Estimation (PA-SWE), a posture‑aware RGB–skeletal framework that uses posture as an auxiliary source of structural information rather than treating it as nuisance variation. The framework comprises an upstream module that simultaneously outputs instance segmentation masks and anatomical keypoints from the top‑view RGB images, and a downstream module that fuses RGB appearance features with a skeletal graph via compact bilinear pooling to jointly predict body weight and posture. Evaluation on a commercial farm dataset containing 48 gestating sows of a single breed follows an event‑level protocol: image‑level predictions within each weighing event are aggregated using the median to produce the final event-level estimate. PA‑SWE achieves an event‑level mean absolute error of 2.814 kg, a root mean square error of 3.513 kg, and an R2 of 0.975, together with a macro‑averaged F1‑score of 92.89% for three‑class posture classification. Pig‑level statistical analyses further showed that the error reduction relative to RGB‑only baselines is significant and consistent across individuals. These results suggest that explicit integration of skeletal cues can reduce posture‑related estimation errors and improve event‑level weight estimation in the current farm‑specific setting. The proposed framework therefore offers a practical option for contactless monitoring of gestating sows without requiring strict standing-posture standardization under crate-based monitoring conditions.

title: A method for quantifying feeding behavior of grass carp in outdoor ponds with complex backgrounds
abstract: In aquaculture, precise quantification of fish feeding behavior is essential for formulating feeding strategies. However, dynamic background factors in outdoor pond farming can interfere with the extraction of fish school behavior characteristics. To address this, a novel method has been proposed for quantifying fish behavior under complex conditions. First, the MusFormer model was developed, integrating a mixed transformer encoder with a custom multi-scale feature fusion decoder. This decoder includes a residual MLP and a multi-scale feature fusion module, enabling the generation of high-precision semantic segmentation images of fish school feeding areas. Subsequently, a new method called QFA (Quantitative Feeding Activity Index) was established to quantify the spatial characteristics of fish school feeding behavior. By assigning weights to pixel points, this method reduces interference from segmentation errors and dynamic changes in the background mask. Finally, to evaluate its effectiveness under complex background conditions, the QFA framework was integrated with three mainstream temporal classification models: RNN, Transformer, and RCNN. This combination yielded classification accuracies of 90.97 %, 88.73 %, and 91.86 %, respectively, outperforming existing fish appetite assessment methods, which achieve a maximum accuracy of 84.17 %. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for quantifying fish feeding behavior in outdoor ponds with typical complex background disturbances.

title: Estimating grass-clover mixtures quality using field spectroradiometry and stacking-based ensemble learning models
abstract: In this study, we designed a stacking ensemble machine learning method for accurate estimation of grass-clover biomass quality from high-resolution hyperspectral field data. Basic learners were support vector machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), random forest (RF), decision tree (DT), partial least square regress (PLS), shallow artificial- (ANN) and deep multi-layer perceptron (MLPs) neural networks. Three meta learners in the second layer were RF (stackingRF), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (stackingXGB), and CatBoost (stackingCat). We used 6 different datasets for the estimation, including the raw spectral reflectance, its 1 st and 2 nd derivatives, and their Standard Normal Variate (SNV). Quality indices were crude ash, crude protein, crude fat, crude fiber, neutral detergent fiber (NDF), acid detergent fiber (ADF), water-soluble carbohydrates (WSC), sugar, and fructans. The results showed that spectral feature selection by the PLS was useful in preprocessing. All machine learning methods predicted well quality from the raw reflectance, with PLS performing best (R 2 = 0.64–0.87) for all indices except crude ash. The stacked ensemble learning benefited the predictions, especially with stackingRF and stackingCat as meta learners (R2 increased by 2–8 % compared with the average of the four best machine learning algorithms in the first layer). SNV generally performed better than the original reflectance across most datasets. In particular, SNV applied to the 2nd derivative, combined with either PLS or StackingRF, yielded the best predictions for carbohydrates (sugar, fructans, WSC) and fiber (crude fiber, NDF, ADF), achieving the highest R 2 values (0.74–0.87) and the lowest nRMSE (5–15 %) among all pre‑processing options. The red‑edge region (700–780 nm) is the most important for all quality indices, except for ADF. This is among the first studies to systematically evaluate stacking ensemble learning, using the outputs of multiple machine‑learning algorithms as inputs, for predicting biomass quality and supporting field management in complex grass–clover mixtures. PLS‑based feature selection combined with stacking ensemble learning on second‑derivative SNV spectra appears particularly promising and warrants testing at larger spatial and temporal scales.

title: TP-Duck: A cage-reared duck behavior recognition model with lightweight interaction mechanism and text prompts
abstract: Accurate and automated behavior recognition is critical for welfare assessment and production management in intensive duck farming. However, cage-reared duck behavior recognition remains challenging due to the high visual similarity among behaviors and the tendency for subtle discriminative motion cues to be misinterpreted by the duck’s dominant body appearance under cage interference. To address these challenges, this study proposes a lightweight vision–language model with partial-star operation and text prompts for cage-reared duck behavior recognition (TP-Duck). Specifically, a Lightweight Partial-Star Operation Block (LPS) is designed to efficiently capture fine-grained discriminative features through partial convolution for channel-sparse computation and star operation for high-dimensional non-linear feature excitation. Building upon LPS, a Text-Prompted LPS Block (TP-LPS) is further developed to leverage pre-trained vision–language embeddings for cross-modal feature modulation, thereby enhancing the model’s capacity to disambiguate behaviors with similar postures in complex cage environments. Extensive experiments were conducted on a self-built cage-reared duck behavior dataset. TP-Duck achieves an F1 score of 89.4%, surpassing the baseline YOLOv11s and state-of-the-art YOLO26s by 2.2 and 5.0 percentage points, respectively, while reducing parameters by 0.64 M and 1.18 M. The results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves superior recognition accuracy with reduced model complexity, providing an effective solution for automated duck behavior monitoring in intensive farming systems.

title: MSSVT: Multi-branch spatial-spectral volumetric transformer for rice lodging segmentation with UAV multimodal fusion
abstract: Deep learning-based fine-grained segmentation of typhoon-induced rice lodging provides important support for high-precision disaster assessment using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing. However, many existing unimodal, flat multimodal, or generic cross-modal segmentation methods process heterogeneous UAV-derived features without explicitly preserving the semantic relationships among feature groups, which may limit modality-specific representation and spatial-spectral interaction. To address this challenge, this study investigates structured UAV multimodal fusion by organizing RGB physical features and multispectral physiological signatures into a semantically grouped volumetric representation. A Multi-branch Spatial-Spectral Volumetric Transformer (MSSVT) is proposed for fine-grained rice lodging segmentation. MSSVT uses a Hybrid Volumetric-Planar Backbone (HVPB), in which the Volumetric Spatial-Spectral Backbone (VSSB) models inter-group spatial-spectral dependencies, while the Planar Spectral Backbones (PSB) preserve fine-grained intra-group attributes. Within VSSB, the Volumetric Hybrid Attention (VHA) module combines dynamic sparse routing and selective scanning to capture salient lodging regions and refine boundary details. A progressive feature fusion mechanism is further used to integrate band-compressed, adaptively modulated, and multimodal aggregated features. To support this study, a multimodal Volumetric Rice Lodging (VRL) dataset was constructed for the investigated typhoon-induced lodging area. The dataset organizes 55 heterogeneous channels spanning RGB, color, texture, structure, multispectral, and vegetation-index features into a structured volumetric representation. Extensive experiments on the VRL dataset demonstrate that MSSVT achieves 90.72 % mIoU, representing a 1.31 % improvement over the strongest competing method. The proposed model obtains class-wise IoU values of 97.59 %, 78.10 %, and 91.02 % for normal rice, mild lodging rice, and severe lodging rice, respectively, with the largest gain observed for mild lodging rice (+5.16 %). These results indicate the potential of structured UAV multimodal fusion for fine-grained rice lodging segmentation under the investigated typhoon-induced field scenario. Code is available at: https://github.com/AG-WDS/MSSVT.

title: SDrAwberry: Scale-referenced Depth-Anything-3 long-sequence reconstruction for Strawberry canopy volume estimation
abstract: Canopy volume is a key structural trait for crop monitoring and phenotyping platforms, but reliable plant-level canopy volume estimation in commercial strawberry fields remains challenging due to repetitive canopy structure, limited texture on bed surfaces, and the need to process long, nearly linear image sequences without loop closure. This paper presents SDrAwberry, a scale-referenced long-sequence 3D reconstruction and plant-level canopy volume estimation pipeline using synchronized tri-view RGB images collected by a ground robot across eight strawberry plant beds on one representative field acquisition date. The proposed pipeline enables a memory-efficient processing of long sequence data by partitioning the data into overlapping batches, fusing the partitioned batches into a global reconstruction in the form of point cloud, and estimating plant canopy volume by segmenting individual plants, mesh reconstruction, and scale calibration with reference boxes. The pipeline was validated by comparing the number of segmented plants and manual plant counts, and by evaluating metric scale recovery with reference-box volume self-validation. The instance extraction stage showed strong agreement with manual plant counts, with a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 5.36 %. Reference-box self-validation also indicated consistent metric scale recovery, with an MAPE of 3.95 %. Direct plant-level canopy-volume ground truth was not available, so plant-volume outputs were interpreted as scale-referenced reconstructed traits rather than direct volume-accuracy validation. These results indicate that feed-forward multi-view geometry transformers can be extended to field-scale, metrically meaningful phenotyping via batching-and-fusion and scale-referenced volumetric reconstruction. Code and data are available at: https://github.com/Sycamorers/SDrAwberry.

title: Context-aware adaptive pesticide spraying for agricultural robots under changing weather and terrain using Vision–Language Models
abstract: Precision pesticide spraying is essential for optimizing application efficiency and ensuring uniform chemical distribution. Spraying performance is influenced by multiple factors, including environmental conditions such as temperature and wind speed, pesticide type, and the robot's capability to accurately perceive crops and target spray locations. Existing approaches predominantly emphasize crop detection and rely on predefined spraying parameters, whereas human operators dynamically adjust their spraying strategies by considering environmental conditions, region-specific crop characteristics, and the type of pesticide being applied. In this study, we propose a context-aware adaptive spraying framework based on Vision-Language Models (VLMs), which enables robots to leverage spatial reasoning and integrate information from multiple sources, including crop type, pesticide type, and weather data, to make adaptive and optimized spraying decisions. Subsequently, a trajectory-tracking controller based on Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control is employed to ensure precise navigation and accurate spraying at crop locations. The comparative results demonstrate that the proposed method improves accuracy by at least 30% in detecting crop rows. In addition, the experimental evaluations conducted in two environments further demonstrate the robot's ability to flexibly adjust spraying volume and travel speed, while reducing pesticide drift.

title: Integrating feature selection and machine learning for nitrogen assessment in grapevine leaves using in-field hyperspectral imaging
abstract: Nitrogen (N) is one of the most critical nutrients in winegrape production, influencing vine vigor, fruit composition, and wine quality. Because soil N availability varies spatially and temporally, accurate estimation of leaf N concentration is essential for optimizing fertilization at the individual plant level. In this study, in-field hyperspectral images (400-1000 nm) were collected from four grapevine cultivars (Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Concord, and Syrah) across two growth stages (bloom and veraison) during the 2022 and 2023 growing seasons at both the leaf and canopy levels. An ensemble feature selection framework was developed to identify the most informative spectral bands for N estimation within individual cultivars, effectively reducing redundancy and selecting compact, physiologically meaningful band combinations spanning the visible, red-edge, and near-infrared regions. At the leaf level, models achieved the highest predictive accuracy for Chardonnay (R^2 = 0.82, RMSE = 0.19 %DW) and Pinot Noir (R^2 = 0.69, RMSE = 0.20 %DW). Canopy-level predictions also performed well, with R^2 values of 0.65, 0.72, and 0.70 for Chardonnay, Concord, and Syrah, respectively. White cultivars exhibited balanced spectral contributions across the visible, red-edge, and near-infrared regions, whereas red cultivars relied more heavily on visible bands due to anthocyanin-chlorophyll interactions. Leaf-level N-sensitive bands selected for Chardonnay and Pinot Noir were successfully transferred to the canopy level, improving or maintaining prediction accuracy across cultivars. These results confirm that ensemble feature selection captures spectrally robust, scale-consistent bands transferable across measurement levels and cultivars, demonstrating the potential of integrating in-field hyperspectral imaging with machine learning for vineyard N status monitoring.
