title: MoeBi-ViT: Non-destructive shoot-stage phenotyping of lettuce in plant factory via dual-branch mixture-of-experts network and enhanced segmentation
abstract: In plant factories, increased crop yield often comes at the price of higher energy inputs. Understanding the relationship between environmental regulation and crop growth helps maximize energy use efficiency. Thus, dynamic monitoring of crop biomass is critical for optimizing crop management practices. The morphological parameters (canopy length and width, plant height, leaf area) and biomass indicators (fresh weight and dry weight) jointly form the key metrics for evaluating crop growth and development. However, traditional manual measurement methods are typically inefficient, costly, labor-intensive, and time-consuming. This study proposed a rapid, non-destructive lettuce biomass estimation method based on two-stage multi-modal deep learning: firstly, a gated attention-enhanced segmentation model—Mambaout-Mask2Former (MOMF)—was adopted to address background interference in lettuce phenotypic estimation, which reduces parameter count and model complexity while enabling accurate lettuce mask extraction and background elimination; secondly, a dual-branch Mixture-of-Experts regression network (MoeBi-ViT) was constructed to lower the computational complexity of the biomass regression network while ensuring generalization across scenarios, which was achieved via the combination of a Transformer-based Mixture-of-Experts encoder (TEME) and bi-attentional feature fusion (BAF). MoeBi-ViT activates only ∼ 37 % of weights per inference (compared to fully parameter-activated models) while maintaining precise biomass regression performance. Experimental results have shown that MoeBi-ViT outperformed the baseline Vision Transformer (ViT) significantly in lettuce biomass estimation with only a marginal increase in inference parameters, achieving a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.936 for fresh weight prediction and a 12.3 % overall improvement in the aggregated R2 metric. Ablation studies confirmed the effectiveness of TEME and BAF. To explain the model’s operating mechanism, activation frequencies were counted to analyze the contribution of different expert types in the final Mixture-of-Experts layer to various phenotypic parameters. Additionally, the trained model was applied to an unlabeled lettuce dataset to verify its accuracy in continuous growth monitoring. The results demonstrated that the predicted growth curves were consistent with their actual one. The framework proposed in this study provides an effective non-destructive monitoring approach for crop management, with potential applications in smart decision-making for plant factories.

title: A unified training framework with masked pixel–semantic reconstruction for agricultural image segmentation
abstract: Accurate agricultural image segmentation (AIS) is crucial for ensuring food security, enhancing agricultural production efficiency, and improving resource utilization. However, constrained by the seasonal nature of agricultural production, incomplete sensor networks, and the specialized nature of annotation, segmentation models trained under data-scarce conditions face challenges of overfitting and poor generalization capabilities. To enhance segmentation accuracy and generalization capabilities of existing models under existing labeled data, this study proposed a two-stage unified training framework for agricultural image segmentation models, named AgriSTF. The first stage employs the developed Masked Pixel-Semantic Reconstruction (MPSR) for self-supervised pretraining of the segmentation model’s encoder. The second stage utilizes labeled data for supervised fine-tuning of the segmentation model. MPSR defines the self-supervised proxy task as jointly predicting masked pixels and semantic tokens, establishing bidirectional constraints between local details and high-level semantics through a carefully designed Joint Decoder. Over 600 experiments conducted across five AIS tasks and seven representative baselines demonstrated that AgriSTF consistently improved baseline accuracy without requiring additional data, achieving competitive results even in settings utilizing only 50% of training epochs or only 50% of labeled data. Additionally, comprehensive ablation experiments were conducted to investigate the optimal hyperparameter settings for MPSR. AgriSTF is model agnostic and data efficient, providing a new approach for training under existing labeled data and showing the potential to become a foundational training paradigm for developing AIS models under limited-data conditions in the future. The code is available at: https://github.com/CAU-COE-VEICLab/AgriSTF.

title: An explainable SR-GAN and MobileNetV2 framework for aerial pest detection in precision agriculture
abstract: As pest problems in agriculture continue to grow, there is now greater demand for systems that can quickly spot them. It is common to use human scouts for spotting pests or standard machine-learning techniques, but they cannot easily process the low-resolution images taken by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles(UAVs). Using blurred or poor quality data in deep learning usually causes the model to miss some items and select the incorrect choice. To deal with the mentioned problems, this research combines Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (SR-GAN) technology with a lightweight classifier called MobileNetV2 for more effective monitoring of aerial pests. The main function of the SR-GAN module is to transform UAV images with low resolution into ones with high resolution that keep important details of each pest. After improving the images, MobileNetV2 is used to classify them effectively and accurately. Trust in the framework is further increased by Grad-CAM which makes it clear which features of the input affect the prediction of the model. Images created using super-resolution are deemed visually better due to the boost in PSNR, SSIM and MSE. Classification tests show that the improved models have superior accuracy, graphs and analysis of important features. The method improved upon the base CNN by 18%, reaching a 92.6% rate of correct predictions. Moreover, the test results indicated that PSNR values were 5.2 dB higher than with the CNN. The proposed method has more consistent outputs and better behavior under varied farming conditions with Accuracy = 92.6%, Precision = 93.1%, Recall = 92.2%, F1 Score = 92.4%, Parameters = 2.3 M, FLOPs = 0.3G, Inference Time = 30 ms, which can effectively detect the pests even in occluded, shadow, or low-visibility cases. It combines various approaches and remedies the existing system problems, offering flexibility for immediate use in agriculture to help save crops and make pesticide use more efficient.

title: Unsupervised keypoint detection for automated livestock phenotyping: A multi-species approach based on pre-trained foundation models
abstract: In the realm of precision livestock farming, the identification of keypoint in livestock is a crucial area of research. Traditional supervised learning approaches face challenges in adapting to the complexities of livestock environments, including varied poses, occlusions, and inter-species differences, due to their reliance on extensive annotated datasets. To overcome these limitations, this research introduces a novel unsupervised keypoint detection methodology grounded in pre-trained foundation models. Our innovative approach combines the strengths of Stable Diffusion (SD), known for its exceptional fine-grained texture perception, with DINOv2′s structural similarity representation. We employ a normalized weighted fusion strategy to seamlessly integrates these complementary features, enabling multi-scale semantic alignment. Additionally, we have developed a unique multi-template voting mechanism that utilizes Mean-Shift clustering and inverse-distance weighting, significantly enhancing both the accuracy and stability of keypoint detection. To support this research, we have compiled a comprehensive livestock dataset encompassing 2204 images horse (804), cattle (309), sheep (767), and pig (324). Our experimental analysis, conducted across these species, reveals a high average detection accuracy (91.21% for horses, 91.09% for cattle, 84.76% for sheep, and 93.78% for pig), using the PCK@0.05 metric, which outperforms the SOTA method by 3.07, 4.62, 11.19, and 3.10 percentage points (pp), respectively. The proposed method demonstrates robust cross-species generalization capabilities, effectively managing significant pose changes and non-rigid deformations. It offers a versatile and efficient solution for keypoint detection, applicable to automated body measurement or animal behavior analysis in precision livestock farming applications. For access to the code and dataset, please visit https://gitee.com/wbxue/keypoints.

title: Autonomous crop and weed detection in multiple agricultural fields using YOLO-based models with combined real and synthesized images
abstract: Accurate crop and weed detection is critical for targeted weed control, particularly for weeds in intra-row areas. Site-specific weeding where weeds appear can reduce herbicide use and labor costs. However, field variability, including crop growth stage, soil texture, illumination, and camera viewpoint, remains challenging. This study presents a practical data-construction workflow that integrates synthetically generated images with labeled real images to train crop-weed detection models. You Only Look Once (YOLO) versions 4 and 8, convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, were evaluated because of their detection performance and computational efficiency. Training YOLOv8 with a mixed synthetic-real dataset derived from four crop types collected across agricultural fields in four Japanese prefectures improved detection of 11 crop and weed classes. On the validation data, the model achieved a precision of 0.92, a recall of 0.89, an F1-score of 0.90, and a mean average precision (mAP50) of 0.92. On independent real test images, the proposed YOLOv8 model achieved a mAP50 of 0.88, with class-level Recall50 values ranging from 0.67 to 0.97 and a mean Recall50 of 0.85. These results show that synthetic images are useful for reducing annotation effort and improving class balance when combined with real field images, but they do not replace independent real-image validation. The method therefore provides a promising perception component for future intra-row weeding systems, while robot-level testing, embedded inference, and actuation accuracy remain necessary before autonomous deployment.

title: Toward optimal sampling rate selection and unbiased classification for precise activity recognition of farm quadruped animals
abstract: With the rapid advancements in deep learning techniques, wearable sensor-aided animal activity recognition (AAR) has demonstrated promising performance, thereby improving livestock management efficiency as well as animal health and welfare monitoring. However, existing research often prioritizes overall performance, overlooking the fact that classification accuracies for specific animal behavioral categories may remain unsatisfactory. This issue typically stems from suboptimal sampling rates or class imbalance problems. To address these challenges and achieve high classification accuracy across all individual behaviors in farm quadruped animals, we propose a novel Individual-Behavior-Aware Network (IBA-Net). This network enhances the recognition of each specific behavior by simultaneously customizing features and calibrating the classifier. Specifically, considering that different behaviors require varying sampling rates to achieve optimal performance, we design a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)-based Feature Customization (MFC) module. This module adaptively fuses data from multiple sampling rates, capturing customized features tailored to various animal behaviors. Additionally, to mitigate classifier bias toward majority classes caused by class imbalance, we develop a Neural Collapse-driven Classifier Calibration (NC3) module. This module introduces a fixed equiangular tight frame (ETF) classifier during the classification stage, maximizing the angles between pair-wise classifier vectors and thereby improving the classification performance for minority classes. To validate the effectiveness of IBA-Net, we conduct experiments on three public datasets for goat, cattle, and horse activity recognition. The results demonstrate that our method exhibits strong and competitive performance across all three datasets compared to existing approaches. Specifically, it achieves the highest values across three datasets: for goat, 93.17 % accuracy, 87.17 % F1-score, and 91.71 % recall; for cattle, 91.42 % accuracy, 90.62 % F1-score, 88.06 % precision, and 93.64 % recall; and for horse, 84.34 % F1-score and 84.05 % precision. Notably, the recall values exhibit substantial enhancements, surpassing the baseline method by 16.98 %, 15.78 %, and 4.91 % on the goat, cattle, and horse datasets, respectively. These improvements are particularly evident for the minority classes, while high recognition performance is maintained for the majority classes. These results confirm that IBA-Net effectively enhances classification accuracy across all animal behavioral categories, while aligning with the initial goal of achieving high recall values and maximizing overall classification performance.

title: XylemVision: A Knowledge-Distilled deep learning framework for High-Throughput quantification of root anatomy in peanut
abstract: Manually quantifying root anatomy from microscope images has been a major bottleneck in crop research. Deep learning can automate this process, but requires large, labeled datasets that are expensive to create. Newer foundation models, like the Segment Anything Model (SAM) or DINOv2, appear to offer a solution but struggle with specialized scientific images. Even after fine-tuning, these models still require precise prompts such as bounding boxes or points to specify what to segment. A common workaround is to use an object detector (like YOLO) to create these prompts, but this reintroduces the original challenge of needing extensive labeled data to train the detectors itself. To address this bottleneck, a knowledge distillation (KD) framework was developed to train object detectors with minimal labeled data. Initially, a large DINOv2 teacher model was used to pretrain student detectors (YOLO11 and RT-DETR) on unlabeled root images, transferring its rich visual feature representation capabilities without requiring any labels. This pretraining phase enabled the student models to extract high-level generalized spatial features of the root images. The pretrained student detectors were then fine-tuned using a small, labeled dataset to detect anatomical features including xylem, vascular bundles, and the total root. Finally, the resulting bounding boxes were passed to a SAM-integrated segmentation pipeline to produce precise, pixel-level masks for trait extraction. Together, these steps form XylemVision, a unified and data-efficient pipeline for xylem phenotyping that demonstrates accurate detection, segmentation, and trait extraction with limited labeled data. Results showed that the KD-pretrained YOLO11 model demonstrated superior detection performance (0.922 mAP50–95) compared to its supervised baseline (0.884) and maintained comparable accuracy (0.917 mAP50–95) even when the labeled dataset was reduced by 25 %-75 %. By leveraging these precise bounding boxes as prompts, the SAM-based segmentation pipeline proved highly effective, achieving mean Intersection over Union (IoU) scores of 0.85–0.95 across all anatomical traits substantially outperforming YOLO11′s built-in segmentation module, which achieved only 0.10–0.58 IoU. Beyond these performance gains, the KD framework ensured strong transferability across species, successfully adapting to soybean root cross-sections without additional fine-tuning. Overall, this study develops a data-efficient framework that makes plant image analysis efficient and more accurate across different crops.

title: Complementary-aware collaborative fusion: Advancing precise wheat lodging mapping using UAV-borne RGB imagery and LiDAR data
abstract: Wheat lodging, where stems bend or fall to the ground, substantially reduces both yield and quality. Accurate mapping is crucial for assessing severity, guiding the selection of resistant varieties, and estimating agricultural losses. Existing deep learning approaches based on unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-acquired RGB imagery often fail to capture vertical structure differences between healthy and lodged wheat. To overcome this limitation, we propose integrating LiDAR-derived Digital Surface Models (DSMs) with RGB imagery to enable multimodal lodging mapping. We present MWLNet, a novel multimodal network designed for wheat lodging characterization. MWLNet incorporates three modules: (1) the Discrepancy Modality Recalibration (DMR) module, which explicitly extracts complementary information across modalities and recalibrates features through cross-modal interaction; (2) the Dynamic Feature Consolidation (DFC) module, which adaptively fuses recalibrated features with contribution-aware weighting; and (3) the Bi-directional Semantic Synchronization (BSS) module, which enhances semantic alignment between modalities and mitigates intra-class diversity caused by varying lodging degrees. Experiments on two UAV wheat lodging datasets show that MWLNet consistently outperforms unimodal and multimodal baselines. These results confirm the effectiveness of multimodal fusion for crop lodging mapping. The code are available at https://github.com/WangYuPeng1/MWLNet.

title: BioLQM: a novel hybrid intelligent model for feed optimization and growth evaluation in juvenile spotted knifejaw (Oplegnathus punctatus)
abstract: Precisely optimizing feeding strategies and evaluating growth of juvenile fish in complex aquaculture environment, remain critical challenges to be addressed. This study proposed a novel hybrid intelligent decision-making model for aquaculture, BioLQM integrates the strengths of bioenergetics, reinforcement learning (Q-learning), and model predictive control (MPC) to accurately evaluate the growth trajectory of juveniles and provides feeding decisions. Juvenile spotted knifejaw (Oplegnathus punctatus) was selected as the research subject. It was validated under offshore aquaculture net pen (OANP) and recirculating aquaculture system (RAS). Results proved that BioLQM exhibits good fitting performance within the limited sample (MSE≈0.0005, MAPE≈0.16 %, and R2≈1). And in retrospective simulation, model feeding strategies reduced the feed conversion ratio (FCR) from 1.79 to 1.42 in OANP and from 2.77 to 1.52 in RAS. A juveniles growth validation experiment confirmed the rationality of model-based feeding decisions, achieving a FCR of 1.2. Furthermore, it met the target weight requirements, with MSE of 0.1558, MAPE of 2.5937 %, and R2 of 0.9989. Comparison results showed that BioLQM addressed the limitations of traditional growth models. It could accurately describe fish growth trajectories and adaptively provide feeding decisions under controlled and uncontrolled conditions. Q-learning was incorporated to mitigate uncertainties in parameters of mechanistic model and to reduce its high sensitivity to external disturbances. MPC was incorporated to mitigate the lack of predictive capability for system dynamics and future states in Q-learning, facilitating continuous optimization and smoothed constraint enforcement to avoid extreme control decisions. BioLQM could be employed in commercial intensive aquaculture to monitor fish growth trajectories and optimize feeding management. It could be extended to other fish species by calibrating specific parameters within the mechanistic model.

title: Wind-excited audio-based leaf area density estimation in apple-tree canopies: Mechanism-guided generative denoising and attention-based spectrogram learning
abstract: Leaf area density (LAD) describes canopy compactness in apple orchards and supports variable-rate spraying decisions. However, real-time in-field LAD sensing remains challenging because occlusion, illumination variability, and strong equipment noise reduce the reliability and learnability of canopy observations. This study proposes a mechanism-guided wind-excited acoustic sensing framework for LAD grade estimation in apple-tree canopies. First, mechanism-based analysis was used to identify the dominant noise sources and key frequency bands, and passive noise reduction was adopted to improve acquisition consistency. Then, a correlation-mean-square-error (MSE) constrained deep neural network (CM-DNN) was used to reconstruct low-SNR wind-excited audio. Finally, a spectral-centroid statistical prior was introduced to guide frequency-axis attention, and a spectral-centroid attention deep convolutional neural network (SCA-DCNN) model was used to classify log-power spectrum spectrograms. The results showed that passive noise reduction decreased device background noise from 72.7 dB to 65.4 dB, and 10 m/s was selected as the unified acquisition condition. On this basis, SCA-DCNN improved accuracy by 3.50 percentage points over the baseline DCNN and achieved 91.50 % accuracy on independent field samples. Overall, the proposed combination of mechanism-guided noise control, low-SNR signal reconstruction, and prior-guided attention improved the learnability of orchard acoustic data and provided a deployable sensing pathway for prescription-oriented canopy grading.

title: Cattle behavior classification using Hidden Markov Models
abstract: The increasing demand for meat production necessitates more sustainable and data-driven livestock management practices. Precision Livestock Farming (PLF) leverages sensor technologies and computational methods to monitor individual animals, enhancing productivity and welfare. In this study, we use Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) to classify free-range cattle behavior using GPS and tri-axial accelerometer data collected from 22 Angus-based cows over a nine-week winter period in western Montana, USA. Following model validation, HMM-predicted behavioral states were used to examine large-scale behavioral patterns across the entire dataset. The analysis revealed pronounced diurnal activity cycles, temperature-dependent shifts in behavior, and significantly greater nighttime grazing activity during full moon periods. Generalized Linear Mixed Models (GLMMs) further demonstrated significant interactions between temperature and time of day, showing that cattle increasingly shifted grazing activity toward cooler periods as temperatures increased. These findings provide insight into how environmental conditions influence free-range cattle behavior and demonstrate the value of sensor-based monitoring for precision grazing management. To enable this analysis, we engineered four features; step size, turning angle, and the mean and variance of Signal Vector Magnitude (SVM), and used these in a three-state HMM to classify grazing, resting, and traveling behaviors. Model development was conducted using leave-one-out cross-validation to assess generalizability across individuals, achieving an average classification accuracy of 92.72%. Our findings demonstrate the utility of HMMs as robust, transparent, and computationally efficient tools for cattle behavior classification in extensive rangeland settings. The approach holds promise for real-time PLF applications such as early anomaly detection, resource allocation, and adaptive grazing management.

title: Energy-Efficient path tracking control for autonomous tractors equipped with Hydro-Mechanical continuously variable transmission based on coordinated control methods
abstract: Autonomous tractors often prioritize tracking performance at the expense of operational energy consumption, negatively affecting their economic efficiency. To address this issue, this study proposes a coordinated control method that considers both tracking accuracy and fuel economy. First, a model predictive control algorithm is used to design the path tracking system, where longitudinal and lateral errors as tracking objectives, while acceleration and front wheel steering angular velocity as constraints. Then, a plowing resistance prediction model for tractors is developed using Long Short-Term Memory neural networks based on historical tractor plowing resistance data. Next, a dual-variable economic control strategy is developed to minimize the engine fuel consumption rate and optimize the hydraulic-mechanical continuously variable transmission efficiency ratio. The predicted working speed from the path tracking system and the predicted plowing resistance from the resistance prediction model are then passed to the economic control strategy, forming a coordinated control method that integrates tracking accuracy with fuel economy. We used pure pursuit and Stanley, both with a single-variable fuel-economy control strategy, as baselines. The proposed strategy’s effectiveness is validated through simulations and hardware-in-the-loop experiments. The results show that, compared with the alternative method, the proposed approach effectively reduces path tracking error and improves economic efficiency. Compared with the first and second comparison methods, the proposed approach reduces the standard deviation of speed variance by 70.27% for both methods, decreases longitudinal tracking error by 57.14% and 33.33%, respectively, reduces lateral tracking error by 33.33% and 55.56%, respectively, and lowers fuel consumption by 28.49% for both methods. This study provides valuable insights for improving both path tracking performance and energy efficiency in autonomous tractors.

title: Salmonella risk prediction in poultry farms via deep learning image classification Models, Cross-Region Validation, and edge computing
abstract: Salmonella remains a major cause of foodborne illnesses that are commonly associated with the consumption of contaminated poultry products. Therefore, there is a strong emphasis and a crucial need to reduce Salmonella across the farm to fork continuum. However, there are no easy and rapid on-farm prediction tools to estimate if a flock carries Salmonella . In this study, we used deep learning to develop a Salmonella risk classification model for chicken feces. The model was developed using a two-part framework combining deep learning and tree-based classification techniques. In the first stage, deep learning models such as ResNet152, Xception, VGG19, and others were employed to extract high-level features from chicken fecal images. In the second stage, these features were used by decision tree classifiers including Random Forest and Gradient Boosting for binary classification into Salmonella PCR Positive or Negative. The model was developed using fixed train-validation-test splits on two datasets: an American dataset with 720 images from a controlled multi-serovar Salmonella challenge study and African dataset with 4333 publicly available images. This integrated approach achieved up to 85% classification accuracy when validated across geographical regions. The developed framework was integrated into a user-friendly mobile and web application and allows users to custom train the deep learning classifiers to improve the classification of unseen fecal images. Although the model was primarily validated with the same dataset, this proof-of-concept framework can serve as a decision-support tool for Salmonella control and intervention, contributing to enhanced food safety. Overall, the objective of this study is to develop and validate a hybrid AI approach for Salmonella prediction using fecal images, with explicit cross-region evaluation and proof-of-concept deployment applications.

title: Concept-guided deep learning with UAV-satellite sample augmentation for daily 10 m crop AGB mapping
abstract: Aboveground biomass (AGB) is a fundamental variable for characterizing crop growth, yield potential, and agricultural carbon cycling. Achieving daily 10 m resolution crop AGB mapping at regional scales remains challenging. Here, a unified UAV-satellite framework is developed that integrates sample augmentation with concept-guided deep learning (DL) to enable high-resolution AGB mapping. UAV-derived canopy structural and spectral information is fused with satellite spectral and cumulative temporal features to generate virtual quadrats aligned with the Sentinel-2 pixel scale, thereby expanding the training dataset and mitigating the scarcity of field-based AGB measurements. These quadrats facilitate the development of a novel light-use-efficiency-guided Long Short-Term Memory model (LUE-LSTM), in which AGB is formulated as a cumulative state variable driven by photosynthetically active radiation, enforcing physiological constraints on AGB dynamics. Experiments in the Hetao Irrigation District demonstrate improved physical consistency of AGB temporal estimation, characterized by near-ideal temporal behavior (Normalized Time Variability Index, NTVI ≈ 1.0) and low deviation from realistic growth dynamics (Logistic Fitting Error, LFE < 60 g m⁻2). Cross-year and cross-region validation further demonstrates enhanced generalization, with R2 increasing from 0.741 to 0.815 and RRMSE decreasing from 0.220 to 0.185. Using the proposed framework, daily 10 m AGB maps were generated for 2019–2025, demonstrating strong potential for regional crop monitoring and agricultural carbon assessment.

title: A physics-informed neural network for continuous rice canopy thermal monitoring and forecasting from sparse UAV observations
abstract: Continuous monitoring of canopy temperature (Tc), a key indicator of crop water-heat stress and physiological dynamics, using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery is inherently limited by temporal discontinuity and the limited physical realism of purely data-driven models. This study develops a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework to transform temporally sparse UAV thermal observations into continuous hourly rice Tc reconstruction and 48 h forecasting products. The model leverages sparse UAV thermal measurements as supervisory signals while integrating them with continuous meteorological forcing and daily UAV-derived crop phenotypic features. Validated through a comprehensive season-long rice field experiment using walk-forward cross-validation, the proposed PINN framework demonstrated superior performance. It achieved R 2 values of 0.92 for reconstruction and 0.90 for forecasting, with RMSE of 0.71 °C and 0.82 °C, respectively. Ablation analysis further showed that crop phenotypic variables contributed more strongly than temporal descriptors, reducing predictive uncertainty by approximately 4.8–14.3 %, while the integration of SEB physical constraints and uncertainty modeling improved R 2 by 8.4–9.5 % and reduced Total STD by 28.4–37.7 %. The model successfully captures diurnal dynamics, spatial variability, and canopy thermal hysteresis while maintaining physical consistency through improved energy closure. This framework bridges sparse aerial observations with continuous physiological monitoring and highlights its potential to support precision irrigation, early stress detection, and high-throughput phenotyping in smart agriculture.

title: Behavioural phenotyping in red deer: Machine learning classification of accelerometer data from micro-movements to grazing
abstract: Monitoring deer behaviour continuously and objectively is essential for accurate welfare assessment in pastoral farming, yet conventional observation methods are labour-intensive and prone to subjective bias. We present an unsupervised machine-learning pipeline for classifying farmed red deer ( Cervus elaphus ) behaviour from wearable accelerometer data. Tri-axial accelerometers mounted on the head and ear of stags recorded movement at 50 Hz over 48 h. k -means clustering of the normalised signals yielded eight prototypical movements spanning three behavioural categories: inactive states (lying, resting with or without rumination/panting), grazing (stationary and walking), and rapid ear flicks. A first-order Markov chain then linked these prototypes into higher-order sequences we call ”super-prototypes”. These compound behaviours included ear-flick bouts and alternating grazing-stepping cycles. Within the single 24-h window, activity varied with time of day, ear flicks being markedly more frequent by day. Against independent video annotation, the eight categories agreed with the observer’s labelling at a mean of 0.96 across prototypes. Because classification reduces to a nearest-centroid operation, the algorithm runs on a 16 MHz microcontroller at over 4 × 1 0 8 classifications per second, four orders of magnitude faster than the sensor sampling rate. The pipeline requires no hand-labelled training data and runs in real time on the animal, a feasible basis for welfare monitoring in extensive deer farming systems once validated under field conditions.

title: Mitigating occlusion: a spatial-aware diffusion model for pose estimation in quadrupedal livestock
abstract: In livestock management, accurately capturing pose changes in quadrupedal livestock is crucial for disease prediction and behavioral analysis. However, due to inter-animal occlusion and obstructions from farming facilities, livestock in practical farming environments are often partially visible, making pose estimation highly challenging. Existing livestock-specific pose estimation models and transferred human pose estimation frameworks are limited by fixed structural constraints and insufficient discrimination of highly similar livestock features, resulting in inaccurate localization and missed detections of body keypoints under occlusion conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes SADPose, a Spatial-Aware Diffusion Model for pose estimation in quadrupedal livestock. The proposed framework combines noise-guided pose generation with hybrid-scale spatial constraints to improve robustness under severe occlusion. Specifically, a Hybrid-Scale Graph Convolutional Network is embedded into the diffusion framework to model local and global skeletal relationships. During the forward diffusion stage, the model constructs a feature space covering diverse livestock pose distributions, while the reverse denoising process progressively suppresses interference through multi-scale feature fusion, thereby reducing localization bias and missed detections of occluded keypoints. Experiments on two public datasets involving representative quadrupedal livestock species demonstrate that SADPose significantly outperforms existing methods in occlusion scenarios, improving keypoint localization accuracy and overall pose estimation performance in complex occlusion scenarios.

title: Modeling the temperature–humidity coupling dynamics of soybean pod borer population and assessing the predictive performance of the PCM-NN algorithm
abstract: Against the backdrop of global climate change and agricultural globalization, soybean production is increasingly threatened by pest outbreaks, with Leguminivora glycinivorella (commonly known as the soybean pod borer) being a major pest species. This pest is widely distributed, particularly in northeastern China, the country's primary soybean-producing region, where its outbreaks have significantly affected both yield and quality. Although statistical and mechanistic models have been applied to pest forecasting, existing approaches often fail to effectively integrate climatic factors with pest dynamics and lack sufficient expressive power. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel pest prediction method based on Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). Specifically, we formulate a logistic-type ordinary differential equation (ODE) that incorporates microclimate factors, temperature, humidity, and time, to describe the temporal dynamics of the soybean pod borer population. This ODE model is embedded into the PINN framework to develop the Pest Correlation Model Neural Network (PCM-NN), which is used to jointly infer the microclimate-driven parameter function alpha(T, H, t) and fit the pest population dynamics. We evaluate PCM-NN using daily monitoring data of soybean pod borer collected in Changchun, Jilin Province, from July to September during 2020-2023. Experimental results demonstrate that PCM-NN preserves biological interpretability while exhibiting strong nonlinear representational capacity, offering a feasible pathway for pest modeling and forecasting under multi-factor climatic conditions. This approach provides valuable support for agricultural pest monitoring, prevention, and control strategies.

title: Comprehensive low-damage mechanical weeding technology considering the spatial distribution of crop roots: A case study of maize farmland
abstract: Weed control is essential for improving fresh maize yield, and mechanical weeding is widely adopted in organic farming due to its environmental and economic advantages. Existing mechanical weeding equipment was not designed with the spatial distribution of crop root systems in mind, which can easily result in damage to the roots. To achieve comprehensive low-damage weeding, a mechanical weeding system integrating maize root spatial distribution characteristics with deep learning was developed. Firstly, morphological parameters of maize seedlings at the 3–5 leaf stage were measured, and an image dataset was constructed. Seedling detection was performed using the open-vocabulary model YOLOv8-world, achieving a precision of 0.958 and an average processing speed of 245.30 FPS on edge devices, which can meet the requirements for seedling recognition and detection in fresh maize field environments. Subsequently, based on the measured morphological parameters, a three-dimensional spatial protection zone was established. Four types of intra-row weeding knives with different angles were designed and tested in field experiments. Field experiments and variance analysis demonstrated that the intra-row weeding knife with a 20° angle was the most suitable for comprehensive low-damage weeding in fresh maize farmland. At an operational speed of 1.5 km/h, the average weed removing rate was 91.05%, with an average crop damage rate of 2.35%. The weeding system exhibited stable and reliable performance, making it suitable for comprehensive low-damage weeding operations in fresh maize farmland. This study provides a reference for the development of comprehensive low-damage weeding equipment.

title: Precision agriculture meets explainable AI: A highly competitive ET0 prediction framework based on hybrid deep learning
abstract: Accurate prediction of reference crop evapotranspiration (ET0) is crucial for smart agriculture and efficient water resource management. However, the strong non-linearity and non-stationarity of ET0 time series pose significant challenges to existing prediction models. To overcome current limitations in prediction accuracy, this study designs and implements an enhanced hybrid deep learning architecture (E-CBT: Enhanced CNN-BiLSTM-Transformer) combined with Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) preprocessing, forming the DWT-E-CBT framework aimed at capturing complex multi-scale spatiotemporal dependencies within ET0 time series. This architecture integrates three optimized components: a deep convolutional network with residual connections, a stacked layer-normalized bidirectional long short-term memory network (BiLSTM), and an advanced Transformer encoder employing a Pre-norm structure. Notably, we introduce a multi-head attention pooling mechanism to replace traditional pooling methods. We rigorously compared the performance of the E-CBT model with various baseline models under a range of signal decomposition preprocessing techniques. Experimental results demonstrate that signal decomposition techniques significantly improve prediction accuracy, with discrete wavelet transform (DWT) performing optimally in providing input for the E-CBT model. Ultimately, the proposed DWT-E-CBT framework exhibits superior prediction performance, achieving highly competitive performance within a comprehensive benchmarking framework for ET0 prediction. The coefficient of determination (R2) reaches 98.99%, while the root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) are as low as 0.1655 mm·day⁻1 and 0.1125 mm·day⁻1, respectively. Through SHAP explainability analysis, we further reveal the model’s decision-making process and identify key driving factors for ET0 prediction. The DWT-E-CBT framework proposed in this study provides a novel and powerful paradigm for complex time series prediction, demonstrating significant application potential in precision irrigation.

title: Early crop type classification and mapping combining remote sensing and ancillary data
abstract: Accurate and timely crop type classification is critical for agricultural management and food security monitoring. Most existing approaches rely on the spectral response time series obtained from satellite imagery, primarily focusing on end-of-season classification. By providing accurate crop maps early in the season, policymakers, irrigation managers, and producer organizations can optimize water allocation, forecast production, and stabilize food prices. This study introduces a novel AI framework that integrates remote sensing data with ancillary information, such as cloud cover percentage, previous-year crop type, and irrigation type, for early crop type classification. The framework is validated on a dataset of approximately 130,000 fields in the region of Lleida, Catalonia (Spain), a representative Mediterranean agricultural landscape. Leveraging remote sensing data from the previous growing season enhanced early-stage classification performance, achieving an accuracy of approximately 70% at the season’s onset—a significant improvement over traditional approaches relying solely on current-season data. Ancillary data played a key role in mitigating challenges such as cloud-induced data gaps and limited spectral information and better predicting crop types in fields with permanent crops or no crop rotation. Incorporating ancillary data boosted accuracy by 10%, resulting in an overall accuracy of 80% early in the season, which increased to 88% by the season’s end. Despite these advancements, underrepresented crop classes remained difficult to classify accurately due to class imbalances, underscoring the need for improved dataset balancing techniques. The findings underscore the potential of integrating multi-source data to improve crop type classification, especially early in the season.

title: Intelligent decision-making method for optimal maize seeding rate based on synergistic driving of multi-source field information
abstract: In variable-rate maize seeding, optimal seeding rate (OSR) decisions are jointly shaped by multiple interacting field factors, including climate, management, and soil conditions. However, the prevailing two-stage “yield prediction-optimal search” framework struggles to effectively capture the synergistic effects among heterogeneous features and is prone to error propagation and accumulation, thereby compromising decision stability. Meanwhile, the long duration of field trials and strong environmental disturbances lead to limited and unevenly distributed OSR ground-truth samples, further constraining predictive accuracy and generalization. Therefore, it is imperative to develop a multi-source, synergy-driven OSR decision-making approach tailored to small-sample scenarios. To this end, climatic variables, field management data, and soil organic matter (SOM) information covering interannual environmental variability were collected over four consecutive years under real-world maize production conditions. Based on these data, a Dual-dimension Adaptive Gating OSR Decision Network (DA-AGNet) was proposed. DA-AGNet incorporates multi-head self-attention, a dual-dimension weighting module, and a gated weighted aggregation mechanism to enable adaptive weighted fusion of multi-source inputs, thereby mitigating the adverse effects of noise in small-sample settings and enabling direct end-to-end prediction of OSR. To improve training stability under small-sample conditions, a coarse-to-fine yield-guided ladder training architecture (CF-YLTA) was constructed. CF-YLTA leverages a yield prediction model to generate pseudo-OSR data for coarse-stage pretraining of DA-AGNet and to initialize transferable prior weights, and then conducts fine-stage end-to-end training by combining these priors with data-augmented OSR ground-truth samples, thus improving prediction accuracy and generalizability. For yield predictor selection, multiple machine learning algorithms were benchmarked, and gradient boosting decision trees (GBDT) achieved the best performance, with the root mean square error (RMSE) of 360.71 kg/ha, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 248.70 kg/ha, and R2 of 0.88. DA-AGNet trained using CF-YLTA delivered the best OSR prediction on the test set (RMSE = 1646.64 seeds/ha, MAE = 1247.96 seeds/ha, R2 = 0.74), outperforming conventional approaches overall. Qualitative analysis of the predicted OSR indicated an S-shaped increasing trend as SOM increased, which can be partitioned into a low-OSR plateau (SOM 16–25 g/kg), a rapid-increase region (SOM 25–37.5 g/kg), and a high-OSR plateau (SOM 37.5–44 g/kg), consistent with established agronomic understanding. To evaluate model effectiveness, the variable-rate seeding prescriptions derived from DA-AGNet were compared with constant low- and high-density seeding schemes, and the variable-rate strategy showed a yield advantage. Overall, the proposed OSR decision model provides reliable intelligent decision support for determining maize OSR in variable-rate seeding operations under varying crop growth environments.

title: Enhancing soil organic matter prediction by Decoupling soil moisture effects with a conditional generative adversarial network
abstract: Soil moisture significantly affects soil spectral reflectance, and its high variability severely undermines the accuracy of soil organic matter (SOM) prediction. To address this issue, soil samples were collected from northern and northeastern China to construct three independent datasets. A deep generative model, Wet Spectrum to Dry Spectrum (Wet2dry) was then developed to capture the structural characteristics of one-dimensional spectral features. On this basis, three moisture-correction methods—Direct Standardization (DS), External Parameter Orthogonalization (EPO), and Wet2dry—with three SOM prediction models: Random Forest, Transformer, and SE-Transformer were systematically compared. Results show that the Wet2dry method effectively eliminates moisture interference and improves SOM prediction accuracy, offering a robust solution for soil property spectral inversion under high moisture variability. In SOM prediction tasks, the SE-Transformer model, which integrates the Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention mechanism, exhibited stronger responsiveness to critical spectral bands. When combined with the Wet2dry correction model, the SE-Transformer consistently achieved excellent prediction performance across different moisture levels (5%, 10%, 15%), with R2 > 0.75 and RPD > 2. This study extends image-generation network architectures to one-dimensional spectral modeling, providing a feasible solution for stable SOM prediction under moisture interference.

title: Estimating fine-scale soil moisture content and wheat yield in drought-heterogeneous farmlands using machine learning regressions on multispectral UAV imagery
abstract: With the development of precision agriculture, soil moisture content (SMC), a key factor affecting wheat yield, requires efficient and near real-time monitoring at the field scale. This study applies soil line indices derived from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) multispectral imagery to estimate fine-scale SMC and wheat yield in two farmlands with distinct spatial SMC distributions (i.e., farmland drought heterogeneity) in Kinmen, Taiwan. By comparing traditional linear regression with several machine learning approaches, including support vector regression (SVR), gradient boosting regression (GBR), and convolutional neural network regression (CNNR), key indices contributing to SMC and yield estimation across different wheat growth stages were identified. The results indicate that both SMC and wheat yield can be reasonably explained when significant farmland drought heterogeneity is present. Linear regression achieved optimal coefficients of determination (p < 0.01) of 0.65 for SMC using the perpendicular vegetation index and 0.93 for wheat yield using the normalized difference vegetation index. Areas with higher SMC within a farmland were found to negatively affect wheat growth. Among the machine learning models, GBR and CNNR based on the selected indices (VAPDI and NDVI, respectively) achieved estimation accuracies of 98.0 % and 72.2 %, respectively, for total wheat yield across the two experimental farmlands. Temporal validation across different growing cycles suggests the potential for cross-year wheat yield prediction. Deviations from expected estimation patterns may be considered preliminary indicators of abnormal yield conditions, and early-stage yield estimation shows promising potential. Overall, these findings provide preliminary evidence for early-stage yield prediction and offer valuable insights for optimizing irrigation timing and enhancing the development of AI-driven agricultural decision support systems.

title: MFFT: an improved method for stable ID tracking and counting of multi-class mango segmentation with multi-feature fusion in complex occlusion scenarios
abstract: Accurate mango segmentation, counting, and biomass estimation are critical for orchard yield prediction. To address the challenges of low fruit segmentation accuracy, frequent ID switches, and large tracking and counting errors under complex occlusion scenarios, this paper proposes a multi-feature fusion tracking method termed MFFT. The method is built on the Swin-T backbone and a customized Transformer decoder, integrated with shallow feature enhancement, boundary attention, and background gating modules. For mango segmentation, the proposed approach achieves 0.71 mIoU and 40.32 FPS for both on-tree and fallen mangoes. In the tracking stage, IOU, HSV, shape, and diagonal features are fused, together with an improved Kalman filter and ID lifecycle management, resulting in a MOTA of 0.6513 and a significant reduction in ID switches. The system innovatively introduces diagonal length as a computational metric, achieving a counting relative error of only 4.30% and a biomass estimation error of 4.49%. It outperforms mainstream algorithms such as Mask R-CNN, YOLOv8, DTER, and ByteTrack across multiple metrics. The proposed method exhibits strong application potential in orchards and provides more precise data support and a decision-making foundation for digital agricultural production management. The code and dataset for this study have been made open source on Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1UzvgiqlXn-C2aJZsHmcLAWSYaVYA0bnH/view?usp=sharing.

title: Boosting cough recognition of livestock animals in farming environments through parameter-efficient tuning of multimodal audio pre-trained models
abstract: Deep learning-based acoustic sensing has significantly advanced the early detection of respiratory diseases in livestock. However, most existing models remain species-specific and rely heavily on manually labeled data, limiting their scalability and generalization across heterogeneous livestock farming environments. In this study, a novel multimodal approach for cough recognition (MAP-DA) across pigs and calves was proposed by integrating waveform-guided multimodal audio pre-training with dense-adapter-based efficient adaptation. During pre-training, the multimodal audio pre-training (MAP) framework exploited complementary information from Mel spectrograms and waveforms, learning robust animal vocalization features. During fine-tuning, dense-adapter (DA) tuning enabled efficient downstream adaptation through densely connected lightweight adapters. The results showed that MAP learned robust feature representations and consistently outperformed evaluated state-of-the-art audio pre-training paradigms, demonstrating the value of multimodal audio representation learning in acoustically complex farming environments DA-tuning effectively translated the learned animal vocalization knowledge into more accurate cough recognition by strengthening feature reuse and task-specific refinement. MAP-DA achieved accuracy values of 92.32% in pigs and 98.34% in calves, surpassing evaluated state-of-the-art cough recognition approaches. Importantly, MAP-DA benefited from joint downstream fine-tuning on larger and more diverse labeled datasets, achieving superior performance compared with the corresponding specialist models and demonstrating the potential as a generalist model across the evaluated livestock animals. Besides, MAP-DA demonstrated its ability to reduce dependence on manual annotation, achieving an accuracy of 90.90% with only 5% of the labeled training samples. This study provides a promising basis for developing scalable acoustic monitoring methods for livestock respiratory health in acoustically complex farming environments.

title: Physics-Informed hybrid path planning for standardized orchard Navigation: A parameter space learning paradigm via Dual-Head Networks
abstract: Standardized orchard navigation requires path planners to balance safety, smoothness, and kinematic feasibility under narrow-row and semi-structured operating conditions. To address the limitations of conventional search-based methods, artificial potential field (APF)-based methods, and end-to-end learning methods, this paper proposes a physics-informed hybrid path-planning framework. The core idea lies in a parameter-space learning paradigm, in which a neural network predicts the key physical parameters of the APF, while the final trajectory is generated by a physics-based executor, thereby enhancing both adaptability and interpretability. To further coordinate global path consistency and local obstacle avoidance, a dual-head architecture is designed to decouple direction prediction from APF parameter adaptation. In addition, a two-stage training strategy that combines supervised warm-up with reinforcement fine-tuning is introduced to improve physical consistency and dynamic smoothness. Experimental results on more than 400 benchmark maps demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a 100 % success rate, together with stable safety margins and a Mean Jerk of 0.0072 rad. Ablation studies, Gazebo simulations, dynamic obstacle-avoidance tests, and real-world orchard experiments further verify the robustness and deployment potential of the proposed framework for safe and smooth autonomous navigation in complex orchard environments.

title: DELKNet + LLM: lightweight multi-model integration real-time perception and pre decision analysis for facility tomato
abstract: Precise phenotypic perception and reliable decision-making are critical for the intelligent management of greenhouse tomatoes. However, existing methods often lack an integrated closed-loop “perception-to-reasoning” workflow and struggle with high computational costs on edge devices. This study proposes PP-LLMs, an innovative framework that bridges visual perception and agronomic reasoning by integrating a lightweight detection model, YOLON, with a fine-tuned Large Language Model, Tomato-Qwen. Our core contributions are threefold. First, we constructed the TGMD (Tomato Growth Multimodal Dataset), a benchmark comprising 9,519 high-quality expert-annotated language pairs covering descriptions of tomato growth status and agricultural production knowledge.Second, we developed YOLON, which employs efficient DELK-Block and GSLK modules to achieve high-precision detection of tomato organs while maintaining a lightweight architecture suitable for real-time edge deployment. Third, by applying a two-stage fine-tuning process (LoRA and prompt learning) to Qwen-7B-Chat, we enabled Tomato-Qwen to perform complex agronomic reasoning based on real-time phenotypic and environmental data. Experimental results demonstrate that this strategy significantly outperforms mainstream baselines. Tomato-Qwen achieved substantial improvements in QA tasks, with BLEU-4 and ROUGE-L scores increasing by 29.42% and 33.13% respectively.This research demonstrates the preliminary effectiveness of visual-language collaboration in agriculture and suggests a potentially scalable solution for autonomous greenhouse management. But the generated agronomic suggestions should be regarded as preliminary candidate outputs whose practical safety and reliability have not yet been validated by domain experts.

title: A collaborative diffusion-VLM data synthesis framework for improving fine-grained cotton pest and disease classification
abstract: Deep learning applications in crop protection are impeded by the scarcity and high redundancy of existing datasets, which hinders models from learning discriminative representations for fine-grained diagnosis. While generative AI offers a potential solution, existing methods struggle to trade-off between pathological fidelity and diversity, as domain-specific models often lack variety while generic models suffer from feature hallucinations. To address this, we propose the collaborative diffusion-VLM framework (CDVF), a novel paradigm that synergizes distinct generative engines to synthesize high-value cotton pest and disease imagery. Specifically, our framework implements a two-stage strategy: (1) Distribution internalization: As the primary engine, a stable diffusion model tailored with category-specific low-rank adaptation is employed to faithfully reconstruct distinctive lesion textures, effectively scaling up sparse dataset. (2) Distribution extrapolation: To further transcend the visual homogeneity of seed samples, we leverage a vision-language model (VLM) via in-context learning. By unlocking its pre-trained world knowledge, the VLM injects diverse open-world contexts (e.g., complex backgrounds and varying illumination) absent in the source domain. Furthermore, we construct CoD14-plus, the most categorically diverse benchmark to date. Experiments demonstrate that expanding the dataset approximately 4 × yielded a 13.19% accuracy improvement in downstream classification, significantly outperforming the traditional augmentation strategy, which yielded a 6.91% gain. This validates our approach as a scalable solution for overcoming data bottlenecks in intelligent agriculture.

title: Pest-induced damage detection in corn leaves using improved Faster R-CNN
abstract: Pest-induced damage detection in cereal crops, such as corn, is challenging because of the small and irregular nature of damage symptoms, which can closely resemble plant diseases or environmental stress and foreign-attached substances in leaves. Delays in identification or misdiagnosis can result in substantial yield and economic losses. Previous studies have primarily focused on pest species or diseases. This study presents a task-specific adaptation of Faster R-CNN for detecting pest-induced damage in corn leaves caused by Grasshoppers and Fall Armyworms by customising the RPN with parallel dilated convolutions and an adaptive attention module. A new field-collected corn leaf pest-induced damage dataset comprising 1,390 images, was annotated in collaboration with an agricultural expert. Forty images containing the artefact were embedded in the training dataset to enhance the model performance. The model was assessed using five-fold cross-validation, and four major evaluation metrics were evaluated. The introduction of the artefacts into the training data resulted in an improvement in mAP, along with a reduction in misdetections attributable to the artefacts. Furthermore, the incorporation of parallel dilated convolutions in the RPN of Faster R-CNN led to enhancements in mAP 50:95 (54.06%) and exhibited a high equilibrium between precision and recall, achieving an F1-score of 80.13% with increased computational cost. Compared with the baseline Faster R-CNN model, the proposed model achieved a +1.38-percentage point increase in recall for Fall Armyworm damage and a +1.79-percentage point improvement in mAP 50:95 for Grasshopper damage. This result suggests an improved detection of small objects (Fall Armyworms) and accurate localisation of larger, irregular objects (Grasshopper), both individually and when co-occurring. This research suggests a potential future applicability for farmers in the timely identification of pest infestations, thereby mitigating yield losses. These findings provide guidance for future research on detecting a wider variety of pest-induced crop damages across diverse geographical regions in agricultural computer vision applications.

title: Improving the cotton leaf area index estimation from multi-source remote sensing data based on ensemble learning model
abstract: As a core parameter characterizing vegetation growth status, the accurate estimation of the leaf area index (LAI) is crucial for the efficient management and optimized cultivation of cotton crops. While most existing studies rely on single data sources and individual algorithms to develop LAI estimation models, limitations persist in the selection of feature variables from multi-source data and the implementation of cross-algorithm ensemble learning strategies. This study aimed to develop a multi-source data-driven ensemble learning model for estimating cotton LAI. Three types of cotton canopy image data, including visible light (RGB), multispectral (MS), and thermal infrared (TIR), along with corresponding in-situ LAI measurements, were collected throughout the entire cotton growth period under a waterlogging stress experimental framework. A comprehensive set of feature variables was extracted from each of these three data modalities. Correlation analysis, decision tree-based feature importance ranking and recursive feature elimination (RFE) were sequentially employed to screen and optimize remote sensing feature variables, after which seven distinct data fusion schemes were designed. Integrating 10-fold cross-validation and paired t-tests, the robustness and performance disparities of LAI estimation models were systematically evaluated across varying conditions: distinct single machine learning algorithms, diverse ensemble learning approaches, and varied data fusion schemes. The results revealed that color and vegetation indices exhibited the strongest correlation with LAI (r = 0.841), whereas texture features generally showed weak correlations. The integration of tree model-based feature importance ranking and RFE effectively filtered feature variables, reducing the initial set of 106 variables to a refined subset of 29 variables with relatively high predictive importance. Among single machine learning algorithms, the artificial neural network (ANN), decision trees (DT), and gaussian process (GP) models demonstrated comparable performance, whereas the support vector machine (SVM) model exhibited inferior performance and high sensitivity to data schemes. Among ensemble learning approaches, the partial least squares (PLS) meta-model achieved the best performance, with the TIR univariate, MS + TIR bivariate, and RGB + MS + TIR trivariate schemes emerging as the optimal data configurations. Furthermore, ensemble learning models, particularly the PLS meta-model, significantly outperformed single machine learning models (e.g., SVM) in terms of accuracy, with improvements reaching up to 277% for the trivariate scheme. Independent validation conducted using the optimal ensemble scheme showed results consistent with those obtained during training, where the MS + TIR bivariate data fusion yielded the highest performance (R2 = 0.90, MSE = 0.21, MAE = 0.34). Overall, this study underscores the significant potential of ensemble learning methods for cotton LAI retrieval, which can facilitate the advancement of cotton production management and agricultural decision-making.

title: Active and incremental learning with RAUNet for advancing soil cover monitoring from mobile digital imaging through deep learning
abstract: Effective soil cover management is vital for sustainable agriculture, influencing soil health, erosion control, and carbon sequestration. Conventional monitoring methods are labor-intensive and often fail to capture spatial and temporal variations in soil and crop residues. To address this, we developed a deep learning framework utilizing the Residual Attention UNet (RAUNet) and a unique dataset comprising diverse residue types and agricultural scenarios. Active and incremental learning paradigms were employed to iteratively enhance segmentation accuracy by targeting underrepresented and complex scenarios, reducing the need for full model retraining. RAUNet demonstrated superior performance, achieving an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 93.09%, precision of 97.08%, and an F1-Score of 96.00% for residue segmentation. Validation against traditional dot-screen methods and ground-truth data confirmed its effectiveness in segmenting bare soil, green cover, and crop residue. The model excelled in challenging agricultural conditions, including diverse textures, lighting variations, and occlusions, underscoring its robustness and adaptability. This framework enhances mapping accuracy and efficiency and supports sustainable farming by accommodating environmental and agricultural variability. RAUNet’s lightweight design facilitates its integration with drone and satellite imagery, enabling real-time, large-scale residue monitoring. By setting a new benchmark in soil cover mapping, this approach paves the way for scalable AI applications in agriculture, promoting precision and sustainability.

title: An automatic parameter search framework for agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification by deeply weakly informed deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification aims to automatically distinguish field operation scenes and road driving scenes by leveraging the spatiotemporal features of massive agricultural machinery trajectories and is a key basis task in precision agriculture. In recent years, machine learning algorithms have been increasingly applied to agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification. However, these models typically depend on hyperparameters, and the empirically determined parameter structures often limit the model’s potential performance, resulting in inferior generalization across different trajectory scenarios. To address this challenge, we propose a parameter search framework based on deeply weakly informed deep reinforcement learning (DWIDRL) for agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification, which can automatically determine the parameter structure according to the features of trajectory samples. First, we leveraged deep reinforcement learning to model parameter search as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and developed an automated parameter search framework, enabling intelligent parameter optimization. Second, it incorporates the state aggregation context module, which encodes both global and local states, enabling the model to adaptively search for parameters according to different trajectory scenarios. Third, we propose a deeply weakly informed learning strategy that enables the model to interact with the agent’s output, adaptively adjusting the optimal parameter search policy based on past experience. Finally, to increase the accuracy of the parameters within extensive search spaces, we propose a gradual search mechanism based on parameter space attenuation, which methodically narrows the search scope at each successive layer, thereby significantly improving the precision of the results. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, we conducted parameter optimization experiments on five agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification models across four distinct trajectory scenarios. Consequently, on one trajectory dataset, our method achieves a maximum improvement of 20.95% in average F1-score and 15.31% in accuracy. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly enhances model performance and generalizability by identifying optimal parameter configurations in a shorter amount of time.

title: A conditional generative diffusion model enables joint retrieval of rice LAI and LCC
abstract: The critical growth stages of crops have short observation windows and are easily affected by environmental factors, which often limits the availability of field measurements for remote sensing inversion. This limitation is more pronounced in the synergistic inversion of leaf area index (LAI) and leaf chlorophyll content (LCC), where canopy structure and chlorophyll related traits may show similar spectral responses in the visible region. Such spectral overlap can lead to parameter confusion and estimation bias, highlighting the need for methods that can expand training samples while preserving the relationships among spectral features and crop traits. With recent advances in generative modeling, Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) provides a potential solution by learning data distributions and generating synthetic samples that preserve these relationships. To address these issues, the study developed a conditional inversion for Remote Sensing model based on a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (CIRS-DDPM). In this model, LAI and LCC were embedded as continuous conditional variables and fused into the noise prediction network during reverse denoising, allowing the generated samples to better preserve the joint distribution among crop traits and remote sensing features. A Fully connected residual network for One-Dimensional Sequence Features (1D-ResMLP) was introduced as the backbone to improve noise prediction for tabular remote sensing data. The samples generated by CIRS-DDPM were compared with those generated by the Tabular Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (Tab-DDPM) and PROSAIL. The results showed that CIRS-DDPM generated data had feature distributions highly consistent with measured samples. Models trained with CIRS-DDPM generated data also showed strong validation performance using real measurements. The one-dimensional residual network (1D-ResNet) model achieved R2 = 0.822, RMSE = 1.314, and MAE = 1.087 for LAI, and R2 = 0.735, RMSE = 10.397, and MAE = 8.251 for LCC. Compared with models trained using PROSAIL and Tab-DDPM generated data, the R2 values increased by 20.0 % and 57.0 % for LAI, and by 18.4 % and 31.8 % for LCC, respectively. These results indicate that CIRS-DDPM can improve data support for the synergistic inversion of LAI and LCC and provide an effective solution for data limited remote sensing modeling in agriculture.

title: Multi-sensor integration and cloud-native AI for climate-smart agricultural monitoring: A systems framework
abstract: Climate change intensifies drought, heat stress, and production instability, requiring scalable monitoring systems to support climate-smart agriculture. Remote sensing has evolved into operational decision-support infrastructure enabled by open-access satellite archives, multi-sensor integration, cloud-native computing, and machine learning. This review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature (2000–2025) and proposes a unified five-layer computational framework for agricultural climate adaptation. The framework integrates data acquisition, cloud processing, machine learning analytics, data fusion, and decision-support outputs into end-to-end workflows. The synthesis is based on a structured review of 120 core peer-reviewed studies, complemented by additional foundational and methodological references to ensure technical depth. Comparative evidence indicates that multi-sensor fusion enhances robustness relative to single-source approaches. Optical-radar integration using Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 has achieved classification accuracies of up to 89 % in cloud-prone regions, compared to approximately 76 % using optical data alone. ML-based yield prediction models frequently improve performance by 5–20 % in R 2 relative to empirical regression under data-rich conditions, while multi-temporal ML approaches enable detection of crop stress 2–4 weeks before visible symptoms occur. However, ML superiority over process-based models is conditional on calibration quality, data availability, and cross-regional transferability. Cloud-based platforms have reduced computational barriers and enabled large-scale time-series analysis, supporting operational monitoring from field to regional scales. Despite these advances, reproducibility limitations, ground-truth data scarcity, and reduced transferability across agroecological zones remain significant constraints, particularly in smallholder-dominated systems. Advancing climate-smart agricultural monitoring therefore depends not only on improved sensing technologies, but on interoperable, reproducible, and transferable computational frameworks capable of delivering reliable decision support across heterogeneous agricultural landscapes.

title: SPROUT: AI-based seedling emergence PRedictiOn and trait extraction using RGB time-series
abstract: Early crop establishment strongly influences plant performance and yield, making seedling emergence an important trait in crop phenotyping, breeding, and stress physiology studies. However, emergence monitoring is still commonly performed manually and typically records only the final emergence percentage, limiting the analysis to other dynamic observations. Automated image-based approaches are promising but remain challenging due to the small size of plant structures, heterogeneous soil backgrounds, and variability across imaging systems. Here, we present SPROUT (AI- based S eedling PR edicti O n and trait extraction U sing RGB T ime-series), a low-cost RGB imaging pipeline for automated prediction of crop emergence dynamics and trait extraction. The system integrates instance segmentation, object-detection–based data reduction, and temporal deep learning to estimate the emergence time of individual seedlings from RGB image sequences. The pipeline then automatically reconstructs emergence curves and extracts associated traits, including final emergence percentage, EC50, and emergence synchronicity. SPROUT was developed and evaluated using barley and wheat datasets acquired with different RGB cameras under controlled growth-chamber conditions. In the development and retraining settings, the best-performing TCN model achieved 90.0% per-well accuracy with a ± 2h tolerance, supporting accurate emergence curve reconstruction. In an independent inference-only dataset, the model still captured approximate emergence dynamics, although accuracy decreased to 59.3%, indicating that SPROUT is best used as a modular pipeline that can be retrained or fine-tuned for new crop, camera, or experimental domains. A cadmium-stress case study in two contrasting wheat genotypes showed that SPROUT-derived traits captured genotype-specific establishment strategies associated with growth and metabolic responses.

title: TreePMNet: a deep matching network for registration of UAV and handheld LiDAR data in fine phenotyping of rubber plantations
abstract: Advanced phenotyping is essential for precise growth monitoring and reliable yield forecasting of economically significant rubber trees. Unmanned laser scanning (ULS) from an aerial perspective and handheld laser scanning (HLS) from the ground can efficiently capture 3D structural information of rubber plantations. Registering these two datasets can compensate for respective information gaps and achieve a more complete 3D representation. However, existing point cloud registration methodologies often suffer from low robustness or computational inefficiency when applied to forest scenes. This study proposes TreePMNet, a deep learning-based point cloud registration method. First, a Local Feature Aggregation (LFA) module is designed to generate salient keypoints and distinctive descriptors. Subsequently, a Progressive Transformation Estimation (PTE) module is used to achieve coarse-to-fine registration. The proposed method was evaluated using the public ULS-HLS-Rubber dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that TreePMNet facilitates both effective and efficient registration of ULS and HLS point clouds. The average RMSE, RRE, and RTE values reached 0.09 m, 0.17°, and 0.22 m, respectively. Furthermore, the average processing time for a 900 m 2 plot was only 0.98 s. The R 2 values for tree height, diameter at breast height (DBH), and crown diameter extracted from the registered point cloud data reached 0.989, 0.856, and 0.914, respectively. This study underscores the developmental potential of deep learning-based methods for ULS and HLS point cloud registration in complex forest environments. Our findings provide invaluable support for the accurate acquisition of 3D structural information and advanced phenotypic characterization in rubber plantations.
