title: Deep transfer learning for spectral prediction of kiwifruit quality across cultivars and instruments
abstract: The Vis/NIR detection of kiwifruit quality is limited by biological variations between cultivars and hardware response offsets among instruments. To address these challenges, a cross-cultivar and cross-instrument prediction method for soluble solids content (SSC) and firmness (FI) was developed by integrating a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) with deep transfer learning (DTL). The proposed approach mitigates spectral discrepancies arising from cultivar and instrument differences by freezing the convolutional layers and fine-tuning the fully connected layers. Spectral data of three representative kiwifruit cultivars were collected using two spectrometers. The 1D-CNN models developed using single-cultivar datasets achieved average residual predictive deviation (RPD) values of 3.2438 and 5.8899 for SSC and FI prediction, respectively. However, cross-cultivar validation experiments revealed that cultivar differences caused the 1D-CNN model to fail significantly. To address this, a DTL strategy that fine-tunes the fully connected layers while freezing the convolutional layers was proposed, outperforming conventional transfer learning methods. Using only 15% of the target-domain samples for fine-tuning, the DTL model achieved average RPD values of 1.9361 and 2.2015 for cross-cultivar prediction of SSC and FI, respectively. In simultaneous cross-instrument and cross-cultivar transfer scenarios, when QEPro was used as the master instrument and STS-NIR as the target, the DTL method achieved average RPD values of 2.6178 and 3.6796 for SSC and FI predictions across three cultivars. Similarly, with only 15% of the master instrument’s update samples, the DTL model provided reliable cross-instrument predictions (RPD > 1.5), effectively offsetting spectral shifts caused by instrument hardware variations. Furthermore, Gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis revealed that the 810–1000 nm spectral region contributed most significantly to model adaptation, providing insights into the mechanism by which DTL enhances cross-domain performance through the reinforcement of informative spectral features. These results demonstrate the robustness of DTL for cross-cultivar and cross-instrument kiwifruit quality detection, providing support for the large-scale deployment of fruit quality monitoring systems.

title: Plant wearables in smart agriculture: advancements, technical challenges, opportunities, and a cyber-physical roadmap in volatile organic compound detection
abstract: The agricultural sector faces escalating challenges from climate-induced abiotic stressors, herbivory, and pathogens. Optimizing crop productivity requires advanced technologies for real-time monitoring. While volatile organic compounds (VOCs) serve as early-onset biomarkers for plant stress, conventional laboratory methods lack high-temporal resolution, and portable electronic noses suffer from limited selectivity. However, transitioning to in situ plant wearables is severely bottlenecked by critical research gaps: severe signal baseline drift caused by fluctuating ambient humidity crosstalk, stomatal shielding from non-porous substrates that disrupts natural leaf transpiration, and a computational void in deploying artificial intelligence for autonomous material stoichiometry optimization and real-time deconvolution of overlapping VOC profiles at the resource-constrained edge. To critically address these gaps, this review systematizes the transition toward Cyber-Physical Plant Systems (CPPS) via wearable VOC-sensing architectures. We evaluate the AI-material nexus, demonstrating how metaheuristic optimization and Explainable AI (XAI) frameworks like SHAP and LIME can autonomously optimize sensor materials and validate biogenic fingerprints. A central contribution of this work is a transdisciplinary and strategic four-phase technical roadmap integrating materials science, edge-computing, and Industry 5.0 principles. This framework outlines the engineering of transpirational-neutral architectures and low-power Edge-AI hardware to resolve multi-stressor profiles. By bridging the gap between plant metabolism and digital intelligence, this review provides a strategic pathway aligning with Agriculture 5.0 to build autonomous bio-information systems for enhanced agricultural resilience.

title: LefNet: Lightweight Explainable Fast-trained Network for wheat growth prediction and mechanism resolving
abstract: Purpose: Investigating mechanisms of crop growth through neural networks presents significant challenges in AI-for-agriculture, since end-to-end deep learning models usually considered as “black-box” and lack interpretability. Method: To solve this issue, we propose LefNet, a Lightweight, Explainable and Fast-trained neural Network for crop growth prediction and mechanism resolving. The core improvement of LefNet is to replace neural connections between layers with Taylor polynomials, whose coefficients are learned during the training of crop growth prediction. Leveraging the parallel-friendly nature of polynomials, LefNet improves computational efficiency by avoiding computationally expensive recursive operations, while also recovering symbolic relationships among variables through finite polynomial expressions. This design both reduces model complexity and generates interpretable symbolic formulas that contains insights of the underlying growth mechanisms. Such polynomials are not the actual mechanism, but they consist unique understandings for further mechanism verification. Results: For the experiment, considering diverse fertilization strategies and sowing dates, we collected a simulated time-series data set reflecting multiyear wheat growth in northeast China to verify the performance of LefNet in both time series forecasting and mechanistic resolving. The performance of LefNet in crop growth forecasting surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods, decreasing 7.5% of mean square error (MSE) with 26.8% improvement of training efficiency, and its recovery of relationships is also validated by the existing literature. Conclusion: These results indicated that our interpretable model achieves accurate crop growth prediction while providing interpretable symbolic expressions that may offer insights into the underlying growth mechanisms, suggesting a promising direction for developing lightweight and explainable crop growth prediction models. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/lsl3/LefNet.

title: Study on pig cough recognition and spatial localization based on multi-source noise separation
abstract: Automatic monitoring of pig coughs at the individual level remains challenging in group-housed production systems because barn recordings are strongly affected by background noise, overlapping vocalizations, and unreliable identity attribution. This study developed an integrated acoustic monitoring framework for individual pig cough recognition and spatial localization under pig-house conditions. The framework combined adaptive spectral subtraction and finite impulse response (FIR) filtering for front-end noise reduction, non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) constrained by Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence with soft masking for source separation, and an improved TFA-Net for sound classification and acoustic identity modeling. The proposed TFA-Net adopted a dual-branch CNN–Transformer architecture with time–frequency attention to jointly capture local transient patterns and long-range time–frequency dependencies. In addition, an eight-channel microphone array coupled with generalized cross-correlation with phase transform (GCC-PHAT) was used for sound-source localization and trajectory estimation. Experiments were conducted on recordings collected from 10 fattening pigs across four sound categories, including cough, feeding, snoring, and normal vocalizations. The annotated recordings were divided into training, validation, and test sets at a ratio of 80:10:10, and data augmentation was applied only to the training set to reduce evaluation bias. The acoustic identity database achieved F1-scores ranging from 91.44 % to 98.10 % across individuals. For sound classification, the proposed model obtained a top-1 accuracy of 96.79 %, mean precision of 96.74 %, mean recall of 96.40 %, mean F1-score of 96.56 %, and mean average precision (mAP) of 98.58 %. For the cough category, precision, recall, and F1-score were all 97.09 %, with an average precision of 98.77 %. Under mixed acoustic interference, NMF-based source separation increased cough recall from 50.60 % to 87.00 % and reduced the cough miss rate from 49.40 % to 13.00 %. Sound-source localization errors ranged from 0.058 m to 0.361 m, and independent validation on unseen pigs yielded an average localization error of 0.158 m. These results indicate that the proposed framework has the potential to support cough detection, individual attribution, and spatial localization under tested pig-house conditions, providing preliminary technical support for precision respiratory health monitoring in swine production.

title: TSA-GAIN method for greenhouse environment data imputation based on encoder and dynamic hint matrix
abstract: Missing data in greenhouse environmental monitoring may substantially compromise the accuracy of predictive models and the effectiveness of control strategies. To address long-gap missing data and the fragmentation of cross-sensor coupling features in greenhouse environmental datasets, this study improves the Generative Adversarial Imputation Network (GAIN) and proposes a Two-Stage Adaptive Generative Adversarial Imputation Network (TSA-GAIN). The main innovations are as follows: an adaptive hint-rate function is designed to optimize the missing-value localization guidance mechanism. By leveraging the dynamic balance between generator and discriminator adversarial losses, the hint rate is updated adaptively, replacing the fixed hint-rate setting in conventional GAIN and thereby constructing a dynamic hint matrix to improve the training process. In addition, the model architecture is enhanced by introducing an encoder module at the front end of the generator. By embedding the distributional characteristics of the original data and the spatiotemporal correlations among variables into the latent noise vector, the model can generate samples more realistically and more stably, effectively addressing the slow convergence and unstable imputation caused by GAIN’s reliance on random noise. Experimental results show that TSA-GAIN significantly outperforms GAIN on three imputation metrics, with MAE reduced by 51.8%, RMSE reduced by 48.7%, and the correlation coefficient increased by 61.7%. Moreover, under high missing rates, the proposed method outperforms traditional approaches such as RF, KNN, and MICE, which can better adapt to the nonlinear relationship in greenhouse climate characteristics.

title: KWATCHNet: Fusion of CNNs and BoVW-based features for potato leaf disease classification
abstract: Potatoes are one of the most widely produced crops worldwide. However, potato yield is significantly affected by fungal diseases, among which early blight and late blight are two of the most widespread and economically damaging. Timely identification of these diseases is crucial to minimising crop damage and supporting sustainable farming practices. In this study, we propose KWATCHNet, a hybrid classification model that integrates deep and handcrafted visual features for robust identification of potato leaf disease. A lightweight architecture, InceptionViT, is introduced for deep feature extraction, which combines Inception-Residual blocks enhanced with Squeeze-and-Excitation modules and a Transformer layer. Deep and handcrafted features are fused and refined using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), then classified using a Support Vector Machine (SVM). In the experimental work, four datasets were used, including three publicly available datasets collected under controlled conditions and one newly created real-world dataset (D4) collected by the authors in Punjab, India, under natural lighting conditions, with varied backgrounds and real farm environments. KWATCHNet achieved 99.81% accuracy on the PlantVillage dataset (USA), 99.79% on the Plant Leaf dataset (Pakistan) and 99.42% on the Kaggle dataset (Ethiopia). On the real-world D4 dataset, the model achieved an accuracy of 93.34%, demonstrating strong generalisation capability across both controlled and uncontrolled conditions. Grad-CAM++ visualisations validate that the model focuses on disease-affected regions, confirming the interpretability of the proposed fusion strategy. KWATCHNet offers a lightweight, interpretable model suitable for scalable, practical deployment in real-world conditions.

title: FedAD: Federated learning with generative data augmentation and adaptive parameter decomposition for rice pest and disease identification
abstract: Rice is a primary global food source, but its production is severely threatened by pests and diseases, leading to significant yield losses and economic instability. Traditional manual identification is labor-intensive and error-prone. Deep Learning (DL) offers automated and accurate diagnosis, but its centralized deployment raises data privacy concerns and incurs high communication costs. Federated Learning (FL) provides a privacy-preserving alternative, but it faces challenges such as statistical heterogeneity (Non-IID data) and stringent resource constraints in the Internet of Agricultural Things (IoAT). To address these issues, we propose a personalized framework called Adaptive Parameter Decomposition Federated Learning (FedAD). FedAD employs a strategy based on Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to decouple model weights into a shared full-rank component and a personalized low-rank component, and we introduce a dynamic rank allocation mechanism to adaptively adjust the personalized capacity for each client without requiring explicit SVD decomposition. In addition, we design a resource-efficient backbone model (SepResNet) to balance model performance with overall resource constraints in federated environments. To mitigate data scarcity and improve robustness, we construct a novel dataset (RP15) by employing a hybrid augmentation strategy that combines traditional transformations with generative AI synthesis. Experiments on both the RP15 dataset and the public PlantVillage dataset demonstrate the superior performance and generalization ability of FedAD. On the RP15 dataset, FedAD achieves 90.40% Accuracy, an 86.79% F1-Score, and 87.10% Recall, outperforming baseline methods by over 10% and doubling the convergence speed. On the PlantVillage dataset, FedAD achieves 99.45% Accuracy, a 99.04% F1-Score, and 99.12% Recall, significantly outperforming baseline models. Finally, we provide both experimental and theoretical validation of the framework’s convergence, which ensures training stability and offers guidance for hyperparameter selection. The source code and RP15 dataset are available at https://github.com/DongfuHou/FedAD.

title: Toward intelligent pig farming: Advancing health and welfare monitoring through computer vision–based behavioral analysis
abstract: Modern pig production is increasingly moving toward smart and intelligent farming systems, integrating advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence for precision management. Camera-based computer vision has emerged as a promising non-contact sensing tool for monitoring pig health and welfare through behavioral analysis, given the strong association between behavioral patterns and physiological status. Following a PRISMA-based search, 45 studies were included for critical synthesis on computer vision-based behavioral analysis in pigs, with emphasis on detectable behavioral indicators, imaging configurations, model architectures, post-processing strategies, and deployment constraints. Findings show that posture and nutritive behaviors are the most mature targets for monitoring because they are visually distinctive, biologically informative, and compatible with lightweight object-detection pipelines. In contrast, aggression, biting, enrichment interaction, suckling, and individual activity metrics require stronger temporal modeling, segmentation, or multi-object tracking, which increases annotation burden, computational cost, and susceptibility to occlusion and identity errors. Recent pig-specific modifications to YOLO, transformer-inspired, segmentation, and tracking models have improved performance through attention mechanisms, multi-scale feature fusion, occlusion-aware regression, lightweight convolution, and detector-tracker coupling. However, high reported accuracies often reflect controlled datasets rather than commercial robustness. Critical barriers include limited multi-farm validation, inconsistent annotation and post-processing rules, insufficient anomaly-detection thresholds, weak long-term identity preservation, and hardware constraints for edge deployment. Future efforts should prioritize developing standardized benchmarks, biologically grounded behavioral metrics, explainable and domain-adaptive artificial intelligence, and edge-ready architectures that convert model outputs into interpretable management alerts. This review provides a deployment-oriented framework for advancing computer vision from experimental behavior recognition toward scalable behavioral monitoring and intelligent decision support in pig production systems.

title: C2BPNet: a crop disease segmentation network based on context-content-boundary perception
abstract: Accurate segmentation of crop disease regions is crucial for disease monitoring, quantification, and precision spraying. However, disease spots in field images often show large-scale variation, blurred boundaries, and irregular shapes, and are also affected by complex backgrounds and illumination changes. This makes it difficult for existing methods to balance long-range context modeling and local boundary detail recovery. To address these challenges, we propose C2BPNet, a crop disease segmentation network based on Context-Content-Boundary Perception, aiming to jointly improve contextual representation, lesion-region perception, and boundary refinement. Specifically, we introduce a grayscale-guided geometric prior attention in the encoder, which combines grayscale structural texture cues with relative position encoding to construct geometric constraints. This guides the network to focus on structurally consistent regions and effectively suppresses background noise. In the decoding stage, we use a DSWA-based segmentation head to adapt feature sampling to irregular lesion shapes and recover finer boundary details. We conduct extensive experiments on the publicly available PlantSeg dataset and our self-built Downy-MildewSeg dataset. C2BPNet achieves competitive performance compared with various mainstream CNN and Transformer segmentation models. To promote real-world applications, we have developed a visual diagnostic system to segment field images and quantify disease-spot regions. Our code is available at https://github.com/JLab724/C2BPNet.git.

title: Hybrid AWD-GCN-BiGRU model for edge-optimized dissolved oxygen prediction in recirculating aquaculture systems
abstract: Accurate prediction of dissolved oxygen in recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) is crucial for precise aeration control, hypoxia mitigation, and energy efficiency optimization. However, conventional methods struggle to capture the complex, nonstationary dynamics of multivariate time series and largely ignore the dual requirements of edge deployment and model interpretability. This study proposes a novel lightweight hybrid framework (AWD-GCN-BiGRU) that integrates adaptive wavelet decomposition (AWD), graph convolutional networks (GCN), and bidirectional gated recurrent units (BiGRU). The pipeline utilizes correlation-based feature engineering to isolate the core driving variables. Structurally, it synergizes multifrequency adaptive denoising, multivariate interaction modeling, and bidirectional temporal extraction operations of AWD, GCN, and BiGRU, respectively, thereby finalizing the predictions via linear regression optimization. Natively optimized for Jetson edge devices, the model significantly outperformed nine benchmarks (including Transformers and long short-term memory networks) across three independent datasets. Ablation studies validated the synergistic effect of the modules in this architecture. The model maintained robust accuracy for multistep forecasting up to 15 steps ahead and achieved a single-sample inference latency of 0.3218 ms, perfectly satisfying real-time operational constraints. Furthermore, noise injection tests confirmed superior robustness against 2% data perturbation. By employing the Shapley additive explanations analysis to quantify key feature contributions, the model ensured algorithmic transparency. This study provides a high-precision, edge-deployable, and interpretable solution for RAS water quality regulation, effectively bridging the gap between theoretical modeling and practical smart aquaculture applications.

title: Multi-site dissolved oxygen prediction using physics-guided graph convolutional network in aquaculture ponds
abstract: Dissolved oxygen is a critical water quality parameter in aquaculture ponds, with its spatiotemporal prediction holding significant importance for aquatic health. In this paper, we propose a novel Spatiotemporal Physics-Graph Fusion Network to achieve accurate prediction of dissolved oxygen at multiple key locations within a large ecological pond. It integrates the Environmental Fluid Dynamics Code mechanistic model with graph convolutional networks by a layer-by-layer residual injection strategy, completing effective fusion of physical constraints and data-driven learning. The model further incorporates dual attention mechanisms within a dual path temporal convolutional network, to concurrently capture short-term fluctuations and long-term dependencies in DO dynamics. Additionally, to enhance temporal modeling efficiency, a lightweight temporal attention mechanism is designed, which can dynamically adjust the update frequency of attention matrices. The experiments in pond verify the effectiveness of the proposed models, with mean RMSE, MAE, and MAPE values of 0.8197 mg/L, 0.5866 mg/L, and 1.29% respectively, outperforming the mainstream baseline models.

title: Conventional MFCC and phase-difference MFCC interaction network for durian days-after-anthesis estimation
abstract: Precise assessment of durian maturity is important for harvest scheduling, whereas conventional methods are often destructive or dependent on human judgment. Although farmers commonly use knocking sounds in practice, systematic estimation of Days After Anthesis (DAA) from acoustic recordings remains limited. Most existing acoustic approaches for durian maturity assessment have focused on discrete ripeness classification or single-feature representations, which provide limited information for fine-grained harvest scheduling. To address this problem, this paper proposes a dual-stream acoustic regression framework, named the Conventional MFCC and Phase-Difference MFCC Interaction Network (CPDMIN), for estimating continuous durian DAA from knocking sounds. The framework is based on conventional Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) and Phase-Difference Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (PDMFCC). The MFCC stream is extracted using the standard MFCC procedure from the original spectral representation. PDMFCC is introduced not as a replacement for conventional cepstral analysis, but as an additional phase-aware representation of the same acoustic signal. Specifically, PDMFCC is derived from a phase-difference-modulated spectral representation formed by combining spectral magnitude with adjacent-bin phase-difference information prior to mel filtering and discrete cosine transformation. By jointly modeling magnitude-related cepstral information and phase-difference-informed cepstral cues, the proposed method aims to provide a more informative acoustic representation than conventional single-stream MFCC-based approaches. The proposed CPDMIN framework employs two parallel encoders, a bidirectional interaction module, and an adaptive gated fusion module to learn and integrate the two feature streams before final DAA prediction. The proposed framework was evaluated against eight representative deep-learning baselines, including ResNet, EfficientNet, MobileNet, ConvNeXt, and vision-transformer-based architectures, under the same experimental protocol. Under the present experimental setting, CPDMIN yielded the most favorable overall results among the compared baselines, with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.33±0.24, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 3.82±0.45, a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 2.18±0.23, and an R2 of 0.965±0.010. These results suggest that jointly modeling MFCC and PDMFCC may be useful for non-destructive durian DAA estimation within the current dataset and acquisition conditions.

title: A lightweight, few-shot ready embedding framework for cattle identification using retinal images
abstract: Precise livestock identification is central to modern livestock management system. It enables health surveillance, supporting insurance and liability verification, and ensuring transparency in trade and market transactions of livestock. Various biometric modalities have been explored for bovines such as muzzles, face, coat pattern and retinal imaging. However, retinal imaging offers distinct advantages with its inherent stability and unique vascular structure. This study proposes a lightweight and few-shot ready embedding framework for cattle identification using retinal images that comprises four main components: (1) a lightweight convolutional neural network backbone for retinal feature extraction, (2) a parameter free attention mechanism to enhance feature representations without increasing model complexity, (3) a triplet Siamese network architecture with hard negative mining function to further enhance a discriminative feature learning, and (4) a few-shot identification module that employs cosine distance to compare a query sample against a single image support set. The proposed method highlights the design that operate effectively even when only two labeled images per animal are available for enrollment and verification. This makes it suitable for data constrained retinal biometric cattle identification scenarios. Our method demonstrates identification accuracy of 97.40% under low data regimes while maintaining a compact model size of 4.4MB and an inference latency of 15ms. In addition, the study enhances transparency in the proposed cattle biometrics by providing interpretable insights into the learned representations through explainability and interpretability tools, such as Grad-CAM and t-SNE visualizations, respectively.

title: PINN-AMF: A physics-informed neural network with attention-based multi-source fusion for robust chlorophyll retrieval from UAV hyperspectral imagery
abstract: Leaf chlorophyll a + b content (Cab, μg cm⁻2) is a key indicator of crop nitrogen status and can support variable-rate fertilization. UAV-based hyperspectral imaging provides rich spectral information, yet retrieval of leaf-level Cab from canopy spectra remains challenging because of reflectance saturation, background mixing, and spectral ambiguity. Purely data-driven models often lack physical grounding and can be sensitive to changes in canopy structure, whereas RTM-based inversion is typically ill-posed and computationally expensive. This study proposes PINN-AMF, a physics-informed framework that fuses canopy spectra with agronomic priors and enforces radiative-transfer consistency within a unified learning architecture. The model uses a dual-stream encoder to extract spectral and metadata embeddings and a gated fusion module to adaptively balance multi-source contributions. Physical consistency is imposed by a PROSAIL-based differentiable surrogate (CanopyEmuNet) embedded as the decoder and optimized end-to-end using a composite objective that combines Cab regression, full-spectrum reconstruction, and red-edge position consistency. Experiments on UAV hyperspectral data from three potato field campaigns (N = 414) showed that PINN-AMF achieved R2 = 0.838 and RMSE = 4.99 μg cm⁻2 under stratified 10-fold cross-validation, corresponding to a 35.5% RMSE reduction relative to the CNN baseline. Together with grouped leave-one-year, leave-one-site, and leave-one-cultivar analyses, these results indicate that PINN-AMF improved within-dataset accuracy and retained partial transferability across the represented years, sites, and cultivar groups.

title: Machine learning and physical modeling for water regulation at different phenological stages in efficient green paddy field production
abstract: Influencing both crop growth and the agro-ecological environment, water regulation is a key factor in agricultural production. However, few studies have considered the impact of dynamic field-scale blue and green water migration processes on farmland water regulation. A water–food–environment multi-objective collaborative optimization model incorporating stage-specific blue–green water migration processes was developed to establish the surrogate-modeling framework. Linear, multiplicative, and Transformer-based yield prediction models were compared, while an empirical drainage-based model served to represent the grey water footprint. To characterize stage-specific blue–green water partitioning and support irrigation optimization under different hydrological scenarios, the Transformer model was coupled with field water-dynamics simulation and the NSGA-II optimization algorithms. This framework allows the evaluation of stage-specific irrigation strategies that consider yield, blue water productivity, and drainage-related non-point source pollution risks. Using four hydrological-year types and six decision preferences, the framework was evaluated using field data from Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, China, a representative rice-growing area in the lower Yangtze River region. The model generated coordinated trade-off solutions across the three objectives. Across the evaluated scenarios, the optimized solutions were associated with higher yield and blue water productivity and lower grey water footprint relative to baseline strategies, with average changes of approximately +30%, +176%, and −35%, respectively. The proposed framework functions primarily as a methodological template for site-specific offline irrigation decision support under different hydrological conditions. Although the quantitative optimization outcomes depend on local agro-hydrological conditions, the stage-based coupling framework and optimization workflow can be adapted to other rice-growing regions after local recalibration, validation, and scenario reconstruction.

title: Rice panicle detection from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery via image restoration and pseudo-depth prior
abstract: Accurate rice panicle detection using Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery is a key prerequisite for automated counting and yield-related phenotyping. However, existing detection methods generally assume clear input imagery and rely primarily on two-dimensional RGB appearance, making them vulnerable to motion-induced texture degradation and the strong visual similarity between rice panicles and background foliage in dense canopies. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework for rice panicle detection via image restoration and pseudo-depth prior fusion. First, we introduce the Spectral-Geometric State Space Network (SG-SSN) to explicitly recover task-relevant high-frequency textures from the temporally accumulated blur commonly generated during UAV cruising. Second, we utilize the Depth Anything V2 vision foundation model to infer pixel-aligned pseudo-depth maps from the deblurred images, providing complementary relative geometric cues. Finally, these dual representations are processed by our proposed Rice Panicle Detection with Pseudo-Depth (RPDet-PD) model, which leverages hierarchical pseudo-depth fusion and frequency-spatial structure preservation to achieve precise panicle localization. Evaluations on a large-scale, multi-site, and multi-variety UAV field dataset show that SG-SSN achieves a PSNR of 32.19 dB on a synthetic temporal-accumulation restoration benchmark. Furthermore, the complete cascaded pipeline utilizing RPDet-PD achieves a mean average precision (mAP@0.5) of 91.6 % under the evaluated field conditions, outperforming the evaluated baseline methods. The experimental results indicate that the proposed cascaded framework provides a feasible approach for rice panicle detection under complex field conditions.

title: LCSNet–FedPerGC: An efficient federated learning framework for rice leaf disease classification in the Mekong Delta
abstract: Rice leaf disease classification under distributed data settings requires strict data privacy preservation and timely decision support across geographically dispersed agricultural regions, which closely reflects practical rice cultivation conditions in Vietnam. In this paper, we propose a federated learning framework that integrates a lightweight deep learning backbone with an optimized federated optimization strategy to address these challenges. We introduce a compact convolutional neural network family, termed LCSNet, designed for efficient feature extraction with high classification accuracy and fast inference. Experimental results demonstrate that LCSNet 3 achieves 95.44% classification accuracy with an inference speed exceeding 325.5 FPS, substantially outperforming conventional backbones in efficiency-critical scenarios. LCSNet also maintains consistently high macro F1-scores across multiple datasets, demonstrating strong cross-dataset generalization and robustness to domain shifts. To further enhance training stability and convergence in federated environments, we propose FedPerGC, an improved federated optimization framework incorporating gradient similarity analysis and contribution-aware weighted aggregation. Under both IID and non-IID data distributions, FedPerGC consistently outperforms FedAvg, FedAdam, FedProx, and baseline FedPer, achieving 96.60%, 97.35%, and 98.25% accuracy on private datasets for α=0.5,0.8, and 1.0, respectively, with stable convergence and balanced client participation. Overall, the simulation results indicate that the proposed LCSNet–FedPerGC framework provides an efficient and scalable solution for rice disease classification, designed to enhance data privacy, and demonstrates strong potential for deployment in distributed agricultural monitoring systems.

title: Real-Time Automated Body Condition Scoring of Dairy Cows in a Commercial Rotary Milking Parlor Using RGB-D Two-Stream Deep Learning
abstract: Automated body condition scoring (BCS) can improve the frequency, objectivity, and decision-making value of dairy cow monitoring, but its deployment in commercial rotary milking parlors remains challenging because animals are imaged under continuous flow, variable posture, changing backgrounds, and strict real-time constraints. This study presents a deployment-oriented RGB-D framework for automated BCS estimation during routine milking in a commercial rotary parlor. Synchronized RGB and depth images were acquired with an overhead Kinect sensor during three daily milking sessions, while RFID-triggered acquisition linked each image pair to individual cow identity. Expert reference scores were assigned using the Ferguson five-point BCS protocol with 0.25-unit increments. After quality control, the dataset comprised 25,700 RGB-D image pairs from 1,025 lactating cows. The proposed pipeline integrates YOLOv26l-based cow localization, RGB-D region-of-interest alignment, pad-and-resize preprocessing, and continuous BCS regression using a Two-Stream ResNet18 architecture with late feature fusion. Performance was assessed using an animal-wise split and compared with single-modality and alternative backbone models. The Two-Stream ResNet18 achieved the best performance, with MAE = 0.076, Accuracy0 = 83.6 %, Accuracy0.25 = 95.76 %, and Accuracy0.50 = 99.35 %, while maintaining an end-to-end latency of 95.0 ms. By combining RFID-linked RGB-D sensing, modality-aligned fusion, and low-latency inference, the framework enables automated BCS estimation under routine commercial rotary milking conditions. The resulting industrial-scale RGB-D dataset provides a reproducible benchmark for future precision dairy monitoring systems.

title: Rapid detection of maize seed vigor via multi-branch interpretable deep learning integrated with multimodal data fusion optimized by environmental factors
abstract: Seed vigor is a core indicator of seed quality and field emergence performance. Existing rapid detection technologies perform poorly in field applications, neglecting the fusion of multimodal data and the effects of environmental factors on seedling emergence. Here, we collected 700 maize seed samples from diverse sources and acquired multimodal phenotypic data, including machine vision (MV), reflectance spectra (RS), and fluorescence spectra (FS). Seed vigor labels were obtained via a cold-soak germination test, with continuous recording of temperature and humidity during the process. Considering the complexity of seed vigor, we constructed a Four-branch Combined Dual-path Attention Mechanism Residual Network (FDRNet) to simultaneously classify seed vigor levels (low/high) and predict physiological indicators (fresh weight, germination energy, germination percentage). Furthermore, an AIseed Vigor software was developed, and its field performance for seed vigor prediction was verified via UAV remote sensing technology. The main conclusions are as follows: (1) Multimodal data fusion (RS + FS) with FDRNet achieved the highest performance in seed vigor classification (Accuracy = 96.8%) and physiological prediction (Rp2 = 0.742/0.582/0.642). (2) SHAP interpretation revealed the spectral preferences of different physiological indicators: seed fresh weight was mainly determined by the 500 nm green band, while germination energy and germination percentage primarily depended on the 453 nm blue band, and combined with feature interaction analysis further verified the complex nonlinear relationships between spectral features and various seed physiological traits. (3) Incorporation of environmental factors reduced the RMSE of model by 5%–33%, with RHmax and Tstd showing greater effects on seedling emergence. (4) Emergence monitoring and vegetation index analysis based on remote sensing imagery confirmed that high-vigor seeds identified by AIseed Vigor exhibited significantly (P < 0.01) higher emergence rates and better early growth than low-vigor seeds, demonstrating robust transferability from laboratory to field.

title: AquaAgent-OSPy: an auditable LLM tool-agent system for simulation-grounded irrigation decision support
abstract: Irrigation scheduling in agricultural water management requires balancing crop yield, water efficiency, and safety constraints under inter-annual rainfall variability. Existing approaches − fixed irrigation calendars, numerical optimizers, and conversational AI advisors − share a common gap: they do not deliver model-grounded recommendations that are simultaneously traceable, safety-checked, and adaptive to climate conditions. AquaAgent-OSPy is an A4-class code-executing large language model (LLM) tool-agent that orchestrates AquaCrop-OSPy irrigation scenario simulations, non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) multi-objective optimization, Google Earth Engine (GEE) site context verification, and an illustrative seasonal-irrigation safety checker to generate auditable action memos with full tool provenance. The system was evaluated at two confirmed Korean paddy rice sites (Gimje, Jeollabuk-do and Hampyeong, Jeollanam-do) across three contrasting climate years (403–824 mm May-September growing-season precipitation) using a five-item binary faithfulness rubric (F1-F5). As a pilot unit-audit of memo traceability, not a statistical reliability estimate for LLM behavior, four confirmed-site action memos passed all rubric items (20/20 combined). The evaluation produced four findings: (1) the GEE land-cover and Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) pipeline caught an automated site-selection error and confirmed paddy rice phenology at both sites; (2) in a severe drought year (2015, 403 mm), the fixed weekly schedule triggered the illustrative high-irrigation safety flag (239 mm > 200 mm) and achieved lower water productivity (WP) than the selected low-irrigation threshold strategy under shared AquaCrop-OSPy assumptions; (3) across all four primary evaluation cases, the agent recommended soil-moisture threshold (SMT) scheduling or zero irrigation and never recommended a safety-flagged strategy, while scenario results from all six case-year combinations supported the same within-model water-saving advisory pattern; (4) AquaCrop-OSPy PaddyRice outputs were qualitatively aligned with a published Thailand site (Veerakachen and Raksapatcharawong, 2020; rainfed yield 4.77 t/ha within a reported 3–5 t/ha range), providing a plausibility check rather than Korean field validation. Soil hydraulic parameters were cross-checked against SoilGrids v2.0. AquaAgent-OSPy is intended for agronomist review: it links recommendations to simulation outputs and safety checks, but it does not authorize or actuate irrigation.

title: WMA-YieldNet: A weather-modulated attention network for cross-year winter wheat yield prediction using multi-stage hyperspectral data
abstract: Accurate prediction of winter wheat yield is essential for precision agricultural management and assessing food security. However, existing methods still have limitations in utilizing multi-stage growth information and adapting to interannual environmental variation. This study proposes WMA-YieldNet, a multimodal deep learning model that integrates canopy hyperspectral data and stage-specific meteorological variables from the jointing, flowering, and filling stages. The model improves environmental adaptation through FiLM-based meteorological modulation, enhances multi-stage feature integration through stage-attention fusion, and strengthens learning from extreme-yield samples through a dynamic weighted-loss strategy. WMA-YieldNet achieved stable performance on the independent 2025 test set, with an R2 of 0.80 ± 0.01, an RMSE of 871.74 ± 28.58 kg ha⁻1, and an nRMSE of 15.11 ± 0.50%, outperforming SVR, RF, 1D-CNN, Bi-LSTM, TCN, and Stage-Transformer. Preliminary independent-site validation using the Xinxiang 2026 field dataset showed moderate transferability, with an R2 of 0.75 ± 0.03, an RMSE of 1255.58 ± 71.60 kg ha⁻1, and an nRMSE of 16.99 ± 0.97%, although predictions showed a tendency toward yield underestimation. Ablation experiments and interpretability analysis revealed that FiLM-based meteorological modulation, stage-attention fusion, and the dynamic weighted-loss strategy all contributed to model performance. Attention-weight and meteorological-importance analyses further indicated that flowering and filling stages contributed most to yield prediction and that radiation and precipitation were key environmental drivers. These results suggest that WMA-YieldNet provides an effective framework for multi-stage, weather-aware winter wheat yield prediction under independent field conditions.

title: A Scalable Pipeline Combining Procedural 3D Graphics and Guided Diffusion for Photorealistic Synthetic Training Data Generation in White Button Mushroom Segmentation
abstract: Industrial mushroom cultivation increasingly relies on computer vision for monitoring and automated harvesting. However, developing accurate detection and segmentation models requires large, precisely annotated datasets that are costly to produce. Synthetic data provides a scalable alternative, yet often lacks sufficient realism to generalize to real-world scenarios. This paper presents a novel workflow that integrates 3D rendering in Blender with a constrained diffusion model to automatically generate high-quality annotated, photorealistic synthetic images of Agaricus Bisporus mushrooms. This approach preserves full control over 3D scene configuration and annotations while achieving photorealism without the need for specialized computer graphics expertise. We release two synthetic datasets (each containing 6000 images depicting over 250k mushroom instances) and evaluate Mask R-CNN models trained on them in a zero-shot setting. When tested on two independent real-world datasets (including a newly collected benchmark), our method achieves state-of-the-art segmentation performance (F1 = 0.859 on M18K), despite using only synthetic training data. Although the approach is demonstrated on Agaricus Bisporus mushrooms, the proposed pipeline can be readily adapted to other mushroom species or to other agricultural domains, such as fruit and leaf detection.

title: Weather-based prediction of black locust (Robinia pseudoacacia L.) honey yield and quality: a reproducible computational system with operational deployment
abstract: Black locust (Robinia pseudoacacia L.; marketed as “acacia”) honey production in South Korea—accounting for over 70% of national honey output—has been increasingly affected by weather-driven disturbances, resulting in substantial production declines, notably in 2018 and 2020 ( Kim et al., 2022 ). Such episodes have been broadly attributed to impacts of climate change; however, a diagnostic framework identifying which weather variables, and at which phenological stages, drive the simultaneous decline in yield and quality has remained unavailable. Existing approaches rely either on uninterpretable machine-learning models that require large training data unavailable at the farm scale, or on single-variable rules-of-thumb that fail under multivariate weather conditions. Therefore, we present a reproducible computational system that addresses this gap through three integrated components: (i) two interpretable hierarchical weather indices—the Honey Harvest Weather Index (HHWI) for yield and the Honey Moisture Weather Index (HMWI) for moisture content—derived from five meteorological variables (maximum temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation) across three phenological stages (bud formation, pre-flowering, and flowering); (ii) a generalized raster pipeline producing spatially-explicit predictions from gridded meteorological data; (iii) an operational forecast module generating real-time decision-support maps via inverse-distance interpolation. The system was validated using 570 farm-year records from 95 black locust apiaries (2020–2025) in South Korea and benchmarked against seven machine-learning alternatives. HHWI achieved a cross-validated R2 value of 0.395 (RMSE = 16.85 kg/colony) using three effective parameters and outperformed XGBoost in terms of cross-validated stability, exhibiting a 15-fold reduction in the overfitting gap. HMWI achieved a cross-validated R2 value of 0.668, with a moisture-grade classification accuracy of 96.0% (within ± 1 grade, Cohen’s κ = 0.41). This demonstrates its operational feasibility for weather-based quality prediction. Retrospective decomposition of the 2020 production minimum (18.4 kg/colony) indicated that approximately 60% of the deficit relative to the 2024 peak year (60.5 kg/colony) was attributable to maximum temperature during the pre-flowering stage. Cumulative temperature contributions across all phenological stages accounted for 80% of the deficit, transforming broad climate-change attribution into actionable diagnoses of specific weather variables and phenological stages. The data-driven breakpoints converged with published physiological thresholds for Apis mellifera , supporting the mechanistic interpretation. The complete system—including analysis script, raster pipeline, forecast module, and 22-checkpoint verification—was released as an open-source code, providing beekeepers and policymakers with a deployment-ready, weather-based decision-support system that requires only routine meteorological data. All codes and anonymized data are available on Zenodo ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20612458) .

title: A ConvNeXt–Liquid Neural Network framework for accurate RL disease classification
abstract: Accurate identification of Rice Leaf (RL) diseases plays a vital role in precision agriculture and global food security. This study proposes a hybrid ConvNeXt–Liquid Neural Network (ConvNeXt–LNN) framework for classification of RL diseases using image data acquired under real-field scenarios. The proposed architecture couples hierarchical convolutional feature extraction provided by ConvNeXt with the continuous-time learning dynamics of LNNs, thereby enabling refinement of disease-related feature representations for RL disease classification. The proposed framework is evaluated on a benchmark RL image dataset comprising ten categories, including multiple disease types and healthy leaves collected under heterogeneous illumination, complex background conditions, and varying levels of disease severity. The proposed architecture achieves the accuracy of 97.51% compared with traditional algorithms. The proposed ConvNeXt-LNN achieves competitive classification accuracy with only 7.8 million trainable parameters, approximately 625.79 s per training epoch, and reduced computational cost. These results indicate the potential of the proposed framework for future deployment in smart agriculture ecosystems, including mobile, edge, and UAV-based crop monitoring platforms.

title: Development of a two-step cross-cultivar grape quality prediction model using outdoor hyperspectral imaging in three grape cultivars: Rondo, Zweigelt, and Kerner
abstract: Sensing technologies that are independent of berry-color variation across grape cultivars, particularly under varying environmental stress conditions, are crucial for advancing precision viticulture. This study developed a two-step cross-cultivar quality prediction model for three grape cultivars with red or white berries—Rondo, Zweigelt, and Kerner—using an outdoor hyperspectral camera (HSC). We introduce a seamless soft-clustering approach that groups spectral characteristics without prior cultivar labels, using a coefficient-boosting method integrated with two dimensionality-reduction techniques: principal component analysis (PCA) and uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP). For Brix prediction across the three grape cultivars, the R 2 values were 0.72 (normal model), 0.75 (PCA-boosted), and 0.83 (UMAP-boosted); for pH prediction, the values were 0.70, 0.75, and 0.82, respectively. UMAP-boosted models consistently outperformed the normal model (without boosting), and PCA-boosted models also improved performance. While both the normal and PCA-boosted models improved performance, the UMAP-boosted models demonstrated superior accuracy for Brix and pH across both single- and cross-cultivar settings suggesting that UMAP more effectively captures the local and global structures of hyperspectral data, accounting for the complex reflectance curve variations between different cultivars. The primary UMAP-boosted model outperformed six mainstream machine learning and deep learning models—including PLSR, SVR, and NN—achieving the highest R 2 values and lowest RMSE. This framework enables automated clustering and enhances Brix and pH prediction from outdoor hyperspectral data under challenging field conditions. Future work should adapt the sensing platform for varying sunlight intensity and diverse geographical regions.

title: Co-optimization of productivity and environmental sustainability in China’s maize systems under future climate scenarios
abstract: Balancing agricultural productivity, environmental sustainability, and economic viability is a central challenge for future food systems under climate change. In maize production, yield gains are often pursued through intensified management, frequently at the expense of higher nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions and production costs. This study integrated interpretable machine learning and multi-objective optimization to balance maize yield and N2O emissions under 2050s climate scenarios, followed by an economic evaluation of the optimized strategies. A national dataset of 10,505 field observations across six maize-growing regions in China was assembled to develop interpretable machine-learning models, achieving strong predictive performance for maize yield (R2 = 0.9146) and N2O emissions (R2 = 0.8651). Future climate conditions were derived from Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 climate projections, and Pareto-optimal solutions were identified using the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II. Results revealed a robust non-linear yield–emission trade-off, with environmental costs increasing sharply as yield approached its upper range. Relative to the baseline scenario, cooperative solutions achieved national average improvements of 48.26% in yield and 13.59% in N2O emission reduction while avoiding excessive input costs. Pronounced regional heterogeneity was observed, with yield generally decreasing from north to south and N2O emissions remaining relatively higher in southeastern regions. Cooperative outcomes were achieved through region-specific combinations of agronomic management practices, with yields spanning 6.71–14.23 t·ha−1 and N2O emissions ranging from 0.42 to 6.05 kg N2O–N·ha−1. These findings demonstrate that shifting from input intensification toward region-specific management provides a viable pathway for economically feasible and climate-resilient maize production.

title: Hybrid modeling of greenhouse tomato growth using a scale-adaptive temporal convolutional network
abstract: Accurate estimation of plants’ growth is critical for precise greenhouse control. Current process-based models are often difficult to parameterize, while general deep learning methods often operate at fixed temporal scales and lack mechanisms to prevent physiologically implausible predictions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a knowledge-and-data-driven hybrid model for tomato plant growth estimation, leveraging adaptive temporal feature extraction. The core contribution is a scale-adaptive temporal convolutional network (SATCN) that dynamically captures multi-scale features from environmental data, thereby strengthening tomato plant growth representation capability by adapting to distinct response patterns to environmental changes across developmental stages. The SATCN is integrated with an Informer module to further strengthen its feature extraction capability. In addition, a threshold-based loss function during training effectively constrains outputs to reasonable ranges. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed SATCN-Informer model achieves high prediction accuracy, with RMSE s of 18.52 gm-2 for cumulative leaf dry mass (CLDM), 7.34 gm-2 for cumulative stem dry mass (CSDM), 19.47 gm-2 for cumulative fruit dry mass (CFDM), and 0.30 for leaf area index (LAI). The model significantly outperforms existing methods, including fixed-scale deep learning approaches. Performance improvement was particularly evident in early growth stages, where it reduced relative error by 10.28 percentage points for CLDM, 6.90 percentage points for CSDM, 21.17 percentage points for CFDM, and 6.37 percentage points for LAI compared to the best baseline, confirming enhanced robustness to growth dynamics. This approach enables non-destructive estimation of the growth of tomato plants based on greenhouse-environment and cultivation factors, holding promising practical value.

title: Computational approaches for modelling soil water repellency: A comprehensive review
abstract: Soil water repellency (SWR) is a significant soil constraint in agricultural systems, impacting water infiltration, crop establishment, and productivity, especially in sandy soils. Accurate assessment and prediction of SWR are essential for enhancing soil and water management practices. Traditional measurement techniques, including molarity of ethanol droplet and water drop penetration time tests, provide reliable assessments on point-based samples. However, these methods require significant labour and time inputs to extend SWR assessments to farm and regional scales. Recent computational approaches integrating statistical analysis, remote sensing, machine learning, deep learning, and geospatial techniques have emerged as promising alternatives for SWR assessment and prediction. This study reviews existing computational approaches used for modelling SWR and related soil properties across agricultural systems. It synthesises commonly used data sources, including remote sensing imagery, vegetation indices, climate variables, topographic information, and soil properties, together with preprocessing techniques, modelling methods, and evaluation metrics. Furthermore, the review examines the strengths and limitations of existing approaches in terms of prediction accuracy, scalability, spatial–temporal generalisation, and interpretability. Particular attention is given to explainable artificial intelligence techniques for understanding the environmental drivers influencing SWR variability. Based on the reviewed literature, this study identifies existing research gaps and presents future research directions for developing scalable, interpretable, and data-driven computational frameworks for SWR modelling and precision soil management.

title: Label-efficient structure-aware learning framework for wheat tiller density estimation from UAV remote sensing
abstract: Tiller density is an important agronomic trait related to wheat growth diagnosis and yield formation. UAV remote sensing enables field-scale monitoring, but reliable estimation is challenged by changing canopy appearance, soil and shadow interference, and costly ground-label collection. We propose a label-efficient, structure-aware framework for wheat tiller-density estimation from UAV RGB and multispectral imagery. The framework integrates 3B-SSCL for self-supervised crop-background segmentation, MVDINO for RGB canopy-context representation learning, and GIDVF for guided fusion with multispectral vegetation indices. Using 377 source-field samples from Field 1 collected across four dates, the model achieved R2 = 0.8811 ± 0.0249 under repeated random validation and R2 = 0.8753 ± 0.0141 under leave-location-out validation. Under cross-field adaptation to an independent Field 2, it achieved R2 = 0.8145 ± 0.0959 with 50 target-field labels under a locked target-test protocol. At this budget, its mean R2 exceeded the corresponding values of the evaluated baseline methods when they used the complete 70-label adaptation pool. Across the tested budgets, the proposed framework maintained this advantage, with its learning curve approaching a stable performance level at approximately 50 labels. Together, these results show that the framework can achieve effective cross-field transfer with a practical target-field label budget while reducing reliance on extensive new labels.

title: An explainable deep learning-integrated decision support system for field diagnosis and management of botrytis grey mold in castor
abstract: Botrytis grey mold (BGM) is one of the most economically damaging diseases of castor, causing severe spike infection and substantial yield losses under conducive field conditions. This study developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled decision support framework that integrates deep-learning based disease diagnosis with four years of operationally validated fungicide efficacy experiments. Multiple machine-learning (ML) and deep-learning (DL) algorithms were evaluated for automated BGM detection. Traditional ML models achieved 90–97% accuracy, with a shallow artificial neural network performing best among ML approaches. Deep-learning architectures consistently outperformed ML models, with the Inception Network achieving the highest classification performance (accuracy = 0.97; precision = 0.98; recall = 0.98; F1-score = 0.98; AUC = 1.00). Confusion matrix analysis showed that Inception produced the lowest misclassification rate (9 errors), compared with CNN + Softmax (27) and VGG16 (15). McNemar’s test confirmed the statistically significant superiority of Inception over CNN + Softmax (χ2 = 13.13, p < 0.001) and the improved performance of VGG16 over CNN + Softmax (χ2 = 4.27, p = 0.039). Explainability analysis using Grad-CAM confirmed biologically meaningful learning, with more than 90% of high-activation regions overlapping with BGM lesions, while t-SNE visualisation revealed clear separation between healthy and infected samples. Learning-curve analysis demonstrated stable convergence of accuracy (0.94–0.98) and precision (0.95–1.00) without overfitting. The trained Inception model was deployed through a web-based decision support system for real-time field diagnosis. Four-year field trials identified propiconazole at 2.0–2.5 ml l − 1 as the most effective treatment, consistently achieving low disease severity (9–12%), high yield gains (108–182%), and superior economic returns (B:C ratio = 2.7–2.8). Yield modelling revealed a strong negative relationship between disease severity and yield (r = −0.98), with an estimated yield loss of 13.4 kg ha⁻1 per 1% increase in disease intensity. Overall, this study presents an interpretable, field-validated AI-driven decision support system for accurate BGM diagnosis and evidence-based fungicide management in castor.

title: A novel light-informed computational framework for structure-radiation optimization and allocable space mapping in agroforestry
abstract: Current agroforestry management systems still lack a computable and reusable framework for explicit structure-radiation evaluation, rapid optimization, and spatially explicit analysis. Existing tools provide limited support for light-environment characterization, and the integration of simulation, optimization, and usable-space mapping remains insufficient. To address this, we propose a novel light-informed computational framework based on structure-radiation coupling, including four core modules: (1) Constructing a virtual stand light-field digital twin to reconstruct three-dimensional stand scenes and designing a novel GPU-accelerated, parallel, component-wise differentiable forward radiative tracing simulator (GPU-PCDFRT) to unify structure reconstruction, quantitative light-transport solution, and radiation-response evaluation; (2) Constructing a structure-radiation surrogate model for rapid representation and repeated invocation of attribute–structure–radiation relationships; (3) Designing a light-integrated stand structure optimization agent (LiSSO-Agent) based on an Elite-enhanced Soft Actor-Critic (E-SAC) to generate selective-harvesting decisions under dual constraints of structural quality and light-environment quality; (4) Identifying, delineating, and mapping potentially allocable understorey space after harvesting to support management-oriented space identification based on post-harvest light-environment reconstruction. The framework enabled detailed three-dimensional reconstruction for 50 pure Chinese fir (Cunninghamia lanceolata) plots and effectively captured radiation distribution patterns within complex stands. The generalized additive model (GAM) trained on 1868 individual-tree samples achieved an R2 of 0.840 in ten-fold cross-validation. The E-SAC-based LiSSO-Agent improved three core optimization metrics NL, LightQ, and SR by 83.45 %, 11.33 %, and 22.58 %, respectively, with optimized NL consistently surpassing the initial state and overall outperforming heuristic baselines, and showing high stability across the 50 plots (mean CV = 0.149 %). The framework also reconstructed post-harvest understorey PAR patterns and identified potentially allocable space for the spatial arrangement of light-demanding understorey crops in agroforestry systems. Overall, this study presents a light ecological process-based optimization paradigm that explicitly integrates light into management decisions, enabling coordinated stand structure-radiation regulation and precise understorey resource allocation in agroforestry systems.

title: Soil fertility prediction using SoilGRU-XNet: An explainable GRU-based framework for precision agriculture
abstract: Soil fertility plays a vital role in precision agriculture by directly affecting crop growth, crop productivity, nutrient intake, and sustainable farming practices. The conventional methods of soil fertility evaluation are labour-intensive and even very complex with temporal, soil, and environmental parameters. This work develops SoilGRU-XNet (Soil Gated Recurrent Unit-eXplainable Network), an explainable deep learning framework for soil fertility prediction using multivariate time-series data from IoT-based soil and crop sensors. The proposed model integrates a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) temporal model with SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) for improved soil fertility prediction accuracy. The proposed SoilGRU-XNet model captures temporal dependencies and effectively generates a continuous soil fertility index. Extensive experiments were conducted to evaluate the proposed SoilGRU-XNet model, and the results are compared with baseline deep learning models. The proposed model produces the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) as 3.268 and 1.0114, respectively, with the highest R2 (0.7753). Thus, the results demonstrate the superiority with better predictive accuracy and stability. The SHAP explanations align with the agronomic proofs, such as soil nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and electrical conductivity, which are the dominant contributors to fertility prediction. Furthermore, Wilcoxon statistical tests confirm that the performance of the proposed SoilGRU-XNet is statistically significant (p < 0.05) over baseline models. Accordingly, statistically validated results ensure that the developed model is well-suited for real-world deployment in precision agriculture and decision-support systems.

title: Performance trade-offs between single-task and multi-task in multi-source prediction of yield and grain protein content in winter wheat
abstract: Early-season prediction of winter wheat yield and grain protein content is essential for guiding fertilizer and irrigation decisions and reducing uncertainty in variable agroecosystems, as yield affects profitability and quality affects market value and nutrition. Although multi-source data and both single-task learning (STL) and multi-task learning (MTL) are widely used for predicting grain yield and quality, the conditions under which each approach performs best remain poorly understood, especially when data availability, noise, and measurement or computational constraints vary. To address this gap, we conducted a three-year field experiment in Henan Province, China, compiling environmental, agronomic, and proximal-sensing variables across five growth stages. Seven subsets were constructed, including environmental, agronomic, sensor, and combined subsets, and STL/MTL variants of Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Transformer, and Random Forest (RF) were benchmarked. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis quantified feature- and stage-level contributions and guided construction of compact Top-K subsets for accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Multi-source fusion substantially improved accuracy over single-source inputs, with the combined agronomic-sensor subset providing the best performance (yield R 2 = 0.823; GPC R 2 = 0.743). Under the current stage-aggregated multi-source representation, MLPs outperformed Transformers and RFs across configurations, indicating that compact nonlinear models were better suited to the present medium-dimensional tabular setting. MTL provided the greatest benefit with sparse feature sets or imbalanced predictive difficulty, whereas STL performed better when information was abundant and signals were strong. SHAP analysis showed that agronomic and sensor features associated with biomass accumulation, nitrogen status, water availability, and canopy light interception were key drivers of model predictions, particularly during erecting and early grain filling. These findings further show that the value of STL versus MTL depends on data-source composition and information richness, and that SHAP can be used not only for interpretation but also for reduced-feature subset design. Within the present plot-scale setting, this study therefore provides a decision-oriented framework for identifying both accuracy-oriented and efficiency-oriented configurations, with efficiency referring to feature parsimony, reduced input and preprocessing burden, and computational time for winter wheat yield and GPC.

title: A lightweight keypoint detection network and pose-based error calibration method for body measurement of dairy goats
abstract: Accurate body measurement is essential for dairy goat breeding and growth assessment, yet existing automated methods are limited by slow processing and difficulty in handling geometric distortions caused by non-standard postures. To address these challenges, a lightweight integrated approach for dairy goat body measurement is proposed. Based on our proposed keypoint detection model LEKDNet (Lightweight Edge Keypoint Detection Network), this model integrates Star Block, C2PSM, and Slim-Neck modules to achieve real-time inference on edge devices with only 1.88 million parameters, maintaining 98.7 % accuracy. By combining detected keypoints with depth images, six body sizes: withers height (WH), hip height (HH), chest width (CW), hip width (HW), body length (BL), and chest depth (CD) are extracted. Measurement errors were observed to increase and consistency to decrease under non-standard postures when evaluated on the GBSK2025 dataset of 77 dairy goats, indicating that pose variations exert a notable effect on measurement accuracy. To address this, 16 skeletal keypoints from the body of dairy goat are further extracted to compute pose feature sets, and a stacking ensemble regression model comprising Neural Network, XGBoost, and Random Forest as base regressors with a Gradient Boosting meta-learner is employed to predict and correct posture-induced measurement errors. After calibration, the mean absolute errors of WH, HH, CW, HW, BL, and CD were reduced to 1.78 cm, 1.53 cm, 1.15 cm, 1.12 cm, 1.73 cm, and 1.22 cm. These results indicate that the proposed calibration method achieved consistent error reduction across all body sizes, thereby enhancing measurement stability and reliability. To implement the aforementioned proposed method in practical pasture applications, a channel-based measurement system equipped with top-mounted and side-mounted depth cameras is developed. This integrated system achieves cumulative delays of only 2.5–3.8 s per cycle for image acquisition, body measurement, and error correction. These findings demonstrate that the proposed method provides a reliable and efficient solution for automated body measurement in the precision management of dairy goats.

title: EDM–UNet: edge–aware and dynamically receptive Mamba–UNet for segmentation of Elymus nutans from UAV RGB imagery on the Qinghai–Xizang Plateau
abstract: Elymus nutans is a dominant perennial forage grass on the Qinghai–Xizang Plateau, and accurate assessment of its coverage in early spring is essential for grassland management. Its regreening is spatially asynchronous, such that newly emerged green leaves and structurally intact yellow tillers that remain viable and will regreen coexist within the same field, and both must be counted as live plants. While manual surveys can reliably identify these plants, they are prohibitively time–consuming and costly over large areas, and existing deep learning methods have rarely been designed for this specific requirement. Furthermore, pasture and meadow scenes often present additional difficulties including ambiguous boundaries between grass and background, large variation in patch size, and weak global context. To address these challenges, we constructed a dedicated UAV dataset and propose EDM–UNet, a lightweight semantic segmentation network for precise Elymus nutans delineation from RGB imagery. EDM–UNet integrates three complementary modules. The ESCCB strengthens boundary perception and reduces feature redundancy in the encoder. The DRFM adaptively fuses multi–scale context to capture both sparse tufts and dense meadows. The Mamba module at the bottleneck models long–range dependencies with linear complexity, improving global semantic consistency. Experiments show that EDM–UNet achieves an mIoU of 93.12% with 25.11 M parameters and an inference latency of 14.2 ms per frame, and it exhibits robust performance across varying flight altitudes, providing a practical solution that advances segmentation quality for intelligent alpine meadow monitoring.

title: An efficient lightweight XHP-CNN with multi-task adaptation for mango leaf disease recognition on mobile edge devices
abstract: Timely and accurate identification of plant diseases is critical for effective disease management and agricultural sustainability. However, existing deep learning-based approaches are often limited by high computational costs and hardware demands, restricting their deployment in field environments. A cross-layer hybrid pooling (XHP) mechanism, combining max and average pooling to enhance feature extraction while mitigating overfitting caused by complex backgrounds, is incorporated into an efficient lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN), termed XHP-CNN, proposed in this study. The proposed model achieves 99.3 % accuracy on field-collected mango leaf disease datasets, utilizing only 0.35 million parameters significantly fewer than conventional models. Moreover, XHP-CNN demonstrates robust generalization, attaining an average accuracy of 96.0 % on previously unseen mango leaf diseases through multi-task learning and fine-tuning without requiring full retraining. The model is successfully deployed on Android-based edge devices, achieving a practical accuracy of 90.7 % in real orchard environments. This lightweight and scalable solution meets the growing demand for cost-effective, edge artificial intelligence (AI)-based mango leaf disease diagnosis in smart agriculture applications.

title: HMSA-Net: A lightweight transfer learning model for agricultural disease segmentation
abstract: Accurate and efficient segmentation of diseased regions in infected leaf images is the cornerstone of precision agriculture and automated crop monitoring. Although current deep learning methods have achieved remarkable results, they often struggle to strike a balance between segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency—particularly when deployed on resource-constrained agricultural equipment. To address this, we propose a lightweight segmentation network, the Hierarchical Multi-Scale Attention Network (HMSA-Net), which adopts a hierarchical encoder–decoder architecture and introduces newly designed bottleneck and skip-connection modules for efficient feature extraction. This paper focuses on binary lesion segmentation tasks (diseased region versus background). Comprehensive experiments on agricultural disease datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 83.78% Intersection over Union (IoU) with only 1.28 million parameters, outperforming comparative networks. To verify the model’s transfer learning capability, cross-domain evaluation on marine animal datasets (74.73% IoU) further confirms the robustness and adaptability of this unified architecture. The model has been successfully deployed on an embedded platform; while the performance metrics are suboptimal due to limitations of the development board itself, it demonstrates practical value for mobile crop lesion detection and localization. This work achieves a favorable trade-off among accuracy, efficiency, and deployability, providing our solution for lesion localization in precision agriculture.

title: A physics-guided hybrid framework for peanut nitrogen monitoring: Fusing radiative transfer physics with machine learning
abstract: Nitrogen, significantly affects peanut agricultural yield and development. Therefore, the effective detection of nitrogen is important for crop growth in the context of agricultural economics. However, conventional measurements of canopy nitrogen concentration are labor-intensive and time-consuming, limiting high-throughput monitoring. In this study, we developed a radiative transfer process-guided model for estimating nitrogen content in peanut canopy by integrating radiative transfer theory with empirical modeling approaches. A hyperspectral platform was utilized to monitor the canopy spectrum of 241 peanut accessions grown under four distinct environmental conditions. The peanuts canopy nitrogen content (CNC) monitoring model was constructed using spectrum data, combining a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Nets (WGAN) physiological parameter optimization with empirical models optimized via hyperparameter tuning. Compared to the conventional empirical model (R2 = 0.7544, mean squared error (MSE) = 13.0612), the proposed POSNH framework, a pre-trained LSTM network guided by optimized radiative transfer processes, attained significantly higher accuracy in CNC estimation (R2 = 0.8815, MSE = 5.8432). The POSNH model also exhibited exceptional robustness across data scarce which maintaining high predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.8612) when the training set is reduced to 10 % and demonstrating generalization across independent environment yielding MSE values of 7.54, 5.07, 5.27, and 2.85 for Experiments 1–4. By leveraging Monte Carlo Dropout (MC Dropout) for simultaneous point estimation and uncertainty quantification, the model ensured high predictive reliability, with 95 % prediction intervals achieving 97.75 % empirical coverage. The POSNH demonstrates the potential of applying an optimized PROSAIL, hyperparameter search and modular training to improve the accuracy and cross-environment robustness of CNC prediction, providing a new approach for sustainable agricultural management.
