title: Tea-shoot pose estimation based on light field multi-cue fusion depth estimation
abstract: Tea shoots exhibit diverse spatial poses and frequent occlusion in field environments, making their three-dimensional localization difficult using two-dimensional images alone. This study presents a light-field-based framework that integrates tea-shoot detection, multi-cue depth reconstruction, and point-cloud-based pose estimation. In the proposed framework, a light field camera is used as the visual sensor, and the R3Det rotated-object detector is used to localize tea shoots and estimate their bounding-box orientations. For the detected tea shoots, a light field depth estimation method based on defocus cues is employed to obtain preliminary depth data as prior information. Subsequently, a multi-cue light field depth estimation algorithm based on the Transformer network is proposed to obtain the final depth estimation results. Finally, an efficient tea-shoot pose estimation algorithm based on point cloud processing is introduced to achieve the estimation of the spatial poses of tea shoots. Unlike active depth sensors that depend on projected illumination, light field imaging passively records both spatial and angular information in a single acquisition. The resulting sub-aperture views enable defocus and angular-parallax cues to be jointly exploited, providing complementary geometric observations for weakly textured tea shoots and partially occluded boundaries. On the public light field benchmark, the proposed method achieved an average MSE of 1.047 with an inference time of 0.214 s, indicating performance comparable to that of the evaluated methods. The framework also achieved mean absolute errors of 3.281°, 2.744°, and 1.989° for pitch, yaw, and roll, respectively, demonstrating its feasibility for vision-guided robotic tea harvesting under the evaluated conditions.

title: Lightweight real-time detection of sweet potato virus disease by a hybrid CNN–Transformer network
abstract: Timely and precise detection of sweet potato virus disease (SPVD) is essential for ensuring crop health and improving yield quality in precision agriculture. However, conventional deep learning models often struggle to capture subtle lesion features under complex field conditions. This paper proposes Swin-SPVDNet, a hybrid CNN-Transformer detection framework with task-specific architectural enhancements that combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with a modified Swin Transformer to effectively integrate local spatial details and global contextual information. Unlike conventional hybrid models that simply stack convolutional and transformer blocks, the proposed network introduces three key structural designs: (1) A C2PSA-enhanced convolutional backbone for improved local feature sensitivity. (2) A C3STR module that tightly integrates convolutional operations with Swin Transformer blocks for joint local–global feature interaction. (3) A Residual Attention Block (RAB) that refines feature representations while stabilizing gradient propagation. A field-collected SPVD image dataset was constructed using handheld RGB imaging under real agricultural conditions. Extensive experiments and ablation studies demonstrate that Swin-SPVDNet achieves competitive performance compared with representative state-of-the-art detectors while providing a favorable balance between detection accuracy and deployment efficiency, attaining a mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5) of 86.8%, a precision of 85.1%, and a recall of 75.6%. Compared to Yolov5-v11 models, our approach demonstrates improved robustness in detecting small and irregular lesions, particularly under occlusion and lighting variability. These results confirm the practical value of Swin-SPVDNet for real-time field deployment and support its application in intelligent disease monitoring.

title: Adapting SAM3 for 3D fruit counting with cross-view contrastive learning and Hough voting
abstract: Fruit detection and 3D localization have been shown to be critical for precision agriculture applications, such as yield estimation and robot harvesting tasks. However, real-world agricultural settings can be associated with high density of fruits, strong occlusions, and variable illumination, leading to difficulty in accurately detecting and localizing fruits. Although there exist 2D approaches dedicated for fruit counting, these approaches may easily merge adjacent fruits due to projection effects in dense occlusions, thus limiting their effectiveness. Motivated by this, in this paper, we explore the problem of 3D fruit detection and localization with vision foundation model adaptation and 3D Gaussian-based scene representation. Particularly, we use low-rank adaptation to leverage SAM3 to generate high-quality instance masks with different crops and illuminations. Meanwhile, to address noisy pseudo label issue, we adopt cross-view contrastive learning with uncertainty weighting for enhanced 3D feature representation. Moreover, we devise a Hough voting procedure in the 3D Gaussian space to integrate multi-view evidence of occluded fruits, followed by clustering to estimate the number of fruits as well as their 3D locations. The proposed approach has been extensively tested with thousands of fruits from synthetic orchard scenes, real apple orchard datasets, as well as greenhouse sweet pepper scenes. Experiment results show significant performance gains for densely occluded cases, with the F1-scores reaching 0.971 and 0.977 for plum and mango, respectively. Meanwhile, our approach can achieve more than a twofold boost for 3D instance segmentation over FruitNeRF. More notably, the adapted weights and the post-processing settings transfer from the open-field apple orchard to greenhouse sweet pepper scenes, where only the SAM3 text prompt is changed and the 3D Gaussian representation is still optimized for each new scene.

title: From sky to ground: Enabling autonomous vineyard traversal with UAV-derived navigation maps
abstract: Reliable structural maps are essential for deploying autonomous ground robots in vineyards, yet producing these maps often still depends on manual real-time kinematic (RTK) surveying or teleoperated data collection. This bottleneck slows robotic deployment and can limit the reuse of spatial data within broader digital-vineyard workflows. In this paper, we present an operational aerial-to-ground pipeline that converts overlapping nadir Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery into robot-ready vineyard maps. The pipeline integrates structural detection, metadata-driven geospatial projection, spatial clustering, and occupancy/topological map generation. By extracting features directly from raw overlapping frames, the system bypasses computationally expensive orthomosaic processing, accelerating the map generation timeline. We evaluate robustness across multiple seasons and flight altitudes, reporting map-level performance and robotic deployment feasibility. Using August 39 ft imagery, all five evaluated models produced sub-metre maps; YOLO11 segmentation achieved an RMSE of 0.242 m, while YOLO11 object detection reached a perfect map-level F1-score. A supplementary best-case capability analysis identified a minimum RMSE of 0.207 m using YOLO11 segmentation on March 39 ft imagery. Field trials on a Thorvald robotic platform, over approximately 500 m of autonomous row traversal per generated map, demonstrated reliable navigation, achieving a Mean Distance Between Interventions (MDBI) of up to 161.4 m. Furthermore, UAV data collection was consistently faster than baseline methods, cutting field survey time by up to 94% compared to robotic teleoperation in a 2.4-hectare commercial-vineyard scalability study. These results demonstrate that overlapping UAV imagery provides a practical route to generating vineyard navigation maps that support autonomous deployment under the tested conditions.

title: A deep learning framework for non-invasive quantification of wing and foot phenotypes in live broiler chickens
abstract: Accurate phenotypic quantification in poultry is essential for precision breeding and genetic improvement. Recent advances in deep learning have substantially improved the automation and accuracy of phenotyping. However, non-invasive and precise measurement of specific anatomical traits, particularly wings and feet, remains challenging. To address this challenge, we propose a CT imaging-based framework combined with deep learning to quantify wing and foot characteristics in live chickens. Specifically, we develop the DGCUNet for estimating the volumes of eight phenotypic targets associated with wings and feet. The encoder incorporates dilation transformer modules and stage-specific learning strategies to capture hierarchical representations, while the decoder employs a multi-scale fusion architecture to enhance feature integration. Four CT datasets covering multiple chicken breeds are constructed to validate the proposed framework. On the WB2024 dataset, five-fold cross-validation results demonstrate that DGCUNet achieves a Dice similarity coefficient of 86.41%, a 95th percentile Hausdorff distance of 3.28 mm, and an average symmetric surface distance of 0.69 mm. Furthermore, regression models establish relationships between segmented volumes and ground truth weights, and Bland-Altman analysis illustrates the agreement between estimated and actual weights. Overall, our framework enables fine-grained quantification of individual phenotypic traits rather than coarse whole-body measurements, demonstrating the potential of CT imaging and deep learning for advancing poultry phenotyping.

title: Pre-symptomatic detection of late blight in potatoes using field spectroscopy and backpropagation neural networks
abstract: Late blight (LB), caused by Phytophthora infestans, remains one of the most destructive diseases in potato (Solanum tuberosum) production. Early detection, before the emergence of visual symptoms, is critical for timely intervention and sustainable disease management. However, previous research has highlighted the challenges of consistent LB detection under variable field conditions, growth stages, and resistance levels. This study investigates the potential of machine learning models, specifically a backpropagation neural network (BPNN), for the early detection of LB across diverse conditions. Spectral data (400–1650 nm) were collected using a handheld spectrometer from two potato cultivars with differing LB resistance levels (low vs. moderate) at two distinct growth stages (establishment vs. vegetative). The BPNN model achieved high accuracy rates (>95%) from the first day post-inoculation, enabling LB prediction up to four days before visual symptom onset. When data were pooled across cultivars and growth stages, a BPNN model trained on time-series data maintained an overall accuracy of 94%, highlighting the importance of temporal data in enhancing detection robustness. Notably, the most informative wavelengths were identified in the short-wave infrared (1100–1650 nm) range. However, the use of the full spectral range proved necessary for reliable detection across varied conditions, as no single wavelength subset consistently provided optimal results. These findings support the integration of BPNN-based spectral tools for precise, pre-symptomatic LB detection, offering a promising pathway for precision agriculture to reduce fungicide application and secure potato yields.

title: Physics-informed deep learning for robust maize leaf area index estimation using multi-source data
abstract: Maize is one of the most important staple crops worldwide. Accurate leaf area index (LAI) estimation is essential for precise maize management. However, most existing methods rely on common machine learning models, which often suffer from poor spatiotemporal generalization. To address these issues, this study proposes PhysLAINet, a physics-informed model for maize LAI estimation based on multi-source data fusion. The model takes bi-temporal spectral–textural features and phenological variables as input, adopting a dual branch structure. The physical branch is built on a dynamic leaf area density (LAD) model, while the phenological branch is based on an enhanced logistic model. The outputs of the two branches are fused using an adaptive weighting strategy. In addition, an uncertainty weighted loss is introduced to constrain multi-stage LAI predictions. PhysLAINet incorporates explicit physical constraints, which helps reduce saturation effects and improves sensitivity to abnormal crop growth. Experimental results show that PhysLAINet achieves strong accuracy and generalization performance. It achieves favorable performance on the 2025 dataset (R2 = 0.8866, RMSE = 0.6147, rRMSE = 15.29%) and the 2023 cross-year and cross-cultivar dataset (R2 = 0.7119, RMSE = 0.4663, rRMSE = 30.63%), surpassing all baseline methods in overall performance under both scenarios. The model is lightweight and can be deployed on edge devices for high-speed inference. Moreover, an end-to-end LAI estimation system was designed and validated in real-world scenarios. Overall, PhysLAINet shows strong potential to integrate physical priors into deep learning for precision agriculture.

title: DINOv3 meets YOLO26 for enhanced crop-weed detection toward precision vegetable weeding
abstract: The development of robust plant perception models for precision vegetable weeding remains constrained by the scarcity of large-scale, annotated datasets and the limited representational capacity of conventional supervised deep learning frameworks. To address these challenges, this study proposes a foundational crop–weed detection framework that leverages unlabeled heterogeneous datasets via self-supervised learning and integrates a DINOv3-finetuned ViT backbone into the YOLO26 architecture. A multi-source pool of 618,642 crop-weed images was assembled and systematically refined to 199,338 images to fine-tune the DINOv3 ViT. Linear probing on a multi-class crop-weed classification task demonstrated that the fine-tuned ViT outperformed the official DINOv3 ViT by 2.2 % on average after Gram Anchoring. Although classification accuracy dropped after high-resolution adaptation, detection performance improved in preliminary experiments, suggesting a trade-off between global context representation and enhanced local spatial features. The fully fine-tuned ViT was integrated into a modified YOLO26, serving either as a primary backbone or part of a dual-backbone architecture. A feature alignment loss was introduced in the dual-backbone design to facilitate feature fusion with minimal computational overhead. Comprehensive evaluations were conducted against advanced real-time detectors, including YOLOv8 to YOLO26 series and DEIMv2, on both in-domain and cross-domain crop-weed detection. Experimental results show that the DINOv3-pretrained ViT-small YOLO26-large (DINOv3-YOLO26*) achieved up to a 5.4 % mAP@50 gain over the original YOLO26-large on in-domain images collected in the 2025 season. Furthermore, the fine-tuned version (DINOv3*-YOLO26*) model demonstrated strong cross-domain generalization with mAP@50 gains of 14.0 % and 11.9 % on datasets collected from the 2021–2023 and 2024 seasons, respectively, compared with the original YOLO26. Despite a 45.6 % increase in parameter count and a 2.9× increase in inference latency, the proposed model maintains real-time performance at 28.7 frames per second. The software programs developed in this study have been made publicly available to support future research in precision agriculture.

title: Assessing social stress in Nile tilapia through AI behavioral analysis and biosensor integration
abstract: Measurements of stress responses in fish using a glucose biosensor make it possible to measure variations in blood glucose concentration – an indicator of stress in fish – as fluctuations in output current, even while the fish are allowed to swim freely. In this study, a new method was developed that integrates the glucose biosensor and AI-based posture estimation. Using the Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), variations in the concentration of stress indicator substances in the fish’s body were measured by the biosensor, and the fish’s behavior in the water tank was quantified using AI posture estimation. By integrating these datasets, we visualized the behavioral impacts of increase of biosensor current output induced by conspecific agonistic interactions. Conventional standalone physiological monitoring cannot characterize how an altered biosensor current output manifests behavioral change. When social interactions between two fish of different sizes were observed, the behavior of each individual differed. In addition, when focusing on the fish that was attacked violently by the dominant individual, it was confirmed that the range of behavior in the water tank changed in conjunction with the increase in biosensor current output. The results of this experiment showed the observational example of impact of aggressive social interactions on the stress levels and behavior of fish. The findings reported in this paper are based on a single aggressive pair and a single non-aggressive pair. Therefore, they primarily serve to demonstrate technical proof of concept.

title: Hyperspectral multi-indicator ripeness perception model for mechanized harvesting of “Yulu Xiang” pears
abstract: Accurate and rapid determination of fruit ripeness is an important prerequisite for the autonomous operation of harvesting robots. However, existing hyperspectral ripeness detection models are mostly constructed using post-harvest laboratory samples, limiting their applicability under field conditions. Moreover, these models often focus on a single quality indicator and fail to fully exploit the intrinsic spectral correlations among multiple indicators. To address these challenges, we propose a multi-indicator ripeness perception framework for “Yulu Xiang” pears to meet the demands of in-field mechanized harvesting. First, multiple quality indicators, including soluble solids content (SSC), pH, and firmness, were integrated, and a ripeness quantification and classification model was established using the weighted k-means clustering algorithm, providing an efficient method for rapid field grading. Second, to overcome the difficulty of acquiring in-situ field samples, we employed theWasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) to generate synthetic hyperspectral data labeled with ripeness, thereby enhancing the diversity and richness of the training dataset. Finally, we designed the multi-scale attention residual network (MSA-ResNet) ripeness perception modelto fully exploit the interrelationships among multiple indicators. Through feature learning and key band selection, the model achieves ripeness grading using only four key spectral bands. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed MSA-ResNet model achieved a classification accuracy of 87.10% on the field test set under a single split, with a mean accuracy of 83.87% ± 3.23% across five repeated random splits. This study provides a feasible method for in-situ ripeness detection and offers a reference for ripeness discrimination in harvesting robots.

title: FusFormer: An efficient transformer-based semantic segmentation method for grafting excision point localization
abstract: In the study of automated grafting machines for cucurbit vegetables, accurate recognition and precise localization of seedling characteristics are essential for successful automation. However, current automatic grafting technologies typically rely on selecting seedlings with similar morphological parameters and manual positioning, leading to increased seedling waste and positioning errors. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a novel method for grafting seedling recognition and target localization based on efficient semantic segmentation. Initially, the FusFormer model was developed by combining the MiT B0 encoder with a custom decoder that incorporates multi-scale feature fusion. The decoder includes a nonlinear post-processing multilayer perceptron (NMLP) and a multi-scale fusion module, enabling the generation of high-precision segmentation images for grafting seedlings. Subsequently, a method for grafting excision point localization was proposed, which utilizes segmentation masks to detect the 2D coordinates of excision points in grafting scenarios. Extensive validation was performed on a self-constructed grafting seedling dataset. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves 81.53 %, 87.78 %, and 88.68 % intersection over union (IoU) for cotyledon, removepart, and stem segmentation, respectively, on the cucurbit seedling dataset, with an MIoU of 90.57 %. For the watermelon seedling dataset, it achieves 99.17 %, 91.34 %, 84.57 %, and 96.98 % IoU for background, cotyledon, stem, and block segmentation, respectively, with an MIoU of 93.02 %. These results significantly outperform current leading models such as DeepLabv3+, U-Net, and PSPNet. Moreover, FusFormer contains only 27.4 %, 12.8 %, 38.7 %, and 20.1 % of the total parameters of PSPNet, U-Net, HRNet, and DeepLabv3+, with its FLOPs comprising 16.4 %, 4.2 %, 46.3 %, and 11.5 %, respectively, of these models. The grafting excision point localization method is employed to determine the grafting excision point coordinates for different segmentation results, which are then compared with the actual positions. The results show that the FusFormer(Feature-Fusion SegFormer)-based method achieves horizontal grafting excision point errors of 1.22 ± 1.2 (cucurbit) and 1.67 ± 1.22 (watermelon), and vertical errors of 9 ± 4.33 (cucurbit) and 1.56 ± 1.13 (watermelon). These errors are notably lower than those achieved by other methods, highlighting the superior localization accuracy of the proposed approach.

title: Transfer learning and multi-branch intermediate fusion deep neural network for wheat nitrogen concentration monitoring using multi-scale multi-modal remote sensing information
abstract: The demand for precise monitoring of wheat plant nitrogen concentration (PNC) has prompted the adoption of remote sensing technology for precision crop management. However, most existing remote sensing studies rely on a single observation scale, making it difficult to fully leverage the synergistic potential of multi-modal data due to inherent scale differences among spectral and texture features. To address this issue, this study developed a multi-scale observation framework to fully explore the representational potential of multi-modal remote sensing data. A data-driven cross-modal feature interaction mechanism was constructed to augment information exchange among heterogeneous features, and a Multi-Branch Intermediate Fusion Deep Neural Network (MBIF-DNN) was proposed to effectively integrate multi-scale and multi-modal information. Transfer learning was also incorporated to support cross-year model generalization. The results demonstrated that spectral features, particularly MS-NIR and RGB-Green bands, were sensitive to scale variations (p < 0.05), while texture features showed even higher sensitivity (p < 0.001). At a single observation scale, multi-modal data fusion significantly improved PNC estimation accuracy. Among all models, MBIF-DNN achieved the best performance, with R2 increasing by 0.087–0.588 and root mean square error (RMSE) decreasing by 0.518–0.837%. Furthermore, integrating optimal features across multiple observation scales further improved model performance, with MBIF-DNN achieving the highest accuracy (R2 = 0.943, RMSE = 0.326%). In cross-year validation, MBIF-DNN combined with transfer learning maintained stable predictive performance (R2 = 0.733, RMSE = 0.560%), demonstrating strong robustness and generalization ability. This study provides an effective framework for wheat PNC monitoring and offers methodological support for precision nitrogen management and agro-ecological sustainability.

title: FlowDelayNet: self-supervised siamese learning for automated flow-delay estimation in yield monitor data
abstract: Yield monitor data are widely used for management zone delineation, prescription map development, and on-farm decision making; however, delay in the data caused by sensor response latency can misassign yield measurements to incorrect locations. Existing correction methods often rely on manual tuning, or handcrafted similarity measures that are sensitive to noise, missing data, and irregular harvesting geometry. This study proposes FlowDelayNet, a self-supervised deep learning framework for estimating field-level flow delay by learning delay-aware spatial representations. FlowDelayNet employs a Siamese convolutional encoder trained to discriminate whether two yield patches have similar or dissimilar delays. A dataset of 632 harvested fields was split at the field level into training (70%), validation (15%), and testing (15%). Yield surfaces were rasterized over candidate delays from −15 to +15 logging intervals, and overlapping patches (24 × 24, stride 12) were extracted. A Gaussian-based spatial smoothness score computed using correlation analysis provided the self-supervised supervisory signal. Model optimization combined contrastive loss on Siamese embeddings with regression loss against the normalized smoothness signal. Compared to hard-argmax selection, a temperature-scaled soft-argmax formulation improves delay estimation by computing the expected delay. Across 95 fields, the mean absolute error was 1.24 delay units, with 64 fields predicted within ±1 delay relative to the Gaussian spatial smoothness reference. Embedding analysis showed a mean anchor–positive distance of 0.25 compared to 0.72 for anchor–negative pairs, with 94.8% of sampled triplets satisfying AP < AN. These results demonstrate that FlowDelayNet provides an automated and robust solution for flow-delay estimation across heterogeneous field conditions.

title: EOL-DQN: An intelligent cutting decision of potato seed tubers based on improved deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Current intelligent seed-tuber cutting decisions mainly rely on preset geometric rules, which suffer from poor adaptability, single decision planning, insufficient multi-objective optimization, and poor dynamic response. There is an urgent need to develop an intelligent seed-tuber cutting decision that can adapt to complex seed-tuber shapes and bud-eye distribution, learn manual cutting experience, and balance bud-eye preservation with uniform tuber quality. Therefore, based on the principle of deep reinforcement learning, a DQN-based intelligent seed-tuber cutting decision was first proposed, which realizes seed-tuber cutting by designing the state space, cutter action space, exploration strategy and reward function. Pre-experiments show that the DQN decision has problems such as frequent collisions with bud-eye areas, disorderly cutting of multi-bud seed tubers, and low cutting qualification rate, leading to low seed-tuber utilization. To address this, this paper further carries out improvements from four aspects: multimodal feature extraction, cutting-direction optimization, reward-function design, and decision-network architecture, and proposes an EOL-DQN seed-tuber cutting decision integrating agronomic seed-cutting requirements. First, a bud-eye protection mechanism was introduced to limit the exploration space of cutter actions and improve the agent’s active obstacle-avoidance ability; second, priority was given to selecting the action set that meets the cutting-direction constraints to cultivate the agent’s awareness of sequential decision-making, and the first-cut workspace was limited to the apical region of the seed tuber; third, a layered mixed reward function was designed with the introduction of tuber-area uniformity rewards to enhance bud-eye allocation capability and reduce the bud-free rate; finally, the decision-network architecture was improved to strengthen the multimodal-feature perception capability for seed-tuber contours and the spatial distribution of bud eyes. Experiments show that the cutting qualification rate (Drate) of the EOL-DQN decision algorithm reaches 90.17 %. Compared with DQN, DDQN, Dueling DQN, PERDQN, Noisy DQN, C51, QR-DQN and Rainbow DQN, the Drate of EOL-DQN is improved by 21.99, 16.02, 19.21, 15.65, 14.77, 22.83, 16.96 and 11.19 percentage points respectively. The single seed-tuber decision time of EOL-DQN is 0.034  s, which satisfies the real-time operation requirements of seed-tuber cutting. Platform cutting experiments demonstrate that EOL-DQN maintains a cutting qualification rate above 90 % for multiple mainstream seed-tuber cultivars, with no significant difference observed among cultivars (F = 0.0498, P > 0.05), and the cut tuber pieces can meet agronomic requirements. The EOL-DQN seed-tuber cutting decision strategy proposed in this paper can provide effective technical support for intelligent potato seed-tuber cutting.

title: Full-season wheat phenotyping using UAV-based multi-source remote sensing: dynamic time-series modeling and high-throughput trait extraction
abstract: High-throughput and full-season phenotypic characterization of wheat is essential for crop breeding and precision agriculture. However, the automated extraction of plot-level traits from unmanned aerial vehicle(UAV)-based multi-source data remains challenging because of complex field backgrounds, inconsistent spatial representations among data modalities, and temporal variation in canopy structure. This study developed an automated framework for full-season wheat phenotyping using UAV-acquired RGB, multispectral, thermal infrared, and three-dimensional(3D)point cloud data. The framework focused on three key tasks: plot-level wheat segmentation from 3D point clouds, spatial integration between 3D point clouds and two-dimensional(2D)imagery, and dynamic analysis of phenotypic traits across growth stages. A 3D wheat point cloud segmentation model, termed 3D Wheat Point-Transformer(3D Wheat PT), was developed to separate wheat plots from background points under different cultivation patterns. Based on the segmented point clouds, projection and feature-matching strategies were used to generate spatially consistent plot masks for 2D multi-source imagery, enabling integrated trait extraction from both 2D and 3D data. In addition, the WheatMorph software system was developed to support visualization, automated segmentation, and quantitative extraction of wheat phenotypic traits, forming an end-to-end workflow from data input to result output. Phenotypic traits extracted from 15 sampling stages were further used to construct dynamic temporal curves for growth stage identification, cultivar classification, and trait prediction. Experimental results showed that the proposed 3D Wheat PT achieved segmentation accuracies of 94.4%, 91.8%, and 92.5% across three experimental sites and cultivation patterns. The extracted canopy height showed strong agreement with measured values(R2 = 0.943). Using canopy height growth-rate dynamics as input features, the Long Short-Term Memory model achieved the highest prediction accuracy of 76.7% at the jointing stage(127 days after sowing). These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective and scalable solution for automated multi-source wheat phenotyping and temporal trait analysis throughout the growing season.

title: Simple but effective unsupervised classification for specified domain images: a case study on fungi images
abstract: High-quality labeled datasets are essential for deep learning. Traditional manual annotation methods are not only costly and inefficient but also pose challenges in specialized domains where expert knowledge is needed. Self-supervised methods, despite leveraging unlabeled data for feature extraction, still require hundreds or thousands of labeled instances to guide the model for effective specialized image classification. Current unsupervised learning methods offer automatic classification without prior annotation but often compromise on accuracy. As a result, efficiently procuring high-quality labeled datasets remains a pressing challenge for specialized domain images devoid of annotated data. Addressing this, an unsupervised classification method with three key ideas is introduced: 1) dual-step feature dimensionality reduction using a pre-trained model and manifold learning, 2) a voting mechanism from multiple clustering algorithms, and 3) post-hoc instead of prior manual annotation. Using fungal image data as an example, the results show that, after rejecting some ambiguous samples, the proposed method outperformed supervised learning methods in classification accuracy, achieving accuracies of 94.1 % and 96.7 % on the public and private datasets, respectively. The proposed unsupervised classification method reduces dependency on pre-annotated datasets, enabling a closed-loop for data classification. The simplicity and ease of use of this method will also bring convenience to researchers in various fields in building datasets, promoting AI applications for images in specialized domains.

title: Accurate prediction of wheat grain protein content via integration of genomic prediction and high-throughput phenotyping in breeding fields
abstract: Grain protein content (GPC) is a critical determinant of baking quality, and its accurate prediction is essential for breeders, decision-makers, and the agricultural industry. Currently, GPC prediction primarily relies on genomics and phenomics. However, the integration of high-throughput phenotypic (HTP) and genotypic data to predict GPC remains underexplored. In this study, a novel approach was proposed, termed phenotypic genomic prediction (PGP), which combines genomic prediction (GP) and phenotypic prediction (PP) using machine learning (ML) to enhance GPC predictive performance. The predictive performance of the PGP method was evaluated using a population of 262 wheat recombinant inbred lines (RILs) under full irrigation (FI) and limited irrigation (LI) conditions. First, the correlations between GPC and 29 traits across four developmental stages including anthesis, early grain-filling, middle grain-filling, and late grain-filling were analyzed in both environments. The results showed that the middle grain-filling stage had the highest correlation under FI conditions, whereas the early grain-filling stage exhibited the strongest correlation under LI conditions. In addition, the correlations under LI conditions were higher than those under FI conditions. Subsequently, eight commonly used ML methods were separately applied to predict GPC using GP and PP datasets. The optimal GP and PP datasets were then selected, combined in pairs to generate nine PGP datasets, and further evaluated using seven ML methods to identify the best performing model. The combination of rrBLUP_GP & RR_PP based on the GB method was identified as the optimal model (FI, 0.60; LI, 0.69). Compared to GP (FI, 0.41; LI, 0.39), PP (FI, 0.43; LI, 0.56) demonstrated superior prediction accuracy. On average, the predictive performance of PGP was 31.10 % and 15.13 % higher than that of GP and PP, respectively. Feature importance analysis of the PGP models under both environmental conditions showed that the relative importance of GP (FI: 54.13 %; LI: 30.41 %) and PP (FI: 45.87 %; LI: 69.59 %) differed across environments, and both contributed positively to the final prediction outcomes. This approach effectively captures the complex relationships between genotypes, HTP, and GPC traits. Overall, the proposed PGP method demonstrates effective GPC prediction capabilities and can be extended to other traits and crops.

title: A non-destructive watermelon sweetness classification via vision transformer with cross-modal knowledge distillation
abstract: The quality of watermelon sweetness is essential to non-destructive classification that can be applied to the agricultural production process, but the current methods usually use expensive or destructive measures like spectrometry. This study presents a novel cross-modal knowledge distillation framework as a proof-of-concept for non-destructive fruit sweetness classification under constrained sample sizes. The framework consists of three main components, namely a pre-trained model of a teacher that processes both image and mineral concentration information, a vision transformer (ViT) that is a student component and takes images only, and a feature alignment network that links their respective intermediate representations. The student model learns the composite loss function that combines the classification loss, feature space alignment loss, and probabilistic distribution matching loss and hence maps the multimoded knowledge of the teacher to a unimodal one. The preliminary results of experiments show that the offered approach is superior to the traditional machine learning and deep learning baselines. The provided framework reaches the rate of 94.5%, which is higher than the unimodal and multimodal baselines. Moreover, the suggested method can be applied to the empirical issue of implementing sweetness prediction in a resource-constrained environment because it needs standard imaging equipment.

title: Adaptive feature learning and wavelet preservation for forest canopy mapping from UAV imagery
abstract: Accurate forest canopy cover mapping serves as a fundamental support for forest resource inventory, ecosystem management and carbon sink accounting. The integration of ultra-high-resolution remote sensing imagery and convolutional neural networks has advanced the efficiency of forest canopy extraction. Nevertheless, current approaches still encounter limitations when applied to scenes with complex backgrounds and dense forest conditions, particularly in accurate canopy boundary delineation and fine-grained target discrimination. Such limitations are primarily attributed to insufficient adaptive modeling of canopy geometric and textural characteristics, as well as the loss of critical structural details during downsampling. This work presents GMNet, a dedicated network for forest canopy mapping, which consists of two core modules, namely Gradient Adaptive Dynamic Convolution and Multi-scale Wavelet Range Downsampling. The Gradient Adaptive Dynamic Convolution module adaptively recalibrates convolutional kernel weights based on gradient cues to facilitate effective canopy feature learning in complex scenarios. The Multi-scale Wavelet Range Downsampling module integrates multi-scale wavelet decomposition with distance statistics to preserve essential structural characteristics, especially boundary details, throughout the downsampling procedure. Evaluated on the BAMFORESTS benchmark dataset, GMNet achieves competitive performance against several state-of-the-art remote sensing segmentation models across commonly adopted metrics. The presented model also maintains comparatively stable performance under changing illumination conditions and canopy shadow interference. The proposed approach is capable of supporting reliable canopy extraction in dense forest scenarios with complex illumination and overlapping tree crowns, showing applicability for forest resource assessment and sustainable forest management. The code is available at https://github.com/WangShiK/GMNet.

title: Agri-CPJ: A training-free explainable framework for agricultural pest diagnosis using Caption-Prompt-Judge and LLM-as-a-Judge
abstract: Crop disease diagnosis from field photographs faces two recurring problems: models that score well on benchmarks frequently hallucinate species names, and when predictions are correct, the reasoning behind them is typically inaccessible to the practitioner. This paper describes Agri-CPJ (Caption-Prompt-Judge), a training-free few-shot framework in which a large vision-language model first generates a structured morphological caption, quality-gated and, when triggered, refined once, before any diagnostic question is answered. Two candidate responses are then generated from complementary viewpoints, and an LLM judge selects the stronger one based on domain-specific criteria. The ablations show that introducing a caption at all, even before any quality refinement, is the single largest contributor to downstream accuracy for both models tested; quality-gated refinement of that caption adds a smaller but systematic further increment. On CDDMBench, the full caption-enhanced pipeline yields +22.7 pp in disease classification and +19.5 points in QA score over no-caption baselines (GPT-5-Nano with GPT-5-mini caption generator), with ablations showing caption introduction accounts for the majority of the gain. Evaluated without modification on AgMMU-MCQs, GPT-5-Nano reached 77.84% and Qwen-VL-Chat reached 64.54%, placing them at or above most open-source models of comparable scale despite the format shift from open-ended to multiple-choice. The structured caption and judge rationale together constitute a readable intermediate record: a practitioner who disagrees with a diagnosis can inspect the specific caption observation the answer was conditioned on, though we make no claim that the judge’s written rationale is a faithful account of the computation that produced its selection. The code and scripts are publicly available.11https://github.com/CPJ-Agricultural/CPJ-Agricultural-Diagnosis.

title: Physiology-guided multi-objective machine learning for robust fructose prediction in Asian pear under interannual climate variability
abstract: Predicting Asian pear fructose concentration under interannual climate variability is challenging because sugar accumulation reflects cumulative interactions among developmental progression, environmental conditions, and prior metabolic state. Using a six-year repeated-measures field dataset from ‘Niitaka’ Asian pear trees, fructose concentration at N days after full bloom (DAFB) was predicted from meteorological and phenological descriptors aligned to each DAFB sampling window and sugar measurements from the preceding sampling point (N − 15 DAFB). We developed a physiology-guided machine learning framework using XGBoost as a fixed regressor and three feature-transformation components: a climate gate that weights precursor-history signals by stage-specific environmental conditions, a Richards growth kernel that constrains developmental trajectories, and lagged sugar features that represent metabolic continuity. Representation parameters were optimized under six-fold leave-one-year-out cross-validation using scalarized single-objective optimization or nondominated sorting genetic algorithm III (NSGA-III), targeting the mean, maximum, and standard deviation of yearwise root mean square error (RMSE). The selected multi-objective model achieved a pooled RMSE of 35.48 mg·g −1 dry weight (DW), compared with 55.53 mg·g −1 DW for the climate–phenology baseline, reducing pooled error by 36.1% and interannual variability by 70.4%. Pareto front analysis revealed an accuracy–robustness trade-off and supported the selection of an operationally balanced solution for reliable fruit-quality prediction.

title: Automated mating monitoring and occlusion-aware identity attribution in breeding chickens using multi-stage deep learning
abstract: Monitoring mating behavior can provide behavioral indicators relevant to reproductive management in poultry breeding. However, traditional manual observation is labor-intensive, subject to observer fatigue, and ill-suited to identifying specific individuals within dense flocks. To address these issues, this study develops a framework that attributes each mating event to persistently and uniquely identified individuals, thereby enabling per-individual and longitudinal mating-frequency analysis rather than flock- or event-level detection alone. Because the hens belong to a single breed, are viewed top-down, and are physically occluded by the rooster during mounting — conditions under which appearance-based re-identification fails — we introduce an occlusion-aware spatiotemporal matching algorithm that infers the occluded hen’s identity from interaction-induced disappearance, combining temporal gap detection, trajectory-based last-position estimation, and spatial validation within a dynamically defined interaction zone. A lightweight wearable vest-tag system, built around an occlusion-robust color–symbol code set, supplies the deterministic identity signal. Within the pipeline, YOLO11 performs rooster localization and tracking, and UniFormer performs spatiotemporal mating recognition. Experimental results from one 2.4 m × 1.2 m pen containing 44 Hy-Line Sonia hens and 4 roosters showed that UniFormer achieved the highest F1-score on each of the three independent test days. When predictions from the three days were pooled, UniFormer achieved an F1-score of 91.2% (95% CI: 88.0%–94.3%) under natural class imbalance (≈1:188), while the identity-matching module correctly identified both individuals in 458 of 487 pair-evaluable events (94.0%), with an overall pair-attribution yield of 91.8% across 499 unique confirmed events after cross-track duplicate removal. The system automatically generates structured mating logs that provide behavioral indicators for early warning and reproductive management.

title: StomataSeg: Semi-supervised instance segmentation for sorghum stomatal components
abstract: Sorghum is a globally important cereal grown widely in water-limited and stress-prone regions. Its strong drought tolerance makes it a priority crop for climate-resilient agriculture. Improving water-use efficiency in sorghum requires precise characterization of stomatal traits, as stomata control of gas exchange, transpiration and photosynthesis have a major influence on crop performance. Automated analysis of sorghum stomata is difficult because the stomata are small (often less than 40 μ m in length in grasses such as sorghum) and vary in shape across genotypes and leaf surfaces. Automated segmentation contributes to high-throughput stomatal phenotyping, yet current methods still face challenges related to nested small structures and annotation bottlenecks. In this paper, we propose a unified semi-supervised instance segmentation framework for multi-class segmentation of three nested sorghum stomatal components. We collect and annotate a sorghum leaf imagery dataset containing 11,060 human-annotated patches, covering the three stomatal components (pore, guard cell and complex area) across multiple genotypes and leaf surfaces. To improve the detection of tiny structures, we split high-resolution microscopy images into overlapping small patches. We then apply a pseudo-labelling strategy with class-specific confidence filtering and expert verification to unannotated images, producing an additional 56,428 pseudo-labelled patches. Patch-based preprocessing increases the top semantic segmentation mIoU from 65.93% to 70.35% and the top instance segmentation AP from 28.30% to 46.10%. Subsequent pseudo-label retraining further increases overall AP from 46.10% to 49.20% for Mask R-CNN with ConvNeXt-V2. These results demonstrate that combining patch-based preprocessing with semi-supervised learning significantly improves the segmentation of fine stomatal structures. The proposed framework supports scalable extraction of stomatal traits and facilitates broader adoption of AI-driven phenotyping in crop science.

title: Harvesting sequence optimization for clustered strawberries using a fruit-level harvesting difficulty score
abstract: Existing fruit-harvesting sequence planning mainly focuses on minimizing manipulator travel distance, while fruit-specific harvesting difficulty is rarely considered in clustered environments. This study proposed a difficulty-aware harvesting-sequence optimization framework integrating fruit-level harvesting difficulty score (HDS) prediction, dynamic HDS updating, and weighted-sum multi-criteria sequence planning. A two-stage convolutional neural network (CNN)-based vision framework was developed to estimate fruit-level HDS, and the harvesting sequence was re-optimized after each virtual fruit removal using genetic-algorithm-based (MOP-GA) and simulated-annealing-based (MOP-SA) solvers. The HDS regression model achieved an MAE of 6.55% and an R2 of 72.39%. In offline experiments, MOP-GA reduced the average HDS per fruit to 0.282, compared with 0.291 for TSP and 0.297 for bottom-up. Indoor robot experiments across nine strawberry-cluster scenes further showed lower HDS values for MOP-GA (0.197) and MOP-SA (0.204) than for TSP (0.235) and bottom-up (0.237), with all four proposed-versus-baseline comparisons remaining significant after Holm correction. MOP-GA also achieved a lower observed failure rate than TSP (19.11% vs. 26.67%), although the overall difference in failure probability among methods was not statistically significant. These results indicated that dynamically incorporating fruit-level harvesting difficulty can improve harvesting-sequence feasibility in clustered environments, while the increased computational cost remained a limitation for real-time deployment.

title: NFGTN: A node-fusion graph transformer network for non-destructive estimation of glucoraphanin content in broccoli leaves using RGB-D imaging
abstract: Non-destructive estimation of crop biochemical traits is important for quality evaluation, precision cultivation, and nutritional breeding. As a major glucosinolate in broccoli, glucoraphanin (GRA) is an important indicator of nutritional and functional quality, yet its quantification still relies mainly on destructive chemical analysis. To address this limitation, this study proposes a node-fusion graph transformer network (NFGTN) for estimating GRA content in broccoli leaves using paired red–green–blue (RGB) images and aligned depth information, collectively referred to as RGB-D data. The proposed RGB-D framework integrates a visual backbone, offline graph construction, node-level multimodal fusion, and graph propagation with joint local–global readout within a unified regression architecture. Specifically, an offline graph is constructed to establish explicit correspondence between visual patch features and local plant regions, while a node fusion module is designed to adaptively integrate RGB appearance cues with depth-derived geometric descriptors. On this basis, graph propagation, weighted local pooling, and iterative global readout are employed to jointly model local structural dependencies and graph-level contextual information for final prediction. Experimental results under five-fold cross-validation show that the proposed NFGTN achieved the lowest RMSE of 0.1369, the highest R2 of 0.9232, and the highest RPD of 3.8239 among the compared RGB and RGB-D methods, with an MAE of 0.1098. Additional comparisons with hyperspectral models based on mean spectral representations showed that NFGTN achieved competitive sample-level GRA prediction performance under the present experimental setting.

title: SpecMCR: A multi-channel spectral regression framework with clustering and GAN-based augmentation for accurate grape sugar prediction
abstract: Accurate estimation of grape sugar content is essential for evaluating fruit maturity and wine quality, yet conventional spectral models often struggle with large variations caused by grape cultivars and environmental conditions. To overcome these challenges, we propose SpecMCR, a spectral multi-channel regression framework that combines unsupervised clustering, score-based conditional GAN (SCGAN) augmentation, and channel-wise regression. The clustering module partitions the spectra into three structurally stable channels, effectively reducing intra-class variability. SCGAN further refines these channels by generating high-quality spectra that enhance boundary regions. With these components, SpecMCR achieves an RMSE of 19.70 and an R2 of 0.85 on the test set while the RMSE values of PLS and SVM above 26, it also outperforms deep models including Inception-v1 and ResNet18, which show test RMSE values around 26.78 and 23.48 respectively. The results demonstrate that SpecMCR captures the heterogeneous structure of spectral data more effectively than single-channel and deep learning baselines, offering a robust and automated solution for agricultural spectroscopy.

title: A physical-context-conditioned multimodal fusion network for estimating maize canopy nitrogen content using multi-source UAV remote sensing data
abstract: Maize canopy nitrogen content (CNC) is a key indicator of crop nitrogen nutritional status. However, under complex field conditions, single-spectral models are susceptible to spectral saturation and environmental heterogeneity, limiting their estimation accuracy and generalization. Many multimodal approaches use concatenation, fixed weighting, or attention across parallel modality streams, but heterogeneous modalities are commonly treated as parallel predictors, failing to leverage observations from heterogeneous modalities to condition spectral representation learning and regulate branch-level contributions. To address this limitation, this study proposes a Physical-Context-Conditioned Multimodal Neural Network (PCCMN) with an asymmetric, two-stage physical-context-conditioned fusion strategy for maize CNC estimation. Rather than treating hyperspectral, LiDAR, and thermal infrared observations as equivalent inputs, PCCMN treats hyperspectral features as the primary information source for CNC estimation, while canopy structure and thermal status are jointly encoded as sample-specific physical context. Instead of being directly concatenated with spectral features, this physical context is used as a query to selectively aggregate nitrogen-sensitive spectral tokens. An adaptive gating mechanism subsequently regulates the relative contributions of the context-conditioned spectral representation and the physical context representation. This study analyzed data from field experiments conducted in two consecutive years, 2024 and 2025. PCCMN consistently outperformed the comparative models, across the three growth stages and both year-specific held-out test sets, with mean R2 values of 0.79–0.85 and RMSE values of 0.17–0.65. Ablation experiments demonstrated that the performance gains arose from the coordinated effects of multimodal complementarity, context-conditioned spectral selection, and adaptive gating-based fusion rather than from simply adding auxiliary modalities. Gating analysis showed stronger weighting toward the context-conditioned spectral representation in the trumpet-stage model and more balanced allocation between the spectral and physical-context representations in the tasseling- and grain-filling-stage models. SHAP analysis further showed that model decisions were primarily associated with stage-dependent spectral responses concentrated in the red-edge region.These results demonstrate that organizing heterogeneous UAV observations according to their functional roles and dynamically regulating their information flow can support more consistent CNC estimation under phenological and interannual variability. PCCMN therefore provides a physical-context-conditioned multimodal framework for field-scale crop nitrogen monitoring.

title: MPRT-DETR: multi-platform real-time rice panicle detection and counting based on the transformer method and complex field imagery
abstract: Automatic and accurate detection and counting of rice panicles provide an important phenotypic basis for high-throughput rice monitoring and yield-related trait assessment. However, the accuracy and robustness of existing methods are often compromised by the challenges inherent to complex field conditions. These challenges include scale variations across multi-platform imagery (proximal vs. UAV), morphological diversity across cultivars and growth stages, and environmental effects such as uneven illumination and dense canopy occlusion. To overcome these hurdles, we constructed a comprehensive, multi-platform RGB image dataset that captures the period from heading to maturity for multiple cultivars, and encompasses a broad range of phenotypic variations and environmental conditions representative of real-world agricultural settings. In addition, we propose the Multi-Platform Real-Time Rice Panicle Detection and Counting Transformer (MPRT-DETR) for rice panicle detection and counting under complex field conditions. The proposed MPRT-DETR is developed as a task-oriented adaptation of RT-DETR for complex field rice panicle detection and incorporates four coordinated modifications: (1) an FEM that extends an illumination-adaptive enhancement framework by integrating WTConv and training-time label enhancement; (2) a FasterNet-based feature extraction network augmented with EMA; (3) an LBFM that reorganizes multi-scale aggregation through bidirectional feature fusion and lightweight DySample and ADown operators; and (4) a lightweight QEH designed in this study for quantity-aware adaptive query-capacity allocation. Comprehensive evaluations show that, compared with the baseline RT-DETR, MPRT-DETR reduces the parameter count by 22.30 % and GFLOPs by 32.50 %, while mAP50 and mAP50–95 increase by 11.52 and 16.43 percentage points, respectively. For panicle counting, the model achieves a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9453, a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 16.2, and a relative Root Mean Square Error (rRMSE) of 14.43 % on the primary test set. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of MPRT-DETR for rice panicle detection and counting under diverse field imaging conditions. Overall, MPRT-DETR provides an efficient approach for image-based rice panicle phenotyping and may serve as an upstream component for future plot-level yield-related trait assessment and breeding applications. Our code and pre-trained models are available at https://github.com/Agricultural-DL/MPRT-DETR.

title: PhySinc-Net: A physics-informed interpretable deep learning architecture for non-contact respiratory rate monitoring in dairy goats
abstract: Respiratory rate (RR) is an important indicator of animal health and thermal status, but its non-contact estimation in small ruminants remains challenging because thoracoabdominal motion is weak, quasi-periodic, and susceptible to body-motion artifacts and environmental clutter. Although 77-GHz frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar enables contact-free sensing independently of ambient illumination, respiratory monitoring in dairy goats is complicated by weak radar reflections, spontaneous body movements, and non-stationary interference. Existing deep-learning approaches commonly rely on black-box feature extraction and lack physiological inductive biases, limiting their robustness in separating weak respiratory harmonics from broadband motion noise. To address these limitations, this study proposes PhySinc-Net, a physics-informed and interpretable framework for non-contact RR monitoring in dairy goats. The model integrates a parameterized Sinc-based spectral front-end to constrain feature learning within plausible respiratory frequency bands, a Frequency-Amplitude Attention module to enhance weak periodic components, and multi-scale temporal branches to capture respiratory dynamics across complementary receptive fields. A Time-Reversal Consistency training strategy exploits the invariance of respiratory frequency under temporal reversal, improving resistance to transient and directional motion artifacts without increasing inference cost. PhySinc-Net was developed using 210 raw ADC radar recordings collected from 20 dairy goats under a controlled channel-based setting and was additionally evaluated on two public human respiratory datasets. In the sample-level held-out test set, PhySinc-Net achieved a mean absolute error of 4.58 breaths/min (bpm), a root mean squared error of 5.97 bpm, and an R2 of 0.95, reducing MAE by 7.85 % and RMSE by 14.71 % compared with the strongest CNN + Transformer. The evaluations on the human datasets provided preliminary evidence of transferability across heterogeneous radar respiratory datasets. With 36,421 trainable parameters, PhySinc-Net offers a compact architecture that warrants future evaluation on embedded hardware. Overall, the proposed framework provides a physics-guided solution to short-duration, non-contact RR estimation in dairy goats under controlled channel-based acquisition conditions.

title: Latent-space feature reconstruction-enhanced semantic segmentation for agricultural field roads under visual degradation
abstract: Visual perception for autonomous agricultural machinery on unstructured inter-field transfer roads is often affected by drastic illumination variations and dust contamination. These degradations reduce the robustness of segmentation models in real-world field-road environments. To address these challenges, we propose LDRSeg, a robust semantic segmentation framework that improves robustness under degradation conditions by reconstructing degraded features in the latent space. First, to expand degraded data under realistic acquisition constraints, a GAN-based degradation synthesis pipeline is constructed to generate multi-type degraded samples while preserving geometry and semantic consistency. Then, a feature reconstruction module guided by a pre-trained latent diffusion prior is introduced to perform implicit denoising and distribution bias correction in the intermediate feature stream, and a progressive decoupled training protocol is adopted to learn a robust mapping from degraded features to clean semantics. Experiments on real degraded test sets show that LDRSeg achieves 75.80 % mIoU and 84.41 % mAcc, outperforming the baseline by 3.17 % and 3.04 %, respectively. It also reduces the Relative Corruption Error (RCE) to 4.20 % for mIoU and 2.97 % for mAcc. In heavy-dust scenes, LDRSeg improves mIoU by 5.19 %. Beyond the primary architecture, cross-architecture experiments further show that the proposed module can improve degraded-scene robustness when integrated into the evaluated CNN- and Transformer-based segmentation architectures.

title: A lightweight dual-task transformer framework with geometry-constrained path extraction for autonomous under-canopy navigation in maize fields
abstract: To address the challenges of reliable perception and navigation in under-canopy maize environments, this study proposes a lightweight dual-task perception-to-navigation framework that jointly performs road and obstacle segmentation and generates geometry-constrained navigation lines. Experiments on a self-collected dataset containing 5051 annotated images show that UC-TwinLiteFormer achieves 95.3 % road mIoU and 86.7 % obstacle mIoU with only 1.46 M parameters, demonstrating a favourable balance between segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. Building upon the segmentation results, the proposed GCP-NLE converts semantic predictions into structured navigation paths under obstacle-free, non-bypassable, and bypassable scenarios. Jetson Nano deployment and closed-loop navigation simulation further demonstrate the effectiveness and practical feasibility of the complete perception-to-navigation pipeline. Overall, the proposed framework provides an efficient and interpretable solution for autonomous under-canopy navigation of agricultural robots. Future work will further validate the system through full-scale field robot experiments and investigate cross-region generalisation under more diverse agricultural environments. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/ayi192/UC-TwinLiteFormer.

title: PineWilt-MultiSeg: Joint spatial–spectral learning enables precise detection of pine wilt disease
abstract: Pine wilt disease (PWD) poses a serious threat to pine forest ecosystems, highlighting the need for timely and accurate identification of affected trees to support targeted removal and epidemic control. UAV remote sensing combined with deep learning has shown considerable potential for individual-tree-level PWD monitoring. However, most existing studies rely on unimodal imagery, which may provide insufficient information for distinguishing diseased trees from complex forest backgrounds. Although RGB imagery captures detailed spatial, textural, and morphological features, multispectral imagery provides additional information on vegetation pigments, canopy water status, and physiological stress. Integrating these complementary information sources may therefore improve detection accuracy and model robustness. Nevertheless, publicly accessible benchmark datasets providing co-registered RGB and multispectral imagery with pixel-level annotations for PWD remain scarce, limiting systematic model development and comparison. To help address this gap, we constructed PineWilt-MultiSeg, a high-resolution multimodal benchmark dataset comprising 3938 spatially aligned pairs of RGB and 10-band multispectral images with pixel-level semantic annotations. The dataset covers pine trees at the middle and late stages of PWD under diverse canopy conditions and forest backgrounds. Five representative semantic segmentation architectures — SegFormer, PSPNet, Twins-PCPVT, DeepLabv3+, and EncNet — were evaluated to establish unimodal RGB and multispectral benchmarks, while the CMX architecture was employed to assess multimodal feature fusion. Experimental results indicate that multimodal fusion provides consistent and measurable performance gains over unimodal RGB and multispectral inputs, with mIoU improvements of 1.75% and 5.95%, respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of joint spatial–spectral information integration. Additionally, the influence of spatial resolution on detection accuracy was investigated, and the physical spectral characteristics of diseased trees were analyzed, confirming the superiority of multimodal data in jointly leveraging spatial and spectral information. This study provides a solid data foundation and methodological reference for multimodal detection of pine wilt disease. The dataset and models will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/caudjcc/PineWilt-MultiSeg.git

title: YOLOv8-MST: a lightweight and efficient real-time detection and counting deep learning algorithm for double-grain peanut seeding
abstract: Double‑seed precision hill‑drop seeding is a critical technique for ensuring effective peanut emergence, where precise seeding quality relies heavily on high‑performance seed metering devices and real‑time operational monitoring. Traditional manual monitoring is inefficient for enclosed, high-speed air-suction duckbill seeders. Conventional photoelectric sensors fail to identify seed number per hill, seed damage, and impurity inclusion, while existing machine vision methods suffer from excessive computational overhead and cannot support high‑precision real‑time monitoring on low‑cost embedded devices. To address these issues, this paper proposed an edge computing-assisted deep learning monitoring method for peanut hill-drop seeding quality and developed an improved YOLOv8s-based detection and counting algorithm (YOLOv8-MST). All data collection and model training were conducted on a test bench at Qingdao University of Technology, Qingdao, China. A total of 11,130 peanut seeding images were collected and partitioned at the video session level to avoid temporal data leakage, yielding 7,769 training, 2,277 validation, and 1,084 test images following a 70%:20%:10% split. Precision, recall, AP, and mAP were adopted as the model evaluation metrics. In the network design, MobileNetV3 was applied as the lightweight backbone for seed feature extraction. The parameter-free SimAM attention mechanism was introduced to enhance feature representation of stacked and damaged seeds, and Focal_GIoU was used for bounding box regression. Furthermore, the Kalman filter combined with the Hungarian algorithm was embedded to optimize object tracking and improve counting accuracy. Experimental results showed that the proposed YOLOv8‑MST achieved a competitive performance with a compact size of 3.88 M parameters, a mAP of 92.9%, and an average inference speed of 15.7 FPS. Compared with the original YOLOv8s, the frame rate was improved by 54.05%. The proposed algorithm accurately identified seeding status and counted qualified holes, achieving promising accuracy and real-time capability in complex scenarios, which satisfied the on-site real-time monitoring requirements of peanut double-seed hill-drop seeding.

title: A physics-informed, behavior-aware digital twin for robust multimodal forecasting of core body temperature in precision livestock farming
abstract: Precision livestock farming requires accurate and timely heat stress prediction to ensure animal welfare and optimize farm management. This study presents a physics-informed digital twin (DT) framework combined with an uncertainty-aware, expert-weighted stacked ensemble for multimodal forecasting of Core Body Temperature (CBT) in dairy cattle. Using the high-frequency, heterogeneous MmCows dataset, the DT integrates an ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based thermoregulation model that simulates metabolic heat production and dissipation, a Gaussian process for capturing cow-specific deviations, a Kalman filter for aligning predictions with real-time sensor data, and a behavioral Markov chain that models activity-state transitions under varying environmental conditions. The DT outputs key physiological indicators, such as predicted CBT, heat stress probability, and behavioral state distributions are fused with raw sensor data and enriched through multi-scale temporal analysis and cross-modal feature engineering to form a comprehensive feature set. The predictive methodology is designed in a three-stage stacked ensemble, where stage 1 trains modality-specific LightGBM ‘expert’ models on distinct feature groups, stage 2 collects their predictions as meta-features, and at stage 3 Optuna-tuned LightGBM meta-model yields the final CBT forecast. Predictive uncertainty is quantified via bootstrapping and validated using Prediction Interval Coverage Probability (PICP). Ablation analysis confirms that incorporating DT-derived features and multimodal fusion substantially enhances performance. The proposed framework achieves a cross-validated R 2 of 0.783, F1 score of 84.25% and PICP of 92.38% for 2-hour ahead forecasting, providing a robust, uncertainty-aware, and physically principled system for early heat stress detection and precision livestock management.

title: From sensing to modeling: machine learning-driven wearable humidity sensors for plant water status monitoring
abstract: Plant water status is a critical phenotypic trait underlying precision agriculture and crop health assessment. Yet, continuous, in situ, and non-invasive monitoring under field conditions remains challenging due to limitations in sensor adhesion stability, environmental interference, and the complexity of interpreting sensor signals. Flexible wearable humidity sensors that can attach to leaf and stem surfaces provide real-time access to near-surface moisture dynamics and transpiration activity. As these sensors generate high-dimensional, strongly coupled, and nonlinear datasets, machine learning has emerged as a promising tool for extracting features and predicting plant water status. However, practical deployment faces obstacles such as signal drift, environmental noise, and biofouling, while model generalizability and interpretability remain key barriers to widespread adoption. This review first systematically outlines the physiological mechanisms governing plant water regulation and summarizes recent advances in materials and device innovations for wearable humidity sensors. It then critically examines the integration of machine learning in sensor data analysis and modeling. Finally, we propose a unified conceptual framework that bridges plant water regulation, sensor-based perception, and data-driven analysis, highlighting how algorithmic strategies can enhance system robustness and enable multiscale characterization. This framework lays a theoretical foundation for intelligent monitoring and precision regulation under real-world agricultural conditions.

title: Use of smartphone images in the evaluation of weed control with glyphosate: A computational approach using Random Forest
abstract: The evaluation of herbicide control efficacy is essential in integrated weed management, and this information is fed back into the database for future crop protection actions. The evaluation of weed control using herbicides is carried out based on on-site visual evaluations, which can be time-consuming and imprecise. In this study, models capable of evaluating the efficacy of Urochloa brizantha control by glyphosate were proposed using computational image analysis with Random Forest. The images were obtained with a smartphone in an area with U. brizantha infestation desiccated by glyphosate. To stratify the control response, glyphosate doses of 0, 144, 288, 576, 864, 1152, and 1440 g a.e. ha −1 were applied. For model estimation, 27 vegetation indices were used as input variables, with the objective of estimating control based on visual evaluation data and on control percentage data determined by the plant mass killed by the action of the herbicide. The model developed with data from visual control scores presented excellent performance, both in training (r 2 of 0.92) and in validation (r 2 of 0.92). The model trained with the percentage of dead plant mass also presented satisfactory performance, with an r 2 of 0.88 for the training sample and 0.90 for the validation sample. The proposed evaluation method presents advantages over the usual methods, due to the ease of obtaining smartphone images and the possibility of inserting the indices and models developed in mobile applications.

title: Improved point cloud segmentation algorithms for in situ individual plant phenotyping and weight prediction of Chinese cabbage plants using UAV imagery
abstract: With the advancement of precision agriculture and modern breeding techniques, large-scale, efficient, and in situ acquisition of plant phenotypic data has become a critical challenge in research. Traditional manual measurement methods are inefficient and struggle to meet the demand for high-throughput phenotypic data in modern breeding. Consequently, this study proposes a method based on low-altitude drones and three-dimensional (3D) point cloud analysis to achieve in situ, nondestructive phenotypic extraction and weight prediction for individual Chinese cabbage plants. First, RGB images are captured in the field using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Large-scale 3D point clouds are reconstructed through structure from motion with multiview stereo technology. Subsequently, an enhanced graph convolutional neural network (AW-GNN) is proposed, integrating wavelet convolution, adaptive graph structure learning, and attention mechanisms to improve the accuracy and robustness of point cloud semantic segmentation. Building on this foundation, a morphology-guided watershed clustering algorithm is introduced. High-density segmentation of individual plants can be achieved in crowded environments by integrating two-dimensional canopy height maps with 3D point cloud spatial information. Based on the segmentation results, 3D phenotypic parameters, such as plant height, canopy width, and volume, are extracted. Individual plant weight prediction models are constructed using machine learning methods, including support vector regression (SVR) and random forest. Experimental results demonstrate that AW-GNN achieves an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 91.63% in point cloud semantic segmentation, significantly outperforming existing mainstream models. Morphological watershed clustering effectively mitigates undersegmentation and oversegmentation problems encountered by traditional methods under dense plant conditions. For individual plant weight prediction, the SVR model delivers optimal performance with a validation set R 2 of 0.8691 and root mean square error of 0.2810 kg. This study demonstrates the feasibility of achieving individual plant phenotyping and weight prediction in large-scale in situ scenarios using a UAV platform and improved point cloud segmentation algorithms, thereby providing an effective technical approach for high-throughput plant phenotyping analysis and digital breeding decision-making.

title: Improving greenhouse fruit-production control by integrating reinforcement learning into short-horizon model predictive control
abstract: Greenhouse fruit-production control aims to maximize the economic performance (fruit revenue minus operating costs) while operating within system constraints under external weather disturbances. Control methods need to balance the delayed economic benefit of fruit yield with current operating costs. For such problems, model predictive control (MPC) can handle constraints under future weather disturbances, but can become computationally demanding when using sufficiently long prediction horizons for (relatively large) nonlinear greenhouse fruit production models. In contrast, reinforcement learning (RL) can learn control policies before deployment while considering economic performance beyond MPC’s prediction horizon. However, desired indoor climate ranges are typically incorporated through penalty terms, and performance may degrade under unseen weather trajectories. This work proposes trajectory-selection RL–MPC , a framework that incorporates the economic benefit of fruit yield beyond the MPC prediction horizon into a finite-horizon optimization problem with a relatively short horizon (one hour). The framework uses an RL rollout trajectory to define a terminal region constraint and terminal cost. Next, a nonlinear MPC solves a short-horizon optimization problem with these terminal ingredients to find a local optimum. Finally, the framework selects and executes the first input from the trajectory with the better objective value, either from the MPC-predicted or the RL rollout trajectory. The method is applied to GreenLight, a large-scale nonlinear greenhouse tomato production model that exhibits stiff dynamics. The simulation results show that trajectory-selection RL–MPC with a one-hour prediction horizon matches the closed-loop performance of a high-performing guiding policy while improving over standalone MPC with the same horizon. On 25 weather trajectories held out during policy training, trajectory-selection RL–MPC achieved ∼ 52 % higher closed-loop performance than standalone RL and ∼ 80 % higher performance than MPC with the same horizon length.
