title: Multi-site benchmarking of deep reinforcement learning for forecast-informed irrigation decision-making in paddy rice
abstract: Forecast-informed paddy irrigation must balance water saving, drainage reduction, and yield protection, but comparative evidence across climates is limited. We benchmarked Deep Q-Network (DQN), Double Dueling Deep Q-Network (D3QN), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), and Rewarded-Region Replay (R3) in one paddy simulation across 15 site-crop combinations in six agroclimatic zones of China. Each policy was trained on synthetic seasons under three random seeds and evaluated on 105 observed site-years against full irrigation (FI), three deterministic forecast-driven rules, a tuned forecast threshold, and a perfect-foresight dynamic programming (DP) reference. The learned policies reduced seasonal irrigation by 12.4%–16.2% relative to FI, versus 5.4%–7.9% for the rules and 4.7% for the tuned forecast threshold, and raised rainfall utilization efficiency from 0.56 to 0.66–0.69; mean simulated potential yield loss was 0.03%–0.13%. The two value-based methods used the least water (350.3 mm for DQN and 350.8 mm for D3QN) and PPO the most (366.2 mm), while the two actor-critic methods incurred the lowest simulated yield loss (0.03% for R3 and 0.04% for PPO); neither the DQN-D3QN nor the PPO-R3 difference was significant in irrigation or simulated yield loss. Water depth and forecast rainfall jointly governed the switch from waiting to irrigating, but at a given depth the actor-critic methods required more forecast rainfall than the value-based methods to keep waiting. Under stochastic multicriteria acceptability analysis of TOPSIS rankings (SMAA-TOPSIS), the leading policy changed with management priorities: DQN led at 9 of the 15 site-crop combinations where irrigation or drainage volume carried the most weight, and PPO and R3 together led at 9 where simulated yield loss did. Perfect-foresight DP reduced irrigation by 30.5% relative to FI, and the learned policies captured 47.8% of that saving, leaving a mean 66.6 mm gap to DP. The benchmark provides a reference protocol for comparing forecast-informed irrigation policies across climates.

title: Forecasting farmland dew intensity using deep learning models optimized via an improved snow goose algorithm
abstract: Farmland dew occurs frequently and in significant amounts. While dew plays a crucial role in enhancing fertilizer and pesticide utilization while reducing their runoff, excessive dew can hinder flowering and pollination. Prolonged dew retention on leaves also increases the risk of fungal infections in rice plants, such as rice blast disease, which can lead to subsequent yield losses. The timely forecasting of farmland dew intensity for the following day can effectively mitigate the related adverse impacts on agricultural production. This study provides critical insights for preliminary decisions on crop foliar humidity, as well as the optimal concentration and application timing of foliar fertilizers and pesticides. Multiyear (2011–2021) continuous observational data on farmland dew and meteorological factors are used to develop a hybrid deep learning model (improved snow goose algorithm (ISGA)–variational mode decomposition (VMD) –convolutional neural network (CNN) –bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) –support vector machine (SVM)) for forecasting the dew intensity 12 h in advance (the following morning). The predictive performance of the ISGA-VMD-CNN-BiLSTM-SVM model was compared with that of linear and physical models. The results demonstrate that the deep learning model achieved an R2 of 0.9266, significantly outperforming the linear model (0.3926) and physical model (0.3061). The mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) between the predicted and observed dew intensities was only 7.15%, with the forecast accuracy reaching 95.58%. The proposed hybrid deep learning model yields advanced forecast-style predictions of dew intensity. Compared with conventional linear models, physical models and existing machine learning methods, this model uses fewer types of meteorological input parameters and achieves obviously higher prediction accuracy. This model provides a novel methodological framework for dew forecasting in agricultural management.

title: GNN-Bézier-RP: A joint path-planning method integrating graph neural networks and Bézier-curve obstacle avoidance for safflower picking with a parallel manipulator
abstract: To address irregular target distributions, local obstacle interference, and insufficient trajectory smoothness in safflower picking path planning, this study proposes a global–local integrated path-planning method for a Delta parallel manipulator. The method couples Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based global picking-order planning with Bézier-curve-based local obstacle-avoidance correction. During global planning, an improved GNN encoder models target–obstacle spatial relationships among mature safflower capitula, obstacle points, and the non-entry region, and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) decoder generates the picking visiting sequence. During local correction, cubic Bézier control-point optimization modifies trajectory segments with potential obstacle conflicts, and minimum-jerk smoothing improves motion continuity. Simulation results show that, under the Active Search strategy, the proposed GNN-LSTM model obtained normalized path lengths of 7.507, 11.711, and 15.857 for the 20-, 30-, and 40-point settings, respectively. After local obstacle-avoidance correction, the path-growth cost remained within 0.037–0.078. Laboratory validation further showed that the actual path lengths changed from 751.6 cm, 1178.6 cm, and 1585.9 cm to 784.23 cm, 1202.95 cm, and 1693.0 cm, respectively, while the total execution times decreased from 38.40 s, 54.36 s, and 74.16 s to 30.24 s, 47.52 s, and 58.60 s. The planned trajectory execution success rates were 91.67%, 88.89%, and 87.50%, respectively. These results demonstrate that the coupled GNN–Bézier strategy is effective for safflower picking under the tested simulation and laboratory conditions, improving local obstacle-avoidance feasibility, motion continuity, and trajectory execution efficiency.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted design and optimization of Fin Ray Effect flexible grippers for lychee harvesting
abstract: The harvesting end effector plays a crucial role in agricultural robots. However, the initial design and configuration optimization have traditionally lacked intelligent methods. To address this issue, this study proposes an Artificial Intelligence (AI) enhanced design and optimization method to develop a novel Gripping-and-Shearing Separation Type Lychee Harvesting End Effector (GS-STLHEE). A case study designs a flexible gripper and uses numerical models to build training and testing datasets for configuration design and optimization. The nonlinear relationships between these parameters and characteristics are predicted by surrogate models, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Back-propagation Artificial Neural Networks (BPANN), and Support Vector Machines (SVM). The Bayesian Optimization (BO) technique is then employed to fine-tune the hyperparameters of the AI-learning models. The aforementioned data-driven optimization functions and constraints are integrated with the Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) to identify Pareto-optimal solutions. Configuration parameters such as supporting beam thickness, incline angle, and spacing distance are optimized, and reaction force and gripper mass are enhanced. The results indicate the CNN model demonstrates superior learning ability, with the advancement of higher prediction accuracy, when handling complicated datasets. The optimization flexible gripper demonstrates larger reaction force and lighter mass, with an improvement rate of around 50 %.

title: Lightweight autonomous construction and application of a knowledge graph for soil acidification constraint management based on LLM agents
abstract: In the red and yellow soil regions of southern China, long-term practices in soil acidification constraint management have revealed several challenges, including fragmented knowledge systems, high technical thresholds, and pronounced regional disparities in technical capacity, which collectively hinder the systematic integration and dissemination of management experience. To address these limitations, this study proposes a lightweight autonomous construction framework for a knowledge graph of soil acidification management based on large language model (LLM) agents. By introducing an "AI associative matrix" and a semantic expansion-retrieval mechanism, the framework enables the system to automatically infer related concepts and relationships from a small set of domain-specific keywords, thereby generating an initial ontology structure and knowledge graph schema for management tasks. In addition, a network protocol-based control strategy is incorporated to semantically parse publicly available governmental reports and monitoring data, facilitating automated processes such as entity recognition and relation extraction. At the system implementation level, a cloud-edge collaborative lightweight architecture is adopted to reduce computational requirements and improve usability. Through an empirical in-situ deployment and lightweight field-level testing conducted directly at the farm sites of Chengmai County, Hainan Province, this framework demonstrated a robust capacity to adapt to users with different technical backgrounds and regions with varying levels of resource input, while providing extensibility for the continuous integration of emerging technologies and updated policy regulations. Overall, this study offers a lightweight, user-friendly, and scalable intelligent approach for cultivated land quality improvement and agricultural ecological management.

title: UAV remote sensing monitoring of tea heat-drought stress in complex tea garden environments
abstract: The monitoring of tea heat–drought stress (THS) via UAV remote sensing involves challenges such as complex plantation environments, strong variations in illumination and shadow, the small scale of the diseased spots, and weak spectral differences between THS spots and healthy areas. To address these issues, this study proposes a UAV remote sensing monitoring method for THS in complex tea plantation environments. A scheme called Multispectral Tea Heat-Drought Stress Detection Network (MS-THSNet) is designed, in which a dual-branch feature extraction backbone is employed to exploit the complementary advantages of different modalities in terms of capturing texture information and spectral characteristics. To further enhance the cross-modal feature integration, a Modality Interaction Transformer Module (MITM) and an Adaptive Multispectral Fusion Network structure (AMF-Net) are introduced. The MITM models the global dependency relationships among different spectral bands through a cross-spectral feature interaction mechanism, enabling complementary enhancement of multispectral features and alleviating the insufficient discriminative representation caused by uneven illumination, shadow, and the weak spectral differences of THS spots. The AMF-Net structure adaptively weights and integrates the fused features to emphasize spot-related characteristics while suppressing interference from complex backgrounds. MS-THSNet also includes a Context-Guided Attention Module (CGAM) to perform cross-channel and cross-spatial contextual attention modeling on the fused features, thereby improving the localization and recognition accuracy of THS spots at different scales. In addition, a lightweight small-object detection head is adopted to enhance the perception of tiny THS spots. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves a precision of 86.4%, a recall of 80.5%, and a mean average precision (mAP) of 87.8%, significantly outperforming other state-of-the-art methods. Compared with mainstream multimodal detection methods, the proposed method has an mAP that is improved by more than 3.5%, with a 7% improvement over the baseline detection network, thus validating its effectiveness for UAV monitoring of THS in complex tea garden environments.

title: Enhancing pesticide-likeness prediction via multimodal deep learning ensemble framework
abstract: Pesticide-likeness prediction is a critical task in agrochemical research and design. However, existing methods are often constrained by negative sample selection bias and overreliance on supervised learning. To address these challenges, we propose RGG, a multimodal deep learning ensemble framework that integrates Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), and Graph Convolutional Attention Network (GCAN) to synergistically capture molecular sequence patterns, topological features, and multimodal correlations. The positive samples were collected from the British Crop Production Council (BCPC) database, whereas the negative samples were selected from the ZINC20 database through Hao’s Rule prescreening and Butina clustering. The framework leverages a voting mechanism to harmonize the predictive strengths of heterogeneous models, thereby balancing classification robustness and generalization capability. Experimental results demonstrate that the RGG model outperformed all individual submodels on the validation sets of the 10-fold cross-validation. This improvement is reflected in a 5.33 % increase in average accuracy, along with gains of 5.05 % in precision and 5.46 % in recall. In independent testing, RGG exhibited potential for prioritizing novel bioactive molecules (AUC = 0.81). RGG generates continuous pesticide-likeness scores for candidate ranking, with a less polarized score distribution than the supervised submodels on the sampled molecules. Additional sensitivity analyses showed that the supervised model was robust to moderate changes in the clustering cutoff and benefited from diversity-oriented negative-sample selection. Furthermore, the framework supports multi-label functional categorization (fungicides, insecticides, herbicides) and enables interpretable predictions through attention mechanisms, highlighting molecular fragments associated with the model predictions. This work proposes a precision-oriented and interpretable methodology for pesticide-likeness prediction, advancing the application of deep learning in agrochemical molecular design. We also developed a web application to facilitate the use of our model: https://rgg.pianlab.team/jobs.

title: Estimating and Forecasting Grapevine Phenology using Deep Learning and Mechanistic models: A comparative study
abstract: Accurate monitoring of key phenological stages, such as bud-break, blooming, veraison, and berries ripe, is essential for optimizing vineyard management, especially in the context of climate change. Grapevine phenology, primarily driven by temperature, has been extensively studied with the most common prediction methods based on the growing-degree-days (GDD) approach. In this paper we propose and compare two novel methodologies, respectively based on a mechanistic and a deep learning approach, to detect and forecast key phenological stages. The mechanistic model simulates the effects of both air temperature and water availability on the major plant metabolic processes that drive the annual phenological cycle (vegetative and reproductive growth, and sugar accumulation in the berry), whereas the deep learning model, based on a Recurrent Neural Network, infers directly the phenological cycle taking as input the time series of the daily weather station measurements. Using seven years of phenological data collected from five grape varieties (‘Aglianico’, ‘Greco’ ‘Syrah’, ‘Touriga Franca’, and ‘Touriga Nacional’) across four Mediterranean sites in Italy, Spain, and Portugal, we evaluate the performance of these models against traditional GDD-based methods. Cross-validation results show that while the mechanistic model excels at predicting bud-break, with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 4.9 days compared to 5.7 and 5.6 days of the GDD-based and the deep learning model, respectively, the deep learning model is an all-around optimal methodology in terms of predicting accuracy across different stages, resulting in an overall MAE slightly under 5 days, with an average error reduction of 0.6 to 1.6 days respect to the two GDD-based models tested. Furthermore, we illustrate how these models can leverage sub-seasonal weather forecasts to predict phenological events in advance, offering practical tools for vineyard managers. This was particularly true for the deep learning model, that was able to predict grapevine phenological stages two weeks in advance with an average error lower than 6 days. These findings highlight the potential of these novel approaches for automating phenology monitoring and improving decision-making in viticulture under changing climate conditions.

title: Hyperspectral olive maturity estimation model for table olives: A non-invasive proof-of-concept study
abstract: The economic significance of olive cultivation and trade is paramount for Mediterranean countries, yielding a substantial impact on their respective local economies. However, the quality of olives is significantly influenced by the harvest timing, which occurs when they reach optimal size and maturity stage. Conventionally, farmers have relied on empirical observation to determine the optimal harvest date, guided by their accumulated expertise and knowledge. While this approach is well-founded, it lacks the rigor and objectivity offered by data-driven methods. The development of an automatic system for determining olive maturity is a significant concern for the industry. This study proposes an artificial intelligence-based system for estimating the maturity of table olives using a novel technological approach. The method involves the identification of olive maturity stages through field methods that utilize proximal hyperspectral imaging technology. A comprehensive analysis was conducted to elucidate the importance of each spectral band and to assess the model’s performance with a reduced feature space. In this proof-of-concept study, a Hyperspectral Olive Maturity Estimation Model (HOMEM) was developed to estimate olives’ maturity by determining their Maturity Index. The model employed visible and near-infrared spectral signatures acquired through in-field hyperspectral imaging. The present study explores the precision of HOMEM and the impact of normalization with hyperspectral images employing various AI-based models. The proposed HOMEM model attained an R2 value of 93 % in its estimation of the Maturity Index through the utilization of visible and near-infrared wavelengths. The results of this study demonstrate the potential of hyperspectral imaging and machine learning techniques to enhance the assessment of olive quality and reduce reliance on traditional, experience-based methods.

title: Structure over sound: A free box count out-predicts in-hive acoustics for honey-bee colony strength
abstract: In-hive microphones are widely promoted for non-invasive estimation of honey-bee colony strength (frames of bees), and benchmarks report near-perfect accuracy. Whether that accuracy survives on unseen colonies and apiaries decides deployability. We re-analysed two open multi-sensor datasets, UrBAN (ten urban colonies) and MSPB (53 rural colonies at two apiaries), harmonised to a shared 20-feature acoustic space with in-hive temperature and humidity. Random forests and hierarchical mixed models were evaluated under progressively stricter validation, from random k -fold to leave-one-apiary-out and cross-dataset transfer, with the acoustic, environmental and structural contributions separated by ablation. Most of the reported skill is not acoustic. Under leave-one-apiary-out validation the acoustic features alone reach R 2 = 0.17 , in-hive temperature and humidity alone 0.56, and the beekeeper’s box count alone 0.71; the box count from the previous visit, fixed before the label existed, still reaches 0.42 alone and 0.55 with climate. Adding acoustics never improved accuracy materially under any configuration tested ( Δ R 2 between −0.12 and ＋0.02). The box count’s 90% conformal intervals keep near-nominal empirical coverage across apiaries, while those of the sensor model cover 70% of cases in one transfer direction and 99% in the other. In an exploratory cross-dataset comparison, limited by a 17-assessment audio-matched UrBAN sample, the box count transferred in both directions and the acoustic features in neither. A plausible reason is sensing geometry: the microphone sits in the bottom brood box, which barely varies, while almost all population variation is above it. The box count mixes physical capacity with management decisions. It is therefore a diagnostic baseline and not a measurement instrument, and the finding is that a single bottom-box microphone adds nothing to it, though acoustics retain value for other targets. The conclusion rests on the within-MSPB cross-apiary comparison and is limited to a single bottom-box microphone, the shared feature space and the frames-of-bees target.

title: Forecasting drought across Canada using a hybrid machine learning approach: a national perspective for adaptations and early warning systems
abstract: Drought is a major natural hazard in Canada, with significant socio-economic impacts across the country’s diverse climatic and geographic regions. This study proposes a hybrid forecasting framework that combines fast adaptive empirical mode decomposition (FAEMD), an ensemble deep random vector functional link (edRVFL) network, and the energy valley optimizer (EVO) to model nonstationary hydrological time series. Using 74 years (1951–2024) of meteorological data from 24 Canadian meteorological stations, we first identified substantial spatial variability and nonstationary trends in historical drought conditions. The proposed FAEMD-edRVFL-EVO framework was then used to forecast the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI 12 ) at one-, two-, and three-month lead times and compared against standalone and hybrid implementations of extreme gradient boosting, random forest, and k -nearest neighbor algorithms. FAEMD-edRVFL-EVO consistently achieved the best performance, with median correlation coefficients of 0.999, 0.980, and 0.906 for one-, two-, and three-month forecasts, respectively. Performance remained strong in climatically complex regions, particularly in Western and Northern Canada. By effectively isolating nonstationary signals, this applied study demonstrates that the integrated pipeline provides a scalable, accurate, and computationally efficient practical solution for large-scale drought forecasting and early warning under increasing climatic uncertainty.

title: Hierarchical deep reinforcement learning for dual-arm robotic pear blossom pollination in dense orchard environments
abstract: Pear blossoms are densely distributed and flower within a relatively short period, imposing stringent efficiency requirements on robotic pollination systems to complete multiple targets within a limited operational window. In unstructured pear orchards, irregular blossom distributions and overlapping reachable workspaces of the two manipulators tightly couple target allocation, workload coordination, shared-workspace conflict avoidance, and continuous motion control, making dual-arm pollination inherently a hierarchical decision-making problem. To address these coupled challenges, this study proposes a hierarchical deep reinforcement learning framework for dual-arm robotic pollination in dense pear blossom environments. At the high level, a Transformer-JointQ scheduler models the interactions between candidate pear blossom targets and dual-arm states and evaluates feasible target combinations through joint state–action values, thereby enabling coordinated target selection for both manipulators under dense-target conditions. At the low level, PCCS-MATD3 dynamically adjusts control preferences while incorporating temporal smoothness and dual-arm coordination constraints into policy optimization, improving motion stability and coordination during continuous execution. Simulation experiments show that Transformer-JointQ achieves task completion rates of 99.5%, 98.5%, and 99.0% for scenarios containing 6, 10, and 15 target pear blossoms, respectively, while maintaining high workload balance; meanwhile, PCCS-MATD3 achieves a 99% task completion rate in low-level evaluations and improves motion smoothness and dual-arm coordination without compromising execution efficiency. Field experiments in a real pear orchard further validate the feasibility of the proposed framework under natural illumination, irregular blossom distributions, occlusions, and environmental disturbances. Overall, the proposed framework provides an effective hierarchical decision-making approach for coordinated autonomous dual-arm pollination in dense pear blossom environments.

title: Image segmentation of sugarcane plants using u-net architecture and pre-trained deep learning models
abstract: Gap identification in the sugarcane ( Saccharum officinarum spp) is important because the uniformity of germination is highly correlated with yield. Field-scale spatial image segmentation using drone imagery to clearly distinguish sugarcane from other materials in the field facilitates a better understanding of gaps and the reasons behind their occurrence. This research reports on the use of this approach to investigate segmentation of sugarcane imagery using six pre-trained transfer learning models and a proposed U-Net model for this purpose. The pre-trained models selected for this study were VGG19, ResNet50, InceptionV3, InceptionResNetV2, MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB7. Model performance metrics such as model accuracy, loss function, F1-score, Dice loss, IoU, and Jaccard loss were used to evaluate the models. The dataset used in this study was RGB imagery captured from a drone. Ground-truth data consisted of 317 masked images (full rows of sugarcane, incomplete rows of sugarcane, and no sugarcane) for training and validating the model. The resultant models were used to perform spatial image segmentation on a proof-of-concept area. Of the models evaluated, five achieved high levels of spatial image segmentation for sugarcane. From a resource constraint, the proposed U-Net model, VGG19, and InceptionV3 generated the most suitable models for sugarcane segmentation. VGG19 resulted in the best performance scores with accuracy 0.893 but was not substantially different from the proposed U-Net and InceptionV3 models. When processing time and available resources were taken into account, InceptionV3 was also found to be a suitable alternative. Therefore, we conclude that image segmentation of sugarcane plants using the VGG19 and InceptionV3 architectures is a suitable choice for this type of application. These algorithms enable clear visualization of the emerging sugarcane plants, allowing them to be distinguished from the other in the row and across the field. Ultimately, this will be of benefit for future research that can help sugarcane farmers plan and make prompt decisions about field activities to achieve sustainable sugarcane farming, including future studies to identify the causes of the gaps in sugarcane rows.

title: Dynamic real-time detection of maize ear dehusking clearance rate based on deep learning and multi-object tracking
abstract: Real-time assessment of maize-ear dehusking clearance rate is important for monitoring harvesting quality, but dynamic harvesting conditions can cause missed detections, false positives, and duplicate counting due to background interference, target-scale variation, motion blur, and severe occlusion. This study presents a real-time dehusking-clearance-rate monitoring framework integrating object detection, multi-object tracking, and identity-based duplicate-aware counting. An improved You Only Look Once version 11 nano (YOLOv11n) detector, termed PPSE-YOLO, was constructed by incorporating a Partial Frequency Dynamic Convolution-based C3k2 module (PFD_C3k2), the Pyramid Sparse Transformer (PST), and a Separated and Enhancement Attention Module (SEAMHead). PFD_C3k2 improves frequency- and texture-related feature representation under background interference and motion blur, PST enhances selective multi-scale feature fusion for maize ears with different apparent sizes, and SEAMHead strengthens the representation of visible features under partial occlusion. BoT-SORT maintains target identities across consecutive frames, and the resulting trajectories are converted into unique counting events for continuous dehusking-clearance-rate estimation. PPSE-YOLO achieved a Precision of 92.7%, a Recall of 91.8%, and an mAP@0.5 of 95.5%, representing improvements of 2.4, 0.9, and 1.5 percentage points, respectively, over YOLOv11n. Meanwhile, its computational complexity and parameter count were reduced from 6.3 to 5.1 GFLOPs and from 2.58 to 2.28 M, respectively. BoT-SORT achieved an MOTA of 92.05% and an IDF1 of 89.87%. At the system level, the framework achieved an overall counting consistency of 97.67%, a mean absolute dehusking-clearance-rate estimation error of 2.02 percentage points across 10 test groups, and an average end-to-end processing speed of 34 FPS. These results indicate the feasibility of the framework for real-time maize dehusking monitoring under the tested harvesting conditions.

title: Predicting and mapping stem water potential in walnut orchards using machine learning, geostatistics, and spatial validation
abstract: Midday stem water potential (SWP) is a widely used indicator of orchard water status, but pressure-chamber measurements are labor intensive and spatially sparse. This study evaluated machine-learning and spatial-statistical approaches using repeated measurements from 30 trees at 10 monitoring sites during 2019–2021. Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and a stacked ensemble used ETo, vapor pressure deficit (VPD), air temperature, soil temperature, solar radiation, wind speed, Easting, and Northing as predictors. Strict leave-one-site-out (Site-LOSO) validation was the primary test of transfer to an unmonitored site. RF had the highest pooled Site-LOSO point estimate (R 2 = 0.41, RMSE = 0.21 MPa, MAE = 0.16 MPa), followed by the ensemble (R 2 = 0.38, RMSE = 0.22 MPa) and XGBoost (R 2 = 0.37, RMSE = 0.22 MPa). Same-date field-assisted inverse-distance weighting achieved R 2 = 0.39 and RMSE = 0.22 MPa. RF reproduced monitored-network date means well (R 2 = 0.97; RMSE = 0.03 MPa) but not within-date spatial anomalies at withheld sites (R 2 = − 0.12; r = 0.09), and leave-one-year-out transfer was weak. The fitted models were applied over canopy pixels for 11 Ceres acquisition dates in 2020. All model maps were spatially smooth at the native grid, but their spatial patterns and within-map variation differed among algorithms and dates. Residual spatial dependence, heterogeneous tree-level performance, and mixed same-date checks indicate substantial uncertainty in fine-scale spatial transfer. The 0.5-m grid is a model-output support and not an independently validated SWP measurement resolution.

title: MCAFNet: A multimodal audio-visual cross-attention fusion network for on-the-branch durian (Durio zibethinus L.) fruit maturity assessment
abstract: Accurate on-the-branch durian maturity assessment is essential for determining appropriate harvest timing, yet conventional experience-based evaluation is operator-dependent, and existing automated approaches have limited applicability in complex orchard environments. This study proposes a Multimodal Cross-Attention Fusion Network (MCAFNet) that integrates fruit images, stem images, and fruit-knocking acoustic signals for in-field durian maturity classification. An improved lightweight detector, SG-YOLO, extracts fruit and stem regions, while Mel spectrogram, mel-frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC), and Chroma representations are stacked into a three-channel acoustic feature map. A Transformer-based cross-attention module subsequently fuses modality-specific features to exploit complementary maturity information. Under five-fold cross-validation, MCAFNet achieved an accuracy of 86.27 % ± 2.32 % and a macro_F1-score of 85.63 % ± 2.55 %, outperforming all 11 evaluated alternative multimodal fusion methods. Compared with the strongest competing method, FDFR-Net, accuracy and macro_F1-score increased by 2.15 and 2.22 percentage points, respectively. Moreover, integrating extracted fruit and stem regions with acoustic information improved accuracy by 6.07 percentage points and macro_F1-score by 5.48 percentage points relative to a full-image-plus-audio strategy. Ablation analyses indicated that fruit images provided the strongest discriminative information, while stem images and acoustic signals contributed complementary maturity cues. A user-oriented application was also developed to support practical assessment. These findings highlight the potential of region-focused visual-acoustic fusion for on-the-branch durian maturity classification and provide a foundation for intelligent harvesting systems.

title: Giving the greenhouse a brain: How artificial intelligence is transforming controlled environment agriculture
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is redefining how we design, manage, and sustain Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA). Traditionally, greenhouses relied on rule-based control systems that operated through predefined thresholds for temperature, humidity, and light. Today, advances in computer vision, machine learning, and robotics are transforming these facilities into intelligent ecosystems capable of perceiving, reasoning, and adapting in real time. This perspective review explores the emerging paradigm of the “greenhouse with a brain,” where data-driven perception and decision-making integrate seamlessly with sensing and actuation networks. Unlike technology-specific reviews that primarily examine individual components of greenhouse automation, this article integrates advances across sensing, artificial intelligence, robotics, modeling, and control within a system-level cognitive framework. We discuss recent progress in visual plant phenotyping, predictive climate control, knowledge-enhanced reinforcement learning, and multimodal data fusion that enable closed-loop intelligence for crop monitoring and management. Beyond technical advances, we emphasize the shift toward self-learning and explainable AI systems that can autonomously optimize productivity, resource efficiency, and environmental sustainability. By synthesizing developments across AI, robotics, and plant science, this article envisions next-generation cognitive greenhouses. In these autonomous yet transparent systems, humans, machines, and biological processes collaborate as partners to achieve resilient and sustainable food production in a changing “world”.

title: Forecasting future individual-tree growth using explainable machine learning across northern Chinese larch forests
abstract: Accurately forecasting tree growth under climate change is essential for adaptive forest management, yet the ability of machine-learning models to predict future growth beyond the calibration period remains poorly evaluated. Using 615 trees and 1,230 increment cores collected from six Larix gmelinii var. principis-rupprechtii forests across northern China, we reconstructed annual basal area increment (BAI) series and developed a tree-level dataset spanning 2000–2023. Tree age, previous-year diameter at breast height (DBH), competition index (CI), and multi-temporal climatic variables were integrated into Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models and compared with a linear mixed-effects model (LMM). Both machine-learning models substantially outperformed the LMM, achieving cross-validation R2 values of 0.45–0.74 and successfully reproducing interannual growth variability. Temporal extrapolation reduced predictive performance relative to conventional cross-validation, but both models retained robust forecasting skill under unseen future conditions. Variable-importance and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analyses revealed that previous-year DBH, tree age, and competition intensity were the most influential predictors of BAI, whereas climatic effects were region-specific, nonlinear, and frequently lagged. Future projections under Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) SSP126, SSP245, and SSP585 scenarios indicated generally stable growth during 2024–2028, with differences among sites exceeding differences among climate scenarios. Our results demonstrate that explainable machine learning can provide robust near-term forecasts of individual-tree growth beyond the calibration period and highlight temporal extrapolation as a critical component of ecological forecasting.

title: From multi-fruit collisions to tissue damage: cross-scale dynamics and prediction of damage patterns during mechanized apple packing
abstract: During mechanized apple packing, fruits undergo successive multi-body collisions and load transfer. Existing studies generally investigate fruit-group dynamics and tissue damage in individual fruits separately, making it difficult to establish a direct link between practical packing conditions and internal fruit damage. To address this limitation, this study proposes a cross-scale damage prediction framework for fresh-market apples during packing, establishing a continuous mapping from packing conditions to collective collisions, tissue stress, and ultimately damage patterns. Fuji apples were used as the study material. Apple models were developed based on reverse engineering and experimentally determined material properties, with the measured minimum pulp yield strength of 0.27 MPa adopted as the threshold for irreversible damage initiation. Multi-body dynamics (MBD) simulations were employed to characterize fruit trajectories, collision behavior, and energy-transfer patterns during packing. Key collision parameters extracted from the MBD simulations were subsequently introduced into finite element method (FEM) models to resolve tissue-scale stress propagation and damage evolution. Building on this framework, a two-stage decoupled GFI-LightMLP surrogate model was developed to enable rapid prediction from packing conditions to mechanical responses and, subsequently, damage volume. The results showed that collision velocity was the dominant factor governing tissue damage. As the collision velocity increased from 1410 to 2450 mm s−1, the maximum equivalent stress increased from 0.27639 to 0.42368 MPa, while the damage volume increased from 2.17 × 103 to 2.74 × 104 mm3. Crate stiffness substantially affected impact-energy dissipation; compared with wooden crates, polypropylene crates reduced the damage volume by approximately 28.5 %. In addition, apples in the bottom layer exhibited a pronounced load-accumulation effect during multilayer packing, indicating that attenuation of macroscopic fruit motion and localized tissue damage can occur simultaneously. On the test set, the surrogate models achieved coefficients of determination above 0.96 for both equivalent stress and damage volume, while validation-set R2 values reached 0.9842 and 0.9415, respectively, demonstrating robust predictive performance. Physical experiments further confirmed that the predicted damage volumes followed the same trend as the experimentally measured values, with relative errors ranging from 3.57 to 19.15 %. Overall, the proposed framework links macroscopic fruit dynamics with tissue-scale damage during apple packing. It further enables rapid damage assessment without repeated computationally intensive simulations. The framework provides a theoretical basis for compliant design of mechanized packing equipment, screening of operating conditions, and optimization of low-damage packing parameters.

title: Species-Conditioned hierarchical decoding and cross-attention for uncertainty-aware veterinary skin disease recognition
abstract: Veterinary dermatology is facing two diagnostic challenges. First, many conditions show overlapping visual signs such as alopecia, erythema, crusting, scaling, nodules, and plaques, making image-based recognition difficult. Second, the same visual pattern may correspond to different diseases in cats, cattle, and dogs, which makes flat disease classification unreliable when host species is ignored. While deep learning has advanced animal health monitoring, existing systems are often limited to single species or binary detection tasks. To address this, we propose a species-conditioned deep learning framework designed to analyze standard RGB images across diverse hosts. Our approach introduces a novel architecture featuring: (1) an EfficientNetV2-S backbone for feature extraction; (2) a dedicated pathway for host-species representation; (3) disease-token construction with species-conditioned spatial-token modulation; and (4) species-gated cross-attention for disease classification. Furthermore, we incorporate uncertainty-aware analysis via MC-Dropout, conformal prediction, and Grad-CAM to ensure decision reliability. Evaluated on an internal dataset of 16,942 images (21 categories), the proposed Unified SGCA model achieved 97.5 % disease accuracy and 98.0 % macro-F1 on the internal test set, while SGCA Cross-Attention achieved 96.9 % accuracy and 97.4 % macro-F1. Crucially, on a heterogeneous external cohort of 1,351 internet-derived images characterized by varying quality and background complexity, the model maintained robust performance with a top-3 accuracy of 93.0 % for Unified SGCA and 88.8 % for SGCA Cross-Attention. This framework offers a scalable solution for veterinary decision support, farmer education, and zoonotic disease surveillance.

title: Real-time semantic segmentation of orchard LiDAR point clouds with a spherical-image convolutional neural network
abstract: Real-time semantic segmentation is essential for intelligent orchard operations. Conventional light detection and ranging (LiDAR) point cloud segmentation methods suffer from limited generalizability and weak adaptability to complex orchard scenarios. Specifically, the widely adopted PointNet++ cannot deliver satisfactory segmentation accuracy when processing multibeam LiDAR data collected from orchards. To address these challenges, this study constructs a nine-class orchard point cloud segmentation dataset and proposes a real-time segmentation framework built upon spherical-image convolutional neural networks. The framework leverages LiDAR-adaptive spherical projection to transform unordered three-dimensional (3D) point clouds into structured multimodal spherical images, thereby enabling dimensionality reduction while retaining geometric and reflectance features. Given the angular anisotropy of LiDAR and the abundance of cylindrical objects in orchard environments, a lightweight, asymmetric Darknet26-AS encoder is devised to establish a favorable balance between segmentation accuracy and inference efficiency. Further, a Gaussian distance–weighted voting strategy is incorporated to refine boundaries within the image domain, with spherical backprojection completing the full 3D segmentation pipeline. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed method attained a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 89.9% across the nine orchard classes, thereby surpassing PointNet++ by 15.9 percentage points (pp). Compared to state-of-the-art models, including PointTransformer v3 and SphereFormer, the proposed method achieved competitive accuracy, with the overall mIoU gap smaller than 1.2 pp. Meanwhile, it exhibited drastically reduced computational overhead: its parameter count was merely 1/12 and 1/8.5 those of the two counterparts, respectively, while its inference latency was approximately 1/7.4 and 1/4, respectively.

title: VisionEV: multimodal large language models for spatially aware electric vehicle charging demand prediction using satellite imagery
abstract: This manuscript presents VisionEV, a multimodal large language model (LLM) framework designed to predict electric vehicle (EV) charging demand by leveraging satellite imagery and structured textual data. Spatial context—including parking availability, land use, and nearby amenities—is critical for accurate demand estimation. However, site selection in EV infrastructure planning remains both labor-intensive and inconsistent, requiring human experts to conduct in-person audits and manually define spatial features. To overcome these limitations, VisionEV introduces an automated spatial reasoning pipeline that integrates satellite imagery of candidate locations as visual inputs, allowing the model to learn nuanced spatial patterns directly from imagery, without relying on predefined descriptors. Complementary station-level attributes, including traffic flow and temporal indicators, are embedded into domain-informed textual prompts to simulate planner reasoning. A core technical challenge lies in enabling coherent reasoning across semantically distinct inputs—structured textual data and perceptual visual context. VisionEV addresses this by reformulating the task as multimodal text generation, aligning both modalities within a shared embedding space through vision-informed prompting and lightweight domain-adaptive fine-tuning. We evaluate VisionEV using a real-world dataset of 22,852 training samples and 2,858 test samples collected from 189 public EV charging stations in Kansas City, Missouri. In the full-shot setting, VisionEV achieves superior accuracy (RMSE: 2.87, MAE: 1.98), outperforming the strongest baseline, LightGBM, by 1.0% and 5.3%, respectively. Few-shot, within-city zero-shot and cross-region spatial hold-out experiments demonstrate VisionEV’s ability to generalize across unseen scenarios, and ablation studies confirm the contributions of visual input, prompt design, and fine-tuning. These results underscore the promise of multimodal LLMs in supporting scalable, data-driven EV infrastructure planning through automated spatial understanding.

title: Interpretable deep reinforcement learning optimizes emergency response for China’s freezing rain-impacted roads
abstract: Freezing rain causes severe transportation disruptions and millions in annual economic losses across China. Current emergency protocols rely on rigid categorical standards are ineffective under extreme conditions. We present the first framework integrating four centrality measures (Degree, Betweenness, Percolation, DomiRank) with interpretable deep reinforcement learning for continuous resource optimization. Using 20-year historical data across 141 cities, we apply Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm with Integrated Gradients for transparent decision-making. Results reveal a critical vulnerability corridor (Guizhou-Hunan-Hubei-Jiangxi) with potential losses exceeding $500 million annually without intervention. Our continuous optimization achieves 18–762 % improvement over categorical standards by maintaining effectiveness when categorical protocols lose effectiveness at 20 mm thresholds. Interpretability analysis shows freight flow dominates decisions over network topology, with destination protection consistently prioritized. This paradigm transforms emergency response from binary to continuous resource allocation, providing managers with both optimized solutions and their underlying logic for climate-resilient infrastructure management.

title: How will arctic shipping emissions evolve? A spatiotemporal topology-aware transformer approach
abstract: This study proposes a novel spatiotemporal forecasting framework that integrates spatial clustering with a transformer-based model, termed the spatiotemporal topology-aware transformer (SToT), to predict maritime emissions across the Arctic region. Using Arctic Ship Traffic Data (ASTD), node-based representations are constructed through spatial clustering, enabling the joint learning of spatial correlations and temporal patterns using SToT. Experimental results demonstrate that our model outperforms existing methods by 17% in terms of the root mean square error, relative standard error, and node-level Pearson correlation coefficient, validating its predictive accuracy and robustness. According to SToT-based forecasts extending through 2030, total emissions are projected to increase by 30.8% compared with 2022 emissions, with N2O and CO2 exhibiting particularly significant growth. Furthermore, this study discusses the environmental, scientific, and political implications of maritime emissions. The proposed framework offers a scalable and accurate solution for climate risk assessments and sustainable policy planning in the Arctic region.

title: A generative physics-informed reinforcement learning-based approach for construction of representative drive cycle
abstract: Accurate driving cycle construction is crucial for vehicle design, fuel economy analysis, and environmental impact assessments. A generative Physics Informed Expected (State Action Reward State Action) SARSA-Monte Carlo (PIESMC) approach that constructs representative driving cycles by capturing transient dynamics, acceleration, deceleration, idling, and road grade transitions while ensuring model fidelity is introduced. Leveraging a physics-informed reinforcement learning framework with Monte Carlo sampling, PIESMC delivers efficient cycle construction with reduced computational cost. Experimental evaluations on two real-world datasets demonstrate that PIESMC replicates key kinematic and energy metrics, achieving up to an 83.9 % reduction in cumulative kinematic fragment errors compared to the Micro-trip-based (MTB) method and a 61.9 % reduction relative to the Markov-chain-based (MCB) method. Moreover, it is over an order of magnitude faster than conventional techniques, delivering more than a 30 × decrease in computational time. Analyses of vehicle-specific power distributions and wavelet-transformed frequency content further confirm its ability to reproduce experimental central tendencies and variability.

title: LSTM-Transformer-based state of charge and short-term remaining range prediction for electric buses
abstract: Electric buses are crucial for sustainable urban transport, yet accurately predicting battery state of charge and short-term remaining driving range remains challenging. This study proposes a multi-task framework based on Long Short-Term Memory-Transformer model for jointly predicting state of charge and short-term remaining driving range under real-world operational conditions. The framework utilizes Long Short-Term Memory model to capture dynamic variations, while Transformer extracts long-term dependencies such as battery ageing. The study further integrates multi-source data including vehicle, battery, and weather information to enhance feature representation and model robustness. Experiments conducted on six real-world electric bus datasets demonstrate the model’s superior predictive performance, achieving an average R2 of 0.9426 for state of charge and 0.9568 for short-term remaining driving range, outperforming single-task and baseline approaches. Ablation studies and comparative analyses further validate the hybrid model architecture and multi-task learning design. This study contributes to strengthening energy management for electric bus fleets.

title: Deep learning driven spatiotemporal prediction of global carbon emissions from container shipping
abstract: Container shipping is a significant source of global CO2 emissions, making accurate predictions essential for meeting international environmental targets. This study proposes ConvLSTM-CBAMNet, a deep learning model integrating channel and spatial attention mechanisms to capture complex spatiotemporal emission trends. The model significantly outperforms four deep learning baselines, including Transformer, ConvGRU, CNN-LSTM, and the traditional ConvLSTM. Compared to the strongest baseline, ConvLSTM, it demonstrates marked improvements, reducing the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) by 19.4% to 0.0914 and the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 16.8% to 0.0432, while increasing the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) by 5.8% to 0.9035. These predictions can inform targeted environmental policies, dynamically adjust Emission Control Areas (ECAs), optimize port scheduling to mitigate pollution peaks, and develop environmental early-warning systems, thereby supporting the shipping industry’s transition toward sustainability.

title: Technical performance evolution of BEVs: range, consumption and weight projections to 2050
abstract: Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs) are assuming a pivotal role in the road electrification, with continuous advancements in technology. This UK-focused study analyses the evolution of the technical parameters of BEVs between 2011 and 2024 and forecasts their development to 2050 for a range of scenarios (pessimistic, realistic and optimistic) focusing on range, energy consumption and vehicle weight. The research is underpinned by a data set of the technical specifications of 575 BEV models. The relationships between the parameters were revealed by machine learning (Random Forest and SHAP), with the forecast performed using the Prophet. The driving range of a typical C segment Sports Utility Vehicle (SUV) is forecast to increase by between 60 % and 180 %, vehicle weight and energy consumption varied between 1051–2000 kg and 267–286 Wh/mile, respectively, depending on the scenarios and underlying assumptions. The findings provide evidence-based insights for automotive technology planning and weight-based fiscal policy responses.

title: Collaborative prediction of bike-sharing demand around metro stations using spatiotemporal neural network
abstract: Accurate prediction of bike-sharing demand around metro stations is essential for enhancing multimodal integration. However, existing approaches often model bike-sharing demand in isolation, neglecting its strong spatiotemporal interdependence with metro ridership. To address this gap, this study proposes a spatiotemporal neural network that fuses multi-source data of bike-sharing trips, metro ridership, built environment characteristics, and weather conditions. The model combines graph convolutional networks to capture station-level spatial correlations with long term memory networks to learn temporal dynamics, while explicitly incorporating metro entry and exit flows to represent cross-modal dependencies. Using large-scale datasets from bike-sharing and metro systems in Shanghai, empirical analyses show that the proposed model substantially outperforms seven baseline models across multiple temporal granularities. Moreover, the model effectively captures peak-period demand surges, spatial clustering patterns, and imbalances between unlock and lock activities of bike-sharing. These findings provide practical insights for optimizing bike-sharing redistribution and enhancing metro–bike integration in urban environments.

title: A dual large language model framework for forecasting maritime greenhouse gas emissions
abstract: Maritime transport is a major source of greenhouse gas emissions, and accurately forecasting them is key to formulating targeted policies such as carbon pricing and emission quotas. The accuracy of existing forecasting models is limited by the challenges they face in processing large multi-source datasets. This study introduces a dual large language model (LLM) framework, MarEmisNet-DualLLM, which integrates a time-series-focused LLM for capturing temporal patterns and a general-purpose LLM for integrating domain knowledge, unstructured text, and contextual reasoning. Empirical tests on three real-world maritime datasets demonstrate that it outperforms baseline methods. The framework could be used by the International Maritime Organization, shipping firms, and ports to support mitigation strategies like route optimization and monitor compliance, thereby advancing maritime decarbonization.

title: Quantifying the counteracting impacts of climate change on large-scale pavement infrastructure serviceability
abstract: This study quantifies competing climate-change effects, temperature rise versus reduced freezing, on pavement networks using over 35 years of records from more than 1,100 sections. We combine explainable machine learning (ML) with Monte Carlo simulation to propagate global climate model (GCM) projections to future infrastructure impacts, considering the two-layer uncertainty from climate ensemble and ML residuals. Results reveal substantial inter-GCM model differences and occasional opposing trends, underscoring climate projection uncertainty. Trained ML models accurately predict long-term pavement performance; the freezing index and air temperature are the two dominant drivers. Reduced future freezing tends to extend service life, partially offsetting warming’s negative effects. Thus, climate change does not always accelerate pavement deterioration: in some regions (notably wet, freeze-prone zones) and for some time horizons or scenarios, net effects can be neutral or beneficial. In wet, freeze zones, pavement service life is being extended in nearly 65 % simulations under SSP585 by 2050–2060, whereas dry, freeze counterparts only show a figure of around 35 %. These findings indicate that pavement resilience assessments should consider both warming and changing freeze–thaw regimes rather than temperature alone under climate uncertainty and inform local adaptation decisions practically.

title: The green gridlock: Projecting the unintended wildfire evacuation risks of EV adoption
abstract: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), while crucial for climate goals, introduces complex challenges for emergency management. This study addresses the urgent, yet under-researched risk of wildfire evacuations in EV-dependent communities, whose mobility is tightly coupled with a vulnerable electrical grid. We develop a novel geospatial framework grounded in the Vulnerability-Exposure-Sensitivity model and operationalized through a Community Preparedness Index that integrates socioeconomic, demographic, mobility, and infrastructural characteristics. Hotspot analysis identifies spatial clusters of wildfire exposure, EV sensitivity, and community preparedness, enabling classification of evacuation risk profiles driven by transportation system dependence on electrified mobility. A Gaussian Process Regression informed S-curve forecasting approach estimates when communities are likely to reach critical risk levels as EV adoption increases. Results show significant spatial disparities, providing evidence to strategically deploy charging resources, grid hardening, and evacuation focused planning. The framework supports proactive, data-informed planning for resilient electrified transportation systems in wildfire-prone regions.

title: A transformer-enhanced causal analysis framework for inter-stop energy consumption of electric bus
abstract: Electric buses (EBs) are central to urban transport electrification, yet their energy consumption patterns remain inadequately characterized at operational scales. This study develops an integrated framework combining high-accuracy prediction with causal inference to analyze inter-stop segment energy consumption. We propose Transformer with C-Mixup and Self-Distillation (TCMSD), employing similarity-based sample mixing to address data sparsity and imbalance, while self-distillation enhances generalization. By embedding TCMSD within Double/debiased machine learning (DML) as base learners, we achieve superior causal effect estimation with reduced bias and variance. Applied to EB fleet operational data, the framework reveals non-linear heterogeneous treatment effects across 10 factors spanning driving behavior, operational characteristics, and weather conditions. Results demonstrate marked improvement in prediction performance. The factors exhibit different characteristics from long-distance trips from a causal perspective. This approach provides transit agencies with predictive tools and causal insights for data-driven energy management and environmental impact reduction.

title: Profit-aware battery swapping station energy scheduling via hybrid hierarchical deep reinforcement learning
abstract: As urban transportation electrification advances, range anxiety has become a key concern for electric vehicles (EVs). Battery swapping stations (BSS) offer a fast and efficient solution, yet traditional scheduling methods struggle to balance profitability with operational risk in dynamic environments. To address this, we propose a data-driven optimization method. First, historical data is used to derive optimal operational decisions, and an EV battery swapping demand forecasting model is built. Based on the forecasted demand and historical strategies, a long short-term memory network predicts the BSS’s overall charging and discharging power. A double deep Q-network is then employed to allocate this power to individual batteries, ensuring timely swaps. Validation using real operational data from Chengdu, China, shows the proposed method effectively meets battery swapping demand, enhances scheduling efficiency and station profitability, and reduces peak loads and power fluctuations, demonstrating the potential for practical application in managing smart EV infrastructure.

title: Sound event detection for modified-exhaust vehicles in urban environment
abstract: Vehicles with illegally modified exhaust systems are a significant source of urban noise and air pollution. This study employs a Sound Event Detection (SED) framework for their automated identification. To address the lack of public data, we generated a dataset with Scaper library, embedding foreground events into authentic background recordings. We employed an SED Transformer and compared six backbones, with the Multi-Scale Residual Network (MSResNet) achieving the best performance. The model achieved an event-based F1-score of 0.7277 on the validation set and 0.6629 in the field test. A Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis confirmed the model’s focus on meaningful acoustic features like acceleration harmonics and afterfire transients, while also revealing a temporal bias from the synthetic data. Analysis of computational performance and an event-covered localization error metric validated deployment feasibility. This work presents an end-to-end SED framework for automated urban noise enforcement, supporting data-driven policy beyond conventional classification.

title: Effects of functional spaces on small logistics facilities: machine learning-based decision-support tool
abstract: Urban logistics have shifted from a “goods-to-store” to a “goods-to-residents” paradigm, resulting in the proliferation of small logistics facilities such as micro-hubs and pick-up points in urban areas. As these facilities are increasingly embedded within urban functional spaces, understanding the driving factors of their spatial layout has become ever more crucial. This study examines the spatial layout characteristics and influencing factors of small logistics facilities in the Wuhan Metropolitan Development Area between 2010 and 2018. A Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) model is employed to analyze the nonlinear relationships and threshold effects of urban spatial variables on facility layout. The results indicate that land price exerts the strongest influence on spatial distribution, followed by transportation accessibility and demand-related variables in 2010 and 2018, respectively. Based on these findings, a decision-support tool is developed to optimize facility placement, offering policy-relevant insights for sustainable urban logistics planning from a supply–demand perspective.

title: Perceived streetscape quality and bike lane effectiveness: a computer vision approach
abstract: This study explores how perceived streetscape quality and bike lane types—striped and protected—are associated with urban cycling behavior. Using computer vision technology to analyze street view images from Berlin, Germany, we assessed visual safety scores and their association with cycling trips. Our findings reveal that both perceived safety and bike lanes significantly enhance cycling activity; however, the interplay between the two varies by the type of bike lanes. Striped bike lanes are more effective than protected bike lanes on streets perceived as safe, while protected bike lanes provide greater benefits in visually unsafe areas compared to striped bike lanes. These results imply that by enhancing the visual appeal and safety of streetscapes alongside bike lane installations, cities can promote active transportation, fostering more sustainable, healthy, and vibrant urban environments.

title: Ai-driven spatiotemporal urban road transport emission mapping using YOLO and COPERT model
abstract: This study proposes a high-resolution, real-time framework for estimating on-road vehicular emissions to support urban air quality management. Implemented in Tirupati Smart City , the approach integrates deep learning, field surveys, and dynamic emission modelling. Traffic data from 18 high-volume intersections were analysed using the YOLOv8 model, achieving 93% accuracy in vehicle classification, count, and speed estimation. Origin-Destination surveys conducted at 25 strategic locations captured vehicle attributes, including age, fuel type, and usage, which enabled classification into 127 categories based on body type, fuel, and Bharat Stage fuel norms. Emissions of CO, NOx, PM, VOCs, CH4, and CO2 were estimated using COPERT v5.0 with speed-dependent factors. The resulting hourly, 100 × 100 m emission grids revealed key diurnal and spatial emission patterns, including peak rush-hour and nighttime freight emissions. This scalable, transferable framework surpasses conventional methods, supporting real-time integration with dispersion models to aid smart city planning and targeted air quality interventions.

title: Disentangling metro passenger travel delays under extreme weather events: An analytical framework
abstract: Extreme weather events (EWEs) like typhoons increasingly disrupt metro systems, threatening urban mobility with widespread travel delays. However, existing studies often oversimplify delay mechanisms and lack context-specific insights. To disentangle the complex impacts of EWEs, we propose and validate a novel analytical framework that quantitatively links macro-scale passenger delays to micro-scale facility performance. The framework integrates two core diagnostic modules: a data-driven attribution method to identify critical facility-level delay sources, and a causally-informed deep learning model to robustly pinpoint the root causes of delay formation. This approach enables the detection of actionable bottlenecks, reveals opportunities for proactive demand management, and infers the dominant impact pathways through which EWEs degrade various facilities. Its strong performance and computational efficiency support both post-hoc diagnosis of past EWEs and near-real-time operational decision-making for ongoing EWEs. Validated on the Shenzhen Metro, this study provides a robust foundation for enhancing system resilience through targeted interventions.

title: AI-based framework for relief resource accessibility under seismic hazards for Taipei city
abstract: Post-earthquake disruptions to transportation network have significantly impeded relief operations. However, existing studies rarely integrated transportation infrastructure with building damage, while often lacking comprehensive quantitative analysis and result visualization, thereby limiting their practical applicability. This study presents an AI and GIS-based framework to assess building damage and evaluate its impacts on post-earthquake road blockages and disaster relief accessibility. Using Taipei City and earthquakes from adjacent faults as the case study, accessibility to emergency resources across regions was analyzed. The results indicate that, under scenarios where widespread building damage caused road network blockages, the redundancy of the road network became a critical factor affecting the accessibility of disaster relief resources. The proposed framework, integrating big data and GIS, enhances building damage evaluation and road condition analysis, providing a reliable foundation for disaster simulation, risk assessment, and the design of scientifically grounded disaster prevention measures.

title: Exploring e-scooters as first- and last-mile with Gaussian mixture and machine-learning models
abstract: E-scooters are emerging as a key urban transportation option that can improve public transportation accessibility and address first- and last-mile issues. However, their utility is uncertain when destinations do not align with transit routes. This study examines whether e- scooters complement or substitute public transit by analyzing travel segments from trip origins to transit stations and from stations to final destinations. Using GPS-based mobility data, Gaussian mixture model, and explainable machine learning, we identified seven distinct patterns of e-scooter use based on population and land-use characteristics. Most patterns show e-scooters complement transit by connecting underserved residential, commercial, and green areas to transit hubs. The results indicate substitution-like patterns in low-density suburban areas characterized by low bus service frequency and limited metro accessibility. These findings highlight the role of e-scooters as a complementary transport mode when conventional public transport coverage is weak, suggesting their relevance for first- and last-mile integration within mobility-as-a-service.

title: An explainable prediction framework for electric-taxi charging demand: Evidence from Shanghai, China
abstract: Electrifying urban shared mobility requires accurate, interpretable charging demand prediction to support sustainable transport and energy management. Existing models rely on simplified spatial assumptions and lack interpretability. This study develops an explainable diffusion graph neural network (XAI-DiffNet) for urban charging systems. The model constructs a multi-semantic small-world graph that integrates geographic adjacency, functional similarity, mobility flows, and historical charging correlations, and applies a multi-scale interpreter to quantify spatial–temporal contributions. Using data from 20,000 electric taxis in Shanghai, the model reduces prediction errors by up to 18% when interpretation-based noise filtering is enabled. The results show that temporal dynamics account for a larger share of predictive contribution than spatial structure, and that high-demand clusters and major transport hubs concentrate structural influence. These findings support coordinated charging scheduling and targeted infrastructure planning in urban energy grids.

title: Role of GHG information presentation in shaping EV preferences: machine learning approach
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) may help address issues such as transportation emissions, climate change, and oil dependency. Accordingly, many environmental and energy policies worldwide intend to shift from internal combustion engine vehicles to EVs. However, the current market penetration of EVs is still rather low. One of the factors significantly contributing to EV preferences is how greenhouse gas (GHG) information is presented. This study aimed to identify the best GHG information presentation to communicate with different populations. Therefore, seven new framings for GHG information presentation were designed based on theories such as psychological distancing. The performance of these new framings was compared with the GHG information presentation applied to current vehicle labels in Canada. To this end, a survey of over 2000 participants was administered. An interpretable machine learning approach was developed for modeling. The optimal label for communicating with different populations was identified, and the influence of different framings on EV preference probability was calculated. The results confirmed the importance of GHG information presentation on EV preference/choice. Further, it was postulated that different framings should be applied to communicate with various populations. Some of the framings developed in this study could increase the probability of EV preference by over 20%. For example, disaster framing (designed using psychological distancing theory) increased the probability of EV choice by 22.64% compared to the present mock-up in Canada for residents of Alberta.

title: From coast to coast: Understanding electric vehicle adoption across Canadian regions
abstract: Battery electric vehicles (BEVs) have experienced rapid growth in market share both in Canada and globally over the past decade. However, adoption rates vary significantly across Canadian regions, raising questions about the sustainability of current growth trajectories. This study (1) identifies the drivers of regional disparities in BEV adoption within Canada, and (2) projects nationwide adoption levels. We exploit a proprietary, nationwide Canadian dataset of vehicle transactions, geocoded at the postal-code level, from 2016 through 2024. Using this dataset, we calibrate and compare three technology‐diffusion models to capture historical uptake and forecast future penetration. Our analysis reveals that regional BEV adoption is predominantly shaped by socio-demographic characteristics while charging station availability and other regional attributes exert comparatively smaller effects. Model comparisons indicate substantial uncertainty in long-term forecasts: adoption trajectories vary markedly depending on model structure and parameterization. These findings underscore the importance of targeted policy interventions and localized strategies.

title: GNN-based spatiotemporal resilience prediction for Maritime Silk Road transportation network
abstract: The resilience of the 21st Century Maritime Silk Road transportation network is crucial for maritime safety. This study develops a resilience theory framework and proposes a graph neural network–based model to quantify and predict the spatiotemporal dynamics of Maritime Silk Road transportation network resilience. A four-layer weighted graph convolution model integrates multi-source heterogeneous data, including ship, environmental, and historical accident information. Using spatiotemporal network analysis and dynamic simulation, annual resilience performance is assessed, and local resilience variations under tropical cyclone impacts are predicted. Results indicate that the Maritime Silk Road transportation network maintains strong overall resilience, with good adaptability and recovery capability. Resilience is generally higher in shipping segments closer to coastlines and exhibits marked spatial heterogeneity and periodic fluctuations. The proposed model provides decision support for optimizing transport resource allocation and enhancing maritime security cooperation along the Maritime Silk Road.

title: Decoding EV user preferences with large language model and charging infrastructure reviews
abstract: User “charging anxiety” remains a barrier to EV adoption, yet its determinants are often inferred from small-scale surveys. This study develops a multimodal framework that decodes charging preferences from 120,052 user reviews of 118 TELD public charging stations in Wuhan, China. A large language model performs aspect-based sentiment analysis, transforming unstructured text into sentiments across ten dimensions of the charging experience. These features are used to estimate a data-driven satisfaction model, while vision–language indicators provide a scene-aware view of on-site environments. Results show that reliability, charging speed, access, price, and amenities dominate user evaluations, with rare but severe failures in reliability, payment, or access sharply depressing ratings compared with the gains from positive experiences. Segmented analysis reveals stable core factors but varying intensities across time, review-frequency, and vehicle brand segments, while scene-aware analysis indicates that greener, safer, and more orderly environments modestly shift attention toward reliability and amenities.

title: Physics-guided machine learning for ship biofouling assessment in support of maritime decarbonization
abstract: Ship biofouling significantly increases hull resistance and propeller loading, resulting in increased fuel usage and greenhouse gas emissions. This study presents a physics-guided machine learning approach for detecting performance degradation caused by biofouling. Physics-informed neural networks are first used to generate warm-up data that represent ideal, unfouled ship states under calm water conditions. A baseline model is built from this data and subsequently refined through an incremental learning scheme with new data collected in sliding temporal windows. The resulting incremental models are applied under reference conditions to quantify biofouling-induced performance changes, expressed as key performance indicators. Validation against conventional retraining approaches and the ISO 19030 standard shows that the proposed method more accurately captures both gradual degradation and rapid post-cleaning recovery. By delivering reliable and timely assessments of fouling impact, the framework supports optimized hull and propeller maintenance planning and contributes to improved energy efficiency and emission reduction.

title: Cross-city traffic noise modeling and inequality analysis via AlphaEarth Geospatial Foundation Models
abstract: Traffic noise is a widespread environmental problem in modern cities. Traditional traffic noise modeling is limited to small-scale coverage by high sensor costs and complex simulation parameter settings. GeoAI-based methods (incorporating remote sensing and street view) can effectively address scalability challenges. However, those methods use RGB imagery and lack physical observation approaches (e.g., LiDAR), which often leads to insufficient characterization of complex urban environments (e.g., three-dimensional buildings, pavement materials, vegetation absorption). This study proposes a cross-city noise exposure framework via the AlphaEarth Foundation (AEF) model. Pre-trained on 3 billion multimodal observations (including SAR, and meteorology), AEF mitigates the reliance on extensive ground-truth datasets through capturing complex coupling between morphology, 3D structures, and acoustic characteristics. Our research findings demonstrate that: (1) The model achieves a coefficient of determination (R2) greater than 0.84 for noise estimation. (2) The traffic noise exposure transfer computations across multiple global cities reveal exposure inequalities.
